commands.name: get_actor_team
commands.description: Reads the native team id (FGenericTeamId) of an actor in the editor world, the team AI Perception uses to tell friend from foe: from the actor itself when it implements IGenericTeamAgentInterface, otherwise from its AAIController when it is a pawn possessed by one; resolved_on says which. When neither implements the interface the call still succeeds, with the engine-reserved NoTeam id 255, is_no_team true and resolved_on "none". Read-only: changes nothing. Editor world only, never a PIE session, so teams assigned at runtime are not seen. An unknown actor is an error. Use it to check set_actor_team, which writes the id; set_native_team_attitude decides whether two team ids are friendly, neutral or hostile; get_ai_perception_senses lists which senses a Blueprint's perception has.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the actor in the editor world (case-insensitive, first match), e.g. "BP_Guard_C_0" (required); a pawn, or the AIController itself.

commands.returns: { actor_name, team_id, resolved_on: "actor"|"controller"|"none", is_no_team }

commands.name: get_ai_perceived_actors
commands.description: List the actors that the AIPerceptionComponent of an AI-possessed pawn, or of an AIController, currently perceives by any sense, without changing anything. The actor is looked up in the editor world, not PIE, so an unpossessed pawn is an error. Returns count and perceived [{actor_name}]; no last-sensed time is included.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or editor label of the pawn or AIController in the editor world; the first match is used.

commands.returns: { actor_name, perceived: [{actor_name}], count }

commands.name: set_actor_team
commands.description: Set the native team id (FGenericTeamId) of an actor in the editor world through IGenericTeamAgentInterface, falling back to its Controller when the actor does not implement it (an ACharacter possessed by an AAIController, the only implementer in vanilla UE 5.8), then refresh that agent's AI Perception listeners so Sight, Hearing and Touch affiliation filtering sees the new team at once. The previous team is overwritten in memory only: no undo step, nothing dirtied or saved, and on an AAIController it is gone when the level reloads. The same id again gives the same result. Read it with get_actor_team; set_native_team_attitude decides whether two teams are friendly, neutral or hostile. An unknown actor, a team_id outside 0-254, or no team interface on the actor or its controller is an error and nothing changes.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the actor in the editor world (a pawn, or the AIController itself), e.g. 'BP_Guard_C_0'.

params.name: team_id
params.description: Team number, an integer in [0, 254], e.g. 1; 255 is the engine-reserved NoTeam id and is refused.

commands.returns: { actor_name, team_id, applied, resolved_on: "actor"|"controller", perception_listeners_refreshed }

The actor is looked up in the editor world, not PIE, so an unpossessed pawn is an error. Returns sight_radius, lose_sight_radius and sight_sense_count; 0 means no sight config, nothing changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or editor label of the pawn or AIController in the editor world; the first match is used.

params.name: sight_radius
params.description: New SightRadius in cm, greater than 0.

params.name: lose_sight_radius

commands.returns: { actor_name, sight_radius, lose_sight_radius, sight_sense_count }

commands.name: set_native_team_attitude
commands.description: Installs (once per process) a custom FGenericTeamId::AttitudeSolver backed by an MCP-owned symmetric table, then records the pairwise attitude for team_a/team_b. params.name: persist
params.description: Also write the snapshot to Saved/MCPAudits/snapshots/<handle>.json so it SURVIVES an editor restart. The in-memory store is a process-lifetime map: without this, a baseline captured before a mandatory restart is gone exactly when you need to compare against it. Default false.

params.name: return_snapshot

params.name: snapshot_id
params.description: Alias of handle: the name to store the snapshot under, used only when handle is absent or empty; an existing snapshot with that name is overwritten

commands.name: check_asset_circular_dependency
commands.description: Depth-first search of an asset's dependency graph looking for a CYCLE, returning has_circular_dependency plus the actual circular_path that closes the loop and its length -- the diagnosis for cook failures, load-order surprises and Blueprints that will not compile in isolation. Complements get_asset_dependencies (one level out) and get_asset_dependencies_recursive (the whole closure without cycle detection). WARNING: check `search_limit_reached` before trusting a false: the walk stops at max_depth / max_visited, and a cycle beyond those limits reads exactly like no cycle at all.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Exact asset name or full package name; the bare-name fallback scans /Game only and takes the first match

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Maximum recursion depth, default 100. Hitting it sets search_limit_reached and makes a `false` answer inconclusive.

params.name: max_visited
params.description: Maximum total nodes visited, default 10000. Hitting it also sets search_limit_reached.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Filter by dependency kind considered at every DFS step: "hard", "soft", or "all" (case-insensitive), default "all"

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, has_circular_dependency: bool, nodes_visited: int, max_depth_reached: int, search_limit_reached: bool, circular_path: [string] (the cycle itself, its first package repeated at the end), cycle_length: int (packages in the cycle), root_in_cycle: bool, lead_in_path?: [string] (root ... first package of the cycle, when the root only leads into it), suggestion?: string (the edge that closes the cycle), dependency_type: string }

commands.name: diff_blueprint_components
commands.description: Compare the COMPONENT trees of two Blueprints (or of one Blueprint against a components[] array captured earlier from get_blueprint_components) and report which components were added, removed or changed, where "changed" means the class, attach_parent, attach_socket, source or relative transform (0.01 tolerance) differ. It reuses get_blueprint_components's full enumeration, so native + own SCS + inherited components are all in scope, most-derived-wins. Use it for "did a reparent or a merge lose a component?" -- feeding a pre-change scs_tree as components_b makes it a before/after check without a second asset. removed = in A only, added = in B only. Read-only. diff_blueprints covers components AND graphs AND variables; get_blueprint_component_overrides goes deeper into ONE component's per-property provenance.

params.name: blueprint_a
params.description: First Blueprint asset path or short name (the "before" / baseline side).

params.name: blueprint_b
params.description: Second Blueprint (the "after" side). Omit if passing components_b.

params.name: components_b
params.description: Alternative to blueprint_b: a prior get_blueprint_components components array (snapshot). A snapshot without transforms reads every transform as changed.

params.name: include_native
params.description: Include native/CDO components on the live side(s) (default true).

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Include components inherited from ancestor Blueprints (default true).

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on components enumerated per live side, 1..10000 (default 2000).

commands.returns: { blueprint_a, a_path, blueprint_b, b_path, side_b_source, added:[record], removed:[record], changed:[{name, class, changes:{class?:{a,b}, attach_parent?:{a,b}, attach_socket?:{a,b}, source?:{a,b}, transform?:{a,b}}}], unchanged_count, counts_a:{native,scs,inherited}, counts_b:{...}, truncated, total_differences }

commands.name: diff_blueprints
commands.description: Structural diff of TWO Blueprints (or AnimBlueprints): parent class, SCS components, variables, functions, and per graph a node-by-node diff of what was added, removed and changed, where a changed node reports its title, per-pin default-value and link changes and -- for AnimGraph nodes -- the internal FAnimNode config and property-binding differences. With graph_name it diffs ONE graph pair only -- far cheaper when you already know the graph you care about (an "AnimGraph", a function, a collapsed composite by title). WARNING: nodes are matched by NodeGuid, which duplicating or forking an asset PRESERVES: this is built to compare a fork against its original, and two independently authored Blueprints will show every single node as added/removed, which is noise, not a finding. Read-only. Siblings: diff_blueprint_components for components only, get_blueprint_component_overrides for per-property provenance, compare_objects for two LIVE UObjects instead of authored structure. Watch `graphs_not_examined[]` -- when the node budget runs out the remaining graphs are listed there instead of being reported as identical.

params.name: blueprint_a
params.description: First Blueprint asset path or short name.

params.name: blueprint_b
params.description: Second Blueprint asset path or short name.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Optional: diff only this graph, resolved deep on each side (function/event/macro/AnimGraph, a collapsed composite by title, or a path form 'EventGraph > Title'); an empty string means the event graph. A graph missing on either side is an error.

params.name: max_nodes
params.description: TOTAL cap on nodes examined across every graph (default 20000). When it runs out, the remaining graphs are listed in graphs_not_examined[] instead of being silently reported as identical.

params.name: max_nodes_per_graph
params.description: Per-graph cap so one fat graph cannot starve the rest (default = max_nodes).

commands.returns: { blueprint_a, blueprint_b, a_path, b_path, a_class, b_class, parent_class:{a,b,changed}, components:{added,removed,changed}, variables:{added,removed,changed}, functions:{added,removed,common}, graphs:[{graph_name, nodes_added, nodes_removed, nodes_changed, node_count_a, node_count_b, nodes_examined_a, nodes_examined_b, truncated}], graphs_identical:[string], graphs_not_examined:[{graph_name, reason}], graphs_only_in_a, graphs_only_in_b, truncated, max_nodes, max_nodes_per_graph, nodes_examined, total_differences } -- with graph_name the reply is that one pair instead: { blueprint_a, blueprint_b, a_path, b_path, a_class, b_class, graph_name, resolved_graph_a, resolved_graph_b, node_count_a, node_count_b, nodes_added, nodes_removed, nodes_changed, nodes_examined_a, nodes_examined_b, truncated, max_nodes, total_differences }.

commands.name: diff_object_snapshots
commands.description: Compare two snapshots taken by capture_object_snapshot and report which properties were added, removed or CHANGED, at the object level and per component, with both values side by side. The second half of the before/after measurement: capture a baseline, run the action, capture again, and this tells you what actually moved -- instead of trusting the acting call's own success flag. Also the way to diff editor-vs-PIE and, in co-op, SERVER-vs-CLIENT state for the same actor, which is the only proof that a value really replicated. Sides can be given as stored handles, as inline snapshot objects (from capture_object_snapshot(return_snapshot=true)), or as paths to persisted snapshot files; `a_origin`/`b_origin` report which route each side came from. compare_objects is the same idea for two LIVE objects at one instant.

params.name: handle_a
params.description: Handle of the first (baseline) snapshot (aliases: a, snapshot_a). Resolved from the in-memory store first, then from the persisted Saved/MCPAudits/snapshots/<handle>.json copy.

params.name: handle_b
params.description: Handle of the second snapshot (aliases: b, snapshot_b). Same resolution.

params.name: snapshot_a
params.description: The baseline snapshot INLINE (a JSON object, e.g. what capture_object_snapshot(return_snapshot=true) handed back). A STRING here is read as a handle.

params.name: snapshot_b
params.description: The second snapshot INLINE (a JSON object). A STRING here is read as a handle.

params.name: path_a
params.description: Path to a persisted baseline snapshot file (bare handles resolve under Saved/MCPAudits/snapshots/).

params.name: path_b
params.description: Path to a persisted second snapshot file.

commands.returns: { handle_a, handle_b, a_origin, b_origin, a_object_path, b_object_path, a_class, b_class, a_world, b_world, properties:{added,removed,changed}, components:{added,removed,changed:[{component, properties:{added,removed,changed}}]}, total_differences }

commands.name: find_erroring_blueprints
commands.description: Scan a content path for Blueprints and AnimBlueprints sitting in a compile ERROR state and report each one with its status, error/warning counts and its FIRST error message -- the search for the culprit when PIE refuses to start because of an asset nobody was working on. It reads the loaded compile Status and recompiles the erroring ones with a results log to extract that message. WARNING: loading every Blueprint under a broad path is heavy enough to stall the editor on thousands of assets: scope `path` narrowly, and reach for only_loaded=true first -- the Blueprint that aborts PIE is usually still in memory, so that fast in-memory pass normally finds it without a single disk load. Complements validate_assets_in_path and audit_blueprint_health by listing EVERY erroring Blueprint with its first error in one call. WARNING: the scope parameter is named `path`, NOT search_path: pass the wrong name and it is silently ignored, the default /Game applies, and the tool sweeps the whole project while the answer looks scoped to your folder.

params.name: path
params.description: Content path to scan, recursive (default "/Game"). WARNING: this exact name -- a `search_path` key is ignored and you get the full /Game sweep. Scope it narrowly to stay cheap.

params.name: only_loaded
params.description: When true, only inspect Blueprints already loaded in memory (no disk load). Default false.

params.name: include_warnings
params.description: Also report Blueprints with compile WARNINGS (not just errors). Default false.

params.name: compile_all
params.description: Recompile EVERY scanned Blueprint (thorough but heavy); otherwise only recompile ones whose loaded Status is already Error. Default false.

params.name: max_scan
params.description: Max Blueprints to load/inspect (default 5000).

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max erroring/warning Blueprints to return (default 500).

commands.returns: { path, scanned, inspected, only_loaded, erroring_count, warning_count, results_truncated, blueprints:[{ asset_path, name, class, status, num_errors, num_warnings, first_error }] }

commands.name: get_asset_dependencies
commands.description: List every package an asset DEPENDS ON (its outgoing edges), each with its class and loaded state -- "what does this asset drag in with it?", the input to a migration or import budget. Direction matters: this is what the asset NEEDS; get_asset_referencers answers who needs IT. Use get_asset_dependencies_recursive for the transitive closure and check_asset_circular_dependency to detect cycles. WARNING: these are PACKAGE-level edges from the Asset Registry: they cannot tell you WHICH node or property creates the edge (that is find_blueprint_node_references), and a name built at runtime or resolved through a DataRegistry produces no edge at all.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Exact asset name or full package name; the bare-name fallback scans /Game only and stops at the FIRST match, without reporting that others existed

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum dependencies to return, 1..50000 (default 5000). Read `results_truncated` for the real answer: `total_dependencies` counts the RAW registry edges before exclude_engine, so it exceeds dependencies_count on almost every asset without anything having been cut.

params.name: exclude_engine
params.description: Skip /Engine and /Script dependencies, default true. Filtered entries do NOT consume the max_results budget, but they ARE counted in total_dependencies.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Filter by dependency kind: "hard", "soft", or "all" (case-insensitive), default "all"

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, dependencies: [object], dependencies_count: int, total_dependencies: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool, exclude_engine: bool, dependency_type: string }

commands.name: get_asset_referencers
commands.description: List every asset that REFERENCES a target asset -- "who breaks if I delete, move or rename this?" -- wrapping AssetRegistry::GetReferencers over the Package category and returning each referencing package with its primary asset's name, path, class and loaded state. It accepts an object path, a package path or a bare name, echoes `resolved_package` so you can confirm it queried the package you meant, and REFUSES an ambiguous bare name with the candidate list instead of picking one. Hard references only by default (the "what keeps this loaded" audit); dependency_type='soft' or 'all' (or include_soft_references=true) brings in TSoftObjectPtr / FSoftObjectPath edges, and exclude_engine=true drops /Engine and /Script referencers. Works for any asset type, a MetaSound included. Its mirror is get_asset_dependencies (what this asset needs), and find_blueprint_node_references finds call sites INSIDE graphs, which package-level references cannot see.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Target asset: an object path ('/Game/X/DT_ItemRows.DT_ItemRows'), a package path ('/Game/X/DT_ItemRows'), or an unambiguous bare asset name ('DT_ItemRows'). An ambiguous bare name is an error listing the candidates, never a silent pick.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Alias of asset_path.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Optional 'hard' | 'soft' | 'all' (case-insensitive): which edges count. When given it wins over include_soft_references; when absent, include_soft_references decides (hard, or all).

params.name: include_soft_references
params.description: If true, also include soft referencers (default false -> hard-only). Shorthand for dependency_type='all'.

params.name: exclude_engine
params.description: Optional bool (default false): skip /Engine and /Script referencers. They do not count against max_results, but they do count in total.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of returned referencers (1..50000); defaults to 5000.

commands.returns: { asset_path, resolved_package, include_soft_references, dependency_type, exclude_engine, total, returned, results_truncated, referencers:[{ package_name, asset_name?, asset_path?, asset_class?, is_loaded? }] } -- total counts every referencer the registry returned, engine ones included; results_truncated says a referencer that would have been listed was left out by max_results; is_loaded is whether the referencing asset is loaded now.

commands.name: get_blueprint_component_overrides
commands.description: Per-property PROVENANCE on a Blueprint's component templates: which values this Blueprint actually OVERRODE and which it merely inherits. Over the same components as get_blueprint_components (native CDO + own SCS + inherited chain) it resolves the effective template down the SCS -> child ICH override -> ancestor SCS -> native CDO cascade, never minting an ICH override, and compares each editable property against a baseline -- the archetype by default, or the same-named template in `other_blueprint` for the "fork vs original" question -- with the ENGINE's equality (FProperty::Identical, PPF_DeepComparison) instead of exported text. Each result is CLASSIFIED (identical | real_override | text_localization_metadata_only | object_outer_only | export_text_only | type_mismatch | no_baseline), so FText localization and object-outer noise stop masquerading as edits. WARNING: component templates can go STALE in memory (values can flip just from an editor restart): pass verify_on_disk to cross-check the raw .uasset bytes -- for anything not string-ish it answers found:null / applicable:false, never a misleading false. Read-only. list_instance_overrides asks the same question about a PLACED ACTOR.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name to audit.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional: restrict the audit to this one component (exact variable name).

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional: restrict the audit to this one property (FName or authored name).

params.name: other_blueprint
params.description: Optional: compare against the SAME-NAMED template in this other Blueprint instead of against the archetype (the "fork vs original" question).

params.name: include_native
params.description: Include native/CDO components (default true).

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Include components inherited from ancestor Blueprints (default true).

params.name: include_identical
params.description: Also emit properties that are equal in BOTH the engine comparison and the exported text (default false -- they are the vast majority).

params.name: only_editable
params.description: Only consider CPF_Edit properties (default true). Transient/DuplicateTransient/NonPIEDuplicateTransient/Deprecated are always skipped.

params.name: verify_on_disk
params.description: Cross-check string-ish values against the raw .uasset bytes of the package that owns the template (default false).

params.name: max_components
params.description: Cap on components enumerated, 1..10000 (default 500).

params.name: max_properties_per_component
params.description: Cap on properties examined per component, 1..20000 (default 1000).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, blueprint_path, other_blueprint?, other_blueprint_path?, baseline_mode, components:[{component, resolved, template_name, template_path, scs_variable_name, component_key_guid, matched_by_scs_node, component_class, source, declaring_class, resolved_from_class, authored_here, baseline_source, baseline_path, baseline_class, component_class_mismatch, properties:[{component, property, property_display, value, baseline_value, inherited_value, inherited_value_available, authored_here, declaring_class, resolved_from_class, template_source, baseline_source, kind, differs, identical_deep, export_text_equal, export_text_value, export_text_baseline, note, on_disk?}], properties_reported, properties_examined, properties_truncated}], components_examined, components_truncated, properties_examined, override_count, noise_count, identical_count, no_baseline_count, on_disk:{found,not_found,not_applicable}, templates_may_be_stale, success }

commands.name: get_blueprint_components
commands.description: Enumerate the COMPLETE component tree of a Blueprint asset -- native components from the C++ CDO, its own SCS nodes, and everything inherited down the ancestor chain -- each classified by source with its class, attach parent/socket, children, transform and template facts (mobility, physics and collision state, static mesh + material count), most-derived-wins. include_native=false + include_inherited=false narrows it to the Blueprint's OWN construction script. `component_class` filters by class OR ANY SUBCLASS across all three sources, which Actor::GetComponentsByClass cannot do (it only ever sees a constructed instance's OwnedComponents, never SCS templates on a Blueprint nobody instantiated). WARNING: before concluding a component does not exist, read `omitted_total`, NOT results_truncated: null templates and name-shadowed ancestor entries are dropped without setting it, and omitted_duplicate_names[]/omitted_null_templates[] name what disappeared (counted before the component_class filter). `scs_cdo_desync` / `generated_property_exists` flag an SCS that disagrees with the compiled class -- the fingerprint of a half-reverted asset. See diff_blueprint_components to compare two trees, get_actor_components for a live instance.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint or AnimBlueprint asset short name (exact) or full /Game path; a bare name that matches more than one Blueprint asset resolves to one of them and lists the others in `ambiguous_matches`, so pass the path when it matters

params.name: include_native
params.description: Include C++/native components from the CDO (default true)

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Include components inherited from ancestor Blueprint classes (default true)

params.name: component_class
params.description: Optional class filter (short name, /Script/Module.Class, or /Game/... Blueprint path). Matches this class OR ANY SUBCLASS of it (same semantics as the engine's own GetComponentsByClass), evaluated against every source (native CDO, own SCS, inherited SCS) -- unlike Actor::GetComponentsByClass/K2_GetComponentsByClass, which only ever see a live actor's already-constructed OwnedComponents and are blind to SCS node templates on a Blueprint that hasn't been instantiated yet.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on components returned, 1..10000 (default 1000)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_valid: bool, ambiguous_matches?: [string], parent_class: string, parent_class_path: string, components: [{ name, source, class, class_path, owner_class, is_root, is_scene_component, attach_parent, attach_socket, parent_is_native, ich_overridden?, transform?: {loc, rot, scale}, children: [string], category, mobility?, simulates_physics?, collision_enabled?, has_static_mesh?, static_mesh_path?, material_count?, generated_property_exists, scs_cdo_desync }], components_count: int, counts: object, has_simple_construction_script: bool, results_truncated: bool, max_results: int, component_class_filter: string|null, component_class_resolved: bool, desync_count: int, blueprint_status: string, generated_class_available: bool, omitted_duplicate_names: [{name, source, owner_class, shadowed_by?}], omitted_duplicate_count: int, omitted_null_templates: [{name, source, owner_class}], omitted_null_template_count: int, omitted_total: int } -- children names the components attached under a record (same SCS tree, or the CDO's own attach children for a native one); category is the text before the first underscore of the name; mobility only on scene components, simulates_physics/collision_enabled on primitives, has_static_mesh/static_mesh_path/material_count on static mesh components. generated_property_exists (bool|null) and scs_cdo_desync (bool|null): the compiler mints one FObjectProperty per SCS node with the SAME FName as the node (SCS_Node.h, KismetCompiler.cpp), so a MISSING property means the SCS and the compiled class disagree -- the fingerprint of an asset left half-reverted. This tool emits Node->GetVariableName() VERBATIM; it does NOT normalize a trailing digit.

commands.name: get_blueprint_exec_path
commands.description: Report which exec nodes and BRANCHES actually RAN inside a Blueprint at runtime -- which Branch went true, which FunctionResult fired -- read from the editor's Blueprint-debugger trace stack. Unlike the static reader get_blueprint_debug_info, which lists every node that exists, this reflects real execution, so it answers "did that path run at all?" when a graph fails silently. WARNING: two-phase by construction: the VM only records the trace for the object currently being DEBUGGED, so call it ONCE with object_path to arm recording (SetObjectBeingDebugged), then drive the PIE scenario, then call it AGAIN to read the recorded path -- a single call returns nothing and that is not a bug. Requires a running PIE session with Blueprint debugging; `world` (including 'server' / 'client' / 'pie:N') selects which instance gets armed, and the response stamps which world it was.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint / AnimBlueprint asset path or short name to filter the trace to.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Optional: only include samples in a function/graph whose name contains this.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Optional live PIE object to set as the debugged instance (arms trace recording).

params.name: set_debug_object
params.description: When object_path is given, call SetObjectBeingDebugged on it. Default true.

params.name: world
params.description: World to resolve object_path in: absent/'editor' (default) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'pie'/'game'/'runtime' (ambiguous). A fully-qualified PIE object path (...UEDPIE...) resolves regardless of this.

params.name: max_samples
params.description: Max trace-stack samples to scan (default 500).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, blueprint_path, debug_object_set, object_path, trace_stack_size, filtered_count, path:[{index, node_id, node_class, node_title, graph, function, context, is_branch, is_function_result, observation_time}], note, world_selector, world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode, pie_instance (the world of the ARMED debug object; nulls when none was armed) }

commands.name: get_blueprint_parent
commands.description: Read which class a Blueprint ASSET inherits from: parent class name and path, whether that parent is native C++ or another Blueprint, and the Blueprint's own type (Normal / Interface / MacroLibrary / FunctionLibrary / LevelScript / Const). The first question to ask about an unfamiliar Blueprint, and the way to tell whether a library class sneaked into the parent chain. It returns ONE level -- get_class_hierarchy walks the whole ancestor chain of the compiled class, list_derived_classes lists descendants, and verify_reparent_success checks the chain against an expectation after a reparent. WARNING: an ambiguous bare name still resolves to the FIRST match and only lists the rest in `ambiguous_matches` (the other match is often a dated backup copy that backup_asset wrote under /Game/MCP_Backups), so run resolve_asset_by_name first or pass the full path.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset short name (exact) or full package name. The full package name is tried first; the bare-name fallback scans /Game only, matching UBlueprint assets, and picks the first hit.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_valid: bool, parent_class: string, parent_class_path: string, has_parent: bool, parent_is_native: bool, blueprint_type: string, ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: verify_reparent_success
commands.description: Check, after a reparent_blueprint, that the Blueprint really ended up where you wanted: it confirms the parent class against an expectation, reports the compile status, and -- when you feed it counts captured BEFOREHAND -- verifies no components or variables were lost, listing every failed invariant in `regressions[]`. This is the oracle for a reparent, because reparent_blueprint's own return value says nothing about whether the class survived it. WARNING: read-only by default, which means it reports the CACHED Blueprint->Status: pass force_compile=true to recompile and get the real status plus the compiler messages (compile_messages[] is empty without it, and `compile_ran` tells you which mode you got). Component count comes from the compiled CDO (native + SCS + inherited). Omit the expected_* counts to skip those invariants; get_blueprint_components or get_blueprint_variables before the reparent is where they come from.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path.

params.name: expected_parent_class
params.description: Class name or path the Blueprint should now inherit from.

params.name: expected_component_count
params.description: Optional: CDO component count captured before the reparent.

params.name: expected_variable_count
params.description: Optional: own-variable (NewVariables) count captured before the reparent.

params.name: force_compile
params.description: Optional (default false): recompile to obtain the real compile status AND the compiler messages (compile_messages[] is empty without it -- compile_ran says which).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, blueprint_path, parent_class, expected_parent_class, parent_match, compile_status, compile_match, compile_ran, compile_messages:[{severity,message}], compile_num_errors, compile_num_warnings, component_count, expected_component_count, components_match, variable_count, expected_variable_count, variables_match, regressions:[string], success }

commands.name: add_anim_composite_segment
commands.description: Add an FAnimSegment that plays a whole UAnimSequence to a UAnimComposite's AnimationTrack in one undo step, re-stack all segments end to end, recompute the composite length and save the asset. The segments are ordered by start_pos before the re-stack, so to append at the end pass start_pos at or past the current composite_length; the default 0 ties with the first segment and normally sorts in front of it. Every call adds another segment (not idempotent). Create the composite first with create_anim_composite, check it with get_anim_asset_info, and take a segment out by index with remove_anim_composite_segment. A composite and sequence on different skeletons, or a path that does not load, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes the reply's success false with saved=false and save_error; the success field inside the data stays true, so read saved.

params.name: composite_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimComposite, e.g. '/Game/Animation/AC_Example' (create_anim_composite makes one).

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence to play, on the composite's skeleton, e.g. '/Game/Anims/A_Walk'; the segment covers its full length.

params.name: start_pos
params.description: Start time in seconds used only to order the new segment among the existing ones before all are re-stacked end to end (default 0, which normally sorts it first); pass the current composite_length or more to append.

params.name: play_rate
params.description: Playback rate of the segment, 1.0 = normal speed, 2.0 = twice as fast (default 1.0).

params.name: loop_count
params.description: How many times the segment repeats, a whole number; values below 1 become 1 (default 1).

commands.returns: { composite_path, animation_path, num_segments, composite_length, segments, success, saved, save_error }

commands.name: add_anim_conduit
commands.description: Add a conduit node named conduit_name to an existing state machine of an Animation Blueprint (a missing blueprint or machine is an error; create the machine with add_anim_state_machine), then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling. Idempotent by name: an existing conduit is returned unchanged (already_existed true). The conduit is placed unconnected: link it to states with add_anim_transition; remove_anim_conduit undoes it. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset

params.name: machine_name
params.description: Name of the target state machine

params.name: conduit_name
params.description: Name for the new conduit

commands.returns: { anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, conduit_name: string, node_class: string, conduit_created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, conduit_count: int, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_anim_curve_name
commands.description: Register a curve name as curve metadata on a USkeleton (USkeleton::AddCurveMetaData) in an undo transaction, then save the skeleton package. Idempotent: a name already registered is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the skeleton is neither modified nor saved. It adds no keys -- to put a keyed float curve on a UAnimSequence use add_anim_float_curve; remove_anim_curve_name is the inverse. An unknown skeleton is an error and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: The curve name to add (e.g. 'Curve_Example').

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Asset path of the USkeleton to edit (/Game/...); when omitted or empty the engine asset /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton is edited and saved.

commands.returns: { skeleton_path, curve_name, present, added, already_existed, curve_count, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: add_anim_float_curve
commands.description: Add a float curve (Editable flag) to a UAnimSequence, or rekey the one already there, through its data controller: its keys become the [time, value] pairs as linear keys with auto tangents, in one undo step, then the package is saved. An existing float curve of that name is kept and its keys are replaced (idempotent); one that already holds exactly those keys is a success with changed=false, applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. curve_found confirms the curve and num_keys counts the keys sent. A missing sequence is an error, and so are keys the data controller rejects, with nothing saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. curve_type=transform is refused before anything is loaded, since [time, value] keys only fit a float curve. Transform curves: add_anim_transform_curve; a skeleton-only name: add_anim_curve_name; read back: get_anim_curve_data.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Float curve name to add or rekey.

params.name: keys
params.description: JSON array of [time, value] pairs, time in seconds (default [[0,0],[1,1]]); entries that are not such a pair are skipped.

params.name: curve_type
params.description: Optional curve type the keys are meant for: float (the default, the only one written). transform is refused with an error pointing at add_anim_transform_curve; any other value is an error.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, num_float_curves, num_keys, curve_found, changed, applied, success, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: add_anim_graph_node
commands.description: Place a UAnimGraphNode_* (by class name) into an AnimGraph or a state's inner graph. Saves the ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path or name of the UAnimBlueprint.

params.name: node_class
params.description: AnimGraphNode class: short name (e.g. "AnimGraphNode_Slot", "AnimGraphNode_PoseSearchHistoryCollector") or full path.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph; omit/"AnimGraph" for the top-level AnimGraph, or a nested name like "MainSM > Idle".

params.name: x
params.description: Node X position (optional, default 0).

params.name: y
params.description: Node Y position (optional, default 0).

commands.returns: { node_id, node_class, graph_name, pins[], saved } (NodeToJson of the created node)

commands.name: add_anim_notify
commands.description: Add an instance of a UAnimNotify class at a time on a UAnimSequence notify track (created when missing) and save the sequence; each call adds another event, and an unknown class is an error. Returns time and success. For montages use add_montage_notify; for durations add_anim_notify_state. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence.

params.name: notify_name
params.description: Class name of a loaded UAnimNotify subclass, tried as given and then with the AnimNotify_ prefix (e.g. 'AN_Footstep', or "PlaySound" for AnimNotify_PlaySound); a Blueprint notify goes by its generated name ending in _C.

params.name: time
params.description: Notify trigger time in seconds (default 0)

params.name: track_name
params.description: Notify track name (default 'Default')

commands.returns: { animation_path, notify_name, time, success, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: add_anim_notify_name
commands.description: Register a notify name in the AnimationNotifies list of a USkeleton inside an undo transaction and save the skeleton package; returns present, notify_count and saved. A name already registered is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the skeleton is neither modified nor saved. Without skeleton_path it edits /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Inverse: remove_anim_notify_name.

params.name: notify_name
params.description: The notify name to register (e.g. 'Footstep').

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Asset path of the USkeleton to edit (/Game/...); when omitted or empty the engine asset /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton is edited and saved.

commands.returns: { skeleton_path, notify_name, present, added, already_existed, notify_count, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: add_anim_notify_state
commands.description: Add an instance of a UAnimNotifyState class with a start time and duration to a UAnimSequence notify track (created when missing) and save the sequence; each call adds another event, and unknown classes are refused. Returns start_time, duration and success. For instant notifies use add_anim_notify. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence.

params.name: notify_state_name
params.description: Class name of a loaded UAnimNotifyState subclass, tried as given and then with the AnimNotifyState_ prefix (e.g. "Trail" for AnimNotifyState_Trail); a Blueprint notify state goes by its generated name ending in _C.

params.name: start_time
params.description: Notify state start time in seconds (default 0)

params.name: duration
params.description: Notify state duration in seconds (default 1.0)

params.name: track_name
params.description: Notify track name (default 'Default')

commands.returns: { animation_path, notify_state_name, start_time, duration, success, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: add_anim_slot_group
commands.description: Add an animation slot group (a named group that montage slots belong to; one slot per group plays at a time) to a USkeleton asset in one undo step and save the skeleton. Use it before giving a montage a slot in a new group; the montage side is create_anim_montage (slot_name) or add_montage_slot, and the inverse is remove_anim_slot_group. get_skeleton_info with load_full_data=true reports slot_group_count. Idempotent: a group that already exists returns added=false and is not changed, but the skeleton is still marked dirty and saved. A skeleton that does not load is an error. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Edit a project copy (create_editable_skeleton), not engine content.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: USkeleton asset as a package or object path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton", as get_skeleton_info returns it.

params.name: group_name
params.description: Name of the slot group to add, compared as an FName (case ignored), e.g. "WeaponGroup".

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, group_name: string, added: bool, slot_group_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_anim_state
commands.description: Add a state node named state_name to an existing state machine of an Animation Blueprint, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). Not an undo step. Idempotent by name: a state of that name (case-insensitive) is returned unchanged with already_existed true, and nothing is saved. The machine must sit on the top-level AnimGraph (add_anim_state_machine creates it); a missing blueprint or machine is an error. The new state is unconnected and its animation graph empty: link it with add_anim_transition, fill it with add_anim_graph_node, check the machine with get_anim_state_machine_info; remove_anim_state is the inverse. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Content path of the UAnimBlueprint (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/ABP_Hero'.

params.name: machine_name
params.description: Name of a state machine on the blueprint's top-level AnimGraph, as get_anim_blueprint_info lists it in state_machines (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Locomotion'.

params.name: state_name
params.description: Name for the new state, e.g. 'Idle'; the reply's state_name is the name its graph actually got.

commands.returns: { anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, state_name: string, node_class: string, state_created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, state_count: int, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_anim_state_machine
commands.description: Add a state machine node named machine_name to the top-level AnimGraph of an Animation Blueprint, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). Idempotent by name: an existing machine is returned unchanged (already_existed true). The node starts with only its entry and is not connected to the Output Pose: wire it with connect_anim_graph_pins, fill it with add_anim_state, add_anim_conduit and add_anim_transition, or build it in one call with build_anim_state_machine. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset

params.name: machine_name
params.description: Name for the new state machine

commands.returns: { anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, node_class: string, state_machine_graph: string, state_machine_created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, state_machine_count: int, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_anim_sync_marker
commands.description: Append an authored sync marker (name and time, on marker track 0) to a UAnimSequence in an undo transaction and save it; duplicates are not checked, nor is the time checked against the sequence length. Returns num_sync_markers. Remove with remove_anim_sync_marker. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: marker_name
params.description: Name of the sync marker (e.g. "LeftFootDown"); sequences in one sync group line up markers that share a name.

params.name: time
params.description: Sync marker time in seconds (default 0.5)

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, marker_name, time, num_sync_markers, success, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: add_anim_transform_curve
commands.description: Add a transform curve (RCT_Transform) to a UAnimSequence via the data controller and set its keys as linear keys per axis, in one undo step, then save the package; the sampling rate of the sequence is left as it is. An existing transform curve of that name is kept and its keys are replaced; one that already holds exactly those keys is a success with changed=false, keys_set=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the transform curve to add.

params.name: keys
params.description: JSON array of {time, location:[x,y,z], rotation:[pitch,yaw,roll], scale:[x,y,z]} objects

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, num_transform_curves, num_keys, keys_set, changed, success, saved, save_error, message? }

commands.name: add_anim_transition
commands.description: Add a transition from source_state to target_state in an existing state machine of an Animation Blueprint, set its crossfade, blend mode, bidirectional flag and priority, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). The machine (top-level AnimGraph) and both endpoints (a state or a conduit) are matched by name without case; a missing one, the same state twice or an unknown blend_mode is an error. Idempotent per pair: an existing source->target transition is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and nothing is saved (to change its settings, remove_anim_transition and add it again). It starts with no rule: wire one with set_anim_transition_rule_from_bool, set_anim_transition_rule_from_comparison or set_anim_transition_rule_automatic. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset

params.name: machine_name
params.description: Name of the state machine that owns both states

params.name: source_state
params.description: Name of the source state or conduit (transition origin), matched without case

params.name: target_state
params.description: Name of the target state or conduit (transition destination), matched without case

params.name: crossfade_duration
params.description: Optional blend duration in seconds (default 0.2)

params.name: blend_mode
params.description: Optional EAlphaBlendOption name, e.g. Linear, Cubic, HermiteCubic (default HermiteCubic); an unknown name is an error

params.name: bidirectional
params.description: Optional, default false; sets the Bidirectional flag so the same transition can also fire target->source (no second transition is added)

params.name: priority_order
params.description: Optional priority order (default 1); when several transitions out of a state pass at once, the smallest value wins

commands.returns: { anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, source_state: string, target_state: string, transition_created: bool, already_existed: bool, crossfade_duration: number, blend_mode: string, bidirectional: bool, priority_order: int, transition_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_animation_asset_to_pose_search_database
commands.description: Append an animation asset to a UPoseSearchDatabase as an enabled entry over its full range, then save the database; an asset already in it is left alone (already_existed=true, saved=false, nothing saved). The asset type is not checked, and the search index is not rebuilt: run build_pose_search_database_index afterwards.

params.name: database_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase (required).

params.name: animation_asset_path
params.description: Asset path of a UAnimSequenceBase / UAnimComposite / UAnimMontage / UBlendSpace (required).

commands.returns: { database_path, animation_asset_path, animation_asset_count, added, already_existed, saved, message }

commands.name: add_blend_space_sample
commands.description: Add one sample (an animation placed at a blend position) to a UBlendSpace or UBlendSpace1D in one undo step, rebuild its runtime data and save the asset. Every call appends a new sample, so it is not a retry-safe call. A sample the engine would reject is refused before anything changes, with success=false, added=false, sample_index -1, saved=false and the reason in the error: an animation whose skeleton is neither the blend space's nor compatible with it, an additive type the blend space does not take or that differs from the existing samples', a position already taken by a sample, or a position an axis cannot widen to in 1000 grid steps or fewer. Otherwise a position past an axis range widens that axis. The sample is read back after the rebuild: animation and blend_x, blend_y, blend_z are what the asset holds at sample_index. Create the asset with create_blend_space and list its samples with get_blend_space_samples; move or swap an existing sample with set_blend_space_sample, and take one out with remove_blend_space_sample. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: blendspace_path
params.description: Object path of the UBlendSpace or UBlendSpace1D asset, e.g. '/Game/Animation/BS_Locomotion' (create_blend_space makes one).

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence played at this position, on the blend space's skeleton or one compatible with it, e.g. '/Game/Animation/Run_Fwd'.

params.name: blend_value
params.description: Blend position in the axis units: one number for a 1D blend space, or [x, y] (up to 3 numbers) for a 2D one, e.g. [0, 300]; default 0 on every axis.

commands.returns: { blendspace_path: string, sample_index: int, num_samples: int, added: bool, animation?: string, blend_x?: number, blend_y?: number, blend_z?: number, saved: bool, save_error?: string, message?: string }

commands.name: add_bone
commands.description: Add a bone named bone_name to the reference skeleton of a USkeleton asset under parent_name (omitted or empty: an extra root bone), with local_transform relative to the parent (a zero or missing scale becomes 1), then save the skeleton. Idempotent by name: an existing bone is returned (added false, already_existed true) without checking its parent or saving. An unknown parent is an error, and so is a failed save. Only the skeleton changes: skeletal meshes using it get no new bone, and there is no undo entry. No commit_bone_changes is needed; set_bone_parent and set_bone_transform edit bones, add_virtual_bone adds virtual ones.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Path to the USkeleton asset

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Name for the new bone; when a bone of that name already exists nothing changes (added false)

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Parent bone name, or empty/null for a new root bone

params.name: local_transform
params.description: Optional {location:[x,y,z], rotation:[p,y,r], scale:[x,y,z]}, defaults to identity

commands.returns: { asset_path, bone_name, bone_index, parent_index, bone_count, added, already_existed, saved, op: "add_bone" }

commands.name: add_foot_ik_node
commands.description: Add a Leg IK node (UAnimGraphNode_LegIK) to the top-level AnimGraph of an Animation Blueprint, or reuse the first one already there, bind the feet into its LegsDefinition, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling. Leg 0 gets left_foot_bone and leg 1 right_foot_bone as the FK foot bone; a leg's IK target bone is set to the same bone when it is unset or the leg's foot changes, so the node compiles but has no effect until each IK target names an IK bone (set_anim_graph_node_property on LegsDefinition with the returned node_id); legs beyond the first two and the other leg settings are kept. Bones the target skeleton lacks are an error and nothing is written. The node is left unwired: connect it with connect_anim_graph_pins. Idempotent; refused while PIE runs unless force=true.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset.

params.name: left_foot_bone
params.description: Left foot bone, written as the FK foot bone of leg 0; checked against the target skeleton when the blueprint has one.

params.name: right_foot_bone
params.description: Right foot bone, written as the FK foot bone of leg 1; checked against the target skeleton when the blueprint has one.

A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

Both bones must exist in the skeleton of the rig; the chain name is made unique, so read chain_name back. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

commands.description: Add a new, unconfigured IK solver at the bottom of an existing IK Rig's solver stack through the IK Rig controller (one undo step), then save the asset. Create the rig first with create_ik_rig; then set its bones with set_ik_solver_bones, its settings with set_ik_solver_settings, attach goals (add_ik_goal) with connect_ik_goal_to_solver, reorder with move_ik_solver_in_stack, take one out with remove_ik_solver, and read the stack back with get_ik_rig_info or one solver with get_ik_solver_details. An unknown solver_type, or a rig that does not load, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the solver kept in memory.

Returns slot_count, the slots list and present. Fill it with add_montage_segment; inverse: remove_montage_slot. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

commands.name: add_motion_warping_component
commands.description: Attach a UMotionWarpingComponent named MotionWarping to an editor-world actor given by full object path, internal name or label. add_component_to_actor (component_type MotionWarpingComponent, idempotent=true) does the same for an actor's internal name only; this tool adds the path/label lookup. Idempotent: if the actor already has one, it is returned with already_existed:true and nothing is written. A new one is an instance component (save_level keeps it, and construction-script reruns do not drop it) added in one undo step; the actor's package is marked dirty, not saved. When another object of the actor already holds the name MotionWarping, the new component gets a unique variant, returned in component_name. Add targets with add_motion_warping_target, read them with get_motion_warping_component_info.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full editor path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/Test.Test:PersistentLevel.ActorName"), internal name or label of the actor.

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, component_name: string, component_path: string, already_existed: bool }

commands.name: add_motion_warping_target
commands.description: Add (or update in-place) a FMotionWarpingTarget on an existing UMotionWarpingComponent, including moving or re-aiming an existing target. Exactly one of four payload shapes must be supplied: (1) component_path -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromComponent(name, comp, NAME_None, false, TargetsForwardVector, ZeroVector, ZeroRotator); (2) location + rotation -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromLocationAndRotation; (3) location only -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromLocation (rotation [0,0,0]); (4) rotation only, on a target that already exists -> its Location is kept and only the rotation changes (a missing target is an error). Shapes 2-4 rebuild the target as a plain transform target, so a component-based one loses its Component, BoneName, follow flag and offsets. The engine API is idempotent by WarpTargetName (replace-in-place). Marks the owning level dirty; WarpTargets is Transient, so the targets are not saved with the level.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full editor path or short name of the actor. actor_name (the internal object name) is accepted as an alias.

params.name: target_name
params.description: FName identifier for the warp target. warp_target_name is accepted as an alias.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional world [x, y, z] location for the target.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional world [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation in degrees for the target; alone, it re-aims an existing target and keeps its location.

params.name: component_path
params.description: Optional name of a USceneComponent on the actor to drive the target transform.

commands.name: add_notify_track
commands.description: Add a named notify TRACK to a UAnimSequence (the track itself, not events on it) in an undo transaction and save it. A track of that name already there is a success with already_existed=true and nothing saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence.

params.name: track_name
params.description: Notify track name to add.

params.name: color
