commands.name: add_pose_search_channel_to_schema
commands.description: Add a feature channel (what motion matching compares: Pose, Trajectory, Position, Velocity or Heading) to a Pose Search schema, or, when the schema already has a channel of that class, set that channel's weight instead (already_existed true), then re-finalize the schema and save it. Use it to shape what a database built on the schema matches on; remove one with remove_pose_search_channel_from_schema, read the result with get_pose_search_schema_info, and rebuild the index afterwards with build_pose_search_database_index, which this does not do. Idempotent per channel class: the check looks at every channel the schema has, finalized or not, so a repeat call never adds a duplicate. finalized says whether the schema finalized with the change: when false (schema_cardinality 0, a finalize_warning, usually a channel naming a bone the skeleton lacks) the channel is still added and saved, but the schema cannot be built until that is fixed. An unknown channel_type or a schema that does not load is an error and nothing changes; a failed save answers success false with the change kept in memory.

params.name: schema_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema (required).

params.name: channel_type
params.description: One of 'Pose', 'Trajectory', 'Position', 'Velocity', 'Heading' (required).

params.name: weight
params.description: How much this channel counts against the others when matching, a float >= 0 (default 1.0); omitting it on an existing channel resets that channel's weight to 1.0.

commands.returns: { schema_path, channel_type, channel_class, weight, schema_cardinality, channel_count (finalized), source_channel_count, finalized, finalize_warning?, added, already_existed, weight_updated, saved, save_error?, message }

commands.name: add_pose_to_pose_asset
commands.description: Add a pose copied from the skeleton reference pose to a UPoseAsset under the given name (a pose of that name is replaced) in an undo transaction and save it; refused when the asset has no skeleton. A pose of that name that already holds exactly that reference pose (every bone a track, zero curve values, no source animation GUID) is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the asset is neither modified nor saved. Returns num_poses, num_tracks and already_existed. For poses from animation frames use create_pose_asset_from_anim_sequence. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: pose_asset_path
params.description: Path to the UPoseAsset (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/Pose_Example').

params.name: pose_name
params.description: Name of the pose to add (e.g. 'RefPose_A').

commands.returns: { pose_asset_path, pose_name, num_poses, num_tracks, present, added, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: add_retargeter_op
commands.description: Add a retarget op to the op stack of an IK Retargeter asset through its controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset; op_index and op_name are where and how the engine placed it. Default type: FK Chains op. An unknown op type, or a singleton op type the stack already has, is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_retargeter_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRetargeter asset

params.name: op_type
params.description: Optional op class path (default "/Script/IKRig.IKRetargetFKChainsOp")

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, op_index: int, op_name: string, op_type: string, op_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_rig_element
commands.description: Add a bone, a null (a space: a transform-only element) or an animation control to the hierarchy of a Control Rig Blueprint, under parent_name or at the root, then compile and save the blueprint; there is no undo step and it is refused while PIE runs unless force is set. element_type picks the kind: a bone or null is placed at location/rotation/scale in rig global space; a control (control_type, Float by default) gets a zero or identity value and no limits, its name doubling as its display name, and an unrecognised control_type makes a Float control with control_type_recognized false instead of failing. The engine keeps names unique, so element_key is the name the element really got (a name in use gets a numbered suffix, so each call adds another element), and parent is the parent read back from the hierarchy. A parent the hierarchy does not have is an error and nothing is added; so is a rig that cannot be loaded, and a failed save makes success false with save_error. Set a control up with set_rig_control_value, set_rig_control_limits and set_rig_control_settings; inspect: get_rig_hierarchy; rename or take out: rename_rig_element, remove_rig_element.

params.name: control_rig_path
params.description: Control Rig Blueprint asset path, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Hero"

params.name: element_name
params.description: Name of the new element. bone_name, null_name and control_name are accepted as aliases.

params.name: element_type
params.description: Optional. "bone" (default), "null" ("space" is accepted) or "control", case ignored; defaults to "control" when control_type is given. Any other value is an error.

params.name: control_type
params.description: Optional, controls only: one of "bool", "float", "scalefloat", "integer", "int", "vector2d", "position", "scale", "rotator", "transform", "eulertransform" (default "float"). Given with element_type bone or null it is an error.

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Existing element to parent the new one under; omitted or empty puts it at the root, and a name the hierarchy lacks is an error. A bone is parented under a bone only.

params.name: parent_type
params.description: Optional element type of the parent for a null or control ("Bone"/"Null"/"Control"/etc, case ignored, "Space" means Null); default Bone for a null and Null for a control, and an unknown type falls back to that default. Bones ignore it.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] location in rig global space for a bone or null (default the origin).

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation in rig global space for a bone or null.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] scale for a bone or null (default 1,1,1).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, element_key: string, element_type: string, parent: string, control_type?: string, control_type_recognized?: bool, bone_count: int, null_count: int, control_count: int, curve_count: int, other_count: int, total: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: add_rigvm_link
commands.description: Link an output pin to an input pin in the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint (URigVMController::AddLink with its undo, as the editor links, so a new link is one undo step); a link already into that input pin, into a pin inside it or into the pin it is part of, or out of an execute output pin, is replaced. Pins are NodeName.PinName paths as get_rigvm_graph lists them. A new link is then compiled and saved; a failed link (pins missing, incompatible or already linked) is an error with linked and saved false, the graph is left as it was (links the attempt broke are restored), nothing is compiled or saved, and the package keeps the dirty flag it had; should the graph still differ from before, the error says so and the package stays dirty. Refused during PIE unless force. Add nodes with add_rigvm_node and set unlinked inputs with set_rigvm_pin_default; Blueprint graphs use connect_pins. Inverse: remove_rigvm_link.

params.name: control_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset

params.name: source_pin
params.description: Output pin path NodeA.PinName

params.name: target_pin
params.description: Input pin path NodeB.PinName

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, source_pin: string, target_pin: string, linked: bool, link_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: add_rigvm_node
commands.description: Add a rig-unit node of node_type to the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint loaded by asset path, at position (default 0, 0), then compile and save the rig. Types match case-insensitively (ForwardsSolve means BeginExecution, Setup means PrepareForExecution); any other is an error. node_name is only a request: a taken name gets a unique suffix (the reply has the real one), and every call adds one more node. An event node the graph already has (BeginExecution, PrepareForExecution) is not added twice: when node_name is its name the call succeeds with already_exists=true and saved=false, nothing compiled or saved, otherwise it is an error. A failed save makes success false with save_error, the node kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Next: add_rigvm_link to wire it, set_rigvm_pin_default for inputs, get_rigvm_graph for pin paths; the inverse is remove_rigvm_node.

params.name: control_rig_path
params.description: Asset path of the UControlRigBlueprint, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Mannequin".

params.name: node_type
params.description: BeginExecution, PrepareForExecution, GetTransform, SetTransform, AimBone, or TwoBoneIKSimple

params.name: node_name
params.description: Optional node name to ask for; defaults to the rig-unit struct name, and a name already in the graph gets a unique suffix.

params.name: position
params.description: Optional [x, y] editor graph position

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_name: string, node_title: string, node_type: string, pin_count: int, node_count: int, saved: bool, already_exists: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: add_skeletal_mesh_lod
commands.description: Append one LOD to a skeletal mesh asset found by content path, its LOD info a copy of LOD 0's (build and reduction settings, material map, flags) with ScreenSize.Default set to screen_size, or 0.5 when omitted. Each call appends another LOD (not idempotent), in one undo step; the mesh is marked dirty but not saved, and its render data is not regenerated: bake_skeletal_mesh_lod with regenerate_even_if_imported=true and new_lod_count omitted builds the new LOD (its defaults skip it, as it copies LOD 0's imported flag; note says which applies), then keep it with save_asset. A mesh that does not load is an error. To append reduced LODs in one call, use bake_skeletal_mesh_lod with a higher new_lod_count instead. Tune this LOD with set_skeletal_mesh_lod_reduction_settings or set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings (screen_size); take one out with remove_skeletal_mesh_lod; inspect it with get_skeletal_mesh_lod_info.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero"

params.name: screen_size
params.description: Optional ScreenSize.Default of the new LOD, the screen size at which it switches in (default 0.5); not clamped

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int, lod_count: int, screen_size: float, added: bool, note: string }

commands.name: add_skeletal_mesh_socket
commands.description: Add a socket on a named bone of a skeletal mesh asset (undoable) and save the mesh. A copy also goes to the mesh's skeleton, which is then saved too; when the skeleton already has a socket of that name, the mesh has no skeleton, or the skeleton is engine content or under a read-only root, no copy is made (added_to_skeleton false) and skeleton_note says why. Errors, writing nothing, when the mesh does not load, the mesh already has a socket of that name, or the bone is missing from the mesh or its skeleton. success is false when a changed package fails to save. Edit existing sockets with set_skeletal_mesh_socket_transform or rename_skeletal_mesh_socket; skeleton-only sockets with add_skeleton_socket.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name for the new socket; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed, and a name the mesh already has is an error.

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Name of the bone to attach the socket to; it must exist in the mesh and, when the copy goes to the skeleton, in the skeleton too.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative location

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation

commands.returns: { socket_name: string, bone_name: string, socket_count: int, location_x: float, location_y: float, location_z: float, added_to_skeleton: bool, skeleton_path: string, skeleton_note: string?, saved: bool, save_error: string?, skeleton_saved: bool?, skeleton_save_error: string? }

commands.name: add_skeleton_socket
commands.description: Add a socket to a USkeleton asset on a bone (the root by default) at a bone-relative location and rotation, then save; an existing socket of that name is updated in place (already_existed true). A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. A socket on a skeletal mesh asset (copied to its skeleton when that skeleton is project content): add_skeletal_mesh_socket.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton".

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name of the socket; an existing socket with this name is updated instead of duplicated.

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Bone to attach the socket to; must exist in the skeleton (default the root bone).

params.name: location
params.description: Socket location relative to its bone as [x, y, z] (default 0,0,0)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Socket rotation relative to its bone as [pitch, yaw, roll] (default 0,0,0)

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, socket_name: string, bone_name: string, socket_count: int, added: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: add_virtual_bone
commands.description: Add a virtual bone from source_bone to target_bone to a USkeleton asset loaded by asset path, then save the skeleton; the engine names it "VB <source>_<target>", returned as virtual_bone_name. An omitted source_bone is the first bone of the reference skeleton (usually the root) and an omitted target_bone the first other bone. Bone names are not checked against the skeleton, so a misspelt one is stored as given; the same bone for both, or a skeleton with fewer than 2 bones, is an error. Idempotent: a virtual bone that already joins that exact pair is returned with already_exists=true and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save (PIE running, read-only file) makes success false with save_error, the bone kept in memory. Inverse: remove_virtual_bone; list them: get_skeleton_info (load_full_data=true); a project copy to edit: create_editable_skeleton.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton".

params.name: source_bone
params.description: Bone the virtual bone starts from (default the first bone, usually the root); not validated.

params.name: target_bone
params.description: Bone the virtual bone points to (default the first bone that differs from source_bone); not validated.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, virtual_bone_name: string, source_bone: string, target_bone: string, virtual_bone_count: int, saved: bool, already_exists: bool }

commands.name: assign_skeletal_mesh_physics_asset
commands.description: Assign a physics asset to a skeletal mesh (or pass null/empty to clear it).

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset

params.name: physics_asset_path
params.description: Content path to the physics asset (e.g. /Game/MyPhysAsset); empty string clears the assignment

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, physics_asset_path: string, assigned: bool, cleared: bool, physics_asset_name: string }

commands.name: bake_skeletal_mesh_lod
commands.description: Regenerate the LODs of a skeletal mesh asset (found by content path) with the engine's mesh reduction, driven by each LOD's reduction settings, then rebuild its render data; nothing is saved, so follow with save_asset. A new_lod_count below the current count drops the LODs above it; above it, appends reduced LODs up to that count; 0, omitted or equal re-reduces the LODs that were generated, plus imported LODs above 0 with regenerate_even_if_imported and LOD 0 with generate_base_lod. A mesh that does not load is an error; during PIE, where the engine regenerates nothing, the call is refused before the mesh is touched, and any other run the engine refuses fails with baked=false and bake_warning. Author the settings first with set_skeletal_mesh_lod_reduction_settings; one empty LOD entry: add_skeletal_mesh_lod; one LOD out by index: remove_skeletal_mesh_lod; triangle counts: get_asset_lod_settings.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero"

params.name: new_lod_count
params.description: Target LOD count; fewer than now drops the extra LODs, more appends reduced ones, and <= 0 (the default when omitted) keeps the current count and re-runs reduction

params.name: regenerate_even_if_imported
params.description: bool, also re-reduce imported LODs above 0 when the count is kept (default false)

params.name: generate_base_lod
params.description: bool, re-derive LOD 0 from its reduction settings when the count is kept (default false)

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, old_lod_count: int, new_lod_count: int, lod_count: int, baked: bool, regenerate_even_if_imported: bool, generate_base_lod: bool, bake_warning?: string }

commands.name: build_anim_state_machine
commands.description: Atomic JSON-spec builder for an Animation Blueprint state machine. Builds (or reuses) the state machine, then iterates states, transitions, and per-transition rules in one idempotent call. Replaces 8+ primitive cmds (add_anim_state_machine + add_anim_state + add_anim_transition + set_anim_transition_rule_*) with a single spec. Re-running with the same spec is a no-op (each primitive is internally idempotent: state-by-name, transition-by-source+target). For repeated invocations that change rule shape, the rule is re-applied on the existing transition.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset

params.name: state_machine_name
params.description: Target state machine name (created if missing via add_anim_state_machine)

params.name: spec
params.description: JSON describing the graph shape. states: [{name: str, animation?: str (/Game/Anim/Foo — optional; load-bearing for the runtime state asset but NOT created here), loop?: bool, pos?: [x, y]}]. transitions: [{from: str, to: str, blend?: number (= crossfade_duration seconds), bidirectional?: bool, priority_order?: int, rule?: object}]. Each rule variant maps 1:1 to an existing primitive cmd: {type: "automatic", enabled?: bool = false, trigger_time?: number = 0.0} | {type: "bool", variable: str (must exist on the AnimBP), invert?: bool = false} | {type: "comparison", variable: str (must be float/double on the AnimBP), operator: "=="|"!="|">"|"<"|">="|"<=", comparison_value: number}. An absent rule leaves the transition inert (no rule wired).

params.name: compile_after
params.description: Optional, default false; if true runs compile_anim_blueprint at the end

commands.returns: { success: bool, anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, machine_already_existed: bool, states_created: int, states_skipped: int, transitions_created: int, transitions_updated: int, transitions_skipped: int, errors: [string], compiled: bool, compiled_after: bool }

commands.name: build_pose_search_database_index
commands.description: Start a fresh build of the motion-matching search index of a UPoseSearchDatabase (FAsyncPoseSearchDatabasesManagement::RequestAsyncBuildIndex with NewRequest), cancelling any build already running for it and replacing the old index, and by default wait for it to finish. Run it after add_animation_asset_to_pose_search_database, remove_animation_asset_from_pose_search_database, set_pose_search_database_schema or a schema channel change, none of which rebuild the index; then test it with evaluate_pose_search_query. The index is derived data, not saved into the asset: nothing is saved and there is no undo step. A database that does not load, has no schema (set_pose_search_database_schema), or whose schema still has no finalized channels after a re-finalize in memory is an error before any build. status says what happened: built (success true), in_progress (success true when wait_for_completion is false, since the build was started; a build still running after a wait is a failure), or failed (success false: a database with no animation assets always fails, because the engine fails an empty index, and the message says so; any other failure is in LogPoseSearch). Repeating the call rebuilds again.

params.name: database_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase, e.g. "/Game/Anim/PSD_Locomotion", as create_pose_search_database returns it (required).

params.name: wait_for_completion
params.description: true (default) blocks until the build ends, pumping the engine meanwhile, so large databases take a while; false returns at once, usually with status in_progress (or built when the index was already up to date).

commands.returns: { database_path, schema_path, schema_cardinality, animation_asset_count, wait_for_completion, result: "Success"|"InProgress"|"Failed", status: "built"|"in_progress"|"failed", success, in_progress, failed, message }

Returns was_bound, is_bound and cleared; an unbound pin gives cleared=false, not an error. Undoable; saves the AnimBP without recompiling (run compile_anim_blueprint).

commands.description: Empty the rule of one transition (source_state to target_state) in an Animation Blueprint state machine: every rule-graph node but the result node is deleted, then the blueprint is marked structurally modified and saved without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint). The transition and its settings stay; with nothing wired it is never taken unless its automatic rule is on (set_anim_transition_rule_automatic). Not an undo step. An already empty rule is a success with removed_count 0, nothing saved; a missing blueprint, machine, state or transition is an error. No need to clear first for a new rule: set_anim_transition_rule_from_bool and set_anim_transition_rule_from_comparison rebuild it; remove_anim_transition drops the whole transition. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

Idempotent: a database already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed true and saved false, nothing saved, its schema_path read from it; the requested schema is not applied, and not even loaded. An invalid path, an asset of another class there, or for a new database a schema that does not load, is an error; a failed save of a new database makes success false. Create the schema with create_pose_search_schema; change the schema of an existing database with set_pose_search_database_schema; add animations with add_animation_asset_to_pose_search_database, then run build_pose_search_database_index.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. 'PoseSearchDatabase_Example').

params.name: schema_path
params.description: Asset path of an existing UPoseSearchSchema (required); loaded only for a database this call creates.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path (default /Game/MCP).

commands.returns: { name, package_path, asset_path, database_path, schema_path, schema_cardinality, animation_asset_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: create_pose_search_schema
commands.description: Create a UPoseSearchSchema data asset at package_path/name (package_path defaults to /Game/MCP) bound to the USkeleton at skeleton_path, with sample_rate clamped to 1..240 and the default Trajectory and Pose channels, then save it. The default Pose channel uses the UE mannequin's foot and hand bones, so on a skeleton without them (the default SkeletalCube one included) the schema does not finalize: finalized false, schema_cardinality 0 and a finalize_warning, and build_pose_search_database_index refuses it until that channel goes (remove_pose_search_channel_from_schema) or the skeleton changes. Idempotent: a schema already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed true and saved false, nothing saved, its skeleton_path and skeleton_paths read from it; the requested skeleton and sample_rate are not applied, and that skeleton is not even loaded. An invalid path, an asset of another class there, or for a new schema a skeleton that does not load, is an error; a failed save of a new schema makes success false. Next create a database with create_pose_search_database; add channels with add_pose_search_channel_to_schema, change settings with set_properties, and inspect it with get_pose_search_schema_info.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. 'PoseSearchSchema_Example').

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path (default /Game/MCP); trailing slashes are stripped.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Asset path of the USkeleton (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton); loaded only for a schema this call creates.

params.name: sample_rate
params.description: Schema SampleRate (int, ClampMin=1, ClampMax=240; default 30); out-of-range values are clamped, and it is applied only to a schema this call creates.

commands.returns: { name, package_path, asset_path, schema_path, skeleton_path, skeleton_paths, sample_rate, schema_cardinality, channel_count (finalized), source_channel_count, finalized, finalize_warning?, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: create_retarget_pose
commands.description: Create a new retarget pose for editing in an IK Retargeter through its controller, then save the asset.  The engine makes the name unique, so read pose_name back. The pose is set as the current pose after creation, ready for bone rotation edits via set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_retargeter_path
params.description: Content path to the IK Retargeter asset.

params.name: pose_name
params.description: Name for the new retarget pose

params.name: source_or_target
params.description: Optional "Source" or "Target" scope; defaults to "Target"

commands.returns: { ik_retargeter_path: string, pose_name: string, source_or_target: string, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_skeletal_mesh_morph_target
commands.description: Register a new morph target on a skeletal mesh asset in memory only, for the rest of the editor session: it is never saved (persisted_to_disk is always false), and a mesh rebuild or reload drops any morph the mesh's imported source data does not contain. Each LOD gets one tiny seed delta on vertex 0 so the morph counts as valid; write real deltas with set_morph_target_deltas. Marks the mesh dirty; it is not an undo step. Idempotent: an existing name returns created=false and already_exists=true.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset (e.g. /Game/MyGame/SKM_Example)

params.name: morph_target_name
params.description: Name for the new morph target

commands.returns: { morph_target_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, created: bool, persisted_to_disk: bool, total_morph_targets: int, note: string }

commands.name: disconnect_anim_graph_pins
commands.description: Break AnimGraph pin links: a specific source->target link, or ALL links on the source pin. Use the specific form to insert a node into an existing chain (break A->B, then wire A->N and N->B). Saves the ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint.

params.name: source_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the source node.

params.name: source_pin
params.description: Pin name on the source node.

params.name: target_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the target node (optional; if omitted, breaks ALL links on source_pin).

params.name: target_pin
params.description: Pin name on the target node (optional; required if target_node_id is given).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph).

commands.returns: { disconnected, broke_all, source_node_id, source_pin, saved }

commands.name: disconnect_ik_goal_from_solver
commands.description: Disconnect a goal from a solver, removing that solver's per-goal effector/settings, through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset.  Inverse of connect_ik_goal_to_solver. Idempotent: disconnecting a goal that isn't connected is a success with was_connected:false, saved:false and a note, and nothing is saved. An out-of-range solver_index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: Content path to the IK Rig asset.

params.name: goal_name
params.description: Name of the goal.

params.name: solver_index
params.description: Index of the solver in the rig's solver stack.

commands.returns: { ik_rig_path: string, goal_name: string, solver_index: int, connected: bool, was_connected: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: evaluate_pose_search_query
commands.description: Run a live motion-matching query on a PIE/Game actor against a loaded UPoseSearchDatabase (UPoseSearchLibrary::MotionMatch) and return the best-match asset + search cost, plus the query trajectory. Diagnoses why a chooser returns null. Best-effort: per-channel cost is not exposed by the BlueprintPure result.

params.name: database_path
params.description: UPoseSearchDatabase asset path to search (required).

params.name: world
params.description: Which world to resolve: absent (default) = prefer the live PIE/Game world | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'pie'/'game' force the live session (errors if none running) | 'editor' forces the editor world.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor name or label whose AnimInstance drives the query. Omitted = the first player controller's pawn.

params.name: pose_history_name

params.name: max_trajectory_samples
params.description: Cap on emitted query trajectory samples (<=0 = all; default 0).

commands.returns: { world_mode, actor_name, actor_resolved, anim_instance_class, pose_history_name, pose_history_found, database_path, query_trajectory_samples[], trajectory_sample_count, is_trajectory_empty, has_match, best_match_asset, best_match_database, best_cost, selected_time, is_continuing_pose_search, wanted_play_rate, is_mirrored, is_looping, per_channel_cost[], note, world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode, pie_instance }

commands.name: get_active_montages
commands.description: Report the animation montages active right now on an actor's skeletal mesh in a running Play-in-Editor session (or the world that world selects), without changing anything: the top montage and every montage still blending out, each with its current section, position (seconds and normalized), length, play rate, blend weights, playing and active flags and the slots it plays on. Use it to debug a montage that does not play, cuts off or blends out too early while the game runs; to read a montage asset's sections, slots and notifies use get_montage_info instead. No montage playing gives montage_count 0, not an error. No resolvable world (for the default, PIE not running), an actor not found in that world, a component that is not found, or a mesh without an anim instance is an error. world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode and pie_instance say which world answered.

params.name: actor
params.description: Live actor in the selected world, by object name, editor label or full object path (whole string, case-insensitive), e.g. "BP_Hero_C_0".

params.name: component

params.name: world
params.description: Which world to resolve the actor in: absent/'pie' (default, ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'editor' | 'game' (alias of 'pie').

commands.returns: { actor, actor_name, component, world, anim_instance_class, montage_count, is_any_montage_playing, top_montage_id, enumeration, montages: [{ index, montage_path, montage_name, is_top, current_section, position, normalized_position, length, play_rate, blend_weight, desired_weight, blend_time, is_playing, is_active, instance_id, slots:[string] }], world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_anim_asset_info
commands.description: Load any animation asset and report its class, skeleton and asset_type (montage, composite, pose, sequence, blendspace or animation_asset) plus the counts of that type: sections/slots/notifies, segments, poses/tracks/curves, length, samples. Read-only; get_montage_info, get_anim_sequence_info and get_blend_space_samples give detail.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Path to the animation asset (UAnimMontage, UAnimComposite, UPoseAsset, UAnimSequence, or UBlendSpace)

commands.returns: { asset_path, class, skeleton, num_segments, num_poses, section_count, slot_count, notify_count, sequence_length, rate_scale, num_tracks, num_curves, sample_count, asset_type }

commands.name: get_anim_blueprint_info
commands.description: Read an Animation Blueprint without compiling or changing it: its Asset Registry identity (object path, class, package, is_loaded, and the size and timestamp of its .uasset, left out when no file is on disk), target skeleton and its bone count, parent and generated class, is_anim_instance, is_abstract, is_template, graph_count, and the state machines at the top level of every function graph (the AnimGraph included) with their graph and state counts (conduits not counted; machines nested inside states are not listed). anim_blueprint_path takes an object path, a package path or a short name searched under /Game; no match is an error, and so is a short name several anim blueprints share, with the candidates listed.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Object path, package path or short name of the UAnimBlueprint asset

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, asset_class: string, package_name: string, is_loaded: bool, file_size_bytes: number?, file_size_kb: number?, file_size_mb: number?, last_modified: string?, target_skeleton: string, target_skeleton_set: bool, skeleton_bone_count: int, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_anim_instance: bool, is_abstract: bool, is_template: bool, graph_count: int, state_machine_count: int, state_machines: [{ name: string, graph_name: string, state_count: int }] }

commands.name: get_anim_curve_data
commands.description: Read one curve of a UAnimSequence's data model without changing it: for a float curve its flags, num_keys and every key as a time/value pair; for a transform curve only its flags and num_keys summed over translation, rotation and scale (no key values). A curve that does not exist is still a success with found=false and no num_keys, flags or keys. Get the curve names first from get_anim_sequence_info (it lists the float and transform curves); rekey a float curve with add_anim_float_curve, retime it with scale_anim_curve, change flags with set_anim_curve_flags. For a standalone UCurveFloat asset use evaluate_curve_at_time instead. A path that does not load as a UAnimSequence is an error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence, e.g. '/Game/Anims/A_Walk' or '/Game/Anims/A_Walk.A_Walk'.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Exact curve name as get_anim_sequence_info lists it, e.g. 'FootLock_L'.

params.name: curve_type
params.description: "float" (default) or "transform", case ignored; any other value reads a float curve.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, curve_type, found, num_keys, flags, keys: [{ time, value }] }

commands.name: get_anim_graph_node_properties
commands.description: Read the internal FAnimNode struct of one AnimGraphNode, found by NodeGuid (node_id) in the AnimGraph or a nested graph_name, as typed JSON: the runtime settings (Pose History PoseCount/CollectorName, Slot SlotName, blend params), not the pin surface get_graph_nodes reports. Use it instead of get_properties, which cannot address a graph node by GUID; a non-anim node returns its EditAnywhere properties. Read-only; write with set_anim_graph_node_property.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint.

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the target AnimGraphNode.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph).

commands.returns: { node_id, node_class, node_struct, node_properties:{...} }

commands.name: get_anim_notifies
commands.description: List the notify events of a UAnimSequence without changing it: name, trigger time, duration, track_index and the notify_class or notify_state_class of each, plus num_notifies, and the names of its notify tracks in track order (track_names, track_count). Use get_montage_info for the notifies of a montage.

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence.

commands.returns: { animation_path, num_notifies, notifies: [{ name, time, duration, track_index, notify_class?, notify_state_class? }], track_names: [string], track_count }

commands.name: get_anim_sequence_info
commands.description: Summarise one animation sequence (a UAnimSequence asset) from its data model: the skeleton it plays on, its length, frame rate and frame count, the names of its bone tracks, float curves and transform curves with their counts, how many sync markers it has, whether root motion is enabled, and its retarget source and reference-pose sequence. Read-only: it changes nothing and needs no PIE. A path that does not load as an AnimSequence is refused, a montage or blend space included -- get_anim_asset_info reads any animation asset. The keys of one curve come from get_anim_curve_data and the notify events from get_anim_notifies.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the sequence, e.g. "/Game/Anims/Run_Fwd" (package or object path).

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Alias of anim_sequence_path; read only when anim_sequence_path is absent.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, skeleton, play_length, frame_rate, num_frames, num_bone_tracks, num_float_curves, transform_curve_count, bone_tracks: [string], float_curves: [string], transform_curves: [string], num_sync_markers, enable_root_motion, retarget_source, ref_pose_seq, success }

commands.name: get_anim_state_machine_info
commands.description: Read the nodes of one state machine of an Animation Blueprint without compiling or changing it: state_count counts the states, conduit_count the conduits and transition_count the transitions; states lists every state, conduit and alias node with its kind (class name) and graph position, transitions excluded. It also checks the machine by those counts: no states is an error, one an info, several without transitions a warning (is_valid is false only on an error); compile_anim_blueprint is the check that the machine compiles.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint

params.name: state_machine_name
params.description: Name of a state machine in the top-level AnimGraph, matched without case (get_anim_blueprint_info lists them).

commands.returns: { state_machine, state_count, conduit_count, transition_count, states:[{name,kind,x,y}], is_valid, errors:[string], warnings:[string], info:[string] }

commands.name: get_blend_space_samples

commands.returns: { animation, blend_x, blend_y, blend_z, rate_scale, blendspace_path, num_samples, samples }

commands.name: get_bone_transform

params.description: Bone to read

commands.name: get_ik_bone_settings
commands.description: Get bone-specific settings for a bone within a solver.  FullBodyIK returns snake_case keys (rotation/position stiffness, axis limits Free/Limited/Locked, min/max angles, preferred angles); StretchLimb (the only other solver with per-bone settings) is serialized generically (camelCase: squashDirection vector). Only FullBodyIK and StretchLimb support per-bone settings; others return a `note`.

commands.description: Get goal-specific settings for a goal connected to a solver.  FullBodyIK returns snake_case keys (chain_depth, strength_alpha, pull_chain_alpha, pin_rotation); BodyMover (the only other solver with per-goal settings) is serialized generically (camelCase: influenceMultiplier, boneName). The goal must be connected to the solver first (connect_ik_goal_to_solver), else a `note` explains that. Solvers without per-goal settings return a `note`.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: Content path to the IK Rig asset.

params.name: solver_index
params.description: Index of the solver.

params.name: goal_name
params.description: Name of the goal to query settings for.

commands.returns: { ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, goal_name: string, settings: object }

commands.name: get_ik_retargeter_info
commands.description: Read the global structure of an IK Retargeter via its controller: source/target IK Rigs, the op-stack, per-op chain mappings, and the current poses.  Read-only. commands.name: get_ik_rig_info
commands.description: Read an IK Rig asset: its skeletal mesh, the number of solvers, and every goal and retarget chain, or with chain_name just that retarget chain (start_bone, end_bone and the IK goal it drives) plus whether the rig has it. commands.description: Read one solver of an IK Rig asset by its 0-based stack index: solver_type (the solver struct name, e.g. "IKRigFullBodyIKSolver") and solver_type_canonical (FullBodyIK, Limb, ...), unique_name ("<index+1> - <display name>"), enabled, start and end bone (end_bone "None" for a solver type without one), the names of the goals connected to it, and its solver-specific settings -- FullBodyIK with the curated snake_case keys set_ik_solver_settings takes, every other solver type serialized generically from its live settings struct (camelCase property names). Read-only; an out-of-range solver_index or a rig that does not load is an error. get_ik_rig_info reads the goals and chains of the whole rig.

params.description: Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset

params.name: solver_index
params.description: 0-based solver index

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, solver_index: int, solver_type: string, solver_type_canonical: string, unique_name: string, enabled: bool, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, connected_goal_count: int, connected_goals: [string], settings: object }

commands.name: get_montage_info
commands.description: Read one UAnimMontage asset without changing it: its skeleton, the counts and names of its composite sections, slot tracks and notifies, its blend-in/out times and modes, its auto blend-out settings and its sync group. For a short summary of any animation type use get_anim_asset_info; for the montages playing on a PIE actor use get_active_montages. Change the blend and sync fields with set_properties, sections with add_montage_section / remove_montage_section, slots with add_montage_slot, notifies with add_montage_notify. A path that does not load as a UAnimMontage is an error.

commands.name: get_morph_target_deltas
commands.description: Read back the vertex deltas of a morph target on a specific LOD (inverse of set_morph_target_deltas).

params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset

params.name: morph_target_name
params.description: Name of the morph target to read

params.name: lod_index
params.description: LOD index to read (default 0)

params.name: max_deltas
params.description: Optional cap on how many deltas to return (default 5000); the response is honestly marked truncated if the LOD has more

commands.name: get_motion_warping_component_info
commands.description: Read the UMotionWarpingComponent of an actor without changing anything: whether warp windows are also searched in animations inside montages, every warp target (name, location, rotation, the component it follows or null, bone name, follow flag, location and rotation offsets, and location_offset_direction as the enum's integer), the modifier count, the owner adapter class (None when unset) and the number of switch-off conditions (a protected array read by reflection; -1 if the engine renames it). Warp targets are transient, so on an editor actor they are the ones added this session with add_motion_warping_target. Change a target with set_motion_warping_target, take one out with remove_motion_warping_target, and flip the montage search with set_properties on "<actor>.<component name>" (property bSearchForWindowsInAnimsWithinMontages). An actor that is not found, or one without a UMotionWarpingComponent (add_motion_warping_component adds it), is an error. For a generic component property dump use get_component_properties.

commands.name: get_pose_search_database_info
commands.description: Read a UPoseSearchDatabase without changing it: its schema path, search mode (BruteForce, PCAKDTree, VPTree or EventOnly), KD-tree neighbours, principal components, base cost bias and tags; every animation entry with its index, enabled flag, sampling range (0 to 0 means the whole asset) and asset path; and the schema's channels with class and weight. Use the entry index with remove_animation_asset_from_pose_search_database; for the schema's own settings and finalized channels use get_pose_search_schema_info; to search it at runtime use evaluate_pose_search_query. A database with no schema gives an empty schema_path and no channels rather than an error. schema_cardinality is not recomputed here, so it can read 0 for a schema loaded but not yet finalized (build_pose_search_database_index finalizes it). A path that does not load as a UPoseSearchDatabase is an error.

params.name: database_path
params.description: Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase, e.g. "/Game/Anim/PSD_Locomotion", as create_pose_search_database returns it (required).

commands.returns: { database_path, schema_path, pose_search_mode, kd_tree_query_num_neighbors, number_of_principal_components, base_cost_bias, tags, schema_cardinality, animation_asset_count, animation_assets[], channel_count, channels[] }

commands.name: get_pose_search_runtime_state
commands.description: Read-only report of the live motion-matching state on a PIE/Game actor (why a chooser returns null): its AnimInstance, its MotionTrajectory samples, whether a PoseSearchHistoryCollector node named pose_history_name exists, and (optionally) the target database's schema/channels.

params.name: world
params.description: Which world to resolve: absent (default) = prefer the live PIE/Game world, else the editor world | 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- what a server-driven character lives in) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'pie'/'game' force the live session (errors if none running) | 'editor' forces the editor world.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor name or label to inspect. Omitted = the first player controller's pawn (the locally-controlled character).

params.name: pose_history_name

commands.name: get_retarget_poses
commands.description: List every retarget pose of an IK Retargeter, for the source and the target side, without changing anything: per pose its name, whether it is the side's current pose, its root translation offset and the per-bone rotation deltas it stores (only the bones that were rotated), as quaternions with the same quat_x/quat_y/quat_z/quat_w keys set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation takes. Use it to check a pose before or after set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation; create one with create_retarget_pose, delete one with remove_retarget_pose. For the retargeter's rigs, chains and op stack use get_ik_retargeter_info, for one op's settings get_retargeter_op_info. A path that does not load as a UIKRetargeter is an error.

params.name: ik_retargeter_path

commands.name: get_retargeter_op_info
commands.description: Read one retarget op's live settings struct from an IK Retargeter by op index.  Read-only (no save). The settings keys are the op settings UPROPERTY names with only the first character lower-cased (FJsonObjectConverter convention), e.g. FK Chains op exposes lODThreshold, bEnabled, bDebugDraw, chainDrawSize, bDrawChainLines. op_type is the settings struct name (e.g. IKRetargetFKChainsOpSettings), which differs from get_ik_retargeter_info.ops[].op_type (the op struct name).

commands.name: get_rig_control_value

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, control_name: string, control_type: string, value: any, limit_enabled: bool, min: number?, max: number? }

commands.name: get_rig_hierarchy
commands.description: Read every element of a Control Rig Blueprint hierarchy in traversal order as elements [{name, type}], plus bone_count, null_count, control_count, curve_count, other_count (sockets, connectors and the rest) and total. Read-only: nothing is compiled or saved.

commands.name: get_rigvm_graph
commands.description: Read the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint, loaded by asset path: every node with its name, title, type (the rig-unit struct, or the node class otherwise) and top-level pins, each pin with its name, NodeName.PinName path, direction and is_execute, plus node_count and link_count. Links are only counted, not listed, and the sub-pins of struct pins are not expanded. Read-only: nothing is compiled or saved, and no PIE is needed. A path that is not a Control Rig Blueprint, or one with no default RigVM model, is an error. Use the pin paths with add_rigvm_link and set_rigvm_pin_default; add nodes with add_rigvm_node, take one out with remove_rigvm_node; the bones and controls of the rig: get_rig_hierarchy.
