commands.name: get_skeletal_mesh_info
commands.description: Summarise a skeletal mesh asset in one call: its LOD, material slot, morph target, socket and bone counts, the names of its first 20 bones in reference-skeleton order (bone_names), and each LOD's vertex and section count. Read-only: it changes nothing; a path that does not load as a USkeletalMesh is an error. Start here, then drill into one area: get_skeletal_mesh_lod_info for one LOD's settings, get_skeletal_mesh_section_info for its sections, get_skeletal_mesh_material_slots for slot names, get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets for morph names, and get_skeleton_info with load_full_data for bones past the first 20.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path of the USkeletalMesh asset (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero'.

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, num_lods: int, num_materials: int, num_morph_targets: int, num_sockets: int, num_bones: int, bone_names: [string], lod_info: [{lod_index, num_verts, num_sections}] }

commands.name: get_skeletal_mesh_lod_info
commands.description: Read the settings of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset found by content path: screen size, material map entry count, CPU access, the build settings, the reduction settings and the flat LOD scalars (hysteresis, prioritization weight, morph error tolerance, skin cache usage, mesh deformer). Enums come back by name, e.g. "SMTC_NumOfTriangles" or "Auto", a form the setters accept. Nothing is written. A mesh that does not load, or a lod_index outside its LOD count, is an error. Each block has its setter: set_skeletal_mesh_lod_build_settings, set_skeletal_mesh_lod_reduction_settings, and set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings (screen_size included). Per-LOD vertex counts: get_skeletal_mesh_info; triangle counts: get_asset_lod_settings; sections: get_skeletal_mesh_section_info.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero"

params.name: lod_index
params.description: 0-based LOD index to read (default 0); it must be below the LOD count of the mesh

commands.returns: { lod_index: int, screen_size: float, num_material_map_entries: int, allow_cpu_access: bool, build_settings: {...}, reduction_settings: {...}, lod_hysteresis: float, weight_of_prioritization: float, morph_target_position_error_tolerance: float, skin_cache_usage: string, allow_mesh_deformer: bool }

commands.name: get_skeletal_mesh_material_slots
commands.description: List the material slots of a skeletal mesh asset found by content path, in slot-index order: slot name, assigned material and overlay material as object paths, "(none)" where a slot has none. Nothing is written; a mesh that does not load is an error. Pass a slot_index or slot_name from here to set_skeletal_mesh_material_slot to assign a material; get_skeletal_mesh_section_info gives the material_index each section of a LOD draws with; get_skeletal_mesh_info gives the slot count next to LODs, morph targets, sockets and bones.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero"

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, num_material_slots: int, material_slots: [{slot_index, slot_name, material_path, overlay_material_path}] }

commands.name: get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets
commands.description: List every morph target on a skeletal mesh asset by name, with whether it holds valid data and how many vertex deltas it has on LOD 0; count is the number of morph targets. Read-only: it changes nothing; a mesh that does not load is an error. Use it to find a morph_target_name, then read one morph's per-vertex deltas on any LOD with get_morph_target_deltas or write them with set_morph_target_deltas; create_skeletal_mesh_morph_target, rename_skeletal_mesh_morph_target and remove_skeletal_mesh_morph_target manage the list itself. get_skeletal_mesh_info only counts them.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path of the USkeletalMesh asset (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero'.

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, count: int, morph_targets: [{name, has_valid_data, num_deltas_lod0}] }

commands.name: get_skeletal_mesh_section_info
commands.description: Read the render sections of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset from its imported model: per section its material slot index, triangle and vertex counts, bone map size and the cast-shadow, recompute-tangent, ray-tracing and disabled flags, plus the LOD's total vertex count. Read-only: it changes nothing. A mesh that does not load, or a lod_index outside the mesh's LOD count, is an error. Use it to pick the section_index that set_skeletal_mesh_section_flags writes; for whole-mesh counts use get_skeletal_mesh_info, for one LOD's settings get_skeletal_mesh_lod_info, and for slot names get_skeletal_mesh_material_slots.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path of the USkeletalMesh asset (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero'.

params.name: lod_index
params.description: 0-based LOD index to read (default 0); it must be below num_lods from get_skeletal_mesh_info.

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int, num_sections: int, lod_num_vertices: int, sections: [{section_index, material_index, num_triangles, num_vertices, recompute_tangent, cast_shadow, visible_in_ray_tracing, disabled, bone_map_count}] }

commands.name: get_skeleton_info
commands.description: Find a Skeleton asset in the Asset Registry and report its object path, class path, package, whether it is loaded, the size and timestamp of its .uasset (left out when no file is on disk), and the skeletal meshes bound to it (mesh_count, mesh_paths, shared when more than one), all without loading it; nothing is changed. skeleton_name takes an object path, a package path or a short name searched under /Game; no match is an error, and so is a short name several skeletons share, with the candidates listed. Only with load_full_data true is the asset loaded, adding bone_count, the first 100 bones (name, index, parent_index) with bones_truncated, socket_count, slot_group_count and every virtual bone with its source and target. One bone's reference pose: get_bone_transform; a skeletal mesh: get_skeletal_mesh_info.

params.name: skeleton_name
params.description: Object path, package path, or bare short name of the Skeleton asset (resolved via mcp_common::ResolveAssetFlexible; an ambiguous short name errors out listing every candidate instead of picking one silently)

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Alias of skeleton_name.

params.name: load_full_data
params.description: When true, loads the asset and reports bone list (capped at 100), sockets, slot groups and virtual bones (optional, default false)

commands.returns: { skeleton_name: string, skeleton_path: string, skeleton_class: string, package_name: string, is_loaded: bool, file_size_bytes: number?, file_size_kb: number?, file_size_mb: number?, last_modified: string?, mesh_count: int, shared: bool, mesh_paths: [string], loaded_successfully: bool?, is_valid: bool?, bone_count: number?, bones: [{ name, index, parent_index }]?, bones_truncated: bool?, socket_count: number?, slot_group_count: number?, virtual_bone_count: number?, virtual_bone_names: [string]?, virtual_bones: [{ name, source_bone, target_bone }]?, load_error: string? }

commands.name: link_montage_sections
commands.description: Chain one montage section to the next by setting its NextSectionName.  add_montage_section creates sections but never links them; this writes FCompositeSection::NextSectionName so playback flows section -> next. Pass next_section_name "" or "None" to clear the link. Done in an undo transaction, then saved. Idempotent: the link the section already has is a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

params.name: section_name
params.description: Name of the existing section whose link to set.

params.name: next_section_name
params.description: Name of the existing section to play next (or "" / "None" to clear).

commands.returns: { montage_path, section_name, next_section_name, linked, changed, section_count, sections, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: move_ik_solver_in_stack
commands.description: Move the solver at from_index so that it ends up at to_index (both 0-based positions in the solver stack) of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset. An index outside the stack is an error and nothing moves; from_index equal to to_index is not an error but moved false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset

params.name: from_index
params.description: Source 0-based solver index

params.name: to_index
params.description: Target 0-based solver index, below the solver count

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, from_index: int, to_index: int, moved: bool, solver_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: play_animation
commands.description: Play an AnimMontage on a skeletal mesh component with UAnimInstance::Montage_Play at play_rate, then jump to start_section if playback started. Editor world unless the world param says otherwise; the component needs an anim instance. playing/success mean Montage_Play returned a length above 0.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path to the AnimMontage (e.g. '/Game/Animations/MyMontage.MyMontage')

params.name: play_rate
params.description: Playback rate multiplier (optional, default 1.0)

params.name: start_section
params.description: Name of the section to jump to after play starts (optional)

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie').

commands.returns: { component_name: string, montage_path: string, montage_name: string, playing: bool, play_rate: number, montage_length: number, return_value: number, success: bool, start_section: string?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: refresh_anim_montage_cache
commands.description: Re-run UAnimMontage::RefreshCacheData on a UAnimMontage in an undo transaction (it sorts the notifies, moves a notify off a missing or overlapping notify track, adding tracks as needed, and rebuilds the branching point markers) and save it. Idempotent: when the refresh rewrites none of those fields the reply is a success with refreshed=false and saved=false, the montage keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

commands.returns: { montage_path, refreshed, sequence_length, slot_count, section_count, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: reimport_anim_sequence
commands.description: Reimport a UAnimSequence from a source file you name (source_file_path), or else from its first recorded source, through FReimportManager, fully automated with no dialogs. The class is not checked, so any asset a legacy reimport handler accepts works. The new content lands in memory only and is not saved (save it with save_asset), and it cannot be undone. Use reimport_asset for a plain reimport from the recorded sources, reimport_interchange_asset for an asset imported through Interchange, and get_asset_import_data to see the recorded source first. Before reimporting it checks the one source file it will use: none recorded, or the file missing on disk (the engine would crash on it), is refused with success=false, reimported=false, source_validated=false and a note, and nothing changes; a reimport the handler reports as failed is success=false too. An asset no handler accepts, or a path that does not load, is an error. Every call reimports again.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence, e.g. '/Game/Anims/A_Walk' or '/Game/Anims/A_Walk.A_Walk'.

params.name: source_file_path
params.description: Absolute path on disk of the file to reimport from, e.g. "D:/Art/Walk.fbx"; omit it to use the first source file recorded in the asset's import data (get_asset_import_data shows it).

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, source_file_path, reimported, source_validated, note? }

commands.name: remove_anim_bone_track
commands.description: Remove the animation track of one bone from a UAnimSequence through its data controller (IAnimationDataController::RemoveBoneTrack, one undo step) and save the package. No track with that bone name is a success with removed=false and nothing saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. List tracks with get_anim_sequence_info (bone_tracks).

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Name of the bone track to remove; a name no track has removes nothing.

commands.returns: { sequence_path, bone_name, removed, saved, save_error }

commands.name: remove_anim_composite_segment
commands.description: Remove one segment (an FAnimSegment) by zero-based index from a UAnimComposite's track in one undo step, re-stack the remaining segments end to end, recompute the composite length and save the asset. An index outside [0, num_segments) is an error and nothing changes. The later segments shift down one index, so a repeat with the same index removes a different segment: re-read segments from the reply before the next call. Count the segments with get_anim_asset_info; add_anim_composite_segment is the inverse. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: composite_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimComposite, e.g. '/Game/Animation/AC_Example' (create_anim_composite makes one).

params.name: index
params.description: Zero-based index of the segment to remove, in [0, num_segments), in the order of the segments list that add_anim_composite_segment and this tool return.

commands.returns: { composite_path, index, num_segments, composite_length, segments, success, saved, save_error }

commands.name: remove_anim_conduit
commands.description: Remove a conduit node from a state machine of an Animation Blueprint, together with its rule graph and every transition into or out of it (cascaded_transitions_removed), then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). Not an undo step. Idempotent by name: a conduit that is not there is a success with already_absent=true, and nothing is changed or saved. A name that belongs to a state is an error (use remove_anim_state), and so is a missing blueprint or machine. List the conduits first with get_anim_state_machine_info; add_anim_conduit is the inverse, and remove_anim_transition takes out a single transition instead. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Content path of the UAnimBlueprint (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/ABP_Hero'.

params.name: machine_name
params.description: Name of a state machine on the blueprint's top-level AnimGraph, as get_anim_blueprint_info lists it in state_machines (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Locomotion'.

params.name: conduit_name
params.description: Name of the conduit to remove, as get_anim_state_machine_info lists it (case-insensitive), e.g. 'ToAirborne'.

commands.returns: { anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, conduit_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, conduit_count: int, transition_count: int, cascaded_transitions_removed: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_anim_curve
commands.description: Remove a float or transform curve by name from a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step) and save the package. No such curve is a success with removed=false and nothing saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Any curve_type other than transform targets float curves.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the curve to remove.

params.name: curve_type
params.description: Curve type to target: float (default) or transform

commands.returns: { sequence_path, curve_name, curve_type, removed, saved, save_error }

commands.name: remove_anim_curve_name
commands.description: Unregister a curve name from the curve metadata of a USkeleton asset (USkeleton::RemoveCurveMetaData), in one undo step, then save the skeleton. Inverse of add_anim_curve_name. It removes only the skeleton's registration: keyed curves of that name on animation sequences stay, and those are removed with remove_anim_curve (or renamed with rename_anim_curve). Idempotent: a name that is not registered changes and saves nothing and returns removed false and already_absent true. present is read back after the removal and curve_names lists what remains. A skeleton that does not load is an error; a failed save makes success false, with saved false and save_error.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Asset path of the USkeleton, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton", as get_skeleton_info (skeleton_path) returns it.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: The registered curve name to remove, exact as listed in curve_names, e.g. "Curve_Example".

commands.returns: { asset_path, curve_name, removed, already_absent, present, curve_count, curve_names, saved }

commands.name: remove_anim_notify
commands.description: Remove every notify event whose NotifyName matches notify_name from a UAnimSequence (UAnimationBlueprintLibrary::RemoveAnimationNotifyEventsByName) in an undo transaction and save it. A name no event has is a success with removed=false, already_absent=true and saved=false, and the sequence is neither dirtied nor saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence.

params.name: notify_name
params.description: Name of the notify to remove (matches FAnimNotifyEvent.NotifyName).

commands.returns: { animation_path, notify_name, removed, removed_count, already_absent, saved, save_error }

commands.name: remove_anim_notify_name
commands.description: Unregister a notify name from the AnimationNotifies list of a USkeleton (USkeleton::RemoveAnimationNotify) inside an undo transaction and save the skeleton package. Inverse of add_anim_notify_name. It only drops the name from the skeleton's list: notify events already placed on animations keep their name (remove_anim_notify takes those off). A name that is not registered is a success with removed=false, already_absent=true and saved=false, and the skeleton is neither modified nor saved. Without skeleton_path it edits /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton, as add_anim_notify_name does. The reply re-reads the list (notify_names). A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: notify_name
params.description: The notify name to unregister (e.g. 'Footstep').

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Asset path of the USkeleton to edit (/Game/...); when omitted or empty the engine asset /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton is edited and saved.

commands.returns: { skeleton_path, notify_name, present, removed, already_absent, notify_count, notify_names: [string], saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: remove_anim_slot_group
commands.description: Remove an animation slot group from a skeleton (idempotent; guarded against missing group).

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Path to the USkeleton asset.

params.name: group_name
params.description: Name of the slot group to remove.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, group_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, slot_group_count: int, slot_group_names: [string], saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_anim_state
commands.description: Remove a state node from a state machine of an Animation Blueprint, together with its animation graph and every transition into or out of it (cascaded_transitions_removed), then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). Not an undo step. Idempotent by name: a state that is not there is a success with already_absent=true, and nothing is changed or saved. A name that belongs to a conduit is an error (use remove_anim_conduit), and so is a missing blueprint or machine. List the states first with get_anim_state_machine_info; add_anim_state is the inverse, and remove_anim_transition takes out a single transition instead. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Content path of the UAnimBlueprint (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/ABP_Hero'.

params.name: machine_name
params.description: Name of a state machine on the blueprint's top-level AnimGraph, as get_anim_blueprint_info lists it in state_machines (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Locomotion'.

params.name: state_name
params.description: Name of the state to remove, as get_anim_state_machine_info lists it (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Idle'.

commands.returns: { anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, state_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, state_count: int, transition_count: int, cascaded_transitions_removed: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_anim_sync_marker
commands.description: Remove every authored sync marker with the given name from a UAnimSequence in an undo transaction and save the package. Returns markers_before, markers_after and removed; no marker with that name is a success with removed=false and nothing saved, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: marker_name
params.description: Name of the marker to remove.

commands.returns: { sequence_path, marker_name, markers_before, markers_after, removed, saved, save_error }

commands.name: remove_anim_transition
commands.description: Remove the transition from source_state to target_state in a state machine of an Animation Blueprint, with its rule graph (kept while a bidirectional twin shares it), then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). Only that direction goes; the states stay. Not an undo step. Idempotent: a missing source or target state, or no transition between them, is a success with already_absent=true, and nothing is changed or saved; a missing blueprint or machine is an error. add_anim_transition is the inverse; clear_anim_transition_rule empties the rule but keeps the transition; remove_state_transition is the StateTree counterpart. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Content path of the UAnimBlueprint (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/ABP_Hero'.

params.name: machine_name
params.description: Name of a state machine on the blueprint's top-level AnimGraph, as get_anim_blueprint_info lists it in state_machines (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Locomotion'.

params.name: source_state
params.description: Name of the state or conduit the transition leaves, as get_anim_state_machine_info lists it (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Idle'.

params.name: target_state
params.description: Name of the state or conduit the transition enters (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Run'.

commands.returns: { anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, source_state: string, target_state: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, transition_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_animation_asset_from_pose_search_database
commands.description: Remove one FPoseSearchDatabaseAnimationAsset entry from a UPoseSearchDatabase by 0-based index (inverse of add_animation_asset_to_pose_search_database). Idempotent: an out-of-range index returns removed:false + note, not an error. The database index is NOT rebuilt here -- run build_pose_search_database_index afterwards.

params.name: database_path
params.description: Full /Game/... asset path of the database.

params.name: animation_asset_index
params.description: 0-based index into DatabaseAnimationAssets[].

commands.returns: { database_path, animation_asset_index, removed, previous_count, new_count }

commands.name: remove_blend_profile
commands.description: Remove a WHOLE UBlendProfile from a skeleton (idempotent). Inverse of set_blend_profile_bone, which is what implicitly CREATES a profile -- there is no separate create_blend_profile to undo.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Path to the USkeleton asset

params.name: profile_name
params.description: Name of the UBlendProfile to remove

commands.returns: { asset_path, profile_name, removed, already_absent, profile_count, profile_names, saved }

commands.name: remove_blend_space_sample
commands.description: Remove a blend sample (by index) from a BlendSpace. WARNING: the remaining indices REORDER -- the engine removes with a swap, so the LAST sample lands in the deleted slot. Never remove a batch by descending index and assume the rest held still: the full post-op sample list is returned so the caller can re-sync before the next call. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: blendspace_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UBlendSpace.

params.name: index
params.description: Index of the sample to remove.

commands.returns: { blendspace_path, removed, num_samples, samples, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: remove_bone
commands.description: Remove a bone from the reference skeleton of a USkeleton asset through FReferenceSkeletonModifier, then save the skeleton; no commit_bone_changes is needed afterwards. Without remove_children its child bones are kept and re-parented to the removed bone's parent; with it the whole branch goes. Only the skeleton changes: skeletal meshes, animations and sockets that use the bone are not updated. Inverse: add_bone; to move a bone instead use set_bone_parent; for virtual bones use remove_virtual_bone. Idempotent: a bone that is not there changes and saves nothing and returns removed false and already_absent true. The only root bone of the skeleton (which the engine will not remove) and a virtual bone are refused with success false, removed false and nothing changed; removed true is only answered after the bone is read back as gone, and bones_removed counts the bones that went (children included). A skeleton that does not load is an error; a failed save makes success false, with saved false and save_error. Work on a project copy (create_editable_skeleton), not engine content.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Asset path of the USkeleton, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton", as get_skeleton_info (skeleton_path) or create_editable_skeleton (asset_path) returns it.

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Exact name of the bone to remove, e.g. "twist_01_l".

params.name: remove_children
params.description: true removes every descendant bone too; false (default) keeps the children and re-parents them one level up.

commands.returns: { asset_path, bone_name, removed, already_absent, remove_children, bone_count, bones_removed, saved, op: "remove_bone" }

commands.name: remove_ik_goal
commands.description: Remove an IK goal from an IK Rig by name through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset.  Inverse of add_ik_goal: also detaches the goal from every solver's effector and clears it from any retarget chain that referenced it. Idempotent: removing a goal that isn't present is a success with removed:false, already_absent:true, saved:false and a note, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset

params.name: goal_name
params.description: Name of the goal to remove

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, goal_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, goal_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_ik_retarget_chain
commands.description: Remove the retarget chain with that name from an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset. A name no chain has is not an error but removed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset

params.name: chain_name
params.description: Name of the retarget chain to remove

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, chain_name: string, removed: bool, chain_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_ik_solver
commands.description: Remove the solver at a 0-based index from the solver stack of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset. An out-of-range index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset

params.name: solver_index
params.description: 0-based index of the solver to remove

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, removed_solver_index: int, solver_count: int, removed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_montage_notify
commands.description: Remove the notify event at a zero-based index from the Notifies array of a UAnimMontage and save it; an index past the end changes nothing and still returns success with removed=false. Returns removed_notify_name, notify_count_before, notify_count and the remaining notify names. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

params.name: notify_index
params.description: Zero-based index into the montage's Notifies array. Use get_montage_info first to list notifies.

commands.returns: { montage_path, notify_index, removed_notify_name?, notify_count_before, notify_count, notifies[], removed, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: remove_montage_section
commands.description: Delete the first composite section with that name (FName match, case ignored) from a UAnimMontage and save it; a missing name is a success with removed=false and nothing saved. Links from other sections (NextSectionName) are not updated. Returns removed_index, section_count and the remaining sections. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

params.name: section_name
params.description: Name of the FCompositeSection to remove; compared as an FName, so case is ignored.

commands.returns: { montage_path, section_name, removed_index?, already_existed, removed, section_count, sections[], saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: remove_montage_segment
commands.description: Remove the segment at segment_index from a slot track of a UAnimMontage, in one undo step, recompute the montage length and save the montage. Inverse of add_montage_segment; the segments after it move down one index, and the gap it leaves on the track stays until collapse_montage_segments closes it. A montage that does not load, a slot it does not have, or an index out of range is an error and nothing changes. The reply re-reads the slot (segment_count, montage_length). A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Read the montage: get_montage_info.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimMontage (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/AM_Example").

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Montage slot name (e.g. DefaultSlot).

params.name: segment_index
params.description: Zero-based index of the segment in that slot's track.

commands.returns: { montage_path, slot_name, segment_index, removed_anim_sequence_path, removed, segment_count, montage_length, success, saved, save_error }

commands.name: remove_montage_slot
commands.description: Remove one slot animation track (the FSlotAnimationTrack and every segment on it) from a UAnimMontage, picked by slot_name or slot_index, in one undo step, and save the montage. List the slots first with get_montage_info; add_montage_slot is the inverse, and remove_montage_segment takes out a single segment instead of the whole track. A slot that is not there is a success with removed=false and already_existed=false, and nothing is changed or saved, so a repeat by slot_name is safe; a repeat by slot_index takes out whichever track moved into that index. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimMontage, e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'.

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Slot name of the track to remove, as get_montage_info lists it, e.g. 'DefaultSlot'; the first track with that name goes. Wins over slot_index when both are given; one of the two is required.

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Zero-based index into the montage's slot tracks, in get_montage_info order (used only without slot_name); an index past the last track is a no-op success with removed=false.

commands.returns: { montage_path, slot_name?, slot_index?, removed_index?, removed_slot_name?, slot_count, slots[], already_existed, removed, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: remove_motion_warping_component
commands.description: Destroy the UMotionWarpingComponent of an actor (the first one found), with all its warp targets; the inverse of add_motion_warping_component. The actor is recorded in the call's undo step (Actor->Modify) and its level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level persists it). Only an instance component stays gone: one that the actor's Blueprint or C++ class defines comes back (when its construction script reruns, or on reload), so remove that one from the class instead. To clear targets but keep the component use remove_motion_warping_target (all=true); check the result with get_motion_warping_component_info. Idempotent: an actor without one returns already_existed=false, removed=false and a note, not an error. An actor that is not found is an error and nothing changes.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Actor as a full object path ('/Game/Maps/Arena.Arena:PersistentLevel.BP_Hero_C_1'), or the internal name or label of an editor-world actor ('BP_Hero_C_1', 'Hero').

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, component_path?: string, removed: bool, already_existed: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_motion_warping_target
commands.description: Remove a FMotionWarpingTarget from a UMotionWarpingComponent by FName, or with all=true every warp target at once. Wraps UMotionWarpingComponent::RemoveWarpTarget(name) (0 or 1 removed; the array is keyed by FName), looped over a snapshot of the names for all=true. Idempotent: removing a non-existent target, or clearing an empty component, returns removed_count 0 without raising an error. Pass target_name or all=true, not both.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full editor path or short name of the actor. actor_name (the internal object name) is accepted as an alias.

params.name: target_name
params.description: FName identifier of the warp target to remove. Required unless all is true.

params.name: all
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When true, remove every warp target of the component; target_name must then be omitted.

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, target_name?: string, all: bool, removed_count: int, removed_names: [string], previous_count: int, warp_target_count: int, cleared: bool }

commands.name: remove_notify_track
commands.description: Remove one named notify track from a UAnimSequence in one undo step and save it: the notify events and sync markers on that track go with it and the tracks after it shift down one index. Idempotent by name: a track that is not there is a success with already_absent=true, and nothing is changed or saved. Removing the sequence's last remaining track is refused with an error and nothing changes. List the track names with get_anim_notifies; add_notify_track is the inverse, and remove_anim_notify takes out a single event instead of a whole track. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence, e.g. '/Game/Animation/Run_Fwd'.

params.name: track_name
params.description: Name of the notify track, as get_anim_notifies lists it in track_names (matched case-insensitively), e.g. '1' or 'Footsteps'.

commands.returns: { animation_path, track_name, track_names, track_count, already_absent, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: remove_pose_curve
commands.description: Delete one named curve, with its value in every pose, from a UPoseAsset (UPoseAsset::DeleteCurves) in one undo step and save the asset. To delete a whole pose use remove_pose_from_pose_asset instead; for a curve on a UAnimSequence use remove_anim_curve, and to unregister a curve name from a skeleton remove_anim_curve_name. No tool adds a pose curve back, so only undo restores it. Idempotent in effect: an absent curve is a success with removed=false, removed_count 0 and saved=false, and the asset is neither modified nor saved. get_anim_asset_info reports the pose asset's curve count. A path that does not load as a UPoseAsset is an error. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: pose_asset_path
params.description: Object path of the UPoseAsset, e.g. '/Game/Anims/PA_Face' or '/Game/Anims/PA_Face.PA_Face'.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Exact curve name, matched as an FName (case ignored), e.g. 'Blink_L'.

commands.returns: { pose_asset_path, curve_name, removed_count, removed, num_curves, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: remove_pose_from_pose_asset
commands.description: Delete the named pose from a UPoseAsset (UPoseAsset::DeletePoses, which also fixes the base pose index) in an undo transaction and save the asset. An absent name is a success with removed=false and saved=false, and the asset is neither modified nor saved. Returns was_present, removed_count, contains_after, num_poses and the remaining pose_names. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: pose_asset_path
params.description: Path to the UPoseAsset (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/Pose_Example').

params.name: pose_name
params.description: Name of the pose to remove.

commands.returns: { pose_asset_path, pose_name, was_present, removed_count, removed, contains_after, num_poses, pose_names, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: remove_pose_search_channel_from_schema
commands.description: Remove one feature channel (a UPoseSearchFeatureChannel_* such as Pose or Trajectory) from a motion-matching UPoseSearchSchema, chosen by index or by type, in one undo step; the schema is then re-finalized (PostEditChange) and saved. The inverse of add_pose_search_channel_to_schema; to only lower a channel's influence, set its weight with that tool instead. List the channels first with get_pose_search_schema_info, and rebuild every database that uses the schema with build_pose_search_database_index afterwards, since the old index no longer matches. An index out of range or no channel of that type is a success with removed=false, already_absent=true and nothing saved. Not idempotent: indices shift after a removal, and by type each call takes the next channel of that class. Passing neither selector, an unknown channel_type, or a schema that does not load is an error. previous_count counts the schema's source channels, while channel_count counts the finalized ones, which can be 0 when finalizing fails. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: schema_path
params.description: UPoseSearchSchema asset as a package or object path, e.g. "/Game/MotionMatching/PSS_Locomotion" (required).

params.name: channel_index
params.description: 0-based index into the schema's source channel list (the order of get_pose_search_schema_info's finalized_channels once the schema is finalized; that tool lists none before); takes precedence over channel_type when both are given.

params.name: channel_type
params.description: "Pose", "Trajectory", "Position", "Velocity" or "Heading", case ignored; removes the first channel of that class, subclasses included. Used only when channel_index is absent.

commands.returns: { schema_path, channel_index, channel_type, channel_class, schema_cardinality, channel_count, previous_count, removed, already_absent, saved, save_error?, message }

commands.name: remove_pose_search_roled_skeleton
commands.description: Remove one roled skeleton entry (FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton: a role name bound to a USkeleton and optional mirror table) from a UPoseSearchSchema, chosen by role or by index, in one undo step; the schema is then re-finalized (PostEditChange), which can change its finalized channels, and saved. Use it to drop a character from a multi-character schema; it is the inverse of set_pose_search_schema_skeleton with a new role. To swap the skeleton of a role use set_pose_search_schema_skeleton, to rename a role set_pose_search_schema_role, and list the entries with get_pose_search_schema_info. Idempotent by role: no matching entry (or an index out of range) is a success with removed=false, already_absent=true, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written; by index a repeat removes the next entry, since indices shift. Passing both or neither selector, or a schema that does not load, is an error. Rebuild databases on the schema with build_pose_search_database_index afterwards. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: UPoseSearchSchema asset as a package or object path, e.g. "/Game/MotionMatching/PSS_Interaction" (required).

params.name: role
params.description: Role name of the entry to remove, compared as an FName (case ignored), e.g. "Defender"; an empty string means the default (None) role. Give this OR skeleton_index.

params.name: skeleton_index
params.description: 0-based index of the entry in the schema's roled-skeleton list, in get_pose_search_schema_info order. Give this OR role.

commands.returns: { asset_path, role, skeleton_index, removed_skeleton_path, roled_skeleton_count, previous_count, removed, already_absent, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: remove_retarget_pose
commands.description: Remove a retarget pose from an IK Retargeter by name through its controller, then save the asset.  Inverse of create_retarget_pose. If the removed pose was the current one, the retargeter falls back to the default pose. Idempotent: removing a pose that isn't present is a success with removed:false, already_absent:true, saved:false and a note, and nothing is saved. The engine's built-in default pose cannot be removed (honest error). A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_retargeter_path

params.name: pose_name
params.description: Name of the retarget pose to remove

params.name: source_or_target
params.description: Optional "Source" or "Target" scope; defaults to "Target"

commands.returns: { ik_retargeter_path: string, pose_name: string, source_or_target: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_retargeter_op
commands.description: Remove the op at a 0-based index, with any child ops, from the op stack of an IK Retargeter asset through its controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset. An out-of-range index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_retargeter_path
params.description: Path to the UIKRetargeter asset

params.name: op_index
params.description: 0-based op index

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, removed_op_index: int, removed: bool, op_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_rig_element
commands.description: Remove one element (by name and type) from a Control Rig Blueprint hierarchy with RemoveElement, then compile and save the blueprint. Errors on an unknown type or a missing element. Returns the per-type counts afterwards; refused while PIE runs unless force is set.

params.name: control_rig_path

params.name: element_name
params.description: Name of the element to remove

params.name: element_type
params.description: Element type, any case: "Bone", "Null" (or "Space"), "Control", "Curve", "Socket" or "Connector"

commands.name: remove_rigvm_link
commands.description: Break links into an input pin in the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint (URigVMController::BreakLink / BreakAllLinks with their undo, one undo step), then compile and save the rig. Inverse of add_rigvm_link: with source_pin only the link from that output pin goes; without it every link into target_pin goes. Pins are NodeName.PinName paths as get_rigvm_graph lists them. A pin that does not exist is an error; a pin with no such link is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing compiled or saved). The reply re-reads the pin (links_left) and the graph's link_count. Refused during PIE unless force. The whole node: remove_rigvm_node.
