commands.returns: { asset_path: string, target_pin: string, source_pin?: string, removed: bool, links_removed: int, links_left: int, link_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: remove_rigvm_node
commands.description: Remove a node from a Control Rig's RigVM solver graph, then compile and save the rig. A node that is not found, or that the controller fails to remove, is an error and nothing is compiled or saved.

params.name: control_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset

params.name: node_name
params.description: Graph node name to remove, as reported by add_rigvm_node

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_name: string, removed: bool, node_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: remove_skeletal_mesh_lod
commands.description: Remove one LOD from a skeletal mesh asset, with its source model and cached reduction data; higher LODs shift down one index. lod_index must be 1 or more and below the LOD count, otherwise an error (LOD 0 is never removed). Marks the mesh dirty without saving or rebuilding render data, so follow with save_asset. Use add_skeletal_mesh_lod to append a LOD, get_skeletal_mesh_lod_info to inspect them, set_skeletal_mesh_min_lod to skip the most detailed LODs while keeping them.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Index of the LOD to remove (must be > 0)

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int, lod_count: int, removed: bool }

commands.name: remove_skeletal_mesh_morph_target
commands.description: Delete one morph target, by name, from a skeletal mesh asset found by content path, including its data in every LOD's source mesh, in one undo step, then save the mesh. Not idempotent: a name the mesh does not have is an error, so a repeat call fails instead of reporting it already gone. A mesh that does not load is an error, and so is a failed save (refused during PIE or under a read-only root, or a locked file), although the deletion stays in memory. remaining_morph_targets counts the morphs left. List names with get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets; rename with rename_skeletal_mesh_morph_target; add one with create_skeletal_mesh_morph_target.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero"

params.name: morph_target_name
params.description: Name of the morph target to delete, as get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets lists it

commands.returns: { morph_target_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, removed: bool, remaining_morph_targets: int }

commands.name: remove_skeletal_mesh_socket
commands.description: Deletes a socket from a skeletal mesh asset, together with the same-named socket on its skeleton and the preview assets attached to that socket name. One undo step, then the mesh package is saved, and a failed save is an error. The skeleton is only changed in memory and left unsaved (save_asset writes it), so a socket that exists only on the skeleton is deleted there but not on disk. Idempotent: a name neither the mesh nor its skeleton has returns already_removed true, with nothing changed or saved. A socket that should go from a Skeleton asset alone is better deleted with remove_skeleton_socket, which saves it; static meshes use remove_static_mesh_socket. Re-add with add_skeletal_mesh_socket; get_skeletal_mesh_info reports the socket count.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Package or object path of the skeletal mesh asset (e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero").

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name of the socket to delete, matched case-insensitively (e.g. "hand_r_socket").

commands.returns: { socket_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, removed: bool, already_removed: bool, socket_count: int }

commands.name: remove_skeleton_socket
commands.description: Remove a socket from the socket list of a USkeleton asset and save it. Idempotent: a missing socket returns removed false and already_absent true without saving. Returns socket_count and the remaining socket_names; sockets that exist only on a skeletal mesh are untouched (use remove_skeletal_mesh_socket).

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton".

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name of the socket to remove (case-insensitive).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, socket_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, socket_count: int, socket_names: [string], saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_virtual_bone
commands.description: Remove a virtual bone from a USkeleton asset, named directly or found by its source and target bones, then save. Idempotent: no match returns removed false and already_absent true without saving. Returns the remaining virtual_bone_names; a failed save returns success false.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton".

params.name: virtual_bone_name
params.description: Full virtual bone name with its "VB " prefix, e.g. "VB pelvis_hand_r"; when given, source_bone and target_bone are ignored.

params.name: source_bone
params.description: Source bone name; used with target_bone to resolve the virtual bone when virtual_bone_name is omitted.

params.name: target_bone
params.description: Target bone name; used with source_bone to resolve the virtual bone when virtual_bone_name is omitted.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, virtual_bone_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, virtual_bone_count: int, virtual_bone_names: [string], saved: bool }

commands.name: rename_anim_curve
commands.description: Rename a float or transform curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step) and save it; errors when the source curve does not exist or the rename is refused. The same name for both is a success with renamed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. Any curve_type other than transform means float. Returns renamed and saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence

params.name: old_curve_name
params.description: Name of the existing curve to rename, as listed by get_anim_sequence_info (float_curves, transform_curves).

params.name: new_curve_name
params.description: Name the curve gets after the rename.

params.name: curve_type
params.description: Curve type to target: float (default) or transform

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, old_curve_name, new_curve_name, renamed, saved, save_error, note? }

commands.name: rename_bone
commands.description: Rename a bone in the reference skeleton of a USkeleton asset and save it. Fails with an error when old_name is not a bone or new_name is already taken; skeletal meshes and animations that use the old name are not updated. A failed save returns success false.

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton".

params.name: old_name
params.description: Current bone name; must exist in the reference skeleton.

params.name: new_name
params.description: Desired new bone name (must not already exist)

commands.returns: { asset_path, old_name, new_name, renamed: true, not_found: false, already_used: false, bone_count, saved, save_error?, op: "rename_bone" }

commands.name: rename_ik_retarget_chain
commands.description: Rename a retarget chain of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction) and save it. The engine makes the new name unique, so read new_name back; an unknown chain_name is not an error but returns renamed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: ik_rig_path
params.description: IK Rig (UIKRigDefinition) asset path, e.g. "/Game/Retarget/IK_Hero".

params.name: chain_name
params.description: Current name of the retarget chain, as get_ik_rig_info lists it.

params.name: new_name
params.description: Requested new name; the engine may add a suffix to keep it unique.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, old_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: rename_montage_section
commands.description: Rename an existing FCompositeSection on a UAnimMontage by zero-based section_index, in an undo transaction, and save it. The name the section already has (FName match, case ignored) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

params.name: section_index
params.description: Zero-based index into CompositeSections (use get_montage_info first to list).

params.name: new_name
params.description: New FName for the section.

commands.returns: { montage_path, section_index, old_name, new_name, section_count, sections, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: rename_pose_in_pose_asset
commands.description: Rename an existing named pose in a UPoseAsset (UPoseAsset::ModifyPoseName) in an undo transaction and save it; renamed is measured by reading the pose names back. An unknown old_pose_name, a new_pose_name another pose already has, or a rename the engine does not take is an error with nothing saved; the same name for both is a success with renamed=false and saved=false, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: pose_asset_path
params.description: Path to the UPoseAsset.

params.name: old_pose_name
params.description: Current name of the pose to rename.

params.name: new_pose_name
params.description: New name for the pose.

commands.returns: { pose_asset_path, old_pose_name, new_pose_name, renamed, contains_new, contains_old, num_poses, pose_names, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: rename_rig_element
commands.description: Rename one element -- a bone, null, control, curve, socket or connector -- in the hierarchy of a Control Rig Blueprint, then compile and save the blueprint; there is no undo step and it is refused while Play-in-Editor runs unless force is set. Read current names and types with get_rig_hierarchy; add_rig_element and remove_rig_element add and take away elements; a bone of a USkeleton asset is rename_bone instead. The engine never fails on a name already in use: it appends a numeric suffix, so element_key is the name the element really got and name_adjusted says when it differs from new_name. Idempotent: renaming to the current name is a no-op that compiles and saves nothing ({ renamed:false, already_named:true }). An unknown element_type, or an element of that type the hierarchy does not have, is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false with save_error.

params.name: control_rig_path
params.description: Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Mannequin"; create_control_rig_blueprint makes one

params.name: element_type
params.description: Element type ("Bone"/"Null"/"Control"/"Curve"/"Socket"/"Connector"), case-insensitive; "Space" also means Null

params.name: element_name
params.description: Current name of the element to rename, as get_rig_hierarchy lists it (case-insensitive)

params.name: new_name
params.description: Desired new name for the element, e.g. "spine_01_ctrl"; a name in use gets a numeric suffix

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, old_name: string, element_key: string, element_type: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, name_adjusted: bool, bone_count: int, null_count: int, control_count: int, curve_count: int, other_count: int, total: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: rename_skeletal_mesh_morph_target
commands.description: Rename a morph target on a skeletal mesh asset and save the mesh. Fails if old_name is not a morph target of the mesh or new_name already exists; a failed save also returns an error although the rename stays in memory. Returns old_name, new_name and renamed.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Skeletal mesh asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero".

params.name: old_name
params.description: Current morph target name, as get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets lists it.

params.name: new_name
params.description: New morph target name; must not already exist on the mesh.

commands.returns: { old_name: string, new_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, renamed: bool }

commands.name: rename_skeletal_mesh_socket
commands.description: Renames a socket of a skeletal mesh asset; a socket of the same name on the mesh's skeleton is renamed too. One undo step, then the mesh package is saved, and a failed save is an error (the rename stays in memory). The skeleton is only changed in memory and left unsaved (save_asset writes it), so a socket that exists only on the skeleton is renamed there but not written to disk. Refused with nothing changed when new_name equals old_name, a socket called new_name already exists on the mesh or its skeleton, or old_name is not found, so a repeat call fails because old_name is gone. Add a socket with add_skeletal_mesh_socket, re-parent one with set_skeletal_mesh_socket_parent, delete one with remove_skeletal_mesh_socket; Skeleton assets: add_skeleton_socket and remove_skeleton_socket; static meshes: rename_static_mesh_socket.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Package or object path of the skeletal mesh asset (e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero").

params.name: old_name
params.description: Current socket name, matched case-insensitively (e.g. "hand_r_socket").

params.name: new_name
params.description: New socket name; must differ from old_name and be free on the mesh and its skeleton (a change of letter case only counts as taken).

commands.returns: { old_name: string, new_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, renamed: bool, already_renamed: bool, socket_count: int } -- already_renamed is always false (a repeat call is an error instead); socket_count adds the mesh's sockets and its skeleton's

commands.name: scale_anim_curve
commands.description: Retime a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package: every key TIME becomes (t - origin) * factor + origin, and the key VALUES are left untouched -- this stretches/compresses a curve in time, it does not scale its amplitude. FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. A retime that moves no key (factor 1, no keys, or every key at the origin) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the float curve.

params.name: factor
params.description: Scale factor applied to each key TIME (default 1.0).

params.name: origin
params.description: Time origin the key times are scaled about (default 0.0).

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, origin, factor, num_keys, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_additive_settings
commands.description: Set the additive-animation type and base pose on a UAnimSequence in an undo transaction and save it. Settings the sequence already has are a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: additive_anim_type
params.description: Additive type: LocalSpaceBase|RotationOffsetMeshSpace|None (default LocalSpaceBase)

params.name: ref_pose_type
params.description: Base pose type: RefPose|AnimScaled|AnimFrame|LocalAnimFrame|None (default RefPose)

params.name: ref_frame_index
params.description: Frame index used for the base pose (default 0)

params.name: ref_pose_anim_path
params.description: Object path of the reference UAnimSequence for the base pose (optional)

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, additive_anim_type, ref_pose_type, ref_frame_index, ref_pose_anim_set, changed, success, saved, save_error, message? }

commands.name: set_anim_bone_track_keys
commands.description: Replace the keys of one bone track of a UAnimSequence with the given per-key transforms (translation, rotation, scale), or, without keys, with num_keys identity keys (zero translation, identity rotation, unit scale), adding the track when it is missing, through its data controller as one undo step, then save the package; num_keys_readback and first_key are read back from the data model. A track that already holds exactly these keys (the stored track data comes out unchanged, measured with the data model GUID; the engine stores a constant track as one value, whatever num_keys is) is a success with changed=false and saved=false, the package keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A bone_name the sequence's skeleton does not have is an error and nothing is written; an omitted bone_name targets the root bone. keys and num_keys together, an empty keys array or a num_keys below 1 are refused. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Name of a bone of the skeleton of the sequence; omitted or empty means the root bone.

params.name: keys
params.description: Optional array of per-key transforms: { translation:[x,y,z], rotation:[pitch,yaw,roll] (deg), scale:[x,y,z] }. translation default [0,0,0], rotation default [0,0,0], scale default [1,1,1]. Omitted: num_keys identity keys are written.

params.name: num_keys
params.description: Optional number of identity keys to write when keys is omitted, rounded, >= 1 (default 2); not checked against the frame count of the sequence.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, bone_name, num_keys, num_keys_readback, num_bone_tracks, first_key:{translation,rotation_euler}, identity_keys, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_curve_color
commands.description: Set the editor display color of a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package (cosmetic: it tints the curve in the editor, it does not affect evaluation). FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written; so is a color that is not 3 or 4 numbers. The color the curve already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Create the curve with add_anim_float_curve; its comment: set_anim_curve_comment.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the float curve.

params.name: color
params.description: Color as [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], usually 0..1 (numbers within the float range); a is 1 when omitted, and an omitted color is white [1,1,1,1]. Any other value is an error.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, color, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_curve_comment
commands.description: Set the author comment of a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package (metadata only; it does not affect evaluation). FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. The comment the curve already has (case-sensitive) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the float curve.

params.name: comment
params.description: Comment string to set (default empty).

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, comment, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_curve_flags
commands.description: Replace the curve flags (the EAnimAssetCurveFlags bitmask) of an existing float or transform curve on a UAnimSequence with one flag, in an undo transaction, then save the package. Despite the name it changes no key interpolation or tangents: linear and editable both set Editable; metadata, drive_track and disabled set those flags. interp_mode is required; an unknown mode, curve or sequence is an error, and any curve_type other than transform means float. old_flags and new_flags are the bitmasks before and after; flags the curve already has are a success with applied=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_anim_curve_data reads the flags.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence

params.name: curve_name
params.description: Name of the curve

params.name: interp_mode
params.description: One of "linear|editable|metadata|drive_track|disabled"

params.name: curve_type
params.description: Curve type to target: float (default) or transform

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, curve_name, interp_mode, old_flags, new_flags, applied, saved, save_error, note? }

commands.name: set_anim_frame_rate
commands.description: Set the frame rate of the data model of a UAnimSequence (IAnimationDataController::SetFrameRate, one undo step) to fps rounded to whole frames per second, then save the package; fps, numerator and denominator are read back from the data model. The data controller only takes a rate that is a multiple or a factor of the current one, and the frame count must stay whole at the new rate: any other rate is an error and nothing changes. The rate the data model already has is a success with changed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_anim_sequence_info reads the rate.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: fps
params.description: New frame rate in frames per second, rounded to a whole number that must be at least 1.

commands.returns: { sequence_path, fps, numerator, denominator, changed, saved, save_error, note? }

commands.name: set_anim_graph_node_pin_binding
commands.description: Bind an AnimGraph node input pin to a variable or property path in the node property-binding map (the Details-panel bind chip), e.g. "TransformTrajectory" to "Trajectory"; set_anim_graph_node_property edits the FAnimNode struct instead. Returns applied and the stored binding; saves the AnimBP without recompiling (run compile_anim_blueprint).

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the target UAnimGraphNode_* (from get_graph_nodes).

params.name: pin_name
params.description: The bound property/pin name (e.g. "TransformTrajectory").

params.name: binding_path
params.description: The variable/property path to bind the pin to (e.g. "Trajectory", or nested "MyStruct.Member"). This tool does not check that the path resolves.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path or name of the UAnimBlueprint (aliases: anim_blueprint, blueprint_name).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph (optional; deep-resolved; default the top-level AnimGraph).

params.name: anim_blueprint
params.description: Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path is absent or empty.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path and anim_blueprint are both absent or empty.

commands.returns: { node_id, pin_name, binding_path, applied, binding:{property_name, property_path[], path_as_text, is_bound, is_promotion, binding_type, pin_category}, saved }

commands.name: set_anim_graph_node_property
commands.description: Write one field of an AnimGraphNode's internal FAnimNode struct (runtime settings, not pins): node by NodeGuid, field by name or dotted path. set_properties cannot address a graph node by GUID; this also takes a dotted path, rebuilds the node's pins, is undoable and saves the ABP, but does NOT recompile -- run compile_anim_blueprint. Read: get_anim_graph_node_properties.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint.

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the target AnimGraphNode.

params.name: property
params.description: Property path inside the FAnimNode (e.g. "PoseCount", "SlotName"). A leading "Node." is tolerated. Nested structs use dots ("A.B").

params.name: value
params.description: Text value (UE ImportText form: number, "EnumName", "(X=1,Y=2)"...). Use for scalars/enums/simple structs.

params.name: value_json
params.description: JSON value applied via JsonValueToUProperty. Use for complex/nested types. Takes precedence over value.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph).

commands.returns: { node_id, property, applied, new_value, saved }

commands.name: set_anim_montage_preview_mesh
commands.description: Set the editor preview USkeletalMesh of a UAnimMontage (SetPreviewMesh, one undo step) and save the montage; it only changes what the asset editor shows, and the mesh skeleton is not checked against the montage. Returns mesh_path, prev_mesh_path and applied; the preview mesh the montage already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

params.name: mesh_path
params.description: Asset path of the preview USkeletalMesh (e.g. '/Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube').

commands.returns: { montage_path, mesh_path, prev_mesh_path, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_montage_skeleton
commands.description: Rebind a UAnimMontage to a different USkeleton (clears existing source link + recomputes bone caches) in an undo transaction and save it. The skeleton the montage already uses is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

params.name: skeleton_path
params.description: Asset path of the new Skeleton (e.g. '/Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton').

commands.returns: { montage_path, skeleton_path, prev_skeleton_path, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_notify
commands.description: Edit an existing FAnimNotifyEvent on a UAnimSequence (identified by name + occurrence) in an undo transaction and save it. No editable field is an error before anything changes; edits that leave the event as it is are a success with applied=false, applied_count 0 and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: animation_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UAnimSequence.

params.name: notify_name
params.description: NotifyName of the event to edit (FName). Names are not unique; see occurrence_index.

params.name: occurrence_index
params.description: Zero-based index AMONG events sharing notify_name (default 0)

params.name: time
params.description: New trigger time in seconds (FAnimNotifyEvent::SetTime). Optional.

params.name: duration
params.description: New duration in seconds (FAnimNotifyEvent::SetDuration; meaningful for notify-state). Optional.

params.name: trigger_chance
params.description: New NotifyTriggerChance in [0,1]. Optional.

params.name: trigger_weight_threshold
params.description: New TriggerWeightThreshold. Optional.

params.name: montage_tick_type
params.description: New MontageTickType: 'Queued' or 'BranchingPoint'. Optional.

params.name: track_index
params.description: New TrackIndex (zero-based). Optional.

commands.returns: { animation_path, notify_name, occurrence_index, matched_count, notify, applied_count, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_number_of_frames
commands.description: Set the number of frames of the data model of a UAnimSequence (IAnimationDataController::SetNumberOfFrames, one undo step), then save the package; frame_count is read back from the data model. When the data model rate differs from the sequence sampling rate (as after set_anim_frame_rate), a count that is not a whole number of frames at the sampling rate is an error naming the multiple to use, with nothing changed. Each per-platform override of the sampling rate that the engine compresses at (a valid rate other than the default that is a multiple or a factor of it) is checked the same way, and the error names the platform; an override with a non-positive numerator is an error too. The current count gives saved=false and a note, with nothing saved. A count the data controller rejects is an error with nothing saved, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: frame_count
params.description: New number of frames (integer > 0).

commands.returns: { sequence_path, frame_count, saved, save_error, note? }

commands.name: set_anim_retarget_source
commands.description: Set a UAnimSequence's retarget source and/or its retarget reference-pose sequence (RefPoseSeq) in one undo step and save it; pass at least one of the two, and an empty or 'None' value clears that field. Read the current values first with get_anim_sequence_info. A ref_pose_seq_path that does not load is an error before anything changes; a retarget_source the skeleton does not define is still written, with a warning in notes. Values the sequence already has are a success with changed=false, applied_count 0, saved=false and a note, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Object path of the UAnimSequence to change, e.g. '/Game/Animation/Run_Fwd'.

params.name: retarget_source
params.description: Retarget-source name (FName). Must name an entry in the owning skeleton's retarget-source map to RESOLVE at runtime, but the property write persists regardless. Use 'None' (or empty) to clear.

params.name: ref_pose_seq_path
params.description: Optional object path of a UAnimSequence used as the additive retarget reference pose (RefPoseSeq). Pass empty/'None' to clear it.

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, retarget_source, ref_pose_seq, ref_pose_seq_set, ref_pose_seq_cleared, applied_count, notes, changed, success, saved, save_error, note? }

commands.name: set_anim_root_motion
commands.description: Write the three root motion settings of a UAnimSequence (bEnableRootMotion, RootMotionRootLock, bForceRootLock) and save it. All three are written on every call, so an omitted one is reset to its default; an unknown root lock name applies RefPose while the reply echoes the given text. Settings the sequence already has are a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

params.name: anim_sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimSequence.

params.name: enable_root_motion
params.description: Whether to enable root motion extraction (default true)

params.name: root_motion_root_lock
params.description: Root lock mode: RefPose|AnimFirstFrame|Zero (default RefPose)

params.name: force_root_lock
params.description: Whether to force the root lock (default false)

commands.returns: { anim_sequence_path, enable_root_motion, root_motion_root_lock, force_root_lock, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: set_anim_transition_rule_automatic
commands.description: Set the automatic rule of one transition (source_state to target_state) in a state machine of an Animation Blueprint: bAutomaticRuleBasedOnSequencePlayerInState and AutomaticRuleTriggerTime, both written every call (omitted means false and 0). Marks it structurally modified and saves without compiling; refused while PIE runs unless force=true.

params.name: anim_blueprint_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint

params.name: machine_name
params.description: Name of the state machine that owns the transition

params.name: source_state
params.description: Name of the source state (transition origin)

params.name: target_state
params.description: Name of the target state (transition destination)

params.name: enabled
params.description: True lets the transition fire on its own when the sequence player of the source state nears its end (bAutomaticRuleBasedOnSequencePlayerInState); omitted writes false.

params.name: trigger_time
params.description: AutomaticRuleTriggerTime in seconds (default 0.0; negative = blend lead)

commands.returns: { anim_blueprint_path, machine_name, source_state, target_state, enabled, trigger_time, rule_graph_has_result_node, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_anim_transition_rule_from_bool
commands.description: Make a bool variable the rule of an existing transition (source_state to target_state) of an Animation Blueprint state machine: every rule-graph node but the result sink is removed, then a getter of variable_name is wired to the sink's bCanEnterTransition, so the transition passes while the variable is true (there is no invert option). A missing blueprint, machine, transition or variable, or one that is not a single bool, is an error before anything changes; a variable not compiled yet (variable_kind new_blueprint) is checked against its declared type. Repeat calls rebuild the same rule (idempotent). Marks the blueprint structurally modified and saves without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint). Float test: set_anim_transition_rule_from_comparison; time-based: set_anim_transition_rule_automatic; empty rule: clear_anim_transition_rule; new transition: add_anim_transition. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

commands.name: set_bone_parent
commands.description: Move a bone, with its children, under another parent in the reference skeleton of a USkeleton asset (FReferenceSkeletonModifier::SetParent), or make it an extra root with an empty parent_name, in one undo step, then save the skeleton; no commit_bone_changes is needed. Use add_bone to create a bone under a parent, rename_bone to rename, set_bone_transform to move its reference pose. A bone or parent not in the skeleton, or a skeleton that does not load, is an error and nothing changes. The engine refuses a parent that is the bone itself or one of its descendants, and a parent it already has: then updated=false and bone_index -1, still a success, and the unchanged skeleton is saved again. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Edit a project copy (create_editable_skeleton), not engine content.

An unknown bone is an error, so not_found is never true in a reply; a failed save makes success false with save_error and keeps the change in memory. Only the skeleton changes: skeletal meshes using it keep their own reference pose. Other bone edits: set_bone_parent, rename_bone, add_bone.

commands.name: set_morph_target_deltas
commands.description: Overwrite all vertex deltas of an existing morph target on one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset with the deltas passed, in one undo step that restores the old deltas, then save the mesh. The undo step records the morph target only, not the mesh: undoing a step that holds the mesh rebuilds it, and the rebuild drops every morph target its imported data does not hold, those of create_skeletal_mesh_morph_target included. The LOD's old deltas are discarded; deltas whose position offset is 0.015 units or less are dropped (normal-only deltas included) and entries that are not objects are skipped, so deltas_set counts what was sent and total_deltas what that LOD kept. When the morph target had no data for a LOD below lod_index, the engine adds an empty one for it (created=true in deltas_per_lod). Every count is read back from the morph target after the save: total_deltas for lod_index, total_deltas_lod0 for LOD 0, deltas_per_lod for each LOD the morph target has, and total_deltas_all_lods. Repeating the same call writes the same data again. A missing morph target or a lod_index outside the mesh's LODs is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Find the morph with get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets (create_skeletal_mesh_morph_target adds one) and read the deltas themselves back with get_morph_target_deltas.
