params.name: silhouette_importance
params.description: SMOI_*: Off|Lowest|Low|Normal|High|Highest.

params.name: texture_importance
params.description: SMOI_* importance of texture density.

params.name: shading_importance
params.description: SMOI_* importance of shading quality.

params.name: skinning_importance
params.description: SMOI_* importance of skinning quality.

params.name: max_bones_per_vertex
params.description: int max bone influences per vertex (ClampMin 1).

params.name: welding_threshold
params.description: float vertex weld distance.

params.name: normals_threshold
params.description: float hard-edge angle in degrees (used when recalc_normals).

params.name: recalc_normals
params.description: bool recompute normals.

params.name: remap_morph_targets
params.description: bool remap morph targets onto the reduced LOD.

params.name: enforce_bone_boundaries
params.description: bool penalize collapses across different major bones.

commands.returns: { lod_index: int, settings_applied: {...}, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings
commands.description: Set the flat per-LOD scalars/enums of FSkeletalMeshLODInfo that no other setter covers (screen size, hysteresis, CPU access, morph error tolerance, skin cache usage, mesh deformer, prioritization weight) on one LOD or, with lod_index -1 or "all", on every LOD of the mesh, then save the mesh. Partial update (idempotent): only fields present are written; a bad skin_cache_usage or lod_index is refused before anything is written. A failed save is an error that leaves the change in memory. Per-platform screen-size overrides are left as they are.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset.

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional. 0-based LOD index to modify (default 0), or -1 / "all" for every LOD. allow_cpu_access with every LOD goes through USkeletalMeshEditorSubsystem::SetAllowCPUAccess.

params.name: screen_size
params.description: Optional float, ScreenSize.Default: the screen size at which this LOD switches in (e.g. 0.3).

params.name: lod_hysteresis
params.description: float, avoids flickering at the LOD boundary.

params.name: allow_cpu_access
params.description: bool, keep this LOD's data on the CPU (e.g. for FX sampling).

params.name: morph_target_position_error_tolerance
params.description: float in microns, Clamp 0.01..10000 (default 20).

params.name: skin_cache_usage
params.description: ESkinCacheUsage by NAME: Auto|Disabled|Enabled (Disabled=255, parsed by name).

params.name: allow_mesh_deformer
params.description: bool, whether a Mesh Deformer is used on this LOD.

params.name: weight_of_prioritization
params.description: float >=0, weight given to BonesToPrioritize/SectionsToPrioritize.

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int (-1 for every LOD), all_lods: bool, applied_lods: int, settings_applied: {...}, old_screen_size?: float (one LOD), old_screen_sizes?: [float] (every LOD), saved: bool }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_material_slot
commands.description: Assign a material to an existing material slot of a skeletal mesh ASSET (writes FSkeletalMaterial.MaterialInterface in USkeletalMesh::GetMaterials()). Address the slot by slot_index OR slot_name (exactly one). Never auto-grows the slot array.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the USkeletalMesh asset.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Content path to the UMaterialInterface to assign.

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Zero-based index of an existing material slot (mutually exclusive with slot_name).

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Name of an existing material slot to resolve to its index (mutually exclusive with slot_index).

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, slot_index: int, slot_name: string, material_path: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_min_lod
commands.description: Set the minimum LOD a skeletal mesh asset (found by content path) renders, so the more detailed LODs below it are skipped while they stay in the asset. It replaces the whole Minimum LOD property with this one value, per-platform overrides included, or the per-quality-level one when the project setting UseSkeletalMeshMinLODPerQualityLevels is on. A missing min_lod, one outside 0 to the LOD count minus 1, or a mesh that does not load is an error. One undo step; the mesh is marked dirty but not saved, so follow with save_asset. old_min_lod is the value in effect before the call. To take a LOD out of the asset use remove_skeletal_mesh_lod; to change switch distances, set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings with screen_size.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero"

params.name: min_lod
params.description: New minimum LOD index, 0-based (must be in [0, NumLODs-1])

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, old_min_lod: int, min_lod: int, lod_count: int, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_section_flags
commands.description: Turn shadow casting, runtime tangent recomputation (a GPU skin cache feature) and/or ray-tracing visibility on or off for one section of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset found by content path; pass at least one of the three flags, and only the flags passed are written. The SkeletalMeshEditorSubsystem writes the section's user data (one undo step per flag) and rebuilds the render data, then the mesh is saved. A mesh that does not load, a LOD or section index its imported model does not have, or a call during PIE (the subsystem refuses it) is an error, and the flags written before the refused one stay in memory unsaved; so is a failed save, which leaves the change in memory. Setting the current value again re-applies and re-saves it. Read the section flags with get_skeletal_mesh_section_info.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero"

params.name: lod_index
params.description: 0-based LOD index containing the section (default 0)

params.name: section_index
params.description: 0-based index of the section within that LOD, as get_skeletal_mesh_section_info lists it (default 0)

params.name: cast_shadow
params.description: Optional bool: whether the section casts shadows.

params.name: recompute_tangent
params.description: Optional bool: whether the GPU skin cache recomputes the section's tangents at runtime.

params.name: visible_in_ray_tracing
params.description: Optional bool: whether the section is visible in ray tracing (bVisibleInRayTracing). b_visible is accepted as an alias.

commands.returns: { skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int, section_index: int, cast_shadow?: bool, recompute_tangent?: bool, visible_in_ray_tracing?: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_socket_parent
commands.description: Re-parent an existing socket on a skeletal mesh to a different bone. Validates the bone exists in the reference skeleton.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the skeletal mesh asset

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name of the socket to re-parent

params.name: parent_bone_name
params.description: Bone name to attach the socket to (must exist in skeleton)

commands.returns: { socket_name: string, parent_bone_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, reparented: bool }

commands.name: set_skeletal_mesh_socket_transform
commands.description: Set the local transform (relative to its parent bone) of an existing socket of a skeletal mesh asset, then save the asset that owns the socket: the mesh for one of its own sockets, else its skeleton for a socket that lives only there (socket_owner and saved_asset say which). location, rotation and scale are each optional but at least one is required; only those passed are written and the rest keep their current values, and the reply reads the transform back from the socket. Not an undo step; repeating the call writes and saves the same transform again. A missing socket, or an owner that cannot be saved (engine content, a read-only root), is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Create the socket with add_skeletal_mesh_socket (or add_skeleton_socket on the skeleton), move it to another bone with set_skeletal_mesh_socket_parent, rename it with rename_skeletal_mesh_socket.

params.name: skeletal_mesh_path
params.description: Content path of the USkeletalMesh asset (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero'.

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name of an existing socket on the mesh (or its skeleton), as add_skeletal_mesh_socket created it, e.g. 'hand_r_socket'.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] offset from the parent bone, in centimetres.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation relative to the parent bone, in degrees.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] scale relative to the parent bone, e.g. [1, 1, 1].

commands.returns: { socket_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, socket_owner: "mesh"|"skeleton", saved_asset: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string, applied: {location, rotation, scale}, location_x: float, location_y: float, location_z: float, rotation_pitch: float, rotation_yaw: float, rotation_roll: float, scale_x: float, scale_y: float, scale_z: float }

commands.name: sort_montage_segments
commands.description: Sort the segments of one slot track of a UAnimMontage asset by their position on the track, ascending (FAnimTrack::SortAnimSegments), which then lays them end-to-end from 0 and clamps each segment's end time to its animation's length, in one undo step, and save the montage. Segment indices follow the new order, and the sort key is the track position, not the AnimStartTime that set_montage_segment_start_time edits. Idempotent: a track the sort leaves unchanged (already in order, end-to-end and within its animations) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is modified or saved. An unknown montage or slot is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. To close gaps but keep the array order: collapse_montage_segments; slot names: get_montage_info.

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example').

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Name of the slot track to sort, e.g. "DefaultSlot" (case-insensitive); an unknown slot is an error.

commands.returns: { montage_path, slot_name, segment_count, applied, saved, save_error, message }

commands.name: stop_animation
commands.description: Stop montage playback on a skeletal mesh component with Montage_Stop and a 0.25 s blend-out: only montage_path when given, otherwise every active montage. Editor world unless the world param says otherwise; an unknown montage_path is an error. was_playing and playing cover any montage.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins

params.name: montage_path
params.description: Full asset path of a specific AnimMontage to stop; if omitted, stops all montages (optional)

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie').

commands.returns: { component_name: string, was_playing: bool, playing: bool, success: bool, montage_path: string?, montage_name: string?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: add_asset_to_collection
commands.description: Add one asset, by object path, to an existing static Content Browser collection of the project and read the membership back. The collection is looked up by collection_name within share_type (default Local; an unrecognised value also means Local), which must be the share type it was created with: a name not found there is an error. The asset itself is not loaded or checked. An asset that is already a member makes the collection manager refuse the add, which comes back as an error with its reason. The manager writes the collection file itself, outside the undo history. verified confirms membership and object_count counts the direct members. Create the collection with create_collection; the inverse is remove_asset_from_collection; list members with get_collection_assets and collections with get_collections.

params.name: collection_name
params.description: Name of the (existing) collection.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path of the asset to add, e.g. "/Game/Props/SM_Chair.SM_Chair"; used as given, without loading or checking the asset.

params.name: share_type
params.description: ECollectionShareType: "Local", "Private", or "Shared" (optional, default "Local"); an unrecognised value falls back to Local

commands.returns: { collection_name: string, share_type: string, asset_path: string, added: bool, verified: bool, object_count: number }

commands.name: add_static_mesh_socket
commands.description: Add a new socket to a UStaticMesh asset (package or object path) with an optional relative location, rotation, scale and tag, then save the mesh; no undo transaction. A socket_name the mesh already has is an error, and so is a location, rotation or scale that is not three numbers; both are checked before the mesh is touched. A failed save is an error, yet the socket stays on the mesh in memory. Edit an existing socket with set_static_mesh_socket_transform or rename_static_mesh_socket; list them with get_static_mesh_info; skeletal meshes use add_skeletal_mesh_socket.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset.

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name for the new socket.

params.name: location
params.description: Socket relative location as [x, y, z] (optional)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Socket relative rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] (optional)

params.name: scale
params.description: Socket relative scale as [x, y, z] (optional; defaults to 1,1,1)

params.name: tag
params.description: Free-form socket tag string (optional)

commands.returns: { socket_name, socket_count, location_x, location_y, location_z, scale_x, scale_y, scale_z, tag }

commands.name: clear_render_target
commands.description: Fill a whole UTextureRenderTarget2D with one solid color via ClearRenderTarget2D, reporting the width and height it covered. Render-target contents live on the GPU only, so nothing is saved or undoable. cleared is false, and the call fails, when the engine skips the clear: a render target without a resource, which is every render target in a process that cannot render (-nullrhi, a commandlet).

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the render target

params.name: color
params.description: Optional [r, g, b, a] clear color, defaults to opaque black

commands.returns: { render_target_path: string, cleared: bool, clear_color: [number], width: int, height: int }

commands.name: compare_asset_versions
commands.description: Apply the binary ref-scan of scan_uasset_references to the SAME asset (rel_path) across N external Content roots, reporting ref-count / size / mtime (and optional pattern-match count) per root so you can tell an incomplete (stub) copy from the complete one at a glance.

params.name: rel_path
params.description: Asset path relative to each root's Content dir, e.g. 'Characters/Mannequin/ABP_Manny.uasset' (a missing extension defaults to .uasset).

params.name: roots
params.description: List of external Content-root directories to compare across.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Optional regex (ECMAScript) forwarded to the scan; when set, roots rank by pattern-match count instead of ref-path count.

commands.returns: { rel_path: string, pattern: string, roots: [{root, full_path, exists, size_bytes, modified, ref_path_unique, ref_path_occurrences, match_unique, match_occurrences}], most_complete_root: string, likely_stub_root: string, message: string }

commands.name: create_collection
commands.description: Create a static Content Browser collection named collection_name in the project's collection container, under share_type (default Local; Private or Shared otherwise, and an unrecognised value falls back to Local). Idempotent: when that name already exists under that share type nothing is created and the call succeeds with created false and already_existed true; the check looks at that share type only. The collection manager writes the collection file itself, outside the undo history, and a creation it refuses is an error carrying its reason. exists is read back afterwards. Fill it with add_asset_to_collection, list collections with get_collections and members with get_collection_assets; the inverse is delete_collection. A Material Parameter Collection is a different asset: create_material_parameter_collection.

params.name: collection_name
params.description: Name of the collection to create.

params.name: share_type
params.description: ECollectionShareType: "Local", "Private", or "Shared" (optional, default "Local"); an unrecognised value falls back to Local

commands.returns: { collection_name: string, share_type: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, exists: bool }

commands.name: create_render_target_2d
commands.description: Create a UTextureRenderTarget2D asset at package_path/name with the given size and format, black clear color, and save it. An existing one there is returned as is: width, height and format are then ignored (already_exists:true). Returns asset_path, width, height, format and pixel_format.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the render target asset to create

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/RenderTargets

params.name: width
params.description: Render target width in pixels, default 256

params.name: height
params.description: Render target height in pixels, default 256

params.name: format
params.description: Render target format, default RTF_RGBA8: RTF_R8, RTF_RG8, RTF_RGBA8, RTF_RGBA8_SRGB, RTF_R16f, RTF_RG16f, RTF_RGBA16f (HDR), RTF_R32f, RTF_RG32f, RTF_RGBA32f or RTF_RGB10A2, RTF_ prefix optional; an unknown value falls back to RTF_RGBA8 with format_warning

commands.returns: { render_target_name: string, asset_path: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, width: int, height: int, format: string, pixel_format: string, format_warning: string, save_error: string }

commands.name: create_render_target_2d_array
commands.description: Creates a persisted UTextureRenderTarget2DArray.  Wraps UTextureRenderTarget2DArray::Init(SizeX, SizeY, Slices, Format) and saves the asset to disk. Re-running deletes and rebuilds the asset deterministically.  format accepts one of "B8G8R8A8"/"BGRA8" (default), "FloatRGBA"/"RGBA16F", "RGBA32F", "R16F".

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the render-target-array asset to create

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder; defaults to /Game/Textures

params.name: size
params.description: Optional square edge in pixels; clamped 1..8192

params.name: slices
params.description: Optional slice count; clamped 1..512

params.name: format
params.description: Optional EPixelFormat name; defaults to BGRA8

commands.returns: { render_target_name: string, asset_path: string, size_x: int, size_y: int, slices: int, format: string, created: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_render_target_cube
commands.description: Creates a persisted UTextureRenderTargetCube (6-face cube render target).  Wraps UTextureRenderTargetCube::Init(SizeX, Format) when a format is given, or InitAutoFormat(SizeX) otherwise, and saves the asset to disk. Re-running deletes and rebuilds the asset deterministically.  format accepts one of "B8G8R8A8"/"BGRA8", "FloatRGBA"/"RGBA16F", "RGBA32F". When omitted the format is auto-derived (InitAutoFormat).

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the cube render-target asset to create

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder; defaults to /Game/Textures

params.name: size
params.description: Optional cube edge in pixels; clamped 1..8192

params.name: format
params.description: Optional EPixelFormat name; defaults to auto-derived

commands.returns: { render_target_name: string, asset_path: string, size_x: int, format: string, created: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_static_texture_from_render_target
commands.description: Bakes a UTexture2D from an existing UTextureRenderTarget2D (editor only).  Wraps UKismetRenderingLibrary::RenderTargetCreateStaticTexture2DEditorOnly and saves the resulting static texture to disk. Re-running deletes and rebuilds the asset deterministically.  render_target_path accepts either short "/Game/MyGame/RT_Example" or fully-qualified "...RT_Example.RT_Example" asset paths.

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the source render target (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/RT_Example" or fully-qualified "...RT_Example.RT_Example")

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the static texture asset to create

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder; defaults to /Game/Textures

commands.returns: { texture_name: string, asset_path: string, render_target_path: string, created: bool, saved: bool, width: int, height: int, format: string, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_texture_2d_array
commands.description: Creates a persisted UTexture2DArray from slices (no external file import).  If ``source_texture_paths`` is given, those UTexture2D assets are loaded into the array's SourceTextures; otherwise ``slice_count`` small solid-color slices of ``size`` x ``size`` are generated. The array Source is then built via UTexture2DArray::UpdateSourceFromSourceTextures(true) and the asset is saved.  source_texture_paths is an optional array of UTexture2D asset paths used as the array's slices. Each must have a valid editor source. If omitted, slices are generated.  size is the per-slice pixel size (clamped 1..2048).

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the texture-array asset to create

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder; defaults to /Game/Textures

params.name: slice_count
params.description: Optional number of generated slices when source_texture_paths is omitted; clamped 1..64; defaults to 2

params.name: size
params.description: Optional per-slice pixel size; clamped 1..2048; defaults to 64

params.name: source_texture_paths
params.description: Optional array of UTexture2D asset paths used as slices

commands.returns: { texture_array_name: string, asset_path: string, width: int, height: int, num_slices: int, format: string, created: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_texture_2d_from_data
commands.description: Create a UTexture2D asset filled with one solid color, with no source file: it allocates a BGRA8 editor source of width x height, fills every pixel with fill_color, sets sRGB with default compression, builds the resource and saves the asset to disk; no undo step. Use it for placeholder or mask textures; to bring in an image file use import_texture_file, to bake a render target create_static_texture_from_render_target, to change compression or sRGB afterwards set_texture_settings, and get_texture_info to read it back. WARNING: an asset already at package_path/name is force-deleted first, whatever its class and even if other assets reference it, so every call rebuilds the texture (not idempotent). An invalid package path is an error. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the texture kept in memory.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name of the texture, no folder, e.g. "T_Mask_White".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder as a long package path, e.g. "/Game/Textures/Placeholders" (default /Game/Textures; one trailing slash is dropped).

params.name: width
params.description: Width in pixels, a whole number clamped to 1..8192 (default 64).

params.name: height
params.description: Height in pixels, a whole number clamped to 1..8192 (default 64).

params.name: fill_color
params.description: [R, G, B, A] as 0-255 numbers, each rounded and clamped, e.g. [255, 0, 0, 255] for opaque red; missing trailing entries keep the default 255 (opaque white).

commands.returns: { texture_name: string, asset_path: string, created: bool, saved: bool, width: int, height: int, format: string, has_source: bool, fill_color: [int, int, int, int], save_error?: string }

commands.name: delete_collection
commands.description: Deletes a Content Browser collection of the project, looked up by name within share_type; only the collection goes, the assets it lists are not touched. The collection manager writes the change to its collection file itself, outside the undo history, so it cannot be undone. Idempotent: a name not found in that share type succeeds with already_absent true and nothing changes, so pass the share type the collection was created with (a wrong one reads as absent); get_collections lists names and share types. A collection that exists but that the manager fails to delete is an error. Inverse of create_collection; to take single assets out instead, use remove_asset_from_collection, and get_collection_assets to see the members first.

params.name: collection_name
params.description: Name of the collection to delete, as get_collections lists it (e.g. "Props_Review").

params.name: share_type
params.description: ECollectionShareType the collection was created with: "Local", "Private", or "Shared" (optional, default "Local"); an unrecognised value falls back to Local.

commands.returns: { collection_name: string, share_type: string, destroyed: bool, already_absent: bool, exists: bool }

commands.name: diff_content_trees
commands.description: Compare two Content folders (project vs external, fork vs source) WITHOUT loading the editor: reports assets added/removed/changed keyed by relative path, using file size and (optionally) a whole-file MD5 content hash. Verifies a Migrate or audits a fork on disk. Each tree may be a disk directory OR a /Game|/Engine mount path.

params.name: tree_a
params.description: First Content folder: absolute disk dir or /Game|/Engine mount path.

params.name: tree_b
params.description: Second Content folder: absolute disk dir or /Game|/Engine mount path.

params.name: hash
params.description: Optional bool (default true). When true, same-size files are compared by MD5 to detect content changes; when false, only size is compared.

commands.returns: { tree_a: string, tree_b: string, dir_a: string, dir_b: string, only_in_a: [string], only_in_b: [string], changed: [{rel, size_a, size_b, hash_a, hash_b, reason}], identical_count: int, only_in_a_count: int, only_in_b_count: int, changed_count: int, message: string }

commands.name: draw_line_to_render_target
commands.description: Draw one straight line onto a UTextureRenderTarget2D asset in a single canvas pass in the editor world (UCanvas::K2_DrawLine), from start to end in render-target pixels, with color and thickness. The line blends over the existing pixels: nothing is cleared, saved or undoable, each call adds another line, and render-target contents live on the GPU only, so keep them with create_static_texture_from_render_target or export_render_target. Wipe it first with clear_render_target; for text, a texture or a material use draw_text_to_render_target, draw_texture_to_render_target or draw_material_to_render_target; get_render_target_info gives the size, create_render_target_2d makes a target. A missing render target is an error; drawn is false, and the call fails, when start and end are the same point (the canvas skips a zero-length line).

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the destination UTextureRenderTarget2D, e.g. "/Game/RT/RT_Canvas"

params.name: start
params.description: Line start [x, y] in render-target pixels from the top-left corner, e.g. [0, 0]

params.name: end
params.description: Line end [x, y] in render-target pixels from the top-left corner, e.g. [256, 128]; it must differ from start

params.name: color
params.description: Optional [r, g, b, a] linear color, each usually 0..1; channels left out keep opaque white, the default

params.name: thickness
params.description: Optional line thickness in pixels, default 1

commands.returns: { render_target_path: string, drawn: bool, thickness: number, start: [number], end: [number] }

commands.name: draw_material_to_render_target
commands.description: Render a material into a UTextureRenderTarget2D: a full-screen quad by default, or, with position and/or size, a rectangle in render-target pixels from the top-left drawn in one canvas pass (full 0-1 UVs) that composites over the existing pixels by the material's blend mode. Nothing is cleared, saved or undoable, and render-target contents live on the GPU only, so keep them with create_static_texture_from_render_target or export_render_target. A missing render target or material is an error. drawn is false, and the call fails, when the engine skips the draw: for the full-screen pass a process that cannot render (-nullrhi, a commandlet) or a render target without a resource; for a rectangle a width or height that is not positive. For a texture use draw_texture_to_render_target.

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the destination render target

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInterface to draw

params.name: position
params.description: Optional [x, y] destination position of a rectangle draw, default [0,0]; giving it (or size) switches to the canvas rectangle draw

params.name: size
params.description: Optional [w, h] destination size of a rectangle draw, defaults to the render target dimensions; giving it (or position) switches to the canvas rectangle draw

commands.returns: { render_target_path: string, material_path: string, drawn: bool, position?: [number], size?: [number] }

commands.name: draw_text_to_render_target
commands.description: Draw a string onto a UTextureRenderTarget2D asset in one canvas pass in the editor world, in the engine's medium font (no font choice), tinted by color and scaled by scale, with position the text's top-left in render-target pixels. The text blends over the existing pixels: nothing is cleared, saved or undoable, and render-target contents live on the GPU only, so keep them with create_static_texture_from_render_target or export_render_target. A missing render target is an error; drawn is false, and the call fails, when nothing was drawn (an empty text, or no engine font: font_resolved says whether one was found). Related: draw_texture_to_render_target, draw_line_to_render_target, clear_render_target.

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the destination render target

params.name: text
params.description: Text to draw

params.name: position
params.description: Optional [x, y] text position, default [0,0]

params.name: color
params.description: Optional [r, g, b, a] text color, defaults to opaque white

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional uniform number or [x, y] scale, default 1

commands.returns: { render_target_path: string, text: string, drawn: bool, font_resolved: bool, position: [number] }

commands.name: draw_texture_to_render_target
commands.description: Draw a texture as a rectangle onto a UTextureRenderTarget2D asset in one canvas pass in the editor world: position and size in render-target pixels from the top-left (size defaults to the whole target), full 0-1 UVs, tinted by color. It alpha-blends over the existing pixels: nothing is cleared, saved or undoable, and render-target contents live on the GPU only, so keep them with create_static_texture_from_render_target or export_render_target. A missing render target or texture is an error; drawn is false, and the call fails, when a width or height that is not positive draws nothing. For a material use draw_material_to_render_target with position and size.

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the destination render target

params.name: texture_path
params.description: Asset path of the UTexture to draw, e.g. /Engine/EngineResources/WhiteSquareTexture

params.name: position
params.description: Optional [x, y] destination position, default [0,0]

params.name: size
params.description: Optional [w, h] destination size, defaults to render target dimensions

params.name: color
params.description: Optional [r, g, b, a] tint color, defaults to opaque white

commands.returns: { render_target_path: string, texture_path: string, drawn: bool, position: [number], size: [number] }

commands.name: evaluate_curve_at_time
commands.description: Sample a curve asset (UCurveFloat, UCurveVector or UCurveLinearColor) at one time without changing it: values holds every channel (1 for a float curve, 3 for a vector, 4 for a color as r,g,b,a), value the channel picks, and vector {x,y,z} or color {r,g,b,a} come with the multi-channel types. A time before the first key or after the last follows the curve's extrapolation. Use it to check what a curve yields at gameplay inputs after editing it; to see the authored keys use get_curve_keys and to add one add_curve_key; a curve table row: get_curve_table_info; an animation curve: get_anim_curve_data. A path that does not load as a curve, or a curve of another class, is an error.

params.name: curve_path
params.description: Asset path of the curve, as a package path ("/Game/Curves/C_Damage") or an object path ("/Game/Curves/C_Damage.C_Damage").

params.name: time
params.description: Time to sample at, on the curve's X axis in its own units, e.g. 0.5; any float, outside the keyed range too.

params.name: channel
params.description: Optional 0-based channel whose value fills the scalar value: 0-2 = x,y,z on a vector curve, 0-3 = r,g,b,a on a color curve (default 0; out of range falls back to 0, and channel reports the one used); ignored on a float curve.

commands.returns: { curve_path: string, curve_class: string, time: float, curve_type: string, num_channels: int, channel: int, value: float, values: [float], vector?: {x,y,z}, color?: {r,g,b,a} }

commands.name: export_render_target
commands.description: Export a render target to an image file on disk: PNG, except an RGBA16f or RGBA32f render target, which writes HDR when filename ends in .hdr and EXR otherwise. exported is measured on disk: the file must exist, hold bytes and have been written by this call. It is false, and the call fails saying why, for a render target without a resource (every render target in a process that cannot render: -nullrhi, a commandlet), an invalid path, a file that cannot be opened for writing, or an image that cannot be read back; an empty file left by a failed export is removed when the call created it.

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the render target to export

params.name: output_directory
params.description: Absolute directory path to write into, created if missing

params.name: filename
params.description: Output file name including extension, e.g. RT_Example.png

commands.returns: { render_target_path: string, output_directory: string, filename: string, file_path: string, exported: bool, file_exists: bool, file_size_bytes: number }

commands.name: find_assets_by_name
commands.description: Find assets by NAME, scanning every mounted content root (/Game, /Engine, /Water, plugin mounts, ...) and returning name, object path, class and package per hit. The broad "does anything called <token> exist, and where?" search. It has TWO match modes and picks one automatically, reporting which in `match_mode`: a pattern WITHOUT `*`/`?` is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING test (FString::Contains) -- pass the bare token, this is the common case; a pattern WITH `*` or `?` is a real glob (FString::MatchesWildcard). WARNING: The glob is ANCHORED AT BOTH ENDS -- it matches the WHOLE name, not a substring -- so `Grass*` means "starts with Grass" and `*Grass*` is what reproduces substring behaviour. It only ever looks at the asset NAME, so it cannot find an asset by its folder or by a class it belongs to: use resolve_asset_by_name to check ONE exact name and get every homonym, get_assets_in_folder to enumerate a directory, get_assets_by_type for the 5 built-in type filters, and get_assets_by_tag for an Asset Registry tag.

params.name: search_pattern
params.description: Matched against the asset NAME. Contains no `*`/`?` -> case-insensitive substring (FString::Contains). Contains `*` or `?` -> glob (FString::MatchesWildcard), ANCHORED at both ends: `*` matches any run including empty, `?` matches 0 or 1 character (UE semantics, not exactly 1). Not a regex.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of matched assets (1..50000); defaults to 1000. WARNING: Hitting the cap ABORTS the enumeration, so `total_scanned` then counts only the assets visited before the early-out, not the whole registry.

params.name: case_sensitive
params.description: When true, match is case-sensitive; defaults to false

params.name: wait_for_scan
params.description: When true (default), force-completes the AssetRegistry scan before enumerating so a still-loading registry cannot report total_scanned:0. Set false to skip the (possibly blocking) wait.

commands.returns: { assets: [{ name, path, class, package, is_loaded }], count: int, total_scanned: int, scan_was_pending: bool, search_pattern: string, match_mode: "substring"|"wildcard", case_sensitive: bool, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool }

commands.name: generate_asset_thumbnail
commands.description: Render and cache an asset's thumbnail (or report the existing cached one).  When the editor can render (FApp::CanEverRender() and the RHI is initialized), this generates a fresh thumbnail via ThumbnailTools and caches it into the package's thumbnail map. When rendering is unavailable, or the object type has no thumbnail renderer, it honestly reports the existing cached thumbnail state.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path or package path of the asset.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, object_path: string, asset_class: string, rendered: bool, has_thumbnail: bool, width: int, height: int, compressed_bytes: int, message: string }

commands.name: get_asset_by_name
commands.description: Retrieve ONE asset by exact name and return its identity (name, class, object path, package, is_loaded, file size) plus, with load_full_data, type-specific detail: a Blueprint's parent class / compile status / generated class, a StaticMesh's section-vertex-LOD counts, whether a material is an instance; with include_tags, its Asset Registry tags (the indexed key/value pairs an asset publishes -- parent class, mesh stats, fork-lineage tags) read without a load. WARNING: When the name is ambiguous it still resolves to the FIRST match and merely lists the rest in `ambiguous_matches` -- check that field, or use resolve_asset_by_name, which refuses to pick for you. The fallback name scan only covers /Game, so an /Engine or plugin-mount asset must be addressed by its full package or object path. Use get_assets_by_names for a batch, get_assets_by_tag to search BY a tag value, and find_assets_by_name when you only know part of the name.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT asset name, or a full package name ('/Game/Foo/BP_Foo') or object path ('/Game/Foo/BP_Foo.BP_Foo'); a path is tried first and is the only form that reaches outside /Game

params.name: load_full_data
params.description: When true (DEFAULT), LOADS the asset to add type-specific details (Blueprint parent class, mesh sections, ...). Pass false to stay metadata-only and avoid a synchronous load.

params.name: include_tags
params.description: Optional bool, default false: add `tags`, every Asset Registry tag of the asset as { name, value }, read from the registry without loading it.

commands.returns: { name: string, class: string, path: string, package: string, is_loaded: bool, file_size_bytes?: int, file_size_kb?: number, parent_class?: string, is_compiled?: bool, is_valid?: bool, generated_class?: string, num_sections?: int, num_vertices?: int, num_lods?: int, is_material_instance?: bool, tags?: [{ name: string, value: string }], ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: get_asset_dependencies_recursive
commands.description: Walk an asset's package dependencies through the Asset Registry, breadth-first and deduplicated, down to max_depth levels, without loading or changing anything: every package it needs directly (depth 1) or through others, each listed once with the depth where it was first reached, /Script/ packages included. Use it for what an asset drags in with it (migration, cooking, memory); for direct dependencies only, with class and loaded state, use get_asset_dependencies; for who uses an asset get_asset_referencers; for the chain between two assets get_reference_path; for loops check_asset_circular_dependency. An asset the registry does not know gives count 0 rather than an error; a path that is not a valid long package name is an error. Deep walks on a large project return thousands of packages, so start with a low max_depth.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Root asset, as a package path ("/Game/Characters/BP_Hero") or an object path ("/Game/Characters/BP_Hero.BP_Hero").

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Levels to walk, 1 = direct dependencies only (1..32, default 3; a value outside the range is clamped).

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Optional "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive, default "all"): hard keeps only references loaded with the asset, soft only soft-object references, at every level; any other value counts as "all".

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, package_name: string, max_depth: int, dependency_type: string, dependencies: [{path, depth}], count: int }

commands.name: get_asset_file_info
commands.description: Stat an asset's package file on disk without loading the asset: its size in bytes, KB and MB, its last-modified timestamp (formatted string + Unix epoch) with its age in days and hours, and the absolute file path it resolved to (.uasset, else .umap for a level, which `extension` names) -- the measurement for a disk-budget question ("what is costing the 491 MB in this import?") and the disk-side oracle for a save whose return value claimed success. A package or object path is stat'ed even when the Asset Registry has no entry for it; a bare name resolves like get_asset_by_name (a /Game-only exact-name scan, first hit wins with the rest in ambiguous_matches). A package with no file on disk, one never saved for instance, is a success with file_exists=false, file_size_bytes 0 and a message. WARNING: Size is NOT a proxy for content or integrity: a DataTable that GREW by 5 KB had lost 46 of its 48 references. To measure content use get_data_table_info, get_data_table_row with include_export_text or get_asset_dependencies; for in-memory cost use get_asset_memory_usage. It is a FILE timestamp: an asset edited in memory but not saved reports its old size and date, and Unreal does not tell creation from modification. Use list_assets_modified_since to sweep a whole folder by date, and list_dirty_packages for unsaved-in-memory changes.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT asset name, or a full package name ('/Game/Maps/L_Main') or object path ('/Game/Foo/BP_Foo.BP_Foo'); a path is tried first, is the only form that reaches outside /Game, and is stat'ed even when the Asset Registry does not list it

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, asset_class?: string, package_name: string, file_path: string, extension: string, file_exists: bool, file_size_bytes: int, file_size_kb?: number, file_size_mb?: number, last_modified?: string, last_modified_timestamp?: int, age_days?: number, age_hours?: number, message?: string, ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: get_asset_import_data
commands.description: Read the source-file record (UAssetImportData) of an asset loaded by path: the file(s) it was imported from, as stored and resolved to absolute paths, with each file's import timestamp. Works for textures, sound waves and any class with an AssetImportData property (static and skeletal meshes, animation sequences). An asset that has none is a success with has_import_data=false, empty source_file and source_files, source_file_count 0 and no import_time. source_file is the first resolved file and import_time the first file's timestamp. Read-only: the asset is loaded if needed, not changed. An asset that does not load is an error. Interchange pipelines and node data: get_interchange_asset_import_data; reimport from the recorded file: reimport_asset or reimport_interchange_asset.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path in object form, e.g. "/Game/Imported/T_Rock.T_Rock", or package form "/Game/Imported/T_Rock".

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, asset_class: string, has_import_data: bool, source_file: string, source_files: [{relative_filename, resolved_filename, import_time}], source_file_count: int, import_time?: string }

commands.name: get_asset_metadata_tags
commands.description: Reads all editor metadata tags (UMetaData) of an asset.  Wraps UEditorAssetLibrary::GetMetadataTagValues and returns each tag as a {key, value} pair. (Distinct from get_asset_by_name with include_tags, which reads Asset Registry tags instead of the asset's stored metadata tags.)

params.name: asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the asset.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, tags: [{ key: string, value: string }], tag_count: number }

commands.name: get_asset_thumbnail
commands.description: Report whether an asset is of a type that CAN carry a thumbnail, alongside its resolved object path, class and loaded state. WARNING: `has_thumbnail` is a CLASS test, not a lookup of stored thumbnail bytes: it is true for any StaticMesh, Material, Texture, Blueprint, SkeletalMesh or Level and false for everything else, whether or not a thumbnail was ever rendered -- and it returns no image data at all. To actually see something rendered, use generate_asset_thumbnail or capture_viewport. Resolution matches get_asset_by_name (full package name first, then a /Game-only exact-name scan, first hit wins with the rest in ambiguous_matches).

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT asset name, or a full package name (which is tried first and is the only form that reaches outside /Game)

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, asset_path: string, has_thumbnail: bool, asset_class: string, asset_loaded: bool, asset_class_name?: string, ambiguous_matches?: [string] }

commands.name: get_assets_by_names
commands.description: Batch variant of get_asset_by_name: resolve N asset names in ONE round-trip instead of N calls, returning per entry a found flag plus that asset's identity (class, object path, package, is_loaded), its Asset Registry tags with include_tags, or the error that stopped it. Delegates to get_asset_by_name literally, so it inherits both its /Game-only fallback scan and its ambiguous_matches transparency -- an ambiguous name still resolves to the first hit, so check that field per entry. max_results caps how many entries are processed.

params.name: asset_names
params.description: Array of exact asset names, full package names or object paths to resolve (required)

params.name: load_full_data
params.description: When true, adds the type-specific details of get_asset_by_name per asset. Defaults to FALSE here -- the opposite of the single-asset tool -- so a batch call cannot accidentally force N synchronous loads.

params.name: include_tags
params.description: Optional bool, default false: add each found asset's Asset Registry `tags` [{ name, value }], as get_asset_by_name include_tags does.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional safety cap on how many array entries get processed (1..5000); omitted processes every entry. Entries past the cap are dropped and results_truncated goes true.

commands.returns: { requested_count: int, processed_count: int, results_truncated: bool, resolved: [{ asset_name, found: bool, name?, class?, path?, package?, is_loaded?, tags?, ambiguous_matches?, error?, ... (same fields as get_asset_by_name when found) }] }

commands.name: get_assets_by_tag
commands.description: Search assets BY an Asset Registry tag (FARFilter::TagsAndValues), server-side and metadata-only -- it never force-loads anything. This is the only tool here that queries by tag rather than by name, path or type: "every asset carrying the fork-origin tag (mcp.forkOrigin by default)", "every Blueprint whose ParentClass tag is X". It is also the general-class search that get_assets_by_type cannot do, since class_filter resolves ANY class (with subclasses) instead of five hardcoded ones. Search by class alone by pairing class_filter with a tag every asset of that class publishes; use get_asset_by_name with include_tags to read the tags OF one asset rather than search by them.

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Asset Registry tag name to filter on, e.g. "ParentClass" or "mcp.forkOrigin" (required). Read the available tag names off a sample asset with get_asset_by_name include_tags=true.

params.name: tag_value
params.description: When given, only assets whose tag equals this value EXACTLY match; when omitted, matches any asset that HAS the tag with any value

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Root package path to search under; defaults to "/Game", so /Engine, /Water and plugin mounts need their root passed explicitly

params.name: recursive
params.description: When true (DEFAULT), recurse into subfolders

params.name: class_filter
params.description: Optional class short name or /Script path (e.g. "Blueprint", "/Script/Engine.DataTable") to additionally constrain the match; subclasses match too (bRecursiveClasses)

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of returned assets (1..50000); defaults to 1000. `total_found` is the uncapped count.

commands.returns: { tag_name: string, tag_value: string, folder_path: string, recursive: bool, class_filter: string, assets: [{ name, path, class, package }], count: int, total_found: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool }

commands.name: get_assets_by_type
commands.description: List every asset of a CLASS under a content path, with name, object path, class, package and is_loaded, plus total_found and results_truncated. Takes any resolvable class -- "DataTable", "NiagaraSystem", "LandscapeGrassType", a "/Script/Module.Class" path -- matched WITH its subclasses, plus five shortcuts kept for convenience: "Blueprint", "StaticMesh", "Texture" (Texture2D exactly), "Sound" (SoundWave exactly) and "Material", which is the one that earns its keep by grouping Material + MaterialInstanceConstant + MaterialInstanceDynamic. Searches /Game by default and any mount via package_path (/Engine, /Water, plugin content). Sister tools: get_assets_in_folder to enumerate a directory whatever the class, find_assets_by_name to search by NAME, get_assets_by_tag to search by an Asset Registry tag.

params.name: asset_type
params.description: A class name ("DataTable"), a "/Script/Module.Class" path, or one of the shortcuts Blueprint | StaticMesh | Material | Texture | Sound. A name that resolves to no class is an error, not an empty result. WARNING: The shortcuts match those classes EXACTLY (Texture finds Texture2D but not TextureCube); any other name matches the class AND its subclasses.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content root to search, recursively. Defaults to "/Game"; pass "/Engine", "/Water", a plugin mount or a subfolder to look elsewhere.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of returned assets (1..50000); defaults to 1000. `total_found` is the uncapped count.

commands.returns: { assets: [{ name, path, class, package, is_loaded }], count: int, total_found: int, asset_type: string, package_path: string, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool }

commands.name: get_assets_in_folder
commands.description: Enumerate every asset under a content FOLDER (recursively by default), each with name, object path, class, package and is_loaded, plus total_found so you can tell a truncated listing from a complete one. The "what is actually in this directory?" inventory -- metadata only, it never loads an asset. Reaches any mounted content root, not just /Game. Pick this over find_assets_by_name when you know WHERE to look rather than what the name contains, over get_assets_by_type when you want everything regardless of class, and over resolve_asset_by_name when you do not have an exact name at all.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Folder to list. A bare/relative name is prefixed with /Game/; a path already starting with "/" (e.g. /Water/Materials, /Engine/..., /<PluginName>/...) is used verbatim, so every mounted content root is reachable.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on number of returned assets (1..50000); defaults to 1000. Compare `count` against `total_found` (which is NOT capped) to see how much was left out.

params.name: recursive
params.description: When true (DEFAULT), include subfolders; false lists only the assets sitting directly in this folder

commands.returns: { assets: [{ name, path, class, package, is_loaded }], count: int, total_found: int, folder_path: string, recursive: bool, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool }

commands.name: get_collection_assets
commands.description: List the object paths of the assets directly in one Content Browser collection (child collections are not included), without changing anything. The collection is looked up by collection_name within share_type, default Local; an unrecognized share_type also falls back to Local, and a name not found under that share type is an error. get_collections lists every collection with its share_type. Returns assets and asset_count; change membership with add_asset_to_collection or remove_asset_from_collection.

params.name: collection_name
params.description: Name of the (existing) collection.

params.name: share_type
params.description: ECollectionShareType: "Local", "Private", or "Shared" (optional, default "Local")

commands.returns: { collection_name: string, share_type: string, assets: [string], asset_count: number }

commands.name: get_collections
commands.description: List every Content Browser collection of the project container, of every share type, without changing anything: name and share_type of each (the share_type that get_collection_assets and the other collection tools need), plus collection_count. Errors when the collection manager is unavailable.
commands.returns: { collections: [{ name: string, share_type: string }], collection_count: number }

commands.name: get_reference_path
commands.description: Find the shortest reference CHAIN through the AssetRegistry dependency graph: with `from`, the shortest from -> ... -> target (walking dependencies); without `from`, the shortest chain from a root (a package nothing references) DOWN to target (walking referencers) -- i.e. 'what keeps target alive / why is it undeletable'. get_asset_referencers gives the direct edges; this gives the PATH.

params.name: target
params.description: The asset whose reference chain to trace (object path or /Game package path).

params.name: from
params.description: Optional starting hub/root asset; when set, traces from -> target via dependencies instead of the referencer-root chain.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Max chain depth to search (optional, default 16; clamped 1..64).

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Optional "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive, default "all"). Filters BOTH BFS directions (the from->target dependency walk and the referencer-root walk) and the always-computed direct_referencers list via the AssetRegistry hard/soft FDependencyQuery split; "all" leaves them unfiltered.

commands.returns: { target: string, target_package: string, from: string, dependency_type: string, found: bool, reached_root: bool, chain: [string], chain_length: int, direct_referencers: [string], direct_referencer_count: int, message: string }

commands.name: get_render_target_info
commands.description: Read the metadata of a render target asset without reading pixels or changing it, for every render-target class: render_target_class, pixel_format and is_srgb always; a UTextureRenderTarget2D adds width, height and format (RTF_*); a UTextureRenderTarget2DArray adds width, height, slices and is_hdr; a UTextureRenderTargetCube adds size (face edge), num_mips, is_hdr and auto_generate_mips; any other render-target class adds width and height. export_render_target writes the image to disk.

params.name: render_target_path
params.description: Asset path of the render target, e.g. /Game/RenderTargets/RT_Example

commands.returns: { render_target_name: string, asset_path: string, render_target_class: string, pixel_format: string, is_srgb: bool, width?: int, height?: int, format?: string, slices?: int, size?: int, num_mips?: int, is_hdr?: bool, auto_generate_mips?: bool }

commands.name: get_static_mesh_info
commands.description: Get detailed info about a static mesh without changing it: LODs, verts, materials (with slots), every socket with its transform and tag, nanite, collision, bounds, and the asset-level lightmap settings (lightmap_resolution, the texel resolution static lighting is baked at, and lightmap_coordinate_index, the UV channel holding the lightmap UVs; an override on a placed component is not read). A mesh that does not load is an error. Per-section flags are get_static_mesh_sections.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Package or object path of the UStaticMesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Crate".

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, num_lods, num_verts_lod0, num_materials, num_sockets, materials: [{slot_index, slot_name, material_path}], sockets: [{name, location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}, tag}], collision_complexity, nanite_enabled, lightmap_resolution, lightmap_coordinate_index, bounds_origin_x, bounds_origin_y, bounds_origin_z, bounds_extent_x, bounds_extent_y, bounds_extent_z, sphere_radius }

commands.name: get_static_mesh_sections
commands.description: List every section of every render LOD of a UStaticMesh asset, loaded from its package or object path, without changing it: lod_index, section_index and the cast_shadow, collision_enabled and visible_in_ray_tracing flags of each, read through the StaticMeshEditor subsystem. A mesh without render data has no LODs and returns an empty list; a mesh that does not load, or a missing subsystem, is an error. total_sections counts the rows. Material slots, vertex counts, sockets, bounds and lightmap settings are get_static_mesh_info; skeletal meshes use get_skeletal_mesh_section_info.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Package or object path of the UStaticMesh, e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Crate".

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path: string, sections: [{ lod_index: number, section_index: number, cast_shadow: bool, collision_enabled: bool, visible_in_ray_tracing: bool }], total_sections: number }

commands.name: get_texture_info
commands.description: Reads the metadata of a UTexture2D or UTexture2DArray asset without changing it; texture_class says which. A UTexture2D reports its size, pixel format, sRGB, compression, LOD group, sampler/LOD settings (address, filter, mip-gen, LOD bias, max size, flip-green), mip count and source; a UTexture2DArray reports its slice size as width/height, num_slices, format, num_mips and source_texture_count. texture_path accepts short or fully-qualified "/Game/MyGame/T_Example.T_Example" asset paths.

params.name: texture_path
params.description: Asset path of the texture or texture array (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/T_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/MyGame/T_Example.T_Example")

commands.name: import_sound_file
commands.description: Import an external WAV file into a USoundWave asset.  Uses the legacy USoundFactory (AudioEditor module) path, no Interchange. The new sound wave is saved to disk and verified by loading it back; the response reports the resulting asset_path, duration (seconds) and num_channels.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination content folder, e.g. /Game/Imported.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Optional destination asset name (default = source file stem).

params.name: replace_existing
params.description: Optional bool, default true: overwrite an asset already at the destination. false refuses with an error when the destination already holds an asset.

commands.returns: { file_path: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_name: string, duration: float, num_channels: int, imported: bool }

commands.name: import_texture_file
commands.description: Import an external image file into a UTexture2D asset.  Uses the legacy UTextureFactory path inline (no Interchange, no IAssetTools::ImportAssets, which asserts when re-entered from the engine tick). Images only -- png/jpg/jpeg/bmp/tga/dds/exr/hdr/tif/tiff/psd/pcx: any other extension is refused before anything is touched (import_sound_file for .wav, import_landscape_heightmap for terrain, import_interchange_asset for FBX/glTF meshes). The new texture is saved to disk and verified by loading it back; the response reports the resulting asset_path, width and height.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute path to the source image on disk; its existence is checked before any work starts.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination content folder, e.g. /Game/Imported. Must start with '/'.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Optional destination asset name (default = source file stem).

params.name: replace_existing
params.description: Optional bool, default true: overwrite an asset already at the destination. false refuses with an error when the destination already holds an asset.

commands.returns: { file_path: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_name: string, width: int, height: int, imported: bool }

commands.name: ingest_external_uassets
commands.description: Copy .uasset/.uexp/.ubulk/.umap from an EXTERNAL Content tree into THIS project, preserving each file's path relative to its Content root, then register the new packages with IAssetRegistry::ScanPathsSynchronous(bForceRescan) and sweep object redirectors under the destination. Fills the gap that migrate_assets only EXPORTS and import_texture_file is image-only. HEAVY: touches project Content on disk + mutates the registry -- run with confirmation.

params.name: source_dir
params.description: External source directory (its Content ancestor defines the preserved relative path; if none, source_dir itself is the root).

params.name: dest_root
params.description: Destination content mount path (optional, default '/Game'); e.g. '/Game/MyGame/Imported'.

params.name: paths
params.description: Optional list of relative sub-paths (relative to the Content root) to restrict the copy to; empty/absent = whole tree.

params.name: overwrite
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When false, destination files that already exist are skipped.

params.name: fixup_redirectors
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Resolve + leave-fixed object redirectors under dest_root after the copy.

commands.returns: { source_dir: string, content_root: string, dest_root: string, dest_dir: string, files_copied: int, files_skipped: int, files_failed: int, scanned_paths: [string], redirectors_fixed: int, copied: [{src, dest, package_path}], message: string }

commands.name: list_assets_modified_since
commands.description: List package files (.uasset/.umap) under a content path whose ON-DISK mtime is newer than a timestamp -- the `find -newermt` recipe for isolating an UE Migrate set or a session's changes, but returning /Game package names. Enumerates the filesystem (so it catches just-migrated assets the registry may not have indexed yet).

params.name: timestamp
params.description: Cutoff time; ISO-8601 (e.g. '2024-07-15T00:00:00Z') or an FDateTime-parseable string. Assets with mtime strictly greater are returned.

params.name: path
params.description: Content path to scan (optional, default '/Game'), e.g. '/Game/MyGame'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max entries to return, newest first (optional, default 500; clamped 1..5000).

commands.returns: { path: string, dir: string, since: string, count: int, truncated: bool, total_matched: int, assets: [{package_name, file_path, modified, size_bytes}], message: string }

commands.name: reimport_asset
commands.description: Reimport an asset from the source file it was imported from (texture, sound, mesh or anything with UAssetImportData), through the legacy FReimportManager handlers, fully automated with no dialogs, overwriting the asset's content in memory with the file's current content. The asset is marked dirty but not saved: save it with save_asset. It cannot be undone. Use it after the source file changed on disk; for assets imported through Interchange pipelines use reimport_interchange_asset; to see the recorded source file first use get_asset_import_data; to bring in a new file use import_texture_file or import_sound_file. success is true only when the asset was reimported. It is false, with reimported false and the reason, when no legacy handler accepts the asset (can_reimport false), when no source file is recorded, when a recorded file is missing on disk (missing_files; refused before the reimport, which can crash the editor then, so nothing changes), or when the handler reports a failure. source_validated says the recorded files were found. Repeating it reimports again. An asset that does not load is an error.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path in object form, e.g. "/Game/Imported/T_Rock.T_Rock" (package form "/Game/Imported/T_Rock" also loads).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, can_reimport: bool, reimported: bool, source_validated: bool, source_files: [string], missing_files?: [string] }

commands.name: remove_asset_from_collection
commands.description: Removes an asset from a collection and reads back its object count (idempotent; inverse of add_asset_to_collection).  If the asset is already absent from the collection a stable payload is returned (already_absent=True).          must match the share type the collection was created with.

params.name: collection_name
params.description: Name of the (existing) collection.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: /Game path / object path of the asset to remove.

params.name: share_type
params.description: ECollectionShareType: "Local", "Private", or "Shared" (optional, default "Local")

commands.returns: { collection_name: string, share_type: string, asset_path: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, verified: bool, object_count: number }

commands.name: remove_asset_metadata_tag
commands.description: Remove one string metadata tag (UMetaData) from an asset and save it (UEditorAssetLibrary::RemoveMetadataTag); no undo step, since package metadata is outside the undo history, and refused by the engine during PIE (the tag stays, reported as an error). Inverse of set_asset_metadata_tag. A key the asset has no tag for is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing saved); an asset that does not exist is an error. The reply re-reads the tags (still_present, tag_count). Read: get_asset_metadata_tags.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the asset (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/M_Example").

params.name: key
params.description: Metadata tag name (FName) to remove, e.g. "Author".

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, key: string, removed: bool, still_present: bool, tag_count: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_static_mesh_socket
commands.description: Remove one socket, found by name, from a UStaticMesh asset loaded from its package or object path, then save the mesh; there is no undo transaction. A name the mesh does not have is a success with removed=false, and nothing is touched or saved (idempotent). A mesh that does not load is an error, and so is a failed save -- refused while PIE runs or under a read-only root -- after which the socket is already gone from the mesh in memory. socket_count is the number of sockets left. List sockets with get_static_mesh_info, add one with add_static_mesh_socket, rename one with rename_static_mesh_socket; skeletal meshes use remove_skeletal_mesh_socket and skeletons remove_skeleton_socket.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Package or object path of the UStaticMesh, e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Crate".

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name of the socket to remove, compared as an FName (case-insensitive).

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, socket_name, removed, socket_count }

commands.name: rename_assets
commands.description: Rename/move multiple assets in one IAssetTools::RenameAssets batch, with per-item disk verification instead of the batch bool. Guards: refuses while PIE is active; refuses paths under readonly_roots (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots setting) on BOTH the source and the destination; pre-detects the native-CDO reference case that makes the engine's FMessageDialog auto-cancel the whole batch (would_block_on_modal) and does NOT call RenameAssets in that case. Also reports referencer packages left DIRTY -- PerformAssetRename discards its FailedPackages list unless UE source control is connected, so a referencer (typically OFPA) can be left unwritten while RenameAssets still returns true.

params.name: assets
params.description: List of rename descriptors: { old_path (required), new_name (optional, default = current name), new_folder (optional, default = current folder) }.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Optional bool (default false). Plan + run every guard and the CDO scan, but never call RenameAssets.

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of long paths that must not be renamed FROM or INTO (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots setting). Pass [] to disable the guard.

params.name: allow_cdo_referenced
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When false, a native-CDO reference to any asset in the batch refuses the batch instead of letting it silently no-op.

commands.returns: { dry_run: bool, readonly_roots: [string], readonly_roots_explicit: bool, planned_count: int, renamed_count: int, failed_count: int, skipped_count: int, batch_api_result: bool|null, would_block_on_modal: bool, cdo_references: [object], soft_scan_is_approximate: bool, referencer_packages_dirty: [object], results: [object] }

commands.name: rename_static_mesh_socket
commands.description: Rename an existing static mesh socket (guards against name collisions; idempotent).

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset.

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Current name of the socket to rename.

params.name: new_name
params.description: New name for the socket.

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, old_name, new_name, renamed, socket_count, saved }

commands.name: resolve_asset_by_name
commands.description: Resolve an exact asset name (or path) to EVERY matching asset and report `match_count` + `unambiguous`, instead of silently picking the first one the way get_asset_by_name, get_blueprint_parent, get_graph_nodes and the rest of the by-name tools do. Run this FIRST whenever you are about to address an asset by bare name: a project can have hundreds of duplicate names (the same name in a vendored pack and in the game's own folders, plus dated backup copies), and `unambiguous:false` is the only warning you will get before another tool hands you a stale backup's contents as if they were the real asset. From there, pass the full path everywhere. match_count:0 with success:true is a valid, informative answer -- it means "no asset with this exact name", which is a real measurement of non-existence (unlike find_assets_by_name's count:0, which can just mean the pattern had a wildcard in it).

params.name: asset_name
params.description: EXACT bare asset name or full package/asset path. This is an equality test, not a substring one -- use find_assets_by_name when you only know part of the name.

params.name: class_filter
params.description: Optional class short name or /Script path (e.g. "Blueprint", "DataTable") to constrain the match; matches subclasses too

params.name: search_root
params.description: Root package path for the fallback scan used when asset_name is not an exact package-name hit; defaults to "/Game", so an asset under /Engine or a plugin mount needs its root passed here explicitly

commands.returns: { asset_name: string, search_root: string, class_filter: string, match_count: int, unambiguous: bool, matches: [{ path, package, class }] }

commands.name: scan_uasset_references
commands.description: Lightweight BINARY scan of a .uasset/.umap on disk (NO editor load): tokenizes the raw package bytes and reports the referenced-asset-path tokens (/Game//Engine//Script) plus, optionally, tokens matching a regex `pattern`. A quick way to compare copies of one asset: an incomplete (stub) copy shows far fewer reference tokens than the complete one. Accepts a disk path OR a /Game|/Engine mount path.

params.name: package_file
params.description: Absolute .uasset/.umap path on disk, or a /Game|/Engine mount path.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Optional regex (ECMAScript); tokens containing a match are counted in the 'matches' fields.

commands.returns: { package_file: string, resolved_path: string, exists: bool, file_size_bytes: number, modified: string, pattern: string, ref_path_unique: int, ref_path_occurrences: number, ref_paths: [{token, count}], match_unique: int, match_occurrences: number, matches: [{token, count}] }

commands.name: set_asset_metadata_tag
commands.description: Sets (or overwrites) a string metadata tag on an asset and saves it.  The asset is loaded, UEditorAssetLibrary::SetMetadataTag is applied, the owning package is saved, and the value is read back to verify. Inverse: remove_asset_metadata_tag.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the asset (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/M_Example").

params.name: key
params.description: Metadata tag name (FName), e.g. "Author".

params.name: value
params.description: String value to associate with the tag.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, key: string, value: string, read_back: string, tag_set: bool, verified: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_static_mesh_collision_complexity
commands.description: Set the collision complexity (BodySetup CollisionTraceFlag) of a UStaticMesh asset, creating its BodySetup when missing, then save it; a failed save is an error. An unrecognized complexity silently becomes default, so check collision_complexity, which is read back.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset.

params.name: complexity
params.description: One of "default", "simple_and_complex", "simple_as_complex", "complex_as_simple", case-insensitive; any other value is stored as default.

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, collision_complexity, saved }

commands.name: set_static_mesh_lightmap
commands.description: Sets the lightmap resolution and/or the lightmap UV channel index stored on a static mesh asset, in one undo step, then saves the asset; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. Only those two properties change: the mesh is not rebuilt and no lighting is rebuilt, so baked lighting picks the values up on the next build_lighting. The values are stored as given, without range checks, and read back into the reply; repeating a call with the same values saves again with the same result. Placed actors that override their own lightmap resolution keep their override. Passing neither value is an error and nothing changes. Read the current values with get_static_mesh_info; check which UV channels exist, and which one is the lightmap, with list_uv_channels and its layout with get_uv_health_report.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Package or object path of the UStaticMesh asset (e.g. "/Game/Props/SM_Crate").

params.name: lightmap_resolution
params.description: Optional lightmap texture size in texels per side, a whole number such as 64, 128 or 256 (powers of two are the usual choice); omitted, it stays as it is.

params.name: lightmap_coordinate_index
params.description: Optional 0-based UV channel the lightmap uses (typically 1); it should name a channel the mesh has (list_uv_channels), since it is not checked. Omitted, it stays as it is.

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, lightmap_resolution, lightmap_coordinate_index, applied_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_static_mesh_material_slot
commands.description: Assign a material to one existing material slot of a UStaticMesh asset, picked by zero-based material_index, then save the mesh. This edits the asset, so every component without its own override of that slot shows the new material. The slot array never grows: an index outside the existing slots is an error, as is a mesh or material path that does not load. No undo transaction and no same-material check, so a repeat call writes and saves the slot again (idempotent). A failed save -- refused while PIE runs, under a read-only root, or a read-only file -- is an error, with the material already set in memory. material_path is read back. Slots: get_static_mesh_info; per-actor override: set_actor_material; skeletal meshes: set_skeletal_mesh_material_slot; a Blueprint component template: apply_material_to_blueprint.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset.

params.name: material_index
params.description: Zero-based index of an existing material slot.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Content path to the UMaterialInterface to assign.

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, material_index, material_path, saved }

commands.name: set_static_mesh_nanite
commands.description: Set the Nanite settings of a UStaticMesh asset through the StaticMeshEditor subsystem, which rebuilds the mesh, then save it; a failed save is an error. Both fields are always written: omitting enabled disables Nanite and omitting keep_percent_triangles resets it to 1.0. Returns nanite_enabled read back.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset.

params.name: enabled
params.description: true enables Nanite, false disables it; default false, so leaving it out disables Nanite.

params.name: keep_percent_triangles
params.description: Fraction of the source triangles Nanite keeps, 1.0 keeps them all (default 1.0, written even when omitted).

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, nanite_enabled, saved }

commands.name: set_static_mesh_socket_transform
