commands.description: Move, rotate or scale an existing socket of a UStaticMesh asset relative to the mesh, writing only the fields given (the others keep their value), in one undo step (undo restores the old transform), then save the mesh. The reply reads back the socket's whole transform. Use it to adjust a socket that add_static_mesh_socket created; to rename one use rename_static_mesh_socket, to delete one remove_static_mesh_socket, to see every socket get_static_mesh_info; skeletal mesh sockets have their own tools. A socket_name the mesh does not have is not an error: updated is false and nothing is touched or saved. A mesh that does not load, or a location, rotation or scale that is not three numbers, is an error before anything changes; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) is an error too, with the new transform already on the mesh in memory. The same values again rewrite them and save.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Package or object path of the UStaticMesh, e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Crate".

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Name of the existing socket, compared as an FName (case-insensitive), as get_static_mesh_info lists it.

params.name: location
params.description: New relative location [x, y, z] in cm from the mesh origin, e.g. [0, 0, 50] (optional).

params.name: rotation
params.description: New relative rotation [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees, e.g. [0, 90, 0] (optional).

params.name: scale
params.description: New relative scale [x, y, z] as multipliers, e.g. [1, 1, 1] (optional).

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, socket_name, updated, location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}, saved }

commands.name: set_texture_settings
commands.description: Sets the given sRGB, compression, LOD group and sampler/LOD fields (address X/Y, filter, mip-gen settings, LOD bias, max size, flip-green) of a UTexture2D asset, rebuilds its resource when one changed (PostEditChange + UpdateResource, no shader recompile) and saves it in every case, returning every setting read back. An unknown compression or LOD group name is still applied, as TC_Default or TEXTUREGROUP_World, with a compression_warning or lod_group_warning; an unknown address, filter or mip-gen name is skipped with an address_x_warning, address_y_warning, filter_warning or mip_gen_settings_warning. Enum params accept the name with or without its prefix.

params.name: texture_path
params.description: Asset path of the texture to modify

params.name: srgb
params.description: True treats the texture as sRGB color, false as linear data such as normal or mask maps; omit to keep the current value

params.name: compression_settings
params.description: TextureCompressionSettings name with or without the TC_ prefix, e.g. "Default", "Normalmap", "Masks", "VectorDisplacementmap", "BC7", "HDR"; omit to keep the current value

params.name: lod_group
params.description: TextureGroup name with or without the TEXTUREGROUP_ prefix, e.g. "World", "UI", "Character", "Effects"; omit to keep the current value

params.name: address_x
params.description: Optional TextureAddress name, with or without TA_: Wrap, Clamp or Mirror; omit to keep the current value

params.name: address_y
params.description: Optional TextureAddress name, with or without TA_: Wrap, Clamp or Mirror; omit to keep the current value

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional TextureFilter name, with or without TF_: Nearest, Bilinear, Trilinear or Default; omit to keep the current value

params.name: mip_gen_settings
params.description: Optional TextureMipGenSettings name, with or without TMGS_: FromTextureGroup, SimpleAverage, NoMipmaps, LeaveExistingMips, Sharpen0..10, Blur1..5, Unfiltered, Angular; omit to keep the current value

params.name: lod_bias
params.description: Optional int LOD bias; omit to keep the current value

params.name: max_texture_size
params.description: Optional int max texture size (0 = no limit, negatives clamp to 0); omit to keep the current value

params.name: flip_green
params.description: Optional bool, flips the green channel; omit to keep the current value

commands.returns: { texture_name: string, asset_path: string, changed: bool, saved: bool, width: int, height: int, format: string, srgb: bool, compression: string, lod_group: string, address_x: string, address_y: string, filter: string, mip_gen_settings: string, lod_bias: int, max_texture_size: int, flip_green: bool, has_source: bool, source_width?: int, source_height?: int, source_format?: string, compression_warning?: string, lod_group_warning?: string, address_x_warning?: string, address_y_warning?: string, filter_warning?: string, mip_gen_settings_warning?: string, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_bus_to_mix
commands.description: Adds a USoundControlBus to a USoundControlBusMix asset as a new stage whose target value is default_value, and saves the mix. A bus already in the mix is left unchanged (already_in_mix true, not saved); edit a stage with set_control_bus_mix_stage_value. Returns mix_path, bus_path, bus_count, added, saved.

params.name: mix_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus

params.name: default_value
params.description: Target value for the new mix stage (default 1.0)

commands.returns: { mix_path, bus_path, bus_count, added, already_in_mix, saved, default_value }

commands.name: add_metasound_graph_input
commands.description: Add a graph input of data_type (default Float) to an existing MetaSound Source through the MetaSound builder, inside an undo transaction, then save the asset. Optionally bakes a typed default into the new input; give at most one of default_value, int_value, bool_value or string_value (bool_value wins, then int_value, string_value, default_value). An unregistered data_type or a source that does not load is an error, and so is a default of the wrong JSON type or one data_type takes no literal of, with nothing written. A name already used by an input is left untouched: with the same data_type the call succeeds with added=false and already_exists=true, saves nothing and does not apply a supplied default (note says so; use set_metasound_graph_input_default); with another data_type it is an error. success is false, with save_error, when the save fails (during PIE, for one). Inverse: remove_metasound_graph_input.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source, as a package path like "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example" or an object path like "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example.MS_Example"

params.name: input_name
params.description: Name of the graph input node to add.

params.name: data_type
params.description: Frontend data type: "Float", "Int32", "Bool", "String", "Audio", "Trigger" (optional, default "Float")

params.name: default_value
params.description: Float default baked into the literal, a JSON number (optional)

params.name: int_value
params.description: Int32 default baked into the literal, a whole JSON number (optional, mutually exclusive with other defaults)

params.name: bool_value
params.description: Bool default baked into the literal, JSON true or false (optional, mutually exclusive with other defaults)

params.name: string_value
params.description: String default baked into the literal, a JSON string (optional, mutually exclusive with other defaults)

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, input_name: string, data_type: string, added: bool, already_exists?: bool, has_default: bool, note?: string, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: add_metasound_graph_output
commands.description: Add a graph output of data_type (default Audio; others include Float, Int32, Bool, String and Trigger) to an existing MetaSound Source through the MetaSound builder, inside an undo transaction, then save the asset. An unregistered data_type or a source that does not load is an error. A name already used by an output is left untouched: with the same data_type the call succeeds with added=false and already_exists=true and saves nothing; with another data_type it is an error. success is false, with save_error, when the save fails (during PIE, for one). Inverse: remove_metasound_graph_output.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: output_name
params.description: Name of the graph output node to add.

params.name: data_type
params.description: Frontend data type for the output node (optional, default "Audio")

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, output_name: string, data_type: string, added: bool, already_exists?: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: add_metasound_interface
commands.description: Adds a registered interface to an existing MetaSound Source's graph.  Obtains a builder for the saved asset via the editor subsystem's FindOrBeginBuilding (the reliable headless path), validates the interface via IsInterfaceRegistered, then calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::AddInterface (which adds the interface's input/output nodes). The asset is saved after the edit. Inverse: remove_metasound_interface.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source (e.g. "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example" or fully-qualified ".MS_Example").

params.name: interface_name
params.description: Name of a registered MetaSound interface to add (required)

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_kind: string, interface_name: string, added: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: add_metasound_node
commands.description: Add a real process node to a MetaSound Source graph by its registered class name (e.g. UE/Sine/Audio).  Unlike add_metasound_graph_input (which adds a graph input node), this instantiates a DSP node so you can author a real signal patch headless. Returns the node's GUID (node_id) and its enumerated input/output pins (name + data_type) for follow-up set/connect calls. The asset is saved. NOT idempotent: each call adds a new node instance (delete + recreate the source for a clean run). Wire it with connect_metasound_nodes, connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node or connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output; edges: list_metasound_connections.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: class_namespace
params.description: Registered node class namespace, e.g. "UE".

params.name: class_name
params.description: Registered node class name, e.g. "Sine".

params.name: class_variant
params.description: Optional class variant, e.g. "Audio" (omit for the default/no-variant class).

params.name: major_version
params.description: Optional major version (default 1).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_id: string, class_namespace: string, class_name: string, class_variant: string, inputs: [{name,data_type}], outputs: [{name,data_type}], added: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: add_modulation_input_to_patch
commands.description: Add a control bus as an input of a sound modulation patch asset, so the patch's output follows that bus, then save the patch. Use it after create_sound_modulation_patch and create_control_bus, which make the two assets; see the inputs with get_sound_modulation_patch_info, take one out with remove_modulation_input_from_patch, and set what the patch drives with set_modulation_patch_output_parameter. Idempotent per bus: a bus whose asset name is already an input is not added again (added false, already_present true) and nothing is saved. A patch or bus path that does not load is an error and nothing changes. One undo step that removes the input again; a failed save answers success false with the change kept in memory.

params.name: patch_path
params.description: Asset path of the sound modulation patch, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/SMP_Ducking", as create_sound_modulation_patch returns it.

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path of the control bus to add, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/CB_Music", as create_control_bus returns it.

params.name: input_name
params.description: Ignored: the engine input struct has no name field, so the value is only written to the log (default empty)

commands.returns: { patch_path, bus_path, input_count, added, already_present, saved }

commands.name: add_sound_cue_node
commands.description: Append a new node of node_type to the AllNodes of a USoundCue asset, in one undo step, and save the cue; node_id is its index there, the id the other sound cue tools take. node_type is matched without case, and an unknown type or a cue that does not load is an error. The node starts unconnected and is not the cue output: wire it with connect_sound_cue_nodes and make the root with set_sound_cue_first_node. For a WavePlayer, sound_wave_path sets its wave; a wave that does not load is not an error (sound_wave_set=false), and other types ignore it. Each call adds another node (not idempotent). A failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error. Node settings: set_sound_cue_node_properties; read back: get_sound_cue_graph; a new cue: create_sound_cue. Inverse: remove_sound_cue_node.

params.name: cue_path
params.description: Full asset path of the cue, e.g. /Game/SoundCues/SC_Foo

params.name: node_type
params.description: One of WavePlayer|Mixer|Random|Looping|Modulator|Delay|Concatenator|Attenuation|Branch|DistanceCrossFade|Doppler|Enveloper|GroupControl|ModulatorContinuous|Oscillator|ParamCrossFade|QualityLevel|SoundClass|Switch|WaveParam (matched without case)

params.name: sound_wave_path
params.description: Optional USoundWave path for WavePlayer nodes only; one that does not load leaves the node without a wave (sound_wave_set false)

commands.returns: { cue_path: string, node_id: int, node_type: string, node_class: string, max_child_nodes: int, child_count: int, sound_wave_set: bool, sound_wave_path: string, node_count: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: add_soundfield_effect_to_submix
commands.description: Append a new effect of a concrete USoundfieldEffectBase class to a USoundfieldSubmix effect chain and save it; an addition succeeds only when the submix reaches disk. A class already in the chain is skipped (added false, already_present true, not saved). When no concrete subclass is loaded (stock UE 5.8 ships none) nothing changes and the call fails, with added false and a note.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Full path to the USoundfieldSubmix (required).

params.name: effect_class_name
params.description: Full class path of a concrete USoundfieldEffectBase subclass, e.g. "/Script/MyAudioPlugin.MySoundfieldEffect"; it is looked up with no outer, so a bare class name does not resolve

commands.returns: { submix_path, effect_path, effect_class, chain_length, added, already_present, saved, note? }

commands.name: add_submix_effect_to_chain
commands.description: Append one effect preset to the end of a USoundSubmix's effect chain and save the submix. effect_preset_path wins: that existing USoundEffectSubmixPreset asset is appended by reference. Otherwise a new preset of effect_preset_class, or, when neither is given, of a concrete class found by reflection (SubmixEffectDynamicsProcessorPreset when it is loaded), is created inside the submix's own package under a unique <Submix>_Effect name; resolved_from says which of the three ran. Every call appends another entry, duplicates included. A submix or preset that does not load, or a class that is not a concrete preset subclass, is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Read the chain with get_submix_effect_chain and tune an entry with set_submix_effect_settings; a soundfield submix takes add_soundfield_effect_to_submix. Inverse: remove_submix_effect_from_chain.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundSubmix

params.name: effect_preset_path
params.description: Optional existing USoundEffectSubmixPreset asset to append by reference; wins over effect_preset_class

params.name: effect_preset_class
params.description: Optional concrete USoundEffectSubmixPreset subclass (short name or path) to instantiate in the submix's package; with neither preset param a class is picked by reflection

commands.returns: { submix_path: string, effect_name: string, effect_class: string, resolved_from: string, effect_added: bool, chain_length: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_subtitle_cue
commands.description: Append one cue (text, start_offset, duration, duration_type, subtitle_type, priority, comment) to the Subtitles list of a USubtitleAssetUserData asset loaded by content path, in one undo step, then save it. Idempotent: a cue equal to it in text, duration_type, duration, start_offset, priority and subtitle_type -- comment is not compared -- is a success with already_existed=true, saved=false and that cue's cue_index, nothing added or saved. Defaults: start_offset 0, duration 3 s, duration_type use_duration_property, subtitle_type subtitle, priority 1. An unknown duration_type or subtitle_type, or an asset that does not load, is an error; so is a failed save, after which the cue is already in memory. Edit a cue (text or timing) with set_subtitle_cue and list them with list_subtitle_cues; the inverse is remove_subtitle_cue. Create the asset with create_subtitles_asset.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Content path of the USubtitleAssetUserData asset.

params.name: text
params.description: The subtitle text (required).

params.name: start_offset
params.description: Initial delay in seconds before the subtitle is visible (default 0).

params.name: duration
params.description: Display duration in seconds (default 3).

params.name: duration_type
params.description: "use_sound_duration" or "use_duration_property" (default "use_duration_property").

params.name: subtitle_type
params.description: "subtitle", "closed_caption", or "audio_description" (default "subtitle").

params.name: priority
params.description: Subtitle priority; higher values play instead of lower (default 1).

params.name: comment
params.description: Editor-only author comment (default "").

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, cue_index: int, text: string, success: bool, already_existed: bool, cue_count: int, saved: bool, message: string? }

commands.name: connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node
commands.description: Wire the graph input graph_input_name of a MetaSound Source to the input to_input_name of node to_node_id, in one undo step, then save the asset -- how a parameter (a Float input "Frequency") drives a node pin. Same rules as connect_metasound_nodes: matching data types, an input already fed is re-fed (replaced=true), the same edge already there changes nothing (already_connected=true), and an unknown graph input, node or pin is an error with nothing changed. Read back: list_metasound_connections; inverse: disconnect_metasound_nodes on the node input. Graph input to graph output: connect_metasound_graph_input_to_output.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: graph_input_name
params.description: Name of the graph input (get_metasound_info lists them).

params.name: to_node_id
params.description: GUID of the node whose input receives the edge.

params.name: to_input_name
params.description: Name of that node's input pin.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, graph_input_name: string, to_node_id: string, to_input_name: string, from_data_type: string, to_data_type: string, connected: bool, already_connected: bool, replaced: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: connect_metasound_graph_input_to_output
commands.description: Connects a graph input node's output to a graph output node's input.  Resolves the source handle from a graph INPUT node by name (FindGraphInputNode -> the input node's output handle) and the destination handle from a graph OUTPUT node by name (FindGraphOutputNode -> the output node's input handle), then calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::ConnectNodes and verifies via NodesAreConnected. The connection is real where the two data types match (e.g. a Float graph input connected to a Float graph output). Saves the asset. Graph input to a node: connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node; edges: list_metasound_connections.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: from_node_output_name
params.description: Name of the graph INPUT to use as the connection source.

params.name: to_node_input_name
params.description: Name of the graph OUTPUT to use as the connection target.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, from_node_output_name: string, to_node_input_name: string, from_data_type: string, to_data_type: string, connected: bool, result: string, verified: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output
commands.description: Connect a concrete node's output pin to a named graph output, completing a signal patch (e.g. Sine.Audio -> the source's audio output).  Uses ConnectNodeOutputToGraphOutput (idempotent: replaces any existing edge). Reports the honest EMetaSoundBuilderResult. Node to node: connect_metasound_nodes; edges: list_metasound_connections.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: node_id
params.description: GUID of the source node (from add_metasound_node).

params.name: node_output_name
params.description: Name of the node's output pin (e.g. "Audio").

params.name: graph_output_name
params.description: Name of the target graph output (discover via get_metasound_info).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_id: string, node_output_name: string, graph_output_name: string, connected: bool, result: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: connect_metasound_nodes
commands.description: Wire the output from_output_name of node from_node_id to the input to_input_name of node to_node_id in a MetaSound Source graph, in one undo step, then save the asset -- the node-to-node edge a patch needs (Sine.Audio -> ADSR.In). Node ids come from add_metasound_node or list_metasound_nodes, pin names from their inputs/outputs. The two pins must carry the same data type. An input takes one edge, so an input already fed from elsewhere is re-fed (replaced=true); the same edge already there changes and saves nothing (already_connected=true). A bad id, an unknown pin or a type mismatch is an error and nothing changes. Read back: list_metasound_connections; inverse: disconnect_metasound_nodes. A graph input as the source: connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node; a graph output as the target: connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: from_node_id
params.description: GUID of the node whose output feeds the edge.

params.name: from_output_name
params.description: Name of that node's output pin (e.g. "Audio").

params.name: to_node_id
params.description: GUID of the node whose input receives the edge.

params.name: to_input_name
params.description: Name of that node's input pin (e.g. "In").

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, from_node_id: string, from_output_name: string, to_node_id: string, to_input_name: string, from_data_type: string, to_data_type: string, connected: bool, already_connected: bool, replaced: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: connect_sound_cue_nodes
commands.description: Link the node child_node_id into an input slot of the node parent_node_id in a USoundCue asset (ids from add_sound_cue_node or get_sound_cue_graph), in one undo step, then save the cue. With input_index that slot is overwritten even when it holds another child (missing slots up to it are added empty); without it the first empty slot is used, or a new one is appended. A cue that does not load, an id out of range, a parent that takes no children (a WavePlayer), an input_index outside [0, max_child_nodes), a full parent, or a cycle (a node into itself or into a node feeding it) is an error, with nothing changed. Duplicate links are allowed: a repeat without input_index adds the child again. A failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error. Inverse: disconnect_sound_cue_nodes; cue output: set_sound_cue_first_node; read back: get_sound_cue_graph.

params.name: cue_path
params.description: Full asset path of the cue

params.name: parent_node_id
params.description: node_id of the upstream node with inputs (its index in the cue AllNodes)

params.name: child_node_id
params.description: node_id of the node to feed into the parent

params.name: input_index
params.description: Optional zero-based target slot; an occupied slot is overwritten. Omitted: the first empty slot, else a new slot appended

commands.returns: { cue_path: string, parent_node_id: int, child_node_id: int, input_index: int, parent_class: string, child_class: string, parent_child_count: int, connected: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_audio_bus
commands.description: Creates a UAudioBus asset at package_path/name and saves it, or loads the one already there (already_exists true) and saves it again; another asset class at that path is an error. channels, when given, sets the channel layout, overwriting an existing bus's layout; when omitted a new bus gets Stereo and an existing one keeps its own. An invalid channels value is refused before any asset is created or loaded. Change the layout later with set_audio_bus_channels and read it with get_audio_bus; create_sound_source_bus makes a source bus that plays this bus's audio.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new Audio Bus asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio

params.name: channels
params.description: EAudioBusChannels: 'Mono' | 'Stereo' (default) | 'Quad' | 'FiveDotOne' | 'SevenDotOne'. The default applies to a new bus only.

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, channels: string, channels_int: int, num_channels: int, applied_channels: bool (this call wrote the layout: channels given, or the Stereo default on a new bus), created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_control_bus
commands.description: Creates a USoundControlBus asset at package_path/bus_name, or loads the one already there, and saves it. initial_value is only echoed back as value, never written to the bus; push a runtime value with set_control_bus_value. Returns bus_path, default_value, created, already_existed, saved.

params.name: bus_name
params.description: Name of the control bus (e.g. "Bus_Volume")

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP)

params.name: initial_value
params.description: Number echoed back as value in the reply; it is not stored on the bus (default 1.0)

commands.returns: { bus_path, bus_name, value, default_value, created, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_control_bus_mix
commands.description: Creates a USoundControlBusMix asset at package_path/mix_name, or loads the one already there, and saves it. A new mix has no stages; add buses with add_bus_to_mix. Returns mix_path, mix_name, bus_count (its stage count), created, saved.

params.name: mix_name
params.description: Name of the control bus mix asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP)

commands.returns: { mix_path, mix_name, bus_count, created, saved }

commands.name: create_dialogue_voice
commands.description: Create a UDialogueVoice asset (idempotent). Populate Gender/Plurality afterwards via set_properties on object_path.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new DialogueVoice asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, object_path: string, asset_class: string, gender: string, plurality: string, already_existed: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_dialogue_wave
commands.description: Create a UDialogueWave asset (idempotent). Populate ContextMappings afterwards via set_properties on object_path.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new DialogueWave asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, object_path: string, asset_class: string, context_mapping_count: int, already_existed: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_metasound_preset
commands.description: Creates a MetaSound preset from an existing source or patch asset.  Uses UMetaSoundBuilderSubsystem::CreateSourcePresetBuilder (or CreatePatchPresetBuilder) to create a transient preset builder referencing the source, then BuildToAsset to persist it as a new /Game asset. A preset of that type already at the path is returned unchanged with already_exists=true, saved=false and preset_type read from its class, nothing saved; an asset of another class there (a MetaSound of the other type included) is an error and nothing is created.

params.name: preset_name
params.description: Name of the new MetaSound preset asset.

params.name: source_asset_path
params.description: Content path of the existing MetaSound source/patch to use as the preset's template.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination /Game folder (default /Game/MetaSounds).

params.name: preset_type
params.description: "source" (default) or "patch".

commands.returns: { preset_path: string, preset_type: string, success: bool, saved: bool, already_exists: bool, message: string? }

commands.name: create_metasound_source
commands.description: Create a UMetaSoundSource asset at package_path/name (default folder /Game/MetaSounds): a one-shot source graph pre-wired with the source interface (OnPlay input, OnFinished output, one audio output per channel), built by the MetaSound builder subsystem and written with BuildToAsset, then saved; no dialog, no undo step. Idempotent: a MetaSound Source already there is returned unchanged with already_exists=true, created=false and saved=false, nothing saved. output_format is mono, stereo, quad, 5.1 or 7.1; anything else is an error and nothing is created. The reply's output_format is read from the source, also for an existing one, whose own format is reported and left as it is. An invalid package name or a failed build is an error; a failed save gives success false with save_error. Next: add_metasound_node, add_metasound_interface; inspect: get_metasound_info; inverse: delete_asset.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the MetaSound Source asset to create.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/MetaSounds")

params.name: output_format
params.description: Output audio format: "mono", "stereo", "quad", "5.1", or "7.1" (optional, default "mono")

commands.returns: { source_name: string, asset_path: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, output_format: string, class_name: string, input_count: number, output_count: number, save_error: string?, message: string? }

commands.name: create_modulation_generator
commands.description: Creates a modulation generator asset of class LFO, ADEnvelope or EnvelopeFollower at generator_path (or package_path/generator_name), with engine default settings, and saves it; for an LFO it also writes the given waveform, frequency, amplitude, offset and phase (looping on), on a new LFO or overwriting those fields of an existing one. An existing generator with no LFO field given is returned untouched with its own class (not saved). LFO fields with another generator_class or on an existing generator of another class, and an unknown waveform, are errors. Returns generator_path, generator_name, generator_class, settings as stored, created, already_existed, updated, saved. Configure the other classes with set_modulation_generator_settings.

params.name: generator_class
params.description: Concrete class name (case-insensitive). One of: LFO, ADEnvelope, EnvelopeFollower

params.name: generator_path
params.description: Full asset path (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Gen_LFO). Optional when generator_name is given.

params.name: generator_name
params.description: Optional asset name, used with package_path when generator_path is absent.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Optional folder for generator_name (default /Game/MCP); ignored when generator_path is given.

params.name: waveform
params.description: Optional, LFO only: shape, case-insensitive: Sine, UpSaw, DownSaw, Square, Triangle, Exponential, Random (RandomSampleHold). Any other value is an error.

params.name: frequency
params.description: Optional, LFO only: frequency in Hz (engine default 1.0).

params.name: amplitude
params.description: Optional, LFO only: amplitude (engine default 1.0).

params.name: offset
params.description: Optional, LFO only: output offset (engine default 0.0).

params.name: phase
params.description: Optional, LFO only: starting phase (engine default 0.0).

commands.returns: { generator_path, generator_name, generator_class, settings: {...}, created, already_existed, updated, saved }

commands.name: create_modulation_parameter
commands.description: Create a sound modulation parameter asset of one concrete class at parameter_path, with the engine's default settings, then save it; there is no undo step. A parameter is what a modulation patch outputs to (set_modulation_patch_output_parameter), and its class sets the unit and mixing (Volume in decibels, Frequency in hertz...). Idempotent: when a modulation parameter already exists at that path it is returned untouched with its real class, parameter_class is not checked, nothing is saved and already_existed is true. An unknown class, a path that does not split into folder and name, or an asset of another type there is an error and nothing changes; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the asset only in memory. Tune it with set_modulation_parameter_settings and read it with get_modulation_parameter_info.

params.name: parameter_path
params.description: Full asset path, folder plus asset name, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/Param_Volume"; the last segment becomes the asset name and a missing folder is created.

params.name: parameter_class
params.description: Concrete class name (case-insensitive). One of: Volume, Frequency, LPFrequency, HPFrequency, Bipolar, Additive, Scaled; the engine spellings LPFFrequency and HPFFrequency are accepted too. Not checked when a parameter already exists at parameter_path.

commands.returns: { parameter_path, parameter_name, parameter_class, created, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_sound_attenuation
commands.description: Create a USoundAttenuation asset at package_path/name, or load the one already there, then force bAttenuate on, apply the optional falloff_distance and sphere radius, and save it (re-running edits the existing asset). Returns the values read back; set_properties edits every other field.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new Sound Attenuation asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio

params.name: falloff_distance
params.description: FalloffDistance in Unreal units (cm): how far beyond the inner shape the volume fades out. Unchanged when omitted.

params.name: radius
params.description: Inner sphere radius in Unreal units (cm); sets the shape to Sphere and AttenuationShapeExtents to (radius, 0, 0). Unchanged when omitted.

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, attenuate: bool, falloff_distance: number, radius: number, shape_extent_x: number, shape_extent_y: number, shape_extent_z: number, applied_falloff_distance: bool, applied_radius: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_sound_class
commands.description: Create a USoundClass asset at package_path/name (package_path defaults to /Game/Audio) and save it. A sound class already at that path is loaded instead (already_exists true, created false) and the volume and pitch you pass overwrite its values before it is saved again; omitted ones keep their current values, the engine defaults on a new class. Idempotent. The reply reads volume and pitch back from the asset, and applied_volume / applied_pitch say which were written. An invalid path, or an asset of another class there, is an error; a failed save (for example during PIE) makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Edit the other properties with set_properties, read them with get_sound_class_properties, and wire the hierarchy with set_sound_class_parent.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new Sound Class asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio

params.name: volume
params.description: Optional Volume multiplier on FSoundClassProperties; also written to a class that already exists, unchanged when omitted

params.name: pitch
params.description: Optional Pitch multiplier on FSoundClassProperties; also written to a class that already exists, unchanged when omitted

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, volume: number, pitch: number, applied_volume: bool, applied_pitch: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_sound_concurrency
commands.description: Creates a Sound Concurrency asset (USoundConcurrency, the rule that caps how many sounds of a group play at once) at package_path/name, or loads the one already there instead of making a duplicate (created and already_exists say which), then saves it; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. With max_count it also sets MaxCount, which on an existing asset overwrites the old value, as one undo step; without it an existing asset is left as it was. Idempotent: the same call again gives the same asset and value. An invalid path, or an asset of another class at that path, is an error. The other concurrency settings (resolution rule, volume scaling, retrigger time) are edited with set_properties on the asset_path this returns, and read with get_properties; sibling audio assets come from create_sound_class, create_sound_attenuation and create_sound_mix.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name of the Sound Concurrency, without a folder (e.g. "SCon_Footsteps").

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Concurrency"; defaults to /Game/Audio.

params.name: max_count
params.description: Optional whole number: most sounds of this group that play at once (MaxCount); values below 1 become 1 and fractions are truncated. Unchanged when omitted.

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, max_count: int, applied_max_count: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_sound_cue
commands.description: Create an empty USoundCue asset (no nodes and no first node, so it plays nothing yet) at package_path/name and save it. Idempotent: a sound cue already at that path is returned unchanged with created=false and already_existed=true, and nothing is saved; an asset of another class there is an error and nothing is written. Not an undo step. Build the graph next with add_sound_cue_node, connect_sound_cue_nodes and set_sound_cue_first_node, and read it back with get_sound_cue_graph; cue_path is the path those tools take. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and the new cue left in memory.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name, e.g. 'SC_Footsteps'; package_path/name must form a valid long package name.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder as a long package path, e.g. '/Game/Audio/Cues' (default /Game/SoundCues); trailing slashes are ignored.

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, cue_path: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, node_count: int, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: create_sound_mix
commands.description: Create a USoundMix asset at package_path/name (package_path defaults to /Game/Audio) and save it; a sound mix already there is loaded instead (already_exists true) and the eq_enabled and duration you pass overwrite its values before it is saved. Omitted fields keep their current values; the reply reads eq_enabled and duration back from the asset. An invalid path, or an asset of another class there, is an error; a failed save is an error with the change kept in memory. Idempotent. Add per-class volume and pitch adjusters with set_sound_mix_class_override; create the classes with create_sound_class.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new Sound Mix asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio

params.name: eq_enabled
params.description: Optional bool, sets USoundMix::bApplyEQ (whether to apply the EQ effect). Left at the asset default when absent.

params.name: duration
params.description: Optional float, sets USoundMix::Duration in seconds (negative means applied until another mix is set). Left at the asset default when absent.

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, eq_enabled: bool, duration: number, applied_eq_enabled: bool, applied_duration: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_sound_modulation_patch
commands.description: Create an empty sound modulation patch asset at package_path/patch_name (no inputs, no output parameter, bypassed with bBypass true), then save it; there is no undo step. A patch combines control buses into the value of one output parameter; for a single bus use create_control_bus, for a time-varying source create_modulation_generator. Idempotent: a patch already at that path is returned untouched as it stands, nothing is saved and already_existed is true. An invalid path, or an asset of another type at it, is an error and nothing changes; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the asset only in memory. Then add buses with add_modulation_input_to_patch, set the output with set_modulation_patch_output_parameter (a parameter from create_modulation_parameter), turn bypass off with set_modulation_patch_bypass, and read it back with get_sound_modulation_patch_info.

params.name: patch_name
params.description: Asset name of the patch without its folder, e.g. "Patch_Volume"; appended to package_path.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod" (default /Game/MCP); created when missing.

commands.returns: { patch_path, patch_name, bBypass, input_count, output_parameter_path, created, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_sound_source_bus
commands.description: Creates a USoundSourceBus asset at package_path/name, or loads the one already there, writes its routing fields and saves it; another asset class at the path is an error. source_bus_channels and duration, when omitted, take the defaults (Stereo, 1.0 s) on a new asset and keep their value on an existing one, whose fields the given values overwrite. Every value is validated before any asset is created or loaded, so an invalid one leaves nothing behind. audio_bus_path, when given, must load as a UAudioBus and becomes the bus whose audio this source bus plays; when omitted that field is left as is. Edit later with set_sound_source_bus_audio_bus or set_sound_source_bus_send_info; read with get_sound_source_bus.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new Sound Source Bus asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio

params.name: source_bus_channels
params.description: ESourceBusChannels: 'Mono' | 'Stereo' (default). USoundSourceBus inherits only Mono/Stereo. The default applies to a new asset only.

params.name: duration
params.description: Duration in seconds, at least 0 (0.0 means indefinite); a negative value is an error. Default 1.0 on a new asset only.

params.name: audio_bus_path
params.description: Optional full content path of a UAudioBus to assign as the AudioBus return.

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, source_bus_channels: string, duration: float, audio_bus_path: string, audio_bus_class: string, applied_channels: bool, applied_duration: bool (each true when this call wrote the field: given, or the default on a new asset), applied_audio_bus: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_sound_submix
commands.description: Create an empty USoundSubmix asset at package_path/name, or load the one already there, and save it. Returns asset_path, created, already_exists and saved; add effects with add_submix_effect_to_chain and read them with get_submix_effect_chain.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new Sound Submix asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_soundfield_submix
commands.description: Create a USoundfieldSubmix asset at submix_path and save it, with its default encoding format and an empty effect chain; a new one succeeds only when it reaches disk. An existing one there is returned unchanged and not re-saved (already_existed true, saved false). Returns soundfield_encoding_format, effect_chain_length and saved; inspect it with get_soundfield_submix_info.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Full asset path like "/Game/Audio/MySFSubmix" (required).

commands.returns: { submix_path, asset_path, soundfield_encoding_format, encoding_settings_class, created, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_subtitles_asset
commands.description: Create a USubtitleAssetUserData asset -- the engine's subtitle authoring asset, a list of timed cues -- at package_path/name (default folder /Game/MCP), register it and save it; no undo step. Idempotent: a subtitles asset already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true, saved=false, a message and its cue_count, nothing saved. An invalid package name, or a name taken by an asset of another class, is an error, and so is a failed save of the new asset -- refused while PIE runs, under a read-only root, or a read-only file -- which leaves it unsaved in memory. Fill it with add_subtitle_cue and read it with list_subtitle_cues; delete it with delete_asset.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new subtitles asset.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination /Game folder (default /Game/MCP).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, success: bool, already_existed: bool, cue_count: int, saved: bool, message: string? }

commands.name: disconnect_metasound_graph_input_from_output
commands.description: Disconnects a graph input node's output from a graph output node's input (inverse of connect_metasound_graph_input_to_output).  Resolves the source handle from a graph INPUT node by name (FindGraphInputNode -> the input node's output handle) and the destination handle from a graph OUTPUT node by name (FindGraphOutputNode -> the output node's input handle), then queries NodesAreConnected first: if the edge is already absent it returns already_disconnected without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::DisconnectNodes and reports the result. Saves the asset.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: from_node_output_name
params.description: Name of the graph INPUT whose output is the connection source.

params.name: to_node_input_name
params.description: Name of the graph OUTPUT whose input is the connection target.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, from_node_output_name: string, to_node_input_name: string, from_data_type: string, to_data_type: string, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, result: string, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: disconnect_metasound_node_from_graph_output
commands.description: Disconnects whatever node output currently drives a named graph output, clearing the edge (inverse of connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output).  Resolves the graph output node's input handle by name (FindGraphOutputNode) and queries NodeInputIsConnected first: if the input is already unconnected it returns already_disconnected without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::DisconnectNodeInput and reports the result. Saves the asset.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: graph_output_name
params.description: Name of the target graph output to disconnect (discover via get_metasound_info).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, graph_output_name: string, data_type: string, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, result: string, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: disconnect_metasound_nodes
commands.description: Drop the edge that feeds the input to_input_name of node to_node_id in a MetaSound Source graph, whatever drives it -- another node's output or a graph input -- in one undo step, then save the asset. Inverse of connect_metasound_nodes and connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node: an input takes one edge, so the input names it. The reply says which output fed it (from_node_id, from_output_name) and re-reads the input. An input with no edge is an honest no-op (disconnected=false, already_disconnected=true, nothing saved); a bad node id or an unknown pin is an error. Read first: list_metasound_connections; a graph output's edge: disconnect_metasound_node_from_graph_output.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: to_node_id
params.description: GUID of the node whose input loses its edge.

params.name: to_input_name
params.description: Name of that node's input pin.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, to_node_id: string, to_input_name: string, from_node_id: string?, from_node_name: string?, from_output_name: string?, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: disconnect_sound_cue_nodes
commands.description: Unwires one input of a node in a USoundCue asset: the parent's input slot, picked by the child wired into it or by its index, is emptied, in one undo step, then the cue is saved; a failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error. Inverse of connect_sound_cue_nodes. The slot itself is kept (empty, -1 in get_sound_cue_graph) so other input indexes do not shift, and the child node stays in the cue: remove_sound_cue_node deletes a node. A slot that is already empty or out of range, or a child not wired into the parent, succeeds with already_disconnected true and nothing changed or saved. A cue that does not load, a node id out of range, or neither child_node_id nor input_index is an error. Read ids and wiring first with get_sound_cue_graph; the cue's output node is set with set_sound_cue_first_node.

params.name: cue_path
params.description: Object or package path of the Sound Cue asset (e.g. "/Game/Audio/SC_Footsteps").

params.name: parent_node_id
params.description: node_id (index in the cue's AllNodes, as get_sound_cue_graph lists it) of the node whose input slot is emptied.

params.name: child_node_id
params.description: Optional node_id of the wired child; the first slot of the parent holding it is emptied. Wins over input_index when both are given.

params.name: input_index
params.description: Optional 0-based input slot of the parent to empty directly (its position in that node's child_ids); supply this OR child_node_id.

commands.returns: { cue_path: string, parent_node_id: int, child_node_id: int, input_index: int, parent_class: string, child_class: string, parent_child_count: int, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: get_audio_bus
commands.description: Read the channel layout of a UAudioBus asset: channels (Mono, Stereo, Quad, FivePointOne or SevenPointOne), channels_int and num_channels. Read-only. is_active is always false because no audio device is queried. Change the layout with set_audio_bus_channels.

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAudioBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/AB_Music".

commands.returns: { bus_path: string, asset_class: string, channels: string, channels_int: int, num_channels: int, is_active: bool (always false: headless — no audio device) }

commands.name: get_audio_component_properties
commands.description: Read an editor-level audio component by object name: volume, pitch, active state, transform, sound and its duration, and the attenuation really applied (override, else asset, else sound). Use it for these derived values; get_component_properties reads raw UPROPERTYs. Every audio component of every actor is searched, the name compared without case. Component names are unique only per actor (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0), so a name that several actors carry is an error listing the owners unless actor_name (object name, not label) picks one; an actor_name that names no actor, or whose actor has no component of that name, is an error too. Read-only.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Object name of the audio component to query (e.g. "AudioComponent0"), compared without case against EVERY audio component of every actor in the editor world.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Optional object name (not label) of the actor that owns the component, compared without case. Needed when several actors own an audio component of that name (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0): without it that is an error listing the owners. An actor_name that names no actor, or whose actor has no such component, is an error.

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, audio_component_found: bool, audio_component_message: string, component_class: string, component_type: string, audio_volume: number, audio_pitch: number, audio_enabled: bool (IsActive), audio_auto_activate: bool, audio_mobility: string, audio_position: { x, y, z }, audio_rotation: { pitch, yaw, roll }, audio_scale: { x, y, z } (component world transform), audio_sound_name: string, audio_sound_class: string, audio_sound_duration: number, audio_sound_path: string ("None" with no sound), audio_sound_is_sound_wave: bool, audio_sound_is_sound_cue: bool, audio_3d_enabled: bool (bAllowSpatialization), audio_3d_attenuation_radius: number (shape extent X), audio_3d_attenuation_falloff: number (both 0 with no attenuation applied), audio_3d_attenuation_cone_angle: number, audio_3d_attenuation_cone_feather: number (cone shape only, else 0), audio_owner_name: string, audio_owner_class: string, audio_owner_path: string, audio_owner_position: { x, y, z }, audio_owner_rotation: { pitch, yaw, roll }, audio_level: string, audio_world: string }

commands.name: get_audio_settings
commands.description: Survey audio in the editor, every value read from the engine: a census of EVERY audio component of every actor in the editor world (even while PIE runs; an actor with several is counted once per component), each entry naming its owner and object path, with its volume, pitch and playing, looping and spatialized state, plus the counts and volume and pitch statistics; the main audio device's live state (audio_api is the module that created the device, then sample rate, buffer size, max channels, mixer and which audio plugins are on), all null with audio_device_note when there is no device (audio off: an editor started with -NoSound, or no device could be created); the audio quality level the engine applies (the user's quality level within the project's Audio settings levels); and the platform audio config the project sets (audio_platform_config, only the keys the config sets). Read-only; no parameters. audio_quality_score (the share of active components, null with none), the recommendations and the complexity score are heuristics. For other project audio settings use get_project_settings_value; for one component in depth, get_audio_component_properties.
commands.returns: { audio_settings_found: bool, audio_settings_message: string, world_name?: string, audio_component_count: int, active_audio_component_count: int, playing_audio_component_count: int, looping_audio_component_count: int, spatialized_audio_component_count: int, sound_wave_count: int, sound_cue_count: int, total_volume: number, average_volume: number, max_volume: number, min_volume: number, total_pitch: number, average_pitch: number, max_pitch: number, min_pitch: number, audio_component_details: [{ audio_component_name: string, audio_component_path: string, audio_owner_name: string, audio_component_class: string, audio_volume: number, audio_pitch: number, audio_enabled: bool, audio_playing: bool, audio_looping: bool, audio_spatialized: bool, audio_mobility: string, audio_sound_name: string, audio_sound_class: string, audio_sound_duration: number, audio_sound_is_sound_wave: bool, audio_sound_is_sound_cue: bool, audio_position: { x, y, z } }], engine_version: string, platform_name: string, platform_architecture: string, platform_os: string, audio_enabled: bool, audio_api: string|null, audio_mixer_loaded: bool|null, audio_max_channels: int|null, audio_sample_rate: number|null, audio_buffer_size: int|null, audio_num_buffers: int|null, audio_spatialization_plugin_enabled: bool|null, audio_reverb_plugin_enabled: bool|null, audio_occlusion_plugin_enabled: bool|null, audio_modulation_plugin_enabled: bool|null, audio_device_note?: string, audio_quality: string|null, audio_quality_level: int|null, audio_quality_max_channels: int|null, audio_quality_level_count: int, audio_platform_config: { section: string, sample_rate?: int, callback_buffer_frame_size?: int, num_buffers?: int, max_channels?: int, num_source_workers?: int }, audio_quality_score: number|null, audio_recommendations: [string], audio_complexity_score: number, audio_complexity_rating: string }

commands.name: get_control_bus_info
commands.description: Read a USoundControlBus asset and its live value in the editor world without changing anything. default_value is the bus default normalized value; current_value is what UAudioModulationStatics::GetModulatorValue returns for the bus in the editor world, and the engine answers 1.0 for a bus that is not active there, so 1.0 alone does not prove a mix is applied; with no editor world it equals default_value. subsystem_active says whether the editor world has an audio modulation manager. A bus that cannot be loaded is an error. Push a value with set_control_bus_value; mix stages: get_control_bus_mix_info; patches: get_sound_modulation_patch_info; parameters and generators: get_modulation_parameter_info, get_modulation_generator_info.

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Bus_Music.Bus_Music"

commands.returns: { bus_path, default_value, current_value, subsystem_active }

commands.name: get_control_bus_mix_info
commands.description: Reads the stages of a USoundControlBusMix asset without changing it. Returns mix_path, stage_count and stages, one per stage with bus_path (empty when the bus reference is cleared), target_value, attack_time and release_time. Edit a stage with set_control_bus_mix_stage_value.

params.name: mix_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix

commands.returns: { mix_path, stage_count, stages: [{ bus_path, target_value, attack_time, release_time }] }

commands.name: get_metasound_info
commands.description: Read the top-level metadata of a MetaSound Source asset (a preset included), loading it if needed: its class, the root graph class name, the graph inputs and outputs (name and type) with their counts, interface_count (the number of interfaces the document declares) and the node, connection (edge) and variable counts of the root graph's default page; with include_defaults, each input's default value too. Read-only; a path that does not resolve to a UMetaSoundSource, a MetaSound Patch included, is an error. list_metasound_nodes lists the nodes; get_assets_by_type with asset_type MetaSoundSource finds sources. The edges themselves: list_metasound_connections.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source, as a package path like "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example" or an object path like "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example.MS_Example"

params.name: include_defaults
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When true, each inputs[] entry gains value: its default as the MetaSound editor builder reads it (a literal string), or "(inherited)" when the builder has none (a preset input taken from its referenced asset). Opens the editor builder for the asset; the asset is not changed.

commands.returns: { source_name: string, asset_path: string, class_name: string, graph_class_name: string, input_count: number, output_count: number, interface_count: number, node_count: number, connection_count: number, variable_count: number, inputs: [{ name: string, type: string, value?: string }], outputs: [{ name: string, type: string }] }

commands.name: get_metasound_node_info
commands.description: Read one node of the default graph of a MetaSound Source by GUID: its name, class name, input/output/environment vertices (name, type_name, vertex_id), each input's stored default literal (has_value, literal_type, value; has_value false means no literal is set), the input literal defaults by vertex, and the Configuration struct class; input_name narrows inputs and input_defaults to one input, and an unknown input name fails listing the valid ones. Read-only; get node ids from list_metasound_nodes, write an input default with set_metasound_node_input_default.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted.

params.name: node_id
params.description: Node GUID, as list_metasound_nodes returns it in id; a value that is not a GUID is refused.

params.name: input_name
params.description: Optional name of one input vertex (FMetasoundFrontendVertex::Name): inputs and input_defaults then hold only that input. A name the node has no input for is an error listing the inputs.

commands.returns: { metasound_path, node_id, name, class_name, input_name?, inputs: [{name, type_name, vertex_id, has_value, literal_type?, value?}], outputs: [{name, type_name, vertex_id}], environment: [...], input_defaults: [{vertex_id, input_name, value, type}], configuration_class }

commands.name: get_metasound_node_property
commands.description: Read one field of the Configuration struct of a MetaSound Source node, found by its node GUID (from list_metasound_nodes), returning its C++ type, has_value and value as JSON. Use it because MetaSound nodes are document structs, not UObjects, so get_properties cannot reach them; input defaults are set_metasound_node_input_default. Fails when the node has no Configuration struct or no such property; Patches are refused. Read-only; write with set_metasound_node_property.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted.

params.name: node_id
params.description: Node GUID, as list_metasound_nodes returns it in id; a value that is not a GUID is refused.

params.name: property
params.description: FProperty name on the Configuration struct.

commands.returns: { metasound_path, node_id, property, type, has_value, value? }

commands.name: get_modulation_generator_info
commands.description: Read the class and settings of a USoundModulationGenerator asset without changing it. settings depend on the class: LFO gives shape, frequency, amplitude, offset and phase; ADEnvelope gives attack_time and decay_time; EnvelopeFollower gives attack_time, release_time, gain and audio_bus_path (empty when no audio bus is set); any other generator class gives an empty settings object. Use it to check create_modulation_generator or set_modulation_generator_settings; for a modulation parameter use get_modulation_parameter_info, for a control bus get_control_bus_info, for a patch get_sound_modulation_patch_info. A path that does not load as a modulation generator is an error.

params.name: generator_path
params.description: Asset path of the generator, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/LFO_Wobble", as create_modulation_generator returns it.

commands.returns: { generator_path, generator_class, settings: {...} }

commands.name: get_modulation_parameter_info
commands.description: Read a sound modulation parameter asset without changing it: its concrete class (e.g. SoundModulationParameterVolume) and its settings, value_normalized (the 0-1 default), clamp_to_normalized_range (left out on Unreal Engine 5.7, which lacks it) and value_unit (the default in the parameter's own unit). Use it to check a parameter before making it a patch output with set_modulation_patch_output_parameter, or after set_modulation_parameter_settings changed it. A path that does not load as a modulation parameter is an error. Create one with create_modulation_parameter; patches and generators have their own readers: get_sound_modulation_patch_info, get_modulation_generator_info.

params.name: parameter_path
params.description: Asset path of the modulation parameter, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/Param_Volume", as create_modulation_parameter returns it (parameter_path).

commands.returns: { parameter_path, parameter_class, value_normalized, clamp_to_normalized_range?, value_unit }

commands.name: get_sound_attenuation_properties
commands.description: Read the whole FSoundAttenuationSettings struct (shape, falloff, spatialization, LPF, occlusion, reverb send) of a USoundAttenuation asset as one settings object, with the keys set_sound_attenuation_properties takes, plus asset_class. A convenience over get_properties on its Attenuation property, shaped for that write tool; it reads the asset, not what an audio component applies (get_audio_component_properties). Read-only.

params.name: attenuation_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundAttenuation.

commands.returns: { attenuation_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object }

commands.name: get_sound_class_properties
commands.description: Read a USoundClass asset: every FSoundClassProperties field that set_properties writes (volume, pitch, filters, reverb and routing flags, output_target, loading_behavior) plus its name and its direct parent and direct children by name and path. A flattened view under the snake_case keys that tool takes; get_properties reads the raw Properties struct or any other UPROPERTY. parent_class is "None" for a root class, and child_count is the number of children listed (null references are skipped). One level only: walk further by calling it again on a parent or child. Read-only; it loads the asset by object or package path, and one that does not load as a USoundClass is an error.

params.name: sound_class_path
params.description: Content path of the USoundClass asset.

commands.returns: { name: string, sound_class_path: string, volume: float, pitch: float, low_pass_frequency: float, attenuation_distance_scale: float, lfe_bleed: float, voice_center_channel_volume: float, radio_filter_volume: float, radio_filter_volume_threshold: float, default_2d_reverb_send_amount: float, apply_effects: bool, always_play: bool, is_ui_sound: bool, is_music: bool, center_channel_only: bool, apply_ambient_volumes: bool, reverb: bool, output_target: string, loading_behavior: string, parent_class: string, parent_class_path: string, child_classes: [{name, path}], child_count: int }

commands.name: get_sound_concurrency_properties
commands.description: Read the whole FSoundConcurrencySettings struct (maxCount, bLimitToOwner, resolutionRule, retriggerTime, volume scaling, voice stealing) of a USoundConcurrency asset as one settings object, with the keys set_sound_concurrency_properties takes, plus asset_class. A convenience over get_properties on its Concurrency property, shaped for that write tool. Read-only.

params.name: concurrency_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundConcurrency.

commands.returns: { concurrency_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object }

commands.name: get_sound_cue_graph
commands.description: Reads the node graph of a USoundCue without changing it: every node in AllNodes with its id (the node_id the other sound cue tools take), class, child_ids (the wired child's id per input slot, -1 for an empty slot), max_child_nodes and editable properties (the keys set_sound_cue_node_properties accepts), plus first_node_id (the output node, -1 when unset) and node_count. Read-only: nothing is modified or saved; a cue that does not load is an error. Call it before connect_sound_cue_nodes, disconnect_sound_cue_nodes, remove_sound_cue_node, set_sound_cue_first_node or set_sound_cue_node_properties to get ids, and after them to check the result; ids are positions, so re-read after remove_sound_cue_node shifts them. Create a cue with create_sound_cue and add nodes with add_sound_cue_node.

params.name: cue_path
params.description: Object or package path of the Sound Cue asset (e.g. "/Game/Audio/SC_Footsteps" or "/Game/Audio/SC_Footsteps.SC_Footsteps").

commands.returns: { cue_path: string, asset_path: string, nodes: [object], node_count: int, first_node_id: int, has_first_node: bool }

commands.name: get_sound_modulation_patch_info
commands.description: Read a USoundModulationPatch asset without changing it: bBypass (a bypassed patch outputs the default value of its output parameter), output_parameter with its path and class (null when none is set), and one inputs entry per input, in order, holding the bus path (empty when that input has no bus) and a name that is always empty because the engine input struct has no name. A patch that cannot be loaded is an error. Change it with set_modulation_patch_bypass, set_modulation_patch_output_parameter, add_modulation_input_to_patch and remove_modulation_input_from_patch; make one with create_sound_modulation_patch; read an input bus with get_control_bus_info and the output parameter with get_modulation_parameter_info.

params.name: patch_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationPatch, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Patch_Duck.Patch_Duck"

commands.returns: { patch_path, bBypass, output_parameter: { path, class } | null, inputs: [{ bus: { path }, name }], input_count }

commands.name: get_sound_source_bus
commands.description: Read the routing fields of a USoundSourceBus asset: source_bus_channels (Mono or Stereo), duration in seconds (0 plays indefinitely) and the UAudioBus it outputs to (audio_bus_path and audio_bus_class, empty when none). Read-only. Writer: set_sound_source_bus_audio_bus.

params.name: ssb_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundSourceBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SSB_Radio".

commands.returns: { ssb_path: string, asset_class: string, source_bus_channels: string, duration: float, audio_bus_path: string, audio_bus_class: string }

commands.name: get_sound_wave_properties
commands.description: Read every reflected property of a USoundWave asset, its USoundBase fields included (CompressionQuality, SampleRateQuality, SoundGroup, Volume, Pitch, Priority, SoundClassObject, AttenuationSettings and the rest), as the settings object FJsonObjectConverter exports, so keys start lower-case (compressionQuality); settings also carries bLooping, echoed as looping. Like get_object_info on the asset, but keyed as set_sound_wave_properties accepts it; get_properties reads a few named fields. Read-only: it loads the asset if needed and changes nothing. A path that does not load as a USoundWave is an error. Write the same fields back with set_sound_wave_properties (bLooping through its looping param); a sound class is read with get_sound_class_properties and a level's audio component with get_audio_component_properties.

params.name: sound_wave_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundWave, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MySound".

commands.returns: { sound_wave_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object, looping: bool }

retired.how: object_path=<sound wave>: every property; get_properties for named ones

commands.name: get_soundfield_submix_info
commands.description: Read a soundfield submix asset without changing it: its encoding format as authored (soundfield_encoding_format) and as the engine resolves it (resolved_format), its encoding settings object (class and path), and every effect of its chain in order with index, class, path and settings class and path. A note is added when no concrete soundfield effect class is loaded (stock Unreal ships none; a spatial audio plugin adds them), which is why the chain is usually empty. Use it after create_soundfield_submix, or to find the effect_index that remove_soundfield_effect takes; append an effect with add_soundfield_effect_to_submix. For an ordinary submix's effects use get_submix_effect_chain. A path that does not load as a soundfield submix is an error.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Asset path of the soundfield submix, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SFS_Ambisonics" or "/Game/Audio/SFS_Ambisonics.SFS_Ambisonics", as create_soundfield_submix returns it (submix_path).

commands.returns: { submix_path, soundfield_encoding_format, resolved_format, encoding_settings_class, encoding_settings: { class, path }, effect_chain: [{ index, class, path, settings_class, settings_path }], chain_length, note? }

commands.name: get_submix_effect_chain
commands.description: Read the effect chain of a USoundSubmix asset in order: one entry per slot with the name, class and path of its USoundEffectSubmixPreset ("None" for an empty slot), plus chain_length. Read-only; add_submix_effect_to_chain appends to it.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundSubmix, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SM_Master.SM_Master".

commands.returns: { submix_path: string, effects: [object], chain_length: int }

commands.name: list_metasound_connections
commands.description: List every edge of the default graph of a MetaSound Source: from which node and output pin to which node and input pin, with each node's name and class (a graph input or output node is named after the input or output), plus count. Read-only. It reads what connect_metasound_nodes, connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node, connect_metasound_graph_input_to_output and connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output write; node ids are those of list_metasound_nodes, and an input's edge is dropped with disconnect_metasound_nodes. Patches are refused.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain".

commands.returns: { metasound_path: string, count: int, connections: [{ from_node_id, from_node_name, from_node_class, from_output_name, to_node_id, to_node_name, to_node_class, to_input_name, data_type }] }

commands.name: list_metasound_node_types
commands.description: List the MetaSound node classes the editor's MetaSound search engine knows, without changing anything: per class its class_name, class_path (Namespace.Name.Variant, e.g. UE.Sine.Audio: the three parts add_metasound_node takes as class_namespace, class_name and class_variant), type (e.g. External, the type of node classes and MetaSound assets), highest version (major.minor; the major is add_metasound_node's major_version), access_flags and is_native (true when the class name has a namespace, as engine and plugin nodes do). Deprecated classes are left out and only the highest version of each is listed; with include_unloaded (default) MetaSound assets not loaded yet are included too. The list is long (hundreds of classes) and has no filter. Use it to find a class before add_metasound_node; the nodes already in one MetaSound's graph are list_metasound_nodes, and one node's pins get_metasound_node_info. Editor only.

params.name: include_unloaded
params.description: true (default) also lists the classes of MetaSound assets not loaded into memory yet, from the MetaSound asset manager's tag data; false lists only the classes registered now.

commands.returns: { count, types: [{ class_name, class_path, type, version, access_flags, is_native }] }

commands.name: list_metasound_nodes
commands.description: List every node in the default graph of a MetaSound Source asset with its GUID id, name, class name and input/output counts, plus count. Read-only; pass the id to get_metasound_node_info and the other node tools.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted.

commands.returns: { metasound_path, count, nodes: [{ id, name, class_name, input_count, output_count }] }

commands.name: list_subtitle_cues
commands.description: List every cue of a subtitles asset (USubtitleAssetUserData, the engine's list of timed subtitle cues) in stored order, without changing anything: per cue its 0-based index, text, start_offset and duration in seconds, duration_type (use_sound_duration or use_duration_property), priority, subtitle_type (subtitle, closed_caption or audio_description) and comment, plus count and max_duration (GetMaximumDuration, the latest end time). Use it to find the cue_index that set_subtitle_cue and remove_subtitle_cue take, or to check add_subtitle_cue's result; create the asset with create_subtitles_asset. An asset with no cues is a success with count 0; a path that does not load as a USubtitleAssetUserData is an error.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Subtitles asset as a package or object path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Subs/SUB_Intro" or "/Game/Audio/Subs/SUB_Intro.SUB_Intro".

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, success: bool, count: int, max_duration: float, cues: [{index, text, start_offset, duration, duration_type, priority, subtitle_type, comment}] }

commands.name: play_sound
commands.description: Starts the sound already assigned to an audio component of the editor world, found by object name (case-insensitive) among EVERY audio component of every actor, so an actor's second or third audio component is reached too; a name that components of several actors carry is an error listing the owners unless actor_name (object name, not label) picks one. Components in a running PIE world are not reached. start_time is an offset in seconds into the sound. A component without a sound is an error: assign one with set_audio_sound. Transient: nothing is saved, marked dirty or undoable. success is true only when the audio device holds a new active sound for this component afterwards, read on the audio thread before and after the call (active_sounds_before/after, sounds of the component not being stopped).
