No audio device (an editor started with -NoSound, or no device could be created), a world that does not allow audio playback, or a sound the device did not start (not playable, out of range, a concurrency limit, a looping sound parked as a virtual loop until a listener comes in range) is an error saying which and naming the component. was_playing and playing (UAudioComponent::IsPlaying) are read just before and just after the call; audio_component_path and audio_owner_name name the component used. Stop with stop_sound; to play an asset at a location without a component use play_sound_at_location.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Object name of the audio component to play (e.g. "AudioComponent0"), compared without case against every audio component of every actor in the editor world.

params.name: start_time
params.description: Optional offset in seconds to start playback at

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Optional object name (not label) of the actor that owns the component, compared without case. Needed when several actors own an audio component of that name (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0); an empty one, one that names no actor, or one whose actor has no such component is an error.

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, audio_component_path: string, audio_owner_name: string, playing: bool, was_playing: bool, sound_name: string, start_time: number, active_sounds_before: int, active_sounds_after: int (active sounds of this component on the device, those being stopped left out), active_sound_started: bool, success: bool }

commands.name: play_sound_at_location
commands.description: Play a sound asset (sound wave, sound cue or MetaSound source) once at a world location in the editor world, as a fire-and-forget one-shot with no audio component (UGameplayStatics::PlaySoundAtLocation) and only the sound's own attenuation. Nothing is saved, dirtied or undoable, and no handle comes back: the sound plays to its end, and a looping one keeps looping with no way to stop it from here. Each call starts another instance. success is true only when the audio device holds a new active sound of that asset afterwards, counted on the audio thread before and after the call (active_sounds_before/after). No audio device (an editor started with -NoSound, or no device could be created), a world that does not allow audio playback, a one-shot out of earshot of every listener (the engine's own audibility test), or a sound the device did not start (not playable, a concurrency limit, a looping sound parked as a virtual loop) is an error saying which. A sound that does not load or a location that is not an array of 3 numbers is an error too. For playback you can stop or inspect, use play_sound and stop_sound on an audio component (set_audio_sound assigns its sound).

params.name: sound_path
params.description: Object path of the sound asset, e.g. '/Game/Audio/MySound.MySound' (the package path '/Game/Audio/MySound' also loads).

params.name: location
params.description: World position [x, y, z] in centimetres, e.g. [0, 0, 100]; required, and the origin [0, 0, 0] is valid.

params.name: volume
params.description: Optional volume multiplier, e.g. 0.5 for half; default 1.0.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Optional pitch multiplier, e.g. 2.0 for an octave up; default 1.0.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees, the facing of the sound (it matters to a directional attenuation); default [0, 0, 0].

commands.returns: { sound_path: string, sound_name: string, location: { x, y, z }, rotation: { pitch, yaw, roll }, volume: number, pitch: number, audio_device_id: int, audible: bool (the engine's audibility test at that location), max_distance: number, looping: bool, active_sounds_before: int, active_sounds_after: int (active sounds of this asset on the device), active_sound_created: bool, success: bool }

commands.name: remove_bus_from_mix
commands.description: Removes every stage that uses a USoundControlBus from a USoundControlBusMix asset and saves the mix; a removal succeeds only when the mix reaches disk. A bus that is not in the mix is already the state asked for: the call succeeds with removed false and already_absent true, and saves nothing. Returns mix_path, bus_path, removed, already_absent, stage_count, saved.

params.name: mix_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus to remove from the mix

commands.returns: { mix_path, bus_path, removed, already_absent, stage_count, saved }

commands.name: remove_metasound_graph_input
commands.description: Removes a graph INPUT (and its node) from a MetaSound Source by name (inverse of add_metasound_graph_input).  Queries GetGraphInputNames first: if the input is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveGraphInput and reports the result. Saves the asset.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: input_name
params.description: Name of the graph input to remove.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, input_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: remove_metasound_graph_output
commands.description: Removes a graph OUTPUT (and its node) from a MetaSound Source by name (inverse of add_metasound_graph_output).  Queries GetGraphOutputNames first: if the output is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveGraphOutput and reports the result. Saves the asset.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: output_name
params.description: Name of the graph output to remove.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, output_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: remove_metasound_interface
commands.description: Remove an interface from a MetaSound Source graph, with the graph inputs and outputs (and their nodes) it declared, in one undo step, then save the asset. Inverse of add_metasound_interface. The reply re-reads the document's interfaces (interface_count, still_declared). An interface the graph does not declare is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing saved); a source that does not load is an error. Removing the source interface a one-shot MetaSound Source needs (UE.Source...) leaves a source the engine may refuse to play; get_metasound_info lists what is declared.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: interface_name
params.description: Name of the declared interface to remove, as add_metasound_interface took it.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, interface_name: string, removed: bool, still_declared: bool, interface_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: remove_metasound_node
commands.description: Removes a node from a MetaSound Source graph by its node_id GUID (inverse of add_metasound_node).  Parses the node_id into a node handle and queries ContainsNode first: if the node is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveNode (pruning unused dependencies) and reports the result. Saves the asset.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: node_id
params.description: GUID of the node to remove (from add_metasound_node).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_id: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }

commands.name: remove_modulation_input_from_patch
commands.description: Remove every input of a USoundModulationPatch asset whose control bus has the same asset name as the bus at bus_path (so a same-named bus in another folder matches too), in one undo step (undo restores the inputs), then save the patch. Inverse of add_modulation_input_to_patch; list the inputs first with get_sound_modulation_patch_info. Idempotent: when no input matches, nothing is changed or saved and the call succeeds with removed false and already_removed true. A patch or bus that does not load is an error and nothing changes; a removal succeeds only when the patch reaches disk, so a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the inputs gone only in memory. input_count is the number of inputs left.

params.name: patch_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundModulationPatch, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/MP_Volume", as create_sound_modulation_patch returns it.

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path of an existing USoundControlBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/CB_Music"; it must load, and only its asset name is compared with the inputs' buses.

commands.returns: { patch_path, bus_path, removed, already_removed, input_count, saved }

commands.name: remove_sound_cue_node
commands.description: Delete one node from a USoundCue asset, in one undo step, then save the cue. Inverse of add_sound_cue_node: every input slot that held the node is emptied (slots are kept, as disconnect_sound_cue_nodes keeps them), the cue output (FirstNode) is cleared when it was this node, the node leaves AllNodes, and its node in the cue editor's graph goes too when the cue has one. node_id is an index into AllNodes, so the nodes after it move down by one: id_remap lists {old_id, new_id} for each, and the ids from earlier calls are stale. A cue that does not load or a node_id out of range is an error and nothing changes. A failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error. Read back: get_sound_cue_graph.

params.name: cue_path
params.description: Full asset path of the cue

params.name: node_id
params.description: node_id of the node to delete (its index in the cue AllNodes, from add_sound_cue_node or get_sound_cue_graph)

commands.returns: { cue_path: string, node_id: int, node_class: string, removed: bool, slots_cleared: int, first_node_cleared: bool, graph_node_removed: bool, id_remap: [{old_id, new_id}], node_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_sound_mix_class_override
commands.description: Remove the sound class adjuster for one sound class from a USoundMix, in one undo step, then save the mix. Inverse of set_sound_mix_class_override, which adds or updates that adjuster. A mix with no adjuster for the class is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing saved); a mix or class that does not load is an error. The reply re-reads the mix's adjusters (remaining_classes). A failed save makes success false with save_error.

params.name: sound_mix_path
params.description: Content path of the USoundMix asset.

params.name: sound_class_path
params.description: Content path of the USoundClass whose adjuster to remove.

commands.returns: { sound_mix_path: string, sound_class_path: string, removed: bool, removed_count: int, total_adjusters: int, remaining_classes: [string], saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_soundfield_effect
commands.description: Detach the effect at effect_index from the effect chain of a soundfield submix asset, in one undo step, then save the submix; later effects shift down one index and the effect object itself stays in the package. The inverse of add_soundfield_effect_to_submix; find the index with get_soundfield_submix_info. The same index again removes the next effect, and an index past the end of the chain is an error with nothing changed. Success needs the save: a failed save makes success false, with saved false, save_error and the change only in memory. When no concrete soundfield effect class is loaded (stock Unreal ships none; a spatial audio plugin adds them) the chain is not touched and the call fails with removed false and a note. A path that does not load as a soundfield submix is an error. For an ordinary submix use remove_submix_effect_from_chain.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Asset path of the soundfield submix, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SFS_Ambisonics", as create_soundfield_submix returns it (submix_path).

params.name: effect_index
params.description: 0-based position in the effect chain, as get_soundfield_submix_info returns it (effect_chain[].index); a negative value is an error.

commands.returns: { submix_path, effect_index, removed_effect_class, removed_effect_path, removed: true, already_absent: false, chain_length, saved, save_error? } -- success only when saved; with no concrete effect class loaded the call fails with { submix_path, effect_index, removed: false, saved: false, note } and the chain is not touched.

commands.name: remove_submix_effect_from_chain
commands.description: Remove the entry at effect_index from a USoundSubmix's effect chain, in one undo step, notify the submix of the edit (as the Details panel does, so a running audio device rebuilds the chain) and save the submix. Inverse of add_submix_effect_to_chain; the later entries move up one index. The preset itself is not deleted: a preset add_submix_effect_to_chain made inside the submix package stays in it unreferenced, one appended by path stays where it was. An index out of range or a submix that does not load is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false with save_error. Read the chain first with get_submix_effect_chain; a soundfield submix's effects: remove_soundfield_effect.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundSubmix

params.name: effect_index
params.description: 0-based position in the chain, as get_submix_effect_chain lists it

commands.returns: { submix_path: string, effect_index: int, removed_effect: string, removed_effect_class: string, removed: bool, chain_length: int, chain: [string], saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_subtitle_cue
commands.description: Remove a single FSubtitleAssetData cue by index. Inverse of add_subtitle_cue; use delete_asset to destroy the whole asset instead. Idempotent: an out-of-range index returns removed:false + note, not an error.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the USubtitleAssetUserData.

params.name: cue_index
params.description: 0-based index into Subtitles[].

commands.returns: { asset_path, cue_index, removed, previous_count, new_count }

commands.name: set_audio_3d_settings
commands.description: Apply a 3D audio preset to one audio component of a placed actor in the editor world, in one undo step that dirties the level without saving it: spatialization (bAllowSpatialization) plus, for every preset but Disabled, an attenuation override sphere with the preset's inner radius and falloff distance (High 1000/2000 cm, Enabled and Medium 500/1000, Low 250/500); Disabled turns both off. audio_3d_configured is read back from the component; attenuation_falloff and the cone numbers only describe the preset. The same preset again gives the same result. The component is found by object name (case-insensitive) among EVERY audio component of every actor, so an actor's second or third audio component is reached too; a name that components of several actors carry is an error listing the owners unless actor_name (object name, not label) picks one, and the reply names the component changed (audio_component_path, audio_owner_name). A missing component or unknown preset is an error and nothing changes. Read the result with get_audio_component_properties; set_audio_volume and set_audio_sound change the rest.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Object name of the audio component, compared without case against every audio component of every actor, e.g. 'AudioComponent0' (get_audio_settings lists them with their owners).

params.name: audio_3d_settings
params.description: Preset name: 'Enabled', 'Disabled', 'High', 'Medium' or 'Low' (case-insensitive); any other name is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Optional object name (not label) of the actor that owns the component, compared without case. Needed when several actors own an audio component of that name (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0); an empty one, one that names no actor, or one whose actor has no such component is an error.

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, audio_component_path: string, audio_owner_name: string, audio_3d_settings: string, audio_3d_configured: bool, audio_3d_message: string, old_3d_enabled: bool, new_3d_enabled: bool, attenuation_override: bool, applied_attenuation_radius?: number, applied_falloff_distance?: number, 3d_enabled: bool, spatialization_enabled: bool, attenuation_distance: number, attenuation_radius: number, attenuation_falloff: number, attenuation_cone_angle: number, attenuation_cone_feather: number, audio_3d_recommendations: [string] }

commands.name: set_audio_bus_channels
commands.description: Change the channel layout (AudioBusChannels) of an existing UAudioBus asset and save it; success requires the save. Returns channels, channels_int and num_channels read back from the asset. To make a new bus use create_audio_bus.

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAudioBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/AB_Music".

params.name: channels
params.description: EAudioBusChannels: 'Mono' | 'Stereo' | 'Quad' | 'FiveDotOne' | 'SevenDotOne', case-insensitive; FivePointOne, 5.1, SevenPointOne and 7.1 are accepted too.

commands.returns: { bus_path: string, asset_class: string, channels: string, channels_int: int, num_channels: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_audio_sound
commands.description: Sets the sound asset of an audio component of the editor world, found by object name (case-insensitive) among EVERY audio component of every actor, so an actor's second or third audio component is reached too; a name that components of several actors carry is an error listing the owners unless actor_name (object name, not label) picks one. Components in a running PIE world are not reached. A component that is playing restarts with the new sound unless it allows multiple instances. The change is not saved, marked dirty or undoable. A missing component or a sound that does not load is an error. previous_sound_name names the sound it replaced (None when there was none); audio_component_path and audio_owner_name name the component changed. Start playback with play_sound.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Object name of the audio component to modify (e.g. "AudioComponent0"), compared without case against every audio component of every actor in the editor world.

params.name: sound_path
params.description: Full asset path to the sound (e.g. '/Game/Audio/MySound.MySound')

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Optional object name (not label) of the actor that owns the component, compared without case. Needed when several actors own an audio component of that name (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0); an empty one, one that names no actor, or one whose actor has no such component is an error.

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, audio_component_path: string, audio_owner_name: string, sound_path: string, sound_name: string, previous_sound_name: string, sound_duration: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_audio_volume
commands.description: Sets the VolumeMultiplier of one audio component placed in the editor world (not PIE); the engine setter also resets its VolumeModulationMin/Max to 1. The component is found by object name (case-insensitive) among EVERY audio component of every actor; a name that components of several actors carry is an error listing the owners, nothing changed, unless actor_name (object name, not label) picks one. No undo step and no dirty mark: the value is lost on reload unless the level gets saved for another reason. A volume outside 0-10 is an error and nothing changes; the same value again gives the same result. Find components with get_audio_settings and read one with get_audio_component_properties; set_audio_sound changes its sound, set_audio_3d_settings its attenuation; to scale a whole sound class use set_sound_mix_class_override.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Object name of the audio component to modify (e.g. "AudioComponent0"), compared without case against every audio component of every actor in the editor world; get_audio_settings lists them with their owners.

params.name: volume
params.description: Volume multiplier from 0.0 to 10.0 (1.0 = the sound's own level, 0.5 = half, 0 = silent); outside that range is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Optional object name (not label) of the actor that owns the component, compared without case. Needed when several actors own an audio component of that name (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0); an empty one, one that names no actor, or one whose actor has no such component is an error.

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, audio_component_path: string, audio_owner_name: string, old_volume: number, new_volume: number, requested_volume: number, volume_set: bool, volume_message: string, audio_enabled: bool, audio_pitch: number, audio_mobility: string, audio_sound_name: string, audio_3d_attenuation_radius: number, audio_position: { x, y, z } }

commands.name: set_control_bus_mix_stage_value
commands.description: Sets the stored target value, and optionally the attack and release fade times in seconds, of the stage a USoundControlBus has in a USoundControlBusMix asset, then saves the mix; success requires the save. Only that bus's first stage is edited, inside an undo transaction; a bus that is not in the mix is an error (add it with add_bus_to_mix). It edits the asset, not a live value: push a runtime value with set_control_bus_value. Read the stages with get_control_bus_mix_info.

params.name: mix_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus whose stage is edited

params.name: target_value
params.description: New stage target value (required float)

params.name: attack_time
params.description: Optional attack interpolation time in seconds

params.name: release_time
params.description: Optional release interpolation time in seconds

commands.returns: { mix_path, bus_path, target_value, attack_time, release_time, updated, saved }

commands.name: set_control_bus_value
commands.description: Pushes a runtime value into a USoundControlBus through a global bus mix of the editor world (UAudioModulationStatics::SetGlobalBusMixValue), fading over fade_time. Transient: the asset is not modified or saved, and applied is always true, not read back; read the live value with get_control_bus_info.

params.name: bus_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundControlBus

params.name: value
params.description: New runtime bus value to push (required float)

params.name: fade_time
params.description: Fade time in seconds; a negative value reuses the last fade time of the global stage, or 0.1 s if none was set (default -1.0)

commands.returns: { bus_path, value, fade_time, applied }

commands.name: set_metasound_graph_input_default
commands.description: Set the default value of one graph input of a MetaSound Source asset (a preset included) through the MetaSound editor builder, in one undo step, then save the asset. Give one typed field: bool_value (true or false), int_value (a whole number), string_value (a string) or value (a number, read as a float); with several, the first in that order wins. Or give parameter_type (float, int, bool or string) and value in that JSON type, the typed fields then being ignored. A missing or mistyped value, an unknown parameter_type, an unknown source, or an input that is missing or does not take that type is an error, with nothing written. value_set means the default reads back as the value; an input already holding it gives changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save makes success false with save_error. Inputs and their defaults: get_metasound_info (include_defaults); a node pin: set_metasound_node_input_default.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: input_name
params.description: Name of the graph input whose default to set.

params.name: preset_path
params.description: Alias of metasound_path.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Alias of input_name.

params.name: parameter_type
params.description: Optional literal type of value: "float", "int", "bool" or "string". When given, value must be of that JSON type (a whole number for int) and int_value/bool_value/string_value are ignored; another type name is an error.

params.name: value
params.description: Float default value, a JSON number (optional, used if no other *_value is provided); with parameter_type, the value in the JSON type it names. Another JSON type is an error

params.name: int_value
params.description: Int32 default value, a whole JSON number (optional, mutually exclusive with value/bool_value/string_value)

params.name: bool_value
params.description: Bool default value, JSON true or false (optional, mutually exclusive with value/int_value/string_value)

params.name: string_value
params.description: String default value, a JSON string (optional, mutually exclusive with value/int_value/bool_value)

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, input_name: string, value_type: string, value_set: bool, changed: bool, verified: bool, value_read_back: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_metasound_node_input_default
commands.description: Set the default literal of a named input pin on a concrete node of a MetaSound Source (node by node_id from add_metasound_node) through the MetaSound editor builder, then read it back and save the asset. Give one typed field: bool_value (true or false), int_value (a whole number), string_value (a string) or value (a number, read as a float); with several, the first in that order wins. A missing or mistyped value, an unknown source, node_id or pin, or a literal the pin refuses is an error. A failed save makes success false. For a graph input use set_metasound_graph_input_default.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: Asset path of the MetaSound Source.

params.name: node_id
params.description: GUID of the node (from add_metasound_node).

params.name: input_name
params.description: Name of the node input pin (discover via the node's enumerated inputs).

params.name: value
params.description: Float default, a JSON number (optional, used if no other *_value is provided).

params.name: int_value
params.description: Int32 default, a whole JSON number (optional, mutually exclusive).

params.name: bool_value
params.description: Bool default, JSON true or false (optional, mutually exclusive).

params.name: string_value
params.description: String default, a JSON string (optional, mutually exclusive).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, node_id: string, input_name: string, value_type: string, value_set: bool, verified: bool, value_read_back: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_metasound_node_property
commands.description: Write one field of a MetaSound Source node's Configuration struct, node found by GUID, by reflection directly in the frontend document (not through the MetaSound builder), then save the asset. set_properties cannot reach it: frontend nodes are document data, not UObjects. No undo step. Re-applying a value returns value_changed false but still saves. Succeeds only when the asset reaches disk; a failed save leaves the value in memory only (saved false, save_error). Read: get_metasound_node_property; GUIDs: list_metasound_nodes.

params.name: metasound_path
params.description: MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted.

params.name: node_id
params.description: Node GUID, as list_metasound_nodes returns it in id; a value that is not a GUID is refused.

params.name: property
params.description: FProperty name on the Configuration struct.

params.name: value
params.description: New value for the field as JSON, converted by FJsonObjectConverter: a number, bool, string, array or object (for a struct field); numbers and booleans can also be passed as strings ("0.5", "true").

commands.returns: { metasound_path, node_id, property, set, value_changed, new_value?, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_modulation_generator_settings
commands.description: Writes the settings that match the class of a USoundModulationGenerator asset (LFO, ADEnvelope or EnvelopeFollower), in one undo step (undo restores the previous settings), and saves it; params of another class are ignored, and other generator classes and an audio_bus_path that does not load are refused with nothing changed. The LFO shape (waveform) is set with create_modulation_generator. Returns generator_path, generator_class, settings as stored, updated, saved.

params.name: generator_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationGenerator

params.name: frequency
params.description: LFO only: oscillation frequency in Hz (optional float)

params.name: amplitude
params.description: LFO only: output amplitude/gain multiplier (optional float)

params.name: offset
params.description: LFO only: output offset added to the waveform (optional float)

params.name: phase
params.description: LFO only: starting phase in degrees (optional float)

params.name: attack_time
params.description: ADEnvelope/EnvelopeFollower: attack interpolation time in seconds (optional float)

params.name: decay_time
params.description: ADEnvelope only: decay interpolation time in seconds (optional float)

params.name: release_time
params.description: EnvelopeFollower only: release interpolation time in seconds (optional float)

params.name: gain
params.description: EnvelopeFollower only: input gain applied before envelope detection (optional float)

params.name: audio_bus_path
params.description: EnvelopeFollower only: asset path to the UAudioBus the follower listens to (optional string)

commands.returns: { generator_path, generator_class, settings: {...}, updated, saved }

commands.name: set_modulation_parameter_settings
commands.description: Change the default value and range settings of a sound modulation parameter asset (the value a modulator starts from, and whether it is clamped to 0-1), then save it. Use it after create_modulation_parameter, which makes the asset; read the settings back with get_modulation_parameter_info. Only the fields you pass change; the others keep their value, and a call with none of them still saves the asset. A path that does not load as a modulation parameter is an error, and so is clamp_to_normalized_range on Unreal Engine 5.7, which lacks that setting; nothing changes then. Idempotent: the same values give the same asset. One undo step that restores the previous settings; a failed save answers success false with the change kept in memory.

params.name: parameter_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationParameter

params.name: value_normalized
params.description: Default value in normalized units, from 0 to 1 (e.g. 0.5); written as given, without clamping.

params.name: clamp_to_normalized_range
params.description: true to keep the parameter's value within 0-1, false to let it go outside; Unreal Engine 5.8 only (refused on 5.7).

params.name: value_unit
params.description: Default value in the parameter's own unit (for example decibels or hertz), shown in the editor; editor-only.

commands.returns: { parameter_path, value_normalized, clamp_to_normalized_range, value_unit, updated, saved }

commands.name: set_modulation_patch_bypass
commands.description: Set the bBypass flag of a USoundModulationPatch asset, in one undo step (undo restores the old value), and save it. A bypassed patch stays active but outputs the default value of its output parameter, so a patch made by create_sound_modulation_patch (which starts bypassed) does nothing until this sets bypass false. Typical order: add_modulation_input_to_patch, set_modulation_patch_output_parameter, then this; read the result with get_sound_modulation_patch_info. It always writes and saves, even when the flag already had that value (updated is always true); bBypass is read back after the write. A patch that does not load or a missing bypass is an error and nothing changes; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the change only in memory.

params.name: patch_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundModulationPatch, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/MP_Volume", as create_sound_modulation_patch returns it.

params.name: bypass
params.description: true bypasses the patch (it outputs its parameter's default); false makes it apply its inputs. Required.

commands.returns: { patch_path, bBypass, updated, saved }

commands.name: set_modulation_patch_output_parameter
commands.description: Sets the output USoundModulationParameter of a USoundModulationPatch asset, or clears it when parameter_path is an empty string, in one undo step (undo restores the previous one), and saves the patch. Returns patch_path, parameter_path and parameter_class as stored (empty after a clear), updated, cleared, saved. Create a parameter with create_modulation_parameter.

params.name: patch_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationPatch

params.name: parameter_path
params.description: Asset path to the USoundModulationParameter (or empty string to clear)

commands.returns: { patch_path, parameter_path, parameter_class, updated, cleared, saved }

commands.name: set_sound_attenuation_properties
commands.description: Merge fields into a SoundAttenuation asset's Attenuation settings (absent keys kept), clamp to ClampMin/ClampMax and save; set_properties neither clamps nor saves. Keys match field names case-insensitively. An empty settings object, a key that names no field (the error lists them), a null value, or a value that is not of the field's kind or does not convert is an error and nothing changes. Plugin sub-objects are not reached. A failed save makes success false.

params.name: attenuation_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundAttenuation.

params.name: settings
params.description: Object of FSoundAttenuationSettings/FBaseAttenuationSettings fields to merge; absent keys untouched. e.g. bAttenuate, bSpatialize, attenuationShape(Sphere/Capsule/Box/Cone), distanceAlgorithm, falloffDistance, dBAttenuationAtMax(-60..0), attenuationShapeExtents{x,y,z}, bAttenuateWithLPF, lPFFrequencyAtMin/Max, bEnableOcclusion, occlusionVolumeAttenuation, bEnableReverbSend, reverbWetLevelMin/Max. Nested plugin sub-objects (pluginSettings, audioLinkSettingsOverride) are NOT authored here. Keys match the field names case-insensitively; an empty object, a key that names no field, a null value or a value that does not convert is an error and nothing is changed.

commands.returns: { attenuation_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object, applied_keys: [string], saved: bool }

commands.name: set_sound_class_parent
commands.description: Make one USoundClass the child of another, wiring ParentClass and ChildClasses, and save both packages. A previous parent loses the child in memory but is not saved; only self-parenting is refused, not cycles. Returns child_count, saved_parent and saved_child, succeeding even when a save fails.

params.name: child_sound_class_path

params.name: parent_sound_class_path

commands.returns: { child: string, parent: string, child_path: string, parent_path: string, child_count: int, saved_parent: bool, saved_child: bool }

commands.name: set_sound_class_properties
commands.description: Write the given FSoundClassProperties fields of a SoundClass asset (volume, pitch, filters, routing and loading flags) as flat named params, then save it. Only fields you pass change; values are not range-checked and an unknown output_target or loading_behavior name is skipped (applied_<field> false). Returns every current value plus saved; get_sound_class_properties reads them.

params.name: radio_filter_volume_threshold

params.name: default_2d_reverb_send_amount
params.description: Reverb send amount for unattenuated (2D) sounds of this class (Properties.Default2DReverbSendAmount)

params.name: apply_effects
params.description: Bool for Properties.bApplyEffects (Output to Master EQ Submix): route referencing sounds to the Master EQ submix

params.name: always_play
params.description: Bool for Properties.bAlwaysPlay: inflate the priority of referencing sounds so they always play

params.name: is_ui_sound
params.description: Bool for Properties.bIsUISound: sounds of this class keep playing while the game is paused in the UI

params.name: is_music
params.description: Bool for Properties.bIsMusic: mark the class as music (propagates to child classes only when the parent is true)

params.name: center_channel_only
params.description: Bool for Properties.bCenterChannelOnly: force sounds of this class to the center channel

params.name: apply_ambient_volumes
params.description: Bool for Properties.bApplyAmbientVolumes: apply the Interior/Exterior volume and low-pass modifiers

params.name: reverb
params.description: Bool for Properties.bReverb (Send to Master Reverb Submix): send referencing sounds to the reverb submix

params.name: output_target
params.description: Properties.OutputTarget enum name (Speaker|Controller|ControllerFallbackToSpeaker); case-insensitive, ignored if unrecognized.

params.name: loading_behavior
params.description: Properties.LoadingBehavior enum name (Inherited|RetainOnLoad|PrimeOnLoad|LoadOnDemand|ForceInline); case-insensitive, ignored if unrecognized.

commands.returns: { sound_class_path: string, success: bool, volume: float, pitch: float, low_pass_frequency: float, attenuation_distance_scale: float, lfe_bleed: float, voice_center_channel_volume: float, radio_filter_volume: float, radio_filter_volume_threshold: float, default_2d_reverb_send_amount: float, apply_effects: bool, always_play: bool, is_ui_sound: bool, is_music: bool, center_channel_only: bool, apply_ambient_volumes: bool, reverb: bool, output_target: string, loading_behavior: string, applied_volume: bool, applied_pitch: bool, applied_low_pass_frequency: bool, applied_attenuation_distance_scale: bool, applied_lfe_bleed: bool, applied_voice_center_channel_volume: bool, applied_radio_filter_volume: bool, applied_radio_filter_volume_threshold: bool, applied_default_2d_reverb_send_amount: bool, applied_apply_effects: bool, applied_always_play: bool, applied_is_ui_sound: bool, applied_is_music: bool, applied_center_channel_only: bool, applied_apply_ambient_volumes: bool, applied_reverb: bool, applied_output_target: bool, applied_loading_behavior: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_sound_concurrency_properties
commands.description: Merge fields into a SoundConcurrency asset's Concurrency settings (maxCount, resolutionRule, volume scaling...; absent keys kept), clamp to ClampMin/ClampMax and save; set_properties neither clamps nor saves. An empty settings object, a key that names no field (the error lists them), a null value, or a value that is not of the field's kind or does not convert is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false.

params.name: concurrency_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundConcurrency.

params.name: settings
params.description: Object of FSoundConcurrencySettings fields to merge (maxCount(int>=1), bLimitToOwner(bool), resolutionRule(enum name), retriggerTime, volumeScale(0..1), volumeScaleMode(enum), bVolumeScaleCanRelease, volumeScaleAttackTime, volumeScaleReleaseTime, voiceStealReleaseTime); absent keys untouched. Keys match the field names case-insensitively; an empty object, a key that names no field, a null value or a value that does not convert is an error and nothing is changed.

commands.returns: { concurrency_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object, applied_keys: [string], saved: bool }

commands.name: set_sound_cue_first_node
commands.description: Make the node at node_id the root (FirstNode, the output) of a USoundCue graph, undoably, and save the asset. Returns first_node_class, first_node_set and saved; an out-of-range node_id is an error. Get node ids from add_sound_cue_node or get_sound_cue_graph.

params.name: cue_path
params.description: Full asset path of the cue

params.name: node_id
params.description: node_id (index in the cue AllNodes array) to use as the root of the cue graph

commands.returns: { cue_path: string, node_id: int, first_node_class: string, first_node_set: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_sound_cue_node_properties
commands.description: Set EditAnywhere properties of one Sound Cue node, located by node_id, then refresh the cue's aggregate values and save it -- the writer twin of get_sound_cue_graph. Use it instead of set_properties, which needs the node's object path rather than the node_id that get_sound_cue_graph and add_sound_cue_node report. Keys are the camelCase UPROPERTY names get_sound_cue_graph reports under each node's properties (e.g. a Modulator: pitchMin/pitchMax/volumeMin/volumeMax; a Delay: delayMin/delayMax).

params.name: cue_path
params.description: Full asset path of the cue, e.g. /Game/SoundCues/SC_Foo

params.name: node_id
params.description: node_id (index in AllNodes) from add_sound_cue_node / get_sound_cue_graph.

params.name: properties
params.description: Object of {camelCaseName: value} to apply to the node.

commands.returns: { cue_path: string, node_id: int, node_class: string, applied_keys: [string], saved: bool }

commands.description: Sets a sound class adjuster override in a USoundMix.  Loads the USoundMix and USoundClass, adds or updates an FSoundClassAdjuster in the mix's SoundClassEffects array, then saves. Inverse: remove_sound_mix_class_override.

params.name: sound_class_path
params.description: Content path of the USoundClass to adjust.

params.name: volume_adjuster

params.name: pitch_adjuster
params.description: Adjuster.PitchAdjuster (default 1.0).

params.description: Adjuster.bApplyToChildren (default false).

commands.name: set_sound_source_bus_audio_bus
commands.description: Point the AudioBus output of a USoundSourceBus asset at a UAudioBus, or clear it when audio_bus_path is empty or omitted, then save; success requires the save. Returns audio_bus_path and audio_bus_class read back, plus cleared. A bus path that does not load is an error, not a clear.

params.name: ssb_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundSourceBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SSB_Radio".

params.name: audio_bus_path
params.description: Asset path of the UAudioBus to assign, e.g. "/Game/Audio/AB_Music"; "" or omitted clears the assignment.

commands.returns: { ssb_path: string, audio_bus_path: string, audio_bus_class: string, cleared: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_sound_source_bus_send_info
commands.description: Write one bus send (an entry of BusSends, routing this sound's audio to another source bus or audio bus at a send level) on a USoundSourceBus asset, in one undo step, then save it. Only the fields given in send_info change, numbers are clamped to the property limits, and send_info in the reply is the whole entry read back (applied_keys only echoes your keys). A send_index past the end grows the list to send_index + 1, filling gaps with default sends. A soundSourceBus or audioBus path that does not load sets that reference to none without an error. Bus output: set_sound_source_bus_audio_bus; CustomCurve send level: set_sound_source_bus_send_level_curve; targets: create_sound_source_bus, create_audio_bus; get_sound_source_bus does not list sends. Idempotent for the same values. A missing or negative send_index, a missing send_info, an asset that does not load, or a field that does not convert is an error; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the change only in memory.

params.name: ssb_path
params.description: Asset path of the USoundSourceBus to edit, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SSB_Radio", as create_sound_source_bus returns it (asset_path).

params.name: send_index
params.description: 0-based position in the BusSends list, e.g. 0; an existing entry is updated in place, a larger index grows the list (required).

params.name: send_info
params.description: Object of FSoundSourceBusSendInfo fields to merge (sourceBusSendLevelControlMethod(Linear|CustomCurve|Manual), soundSourceBus(path), audioBus(path), sendLevel(Manual), minSendLevel/maxSendLevel(Linear), minSendDistance/maxSendDistance(Linear), customSendLevelCurve(object), bEnableLPFCutoff(bool), lPFCutoff(20..20000Hz), bEnableHPFCutoff(bool), hPFCutoff(20..20000Hz)), e.g. {"sourceBusSendLevelControlMethod":"Manual","audioBus":"/Game/Audio/AB_Reverb","sendLevel":0.5} (required).

commands.returns: { ssb_path: string, send_index: int, bus_sends_count: int, send_info: object, applied_keys: [string], saved: bool }

commands.name: set_sound_source_bus_send_level_curve
commands.description: Merge a FRuntimeFloatCurve JSON into BusSends[send_index].CustomSendLevelCurve of a USoundSourceBus asset (BusSends grows with default entries past its end) and save it; success requires the save. Returns the curve read back. The curve only takes effect when that send uses the CustomCurve control method: see set_sound_source_bus_send_info.

params.name: ssb_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundSourceBus (USoundBase.BusSends is the target array).

params.name: send_index
params.description: 0-based index into BusSends; the entry is mutated in place. Resized/extended with default-constructed entries if out of range.

params.name: distance_curve
params.description: FRuntimeFloatCurve fields by their UPROPERTY names, e.g. {"EditorCurveData": {"Keys": [{"Time": 0.0, "Value": 1.0}, {"Time": 1.0, "Value": 0.0}]}}; Time 0-1 maps to MinSendDistance-MaxSendDistance and Keys replaces the key list. Fields left out keep their current values; unknown keys are ignored without error.

commands.returns: { ssb_path: string, send_index: int, bus_sends_count: int, distance_curve: object, applied_keys: [string], saved: bool }

commands.name: set_sound_wave_properties
commands.description: Merge USoundWave/USoundBase fields into a SoundWave asset (absent keys kept), set bLooping via looping, clamp to ClampMin/ClampMax and save; set_properties neither clamps nor saves. Each property whose value changes runs PostEditChangeProperty, as a details-panel edit does: compression settings rebuild the audio and MaxDistance follows AttenuationSettings. Keys match property names case-insensitively. A key that names no property (the error lists them), a deprecated or instanced-subobject one, a null value, a value of the wrong kind or that does not convert, bLooping inside settings, or a looping that is not true or false is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false.

params.name: sound_wave_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundWave (e.g. /Game/Audio/MySound).

params.name: settings
params.description: Object of USoundWave/USoundBase UPROPERTY fields to merge, keyed by property name (matched case-insensitively); absent keys untouched. e.g. CompressionQuality(1..100), SampleRateQuality(Max/High/Medium/Low/Min), SoundGroup(SOUNDGROUP_Default/SOUNDGROUP_Effects/SOUNDGROUP_UI/SOUNDGROUP_Music/SOUNDGROUP_Voice), SoundAssetCompressionType(BinkAudio/ADPCM/PCM/Opus/PlatformSpecific/ProjectDefined), Volume(>=0), Pitch(0.125..4.0), Priority(0..100), VirtualizationMode(Disabled/PlayWhenSilent/Restart/SeekRestart), SoundClassObject(asset path), AttenuationSettings(asset path). A key that names no property, a deprecated one or one holding instanced subobjects, a null value, a value that does not convert, a settings value that is not an object, or `bLooping` (use the `looping` param) is an error and nothing is changed.

params.name: looping
params.description: Optional bool; sets the bLooping bitfield directly (when this sound is played directly, not via a cue). A value that is not true or false is an error and nothing is changed.

commands.returns: { sound_wave_path: string, asset_class: string, settings: object, applied_keys: [string], applied_looping: bool, looping: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_submix_effect_settings
commands.description: Change the Settings struct of one effect preset in a USoundSubmix's effect chain, picked by chain index, through reflection: only the keys given are written, each clamped to its ClampMin/ClampMax, and settings echoes the whole struct read back. Read the chain first with get_submix_effect_chain; add_submix_effect_to_chain appends a preset and remove_submix_effect_from_chain takes one out. One undo step, then the submix package is saved, and so is the preset's own package when the preset is a separate asset appended by path (preset_in_submix_package=false) -- that asset is shared, so every submix that uses it hears the change. submix_saved and preset_saved report each save, and saved is both; a failed save of either makes success false with save_error. Repeating the same values changes nothing more. An index out of range, an empty slot, a preset class with no Settings struct or a value that does not convert is an error.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Full content path of the target USoundSubmix, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Submix_Music"

params.name: effect_index
params.description: 0-based index into SubmixEffectChain (same order add_submix_effect_to_chain appended / get_submix_effect_chain reports)

params.name: settings
params.description: Object of fields to merge into the preset's Settings struct, keyed by property name (case-insensitive), e.g. {"ThresholdDb": -12, "Ratio": 4} for a dynamics processor; absent keys untouched, unknown keys ignored

commands.returns: { submix_path: string, effect_index: int, preset_class: string, preset_path: string, preset_in_submix_package: bool, submix_saved: bool, preset_saved: bool, settings: object, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_subtitle_cue
commands.description: Updates the text and timing fields on an existing subtitle cue.  Loads the USubtitleAssetUserData, applies any combination of text / start_offset / duration / duration_type to Subtitles[cue_index], and saves. Fields not provided are left untouched.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Content path of the USubtitleAssetUserData asset.

params.name: cue_index
params.description: Zero-based index into the Subtitles array (required).

params.name: text
params.description: Optional new subtitle text (Subtitles[cue_index].Text); an empty string clears it.

params.name: start_offset
params.description: Optional new StartOffset (seconds).

params.name: duration
params.description: Optional new Duration (seconds).

params.name: duration_type
params.description: Optional new SubtitleDurationType ("use_sound_duration" or "use_duration_property").

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, cue_index: int, success: bool, applied_text: bool, applied_start_offset: bool, applied_duration: bool, applied_duration_type: bool, text?: string (when text was given, read back), start_offset: float, duration: float, duration_type: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: stop_sound
commands.description: Stop playback on an audio component of the editor world (UAudioComponent::Stop), found by object name (case-insensitive) among EVERY audio component of every actor, so an actor's second or third audio component is reached too; a name that components of several actors carry is an error listing the owners unless actor_name (object name, not label) picks one. Components in a running PIE world are not reached. Returns was_playing and playing, and audio_component_path and audio_owner_name naming the component stopped; success is always true once the component is found. Start playback with play_sound.

params.name: audio_component_name
params.description: Object name of the audio component to stop (e.g. "AudioComponent0"), compared without case against every audio component of every actor in the editor world.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Optional object name (not label) of the actor that owns the component, compared without case. Needed when several actors own an audio component of that name (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0); an empty one, one that names no actor, or one whose actor has no such component is an error.

commands.returns: { audio_component_name: string, audio_component_path: string, audio_owner_name: string, playing: bool, was_playing: bool, success: bool }

commands.name: audit_asset_references
commands.description: Sweeps the assets under folder_path for two reference problems: orphans (assets no package references, by Asset Registry metadata) and broken references (a dependency on a package that is no longer on disk; /Script/ C++ modules are skipped). Metadata-only: it never loads, changes or saves an asset, so it scales to large projects. Not read-only, though: the full lists go to a new JSON report under <Project>/Saved/MCPAudits/ (a call within the same second replaces the previous one), and the reply carries only the counts and the report path; read the lists with get_mcp_audit_report. Orphans are candidates, not proof: levels and assets loaded by name or from config have no referencers either. For one asset use get_asset_referencers or get_asset_dependencies; for unused assets only, find_unused_assets; delete with delete_asset and clean redirectors with fixup_redirectors.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to scan, e.g. "/Game/Props" or a plugin mount such as "/MyPlugin". Defaults to "/Game".

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders. Defaults to true.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on assets processed, clamped to 1-100000; defaults to 5000. The summary has no truncation flag: asset_count equal to the cap means the sweep was cut.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive), default "all"; any other value is treated as "all". Scopes BOTH the referencer check (orphan detection) and the dependency check (broken-reference detection) to that dependency kind. Use "hard" to find only the broken references that actually break loading -- a broken SOFT reference (TSoftObjectPtr/FSoftObjectPath) does not. "all" applies no Hard/Soft requirement at all.

commands.returns: { path: string, summary: { asset_count: int, orphan_count: int, broken_reference_count: int, dependency_type: string } }

commands.name: audit_blueprint_health
commands.description: Project-wide compile-sweep: RECOMPILES every Blueprint under folder_path and records error/warning counts. By far the heaviest audit here (it compiles, it does not just read metadata) and it runs synchronously in the editor -- ALWAYS scope it with folder_path on a large project, and lean on max_results, which is a hard cap. It returns only a summary plus a report path; read the detail back with get_mcp_audit_report. To find already-broken Blueprints WITHOUT recompiling anything, use find_erroring_blueprints instead.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content-relative folder to scan. Defaults to "/Game".

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders. Defaults to true.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on Blueprints compiled (1-100000). Defaults to 200 (lighter than the other audits -- compiling is expensive).

commands.returns: { path: string, summary: { blueprint_count: int, clean_count: int, error_count: int, warning_count: int } }

commands.name: audit_collision_profiles
commands.description: Aggregate report of every project collision profile AND every collision channel (built-in + custom), including which custom ECC_GameTraceChannelN slots are already taken -- the question to ask before add_collision_channel. Cheap: it reads the collision settings in memory, with no AssetRegistry scan and no asset loading, so unlike the other audit_* sweeps it takes no folder_path and no max_results. Returns a summary + a report path (read the detail with get_mcp_audit_report).
commands.returns: { path: string, summary: { profile_count: int, channel_count: int, custom_channels_in_use: int } }

commands.name: audit_replication
commands.description: Project-wide replication audit: for every Blueprint under folder_path, which variables are Replicated (CPF_Net), whether the class itself replicates (AActor::GetIsReplicated on the GeneratedClass CDO), and which UFUNCTIONs are RPCs (FUNC_NetFuncFlags). It returns only a SUMMARY plus a report path -- the full per-Blueprint detail is written to Saved/MCPAudits/ and must be read back with get_mcp_audit_report. For one actor rather than a sweep, use get_actor_replication_info.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content-relative folder to scan. Defaults to "/Game".

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders. Defaults to true.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on Blueprints processed (1-100000). Defaults to 1000.

commands.returns: { path: string, summary: { blueprint_count: int, replicated_class_count: int, replicated_variable_count: int, rpc_count: int } }

commands.name: audit_widget_accessibility
commands.description: Sweep Widget Blueprints for the accessibility problems that are measurable from what was AUTHORED: text/background contrast against the WCAG 2.x threshold, text smaller than a legible minimum, interactive widgets with no accessible label for a screen reader, and buttons below a minimum touch/focus size. On console this is a CERTIFICATION requirement, not a nicety. READ THE LIMITS BEFORE TRUSTING A PASS: contrast is computed against the FIRST ancestor holding a solid colour -- a UBorder's brush, a UButton's WidgetStyle.Normal, or a flat UImage -- so a background painted by a texture, a material, a video or a sibling drawn underneath is INVISIBLE to this, and those cases come back as background_source:"none" rather than quietly passing, because "could not judge" and "fine" are different answers. A brush only counts when it has no ResourceObject, its TintColor is UseColor_Specified, and its DrawAs actually FILLS the middle: Box, Image or RoundedBox. DrawAs=Border is excluded on purpose (it tiles the sides and leaves the centre empty, which is exactly where the text sits). Colours coming from a CommonUI style asset or a property binding are equally invisible: only authored values are read. What IS exact is the maths -- relative luminance 0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B over LINEAR values (which is what an FLinearColor already is) and ratio (Llight+0.05)/(Ldark+0.05), straight from WCAG.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to sweep (default /Game).

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders (default true).

params.name: min_contrast_ratio
params.description: Contrast floor for normal-size text (default 4.5, the WCAG AA rule). Text at or above large_text_size only needs 3.0, applied automatically.

params.name: large_text_size
params.description: Font size from which text counts as "large" for the contrast rule (default 18.0, per WCAG).

params.name: min_font_size
params.description: Smallest legible font size; anything under it is reported (default 12.0).

params.name: min_touch_size
params.description: Minimum width/height in pixels for an interactive widget's authored slot size (default 44.0, the common touch-target guideline). Only checkable when the slot actually carries a size -- an auto-sized slot reports size_known:false instead of a false pass.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max Widget Blueprints to load (default 500).

commands.returns: { folder_path, widget_blueprints_scanned, widgets_examined, issue_count, issues_by_kind: {low_contrast, contrast_unknown, small_text, missing_accessible_text, small_touch_target}, entries: [{ widget_bp_path, widget_name, widget_class, kind, detail, contrast_ratio?, required_ratio?, text_color?, background_color?, background_source?, font_size?, width?, height? }], truncated }

commands.name: audit_widget_style
commands.description: Sweep Widget Blueprints and report every widget whose style DEVIATES from a reference widget -- the "who is off-theme" question, which is the one that scales badly by hand once there are more than a couple of screens. You designate one widget as the truth (reference_bp_path + reference_widget_name), list the property paths that define the style (dotted paths work: "WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor"), and this reports, per matching widget, which of those paths differ and what each side holds. Comparison is on the property's exported text, so it is type-agnostic and reports a real difference rather than a formatting one. Pair it with apply_widget_style_preset, which can copy those same paths off that same reference widget to FIX what this finds.

params.name: reference_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint holding the reference widget (the style source of truth).

params.name: reference_widget_name
params.description: Name of the reference widget inside that Widget Blueprint.

params.name: property_paths
params.description: The paths that define the style, e.g. ["WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor","WidgetStyle.NormalPadding"]. A path that does not resolve on the REFERENCE is an error (the reference must define the style); one that does not resolve on a target is reported as unresolved, not as a deviation.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to sweep for targets (default /Game).

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders (default true).

params.name: target_class
params.description: Only compare widgets of this class, matched with IsA (defaults to the reference widget's own class, which is almost always what you want).

params.name: include_matching
params.description: Also report the widgets that already match (default false).

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max Widget Blueprints to load (default 500).

commands.returns: { reference, property_paths, widget_blueprints_scanned, widgets_compared, deviating_count, matching_count, entries: [{ widget_bp_path, widget_name, widget_class, deviations: [{path, actual, expected}], unresolved_paths: [string], matches: bool }], truncated }

commands.name: audit_widget_text
commands.description: Sweep Widget Blueprints and report which player-visible texts are typed INLINE rather than coming from a String Table -- the localization-maintainability question. NOTE: this corrects the intuition most people start with: a text written as a bare string is NOT lost to localization. Unreal assigns it a stable key when the package is saved, and FTextInspector::ShouldGatherForLocalization returns true, so it DOES get collected and translated. What it lacks is a MEANINGFUL identity: the namespace comes out empty and the key is an opaque GUID like 971E3B3B436AEE91028BA1ADB97B3046. That still costs -- translators see no context, and re-authoring the text churns the key, orphaning the translation. So this reports identity_kind per text: string_table (best), explicit (an author-given namespace/key), auto_key (typed inline, key generated on save) and none (never saved, no identity yet). Default output is everything that is NOT string_table or explicit.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to sweep (default /Game). Every UWidgetBlueprint under it is loaded and walked.

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subfolders (default true).

params.name: include_all
params.description: Also report the texts that already have a good identity, string_table and explicit ones included (default false).

params.name: include_data_assets
params.description: Also sweep DataTables and DataAssets under the same folder (default false). This is where an AAA game actually keeps its text -- item names, quest descriptions, tooltips -- and it is text the widget walk cannot reach, because there the FTexts sit in nested struct fields rather than on a widget class. Nested structs and arrays of structs are walked too.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max Widget Blueprints to load (default 500). Loading a WBP is not free; a whole-project sweep is a heavy call.

commands.returns: { folder_path, widget_blueprints_scanned, texts_examined, counts_by_identity: {string_table, explicit, auto_key, none}, not_gathered_count, entries: [{ widget_bp_path, widget_name, widget_class, property_name, text, identity_kind, will_be_gathered, namespace, key, string_table }], truncated } -- not_gathered_count is the engine's own ShouldGatherForLocalization saying a text will NOT be collected at all; in a saved asset that is normally 0, and anything above it is a real alarm.

commands.name: capture_pie_state
commands.description: Snapshot of every actor in the ACTIVE PIE world, with every property flagged Replicated or SaveGame (generic -- no judgment call about what is "relevant"). It requires a live PIE session: with none running for pie_client_index it errors cleanly instead of silently snapshotting the EDITOR world, which is what makes it usable as co-op evidence -- point it at a client index to prove a value really replicated. On a large world ALWAYS pass class_filter and/or max_actors. Returns a summary plus a report path; read the detail with get_mcp_audit_report.

params.name: pie_client_index
params.description: Which PIE client's world to snapshot (0 = first/server/standalone). Defaults to 0.

params.name: class_filter
params.description: Optional actor-class guardrail. Accepts a single class name OR an array of them (the hint is deliberately absent: the type-hint grammar has no union, and `[string|array]` would make this whole @param unparseable, leaving it an EMPTY description in the catalog). Detail: one class name or an array of them, each resolved to a UClass (object/script path, short name, or the Blueprint asset name -- "<Name>_C" is tried too) and matched with IsA, so subclasses match. An entry that does not resolve, or that resolves to a non-AActor class, is a hard ERROR rather than being dropped: dropping it would silently snapshot the whole World Partition world, keeping it would silently return an empty snapshot. Defaults to no filter (every actor).

params.name: max_actors
params.description: Optional cap on how many actors get their properties reflected into the report; 0 (the default) means UNLIMITED, and negative values are clamped to 0. Actors past the cap are still COUNTED (cheap) but not reflected (the expensive part), so total_matching_actors and truncated are exact, not estimated.

commands.returns: { path: string, truncated: bool, summary: { actor_count: int, actors_seen: int, total_matching_actors: int, max_actors: int, truncated: bool, class_filter: [string], replicated_property_count: int, savegame_property_count: int, savegame_filter_status: "active"|"dead_in_this_run" }, report_size_bytes: int, verification: {...}, verification_checks: [...] } -- class_filter lists the resolved class paths; success is false when the report is missing or empty on disk.

commands.name: get_mcp_audit_report
commands.description: Read back the FULL report that an audit_* or capture_pie_state command wrote to disk. Those commands return only a summary plus a path, so this is the second half of every one of them -- without it you never see the per-Blueprint / per-asset / per-actor detail. Restricted to Saved/MCPAudits/: it is not a general file reader.

params.name: path
params.description: Path returned by a prior audit command

commands.returns: the full parsed JSON report object

commands.name: add_behavior_tree_child
commands.description: Add a child under a BehaviorTree composite: a composite (Selector/Sequence/SimpleParallel) when composite is given, or a leaf task (Wait/MoveTo/PlaySound/RunBehavior/...) when task_class is given; exactly one of the two. The child is appended to the parent's Children (array order = execution order). Authoring is data-only: ParentNode/ExecutionIndex are assigned by the BT runtime at load (run_behavior_tree). Idempotent by child_name within the parent, whatever its kind. The returned child_name is how you address a composite as a parent for further children. Configure the node (a MoveTo's key, a Wait's time) with set_behavior_tree_node_property; read its settings with get_behavior_tree_node_properties.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Path to the UBehaviorTree asset (its RootNode must already be set via set_behavior_tree_root).

params.name: composite
params.description: Concrete composite class: "Selector" | "Sequence" | "SimpleParallel" (or a BTComposite_* class name). Give this or task_class, not both.

params.name: task_class
params.description: Concrete task class: "Wait" | "MoveTo" | "PlaySound" | "RunBehavior" | "FinishWithResult" (or a BTTask_* class name). Give this or composite, not both.

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional parent composite name (a child_name from a prior add); "Root" or omitted targets the RootNode.

params.name: child_name
params.description: Optional stable name for the new node (its identity for idempotency/addressing); defaults to the class type without its BTComposite_/BTTask_ prefix.

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path: string, parent_name: string, child_name: string, child_class: string, child_kind: "composite"|"task", already_exists: bool, child_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_behavior_tree_decorator
commands.description: Attach a decorator (execution condition) to a specific child-edge of a BehaviorTree composite.  The decorator is appended to that child's Decorators array and gates whether the child may run. Authoring is data-only: ParentNode/ExecutionIndex are assigned by the BT runtime at load (run_behavior_tree). Idempotent by decorator_name within the child-edge. Configure it (key, condition) with set_behavior_tree_node_property; read: get_behavior_tree_node_properties.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Path to the UBehaviorTree asset (its RootNode must already be set, with the target child added).

params.name: child_name
params.description: Name of the existing child (a child_name from a prior add_behavior_tree_child) whose edge the decorator gates.

params.name: decorator_class
params.description: Concrete decorator class: "Cooldown" | "Loop" | "TimeLimit" | "Blackboard" | ... (or a BTDecorator_* class name).

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional parent composite name owning the child-edge; "Root" or omitted targets the RootNode.

params.name: decorator_name
params.description: Optional stable name for the new decorator (its identity for idempotency); defaults to the decorator type.

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path: string, parent_name: string, child_name: string, decorator_name: string, decorator_class: string, already_exists: bool, decorator_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_behavior_tree_service
commands.description: Attach a service (background tick) to a BehaviorTree composite.  The service is appended to the composite's Services array and ticks while that composite branch is active. Authoring is data-only: ParentNode/ExecutionIndex are assigned by the BT runtime at load (run_behavior_tree). Idempotent by service_name within the composite. Configure it with set_behavior_tree_node_property; read: get_behavior_tree_node_properties.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Path to the UBehaviorTree asset (its RootNode must already be set via set_behavior_tree_root).

params.name: service_class
params.description: Concrete service class: "DefaultFocus" | "RunEQS" | ... (or a BTService_* class name).

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional composite name to attach the service to; "Root" or omitted targets the RootNode.

params.name: service_name
params.description: Optional stable name for the new service (its identity for idempotency); defaults to the service type.

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path: string, parent_name: string, service_name: string, service_class: string, already_exists: bool, service_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_blackboard_key
commands.description: Append one key to the own Keys of a UBlackboardData asset loaded by path, re-index its key IDs and save it; no undo step. key_type is Bool, Int, Float, Vector, Rotator, String, Name, Object, Class or Enum (case-insensitive); instance_synced defaults to false. An Object, Class or Enum key gets no base class or enum here: use set_blackboard_key_subsettings. Idempotent: a key of that name and type already there is a success with already_exists=true and saved=false, nothing added or saved (its instance_synced untouched); the same name with another type is an error. A name a parent blackboard already has is an error naming that parent, nothing added: a key of that name would shadow the parent's. verified confirms the key resolves by name. A failed save gives success false, saved=false and save_error, with the key added in memory. Inverse: remove_blackboard_key; read: get_blackboard_data; create the asset: create_blackboard_data.

params.name: blackboard_path
params.description: Path to the UBlackboardData asset.

params.name: key_name
params.description: New key name (must be unique on the asset).

params.name: key_type
params.description: One of Bool|Int|Float|Vector|Rotator|String|Name|Object|Class|Enum.

params.name: instance_synced
params.description: Whether the key is instance-synced (optional, default false)

commands.returns: { blackboard_path: string, key_name: string, key_type: string, key_count: number, verified: bool, saved: bool, already_exists: bool?, save_error: string?, note: string?, keys: [{ name, type, instance_synced }] }

commands.name: create_behavior_tree
commands.description: Create a UBehaviorTree asset at package_path/name (default folder /Game/AI), optionally bound to the UBlackboardData at blackboard_path, register it and save it; no undo step, and the tree starts with no root node (add one with set_behavior_tree_root). An existing tree at that path is returned with already_exists=true: when blackboard_path names a different blackboard it is rebound and saved (blackboard_rebound=true), otherwise it is left unchanged with saved=false and a message, nothing saved, so a repeat call is idempotent. A blackboard_path that does not load, or a name taken by an asset of another class, is an error; a failed save of a new or rebound tree gives success false with saved=false and save_error. Make the blackboard with create_blackboard_data; read the tree with get_behavior_tree_info; add nodes with add_behavior_tree_child.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. "BT_Enemy").

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/AI")

params.name: blackboard_path
params.description: Path to a UBlackboardData asset to bind to the new BT (optional)

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, behavior_tree_path: string, asset_path: string, blackboard_asset: string?, already_exists: bool, blackboard_rebound: bool?, saved: bool, save_error: string?, message: string? }

commands.name: create_blackboard_data
commands.description: Create a UBlackboardData asset with no parent at package_path/name (default folder /Game/AI), register it and save it; no undo step. Its only key is the one the engine seeds every new blackboard with, the SelfActor Object key (while AISystem bAddBlackboardSelfKey is on, the default), counted in key_count. Idempotent: a blackboard already at that path is returned unchanged with already_exists=true, saved=false, a message and its key_count, nothing saved. An invalid package name, or a name taken by an asset of another class, is an error; a failed save of the new asset -- refused while PIE runs, under a read-only root, or a read-only file -- gives success false with saved=false and save_error. blackboard_path is the object path the other blackboard tools take. Add keys with add_blackboard_key and constrain them with set_blackboard_key_subsettings; read them with get_blackboard_data; bind it to a tree with create_behavior_tree.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. "BB_Enemy").

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/AI")

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, blackboard_path: string, asset_path: string, key_count: number, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, message: string? }

commands.name: get_behavior_tree_info
commands.description: Read a UBehaviorTree asset found by content path: its name, its blackboard asset with every key it holds in key-ID order, parent blackboard keys first (name, type, instance_synced, the base class or enum subsettings, inherited, and defined_in naming the blackboard that declares the key), and the node tree from RootNode -- each node's name and class, a composite's services and children, and the decorators on each child edge, nested up to 64 levels. Nothing is written. A missing path, or one that does not load as a behavior tree, is an error; a tree with no root gives root_node null. The runtime state of a tree running on an AI actor is get_behavior_tree_status; blackboard asset details: get_blackboard_data; build the tree with set_behavior_tree_root, add_behavior_tree_child, add_behavior_tree_decorator and add_behavior_tree_service. A node's settings: get_behavior_tree_node_properties.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Content path of the UBehaviorTree asset, e.g. "/Game/AI/BT_Enemy"; a bare asset name is not resolved

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path: string, name: string, blackboard_asset: string|null, blackboard_keys: [{ name: string, type: string, instance_synced: bool, inherited: bool, defined_in: string }], root_node: object|null }

commands.name: get_behavior_tree_node_properties
commands.description: Read the settings of one node of a BehaviorTree asset -- a composite, a task, a decorator or a service, found by its node name anywhere in the tree -- as typed JSON: every editable property of its class (name, type, category, value), a blackboard key selector read as its key name with the key types it accepts (allowed_key_types), a value-or-key pair (a Wait's WaitTime) as {Key, DefaultValue}. property_name narrows it to one. Read-only. It reads what set_behavior_tree_node_property writes; the tree's shape and node names come from get_behavior_tree_info. A missing tree or node is an error listing the nodes; a name several nodes share is an error naming each, to narrow with parent_name.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Path to the UBehaviorTree asset.

params.name: node_name
params.description: Name of the node: the child_name, decorator_name or service_name given when it was added; "Root" for the root composite.

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional name of the composite (or, for a task's service, the task) holding the node, to pick one of several nodes with the same name; "Root" for the root.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional: read only this property (a dotted path into a struct is accepted, e.g. "WaitTime.DefaultValue").
