commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path, node_name, node_class, role: "root"|"composite"|"task"|"decorator"|"service"|"root_decorator", parent_name, blackboard_asset, property_count, properties: [{name, type, category, value, blackboard_key?, allowed_key_types?, value_or_blackboard_key?}] }

commands.name: get_behavior_tree_status
commands.description: Read the live state of the behavior tree component driving one actor: has_bt (whether a UBehaviorTreeComponent was found, through the actor's AIController brain or on the actor itself), is_running, is_paused, bt_asset_name (the tree it is running) and active_node_name (the node it is executing, empty when none). The actor is looked up in a running PIE world first, where possessed AI pawns run their trees, then in the editor world; world says which answered (pie or editor) and world_name names it. Read-only. An actor without a tree is a success with has_bt false; an actor found in neither world is an error. Inspect the tree asset itself with get_behavior_tree_info and blackboard values with get_blackboard_value; change the run state with run_behavior_tree, pause_behavior_tree, resume_behavior_tree, restart_behavior_tree or stop_behavior_tree, which look the actor up the same way.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the AI-possessed pawn, or of its AIController, e.g. 'BP_Guard_C_0'; searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world.

commands.returns: { actor_name, world: "pie"|"editor", world_name: string, has_bt: bool, is_running?: bool, is_paused?: bool, bt_asset_name?: string, active_node_name?: string }

commands.name: get_blackboard_data
commands.description: Dump a blackboard from its asset or from a running component. With blackboard_path, which wins when both are given, it reads the UBlackboardData asset: name, parent and key definitions (name, type, instance_synced, base class or enum subsettings). With actor_name, it reads the running UBlackboardComponent of that actor (its AIController blackboard, else one on the actor), the actor looked up in a running PIE world first, then in the editor world, with world (pie or editor) and world_name saying which answered: the component's name, has_valid_asset and num_keys, the key definitions of its blackboard asset as keys, and entries with each key's name, type and current value as text; a component with no asset gives empty lists. Either way every key is listed in key-ID order, those inherited from parent blackboards first, each with inherited and defined_in naming the asset that declares it. Nothing is written. No parameter, an asset that does not load, an actor found by object name or label in neither world, or no running blackboard is an error. One key: get_blackboard_value; write a value: set_blackboard_value; add a key: add_blackboard_key.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the pawn, its AIController, or an actor with its own UBlackboardComponent, whose running blackboard to dump, searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world (first match); ignored when blackboard_path is given

params.name: blackboard_path
params.description: Content path of a UBlackboardData asset to read instead, e.g. "/Game/AI/BB_Enemy"; takes precedence over actor_name

commands.returns: { actor_name: string?, world: "pie"|"editor"? (actor mode), world_name: string? (actor mode), blackboard_asset: string?, name: string?, parent: string?, component_name: string? (actor mode), has_valid_asset: bool? (actor mode), num_keys: number? (actor mode), keys: [{ name, type, instance_synced, base_class?, enum_type?, enum_name?, inherited, defined_in }], entries: [{ name, type, value, inherited, defined_in }]? (actor mode), key_count: number }

commands.name: get_blackboard_value
commands.description: Read one key of the running blackboard of an actor (its AIController blackboard, else one on the actor). The actor is looked up in a running PIE world first, then in the editor world; world says which answered (pie or editor) and world_name names it. value is a number for Int, Float and Enum keys, a bool for Bool, else a string (objects as paths). Read-only.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the actor whose blackboard to query, searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world (first match)

params.name: key_name
params.description: Name of the blackboard key to retrieve

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, world: "pie"|"editor", world_name: string, key_name: string, key_type: string, value: number|string|bool }

commands.name: pause_behavior_tree
commands.description: Pause the behavior tree of an actor (its AIController brain component, else a UBehaviorTreeComponent on the actor) with PauseLogic. The actor is looked up in a running PIE world first, then in the editor world; world says which answered (pie or editor) and world_name names it. paused is always true, not read back; was_running is measured. Runtime state only, nothing saved. An actor found in neither world, or one with no behavior tree component, is an error. Continue it with resume_behavior_tree.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the pawn, its AIController, or an actor with a UBehaviorTreeComponent, searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world (first match).

commands.returns: { actor_name, world: "pie"|"editor", world_name: string, paused, was_running }

commands.name: remove_behavior_tree_child
commands.description: Remove a child, composite or task, from a BehaviorTree composite.  Inverse of add_behavior_tree_child: drops the matching entry from the parent's Children array and saves. With kind, only child-edges of that kind are considered (a node of the other kind with the same name is untouched, and an index pointing at the other kind is an error); omitted, an edge of either kind matches. child_kind reports the kind of the edge removed. Idempotent: a missing child returns removed:false / already_absent:true.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Path to the UBehaviorTree asset.

params.name: child_name
params.description: Name of the child to remove (a child_name from a prior add_behavior_tree_child); provide this or 'index'.

params.name: index
params.description: Alternative to child_name: 0-based position in the parent's Children array.

params.name: kind
params.description: Optional edge kind to match: "composite" or "task"; omitted matches either. Any other value is an error.

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional parent composite name owning the child; "Root" or omitted targets the RootNode.

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path: string, parent_name: string, child_name: string, child_kind: "composite"|"task" (the edge removed; the requested kind, or absent, when nothing matched), removed: bool, already_absent: bool, child_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_behavior_tree_decorator
commands.description: Remove a decorator (execution condition) from a specific child-edge of a BehaviorTree composite.  Inverse of add_behavior_tree_decorator: drops the matching entry from that child's Decorators array (FBTCompositeChild::Decorators). Idempotent: a missing decorator returns removed:false / already_absent:true.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Path to the UBehaviorTree asset.

params.name: child_name
params.description: Name of the existing child (a child_name from a prior add) whose edge the decorator gates.

params.name: decorator_name
params.description: Name of the decorator to remove (a decorator_name from a prior add_behavior_tree_decorator); provide this or 'index'.

params.name: index
params.description: Alternative to decorator_name: 0-based position in the child-edge's Decorators array.

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional parent composite name owning the child-edge; "Root" or omitted targets the RootNode.

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path: string, parent_name: string, child_name: string, decorator_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, decorator_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_behavior_tree_service
commands.description: Remove a service (background tick) from a BehaviorTree composite.  Inverse of add_behavior_tree_service: drops the matching entry from the composite's Services array (UBTCompositeNode::Services). Idempotent: a missing service returns removed:false / already_absent:true.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Path to the UBehaviorTree asset.

params.name: service_name
params.description: Name of the service to remove (a service_name from a prior add_behavior_tree_service); provide this or 'index'.

params.name: index
params.description: Alternative to service_name: 0-based position in the composite's Services array.

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional composite name the service is attached to; "Root" or omitted targets the RootNode.

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path: string, parent_name: string, service_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, service_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_blackboard_key
commands.description: Remove a key from a UBlackboardData asset and save it.  Inverse of add_blackboard_key: drops the matching FBlackboardEntry from UBlackboardData::Keys (then UpdateKeyIDs to re-index). Addresses the key by key_name (as add_blackboard_key created it) or by index into the asset's own Keys array (parent-chain keys are not touched). Idempotent: a missing key returns removed:false / already_absent:true.

params.name: blackboard_path
params.description: Path to the UBlackboardData asset.

params.name: key_name
params.description: Name of the key to remove (as passed to add_blackboard_key); provide this or 'index'.

params.name: index
params.description: Alternative to key_name: 0-based position in this asset's own Keys array (excludes inherited parent keys).

commands.returns: { blackboard_path: string, key_name: string, key_type: string?, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, key_count: number, saved: bool, save_error?: string, keys: [{ name, type, instance_synced }] }

commands.name: restart_behavior_tree
commands.description: Restart the current behavior tree of an actor from its root (RestartTree), through its AIController brain component or a UBehaviorTreeComponent on the actor; a stopped tree starts again from the last tree it ran. The actor is looked up in a running PIE world first, then in the editor world; world says which answered (pie or editor) and world_name names it. restarted is always true, not measured: check get_behavior_tree_status. Runtime state only, nothing saved. An actor found in neither world, or one with no behavior tree component, is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the AI-possessed pawn (or AIController) whose UBehaviorTreeComponent to restart, searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world.

commands.returns: { actor_name, world: "pie"|"editor", world_name: string, restarted: bool }

commands.name: resume_behavior_tree
commands.description: Resume a behavior tree paused by pause_behavior_tree (ResumeLogic), through the actor's AIController brain component or a UBehaviorTreeComponent on the actor. The actor is looked up in a running PIE world first, then in the editor world; world says which answered (pie or editor) and world_name names it. Returns was_paused and is_paused, both read from the component. Runtime state only, nothing saved. An actor found in neither world, or one with no behavior tree component, is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the AI-possessed pawn (or AIController) whose UBehaviorTreeComponent to resume, searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world.

commands.returns: { actor_name, world: "pie"|"editor", world_name: string, was_paused: bool, is_paused: bool }

commands.name: run_behavior_tree
commands.description: Start a BehaviorTree asset with AAIController::RunBehaviorTree on an AIController or the pawn it possesses. The actor is looked up in a running PIE world first, where a placed pawn is possessed by its AI controller, then in the editor world, where no pawn is possessed (so an editor-world pawn errors with no AIController); world says which answered (pie or editor) and world_name names it. Returns started and ai_controller; runtime state only, nothing is saved. An actor found in neither world, a tree that does not load, or no AIController is an error. Read the run with get_behavior_tree_status; stop it with stop_behavior_tree.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the pawn or AIController, searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world (first match).

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Asset path of the UBehaviorTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/BT_Enemy"; a bare asset name is not resolved.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, world: "pie"|"editor", world_name: string, behavior_tree_path: string, started: bool, ai_controller: string }

commands.name: set_behavior_tree_node_property
commands.description: Write one setting of one node of a BehaviorTree asset -- a composite, task, decorator or service found by its node name -- then save the tree; no undo step. This is how a placed node is told what to do: a MoveTo's BlackboardKey, a Wait's WaitTime, a Blackboard decorator's key and condition. property_name is an editable property of the node's class or a dotted path into it. A blackboard key selector takes the key's NAME as a string: the key must exist in the tree's blackboard (or a parent) and be a type the selector accepts, else an error naming the keys; a value-or-key pair (WaitTime) takes a plain value for its DefaultValue or {"key": "<blackboard key>"}, a key of a type the pair accepts (a float pair takes a Float key); anything else takes typed JSON (numbers, bools, enum names, structs as objects). A property the class does not have, one that is not editable, or a value that does not fit is an error and nothing is written. The reply re-reads the property (value_after). Read: get_behavior_tree_node_properties; place nodes: add_behavior_tree_child / add_behavior_tree_decorator / add_behavior_tree_service.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: Path to the UBehaviorTree asset.

params.name: node_name
params.description: Name of the node (its child_name, decorator_name or service_name); "Root" for the root composite.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Editable property of the node's class (e.g. "BlackboardKey", "WaitTime", "AcceptableRadius") or a dotted path into one ("WaitTime.DefaultValue").

params.name: value
params.description: The value: a key name string for a blackboard key selector; a plain value or {"key": name} for a value-or-key pair; typed JSON otherwise.

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional name of the composite (or task) holding the node, to pick one of several nodes with the same name.

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path, node_name, node_class, property_name, value_after, key_type?, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_behavior_tree_root
commands.description: Give a BehaviorTree asset a new, empty root composite (Selector or Sequence) in one undo step, then save the asset. WARNING: the current root and everything under it (children, decorators, services) are dropped from the tree, so use it once on a tree from create_behavior_tree, which starts with no root, or to start a tree over. Then build under the root with add_behavior_tree_child, add_behavior_tree_decorator and add_behavior_tree_service, inspect with get_behavior_tree_info and run it with run_behavior_tree; for a StateTree use set_state_tree_root instead. Each call makes a fresh empty root, so repeating it ends in the same state but discards anything added since. An unsupported composite or a tree that does not load is an error and nothing changes. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the new root kept in memory.

params.name: behavior_tree_path
params.description: UBehaviorTree asset as a package or object path, e.g. "/Game/AI/BT_Guard".

params.name: composite
params.description: "Selector" (default: runs children until one succeeds) or "Sequence" (runs children until one fails), case ignored.

commands.returns: { behavior_tree_path: string, composite: string, has_root_node: bool, root_node_class: string, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: set_blackboard_key_subsettings
commands.description: Constrain an existing blackboard key's subsettings on a UBlackboardData asset and save. This is the SECOND HALF of add_blackboard_key, which only sets EntryName/KeyType/bInstanceSynced: it fills the per-type filter the editor would otherwise make you pick by hand -- BaseClass for an Object/Class key, EnumType for an Enum key. At least one of base_class / enum_type is required, and the one you supply must match the key's type. A value already in place is a no-op: already_set=true and saved=false, nothing saved.

params.name: blackboard_path
params.description: Path to the UBlackboardData asset.

params.name: key_name
params.description: Name of the existing key to constrain.

params.name: base_class
params.description: Class path/name (e.g. "/Script/Engine.Actor" or "Actor") for an Object/Class key (optional).

params.name: enum_type
params.description: Enum path/name (e.g. "/Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel") for an Enum key (optional).

commands.returns: { blackboard_path: string, key_name: string, key_type: string, base_class: string?, enum_type: string?, enum_name: string?, already_set: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string?, keys: [...] }

commands.name: set_blackboard_value
commands.description: Write one key of the running blackboard of an actor (its AIController blackboard, else one on the actor), converting the value string by key type. The actor is looked up in a running PIE world first, then in the editor world; world says which answered (pie or editor) and world_name names it. Not read back: set is always true, and an unparsable number or vector is written as 0. Runtime state only, nothing saved. Verify with get_blackboard_value.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the actor whose blackboard to modify, searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world (first match)

params.name: key_name
params.description: Name of the blackboard key to set

params.name: value
params.description: Value as a string, converted by key type: "42", "0.5", "true" or "1", a name, an enum index, a vector "X=1 Y=2 Z=3", a rotator "P=0 Y=90 R=0", an object or class path. Omitted means empty (0, false, none).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, world: "pie"|"editor", world_name: string, key_name: string, key_type: string, value: string, set: bool }

commands.name: stop_behavior_tree
commands.description: Stop the behavior tree of an actor with StopTree (Safe mode), through its AIController brain component or else a UBehaviorTreeComponent on the actor. The actor is looked up in a running PIE world first, then in the editor world; world says which answered (pie or editor) and world_name names it. Runtime state only, nothing saved. was_running is read before the stop (running and not paused); stopped is true when a started tree, running or paused, is no longer started afterwards. A tree that was not started is not an error: success with stopped false and a note. A tree still started after the call (a task still aborting) is an error. An actor found in neither world, or one with no behavior tree component, is an error. Unlike pause_behavior_tree it cannot be continued with resume_behavior_tree: start again with restart_behavior_tree (the last tree) or run_behavior_tree.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the pawn or AIController, searched in the PIE world first, then the editor world (first match)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, world: "pie"|"editor", world_name: string, was_running: bool, stopped: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: add_ai_perception_sense
commands.description: Configure a sight or hearing sense on an AIPerceptionComponent TEMPLATE of a Blueprint, creating the config as an Instanced subobject of the template so it persists with the asset, and saving the package. Idempotent: ConfigureSense dedups by config class, so re-calling with the same sense_type UPDATES the existing config in place instead of stacking a second one. Only "sight" and "hearing" are supported (no damage, touch or team senses). It authors the TEMPLATE only -- whether the AI actually perceives anything is a live-PIE question this cannot answer; read the authored result back with get_ai_perception_senses. Inverse: remove_ai_perception_sense.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint owning the component

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the AIPerceptionComponent SCS node

params.name: sense_type
params.description: "sight" or "hearing"

params.name: dominant
params.description: Optional bool; if true, sets this sense as the component's dominant sense

params.name: sight_radius
params.description: (sight) Maximum sight distance, cm (ClampMin 0)

params.name: lose_sight_radius
params.description: (sight) Distance to keep seeing an already-seen target, cm (ClampMin 0)

params.name: peripheral_vision_angle
params.description: (sight) Peripheral vision half-angle, degrees (Clamp 0..180)

params.name: hearing_range
params.description: (hearing) Hearing range, cm (ClampMin 0)

params.name: detect_enemies
params.description: Optional bool affiliation filter

params.name: detect_neutrals
params.description: Optional bool affiliation filter

params.name: detect_friendlies
params.description: Optional bool affiliation filter

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, sense_type, config_class, <sense fields>, note }

commands.name: add_blueprint_function
commands.description: Create a NEW function graph on a Blueprint, or with override=true a real OVERRIDE of an inherited/interface member: an event-shape member (no return value) becomes a genuine event OVERRIDE node in the event graph (node_id returned, placed at node_position), a value-returning one a real override FUNCTION graph (in ImplementedInterfaces[].Graphs for an interface member) -- the only correct route for interface events, since a hand-placed event node can compile yet never fire. The override is idempotent (was_already_overridden) and leaves the Blueprint needing a compile, unsaved. It REFUSES rather than guessing: a name that collides with an overridable inherited function errors with a hint instead of silently creating a "<name>_0" shadow, and an EVENT-shape member already shadowed by a local function graph errors telling you to remove that graph first. The new graph does not exist in the generated class until compile_blueprint, so compile BEFORE add_function_parameter or any node that calls it -- otherwise a build_blueprint_graph step fails with "Function not found" and rolls the whole batch back.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint (for override=true it must already implement the interface / inherit the virtual; implement_interface first).

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name for the new function; with override=true, the EXACT name of the inherited (interface or parent-class) function to override (e.g. "CanInteract", "GetInteractText").

params.name: override
params.description: Optional. When true, create an OVERRIDE of an inherited function ('My Blueprint > Override'): resolves the interface/parent-virtual signature and creates the override graph (function-shape) or event override node (event-shape) with the inherited signature + exact name -- NOT a new deduped function. When omitted and the name collides with an inherited overridable function, the call errors with a hint (instead of silently making a '<name>_0' shadow); pass override=false to force a brand-new function anyway.

params.name: node_position
params.description: Optional [x, y] canvas position for an event-override node that override=true CREATES (an existing one is not moved; a function graph has no single node to place).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, function_name: string, graph_name: string, success: bool [, kind, already_existed, created, was_already_overridden, node_id, already_exists, is_interface_function, note] } -- with override=true: kind='function' (graph_name is an editable function-override graph, ready to wire with get_graph_nodes / connect_pins) or kind='event' (an event OVERRIDE node was created or reused in the event graph graph_name names, and node_id is that node); created is !already_existed, and was_already_overridden is already_existed. success:true can come back WITHOUT the graph actually appearing, so confirm with get_blueprint_functions before wiring it.

commands.name: add_blueprint_timeline_track
commands.description: Add a track to a Timeline of a Blueprint, with optional keys, as the Timeline editor's "+ Track" does: a float, vector, color or event track whose curve is made inside the Blueprint, then the timeline node is reconstructed (a float/vector/color track gets an output pin of its name, an event track an exec output) and the Blueprint compiled; one undo step (the compile is not undone). The reply re-reads the timeline (tracks, output_pins). keys is [[time, value], ...]: value a number for float, [x,y,z] for vector, [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] for color, nothing for event ([time] or a bare time). A track name already used on the timeline, a malformed key or an unknown track_type is an error and nothing changes; so is a missing Blueprint or timeline. Keys past the timeline length stay but play only if length grows. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Timelines come from add_timeline_to_blueprint; read: get_blueprint_timeline_info; inverse: remove_blueprint_timeline_track.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint.

params.name: timeline_name
params.description: The timeline's variable name, as add_timeline_to_blueprint returned it.

params.name: track_type
params.description: float | vector | color | event

params.name: track_name
params.description: Name of the new track, unique on this timeline; it names the node's output pin.

params.name: keys
params.description: Optional keys, [[time, value], ...] (see the description for value by track type).

params.name: interpolation
params.description: Optional key interpolation for float/vector/color: "linear" (default) | "cubic" | "constant".

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, timeline_name, track_name, track_type, added, keys_added, curve, length, length_mode, auto_play, loop, replicated, ignore_time_dilation, track_count, tracks: [{track_name, track_type, curve, external_curve, key_count, keys: [{time, value}]}], node_id, graph_name, output_pins: [string] }

commands.name: add_blueprint_variable
commands.description: Add a MEMBER variable to a Blueprint (add_function_local_variable is the function-scoped twin), then read/write it with add_graph_node node_type=variable_get/variable_set. TRAP 1: the variable is born NOT editable per instance -- placing the actor and writing that variable fails with "cannot be edited on instances" -- and get_blueprint_variables reports instance_editable:true anyway; fix it with set_blueprint_variable_metadata(instance_editable=true). TRAP 2: on a class that ALREADY has actors placed in a level, those instances keep the value of the first compile, so a default set afterwards never reaches them -- verify on the instances, not on the CDO.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: New variable name (fails if the name already exists on this Blueprint).

params.name: variable_type
params.description: Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, or the name/path of a struct, enum, class or object (e.g. Vector, /Game/Dir/S_Foo.S_Foo, /Script/Engine.Actor).

params.name: is_array
params.description: When true, make the variable an array container; defaults to false. This is the ONLY array authoring path -- add_function_parameter has no equivalent.

params.name: default_value
params.description: Initial default value for the new variable, in exported-text form; optional

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, variable_type, is_array } -- an echo of the request, NOT a verification: read the variable back with get_blueprint_variables (or the CDO) before relying on it.

commands.name: add_broadcast_node
commands.description: Add the node that BROADCASTS (fires) an event dispatcher on self -- own or inherited -- with one input pin per signature parameter, so listeners run. Does NOT compile. The dispatcher must already exist in the compiled class (add_event_dispatcher then compile_blueprint), and its parameter pins only appear after set_event_dispatcher_signature. The opposite direction (LISTENING) is add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate" for self, add_object_bound_event for another object's dispatcher.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint that owns (or inherits) the dispatcher

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: Exact name of the multicast delegate to broadcast; resolved on the skeleton class, so inherited dispatchers work

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[execute, then, one input per signature param], blueprint_name, graph_name, dispatcher_name } -- an empty parameter list means the dispatcher has no signature yet.

commands.name: add_comment_node
commands.description: Add a resizable comment box (UEdGraphNode_Comment) with text to a graph, in one undo step. The text is written after the engine places the node (its PostPlacedNewNode resets the box to "Comment"), and the returned "comment" field is the box's text read back; without text the box keeps the engine's "Comment". It has NO pins, so a pin_defaults entry aimed at it breaks a whole build_blueprint_graph batch. Read back: get_graph_nodes (compact=false: compact skips comment boxes); remove: delete_node.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: text
params.description: Comment text shown in the box; omitted or empty leaves the engine default "Comment"

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: width
params.description: Comment box width in pixels; defaults to 400

params.name: height
params.description: Comment box height in pixels; defaults to 200

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment } -- no pins array; comment is the text the box holds, read back after placement.

commands.name: add_component_bound_event
commands.description: Bind a multicast delegate OF ONE OF THIS BLUEPRINT'S OWN COMPONENTS (OnComponentBeginOverlap, OnComponentHit, a vendor component's dispatcher...) to a generated handler event in the event graph -- the editor's component-event flow -- then compile and re-check that the binding registered (bound). ALSO WORKS ON A WIDGET BLUEPRINT: pass the WBP and a WIDGET's name as component_name to wire a Button's OnClicked, a Slider's OnValueChanged, a CheckBox's OnCheckStateChanged -- exactly what the Designer's "+ OnClicked" green button does, and the only headless route to it (bound:true, with a BndEvt__..._OnButtonClickedEvent created). A UMG widget is not an SCS component but IS a property of the generated class, which is all this needs. Idempotent: an identical binding is returned instead of duplicated. The Blueprint must already be compiled, since the component/widget has to exist as a property of the generated class. For a dispatcher on an object that is NOT self and NOT one of its components, use add_object_bound_event; for one on SELF, add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate".

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint OR a Widget Blueprint (already compiled).

params.name: component_name
params.description: SCS component variable name on this Blueprint (e.g. "BodyMesh"), OR -- on a Widget Blueprint -- the name of a widget in its tree (e.g. "Btn_Play"); resolved on the skeleton class, so inherited components and widgets work too.

params.name: delegate_name
params.description: Exact multicast delegate property name on the COMPONENT's class (e.g. "OnComponentBeginOverlap"). On a miss the error names the component class so the right delegate can be looked up.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...the delegate's params as OUTPUT pins...], blueprint_name, graph_name, component_name, delegate, custom_function_name, bound, already_exists? } -- bound is a post-compile re-lookup (the real oracle); already_exists is only present when an existing binding was reused.

commands.name: add_component_to_blueprint
commands.description: Add a component of any class (engine class or a Blueprint AC_* class) to a Blueprint's SCS, with an optional relative transform and parent, then compile. Pick it to change the Blueprint so every instance gets the component; add_component_to_actor adds one to a single placed actor only, and attach_blueprint_component re-parents a component that already exists. TRAP 1: on a CHILD Blueprint whose scene root is INHERITED, a SCENE component can end up written into the PARENT's SCS (source:"inherited", owner_class = the parent) -- which silently edits a vendor/library asset; non-scene ActorComponents land correctly on the child. TRAP 2: a scene component of a BLUEPRINT class, or one given a location, can report success without persisting and then materialize LATER as a duplicate. Both have the same oracle: get_blueprint_components right after, checking owner_class and source of the new node -- never the return value.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_type
params.description: Component class: a native short name ('StaticMesh', 'Box', 'Sphere'), a /Script path ('/Script/Engine.StaticMeshComponent'), OR a Blueprint component class given as its object path ('/Game/.../AC_Foo.AC_Foo_C'), a bare package path ('/Game/.../AC_Foo'), or a bare '<Name>_C' ('AC_Foo_C').

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name for the new component instance

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative location for scene components

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation for scene components

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative scale for scene components

params.name: transform
params.description: Optional {"location":[x,y,z], "rotation":[p,y,r], "scale":[x,y,z]} alias for scene components; any flat location/rotation/scale arg above wins over the matching axis in here if both are given.

params.name: parent_component_name
params.description: Optional parent for scene components; omit / "root" attaches under the Blueprint's EXISTING scene root (SCS or native) instead of force-adding a second orphan root node. May also name a NATIVE inherited scene component (e.g. ACharacter's "CharacterMesh0"), mirroring attach_blueprint_component. Ignored for non-scene ActorComponents (no transform, no hierarchy to join).

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Optional socket/bone name on the parent (AttachToName)

commands.returns: { component_name: string, component_type: string } -- an ECHO of the request with no owner, no source and no verification. It says nothing about WHERE the node landed: read get_blueprint_components afterwards.

commands.name: add_enhanced_input_action_node
commands.description: Add an Enhanced Input action event node (UK2Node_EnhancedInputAction) bound to a UInputAction asset. Unlike add_input_action_event_node -- which creates the LEGACY UK2Node_InputAction that does NOT fire under Enhanced Input -- this node exposes the real ETriggerEvent exec pins (Triggered/Started/Ongoing/Canceled/Completed) that fire from the Enhanced Input pipeline. Use this instead of polling IsInputKeyDown in a timer; it is rebind-aware (bound to the InputAction asset, not a raw key).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor/Pawn Blueprint.

params.name: input_action
params.description: Asset path (or short name) of the UInputAction to bind, e.g. "/Game/Input/IA_Crouch".

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, pins:[{name, direction, type, linked_to, default}], blueprint_name, graph_name, input_action, node_class } -- the created node WITH its freshly-allocated pins: ETriggerEvent exec outputs (Triggered/Started/Ongoing/Canceled/Completed) plus data outputs (ActionValue/ElapsedSeconds/TriggeredSeconds/InputAction). Wire it via connect_pins WITHOUT a follow-up get_graph_nodes.

commands.name: add_event_dispatcher
commands.description: Create an event dispatcher (multicast delegate) on a Blueprint: adds BOTH the delegate member variable and its signature graph, the way the editor's "+ Event Dispatcher" does. It starts with NO parameters -- give it a signature with set_event_dispatcher_signature. Everything downstream needs the class REGENERATED first, so compile_blueprint before add_broadcast_node (to fire it) or add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate" / add_object_bound_event (to listen).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: Name of the new event dispatcher; fails if a member variable of that name already exists

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, created } -- created is always true on success; confirm with get_event_dispatchers.

commands.name: add_function_local_variable
commands.description: Add a variable scoped to ONE function graph (interface-override graphs included), instead of a class member like add_blueprint_variable -- use it for scratch state that no other graph should see. Reach it from the graph with add_graph_node node_type=variable_get/variable_set and scope="local" (the default scope="auto" already prefers a local over a member of the same name). Inverse: remove_function_local_variable, whose reply lists the function's locals.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of an existing function graph (FunctionGraphs or an interface-override graph)

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Variable name; the call fails if the name already exists in that function

params.name: variable_type
params.description: Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, or a struct/enum/class/object name or path

params.name: default_value
params.description: Initial default value for the local variable, in exported-text form; optional

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, variable_name, variable_type } -- an echo of the request; local variables do NOT appear in get_blueprint_variables (which lists members), so verify from the graph itself.

commands.name: add_function_parameter
commands.description: Add an input or output (return) parameter to an existing Blueprint FUNCTION graph -- interface-override graphs included -- or to a MACRO graph (create_blueprint_macro), and reconstruct its Entry/Result node or the macro's input/output tunnel. A macro also takes param_type "exec", an execution pin, so it can get several exec inputs and outputs. TWO HARD LIMITS, both silent-ish: it cannot create an ARRAY parameter (there is no is_array; the param comes out SCALAR with success), so redesign the signature to read the array where it lives; and it cannot reach a CUSTOM EVENT ("Function graph not found"), so a Server/Client RPC WITH arguments must be authored as a function plus set_blueprint_function_rpc. On a Blueprint just given a new function, compile_blueprint between creation and this call. Inverse: remove_function_parameter.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of an existing function graph (FunctionGraphs or an interface-override graph), or of a macro graph of this Blueprint when no function has that name. A custom event is NOT a function graph and is rejected here.

params.name: param_name
params.description: New parameter name; made unique, so the applied name is the one echoed back in the response.

params.name: param_type
params.description: Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, or a struct/enum/class/object name or path; "exec" on a macro. Arrays are NOT expressible.

params.name: is_output
params.description: When true, add an output/return param (an input pin on the Result node) instead of an input; defaults to false

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, param_name, param_type, is_output, graph_kind? } -- param_name is the pin name actually created (uniquified); graph_kind is "macro" when the parameter went on a macro. Verify with get_graph_nodes at compact=false: compact hides the new, still-unlinked pin and makes it look like nothing was created.

commands.name: add_graph_node
commands.description: Create ONE node in a Blueprint's event/function graph (node_type selects the kind) and return it WITH its freshly allocated pins, so connect_pins / set_pin_default_value can wire it immediately without a follow-up get_graph_nodes; with compile=true it also compiles the Blueprint afterwards. Use build_blueprint_graph instead when several nodes must be created AND wired in a single undo transaction, and get_function_pins to learn a call_function's pin names BEFORE creating anything. node_type='event' creates a REAL override (the declaring interface/parent class is resolved automatically and bOverrideFunction is set; target_class is ignored here; an existing override is returned with already_exists:true) and fails loudly for a name that is not an overridable event -- an interface method WITH a return value is not an event, use add_blueprint_function with override=true. node_type='custom_event' is idempotent by name (an existing custom event of that name in the graph comes back with already_existed:true, since a second one breaks the compile); a custom event cannot be given parameters, so anything that needs arguments (an RPC in particular) must be a function. node_type='get_component_by_class' makes a GetComponentByClass node BORN TYPED to target_class, so its ReturnValue connects without a cast -- inside build_blueprint_graph a generic one would be connected before its class pin default is applied and fail.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name (resolved under /Game/Blueprints) or full asset path. Pass the FULL path when the short name is ambiguous: a bare name that matches two assets resolves to one of them silently.

params.name: node_type
params.description: One of event, custom_event, call_function, print_string, variable_get, variable_set, branch, sequence, self, cast, spawn_actor (alias spawn_actor_from_class), create_widget, make_struct, break_struct, get_array_item, select, make_array, make_set, make_map, switch_int, switch_string, switch_name, switch_enum, enum_literal, format_text, foreach, foreach_with_break, do_once, gate, flipflop, for_loop, while_loop, is_valid, add_delegate, macro_instance, get_component_by_class

params.name: event_name
params.description: Event name; required for event and custom_event node types (e.g. "ReceiveActorBeginOverlap", "ReceiveBeginPlay" for event)

params.name: function_name
params.description: Function to call; required for call_function node type

params.name: target_class
params.description: Class owning the function or cast/spawn target class; required for cast, create_widget and get_component_by_class. For call_function it is searched STRICTLY: a function that is not on that class is an error, never a silent fallback to another library; it also resolves a user BlueprintFunctionLibrary by asset path ("/Game/Dir/BFL_X"). For get_component_by_class it is the component class to fetch (a UActorComponent subclass). For variable_get/variable_set it names the class that owns the variable, producing a non-self member-access node (with a 'target' pin) instead of a self-context node. For create_widget it names the widget class to construct (e.g. WBP_Foo_C, a full asset path, or the widget Blueprint short name); the node exposes that widget's Expose-On-Spawn pins.

params.name: function_library
params.description: Optional, call_function only: the library class owning function_name, used instead of target_class -- an engine library by name ("KismetMathLibrary", "KismetSystemLibrary", "GameplayStatics", "KismetStringLibrary", with or without the U prefix, or any /Script/Engine class) or a user BlueprintFunctionLibrary asset path ("/Game/Dir/BFL_X", "/Game/Dir/BFL_X.BFL_X" or the "..._C" class). Searched strictly, like target_class.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Variable to get/set; required for variable_get and variable_set

params.name: scope
params.description: Optional scope hint for variable_get/variable_set: 'auto' (default; a function-local variable declared in the target graph wins, else a self/member variable), 'local' (function-local variable ONLY), or 'member' (member variable only -- self, or on target_class when supplied). Ignored by other node types.

params.name: struct_type
params.description: Struct type; required for make_struct and break_struct nodes: a UScriptStruct path (/Game/.../S_Foo.S_Foo), bare name, or engine alias (Vector/Rotator/Transform...)

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Enum path or name; required for switch_enum and enum_literal nodes. Optional for select: the enum then drives the Index pin and one option pin is generated per enum entry.

params.name: index_type
params.description: Optional alias of enum_path for node_type=select.

params.name: option_count
params.description: Optional, select only: total number of option pins to end up with (default the built-in 2; ignored when an enum drives the index).

params.name: num_inputs
params.description: Optional input-pin count for make_array/make_set/make_map (added after spawn)

params.name: cases
params.description: Optional string array of case pins for switch_int/switch_string/switch_name

params.name: arguments
params.description: Optional string array of argument names for format_text

params.name: dispatcher
params.description: Event-dispatcher (multicast delegate) name; required for add_delegate node type. Must already exist in the COMPILED class (add_event_dispatcher + compile_blueprint), and it binds on self only -- for a dispatcher on another class use add_object_bound_event.

params.name: macro_graph_name
params.description: Macro graph name; required for node_type=macro_instance. Resolved against this Blueprint's own MacroGraphs first, then the engine StandardMacros; "<library-path>:<MacroGraphName>" (e.g. "/Game/Lib/ML_X.ML_X:MyMacro") resolves it in that macro library instead.

params.name: macro_library
params.description: Optional, macro_instance only: asset path of a macro LIBRARY Blueprint to resolve macro_graph_name in -- the only way to reach a third-party or project macro library.

params.name: macro_source
params.description: Set to "standard_macros" to skip this Blueprint's own MacroGraphs and resolve macro_graph_name only in the engine StandardMacros library. Only read for node_type=macro_instance.

params.name: compile
params.description: Optional bool, default false: compile the Blueprint after placing the node. Ignored inside build_blueprint_graph, which never compiles its steps.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment, pins:[{name, direction:'input'|'output', type, linked_to, default}], blueprint_name, graph_name, compiled, event_name?, node_title?, already_existed?, is_override?, already_exists?, cast_to?, function_library?, function?, struct_type?, index_pin?, return_value_pin?, option_pins?, option_count?, index_enum?, input_pins?, output_pins?, component_class?, return_pin_type? } -- the created node WITH its freshly-allocated pins. The pin names are already here, so you can wire the node via connect_pins/set_pin_default_value WITHOUT a follow-up get_graph_nodes. The optional fields belong to their node_type: event_name/node_title/already_existed for custom_event; event_name/is_override/already_exists for event (is_override:true is what tells a live override from a dead look-alike); cast_to for cast; function_library/function for call_function; struct_type for make_struct/break_struct; index_pin/return_value_pin/option_pins/option_count/index_enum for select; input_pins/output_pins (pin names by direction) for macro_instance; component_class/return_pin_type for get_component_by_class (return_pin_type is the oracle: if it does not name the requested class, the pin stayed generic). Read "class" as a sanity check: a node_type that was expected to produce an async/latent node and comes back as "K2Node_CallFunction" is a mute no-op that still compiles 0/0.

commands.name: add_input_action_event_node
commands.description: Add the LEGACY action-mapping event node (UK2Node_InputAction) bound to an action mapping NAME, and compile. WARNING: this node does NOT fire under Enhanced Input, which is what UE5 projects use -- it compiles clean and simply never runs. For an Enhanced Input action asset use add_enhanced_input_action_node, whose Triggered/Started/Completed pins actually execute. Only reach for this one on a project still using the legacy input mappings.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor/Pawn Blueprint (SupportsInputEvents is enforced).

params.name: input_action_name
params.description: Name of the LEGACY action mapping. It is not validated against the project's mappings: a typo yields a node that never fires.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[Pressed, Released, Key], blueprint_name, graph_name, input_action_name, node_class } -- node_class should read K2Node_InputAction (the legacy node); nothing here proves the mapping exists.

commands.name: add_object_bound_event
commands.description: Bind a BlueprintAssignable event dispatcher of an EXTERNAL object (not self, not a component) to a handler custom event -- the editor's right-click "Assign" flow (FEdGraphSchemaAction_K2AssignDelegate). Use this to react to a dispatcher on a widget/actor instance held in a variable (e.g. a UMG widget's "On Radial Menu Item Selected"): it spawns a UK2Node_AddDelegate bound to target_class' dispatcher with its self/target pin LEFT UNCONNECTED (you wire the instance) and a UK2Node_CustomEvent whose OUTPUT pins mirror the dispatcher's params (e.g. the segment-data struct), already wired to the AddDelegate's Delegate pin. Unlike the add_delegate node_type (self-context only), this reaches a dispatcher on a foreign class. Does NOT compile the Blueprint (mirrors the engine action); compile afterward.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint being edited (the object that will bind the event, e.g. the hub component BP).

params.name: target_class
params.description: The EXTERNAL class that owns the dispatcher. Accepts a Blueprint/widget short name, a full asset path, a full class path (/Game/.../WBP.WBP_C), a native /Script path, or the generated "..._C" class name. Prefer a full path or the "_C" class for reliable resolution.

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: The multicast delegate (event dispatcher) property to assign. Matched tolerantly: exact name, spaces stripped, or the display name (so "On Item Selected" resolves to the spaceless FName). On failure the error lists the assignable delegates found on target_class.

params.name: event_name
params.description: Optional desired name for the handler custom event; made unique in the Blueprint. Defaults to "<Dispatcher>_Event".

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, graph_name, target_class, dispatcher, add_delegate_node_id, custom_event_node_id, custom_event_name, wired, node_id, pins:[...] (the AddDelegate node's pins -- wire 'self'/Target = the widget instance and 'execute'/'then' into your exec flow), custom_event:{ node_id, pins:[...] } (hang handler logic off its 'then'/'output_delegate' and read the dispatcher's param output pins) }

commands.name: add_parent_call_node
commands.description: Add a "Parent: <Function>" node that calls the parent-class implementation of an overridden function/event -- the second half of the child-first shape "Event X -> Parent: X -> our logic" that keeps a vendor base class working while the child adds behaviour. Searches the WHOLE ancestor chain, not just the immediate parent. Does NOT compile, and IS allowed inside build_blueprint_graph, so the event + super + logic can be built in one transaction.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint whose parent function is called

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the overridden function/event whose parent implementation to call; must exist on some ancestor or the call errors

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph (usually the override's own graph); defaults to the event graph

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[execute, then, the parent's params], blueprint_name, graph_name, function_name, parent_class } -- parent_class names the ancestor that actually declares the implementation being called.

commands.name: add_reroute_node
commands.description: Add a reroute/knot node: pure layout, it re-emits whatever is wired into it and changes no behaviour. Does NOT compile. Note when reading graphs back: get_graph_nodes with compact=true excludes knots by default, so a chain that looks broken there may simply route through one -- re-read with exclude_classes=[].

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...wildcard in/out until wired...], blueprint_name, graph_name }

commands.name: add_timeline_to_blueprint
commands.description: Add a Timeline to an Actor Blueprint: creates BOTH the UTimelineTemplate variable and its UK2Node_Timeline node in one call, sets a fixed length in seconds, compiles, and verifies the template really registered (timeline_created). Actor-derived Blueprints only. It authors no curves or tracks itself -- the node comes with Play/Stop/Reverse inputs and Update/Finished outputs and nothing driven; add tracks with add_blueprint_timeline_track and read them with get_blueprint_timeline_info. A requested name already in use is silently uniquified, so wire the RETURNED timeline_name.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint.

params.name: timeline_name
params.description: Desired variable name for the timeline; if it is taken, a unique one is generated and returned instead.

params.name: length
params.description: Timeline length in seconds (sets fixed-length mode); defaults to 5.0

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, class, title, pins:[...], blueprint_name, graph_name, timeline_name, length, timeline_created, timeline_guid } -- timeline_name is the name ACTUALLY used and timeline_created is a post-compile re-lookup of the template, so false means the variable did not survive.

commands.name: apply_material_to_blueprint
commands.description: Assign a material ASSET to one slot of a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (an OWN SCS node, not a placed actor) -- the persistent counterpart of set_mesh_material_color, which only builds a runtime dynamic instance. Does NOT compile and does NOT save. Actors ALREADY placed in a level keep their serialized material: change the template and the placed instances stay as they were.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS component; must be a UPrimitiveComponent

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInterface (material or material instance) to assign; a path that does not load is an error

params.name: material_slot
params.description: Optional material slot index; defaults to 0. It is not range-checked against the mesh's slot count.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, material_path: string, material_slot: int, success: bool } -- an echo: success:true only means the material loaded and SetMaterial was called. Read it back with get_blueprint_material_info.

commands.name: attach_blueprint_component
commands.description: Re-parents a component already in a Blueprint's Components tree (an SCS component), at an optional socket or bone: under another SCS component, under a native scene component inherited from a C++ parent (e.g. ACharacter's "CharacterMesh0", so its sockets are reachable), or under the scene root when parent_component_name is omitted or "root". The Blueprint is then compiled and left unsaved (save_asset writes it). Idempotent: a component already under that parent with the same socket returns already_attached true and nothing is recompiled. Refused with nothing changed when the Blueprint, the component or the parent is not found, or when the parent is the component itself or one of its descendants. Refused while Play-in-Editor runs unless force=true. To add a new component use add_component_to_blueprint (inverse: remove_component_from_blueprint); read the tree with get_blueprint_components; for actors placed in a level use attach_actor.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path (e.g. "/Game/Characters/BP_Hero") or bare asset name, looked up under /Game/Blueprints first and then anywhere under /Game.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Variable name of the SCS component to move (the child), as get_blueprint_components lists it; inherited native components cannot be moved.

params.name: parent_component_name
params.description: Optional parent component name, as get_blueprint_components lists it; omit / "root" / the native root name attaches to the scene root. May also name a NATIVE inherited scene component (e.g. "CharacterMesh0") to parent the child natively to it.

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Optional socket or bone name on the parent (AttachToName), e.g. "hand_r"; not checked against the parent's mesh, and omitting it clears any socket.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, parent, parent_is_native, attach_socket, already_attached }

commands.name: build_blueprint_graph
commands.description: Build several nodes, wire their pins, and set pin defaults in one pass, wrapped in a single undo transaction -- the way to author a whole graph shape without create -> get_graph_nodes -> connect round-trips (get_function_pins gives you the pin names up front). THE ORDER IS FIXED AND MATTERS: every node first, then ALL connections, then pin_defaults -- so a node whose TYPE depends on a pin default (a generic GetComponentByClass) is connected while still untyped, fails with "... is not compatible with ..." and, under stop_on_error's default true, takes the whole call down; use add_graph_node node_type="get_component_by_class", which is born typed. add_comment_node has no pins at all, so a pin_defaults entry aimed at one also kills the batch. Self-contained: each sub-step runs its command directly, never through the bridge (only these: add_graph_node, add_timeline_to_blueprint, add_component_bound_event, add_input_action_event_node, add_enhanced_input_action_node, add_reroute_node, add_comment_node, add_parent_call_node, add_broadcast_node, add_object_bound_event), and no step compiles: an add_graph_node step's compile param is ignored, so compile_blueprint once afterwards.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: nodes
params.description: [{id: string, command_type: string, params?: object}, ...] (required, non-empty). 'id' is a caller-chosen local key used to reference the node from 'connections'/'pin_defaults'; 'params' is that command's own param object (blueprint_name/graph_name are auto-filled if omitted). WORKED EXAMPLE (print "hi" on BeginPlay, one call): nodes=[{"id":"beg","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"event","event_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}},{"id":"print","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"print_string"}}], connections=[{"from_node":"beg","from_pin":"then","to_node":"print","to_pin":"execute"}], pin_defaults=[{"node":"print","pin":"InString","value":"hi"}]. Pin names for a call_function node are knowable up front via get_function_pins (so no create->get_graph_nodes->connect round-trips). Child-override canonical shape (call the parent first), one call: nodes=[{"id":"evt","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"event","event_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}},{"id":"super","command_type":"add_parent_call_node","params":{"function_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}}], connections=[{"from_node":"evt","from_pin":"then","to_node":"super","to_pin":"execute"}]. NOTE on add_object_bound_event: it creates TWO nodes; the step's local 'id' resolves to the UK2Node_AddDelegate (wire the external instance into its 'self' pin and the exec flow into 'execute'), while the handler custom event is addressable as "<id>.custom_event" and its real NodeGuid is echoed back as custom_event_node_id.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: connections
params.description: [{from_node, from_pin, to_node, to_pin}, ...]; from_node/to_node may be a local 'id' from 'nodes' (or "<id>.custom_event" for an add_object_bound_event step's handler event) or a pre-existing real NodeGuid.

params.name: pin_defaults
params.description: [{node, pin, value}, ...]; node may be a local 'id' from 'nodes' (or "<id>.custom_event") or a pre-existing real NodeGuid.

params.name: stop_on_error
params.description: Stop (and try to roll back the whole transaction) on the first failing step; defaults to true, unlike batch's default false, since connections/pin_defaults depend on earlier nodes existing. With stop_on_error:false there is NO rollback at all -- the editor's global undo is never touched, every step is attempted, and whatever half-built shape remains is cleaned up with delete_node/disconnect_pin. That is the safer mode when other work is live in the editor's undo buffer.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, graph_name, nodes: [{index, id, command_type, ok, node_id?, custom_event_node_id?, error?}], connections: [{index, ok, error?}], pin_defaults: [{index, ok, error?}], stopped_early, rollback_required, rolled_back, transaction_opened, undo_queue_len_before, undo_queue_len_after, top_transaction_title, rollback_refused_reason?, warning? }. rolled_back reports whether the undo ACTUALLY ran, not the intention: the rollback is refused (rolled_back:false + rollback_refused_reason + warning) whenever the top of the editor's undo stack is not this call's own transaction, because GEditor->UndoTransaction is global and would otherwise revert another agent's or another session's work in memory while the disk stays clean. A payload that fails pre-validation returns instead { success:false, error, validation_errors: [{section, index, id?, error}], transaction_opened:false, blueprint_name, graph_name } and never opens a transaction.

commands.name: compile_blueprint
commands.description: Compile a Blueprint to regenerate its class, returning the REAL outcome (succeeded == zero errors) plus the error/warning counts, and with return_messages=true the per-message log with each message anchored to its node_id/graph. Required after authoring functions, variables or RPCs and before anything calls them. TRAP: num_errors:0 is not a promise the graph works -- an unresolved WILDCARD pin on an array/ForEach node can compile clean and still block PIE, and warnings (a "was pruned" node whose consumers silently read defaults) do not lower it, so read the warnings too. Compiling dirties the package and can cascade into other packages; check_blueprint_errors / find_erroring_blueprints answer without a compile.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint, or its full asset path (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Core/BP_MyActor). A short name matching two assets compiles ONE of them silently -- pass the full path when in doubt.

params.name: return_messages
params.description: Optional (default false). When true, ALSO returns the per-message compiler results log so callers can see node-anchored errors/warnings. When false/absent the response omits the `messages` array but still reports the REAL compile status.

commands.returns: { name: string, compiled: bool, succeeded: bool, num_errors: int, num_warnings: int } -- `compiled`/`succeeded` reflect the ACTUAL compile outcome (true iff zero errors; warnings still compile). Both the default and return_messages paths return these fields. When return_messages=true additionally { messages: [{severity: 'error'|'warning'|'note', text: string, node_id: string, node_title: string, graph_name: string}] } (node_id/node_title/graph_name are empty strings when the message is not anchored to a graph node)

commands.name: connect_pins
commands.description: Wire one node's OUTPUT pin to another node's INPUT pin inside one Blueprint graph, type-checked by the K2 schema (an incompatible pair is returned as an error, never a silent no-op). Nodes are addressed by NodeGuid, pins by name. Either node that still carries a WILDCARD pin is reconstructed afterwards, so array / ForEach / Select pins really re-type instead of compiling into "The type of Target Array is undetermined" (which compile_blueprint reports as compiled:true). Use validate_pin_connection to test a pair without mutating, and build_blueprint_graph to create+wire in one transaction.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: source_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the source node (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes).

params.name: source_pin
params.description: Output pin name on the source node (e.g. "then", "ReturnValue"). An output pin of that name is preferred; any pin with the name is accepted as a fallback.

params.name: target_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the target node.

params.name: target_pin
params.description: Input pin name on the target node (e.g. "execute", "Condition").

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. BOTH nodes must live in this same graph.

commands.returns: { connected, source_node_id, target_node_id } -- connected is always true when the call succeeds; the failure path is an error response, so there is no false to check.

commands.name: create_blueprint
commands.description: Create a new Blueprint asset, optionally as a child of ANY parent class -- native or another Blueprint (pass its "..._C" class or asset path) -- and save it to disk immediately unless PIE is running or save=false. This is also the way to make the framework classes (a GameMode, GameState, PlayerController, PlayerState, GameInstance or HUD Blueprint: pass that class as parent_class) and Blueprint subsystems (parent_class a USubsystem class such as "GameInstanceSubsystem"; lifetime says which family), and it makes Blueprint Function Libraries and Macro Libraries, which have no Actor parent and which the normal path would reject. It does NOT create interfaces (create_blueprint_interface). A plain Blueprint already at the path is returned unchanged with already_exists=true and saved=false, nothing saved and blueprint_type not applied -- when parent_class is given, only if its parent is parent_class or derives from it, otherwise it is an error and nothing is changed; another asset class there (a Widget or Anim Blueprint included) is an error and nothing is created. It never confirms the parent of a new Blueprint: read it back with get_blueprint_parent.

params.name: name
params.description: Blueprint name. Either a bare name (created under 'path' or /Game/Blueprints/) OR a full content path ("/Game/MyGame/Systems/World/BP_Foo"); an object-path form ("/Game/.../BP_Foo.BP_Foo") is also accepted.

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Optional parent class. Accepts a native name ("Actor", "Pawn", "Character", "GameModeBase", "PlayerController", "GameInstanceSubsystem", "BlueprintFunctionLibrary"), a "/Script/Module.Class" path, a Blueprint generated-class path ("/Game/.../BP_X.BP_X_C"), or a Blueprint asset path ("/Game/.../BP_X"). Defaults to AActor. Passing "BlueprintFunctionLibrary" makes a Function Library. When given, a Blueprint already at the path must have it (or a subclass of it) as parent.

params.name: blueprint_type
params.description: Optional Blueprint type override: "normal" (default), "function_library" (a UBlueprintFunctionLibrary of static functions; parent_class is ignored/forced), or "macro" (a Macro Library; keeps parent_class or defaults to Actor). Function-library is also auto-detected from parent_class="BlueprintFunctionLibrary".

params.name: path
params.description: Optional target content folder ("/Game/MyGame/Systems"). Used only when 'name' is a bare name; ignored when 'name' is already a full path.

params.name: save
params.description: Optional bool (default true). false registers the new Blueprint and marks its package dirty without saving it -- persist it later with save_asset.

commands.returns: { name: string, path: string, package_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, blueprint_type: string, already_exists: bool, saved: bool (false for a Blueprint already there: nothing saved), save_error?: string, note?: string, is_multiplayer?: bool, lifetime?: string } -- parent_class is, for a new Blueprint, what was REQUESTED and resolved, not proof the asset carries it (confirm a child's real parent with get_blueprint_parent), and for one already there its own parent. is_multiplayer appears for a GameMode (true when the parent derives from AGameMode); lifetime for a subsystem (Editor, Engine, GameInstance, World, LocalPlayer or Unknown). saved:false is honest: it carries save_error when PIE was running or the Blueprint already there has unsaved changes, and a note when save=false or an existing Blueprint is returned unchanged -- an unsaved Blueprint exists only in the editor and a later compile on it also returns success.

commands.name: create_blueprint_macro
commands.description: Create an EMPTY, Tunnel-terminated macro graph owned by this Blueprint's MacroGraphs (a reusable snippet, not a function: macros inline at compile time and can carry multiple exec outputs). Idempotent -- an existing macro of that name is returned with already_existed:true. Fill it with add_graph_node using graph_name=<macro>, then instantiate it with add_graph_node node_type="macro_instance", which finds the Blueprint's own macros. Give it inputs and outputs (exec included) with add_function_parameter function_name=<macro>; inverse: remove_blueprint_macro.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: macro_name
params.description: Name for the new macro graph.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, macro_name, graph_name, already_existed } -- graph_name is what to pass as graph_name / macro_graph downstream.

commands.name: create_editor_utility_blueprint
commands.description: Create an Editor Utility Blueprint at package_path/name with the editor factory, parented to parent_class, then compile and save it. Idempotent by path: an Editor Utility Blueprint already there is returned as it is (created=false, already_existed=true, saved=false), nothing compiled or saved, with the parent_class it really has; the requested parent_class is not applied to it. A parent_class that does not resolve or cannot back a Blueprint, another kind of asset at that path, or an invalid path is an error and nothing is created. A failed save makes success false with save_error and keeps the new asset in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. A tool with a UI panel: create_editor_utility_widget_blueprint. Right-click actions are made here too: parent_class "AssetActionUtility" (Content Browser assets) or "ActorActionUtility" (level actors) -- their CallInEditor functions become the actions.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities"; a trailing slash is ignored.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without path or extension, e.g. "EUB_BatchRename".

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Parent class by name without the U or A prefix, e.g. "EditorUtilityActor", or by path such as "/Script/Blutility.EditorUtilityObject" (default EditorUtilityObject); it must be Blueprintable.

commands.returns: { name, package_path, asset_path, blueprint_class, parent_class, created, already_existed, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: create_editor_utility_widget_blueprint
commands.description: Create an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint at package_path/name with the editor factory, parented to UEditorUtilityWidget, give it a CanvasPanel root named RootCanvas when the factory made no root, then compile and save it. Idempotent by path: an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint already there is returned as it is (created=false, already_existed=true, saved=false), nothing compiled or saved, with the parent_class and root it really has. Another kind of asset at that path, or an invalid path, is an error and nothing is created. A failed save makes success false with save_error and keeps the new asset in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Open it as a tab with run_editor_utility_widget; find them with list_editor_utility_widgets; a plain Widget Blueprint is create_widget_blueprint.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities"; a trailing slash is ignored.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without path or extension, e.g. "EUW_LevelTools".

commands.returns: { name, package_path, asset_path, blueprint_class, parent_class, root_widget, root_widget_class, created, already_existed, root_created, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: delete_blueprint_variable
commands.description: Remove a member variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited/native variables are refused) and report whether it is really gone by re-looking it up. Nodes that still read/write it survive as broken references, so run compile_blueprint with return_messages=true afterwards. For an event dispatcher use remove_event_dispatcher instead -- this call would drop the delegate variable and strand its signature graph.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint
