commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, deleted } -- deleted is re-checked after the removal, so false means it is still there.

commands.name: delete_node
commands.description: Delete ONE node from a graph by its NodeGuid, breaking its links; refused for nodes the editor protects (FunctionEntry, Result, tunnels). This is the cleanup for orphan nodes left behind when a build_blueprint_graph batch fails and its rollback is refused, and it is reversible (the .uasset on disk is untouched until save_asset). It does NOT compile -- follow with compile_blueprint with return_messages=true.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node to delete

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { deleted, node_id }

commands.name: disconnect_pin
commands.description: Break ALL links on one pin of one node (there is no way to drop a single link of a multi-linked pin). Main use: clearing links that point at nodes which no longer exist after a failed or refused build_blueprint_graph rollback -- get_graph_nodes with compact=false shows those as linked_to entries with dead GUIDs. To remove the whole node instead, use delete_node.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node owning the pin (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes)

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Pin name, in either direction

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { disconnected, node_id, pin_name }

commands.name: find_blueprint_node_references
commands.description: "Find in Blueprints" over MCP: locate every Blueprint NODE that references a symbol -- variable, function, event, custom event, multicast delegate, macro, timeline, cast target, component, or a class/object in a pin default -- across a content path, returning each hit's asset, graph chain, node_id, title, match_kind and RESOLVED declaring class (resolved:false = a name-only guess). READ-ONLY. THE RULE FOR READING A ZERO: matches_found:0 only measures NON-EXISTENCE when `assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match` comes back EMPTY -- if it names assets, the symbol's string IS in those packages, so either the real name is spelled differently or the reference lives outside a graph (component template, property default). Check coverage_complete too: a truncated, timed-out or capped scan proves nothing. Blind by construction: Level Script Blueprints inside a .umap, and C++ callers.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Required (unless component_name is given): the name to look for, matched EXACTLY (variable/function/event/macro/class/component name). A misspelling returns 0 with a full-coverage report -- see assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match before believing it.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional: search for an actor COMPONENT by name; implies mode="component" and, with owner_blueprint, also matches GetComponentByClass/Cast pins that target the component's class.

params.name: owner_blueprint
params.description: Optional: Blueprint that DECLARES component_name (asset name or path); required to resolve the component's class for the class-pin matching.

params.name: mode
params.description: Optional (default "auto"): auto|all|variable|function|event|delegate|macro|component|class|pin_default. Filters which match kinds are returned; an unrecognized value returns everything and sets mode_recognized=false.

params.name: path
params.description: Optional (default "/Game"): content path root to scan.

params.name: recursive
params.description: Optional (default true): recurse into subfolders of path.

params.name: exclude_paths
params.description: Optional: array of package-path prefixes to skip (e.g. ["/Game/VendorPack/Demo"]).

params.name: include_paths
params.description: Optional: array of package-path prefixes to restrict the scan to (applied after path).

params.name: prefilter
params.description: Optional (default true): byte-scan the .uasset name map before loading. Turning it OFF loads every Blueprint under path (slow, but the ground truth to compare against).

params.name: case_sensitive
params.description: Optional (default false): case-sensitive symbol matching (both the byte prefilter and the node classifier).

params.name: include_pin_defaults
params.description: Optional (default true): also report pin defaults / pin types that name the symbol, on nodes with no structural match.

params.name: include_node_json
params.description: Optional (default false): embed the full NodeToJson serialization of each matching node.

params.name: include_pins
params.description: Optional (default false): when include_node_json is on, include the node's pins.

params.name: max_assets
params.description: Optional (default 20000): hard cap on candidate assets examined.

params.name: max_matches
params.description: Optional (default 200): stop after this many matches (sets truncated=true).

params.name: max_seconds
params.description: Optional (default 60): wall-clock budget; on expiry the scan stops and timed_out=true.

commands.returns: { symbol, mode, mode_recognized, path, recursive, prefilter_enabled, component_class, component_declared_in, assets_in_path, assets_scanned, assets_prefiltered_out, assets_prefilter_unavailable, assets_prefilter_bypassed_dirty, assets_loaded, assets_load_failed, assets_with_matches, graphs_visited, nodes_visited, foreign_subgraphs_skipped, matches_found, truncated, timed_out, coverage_complete, elapsed_ms, assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match:[string], notes:[string], matches:[{asset_name, asset_path, package_name, graph, graph_chain, graph_kind, node_id, node_class, node_title, match_kind, member_name, declaring_class, resolved, is_component_ref, is_interface_call, exact, detail, pin, pin_value, node?}], success }

commands.name: fork_class_chain
commands.description: One-call thin-fork + optional reparent + verify: collapses the create->reparent->verify pattern into a single call. It creates a NEW thin child Blueprint of base_class at fork_name (the seam you insert between a shared-library base and your own class), optionally tags it with the fork-origin metadata tag (project setting ForkOriginTag), saves it, and then -- only if reparent_target is given -- reparents that existing Blueprint onto the new fork through the guarded reparent_blueprint path (snapshot + compile flags + post-check + rollback) and reports its verification. WARNING: no durable backup is taken -- the rollback is in-memory only, so call backup_asset yourself first if you want a rollback-to-disk safety net.

params.name: fork_name
params.description: Name or full /Game path for the NEW thin child Blueprint to create.

params.name: base_class
params.description: Parent class for the new fork (native /Script, /Game/.../BP.BP_C, or a BP asset path).

params.name: path
params.description: Optional folder for fork_name when it is a bare name (default /Game/Blueprints).

params.name: fork_origin
params.description: Optional: value stored in the fork's fork-origin metadata tag (project setting ForkOriginTag, default 'mcp.forkOrigin'), recording its fork lineage.

params.name: reparent_target
params.description: Optional: an existing Blueprint to reparent onto the new fork.

params.name: auto_rollback
params.description: Optional (default true): forwarded to the safe reparent of reparent_target.

params.name: rename_colliding_vars
params.description: Optional (default false): forwarded to the safe reparent of reparent_target.

commands.returns: { fork_name, fork_path, fork_generated_class, base_class, already_exists, fork_origin_set, saved, save_error?, reparent:{...safe-reparent result...}|null, verification, verification_checks, error?, success }

commands.name: get_actor_material_info
commands.description: List the material slots of an actor PLACED IN THE EDITOR WORLD, one row per slot per StaticMeshComponent, with the material actually assigned (name, path, class) or "None". Scope limits worth knowing: it only walks UStaticMeshComponents (a skeletal mesh's slots are invisible here) and only the EDITOR world (no PIE selector), and the actor is matched by its object NAME, not its outliner label. The Blueprint-template twin is get_blueprint_material_info.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name of the actor in the EDITOR world (GetName(), not the display label shown in the outliner)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, material_slots: [{ slot, component, material_name, material_path, material_class }], total_slots: int } -- total_slots 0 means no StaticMeshComponent had slots, NOT that the actor has no materials.

commands.name: get_ai_perception_senses
commands.description: Read back the senses configured on an AIPerceptionComponent TEMPLATE of a Blueprint: for each one its config class plus the fields that matter (sight radius / lose-sight radius / peripheral angle, or hearing range) and the three affiliation filters. This is the verification step for add_ai_perception_sense. It reads the OWN SCS template, so an AIPerception component inherited from a parent Blueprint is not found, and a config class other than Sight or Hearing comes back with sense_type "unknown" and no fields.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint owning the component

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS AIPerceptionComponent node; another component type is an explicit error

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, senses: [ { config_class, sense_type, sight_radius|hearing_range, ... , detect_enemies, detect_neutrals, detect_friendlies } ], sense_count } -- sense_count 0 means the template has no configured sense, which is also what an AI that never perceives anything looks like.

commands.name: get_available_materials
commands.description: Enumerate material assets under a content path and return each one's name, object path, package and class -- the object path is what apply_material_to_blueprint / set_actor_material expect. One Asset Registry query on UMaterialInterface and all its subclasses (materials, material instances, project or plugin material classes); nothing is loaded, so a wide path is cheap. For one known name prefer resolve_asset_by_name.

params.name: search_path
params.description: Optional content path filter (e.g. "/Game/Materials"); empty/absent means the whole project and is reported back as "/Game/"

params.name: include_engine_materials
params.description: When true, also include /Engine/ materials; defaults to true, so the list is large unless a search_path narrows it

commands.returns: { materials: [{ name, path, package, class }], count: int, search_path_used: string } -- there is no truncation flag: count is everything that matched.

commands.name: get_blueprint_component_object_path
commands.description: Resolve a Blueprint component's TEMPLATE archetype and return its object path, so get_properties/set_properties/call_function can target that component directly.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name/path of the Blueprint that owns the component.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component variable name. Resolves an OWN SCS component (the _GEN_VARIABLE archetype on USCS_Node::ComponentTemplate) or an INHERITED/native component (the like-named subobject on the generated-class CDO).

commands.returns: { object_path: string, class: string, source: 'scs'|'inherited' } -- object_path is GetPathName() (feed it to get_properties / set_properties); class is the component class' full path.

commands.name: get_blueprint_component_property
commands.description: Read the EFFECTIVE default of a property (or, without property_name, ALL properties) on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE as typed JSON, resolving components INHERITED from a parent/grandparent Blueprint. Use it instead of get_component_properties with blueprint_name, which sees only own SCS nodes and native subobjects, not inherited SCS components or their ICH overrides. Order: own SCS template -> nearest existing ICH override -> ancestor's declaring SCS template -> native CDO subobject; source says which. NEVER mints an ICH override. group_by_field flags duplicate keys in an array of structs. Write: set_blueprint_component_properties.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component variable name (own or inherited)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property to read; omit to return ALL properties of the resolved template

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Also resolve inherited/ICH/native components (default true); when false only this Blueprint's own SCS components are considered

params.name: group_by_field
params.description: Optional. Only with property_name pointing at a TArray of STRUCTS: group the elements by this struct member and report duplicate_groups[]/empty_key_indices[]/has_duplicates. Two elements sharing a key is invisible in a plain value dump, yet when that array feeds a TMap the LAST one silently wins (Map.Add overwrites) -- this is the guardrail for exactly that class of bug.

params.name: report_duplicates
params.description: Optional bool. Implied true when group_by_field is given; pass true WITHOUT group_by_field to group by the WHOLE element value instead of one member.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, source: 'scs'|'inherited-ich'|'inherited-scs'|'inherited-native', resolved_from_class: string, property_name: string, value: any (single-property mode), properties: object, property_count: int (all-properties mode), duplicate_analysis?: { grouped_by, element_count, distinct_keys, duplicate_groups: [{key, count, indices[]}], empty_key_indices: [int], has_duplicates: bool, keys: [string] } }

commands.name: get_blueprint_functions
commands.description: List the graphs of a Blueprint -- functions, interface implementation graphs, macros, delegate signatures and, on request, event graph pages -- each with its node count, a REAL is_override (resolved against the parent class chain AND every implemented interface, naming the declaring class) and is_pure (read off the graph's FunctionEntry FUNC_BlueprintPure flag, not guessed). Enumerates the FULL graph set (UBlueprint::GetAllGraphs), not just Blueprint->FunctionGraphs: an INTERFACE override graph lives in ImplementedInterfaces[].Graphs, which FunctionGraphs alone misses (a function that exists would read as "missing"). Each entry carries graph_type so the caller can tell a plain function from an interface override, a macro or a delegate signature. The map to read before get_graph_nodes, which needs an exact graph name. WARNING: graph_type 'event_graph' entries are the TRANSIENT compiled event graphs and are absent on a Blueprint not compiled this session -- the authored EventGraph is the 'ubergraph' page. get_class_functions has the compiled class surface (inherited and native functions included).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint, or its full path. A bare name that matches more than one Blueprint asset (a backup copy shares the original's name) resolves to one of them and lists the others in `ambiguous_matches` -- pass the full path then.

params.name: filter_type
params.description: Optional 'all' (default), 'functions' or 'events' (case-insensitive, singular accepted). 'functions' keeps function, interface, macro and delegate_signature graphs; 'events' keeps the event side (ubergraph pages and compiled event graphs) and lists it without include_ubergraphs.

params.name: include_ubergraphs
params.description: Optional bool (default false): also list the event side -- the authored EventGraph/ubergraph pages (graph_type='ubergraph') and the transient compiled event graphs (graph_type='event_graph'). Off by default so 'functions' stays function-shaped.

params.name: include_macros
params.description: Optional bool (default true): list MacroGraphs (graph_type='macro').

params.name: include_interface_graphs
params.description: Optional bool (default true): list ImplementedInterfaces[].Graphs (graph_type='interface').

params.name: include_subgraphs
params.description: Optional bool (default false): also list nested/collapsed sub-graphs reached by GetAllGraphs but owned by no top-level list (graph_type='subgraph')

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional maximum number of entries to return, 1..10000 (default 1000); results_truncated says whether any were left out.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_valid: bool, ambiguous_matches?: [string], filter_type: string, functions: [{ name, node_count, graph_type, is_interface, interface_name?, interface_class?, is_user_constructed, is_pure?, is_override?, override_declaring_class? }], function_count: int, override_count: int, own_function_graph_count: int, interface_graph_count: int, macro_graph_count: int, delegate_graph_count: int, ubergraph_count: int, event_graph_count: int, subgraph_count: int, graphs_total: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool } -- graph_type is function|interface|macro|delegate_signature|ubergraph|event_graph|subgraph; is_pure/is_override are on function, interface and macro entries (a macro is neither), override_declaring_class names the class or interface (path) that declares what is overridden; is_user_constructed is just node_count>2, i.e. "someone wrote something beyond the auto Entry/Result terminators", because implementing an interface pre-creates empty graphs. The *_count totals count every graph of that kind, listed or not: subgraph_count>0 with include_subgraphs off is the warning that collapsed graphs exist and are not listed.

commands.name: get_blueprint_info
commands.description: One cheap overview of a Blueprint: parent class, compile status, and the counts + names of its OWN components, variables, function graphs and ubergraph pages. Everything here is what THIS asset declares -- nothing inherited, and interface-override graphs are not listed. So use it to orient, and the specialists to decide: get_blueprint_components for the real component set including ancestors, get_blueprint_functions for interface/macro/delegate graphs, get_blueprint_variables for variable flags, get_graph_nodes to read a graph.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, parent_class: string, components: [{ name, type }], component_count: int, variables: [{ name, type }], variable_count: int, functions: [{ name }], function_count: int, graphs: [{ name, type }], graph_count: int, has_event_graph: bool, event_graph_name?: string, status: string } -- parent_class is a short NAME (ambiguous between an engine class and a same-named project one), variable "type" is only the pin CATEGORY (no struct/class), and status is UpToDate/Error/Unknown.

commands.name: get_blueprint_material_info
commands.description: Read the material slots of ONE StaticMeshComponent TEMPLATE in a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node), with the material assigned to each slot or "None". This is the verification step after apply_material_to_blueprint / set_blueprint_component_properties. The slot count comes from the assigned static mesh's LOD 0 sections, so with no mesh assigned it returns ZERO slots and has_static_mesh:false -- which is a missing mesh, not a missing material. For a placed actor use get_actor_material_info.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS component; it must be a UStaticMeshComponent (any other type is an error)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, material_slots: [{ slot, component, material_name, material_path, material_class }], total_slots: int, has_static_mesh: bool } -- read has_static_mesh FIRST: total_slots:0 with has_static_mesh:false means no mesh was assigned, so the array says nothing about materials.

commands.name: get_blueprint_timeline_info
commands.description: Read one Timeline of a Blueprint: its length and length mode, auto_play, loop, replicated and ignore_time_dilation, every track (float, vector, color, event) with its curve and keys ({time, value}; value an array for vector and color), and its node (node_id, graph_name, output_pins: Update, Finished, Direction and one pin per track). Read-only. Timelines are made by add_timeline_to_blueprint and their tracks by add_blueprint_timeline_track / remove_blueprint_timeline_track; get_timeline_info is about Level Sequences. A missing Blueprint or timeline is an error listing the timelines it has.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: timeline_name
params.description: The timeline's variable name, as add_timeline_to_blueprint returned it.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, timeline_name, length, length_mode, auto_play, loop, replicated, ignore_time_dilation, track_count, tracks: [{track_name, track_type, curve, external_curve, key_count, keys: [{time, value}]}], node_id?, graph_name?, output_pins?: [string] }

commands.name: get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info
commands.description: Read ONE variable's full detail: its default value, the structured type (category, sub-category object and container kind -- not just the pin category get_blueprint_variables gives you), and every checkbox of the variable Details panel -- is_instance_editable / is_expose_on_spawn / is_blueprint_read_only / is_expose_to_cinematics / is_replicated / replication_condition / save_game. This is the headless oracle for "does this variable really persist into a .sav?", which otherwise costs a co-op PIE session plus a binary grep of the slot file. save_game is reported from BOTH places the flag lives, because they disagree until you compile: `save_game` is CPF_SaveGame as AUTHORED (FBPVariableDescription::PropertyFlags, exactly what the editor checkbox writes) while `save_game_generated` is the same flag on the FProperty of the GENERATED class, which is the one the save archive consults -- so save_game:true + save_game_generated:false means MARKED BUT NOT COMPILED, and nothing will persist yet; `save_game_matches` says it in one field. Read is_replicated FIRST: replication_condition is always populated (COND_None by default) and only means anything when replication is on. `default_value` is read from the CDO when the class is compiled (`default_value_source:"cdo"`), so it does not come back EMPTY for arrays, maps and every variable of an already-compiled Blueprint. Booleans of this family are contrasted, not believed -- audit_replication is the ground truth for replication.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (e.g. "MyFloat"); inherited variables are not covered

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, variable_name: string, default_value: string, default_value_source: "cdo"|"blueprint_description", default_value_serialized: string, var_type: string, property_type: string, var_type_detail: {category, sub_category, sub_category_object, sub_category_object_path, container}, is_instance_editable: bool, is_expose_on_spawn: bool, is_blueprint_read_only: bool, is_expose_to_cinematics: bool, is_replicated: bool, replication_condition: string, save_game: bool, save_game_generated: bool, save_game_generated_found: bool, save_game_matches: bool }

commands.name: get_blueprint_variables
commands.description: List the variables this Blueprint DECLARES (its NewVariables) with name, pin category, editor category, tooltip and the flags that matter for co-op and UI work: is_public (BlueprintVisible), is_editable, is_blueprint_read_only, is_replicated (CPF_Net) and is_expose_on_spawn. Inherited variables, native C++ UPROPERTYs, function locals and components are NOT here -- get_class_properties on the generated class (..._C) has the full property surface. THE FLAGS ARE READ OFF THE STORED VARIABLE DESCRIPTION, not the compiled property, and two of them mislead: is_editable checks CPF_Edit and ignores CPF_DisableEditOnInstance, so it says true for variables the editor refuses to edit per instance; is_expose_on_spawn checks a property flag while set_blueprint_variable_metadata writes the ExposeOnSpawn METADATA, so it says false for variables that DO show up as SpawnActor pins. Oracles: write the placed instance for editability, the spawn node's pins for exposure, get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info for type/replication and one variable's default value.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint, or its full path. A bare name that matches more than one Blueprint asset resolves to one of them and lists the others in `ambiguous_matches`.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional maximum number of variables to return, 1..10000 (default 1000); results_truncated says whether any were left out.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_valid: bool, ambiguous_matches?: [string], variables: [{ name, type, category, tooltip, is_public, is_editable, is_blueprint_read_only, is_replicated, is_expose_on_spawn, instance_editable, expose_on_spawn }], variable_count: int, variables_count: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool } -- "type" is only the pin CATEGORY (e.g. "struct", "object"), not the struct or class; instance_editable and expose_on_spawn repeat is_editable and is_expose_on_spawn; variable_count and variables_count are the same number.

commands.name: get_event_dispatchers
commands.description: List a Blueprint's event dispatchers (multicast delegates) WITH each one's full parameter signature (name, C++ type, is_output) and whether it is inherited. Read from the SKELETON class, so it reflects edits made since the last full compile. Use it before add_broadcast_node / add_object_bound_event / set_event_dispatcher_signature, whose pins mirror this signature; only the dispatchers this Blueprint DECLARES can have their signature edited.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: include_inherited
params.description: Also include dispatchers inherited from parent classes; default false = only the ones this Blueprint declares (i.e. the editable ones)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, dispatchers: [ { name: string, is_inherited: bool, param_count: int, params: [ { name: string, type: string, is_output: bool } ] } ], dispatcher_count: int }

commands.name: get_function_pins
commands.description: Preview the EXACT pins an add_graph_node call_function node WOULD expose for a UFunction WITHOUT creating anything: owner_class, is_pure, is_static, exec_input/exec_output ("execute"/"then", null when pure), self_pin (null when static), input_params, output_params and return_value. This is what lets a whole build_blueprint_graph (nodes + connections + pin_defaults) be written in ONE call instead of create -> get_graph_nodes -> connect round-trips. It answers "what pins would it have", NOT "can a Blueprint call it": some engine functions resolve and preview here and are still rejected by the compiler, so the oracle for callability is compile_blueprint with return_messages=true.

params.name: function_name
params.description: UFunction name, matched EXACTLY against the reflected name (e.g. "PrintString", "K2_GetActorLocation", or a Blueprint function graph's own name, which may contain spaces like "Emit Noise At Location"). A guessed name that does not exist just errors -- it never returns an empty preview.

params.name: target_class
params.description: Optional class searched FIRST: native name ("KismetSystemLibrary"), "/Script/Module.Class", a Blueprint class path ("/Game/...X_C"), or a user BFL. Also always searched: the blueprint's own class + KismetSystem/GameplayStatics/KismetMath.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Optional Blueprint whose generated class joins the search (for self / BP-local functions).

commands.returns: { function_name, owner_class, is_pure, is_static, exec_input, exec_output, self_pin, input_params:[{name,type}], output_params:[{name,type}], return_value:{name,type}|null, note }

commands.name: get_graph_nodes
commands.description: Read one Blueprint graph: every node with its node_id (NodeGuid), class, title, position, comment and pins (name, direction, type, linked_to, default) -- the read that feeds connect_pins / set_pin_default_value / delete_node, and the way to see what a graph actually DOES. TRAP: compact=true drops per-pin type metadata AND omits every pin that is unlinked and default-less (plus knots and comment boxes), so a pin missing from a compact listing is NOT proof the pin does not exist -- re-read with compact=false before concluding anything about pins. Also: a bare blueprint_name that matches two assets picks one silently (pass the full path), and reading a graph under a read-only vendor root leaves that package DIRTY in memory (reload_asset_package with on_dirty="discard" cleans it).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path. Prefer the FULL path: a short name with more than one match resolves silently to one of them, and stale backup copies share the original's name.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. Also resolves a collapsed composite subgraph by its title (e.g. 'In Game HUD') and accepts a path form ('EventGraph > In Game HUD').

params.name: expand_composites
params.description: When true, inline the nodes of collapsed composite subgraphs recursively; each node gains a "graph" tag naming the graph it came from. Macro-library graphs are never inlined. (Optional, default false)

params.name: compact
params.description: Token-lean listing: drops pin types, positions and comments, and skips pins that are unlinked AND have no default. Also excludes K2Node_Knot + EdGraphNode_Comment unless exclude_classes is given. Good for reading topology, WRONG for checking whether a pin exists. (Optional, default false)

params.name: exclude_classes
params.description: Array of leaf node class names to skip, matched against each node's "class" field (e.g. ["K2Node_Knot"]). Pass [] to include everything even in compact mode. Absent + compact=true means knots and comments are excluded; absent + compact=false excludes nothing.

params.name: max_nodes
params.description: Cap on the number of nodes emitted (<=0 or absent = unlimited); the response still counts every non-excluded node in total_node_count and sets truncated=true.

params.name: node_id
params.description: Optional NodeGuid (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes): return ONLY that node of the graph, always at full fidelity (compact, exclude_classes, expand_composites and max_nodes are ignored) -- every pin with name, direction, type, linked_to and default, at a fraction of the tokens of a whole graph. A node_id the graph does not contain is an error.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, graph_name, nodes:[{node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment, pins:[...], subgraph?}], node_count, compact, total_node_count, excluded_count, truncated } -- node_count is what was EMITTED, total_node_count what exists; a node owning a nested graph (composite / macro instance) carries "subgraph" with the name to pass back as graph_name. With node_id, nodes holds that one node (nodes[0]) and node_count is 1.

commands.name: get_property_access_path
commands.description: Read a UK2Node_PropertyAccess node's binding Path -- the anim-Blueprint property binding (InAnimInstance.Foo, InDeltaTime...) that no ordinary pin read exposes -- as segments plus its display text_path, and say whether the leaf actually RESOLVED (a still-wildcard Value pin means the path points at nothing). Read-only; errors on any node that is not a K2Node_PropertyAccess. Writer twin: set_property_access_path.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path (usually an Animation Blueprint).

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the property-access node (from get_graph_nodes).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

commands.returns: { node_id, graph_name, path:[string], text_path, resolved, resolved_pin:{name,direction,type,...} } -- resolved:false (Value pin still wildcard) is the signal that the binding is broken.

commands.name: implement_interface
commands.description: Add a Blueprint Interface to a Blueprint's implemented list (asset path or class name). NOT idempotent: an interface already implemented comes back as an error, unlike remove_interface. It only registers the contract -- the graphs that IMPLEMENT each member are created by add_blueprint_function with override=true, which is also the only correct route for interface EVENTS.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: interface_path
params.description: Blueprint interface asset path (e.g. /Game/Dir/BPI_Foo.BPI_Foo), or a resolvable interface class name/path

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, interface, implemented } -- implemented is always true on success; failure is an error response. Confirm the member set with get_blueprint_functions (interface graphs live in ImplementedInterfaces, not FunctionGraphs).

commands.name: lint_blueprint_graph
commands.description: Read-only lint of a Blueprint's graphs for four authoring bugs that COMPILE CLEAN and only show up in play: eclipsed_interface_event and custom_event_shadowing_override (a node that looks like an override and is not, so the base contract never runs), unreachable_exec_node (a node no exec chain reaches from any entry) and function_exit_without_return (a live exec path that falls off the end of a value-returning function, so the caller silently gets false/0/None). Scans ALL ubergraph + function + macro graphs by default. HONESTY LIMIT: findings:[] is NOT a clean bill of health -- by deliberate design it never flags a merely unconnected exec output, so a Branch or Is Valid with dangling outputs can pass; check linked_to yourself with get_graph_nodes (compact=false, or node_id for one node).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint to analyze.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Optional single graph to analyze; when omitted, scans ALL ubergraph (event) pages + function graphs + macro graphs owned by this Blueprint. Interface-override graphs are NOT in that default set -- name one explicitly to lint it.

commands.returns: { findings: [ { kind, node_id, node_title, graph_name, why, fix_hint, pin? } ] } -- kind is one of eclipsed_interface_event, custom_event_shadowing_override, unreachable_exec_node, function_exit_without_return (this one also reports the offending exec pin in "pin"); "why" carries a best-effort pointer at the likely upstream break. No counters and no coverage flags: an empty array only means these four rules found nothing.

commands.name: list_editor_utility_widgets
commands.description: List the Editor Utility Widget Blueprint assets under a content folder and its subfolders, read from the Asset Registry without loading them. Returns search_path, count and widgets [{name, asset_path, package_name, package_path}]; open one as an editor tab with run_editor_utility_widget.

params.name: path
params.description: Content folder to search recursively, without a trailing slash, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities" (default /Game).

commands.returns: { name, asset_path, package_name, package_path, search_path, count, widgets }

commands.name: list_overridable_functions
commands.description: Enumerate the functions/events that a Blueprint deriving from a class could override. Works on an EXISTING Blueprint (blueprint_name) or on ANY class (class_name) so the override surface can be inspected BEFORE the child exists. Gated with UEdGraphSchema_K2::CanKismetOverrideFunction -- the same predicate add_blueprint_function(override=true) enforces -- so discovery and authoring agree (a bare NativeEvent||FUNC_BlueprintEvent filter lets a parent Blueprint's *__DelegateSignature through as "overridable"). Each entry reports where the member is DECLARED and where it is last IMPLEMENTED, with is_stub, which is what distinguishes a concrete ancestor from its `_Abstract` sibling.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name/path of an existing Blueprint. Its ParentClass is the override surface.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Alternative to blueprint_name: any class ("Actor", "/Script/Engine.Pawn", "/Game/.../BP_X.BP_X_C", or a Blueprint asset path). The override surface is THAT class, i.e. what a new child would get. Ignored when blueprint_name is given.

params.name: include_non_overridable
params.description: Optional bool (default false). true also lists the entries a NativeEvent||FUNC_BlueprintEvent filter passes but CanKismetOverrideFunction rejects (delegate signatures, BlueprintInternalUseOnly, deprecated), each flagged can_kismet_override=false. Nothing is lost silently.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name?, class_name?, source_mode, resolved_class, base_class, ancestors: [string], count, functions: [{ function_name, display_name, declaring_class, is_native_event, is_event, is_interface, interface_name?, kind, can_kismet_override, has_override_graph, has_user_logic, is_implemented, parent_impl_kind, parent_impl_owner_class, parent_impl_graph, parent_impl_node_count, is_stub, is_stub_basis }] }

commands.name: list_scripted_action_utilities
commands.description: List the Editor Utility Blueprints under a content folder (subfolders included) whose class derives from UAssetActionUtility (kind asset: Content Browser right-click actions) or UActorActionUtility (kind actor: level actor actions). Each Editor Utility Blueprint found is LOADED to test its class, so a large folder is slow; plain Blueprints and Editor Utility Widgets are not listed. Read-only; a folder with none, or one that does not exist, is an empty list, not an error. Run one with run_asset_action_utility, which also lists its CallInEditor actions; create one with create_editor_utility_blueprint (parent_class "AssetActionUtility" or "ActorActionUtility"); Editor Utility Widgets: list_editor_utility_widgets.

params.name: path
params.description: Content folder to search, subfolders included, e.g. "/Game/EditorTools", without a trailing slash (default /Game).

commands.returns: { search_path: string, count: int, utilities: [{ name: string, path: string, package_name: string, kind: string, parent_class: string }] }

commands.name: list_widget_bound_events
commands.description: List every event-dispatcher BINDING wired in a Blueprint, across the three node kinds that make one in practice: UK2Node_AddDelegate (from add_object_bound_event / add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate"), UK2Node_ComponentBoundEvent (from add_component_bound_event -- a component's dispatcher OR a UMG widget's, e.g. a Button's OnClicked) and UK2Node_ActorBoundEvent (a level actor's, bound from the Level Blueprint). Each entry reports which kind it is (binding_kind), what it is bound ON (bound_to: the component/widget variable, or the actor), the delegate's owner class and name, and the handler on the other end. Despite the name it works on ANY Blueprint -- but it only walks Ubergraph pages and FunctionGraphs, so a binding inside a macro or interface graph is out of scope. Run it BEFORE add_object_bound_event / add_component_bound_event: double-binding one delegate to two handlers compiles fine and silently runs BOTH. A reader that cannot see what the writer wrote is worse than no reader: a 0 reads as "not wired" and sends you to re-wire what is already there.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path (Actor Blueprint, Widget Blueprint or Level Blueprint).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, bindings:[{ graph_name, node_id, binding_kind, bound_to, delegate_owner_class, delegate_name, delegate_resolved, wired, custom_event_name, custom_event_node_id }], binding_count, kind_counts:{add_delegate,component_bound_event,actor_bound_event} } -- binding_kind names the node class behind the entry. bound_to is the component/widget variable name (component_bound_event), the actor name (actor_bound_event), or empty for add_delegate, whose target pin is left unconnected by design. delegate_resolved=false means the delegate no longer resolves live (renamed/removed). wired=false is a DANGLING add_delegate bind (its Delegate pin has no handler); the two *BoundEvent kinds ARE their own handler, so they are always wired and custom_event_name is the generated BndEvt__ function.

commands.name: move_node
commands.description: Move a node to a new [x, y] canvas position. Purely cosmetic layout: no pin, link, default or type changes, and no compile. Returns the position actually applied.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node to move

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

params.name: position_x
params.description: Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: position_y
params.description: Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set)

params.name: node_position
params.description: Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y

commands.returns: { node_id, pos_x, pos_y }

commands.name: recombine_blueprint_pin
commands.description: Collapse a previously split struct pin back into ONE pin (inverse of split_blueprint_pin), which is what set_pin_default_value needs before it will write a struct literal. Accepts either the parent pin's name or any of its sub-pin names; links on the sub-pins are dropped by the engine as part of recombining.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node owning the pin.

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Name of the parent pin OR of any of its sub-pins.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { recombined } -- always true on the success path; a pin that is not split is an error response instead.

commands.name: reconcile_function_signature
commands.description: Repair a LOCAL function graph's parameter pins so they match a parent UFUNCTION -- for an override whose signature went stale after a reparent -- WITHOUT nuking the graph's downstream nodes, which is what re-creating the override by hand costs you. It diffs the parent's parameters against the function's entry/result pins: mode='add_missing' (the default) only ADDS the missing pins, so it is non-destructive and safe to run blind; mode='remove_extra' / 'mirror' also DROP pins the parent lacks, which can sever downstream connections, and are therefore gated behind force_remove=true -- without it the extra pins are merely REPORTED (partially_implemented=true).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path owning the function.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the local function graph to reconcile.

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Optional: class whose UFUNCTION defines the target signature (default: the Blueprint's current ParentClass).

params.name: mode
params.description: Optional (default 'add_missing'): 'add_missing' | 'remove_extra' | 'mirror'.

params.name: force_remove
params.description: Optional (default false): actually remove extra pins for 'remove_extra'/'mirror' (may drop connections).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, parent_class, mode, added:[{name,direction}], removed:[{name,direction}], extra_pins:[{name,direction}], missing_pins:[{name,direction}], removal_performed, partially_implemented, note, success }

commands.name: remove_ai_perception_sense
commands.description: Remove a sense (its config) from an AIPerceptionComponent TEMPLATE of a Blueprint, then compile the Blueprint and save the package, as add_ai_perception_sense does; no undo step. Inverse of add_ai_perception_sense: sense_type "sight" or "hearing", or any other configured sense by its config class name (AISenseConfig_Damage...). When it was the dominant sense, the dominant sense is cleared (dominant_cleared). A sense the template does not configure is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing compiled or saved); a missing Blueprint or component, or a component that is not an AIPerceptionComponent, is an error. The reply re-reads the template's senses; read them with get_ai_perception_senses. Refused during PIE unless force=true.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint owning the component

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the AIPerceptionComponent SCS node

params.name: sense_type
params.description: "sight", "hearing", or the short name / class name of another configured sense ("damage", "AISenseConfig_Damage")

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, sense_type, removed, removed_count, dominant_cleared, senses: [string], sense_count, saved, note? }

commands.name: remove_blueprint_function
commands.description: Delete a function graph OWNED BY the Blueprint (Blueprint->FunctionGraphs) by name. WARNING: It resolves more graphs than it can delete: name lookup goes through FindGraph (all graphs, interface overrides and macros included) but the delete only touches FunctionGraphs and only when bAllowDeletion is true, so an INTERFACE OVERRIDE resolves and cannot be removed. That case is a hard error naming the reason -- to change an interface override, author the signature on the INTERFACE and re-create it (add_function_parameter on the BPI_ -> compile_blueprint -> add_blueprint_function with override=true). Not idempotent: a name that does not resolve is an error. TRAP when deleting to re-create: the class is NOT regenerated here, so an immediate add_blueprint_function with the same name fails with "is an inherited overridable function (declared on <this very class>)" because the stale UFunction is still in the generated class -- put a compile_blueprint BETWEEN the two calls. Callers of the removed function are left broken until the next compile. A macro graph: remove_blueprint_macro.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function graph to remove; must exist, be owned by this Blueprint and be deletable, or the call errors

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, removed_function: string, success: bool } -- success:true means the graph is gone from Blueprint->FunctionGraphs (re-read after the delete), not merely that the call ran.

commands.name: remove_blueprint_macro
commands.description: Delete a macro graph owned by the Blueprint (Blueprint->MacroGraphs), in one undo step. Inverse of create_blueprint_macro; remove_blueprint_function deletes function graphs only. The macro's instances in the Blueprint's graphs go with it, so a macro still in use is refused (instance_count says how many) unless delete_instances=true. Nothing is compiled or saved. A macro that is not there is an honest no-op (removed=false); a missing Blueprint is an error. The reply re-reads MacroGraphs; list the graphs with get_blueprint_functions. Refused during PIE unless force=true.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: macro_name
params.description: Name of the macro graph, as create_blueprint_macro returned it in graph_name.

params.name: delete_instances
params.description: true to delete the macro even when nodes of this Blueprint instance it (they are deleted too); default false refuses.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, macro_name, removed, instance_count, instances_removed, macro_count, note? }

commands.name: remove_blueprint_timeline_track
commands.description: Remove a track (float, vector, color or event) from a Timeline of a Blueprint by its name, as the Timeline editor's Delete Track does, then reconstruct the timeline node (the track's output pin goes, and its links with it) and compile the Blueprint; one undo step (the compile is not undone). Inverse of add_blueprint_timeline_track. A track that is not there is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing compiled); a missing Blueprint or timeline is an error. The reply re-reads the timeline (tracks, output_pins). Refused during PIE unless force=true. The whole timeline: delete_node on its node; read: get_blueprint_timeline_info.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint.

params.name: timeline_name
params.description: The timeline's variable name.

params.name: track_name
params.description: Name of the track to remove (get_blueprint_timeline_info lists them).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, timeline_name, track_name, track_type?, removed, length, length_mode, auto_play, loop, replicated, ignore_time_dilation, track_count, tracks: [...], node_id, graph_name, output_pins: [string], note? }

commands.name: remove_component_from_blueprint
commands.description: Remove one or more component nodes from a Blueprint's SCS, with a DOUBLE CENSUS (flat AllNodes vs a walk of RootNodes) so collateral losses are reported instead of hidden: also_removed names descendants that went with their parent and unexpected_losses names nodes left in AllNodes but unreachable from any root. Batch-capable and that is the point -- chaining SINGLE-node calls on the same Blueprint is exactly the pattern that deletes components nobody asked for, so pass component_names and take ONE compile for the lot. A re-added component comes back with its CLASS defaults: per-instance overrides are gone and do not come back on save. IDEMPOTENT, so it is safe in scripts that re-run: a requested component that is not there is listed in not_found, and when none of them is there the call still succeeds with already_removed:true and nothing removed.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name/path of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of the component to remove (single form; matches the variable name or the _GEN_VARIABLE internal name)

params.name: component_names
params.description: Optional array of component names removed as ONE batch with a SINGLE compile. Chaining single-node calls is the pattern that causes collateral deletions. Merged with component_name when both are given.

params.name: promote_children
params.description: Optional bool, default true: keep descendants by re-parenting them (RemoveNodeAndPromoteChildren). Pass false for plain RemoveNode, which orphans the whole subtree.

commands.returns: { success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, removed_component, component_name, removed, already_removed, requested[], removed_components[], also_removed[], unexpected_losses[], not_found[], still_present[], node_count_before, node_count_after, reachable_before, reachable_after, orphans_before[], orphans_after[], root_nodes_before[], root_nodes_after[], root_nodes_changed, promote_children, compiled, compile_count, success, verification } } -- removed: at least one node went; already_removed: none of the requested names was there (a no-op, not an error).

commands.name: remove_event_dispatcher
commands.description: Remove an event dispatcher, dropping BOTH artifacts add_event_dispatcher created: the delegate member variable AND its signature graph (delete_blueprint_variable removes only the variable and strands the graph, which is why this exists). Idempotent -- when neither artifact is present it returns removed:false instead of erroring. Broadcast/bind nodes that referenced it are left broken: compile_blueprint with return_messages=true after.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: Name of the event dispatcher to remove (must be one this Blueprint owns; inherited ones have no local artifacts)

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, removed } -- removed:false means nothing was there (no-op), not a failure.

commands.name: remove_function_local_variable
commands.description: Remove a local variable from one Blueprint function graph (interface-override graphs included), with the get/set nodes that read or write it in that function, in one undo step -- what deleting it from the My Blueprint panel does. Inverse of add_function_local_variable; delete_blueprint_variable removes MEMBER variables only. Nothing is compiled or saved. A local that is not there is an honest no-op (removed=false); a missing Blueprint or function is an error. The reply re-reads the function's locals (local_variables), the only reader of them: get_blueprint_variables lists members. Refused during PIE unless force=true.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function graph (FunctionGraphs or an interface-override graph)

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of the local variable to remove

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, variable_name, removed, local_variables: [string], note? }

commands.name: remove_function_parameter
commands.description: Remove an input or output parameter from a Blueprint function graph -- interface-override graphs included -- or from a macro graph, in one undo step: the user pin leaves the Entry node (inputs) or every Result node (outputs), or the macro's input or output tunnel, and the node is reconstructed, so links to that pin break. Inverse of add_function_parameter; for an override of a C++ or interface function, reconcile_function_signature fits the signature to the parent instead. Nothing is compiled or saved: call sites update at the next compile_blueprint. A parameter that is not there is an honest no-op (removed=false, the parameters it does have in params); a missing Blueprint or graph is an error. The reply re-reads the signature (params_left). Read the pins: get_graph_nodes at compact=false. Refused during PIE unless force=true.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function graph, or of a macro graph when no function has that name.

params.name: param_name
params.description: Name of the parameter to remove, as add_function_parameter returned it.

params.name: is_output
params.description: true to remove an output/return parameter, false (default) an input.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, param_name, is_output, graph_kind, removed, params_left: [string], params?: [string], note? }

commands.name: remove_interface
commands.description: Remove an implemented Blueprint Interface (inverse of implement_interface) and, unless preserve_functions is set, DELETE the graphs that implemented it -- work is lost, so pass preserve_functions=true to keep them as ordinary Blueprint functions. Idempotent, unlike implement_interface: an interface that is not implemented returns removed:false instead of erroring.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: interface_path
params.description: Blueprint interface asset path (or class name) to remove

params.name: preserve_functions
params.description: When true, keep the interface's function graphs as normal Blueprint functions instead of deleting them; defaults to false

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, interface, removed } -- removed:false means it was not implemented (no-op), not a failure.

commands.name: remove_unused_variables
commands.description: Delete EVERY variable the engine considers unused from a Blueprint in one shot (GatherUnusedVariables + RemoveUnusedVariables) and report which ones went. Destructive and non-selective -- "unused" means no graph node reads or writes it, so a variable only touched from C++, a DataTable, a save game or a runtime name lookup counts as unused and is deleted. Preview it by comparing get_blueprint_variables before/after, or delete a specific one with delete_blueprint_variable.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

commands.returns: { blueprint_name: string, removed_count: int, removed_variables?: [string] } -- removed_variables is the list gathered BEFORE the removal and removed_count what the engine reported removing; when they disagree, trust neither and re-read get_blueprint_variables.

commands.name: rename_blueprint_variable
commands.description: Rename a member variable DECLARED on this Blueprint, KEEPING everything the delete+re-add workaround throws away: the VarGuid, the type, the default value, the category, the tooltip and the replication flags -- and, crucially, RE-WIRING every Get/Set node that reads it, in this Blueprint and in every dependent one. This is the only correct way to rename an authored variable in place (e.g. to translate its name). WARNING: it refuses a variable that has a RepNotify function: the engine's own rename opens a MODAL dialog for that case (FSuppressableWarningDialog, which does NOT honour unattended mode) and would hang the editor waiting for a click -- clear the RepNotify with set_blueprint_variable_replication, rename, then set it back. WARNING: dependent Blueprints are only repaired if they are LOADED: this command loads the ones the Asset Registry reports as referencers first, and reports them in `referencers_loaded`, but an asset that references it in a way the registry does not see keeps the old name silently. It does NOT create CoreRedirects, so a saved game, a DataTable cell or a Python set_editor_property that names the variable as text is NOT fixed -- grep for those. Run compile_blueprint afterwards and save_asset on this Blueprint AND on every referencer.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path owning the variable.

params.name: old_name
params.description: Current name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint; inherited/native ones are refused.

params.name: new_name
params.description: New name. Must be a legal identifier and free across the WHOLE class chain (the engine does not check this and would happily create a duplicate). Case-only changes are allowed.

params.name: load_referencers
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Load the Blueprints the Asset Registry lists as referencers BEFORE renaming, so the engine's reference fixup reaches them; it only ever sees what is already in memory.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, old_name, new_name, renamed (re-read: true only if new_name exists and old_name is gone), referencers_loaded: [string], repnotify_cleared: bool, warning? }

commands.name: rename_function_parameter
commands.description: Rename a PARAMETER of a Blueprint function graph -- the parameter counterpart of rename_blueprint_variable, and the only headless way to do it: add_function_parameter only ADDS, there is no remove_function_parameter, so "delete and re-add" is not even available. It renames the pin on the Entry node and on EVERY Result node of the graph, and registers a CoreRedirect so that call sites re-map themselves. That redirect is not a nicety: it is what stops this from being a PHANTOM PIN FACTORY. With the redirect, the call site's pin takes the new name AND KEEPS ITS LITERAL VALUE; renamed WITHOUT one, the old pin stays alive and ORPHANED on the caller. WARNING: that orphan is silent: it survives compiles that report num_errors:0 -- so `compile_blueprint` is NOT the oracle here. The oracle is get_graph_nodes(compact=false) on the callers, checking that NO pin still carries the old name. The redirect matches on `Class.Function.Param`, so it reaches callers that merely CALL the function (K2Node_Message included) without implementing its interface, and dependents that are not even loaded -- both of which rename_blueprint_variable cannot reach. It does NOT rename anything that names the parameter as TEXT (a DataTable cell, a saved game, Python). Run compile_blueprint afterwards and save_asset on this Blueprint AND on every caller. AND THE COMPILE IS NOT THE END OF IT: what reaches the .uasset is UserDefinedPins, not the EdGraphPins you read back -- a rename checked only on the latter can report renamed:true, compile at num_errors:0, be saved and COMMITTED, and still come back as the OLD name the next time the editor starts. So it also reports entry_user_pins_after/result_user_pins_after (the serialized side, legitimately EMPTY on an interface-override graph) and refuses to claim success while any UserDefinedPin still carries the old name. The end-to-end oracle is still disk: save_asset -> reload_asset_package -> get_function_pins.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path owning the function graph.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function graph (an interface's own function graph and an interface-override graph both work).

params.name: old_name
params.description: Current parameter name, matched on the Entry node and on every Result node. A name present on only one of them is fine.

params.name: new_name
params.description: New parameter name. Must be free on the terminal nodes; a collision is refused up front via the engine's own dry-run, before anything is touched.

params.name: write_redirect
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Also PERSIST the redirect as a +PropertyRedirects line in Config/DefaultEngine.ini, so it survives a restart and reaches the other machine. With false the redirect is registered in memory only and the rename EVAPORATES for anyone who opens the project later.

params.name: load_referencers
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Load the Blueprints the Asset Registry lists as referencers BEFORE renaming, so their nodes reconstruct in this session instead of the next one.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, old_name, new_name, renamed: bool, terminals_renamed: [string], entry_pins_after: [string], result_pins_after: [string], entry_user_pins_after: [string], result_user_pins_after: [string], redirect_registered: string, redirect_persisted_to: string|null, referencers_loaded: [string], must_compile_and_save: [string], warning: string } -- the *_user_pins_after pair is the SERIALIZED side (UserDefinedPins): empty on an interface-override graph is normal, but the old name appearing there is the rename that will revert on restart.

commands.name: reparent_blueprint
commands.description: Change a Blueprint's parent class, guarded and rollback-capable; asking for the parent it already has is a no-op (reparented:false), not an error. On top of the reparent itself it takes: a pre-flight snapshot (parent chain, own-variable count, CDO component count); an OPTIONAL variable de-collision rename (rename_colliding_vars) for own variables whose name collides with a member the NEW parent already declares, which a plain reparent would otherwise clobber; the delta-serialization compile flags, without which a Blueprint with more than ~10 type-pinned variables CRASHES the editor during reinstancing; the same SCS-root reconciliation the Blueprint editor itself does, so a silently renamed component ("Mesh" -> "Mesh1") is reported instead of hidden; an invariant post-check (parent matches, no compile error, own-variable count did not shrink); and, on failure, an in-memory auto_rollback that restores the original parent, restores the component names and recompiles (auto_rollback=false leaves a failed reparent in place). It never saves to disk. This is a genuinely destructive multi-step transaction: run it with dry_run=true first on any real fork -- that reports the plan and the would-rename set without mutating anything.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path to reparent.

params.name: new_parent_class
params.description: New parent class name or path (native /Script, /Game/.../BP.BP_C, or a BP asset path -> its GeneratedClass).

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Optional (default false): analyze + report the plan (snapshot, would-rename vars, component collisions) without mutating.

params.name: rename_colliding_vars
params.description: Optional (default false): before reparenting, rename own NewVariables that collide by name with a member on the new parent.

params.name: auto_rollback
params.description: Optional (default true): on post-check failure, restore the original parent, restore the SCS node names and recompile.

params.name: reconcile_scene_root
params.description: Optional (default true): run the editor's own post-reparent conform pass -- ValidateSceneRootNodes + PrepareToConformSparseClassData + a second pass after the compile. Setting it FALSE disables all three; it exists only as a bisect escape hatch.

params.name: treat_component_renames_as_regression
params.description: Optional (default false): count a silently renamed SCS component as a post-check regression (which triggers auto_rollback).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, blueprint_path, old_parent, new_parent, dry_run, reparented, renamed_variables:[{from,to}], pre_variable_count, post_variable_count, pre_component_count, post_component_count, pre_scs_node_count, post_scs_node_count, scene_root_reconciled, scene_root_reconciled_post_compile, default_scene_root_removed, sparse_class_data_conform_prepared, compile_messages:[{severity,text}], compile_error_count, compile_warning_count, renamed_components:[{guid,from,to,matched_by}], removed_components:[{guid,name}], components_without_guid, colliding_components:[{name,own_class,parent_class}], child_only_components:[{name,class}], compile_status, parent_match, compile_ok, variables_intact, components_intact, post_check_ok, rolled_back, rollback_complete, rollback_restored_components:[{guid,name}] (snapshotted nodes whose name MATCHES again after the rollback), rollback_unrestored_components:[{guid,expected_name,actual_name}], rollback_compile_messages:[{severity,text}], regressions:[string], saved_to_disk (always false -- this tool never saves), persistence_note, verification, verification_checks, success }

commands.name: run_asset_action_utility
commands.description: Invoke one CallInEditor action of a scripted Asset or Actor Action Utility Blueprint (by asset path) on a new transient instance of its class, as the right-click menu does but with no Content Browser or level selection. function_name picks the action, case-insensitive, else the first one found; the reply always lists every action in action_functions. Only a parameterless action runs: one that takes parameters, a name that matches no action, a utility with no actions or an abstract utility class is a success with invoked=false and a note saying why. What the action does is up to its Blueprint; this tool saves nothing itself. A missing asset, one that is not a Blueprint, or a Blueprint that is not an Asset/Actor Action Utility is an error. Find them with list_scripted_action_utilities; create one with create_editor_utility_blueprint (parent_class "AssetActionUtility" or "ActorActionUtility").

params.name: utility_path
params.description: Asset path of the utility Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/EditorTools/EUA_RenameTextures" (the object path form also works).

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the CallInEditor action to run, case-insensitive; when absent the first action found on the class runs.

commands.returns: { utility_path, kind, generated_class, action_functions, function_name, function_found, invoked, note }

commands.name: run_editor_utility_widget
commands.description: Open an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint (by asset path) as an editor tab through UEditorUtilitySubsystem: register its tab spawner and invoke the tab, which creates the widget and so runs whatever its Blueprint does on construct. The tab ID is the asset path plus _ActiveTab, so a repeat call brings back the same tab instead of adding a second one. Nothing is saved. widget_spawned is false when no live widget came back; in a commandlet nothing is registered and tab_id is empty. A missing asset, or one that is not an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint, is an error. Create one with create_editor_utility_widget_blueprint; find them with list_editor_utility_widgets; right-click actions: run_asset_action_utility.

params.name: widget_blueprint_path
params.description: Asset path of the Editor Utility Widget Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/EditorTools/EUW_Tools" (the object path form also works).

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_path, asset_path, tab_id, registration_name, registered, tab_exists, widget_spawned }

commands.name: set_blueprint_class_replication
commands.description: Set class-level ACTOR replication on a Blueprint's CDO (bReplicates, optionally bAlwaysRelevant), compile, and read the values back off the RE-FETCHED post-compile CDO. Actor Blueprints only: a component Blueprint is refused (component replication is set_component_replication). Related reader trap: audit_replication's class_replicates reads the ACTOR flag, so it reports false for every component Blueprint whatever its CDO says.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint (must be compiled at least once).

params.name: replicates
params.description: Whether the Actor class replicates to network clients. Required.

params.name: always_relevant
params.description: Sets the Actor's bAlwaysRelevant flag; only applied when the field is present

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, replicates, always_relevant_set, always_relevant } -- values re-read from the CDO after compiling; always_relevant is only present when it was requested.

commands.name: set_blueprint_component_array_element
commands.description: Author ONE element of a TArray property on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (own SCS, or ICH-aware for a component inherited from an ancestor Blueprint): patch named struct members of an existing element, insert a new element at an index, or remove one. Every OTHER element is exported before and after and compared, so a whole-array rewrite that quietly loses the empty/None gaps cannot pass itself off as a targeted edit. There is deliberately NO 'move' operation.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component variable name (own or inherited)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Name of the TArray property on the component template

params.name: index
params.description: 0-based element index. set_fields/remove need an existing index; insert accepts 0..Num (Num appends)

params.name: operation
params.description: 'set_fields' (default), 'insert' or 'remove'

params.name: fields
params.description: Object of { StructMemberName: value } applied to the element. Used by set_fields, and by insert when the element type is a struct

params.name: element
params.description: Whole-element JSON value. Used by insert for NON-struct element types (or instead of 'fields' for a struct)

params.name: compile
params.description: Optional bool (default true): compile so the edited template reinstances

params.name: save
params.description: Optional bool (default true): save the Blueprint package after the compile

commands.returns: { success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, component_name, property_name, source, operation, index, inner_type, num_before, num_after, fields_applied[], field_errors[], siblings_unchanged, siblings_changed[], element_value, post_compile_num, post_compile_element, compiled, saved, save_error?, verification } }

commands.name: set_blueprint_component_collision
commands.description: Set collision on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (own SCS or inherited via ICH), not on a spawned actor, applying in this order: `profile` through SetCollisionProfileName (which expands the profile into the FBodyInstance response array -- a raw reflection write would set the string and leave BodyInstance inconsistent, and that is the whole reason this is a separate tool), then `collision_enabled`, then per-channel `responses`. Use it instead of set_blueprint_component_properties for anything collision-shaped. Unknown channel, response or collision_enabled names are hard errors, never a silent default. Note the ORDER: a later profile would reset the per-channel responses, so responses always win here.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or name (required)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component to modify (required); must resolve to a UPrimitiveComponent or the call errors with "no collision to set"

params.name: profile
params.description: Collision profile name, e.g. "BlockAll" (optional). Applied FIRST, so it does not undo the per-channel responses below.

params.name: collision_enabled
params.description: ECollisionEnabled value name: NoCollision, QueryOnly, PhysicsOnly or QueryAndPhysics (optional). Any other string is an error.

params.name: responses
params.description: Object mapping channel -> response, e.g. {"Visibility":"Ignore","ECC_Pawn":"Overlap"} (optional). Channels accept the friendly display name or an ECC_* token (custom project channels included); responses are Ignore, Overlap or Block. An unknown channel is refused rather than defaulting to WorldStatic.

params.name: compile
params.description: Optional bool (default FALSE): compile the Blueprint afterwards so the FBodyInstance change reinstances on the next spawn/PIE. Without it the edit stays in the uncompiled template.

params.name: return_messages
params.description: No effect here: it is only read by the compile this tool may run internally, whose message log is discarded. Call compile_blueprint directly if you want the messages.

commands.returns: { success, data: { blueprint_name, component_name, source ("scs" | "inherited-ich" | "inherited-native": which template was written), profile?, collision_enabled?, responses_applied: [{channel, response}], compiled } } -- responses_applied lists ONLY the per-channel writes; profile and collision_enabled appear as their own fields only when they were given. Nothing is re-read: verify with get_blueprint_component_property or get_collision_info.

commands.name: set_blueprint_component_properties
commands.description: Set the DEFAULT of one or several properties on Blueprint component TEMPLATES -- own SCS components, ones INHERITED from a parent Blueprint (written as an InheritableComponentHandler override) and native subobjects -- with ONE compile and ONE save, then verify each value on the post-compile template. Use it for component templates: set_properties neither creates an inherited override nor compiles or saves; set_component_property edits placed actors. One write: component_name + property_name + property_value; several: overrides[]. TRAPS behind a green reply: (1) it can drop another component IN MEMORY -- count get_blueprint_components before and after, cure with reload_asset_package(on_dirty="discard"); (2) an object-reference write can land None and still report override_persisted:true -- check get_blueprint_component_overrides; (3) actors already placed keep their serialized value. Collision: set_blueprint_component_collision; override-free read: get_blueprint_component_property.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset path or short name

params.name: overrides
params.description: Optional array of { component_name, property_name, property_value } objects, applied in the given order. Required unless the single-write form (component_name + property_name + property_value) is given; both together apply overrides[] first, then the single write.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional single-write form: component variable name (own or inherited). Needs property_name and property_value too.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional single-write form: property to set on that component template.

params.name: property_value
params.description: Optional single-write form: the new value (any JSON type; same importer as set_component_property). An array value REWRITES THE WHOLE ARRAY, including the empty/None gaps -- set_blueprint_component_array_element edits one element and proves the siblings did not move.

params.name: compile
params.description: Optional bool (default true). false skips the compile: nothing is verifiable, every entry reports matches_requested=false with verification_status='not_verifiable'

params.name: save
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Saves the Blueprint package ONCE, after the compile

commands.returns: { success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, requested_count, applied_count, verified_count, mismatched_count, failed_count, compiled, saved, save_error?, equality_predicate, results: [{ index, component_name, property_name, source, component_class, override_persisted, applied, apply_error?, verification_status, matches_requested, post_value, post_source, note? }], verification } } -- source tells which template was hit (scs / inherited-ich / inherited-scs / inherited-native); component_class is that template's class, read before the compile; override_persisted is false only when an inherited-ich override did not survive the compile.

commands.name: set_blueprint_function_pure
commands.description: Mark a Blueprint function as PURE (or back to impure), the editor's "Pure" checkbox: a pure function has no exec pins and is re-evaluated wherever its output is read. REQUIRED to finish a UMG property binding -- FDelegateEditorBinding::IsBindingValid refuses any function that is not FUNC_BlueprintPure or const, so add_widget_property_binding will report valid:false until this has been run on the function. The counterpart reader is get_blueprint_functions's is_pure, which reads the same flag off the same UK2Node_FunctionEntry. WARNING: Turning a function pure REMOVES its exec pins: any existing wire into or out of them is dropped by the reconstruct, so do this BEFORE building the function's body, not after.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint owning the function.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function GRAPH (not an event; events cannot be pure).

params.name: is_pure
params.description: true to mark pure (default true), false to make it impure again.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, is_pure, was_pure, changed, function_flags } -- is_pure is RE-READ from the entry node after the compile, so it is evidence and not an echo.

commands.name: set_blueprint_function_rpc
commands.description: Turn a Blueprint FUNCTION into an RPC (rpc_type Server / Client / NetMulticast, or NotReplicated to undo it, plus reliable), then compile and read the FUNC_Net* flags back off the entry node. This is the ONLY headless way to author an RPC THAT TAKES ARGUMENTS: add_function_parameter cannot reach a custom event, so build the RPC as add_blueprint_function -> compile_blueprint -> add_function_parameter -> here.
