Engine limits that follow: a replicated function cannot return a value and cannot host latent nodes (put a Delay in a separate, parameterless custom event).

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of an existing FUNCTION graph on the Blueprint (a custom event has no entry node here and is refused).

params.name: rpc_type
params.description: One of "NotReplicated", "Server", "Client", "NetMulticast" (case-insensitive).

params.name: reliable
params.description: Mark the RPC reliable; ignored (and cleared) when rpc_type is NotReplicated; defaults to false

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, function_name, rpc_type, is_net, reliable, function_flags } -- re-read from the entry node's flags after compiling; rpc_type is the RESOLVED type, so compare it with what you asked for. Proof that the call really crosses the wire is not here: drive it in PIE and read the resulting state on the OTHER side.

commands.name: set_blueprint_variable_default
commands.description: Set the default value of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint: writes the live CDO and mirrors the result back into the serialized variable description so it survives save/reload. LIMIT (not a lie, a hard boundary): it CANNOT touch an INHERITED variable -- it answers "Variable 'X' is not declared on this blueprint" -- so the "child that only overrides a parent default" pattern needs the CDO route (execute_python + set_editor_property + compile_blueprint + save). And on a class with actors already placed in a level, the placed instances keep their serialized value: verify on the instances, never on the CDO.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint (inherited ones are refused)

params.name: value
params.description: New default in exported-text form, parsed into the variable's type; empty allowed. A value the type cannot parse is an error AND the previous value is restored (the engine's struct import zeroes the target before parsing, so a failed parse wipes the CDO).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, default_value, roundtrip_verified } -- default_value is re-exported from the CDO after the write, so it is the real stored value. WARNING: roundtrip_verified:false means the exported text does NOT re-import into the type (e.g. FGameplayTagContainer): the CDO holds the right value and the compiler's property copy carries it, but the serialized description was deliberately left empty because feeding an unparseable string back through a Full compile ZEROES the default. Verify that variable on the CDO after compiling, and prefer wiring it in the graph if it must survive a fresh regeneration.

commands.name: set_blueprint_variable_metadata
commands.description: Set the editor-facing checkboxes and text of an existing Blueprint variable: instance_editable (per-instance editability), save_game (CPF_SaveGame -- whether the variable goes into a .sav), expose_on_spawn (adds the variable as a pin on SpawnActor), category and tooltip. Only the fields present are touched; passing none is an error. This is the fix for a variable created by add_blueprint_variable, which is born NOT instance-editable while the readers report it as editable. Variable must be declared on THIS Blueprint; on a library variable the answer is a child class of your own, not this call. WARNING: this call does NOT compile: it structurally-modifies the Blueprint, which regenerates the SKELETON only, so a save_game just written is authored but NOT yet on the generated class the save archive reads -- the response says so in save_game_needs_compile, and the loop that finishes the job is compile_blueprint -> save_asset -> get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info and check save_game_generated.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint (inherited ones are refused).

params.name: instance_editable
params.description: true = editable on each placed actor. Verify by WRITING the placed instance and reading it back; the reporting field is unreliable for every variable.

params.name: save_game
params.description: true = tick "SaveGame" (CPF_SaveGame), so a SaveGame archive (ArIsSaveGame) serializes this variable; false unticks it. The only headless way to set this flag -- set_properties, Python, set_blueprint_variable_replication and BlueprintEditorLibrary all refuse it. Needs a compile to reach the generated class.

params.name: expose_on_spawn
params.description: true = the variable shows up as an input pin on SpawnActorFromClass. Verify on the NODE's pins, not on get_blueprint_variables' expose_on_spawn, which reports false for variables that ARE exposed.

params.name: category
params.description: Category to group the variable under in the editor

params.name: tooltip
params.description: Tooltip text shown for the variable

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, updated, save_game?, save_game_generated?, save_game_needs_compile? } -- updated:true only means at least one field was applied, not that it persisted. The three save_game_* fields appear only when save_game was passed, and are READ BACK after the write: save_game off the variable descriptor, save_game_generated off the FProperty of the generated class.

commands.name: set_blueprint_variable_replication
commands.description: Set a Blueprint variable's replication mode -- None / Replicated / RepNotify (RepNotify also creates the OnRep_<Variable> function graph if missing) -- then compiles and reads CPF_Net/CPF_RepNotify back. TRAP: the full green report can come back WITHOUT the flag surviving into the generated class (a variable reported is_replicated:true that never replicates; re-running this same call fixes it). The ground truth is audit_replication (its payload's replicated_variables list), then compile and re-audit -- never this return, and never one client alone.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited/native variables are refused).

params.name: mode
params.description: One of "None", "Replicated", "RepNotify" (case-insensitive). "None" also clears the RepNotify function and resets the lifetime condition.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, mode, is_replicated, is_rep_notify, rep_notify_func, property_flags } -- read back from the variable's flags after compiling, which is necessary but NOT sufficient (see the trap above).

commands.name: set_component_replication
commands.description: Set bReplicates on ONE SCS component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (the archetype, not a spawned actor's instance), compile, and read it back off the template. It governs the component's own PROPERTY replication; note that a component declared in the SCS already routes its RPCs through its stable network name WITHOUT this flag (a component added at RUNTIME does not, and loses them). For the owning actor use set_blueprint_class_replication.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint.

params.name: component_name
params.description: SCS component variable name on this Blueprint (inherited-only components have no local SCS node and are not found).

params.name: replicates
params.description: Whether the component should replicate. Required.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, component_name, replicates } -- replicates is re-read from the template after compiling.

commands.name: set_event_dispatcher_signature
commands.description: Add to (mode="add", the idempotent default) or rewrite (mode="replace") the parameter list of a dispatcher this Blueprint OWNS -- inherited dispatchers have no local signature graph and are refused with the list of owned ones. Every requested type is resolved BEFORE anything is mutated, so a bad type aborts cleanly. The parameters become the OUTPUT pins of every bound handler and the INPUT pins of add_broadcast_node; existing nodes keep stale pins until compile_blueprint reconstructs them.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path that OWNS the dispatcher (inherited dispatchers cannot be edited here).

params.name: dispatcher_name
params.description: Name of an existing event dispatcher (created by add_event_dispatcher or the editor).

params.name: params
params.description: Array of parameter specs to add: [ { name: string, type: string } ]. Dispatcher params are input-only; 'type' accepts the same strings as add_function_parameter (bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, Array<T>, an object/class/struct/enum name or path).

params.name: mode
params.description: "add" (default, idempotent: skip a param whose name already exists) or "replace" (clear the existing signature first, then add the given params).

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, mode, added: [string], params: [ { name, type } ], param_count }

commands.name: set_mesh_material_color
commands.description: Tint one material slot of a Blueprint component template by creating a DYNAMIC material instance (MID) over the current or given material, setting one vector parameter, and assigning the MID to the slot. A MID is a RUNTIME object, so this is a quick preview, NOT the way to author a change that must survive save/reload -- for a persistent tint make a MaterialInstanceConstant and assign it with apply_material_to_blueprint. A parameter_name the material does not declare is accepted silently and simply does nothing.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS component; must be a UPrimitiveComponent

params.name: color
params.description: RGBA color [R, G, B, A] as floats, each clamped to 0.0-1.0; exactly 4 values are required

params.name: material_slot
params.description: Optional slot index; defaults to 0

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Optional vector parameter name; defaults to "BaseColor". A name the material does not declare is NOT reported as an error -- it just has no visible effect.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Optional material asset path to use as the MID's parent; without it the component's current slot material is used, falling back to /Engine/BasicShapes/BasicShapeMaterial

commands.returns: { component: string, material_slot: int, parameter_name: string, color: [number, number, number, number], success: bool } -- success:true only means the MID was created and assigned; re-read with get_blueprint_material_info after a save/reload to see whether anything persisted.

commands.name: set_physics_properties
commands.description: Set simulate-physics, mass override, linear and angular damping on ONE primitive component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node only -- inherited components are not found here, and it is the template, not a placed actor). Only the fields present are touched. It does NOT compile and does NOT save. For any other property of a component template use set_blueprint_component_properties, which is ICH-aware and reaches inherited components.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS component; must resolve to a UPrimitiveComponent or the call errors

params.name: simulate_physics
params.description: Optional bool to toggle physics simulation

params.name: mass
params.description: Optional mass override in kg (applied as SetMassOverrideInKg, not a scale)

params.name: linear_damping
params.description: Optional linear damping coefficient

params.name: angular_damping
params.description: Optional angular damping coefficient

commands.returns: { component: string } -- just the component name back. NOTHING is read back, so verify with get_blueprint_component_property on each property you set.

commands.name: set_pin_default_value
commands.description: Write the literal default of an UNCONNECTED input pin and return the value read BACK off the pin. Struct pins are canonicalized: a bare GameplayTag name becomes (TagName="X") and an UNREGISTERED tag is rejected up front instead of silently landing as an empty tag; value_json nativizes any struct (and is the only way to put SEVERAL tags in a GameplayTagContainer). Array/set/map pins are refused (use a MakeArray/MakeSet/MakeMap node) and so are pins currently split into sub-pins (recombine_blueprint_pin first). A plain string is fine for an FText pin. TRAP: on a FormatText "Format" pin the literal IS written but the {argument} pins are NOT created, leaving a valid, useless node -- build the string with Concat_StrStr / Conv_StringToText instead.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint asset name or path

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node owning the pin

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Pin name; an INPUT pin of that name is preferred, any pin with the name is the fallback

params.name: value
params.description: Literal default in the pin's exported-text form; empty string allowed (clears it). For a struct pin, "()" clears and a leading "(" is passed through untouched.

params.name: value_json
params.description: Optional JSON object nativized into the struct's export-text form, for STRUCT pins only. For an FGameplayTagContainer it must carry a "GameplayTags" array (["A","B"] or [{"TagName":"A"}]) and every tag is validated; takes precedence over 'value'.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { node_id, pin_name, default_value } -- default_value is re-read from the pin AFTER the write, so it is the oracle for what actually landed (a rejected value shows up as the old one).

commands.name: set_property_access_path
commands.description: Rewrite a UK2Node_PropertyAccess node's binding Path and reconstruct the node so the leaf property re-resolves and the Value pin re-types, then return the path READ BACK -- so resolved:true is real evidence the new binding points at something. It does NOT recompile: follow with compile_blueprint with return_messages=true. reconstructed:false means the PropertyAccessEditor feature was unavailable: the path WAS written but text_path/resolved_pin stay stale until the graph reopens.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path (usually an Animation Blueprint).

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the property-access node; any other node class is refused by name.

params.name: path
params.description: The new path: either an array of segment strings (["InAnimInstance","Foo"]) OR a dotted string ("InAnimInstance.Foo"). An empty result is an error, never a cleared binding.

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted.

commands.returns: { node_id, graph_name, reconstructed, path:[string], text_path, resolved, resolved_pin, note? } -- path/text_path/resolved are re-read AFTER the reconstruct, so they are the oracle rather than an echo.

commands.name: set_replication_condition
commands.description: Set the ELifetimeCondition (COND_OwnerOnly, COND_SkipOwner, COND_InitialOnly...) that decides WHICH clients get a replicated variable, then compile. It is the second half of set_blueprint_variable_replication, which decides WHETHER it replicates at all: on a variable that is not Replicated/RepNotify the condition is stored and completely INERT, and the response says so through is_replicated:false plus a "note". Blueprint-declared variables only.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited ones are refused).

params.name: condition
params.description: ELifetimeCondition name, with or without the COND_ prefix (e.g. "OwnerOnly" or "COND_OwnerOnly"); an unknown name is an error.

commands.returns: { blueprint_name, variable_name, condition, is_replicated, note? } -- condition is the canonical COND_ name that was stored; is_replicated:false means the setting has no effect yet.

commands.name: set_static_mesh_properties
commands.description: Assign a static mesh asset and/or a slot-0 material to a mesh component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node, not a placed actor) through the component's SetStaticMesh/SetMaterial. Does NOT compile and does NOT save; the reply reads the template back (static_mesh, material and a *_set flag for each). A path that does not load as a mesh or material, or a call with neither, fails with nothing changed. Use apply_material_to_blueprint when only a material is changing or the slot is not 0, and set_blueprint_component_properties for any other template property or an inherited component.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name of an OWN SCS mesh component

params.name: static_mesh
params.description: Optional asset path of the UStaticMesh to assign; a path that does not load as a StaticMesh fails the call and nothing is changed

params.name: material
params.description: Optional asset path of the UMaterialInterface for slot 0; a path that does not load as a material fails the call and nothing is changed. At least one of static_mesh and material is required.

commands.returns: { component: string, static_mesh: string, material: string, static_mesh_set: bool, material_set: bool } -- read back from the template: static_mesh is the mesh it holds and material its slot-0 material (the override, else the mesh's own), each an object path or "None"; <field>_set is true when that field was passed and the template now holds it. Nothing is compiled or saved.

retired.how: blueprint_name, component_name, property_name="StaticMesh", property_value="/Game/SM_..."; the material with apply_material_to_blueprint

commands.name: spawn_blueprint_actor
commands.description: Spawn an instance of a Blueprint class as an actor and report WHICH world took it and whether the actor has AUTHORITY. Pick it for any Blueprint class; spawn_actor places the built-in engine types (StaticMeshActor, lights, CameraActor, Character), and the typed spawn_* tools place an engine class with its own fields. The default (world absent or 'editor') places it in the EDITOR level, not in play. For anything that must exist for every player during PIE use world='server'; world='pie' is ambiguous and can land on the CLIENT, where the actor has no authority, no AI controller and no server-side existence while looking identical in the payload. The actor is NOT saved into the map: save_level afterwards for an editor-world spawn.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Name of the blueprint

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label applied to the spawned actor (SetActorLabel); it is not the object name and is not made unique

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) spawns into the editor level | 'server' spawns into the PIE world WITH AUTHORITY (what you want for anything that must exist for every player: an actor spawned into the client world has no authority and no server-side existence) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context -- can land on the CLIENT) | 'game' (alias of 'pie')

commands.returns: { actor JSON via DescribeActorObject, world: string, has_authority: bool (AActor::HasAuthority() read off the spawned actor), local_role: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

retired.how: type=<Blueprint asset path>, name, location, rotation, world (has_authority is in the reply)

commands.name: split_blueprint_pin
commands.description: Split a struct-typed pin (Vector, Rotator, Transform...) into its scalar sub-pins and return their names, so each component can be wired or defaulted on its own instead of writing the whole struct literal. Refused when the schema says the pin is not splittable. Note the interaction: set_pin_default_value REFUSES a pin that is currently split -- recombine_blueprint_pin first if you want to write the struct as one value.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the node owning the pin.

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Name of the struct pin to split (either direction).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { split, sub_pins:[string] } -- sub_pins are the names to pass to connect_pins / set_pin_default_value from now on (e.g. "NewLocation_X").

commands.name: validate_pin_connection
commands.description: Dry-run the K2 schema's verdict on a pin pair WITHOUT touching the graph: returns valid plus the schema's own message (which names the incompatible types) and its raw response code. connect_pins runs the same check and then connects, so use this one to test a plan before committing a build_blueprint_graph batch whose rollback can be refused, or to find out WHY a connection was rejected without leaving anything behind.

params.name: blueprint_name
params.description: Blueprint name or path.

params.name: source_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the source node.

params.name: source_pin
params.description: Output pin name on the source node (falls back to any pin with that name).

params.name: target_node_id
params.description: NodeGuid of the target node; must be in the same graph as the source.

params.name: target_pin
params.description: Input pin name on the target node (falls back to any pin with that name).

params.name: graph_name
params.description: Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted

commands.returns: { valid, message, response_code } -- valid is false only for an outright DISALLOW; a response that would connect WITH a conversion node or by breaking an existing link still reports valid:true, and "message" is where that shows.

commands.name: add_camera_component
commands.description: Add a UCameraComponent to an actor placed in the editor world, found by name or label, attached to its root or to parent_component (e.g. a boom from add_spring_arm), and set FOV, projection, aspect, transform, rotation flags and post-process in one undo step. Pick it over add_component_to_actor for a non-root parent or for post_process_settings: each value it sets also turns on its bOverride_ flag, which a plain property write does not, so it takes effect; for a Blueprint's camera use add_component_to_blueprint. If the actor already has a camera component, that first one is configured instead, whatever its name, overwriting only the fields you pass. The level is marked dirty, not saved. An invalid projection_mode or a post_process_settings key that names no property is an error and nothing is created or written.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the target actor.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional name for a new component (defaults to "Camera"); a name another object of the actor already has gets a unique variant, returned in component_name. Ignored when the actor already has a camera component, which is configured whatever its name.

params.name: parent_component
params.description: Optional name of a USceneComponent on the same actor to attach to (e.g. "SpringArm"). Default = actor root component.

params.name: field_of_view
params.description: Optional float. Horizontal FOV in degrees (1..170).

params.name: aspect_ratio
params.description: Optional float. Aspect ratio (e.g. 16/9). 0 = auto.

params.name: ortho_width
params.description: Optional float. Orthographic width (only used when projection_mode = "Orthographic").

params.name: projection_mode
params.description: Optional string. "Perspective" or "Orthographic".

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] relative location vs parent.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] relative rotation vs parent.

params.name: b_use_controller_view_rotation
params.description: Optional bool. Match pawn control rotation.

params.name: b_use_pawn_control_rotation
params.description: Optional bool. Alias for b_use_controller_view_rotation — sets UCameraComponent::bUsePawnControlRotation.

params.name: b_lock_to_hmd
params.description: Optional bool. Lock orientation to the HMD.

params.name: post_process_settings
params.description: Optional object of FPostProcessSettings fields by property name, e.g. {"BloomIntensity": 2}; each value also turns on its bOverride_ companion unless the object sets that companion itself; a key that names no property is an error.

params.name: post_process_blend_weight
params.description: Optional float. Weight of post-process (0..1). 0 means post-process disabled.

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, parent_component, already_existed, applied_count, field_of_view, aspect_ratio, projection_mode, location: [x,y,z], rotation: [pitch,yaw,roll], post_process_blend_weight }

commands.name: add_camera_node_child
commands.description: Populates the Children of a composite rig node (the rig RootNode must be a UArrayCameraNode ("Sequence"); set it via set_camera_rig_root_node node_type=ArrayCameraNode). Creates a new UCameraNode of child_node_type outered to the rig and appends it, in one undo step, then saves the rig. Idempotent via optional index: index<Children.Num() REPLACES that slot instead of appending. added is the read-back of the new child in its slot; a failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory. Gameplay Camera System is EXPERIMENTAL (plugin GameplayCameras). Set its parameters with set_camera_node_parameters child_index; inverse: remove_camera_node_child.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset whose composite RootNode is edited (required)

params.name: child_node_type
params.description: A concrete UCameraNode subclass name for the new child, e.g. "OffsetCameraNode", "FieldOfViewCameraNode" (required)

params.name: index
params.description: Optional child slot. If given and < current child count, REPLACES that slot (deterministic re-runs); otherwise appends.

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, child_node_type, child_class, child_index, children_count, added, replaced, saved, save_error }

commands.name: add_gameplay_camera_component
commands.description: Add a UGameplayCameraComponent to an editor-world actor (name or label) and point it at a UCameraAsset via SetCameraAsset, which also rebuilds its parameter overrides; add_component_to_actor does neither. A new one is an instance component attached to the actor's root (an actor without a root takes it as its root), in one undo step; parent_component and is_root say where it went. Idempotent: an actor that already has one has that first one re-pointed, its attachment kept, and when it already points at the asset nothing is written (changed false). A camera asset that does not load is an error and nothing changes. The level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level). Activation needs a running game or PIE.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor (required)

params.name: camera_asset_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraAsset to reference (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, already_existed, camera_asset_path, camera_set, changed: bool (false when the component already pointed at the asset: nothing written), parent_component: string (what the component is attached to; empty when it is the root or unattached), is_root: bool }

commands.name: add_spring_arm
commands.description: Add a USpringArmComponent (camera boom) to an actor placed in the editor world, found by name or label; if the actor already has a spring arm, that first one is configured instead, whatever its name, overwriting only the fields you pass. A new arm becomes an instance component attached to the root. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved. Negative lengths, sizes and speeds clamp to 0; an unknown probe_channel is an error and nothing is created or written. Attach a camera with add_camera_component (parent_component = the returned component_name); for a Blueprint asset use add_component_to_blueprint.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the target actor in the editor world.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional name for a new component (defaults to "SpringArm"); a name another object of the actor already has gets a unique variant, returned in component_name. Ignored when the actor already has a spring arm, which is configured whatever its name.

params.name: target_arm_length
params.description: Optional float. Natural length of the spring arm (uu). Default 300.

params.name: socket_offset
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] relative offset applied at the spring-arm tip.

params.name: target_offset
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world-space offset applied at the start of the spring.

params.name: probe_size
params.description: Optional float. Collision probe radius.

params.name: probe_channel
params.description: Optional string name of ECollisionChannel (e.g. "Camera", "Visibility"). Default "Camera".

params.name: b_do_collision_test
params.description: Optional bool. Enable camera collision probe.

params.name: b_use_pawn_control_rotation
params.description: Optional bool. Use the parent pawn's view rotation.

params.name: b_inherit_pitch
params.description: Optional bool. Inherit pitch from parent.

params.name: b_inherit_yaw
params.description: Optional bool. Inherit yaw from parent.

params.name: b_inherit_roll
params.description: Optional bool. Inherit roll from parent.

params.name: b_enable_camera_lag
params.description: Optional bool. Enable positional lag.

params.name: b_enable_camera_rotation_lag
params.description: Optional bool. Enable rotational lag.

params.name: camera_lag_speed
params.description: Optional float. Positional lag speed (units/sec).

params.name: camera_rotation_lag_speed
params.description: Optional float. Rotational lag speed (deg/sec).

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, already_existed, applied_count, target_arm_length, socket_offset: [x,y,z], target_offset: [x,y,z], probe_size, probe_channel, b_do_collision_test, b_use_pawn_control_rotation, b_inherit_pitch, b_inherit_yaw, b_inherit_roll, b_enable_camera_lag, b_enable_camera_rotation_lag, camera_lag_speed, camera_rotation_lag_speed }

commands.name: build_camera_rig
commands.description: Build a Gameplay Cameras UCameraRigAsset, found by content path, in memory as the rig editor's Build does: its node hierarchy, interface and parameters are rebuilt from the current nodes, replacing the previous build data. built is true when build_status comes back Clean or CleanWithWarnings; WithErrors fails the call with the build errors in its message, and messages lists every build message with its severity (the editor log gets them too). Nothing is saved (saving the rig builds it again anyway); what the build changes is recorded in the call's undo step. A rig that does not resolve is an error. Edit the rig first with set_camera_rig_root_node, set_camera_node_parameters or add_camera_node_child; read its nodes with get_camera_rig_nodes; create one with create_camera_rig_asset.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: Content path to the UCameraRigAsset, e.g. "/Game/Cameras/CR_Player" (required)

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, built, build_status, messages: [{ severity, message }] }

commands.name: create_camera
commands.description: Spawn a new ACameraActor in the editor world (never in PIE) at an optional location and rotation, with camera_name as its outliner label. Labels need not be unique, so address the camera later by the returned actor_name. Each location axis must be within +-100000, otherwise an error. The level is marked dirty, not saved. location_set, rotation_set and label_set compare what the spawned actor reports with the request. Move or re-aim it with set_camera_transform; spawn_actor places a CameraActor in PIE too; add_camera_component puts a camera on an existing actor.

params.name: camera_name
params.description: Name to assign to the new camera actor.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location for the new camera (defaults to origin)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] world rotation for the new camera (defaults to zero)

commands.returns: { camera_name: string, camera_created: bool, actor_name: string, location_set: bool, rotation_set: bool, label_set: bool, actual_label: string, actual_location: [number, number, number] }

commands.name: create_camera_asset
commands.description: Create a UCameraAsset (Gameplay Camera System, Experimental plugin) at package_path/name and save it; one already there is returned unchanged with created=false, already_existed=true and saved=false (nothing is written), another asset class there is an error. A failed save of a new asset makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Returns asset_path and saved. Next: set_camera_asset_director, then add_gameplay_camera_component.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the UCameraAsset to create, e.g. "CA_Player"; also the last segment of its path

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content folder (default "/Game/Cameras")

commands.returns: { name, asset_path, asset_class, created, already_existed, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: create_camera_rig_asset
commands.description: Create an empty camera rig asset (UCameraRigAsset, from the Experimental Gameplay Cameras plugin) at package_path/name and save it; it has no root node yet. Idempotent: a camera rig already at that path is returned unchanged with created=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, since nothing is written; an asset of another class there is an error. Not an undo step. Then give it a root node with set_camera_rig_root_node, tune it with set_camera_node_parameters or add_camera_node_child, build it with build_camera_rig, and run it from a camera asset (create_camera_asset) through set_camera_asset_director; get_camera_rig_nodes reads it back. A failed save of a new rig makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, and the rig left in memory.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name, e.g. 'CR_Player'; package_path/name must form a valid long package name.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder as a long package path, e.g. '/Game/Cameras/Rigs' (default "/Game/Cameras").

commands.returns: { name, asset_path, asset_class, created, already_existed, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: create_camera_rig_crane
commands.description: Spawn an unrotated CameraRig_Crane actor in the editor world with the given pitch, yaw and arm length; it is always labelled "CameraRigCrane_MCP", so address it later by the returned internal_name. Returns location and the read-back crane values; the level is not saved.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin; each axis within -100000 to 100000)

params.name: crane_pitch
params.description: Crane pitch angle in degrees (optional, default 0)

params.name: crane_yaw
params.description: Crane yaw angle in degrees (optional, default 0)

params.name: arm_length
params.description: Crane arm length (optional, default 500.0, valid 0-100000)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, internal_name: string, location: [number, number, number], crane_pitch: number, crane_yaw: number, arm_length: number, success: bool }

commands.name: create_camera_rig_rail
commands.description: Spawn an unrotated CameraRig_Rail actor in the editor world; with more than 2 points the rail is rebuilt as a straight 500-unit line along local X. Always labelled "CameraRigRail_MCP", so address it by the returned internal_name, e.g. in set_camera_rig_rail_position. Not saved.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin; each axis within -100000 to 100000)

params.name: num_spline_points
params.description: Number of spline points on the rail (optional, default 2, valid 2-100)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, internal_name: string, location: [number, number, number], num_spline_points: number, success: bool }

retired.how: type="CameraRig_Rail", name, location; reshape the rail with set_spline_points

commands.name: create_camera_shake_blueprint
commands.description: Create a Blueprint asset parented to UCameraShakeBase, compile and save it.  UCameraShakeBase is abstract but Blueprintable; the generated Blueprint subclass is concrete. Idempotent: if the asset already exists it is loaded and returned.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. BP_ExplosionShake)

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/Blueprints")

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_camera_shake: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: get_camera_asset_info
commands.description: Reports which camera director a Gameplay Cameras camera asset (UCameraAsset) uses and, for a SingleCameraDirector (the one-rig director), the camera rig asset it runs. Read-only: loads the asset, changes and saves nothing; a path that does not load a UCameraAsset is an error. An asset without a director gives has_director false and director_class "None"; any director other than SingleCameraDirector gives an empty camera_rig_path, as does one whose rig is unset. To give the asset a one-rig director use set_camera_asset_director; to look inside the rig, get_camera_rig_nodes; to create an asset, create_camera_asset; to use it on an actor, add_gameplay_camera_component.

params.name: camera_asset_path
params.description: Package or object path of the UCameraAsset (required), e.g. "/Game/Cameras/CA_ThirdPerson", as create_camera_asset returns it.

commands.returns: { camera_asset_path, has_director, director_class, camera_rig_path } -- camera_asset_path is the resolved object path; camera_rig_path is empty unless a SingleCameraDirector has a rig

commands.name: get_camera_post_process
commands.description: Read the overridden PostProcessSettings off a camera actor's camera component: only the fields whose bOverride_* companion is on are returned (those actually contributing). set_properties writes them (PostProcessSettings with its bOverride_* flags). Pure reader.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the camera actor to query.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, post_process_blend_weight: number, overridden_count: int, settings: object (overridden field -> value; scalars as numbers, wheels as [R,G,B,master], scene_color_tint as [R,G,B,A]) }

commands.name: get_camera_rig_nodes
commands.description: Reports a camera rig's RootNode class and its camera-parameter fields (name + value), plus, for a composite ArrayCameraNode root, its Children (index, class and their own camera-parameter fields). Read-only. It reads what set_camera_node_parameters writes (child_index for a child), add_camera_node_child adds and remove_camera_node_child removes.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset (required)

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, has_root_node, root_node_class, parameters:[{name, value}], children:[{index, class, parameters:[{name, value}]}] }

commands.name: get_cameras
commands.description: List the camera actors (ACameraActor or CineCameraActor) in the editor world with their world location [X, Y, Z], rotation [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] in degrees and FOV, or with camera_name only the one camera found by object name or label (case-insensitive, first match; an unknown name is an error). set_actor_transform is the writer of the transform.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum number of cameras to return (optional, default 1000, valid 1-10000)

params.name: camera_name
params.description: Optional camera to report alone, matched by actor name or label; a camera without a camera component reports fov 90

commands.returns: { cameras: [{ name: string, label: string, is_valid: bool, location: [number, number, number], rotation: [number, number, number], fov: number? }], total_count: number, max_results: number, truncated: bool, camera_name?: string }

commands.name: get_cine_camera_settings
commands.description: Read the full cine-camera configuration off a CineCameraActor's CineCameraComponent: filmback (sensor size/offsets/aspect + preset), lens (focal/f-stop range, squeeze, blades, preset), focus (method/manual distance/offset/smoothing) and the current focal length / aperture / focus distance. Pure reader; mutates nothing.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the CineCameraActor to query.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, filmback: { sensor_width, sensor_height, sensor_horizontal_offset, sensor_vertical_offset, sensor_aspect_ratio, preset_name }, lens: { min_focal_length, max_focal_length, min_fstop, max_fstop, minimum_focus_distance, squeeze_factor, diaphragm_blade_count, preset_name }, focus: { method, manual_focus_distance, focus_offset, smooth_focus_changes, focus_smoothing_interp_speed }, current_focal_length, current_aperture, current_focus_distance, horizontal_fov, vertical_fov, note }

commands.name: list_camera_node_types
commands.description: Lists all concrete UCameraNode subclasses usable in a camera rig. Read-only reflection (GetDerivedClasses).
commands.returns: { base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }

commands.name: remove_camera_node_child
commands.description: Remove the child at index from the composite ArrayCameraNode root of a camera rig, in one undo step, then save the rig. Inverse of add_camera_node_child; the children after it move down one index. A root that is not an ArrayCameraNode or an index out of range is an error and nothing changes; a failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory. The reply re-reads the children (children). Gameplay Camera System is EXPERIMENTAL (plugin GameplayCameras). Read: get_camera_rig_nodes.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset whose composite RootNode is edited (required)

params.name: index
params.description: Index of the child to remove (get_camera_rig_nodes lists them) (required)

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, index, removed_class, removed, children_count, children:[string], saved, save_error }

commands.name: set_camera_asset_director
commands.description: Wires a new USingleCameraDirector on a UCameraAsset, pointing it at a UCameraRigAsset (the "one rig" director) and replacing any director it had, then saves the asset. One undo step. director_set is the GetCameraDirector read-back; a failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory.

params.name: camera_asset_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraAsset (required)

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset the director runs (required)

commands.returns: { camera_asset_path, camera_rig_path, director_class, director_set, saved, save_error }

commands.name: set_camera_fov
commands.description: Set the field of view (degrees, above 0 up to 180) of the camera component of an ACameraActor or CineCameraActor in the editor world, found by object name or label. No undo transaction and nothing is saved. Returns previous_fov, actual_fov and fov_set; get_cameras with camera_name reads it.

params.name: camera_name
params.description: Name of the camera to modify (matches actor name or label).

params.name: fov
params.description: Field of view in degrees. Must be between 0.0 and 180.0.

commands.returns: { camera_name: string, requested_fov: number, previous_fov: number, actual_fov: number, fov_set: bool, camera_valid: bool }

commands.name: set_camera_node_parameters
commands.description: Sets parameters on a camera rig's RootNode by reflection, all or nothing: every property is parsed first, and an unknown property or a value that does not fit fails the call, naming each one in failed, with nothing written or saved. FXxxCameraParameter props take the raw value, a bool or a number (a whole one for an integer), written to the nested .Value; other props set directly. Otherwise all of them are written in one undo step and the rig is saved; applied reads the stored values back. Values the node already holds are a success with changed false, saved false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory. With child_index the node edited is that child of a composite ArrayCameraNode root (add_camera_node_child); an index out of range, or a root that is not an ArrayCameraNode, is an error. Read the values back with get_camera_rig_nodes.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset whose RootNode is edited (required)

params.name: properties
params.description: JSON object { PropertyName: value, ... } (e.g. {"FieldOfView": 90})

params.name: child_index
params.description: Optional index of a child of the composite ArrayCameraNode root to edit instead of the root node itself

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, node_class, child_index?, changed, set:[name], failed:[{name, error}], applied:{name: stored_value_text}, saved, save_error, note }

commands.name: set_camera_post_process
commands.description: Write PostProcessSettings on a camera actor's camera component (plain or cine) by field presence, turning on each field's bOverride_* companion so it takes effect (like a PostProcess Volume). Supplied fields only; scalars are numbers, color-grading wheels are [R,G,B,master] arrays, scene_color_tint is [R,G,B,A]. Absolute + idempotent. Forces PostProcessBlendWeight>0 and marks the render state dirty.

params.name: actor_name

params.name: bloom_intensity
params.description: Optional bloom intensity (number).

params.name: bloom_threshold
params.description: Optional bloom threshold (number).

params.name: vignette_intensity
params.description: Optional vignette intensity 0..1 (number).

params.name: film_grain_intensity
params.description: Optional film grain intensity 0..1 (number).

params.name: chromatic_aberration_intensity
params.description: Optional chromatic aberration / scene fringe intensity (number).

params.name: chromatic_aberration_start_offset
params.description: Optional chromatic aberration start offset 0..1 (number).

params.name: exposure_bias
params.description: Optional auto-exposure bias / EV compensation (number).

params.name: exposure_min_brightness
params.description: Optional auto-exposure minimum brightness (number).

params.name: exposure_max_brightness
params.description: Optional auto-exposure maximum brightness (number).

params.name: exposure_speed_up
params.description: Optional auto-exposure adaptation speed up (number).

params.name: exposure_speed_down
params.description: Optional auto-exposure adaptation speed down (number).

params.name: ambient_occlusion_intensity
params.description: Optional ambient occlusion intensity 0..1 (number).

params.name: ambient_occlusion_radius
params.description: Optional ambient occlusion radius (number).

params.name: color_saturation
params.description: Optional color saturation wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: color_contrast
params.description: Optional color contrast wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: color_gamma
params.description: Optional color gamma wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: color_gain
params.description: Optional color gain wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: color_offset
params.description: Optional color offset wheel [R,G,B,master] (array).

params.name: scene_color_tint
params.description: Optional scene color tint [R,G,B,A] (array).

params.name: white_temp
params.description: Optional white balance temperature (number).

params.name: white_tint
params.description: Optional white balance tint (number).

params.name: depth_of_field_fstop
params.description: Optional depth-of-field f-stop (number).

params.name: depth_of_field_focal_distance
params.description: Optional depth-of-field focal distance in cm (number).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, applied_count: int, applied: object (field -> value read back), post_process_blend_weight: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_camera_rig_rail_position
commands.description: Set CurrentPositionOnRail of a CameraRig_Rail actor in the editor world, found by object name or label (case-insensitive, first match): 0.0 is the start of the rail spline and 1.0 its end, and the rig moves its camera mount there on its next tick. The property is written directly and read back: no undo step, the level is not marked dirty and nothing is saved. A position outside 0 to 1, an empty name or no such rail is an error; success is false (an outcome error) only when the read-back differs. Spawn a rail with create_camera_rig_rail and pass its internal_name here; a crane rig is create_camera_rig_crane; a plain camera moves with set_camera_transform.

params.name: rig_actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the CameraRig_Rail actor, e.g. the internal_name create_camera_rig_rail returns.

params.name: position
params.description: Normalised position on the rail, 0.0 to 1.0, as a fraction of the spline length.

commands.returns: { rig_actor_name: string, position: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_camera_rig_root_node
commands.description: Replace the RootNode of a Gameplay Cameras UCameraRigAsset with a new, default-valued node of node_type; the previous root and everything under it (children, parameter values) is dropped. Runs in an undo transaction and saves the rig; a failed save fails the call, with saved false and save_error, and leaves the change in memory. Does not build the rig (build_camera_rig does). Valid node_type names come from list_camera_node_types; configure the new root with set_camera_node_parameters, give an ArrayCameraNode root children with add_camera_node_child, and read it back with get_camera_rig_nodes.

params.name: camera_rig_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UCameraRigAsset (required)

params.name: node_type
params.description: A concrete UCameraNode subclass name, e.g. "FieldOfViewCameraNode", "OffsetCameraNode", "ArrayCameraNode" (required)

commands.returns: { camera_rig_path, node_type, node_class, root_set, saved, save_error }

commands.name: set_camera_transform
commands.description: Update the location and/or rotation of an existing camera.

params.name: camera_name
params.description: Name of the camera to modify (matches actor name or label).

params.name: location
params.description: Optional new [X, Y, Z] world location; if omitted, location is preserved

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional new [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] world rotation; if omitted, rotation is preserved

commands.returns: { camera_name: string, transform_set: bool, location_set: bool, rotation_set: bool, actual_location: [number, number, number], actual_rotation: [number, number, number] }

commands.name: set_cine_camera_aperture
commands.description: Set CurrentAperture, the f-stop that drives depth of field, on the CineCameraComponent of an editor-world actor found by object name or label (case-insensitive, first match): a CineCameraActor, or any actor carrying that component. The component clamps it to its lens MinFStop and MaxFStop, so the value is read back and success is false (an outcome error) when it differs from the request. No undo step, the level is not marked dirty, nothing is saved. An aperture outside 0.01 to 512, an empty name, or an actor without the component is an error. Widen the f-stop range with set_cine_camera_lens; focal length: set_cine_camera_focal_length; focus distance: set_cine_camera_focus; read back with get_cine_camera_settings.

params.name: camera_actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the CineCameraActor (or other actor with a CineCameraComponent) to modify.

params.name: aperture
params.description: F-stop value. Must be between 0.01 and 512.0.

commands.returns: { camera_actor_name: string, aperture: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_cine_camera_filmback
commands.description: Set the sensor size (filmback, in mm) of the CineCameraComponent on an editor-world actor found by name or label; sensor offsets are reset to 0. No undo transaction, nothing saved. Returns the read-back sensor_width, sensor_height and aspect_ratio; success is false when they do not match.

params.name: camera_actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the CineCameraActor to modify.

params.name: sensor_width
params.description: Sensor width in mm. Must be positive and <= 200.

params.name: sensor_height
params.description: Sensor height in mm. Must be positive and <= 200.

commands.returns: { camera_actor_name: string, sensor_width: number, sensor_height: number, aspect_ratio: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_cine_camera_focal_length
commands.description: Set CurrentFocalLength (mm) on the CineCameraComponent of an editor-world actor found by object name or label (case-insensitive, first match): a CineCameraActor, or any actor carrying that component. The component clamps the value to its lens MinFocalLength and MaxFocalLength, so it is read back with the resulting horizontal and vertical FOV, and success is false (an outcome error) when the read-back differs from the request. No undo step, the level is not marked dirty, nothing is saved. A focal_length outside 0 to 1000, an empty name, or an actor without the component is an error. Widen the lens limits with set_cine_camera_lens; aperture: set_cine_camera_aperture; focus: set_cine_camera_focus; read all of it back with get_cine_camera_settings.

params.name: camera_actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the CineCameraActor (or other actor with a CineCameraComponent) to modify.

params.name: focal_length
params.description: Focal length in millimetres. Must be between 0.0 and 1000.0.

commands.returns: { camera_actor_name: string, focal_length: number, horizontal_fov: number, vertical_fov: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_cine_camera_focus
commands.description: Replace the focus settings of the CineCameraComponent on an editor-world actor found by name or label: method, manual focus distance and smoothing; other focus fields, including the tracked actor, reset to defaults. Returns the read-back focus_method and focus_distance; no undo, nothing saved.

params.name: camera_actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the CineCameraActor to modify.

params.name: focus_method
params.description: Focus method — one of "Manual", "Tracking", or "Disable".

params.name: focus_distance
params.description: Manual focus distance in cm (optional, default 1000.0)

params.name: smoothing_speed
params.description: Focus smoothing interpolation speed; 0 disables smoothing (optional, default 4.0)

commands.returns: { camera_actor_name: string, focus_method: string, focus_distance: number, success: bool }

commands.name: set_cine_camera_lens
commands.description: Replace the lens limits of the CineCameraComponent on an editor-world actor found by name or label: focal length and f-stop ranges plus blade count; minimum focus distance resets to 0 and squeeze factor to 1. Returns the read-back focal range; no undo, nothing saved.

params.name: camera_actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the CineCameraActor to modify.

params.name: min_focal_length
params.description: Minimum focal length in mm. Must be positive.

params.name: max_focal_length
params.description: Maximum focal length in mm. Must be >= min_focal_length.

params.name: min_fstop
params.description: Minimum f-stop. Must be positive.

params.name: max_fstop
params.description: Maximum f-stop. Must be >= min_fstop.

params.name: diaphragm_blades
params.description: Number of diaphragm blades for bokeh shape (optional, default 8, valid 4-16)

commands.returns: { camera_actor_name: string, min_focal_length: number, max_focal_length: number, success: bool }

commands.name: add_chooser_column
commands.description: Add a column of column_type, its input left unbound, to a UChooserTable asset as one undo step, then compile and save the table; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. Each call adds a new column, even of a type the table already has, except Randomize: a table holds at most one, so an existing Randomize column is returned with already_existed=true and nothing changes. The column goes where the Chooser editor puts it: a filter column before the first output or Randomize column, so filters stay ahead of them; an output column at the end but before a trailing Randomize column; a Randomize column last. The columns after it move up one index; column_index is where the new column went. The new column gets one cell, its DefaultRowValue, per row already in the table, so columns and rows stay in step whichever is added first. Besides the types listed under column_type it accepts OutputFloat, OutputBool, OutputName, OutputEnum, ObjectClass, Name, MultiEnum and Randomize.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: column_type
params.description: Column struct to add: "FloatRange", "Bool", "Enum", "Object", or "OutputObject". Name and OutputName need UE 5.8.

params.name: column_name
params.description: Label echoed back in the reply only; it is not stored on the column.

commands.returns: { table_path: string, column_index: int, column_name: string, column_type: string, already_existed: bool, row_count?: int, saved?: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_chooser_row
commands.description: Add one implicit row to a UChooserTable. Grows every column's RowValues by one (using each column's DefaultRowValue where available) and grows ResultsStructs by one, as one undo step, then compiles and saves the table; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

commands.returns: { table_path: string, row_index: int, row_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_chooser_table
commands.description: Create (or load if it already exists) a UChooserTable asset under the given package path. A new table is compiled and saved. On an existing table only the result_type and output_object_class the call gives are applied, as one undo step, and the table is compiled and saved only when that changes it (saved false otherwise). success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. An unknown result_type, or an output_object_class that does not load as a UClass, is an error checked before the asset is created or loaded.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset short name (e.g. "MyChooser"); becomes the package short name.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Long package root (default "/Game/MCP"); full asset path = <package_path>/<name>.

params.name: result_type
params.description: EObjectChooserResultType: "Object" (default), "Class", or "NoPrimaryResult".

params.name: output_object_class
params.description: UClass path used as OutputObjectType (default UObject), loaded via LoadObject<UClass>; a path that does not load is an error.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, already_existed: bool, result_type: string, output_object_class: string|null, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: delete_chooser_table
commands.description: Destroy a UChooserTable asset at a /Game path (mirror of create_chooser_table). Typed-delete: it loads the asset and REFUSES to delete it if it is not a UChooserTable, so it cannot wipe the wrong asset the way the generic delete_asset can; that refusal, and a delete the engine does not carry out, make success false with deleted false. Idempotent on missing assets.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full /Game/.../Chooser asset path.

commands.returns: { table_path, deleted, already_existed, asset_class?, note? }

commands.name: evaluate_chooser_table
commands.description: Actually RUN a UChooserTable and get the SINGLE chosen result, or with all_results EVERY matching result (for a chooser meant to select a set) -- the way to test a chooser you just authored without opening the editor. Headless-safe: it is a pure runtime API, so it needs no PIE and no render. Pass context_object_path (any UObject in the editor world) to seed the evaluation context. A table with no columns, or one where no context property matches, falls through to the table's FallbackResult (reported as fallback_used); a table that matches nothing and has no fallback returns null (an empty results list with all_results). With all_results, null entries the engine interleaves in its array are skipped, so result_count is the count of REAL results, and result_object_path is the first of them.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: context_object_path
params.description: Optional UObject path used to seed the evaluation context.

params.name: object_class
params.description: Optional UClass path for the expected result type (default = /Script/CoreUObject.Object); results are filtered with IsA.

params.name: all_results
params.description: Optional bool, default false: true evaluates with EvaluateChooserMulti and returns every matching result in results.

commands.returns: { table_path, evaluated, result_object_path, result_object_class, fallback_used, column_count, result_count?: int, results?: [{ result_object_path, result_object_class }], note? }

commands.name: get_chooser_column_values
commands.description: Read ONE COLUMN ACROSS ALL ROWS of a UChooserTable, plus that column's DefaultRowValue -- the column-wise counterpart of get_chooser_row_values (one row across all columns), with the same typed cell shapes. The per-column default is EDITOR-ONLY: outside an editor build it comes back null with a note, while the row values themselves always resolve. column_index out of range is an honest error. Read-only: no compile, no save.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: column_index
params.description: 0-based column index to read.

commands.returns: { table_path, column_index, column_type, row_count, default: {<typed>}|null, row_values: [{<typed>}] }

commands.name: get_chooser_row_values
commands.description: Read ONE ROW ACROSS ALL COLUMNS of a UChooserTable, as typed cells -- the row-wise counterpart of get_chooser_column_values (one column across all rows) and finer-grained than get_chooser_table_info. Cell shapes by column type: FloatRange {min,max,b_no_min,b_no_max}; Bool {cell_value}; Enum {comparison,value}; Object {comparison,asset_path}; OutputObject {asset_path}. row_index out of range is an honest error. Read-only -- no compile, no save -- and it works headless, since row data is not editor-only. A cell of a row is written with set_chooser_cell.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: row_index
params.description: 0-based row index to read across all columns.

commands.returns: { table_path, row_index, row_count, cells: [{ column_index, column_type, <typed fields> }] }

commands.name: get_chooser_table_info
commands.description: Read the shape of one Chooser Table asset without changing it: its result type, output object class, columns (index and column struct type), row count, result count and context-data count. Use it first, to learn the column indices and row count that get_chooser_column_values (one column across all rows), get_chooser_row_values (one row across all columns), set_chooser_cell and remove_chooser_row take; to see which row a context would pick, use evaluate_chooser_table; to find tables, list_chooser_tables. row_count is the largest of the result count and every column's row array, so a half-built table still reports all its rows. A path that does not load a Chooser Table is an error and nothing is read.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of the Chooser Table, without the object suffix, e.g. "/Game/Animation/CHT_Locomotion", as list_chooser_tables returns it.

commands.returns: { table_path: string, result_type: "Object"|"Class"|"NoPrimaryResult", output_object_class: string (empty when none), column_count: int, columns: [{index, type}], row_count: int, results_count: int, context_data_count: int }

commands.name: list_chooser_tables
commands.description: Lists the Chooser Table assets under a content folder and all its sub-folders, found through the Asset Registry, each with its name, object path, class and row and column counts. Each match is loaded to count its rows and columns; nothing is changed or saved. A folder without Chooser Tables returns total 0, not an error, and only assets of exactly the UChooserTable class are listed. Use it to find the table_path the other chooser tools take; then get_chooser_table_info for one table's columns and result type, evaluate_chooser_table to run one, create_chooser_table to make a new one.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Optional content folder to scan, sub-folders included (default "/Game"; an empty string also means /Game), e.g. "/Game/Animation/Choosers"; plugin content lives under its mount point, such as "/MyPlugin".

commands.returns: { package_path, total, tables:[{ asset_name, asset_path, asset_class, row_count, column_count }] }

commands.name: remove_chooser_column
commands.description: Remove a column from a UChooserTable by index (inverse of add_chooser_column). The column's per-row cells go with it -- a column owns its own RowValues, so nothing needs re-syncing across the other columns and the row COUNT is unchanged (use remove_chooser_row for that). The removal is one undo step; the table is then compiled and saved, and success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. A table with no columns is left as it is (note, saved false). Omit column_index (or pass -1) to remove the LAST column, matching remove_chooser_row's default.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: column_index
params.description: Optional 0-based column index (default -1 = last column).

commands.returns: { table_path, removed_column_index, previous_column_count, new_column_count, column_type, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: remove_chooser_row
commands.description: Remove one implicit row from a UChooserTable (inverse of add_chooser_row). A chooser row is not a real object: this shrinks EVERY column's RowValues array by one -- at row_index if given, else the last row -- and shrinks ResultsStructs to match, as one undo step, then compiles and saves the table like add_chooser_row; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. A table with no rows is left as it is (note, saved false). Use remove_chooser_column to drop a column instead.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: row_index
params.description: Optional 0-based row index to remove (default: last row).

commands.returns: { table_path, removed_row_index, previous_row_count, new_row_count, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: set_chooser_cell
commands.description: Set the cell of one existing row in one column of a UChooserTable -- a filter cell (FloatRange range, Bool match, Enum or Name comparison and value, Object or ObjectClass match) or an output cell -- as one undo step, then compile and save the table. It takes the same typed fields as set_chooser_column_default, which sets the value rows added LATER inherit; this one edits a row already there (set_chooser_row_outcome sets a row's result object). The fields that apply depend on the column type; default_value carries the cell of a Bool (MatchFalse|MatchTrue|MatchAny), OutputFloat, OutputBool, OutputName or Randomize column. A row or column index out of range, a missing or ill-typed field, or a column type no tool writes is an error and nothing changes; a cell already holding the value changes nothing (already_existed true, saved false). The reply re-reads the cell in the shape get_chooser_row_values gives; a failed save makes success false with save_error.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: row_index
params.description: 0-based row whose cell to set (get_chooser_table_info gives the row count).

params.name: column_index
params.description: 0-based column of the cell.

params.name: min
params.description: FloatRange column: lower bound of the row's float range.

params.name: max
params.description: FloatRange column: upper bound of the row's float range.

params.name: b_no_min
params.description: FloatRange column: when true, the range has no lower bound.

params.name: b_no_max
params.description: FloatRange column: when true, the range has no upper bound.

params.name: default_value
params.description: The cell value of a Bool column ("MatchFalse", "MatchTrue" or "MatchAny"), OutputFloat (a number), OutputBool (a bool), OutputName (a name string) or Randomize column (a probability weight).

params.name: comparison
params.description: Enum and Name columns: "MatchEqual", "MatchNotEqual", "MatchAny" or "Modulus"; ObjectClass column: "Equal", "NotEqual", "SubClassOf" (default), "NotSubClassOf" or "Any". Case-insensitive.

params.name: value
params.description: Enum and OutputEnum columns: enum ordinal (clamped to 0-255); Name column: the name string to compare; MultiEnum column: the bitmask as an integer.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object/OutputObject column: long package path of the UObject the cell holds.

params.name: class_path
params.description: ObjectClass column: path of the UClass to match, used with comparison (default SubClassOf).

commands.returns: { table_path, row_index, column_index, column_type, <typed cell fields as get_chooser_row_values>, already_existed, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_chooser_column_default
commands.description: Set the DefaultRowValue of one UChooserTable column, the cell value rows appended by add_chooser_row inherit; set it before adding rows (a row already there: set_chooser_cell). The fields that apply depend on the column type (see the params); others are ignored. A change is one undo step and is compiled and saved, and success is false, with save_error, when the save fails; a value the column already holds changes nothing (already_existed true, saved false).

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable.

params.name: column_index
params.description: 0-based column index to update.

params.name: min
params.description: FloatRange column: default lower bound of the row's float range.

params.name: max
params.description: FloatRange column: default upper bound of the row's float range.

params.name: b_no_min
params.description: FloatRange column: when true, disables the lower bound (row matches any value <= max).

params.name: b_no_max
params.description: FloatRange column: when true, disables the upper bound (row matches any value >= min).

params.name: default_value
params.description: Bool column: "MatchFalse", "MatchTrue" or "MatchAny"; OutputFloat: a number; OutputBool: a bool; OutputName: a name string; Randomize: a probability weight. Ignored by other column types.

params.name: comparison
params.description: Enum and Name columns: "MatchEqual", "MatchNotEqual", "MatchAny" or "Modulus"; ObjectClass column: "Equal", "NotEqual", "SubClassOf" (default), "NotSubClassOf" or "Any". Case-insensitive.

params.name: value
params.description: Enum and OutputEnum columns: enum ordinal (clamped to 0-255); Name column: the name string to compare; MultiEnum column: the bitmask as an integer.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object/OutputObject column: long package path of the UObject bound as the default row value.

params.name: class_path
params.description: ObjectClass column: path of the UClass to match (e.g. "/Script/Engine.Pawn" or "/Game/BP_Enemy.BP_Enemy_C"), used with comparison (default SubClassOf).

commands.returns: { table_path, column_index, column_type, default_value?, asset_path?, comparison?, already_existed, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_chooser_row_outcome
commands.description: Sets the object a Chooser Table row outputs: writes an FAssetChooser holding asset_path into that row's cell of the table's FIRST OutputObject column, in one undo step, then compiles and saves the table; success is false, with save_error, when the save fails. Idempotent: a row already holding that asset is left as it is (already_existed true, saved false). Refused with nothing changed when the table has no OutputObject column (add one with add_chooser_column, column_type OutputObject), row_index is out of range, or the asset does not load. The row's filter cells and its primary result entry are not touched. For a cell of another column, or of a second OutputObject column, use set_chooser_cell; read the row back with get_chooser_row_values; add rows with add_chooser_row.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Long package path of an existing UChooserTable (e.g. "/Game/Choosers/CT_Locomotion"), as list_chooser_tables lists it.

params.name: row_index
params.description: 0-based row index, below the row count get_chooser_table_info reports (checked against the OutputObject column's rows).

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Long package path (e.g. "/Game/Anims/AS_Run") or object path of the asset the row outputs; it must load, or the call is refused.

commands.returns: { table_path: string, row_index: int, asset_path: string, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_collision_channel
commands.description: Register a custom project collision channel (claims the first free ECC_GameTraceChannelN slot). Idempotent on channel_name. Inverse: remove_collision_channel.

params.name: channel_name
params.description: Friendly name for the new channel, e.g. "Harvestable"

params.name: default_response
params.description: "Block" | "Ignore" | "Overlap". Defaults to "Block".

params.name: trace_type
params.description: True for a trace channel, false for an object channel. Defaults to false.

params.name: static_object
params.description: Whether this channel represents a static object type. Defaults to false.

commands.returns: { channel_name: string, channel: string, default_response: string, trace_type: bool, static_object: bool, already_existed: bool, note: string }

commands.name: add_collision_profile
commands.description: Create a project collision profile, or replace an existing one of that name in full (omitted fields reset, custom responses cleared, can_modify not checked), then write Config/DefaultEngine.ini via TryUpdateDefaultConfigFile, unverified. Returns custom_response_count and already_existed; read it back with get_collision_profile; inverse: remove_collision_profile.

params.name: profile_name
params.description: Name of the collision profile to create or replace, e.g. "MyPawnProfile"

params.name: object_type_name
params.description: Channel this profile's object type resolves to, e.g. "WorldDynamic" or a custom channel's friendly name

params.name: collision_enabled
params.description: "NoCollision" | "QueryOnly" | "PhysicsOnly" | "QueryAndPhysics" | "ProbeOnly" | "QueryAndProbe". Defaults to "QueryAndPhysics".

params.name: custom_responses
params.description: [{channel: string, response: "Block"|"Ignore"|"Overlap"}, ...] per-channel overrides

params.name: can_modify
params.description: Whether this profile is user-editable in the editor UI. Defaults to true.

params.name: help_message
params.description: Editor tooltip text.

commands.returns: { profile_name: string, object_type_name: string, collision_enabled: string, custom_response_count: int, already_existed: bool }

commands.name: diff_project_config
commands.description: Diff THIS project's Config/Default*.ini against ANOTHER project's, aligned by section+key (pure file read via FConfigFile::Read; no world, no editor state). Surfaces settings that differ or failed to migrate: custom collision channels (GameTraceChannel/ObjectChannel under [/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile]), input mappings, enabled plugins ([Plugins]/[/Script/...]), and every other key. Perspective is THIS -> OTHER: 'added' = present in OTHER but not THIS; 'removed' = present in THIS but not OTHER; 'changed' = present in both with different value(s). Multi-value keys (array-of-struct like +Channels/+ActionMappings) are compared as sorted value lists so hash-ordering never yields a false diff.

params.name: other_project_dir
params.description: Filesystem path to the OTHER project. Either the project ROOT (its 'Config' subfolder is used automatically) or a Config folder directly.

params.name: files
params.description: Optional array of ini base filenames to compare (e.g. ["DefaultEngine.ini","DefaultInput.ini"]). Default: the union of Default*.ini present in EITHER project's Config folder.

params.name: sections
params.description: Optional array of exact section names to restrict the diff to (e.g. ["/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile","/Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings"]). Default: all sections.

commands.returns: { this_project_dir: string, other_project_dir: string, this_config_dir: string, other_config_dir: string, files: [ { file: string, this_exists: bool, other_exists: bool, this_section_count: int, other_section_count: int, added: [{ section, key, values:[string] }], removed: [{ section, key, values:[string] }], changed: [{ section, key, this_values:[string], other_values:[string] }], added_count: int, removed_count: int, changed_count: int } ], total_added: int, total_removed: int, total_changed: int, identical: bool }

commands.name: get_collision_profile
commands.description: Read one project collision profile by name, read-only: object_type_name, collision_enabled, can_modify, help_message and custom_responses [{channel, response}], which lists only the per-channel overrides. An unknown name is an error; add_collision_profile is the writer.

params.name: profile_name
params.description: Name of an existing collision profile, e.g. "BlockAll" or "Pawn"

commands.returns: { profile_name: string, object_type_name: string, collision_enabled: string, can_modify: bool, help_message: string, custom_responses: [{channel: string, response: string}] }

commands.name: get_component_properties
