commands.description: Builds a documentation record of one asset from the Asset Registry, without loading it: name, class, package and object path, .uasset size and timestamp, a coarse category and usage line chosen by exact class (StaticMesh, Material, Texture2D, Blueprint; every other class, sound waves and material instances included, is Other), and its direct package dependencies and referencers, 100 of each at most with truncation flags. Read-only despite its name: nothing is loaded, written or saved, and the record comes back in the reply only. An asset the registry does not know, or no editor world, is an error. For complete edge lists use get_asset_dependencies and get_asset_referencers (get_asset_dependencies_recursive beyond depth 1); for every Blueprint at once, generate_blueprint_docs; for project-wide counts, create_project_overview.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Package path ("/Game/Props/SM_Chair") or object path ("/Game/Props/SM_Chair.SM_Chair") of the asset; a bare asset name is not resolved (find_assets_by_name turns a name into a path).

commands.returns: { asset_documentation: { asset_name, asset_path, asset_class, asset_type, package_name, object_path, file_name, file_size: int (bytes, 0 if file_exists=false), last_modified: string, file_exists: bool, asset_category, usage, dependencies: [string] (package names, depth-1, capped at 100), dependencies_truncated: bool, dependents: [string] (referencers, depth-1, capped at 100), dependents_truncated: bool }, generation_date: string, project_name: string }

commands.name: create_project_overview
commands.description: Summarize the project in one read that writes nothing, neither a file nor an asset: project name, engine version and platform; /Game asset counts per class from the Asset Registry; the Blueprint total split into normal Blueprints and macro libraries, read from the registry's BlueprintType tag without loading any Blueprint; the name, world_type, net mode, actor count, level count and actors per class of one world, the PIE world while a play session runs and the editor world otherwise; and the totals of materials (any UMaterialInterface), Texture2D and sound assets. Without an editor world it is an error. Project metadata alone: get_project_info; one asset: create_asset_documentation; every Blueprint in detail: generate_blueprint_docs; the actors themselves: get_actors_in_level.
commands.returns: { project_info: { project_name, engine_version, platform, generation_date, is_editor }, asset_types: [{ asset_type, count }], blueprint_info: { total_blueprints, normal_blueprints, macro_blueprints }, world_info: { world_name, world_type, net_mode, actor_count, level_count }, actor_types: [{ actor_type, count }], material_info: { total_materials }, texture_info: { total_textures }, audio_info: { total_audio_assets }, statistics: { total_assets, total_blueprints, total_materials, total_textures, total_audio_assets, total_actors } }

commands.name: generate_blueprint_docs
commands.description: Documents every Blueprint asset under /Game in one reply, subclasses included (Widget, Anim and other Blueprints): per Blueprint its name, package path, class, parent class, type, compile state, component templates, the names of its function and event graphs, and its own variables with their pin category. Read-only despite its name: it loads every Blueprint to read it, but writes and saves nothing, and the result comes back in the reply only, never as a file. On a big project it can take long and return a very large reply; plugin and engine content are not included, and an editor world is required. For one Blueprint use get_blueprint_info (get_blueprint_components for its real component tree) or export_blueprint_data; for one asset of any kind, create_asset_documentation; for project-wide counts without loading, create_project_overview.
commands.returns: { blueprint_documentation: [{ blueprint_name, blueprint_path, blueprint_class, parent_class, blueprint_type, compilation_status, components, functions: [string], variables: [{name, type}] }], total_blueprints: int, generation_date: string, project_name: string } -- blueprint_type is Normal, or MacroLibrary for every other kind (interfaces and function libraries included); compilation_status is UpToDate or NeedsCompilation (errors included); components are the Blueprint's ComponentTemplates, which do not include the components of its Components panel

commands.name: add_component_to_actor
commands.description: Attach a new component of any class to one actor already placed in the editor world, as an instance component in one undo step; the actor's Blueprint is not changed. Pick it for a single placed actor; add_component_to_blueprint changes the Blueprint so every instance gets it, and a typed add_*_component tool (add_spline_component, add_camera_component...) also sets that class's fields. Each call adds another component, so a retry makes a duplicate; with idempotent=true an existing component of that class is returned instead (already_existed true). The reply's object_path feeds set_properties and call_function; component_name, suffixed when the name is taken, feeds remove_component_from_actor, the inverse. An unknown actor or a class that is not an actor component is an error. It dirties the actor's package; save_level keeps it.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Internal object name (not the label) of the placed actor in the editor world, e.g. 'StaticMeshActor_3'.

params.name: component_type
params.description: Component class by name or path, with or without the U prefix or the Component suffix, e.g. 'StaticMeshComponent', 'Box' or '/Script/Engine.PointLightComponent'.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Name for the new component, e.g. 'TriggerBox'; a taken name gets a unique variant, reported back in component_name.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative location (for scene components)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation (for scene components)

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] relative scale (for scene components)

params.name: idempotent
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When true, if the actor already has a component of this class, return it instead of adding a duplicate (already_existed:true). Use for single-instance components.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, object_path: string, requested_component_name: string, component_type: string, already_existed: bool, success: bool }

commands.name: add_enum_entry
commands.description: Append one enumerator to a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum) and give it a display name.  Idempotent (an entry whose display/internal name already exists reports already_existed with added=false, leaving the enum unchanged -- the engine itself does NOT dedup). The new entry lands at the end, before the hidden _MAX sentinel.

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum).

params.name: entry_name
params.description: Display name for the new enumerator.

commands.returns: { enum_path: string, entry_name: string, added: bool, already_existed: bool, entry_count: int, entries: [string] }

commands.name: add_message_log_entry
commands.description: Add one message to a named editor Message Log listing (for example "PIE", "MapCheck" or a new name, created on demand) at Info, Warning or Error severity; an unrecognised severity becomes Info, and a missing log_name or message is an error. Entries stay in memory for the editor session and are never saved. Use it for diagnostics meant for Window > Message Log; print_to_output_log writes to the Output Log instead. message_count is the listing's message count after the add. Read entries back with get_message_log_entries, show the window with open_message_log, empty the listing with clear_message_log.

params.name: log_name
params.description: The message log listing name (e.g. "PIE", "MapCheck", or a custom name).

params.name: message
params.description: The message text to add.

params.name: severity
params.description: EMessageSeverity token: "Info" (default), "Warning", "Error".

commands.returns: { added: bool, log_name: string, message: string, severity: string, message_count: int }

commands.name: add_struct_member
commands.description: Add a field to a Blueprint (user-defined) struct: the way to grow a data shape -- a DataTable row struct, a save record, a component's payload -- without opening the struct editor. Honest on collisions: if the new name is invalid or already used it ROLLS BACK the auto-named member it had to create first and returns an error, instead of reporting success under the engine's MemberVar_N name and leaving orphans behind. Adding a field to a struct a DataTable already uses changes every row (new field at its default), so re-read the table afterwards. get_struct_members lists what is there; rename_struct_member and remove_struct_member are the edits.

params.name: struct_path
params.description: Full asset path of the struct (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyStruct).

params.name: member_name
params.description: New member name.

params.name: member_type
params.description: Type string resolved through the Blueprint pin-type resolver: scalars (bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte), plus struct/enum/class/object types addressed by name or asset path. An unresolvable string is an error, not a silent default.

commands.returns: { struct_path, member_name, member_type, member_count }

commands.name: align_actors
commands.description: Snap two or more editor-world actors onto a shared location, rotation and/or scale taken from a reference (the first, the last, their average, or a named actor). Use it to straighten a hand-placed row or make a set of props share an orientation, in one undoable step; execute_batch of set_actor_transform calls, with transaction=true, is the tool when each actor needs a DIFFERENT transform. WARNING: aligning "location" collapses them onto the same point -- for a row, align only rotation/scale and set positions yourself.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Array of at least 2 INTERNAL actor names (GetName) in the editor world; fewer is an error, and editor labels do not resolve.

params.name: align_type
params.description: "location" (default), "rotation", "scale" or "all" -- which transform components get copied from the reference.

params.name: reference
params.description: Where the target values come from: "first" (default), "last", "average" (the componentwise mean of all of them), or the internal name of one of the listed actors.

commands.returns: { aligned_count: int, align_type: string, reference: string, aligned_actors: [actor JSON] }

commands.name: backup_asset
commands.description: Duplicate an asset into a timestamped /Game/MCP_Backups/ folder.  Call this before destructive operations (delete, reparent, overwrite). Accepts a package path or a full object path.

params.name: path
params.description: Source asset path (package path like /Game/Foo/Foo or full object path .Foo)

commands.returns: { source: string, backup_path: string }

commands.name: begin_transaction
commands.description: Open one undoable transaction so a whole batch of edits collapses into a SINGLE undo entry: every Modify() between this and end_transaction joins it, and cancel_transaction rolls the lot back without leaving anything on the stack. Use it to make a multi-step edit atomically reversible; the returned transaction_index is what end_transaction / cancel_transaction need. already_open:true means one was already running -- transactions do not nest here.

params.name: description
params.description: Label shown in the editor's undo history (e.g. 'MCP: retag turrets'). Make it recognisable; it is what get_transaction_history and next_undo report.

params.name: primary_object_path
params.description: Optional object path recorded as the transaction's PrimaryObject, so the undo entry is attributable to one asset/actor.

commands.returns: { description: string, transaction_index: int, already_open: bool, undo_count: int }

commands.name: cancel_transaction
commands.description: Abort the transaction opened by begin_transaction: the edits made inside it are rolled back (rolled_back true) and NO entry is written to the undo stack (undo_count is unchanged). The escape hatch when a multi-step edit goes wrong halfway -- cleaner than committing with end_transaction and then calling undo, which leaves history behind. Only what the transaction recorded rolls back: a change the editor does not record for undo (one to a Play-in-Editor object, for instance) stays, and rolled_back is false when nothing was recorded.
commands.returns: { success: bool, transaction_index: int (the one that was cancelled), rolled_back: bool (whether recorded edits were reverted), undo_count: int (unchanged -- nothing was recorded), note?: string }

commands.name: capture_high_res_screenshot
commands.description: Capture a high-resolution (supersampled) screenshot and write it to a PNG SYNCHRONOUSLY. Prefers the Play-In-Editor game view when PIE is active (captured_pie=true); otherwise the active editor viewport. Drives FViewport::TakeHighResScreenShot() + FViewport::Draw(), which renders at resolution_multiplier x the viewport size and blocks (via ProcessScreenShots) until the file is on disk. The "HighResShot" exec path defers the write to the next render frame, which never runs headless, so it writes nothing. Requires a real RHI (errors honestly under -nullrhi) and a live viewport. Note: the supersampled path re-renders the scene, so the UMG/Slate HUD is NOT included; use capture_pie_screenshot for a HUD-inclusive PIE shot.

params.name: resolution_multiplier
params.description: Resolution multiplier (clamped 1..16, default 2).

params.name: filename
params.description: Optional output path; a bare name lands under <ProjectSaved>/Screenshots/, an absolute path is respected verbatim. ".png" is appended if missing. Defaults to a timestamped name.

commands.returns: { written: bool, file_path: string, resolution_multiplier: int, width: int, height: int, captured_pie: bool }

commands.name: capture_viewport
commands.description: Screenshot the active editor viewport to a PNG (forcing a fresh draw first), optionally resized and optionally returned inline as base64. Use it to SHOW a result -- proof that something looks right, an image to hand to a human. Do NOT use it to diagnose: an image costs far more context than a command and is read far less reliably than one, so for "is the actor there / did the value change / did it move" prefer get_actor_bounds, get_component_properties, raycast_scene or a property read, which answer exactly and cheaply. Captures the EDITOR viewport, not a PIE window; capture_high_res_screenshot is the higher-resolution sibling.

params.name: width
params.description: Optional target width to downscale/upscale to (omit to keep native viewport size).

params.name: height
params.description: Optional target height (only used when width is also supplied).

params.name: filename
params.description: Optional output filename (default MCP_Capture_<timestamp>.png); ".png" extension is added if missing.

params.name: return_base64
params.description: bool, also include image_base64 + image_format in the response (default false).

commands.returns: { file_path: string, width: int, height: int, byte_size: int, image_base64: string, image_format: string }

commands.name: clear_message_log
commands.description: Clear all messages from a named engine Message Log listing.

params.name: log_name
params.description: The message log listing name (e.g. "PIE", "MapCheck", or a custom name).

commands.returns: { cleared: bool, log_name: string, cleared_count: int, messages_after: int }

commands.name: consolidate_assets
commands.description: Redirect every reference to the source assets onto the target with UEditorAssetSubsystem::ConsolidateAssets, which DELETES the sources (leaving redirectors) and saves what it changed. Only class-compatible sources are used; others are listed in skipped_incompatible and unloadable ones are dropped silently. dry_run=true only reports.

params.name: target_asset_path
params.description: The asset to keep, all references point here

params.name: source_asset_paths
params.description: Assets to consolidate into the target

params.name: dry_run
params.description: If true, skip ConsolidateAssets entirely and only report what would happen, default false

commands.returns: dry_run=true: { target_asset_path, target_class, dry_run: true, would_consolidate: [string], skipped_incompatible: [{path,class}], compatible_count: int, incompatible_count: int }; dry_run=false (default): { target_asset_path, target_class, dry_run: false, consolidated_count: int, source_count: int, success: bool, skipped_incompatible: [{path,class}], incompatible_count: int }

commands.name: copy_actors
commands.description: Put editor-world actors on the editor CLIPBOARD (edactCopySelected), either by name or whatever is currently selected, so paste_actors can drop them back -- the way to clone a group while keeping their relative layout, which duplicate_actor (one actor, in place) does not do. WARNING: naming them REPLACES the current selection as a side effect, and matching is by INTERNAL name only. One of actor_names or copy_selected=true is required.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Optional array of internal actor names (GetName) to copy; supplying it re-selects exactly those actors first.

params.name: copy_selected
params.description: Optional bool. True (with actor_names omitted) copies whatever is selected right now, leaving the selection alone.

commands.returns: { copied_count: int, success: bool (hardcoded; verify with paste_actors' pasted_count) }

commands.name: create_blueprint_interface
commands.description: Create an empty Blueprint Interface asset at path/name (a contract of function signatures that unrelated Blueprints implement, so a caller sends the message without knowing the concrete class) and mark its package dirty without saving it; there is no undo step. Use it when several kinds of actor must answer the same request (interact, take damage, work) without sharing a base class; when they can share one, use create_blueprint with a common parent instead. An asset already at that path, or an invalid name, is an error and nothing changes, so a repeat call fails. Refused while Play-in-Editor runs unless force=true. Next: add each signature with add_blueprint_function, add the interface to each class with implement_interface, implement each function there with add_blueprint_function (override=true), and save with save_asset.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without folder, e.g. "BPI_Interactable"; must be a valid asset name not already used in that folder.

params.name: path
params.description: Content folder for the new asset, e.g. "/Game/Blueprints/Interfaces" (default /Game/Blueprints); a trailing slash is ignored.

commands.returns: { name, path, type }

commands.name: create_directory
commands.description: Make a content-browser folder at a UE long path (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Systems/Foo). Idempotent: an existing folder is not an error, it comes back already_existed:true. Use it to lay out a system's folders before creating assets there; a path that does not start with '/' is rejected.

params.name: path
params.description: UE long path of the folder to create, e.g. /Game/MyGame/Systems/Foo. Must start with '/', not a disk path.

commands.returns: { path: string, already_existed: bool (true = nothing was created, and that is a success) }

commands.name: create_enum
commands.description: Create a Blueprint enum asset from an ordered list of enumerator DISPLAY names -- states, categories and types that Blueprints and DataTable columns switch on. Errors if the asset already exists (not idempotent). Beware the display/internal split that follows: the engine stores enumerators internally as NewEnumerator0, NewEnumerator1, ... and writers into DataTables must use those internal names, because a display name containing spaces is cut at the first space by the text importer and silently lands on index 0. So keep single-word display names, or expect to write NewEnumeratorN. add_enum_entry / rename_enum_entry / reorder_enum_entry edit it afterwards.

params.name: name
params.description: Enum asset name.

params.name: entries
params.description: Ordered list of enumerator display-name strings.

params.name: path
params.description: Target content path for the new asset (default /Game/Blueprints)

commands.returns: { name, path, entry_count }

commands.name: create_file_media_source
commands.description: Create a UFileMediaSource asset at package_path/name that points at a movie file path, register it and save it; the file does not need to exist. An existing asset is returned unchanged (file_path is not applied). Returns asset_path, the stored file_path, created and saved.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the file media source asset to create.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Movie file on disk, absolute or "./"-relative to the project Content folder, e.g. "./Movies/Intro.mp4"; a path inside Content is stored in that relative form.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Media)

commands.returns: { media_source_name, asset_path, created, already_exists, file_path, saved, save_error }

commands.name: create_functional_test
commands.description: Create a Blueprint subclass of AFunctionalTest (an actor placed in a test map that runs scripted checks and reports pass or fail to the automation framework) at package_path/asset_name, then save it; there is no undo step. Use it to author a level-based gameplay test; for an ordinary actor Blueprint use create_blueprint, and to run registered tests use run_automation_test (list them with list_automation_tests). Idempotent: when a Blueprint already exists at that path it is returned as it is, with already_existed true, and saved again; its parent is not checked and parent_class echoes the requested one. A parent that is not found or is not a Functional Test, or an asset of another type at the path, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false, with saved false and the Blueprint only in memory. Refused while Play-in-Editor runs unless force=true. Then script it with add_blueprint_function and add_graph_node, and place it in a map with spawn_actor.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Asset name of the new Blueprint without folder, e.g. "BP_FT_PlayerHealth".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/Tests" (default /Game/MCP).

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Optional parent: a class deriving from AFunctionalTest, by name without prefix (e.g. "FunctionalTest", the default) or by /Script/ path; a Blueprint parent must be loaded and named by its generated class (e.g. "BP_FT_Base_C").

commands.returns: { asset_name, asset_path, package_class, parent_class, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_media_player
commands.description: Create a UMediaPlayer asset at package_path/name with PlayOnOpen and looping set, optionally with a linked UMediaTexture named "<name>_T" beside it, and save both. An existing player is returned unchanged (flags not applied). Returns asset_path, play_on_open, loop, media_texture_path, saved and texture_saved.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the media player asset to create.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Media)

params.name: create_output_texture
params.description: Also create a UMediaTexture "<name>_T" next to the player and link it (default true).

params.name: play_on_open
params.description: Set the player's PlayOnOpen flag (default true)

params.name: loop
params.description: Set the player to loop via SetLooping (default false)

commands.returns: { media_player_name, asset_path, created, already_exists, play_on_open, loop, texture_created, media_texture_path, saved, texture_saved, save_error, texture_save_error }

commands.name: create_media_texture
commands.description: Create a UMediaTexture asset at package_path/name (AutoClear on, no player linked) and save it; an existing texture is returned unchanged, with its linked player if any. Link a player with link_media_texture_to_player. Returns asset_path, created, has_media_player and saved.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the media texture asset to create.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Media)

commands.returns: { media_texture_name, asset_path, created, already_exists, has_media_player, media_player_path, saved, save_error }

commands.name: create_struct
commands.description: Create a Blueprint Struct (UUserDefinedStruct). Idempotent by reset+rebuild: a stale struct already at the path is deleted and recreated fresh (reset_stale:true); a same-path asset of a different type is an honest error.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (no path)

params.name: path
params.description: Target content path for the new asset (default /Game/Blueprints)

commands.returns: { name, path, reset_stale }

commands.name: delete_actor
commands.description: Remove one actor from the EDITOR level through the editor's own delete path (select + edactDeleteSelected), so it is transacted and undoable, and echo back the deleted actor's JSON. WARNING: two edges that bite: it matches the INTERNAL name only -- unlike set_actor_transform, an editor LABEL will not resolve -- and it clears the current selection as a side effect. It cannot touch PIE actors (editor world only), and the deletion lives in memory until save_level writes the .umap. Use delete_actors for several at once.

params.name: name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName), case-insensitive but WHOLE-string. Editor labels are NOT accepted here; resolve one first with find_actors_by_name.

commands.returns: { deleted_actor: actor JSON captured before the delete }

commands.name: delete_actors
commands.description: Delete several editor-world actors at once through the editor's own delete path, in ONE undoable transaction (a single undo brings them all back), returning the count and the JSON of each actor captured before deletion. WARNING: matches INTERNAL names only -- editor labels do not resolve -- names it cannot find are skipped silently, so compare deleted_count against how many you asked for; and if NONE resolve it errors with "No actors found to delete". Editor world only, and the removal is in memory until save_level writes the .umap.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Array of internal actor names (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Unmatched entries are dropped without an error; resolve labels first with find_actors_by_name.

commands.returns: { deleted_count: int (compare against your input length), deleted_actors: [actor JSON captured before the delete] }

commands.name: delete_assets
commands.description: GUARDED batch asset deletion. ***dry_run DEFAULTS TO TRUE*** (deliberate: it is the most destructive command in the plugin, `delete_assets(["/Game/VendorPack"], recursive=true)` would be a valid unconfirmed call, and agent allowlists may run mutating tools with no prompt). Four independent gates REFUSE per item instead of skipping silently: readonly_roots (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots), protect_paths (wildcards -- the only gate that saves a zero-referencer asset), the currently-open editor world, and the OPT-IN require_zero_referencers gate whose referencer count EXCLUDES referencers that are themselves in this batch (so a self-contained dead subgraph can still be deleted whole). Deletion is a single ObjectTools::ForceDeleteObjects over the whole eligible batch -- resolving each object here via StaticFindObject/StaticLoadObject rather than through UEditorAssetSubsystem::DeleteAsset, whose UE::EditorAssetUtils::LoadAssetFromPath/EnsureAssetsLoaded preamble is a known crash site ("Array index out of bounds", deterministic on corrupted leftovers). deleted_count counts ONLY items that passed BOTH post-delete probes -- the package file is gone (FPackageName::DoesPackageExist) AND the object no longer resolves at its original path (StaticFindObject) -- never the API's own return value. Both are required because for a never-saved, registry-visible asset the disk probe is vacuously true (it was never on disk), so residency is the only real evidence; each failure names which probe still sees the item.

params.name: asset_paths
params.description: List of asset paths (or folder paths when recursive is true). Required, non-empty.

params.name: recursive
params.description: If true, expand folder paths to all contained assets. Default false.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Default TRUE. Nothing is deleted; would_delete reports what WOULD go, with each item's gate verdict. Pass false to actually delete.

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Content roots that may never be deleted from. Default: the project's Read Only Content Roots; pass [] to disable the gate entirely. Matches are REFUSED (refused_readonly_root), never silently skipped. (Read via mcp_common::ParseReadonlyRoots, so the type is declared here.)

params.name: protect_paths
params.description: Wildcard patterns (FString::MatchesWildcard, case-insensitive, `*` spans '/') matched against both the package name and the object path. Default [] (gate off). Matches are REFUSED (refused_protected).

params.name: require_zero_referencers
params.description: Default FALSE. When true, an asset with at least one referencer OUTSIDE this batch is refused. The per-item external_referencer_count is reported either way.

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Referencer filter for the count above: "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive), default "all".

commands.returns: { requested_count, expanded_count, recursive, dry_run, readonly_roots: [string], protect_paths: [string], require_zero_referencers: bool, dependency_type: string, expanded_folders: [{folder, asset_count}], eligible_count, would_delete: [{path, package_name, external_referencer_count, external_referencers: [string], on_disk}], deleted: [{path, package_name, deleted, still_loaded, error?}], deleted_count, failed_count, force_delete_reported_count, refused_readonly_root: [{path, matched_root}], refused_protected: [{path, matched_pattern}], refused_referenced: [{path, external_referencer_count, external_referencers: [string]}], refused_open_world: [{path, reason}], refused_count, results: [{path, success, error}], note, verification: {...} }

commands.name: delete_directory
commands.description: DESTRUCTIVE: removes a content-browser folder AND every asset inside it, recursively, with no dry-run and no referencer check (unlike delete_assets, which defaults to dry_run and refuses vendored roots). Driven through UEditorAssetSubsystem, which is the pair that works headless. Idempotent: an already-absent folder answers already_absent:true. Verify afterwards with `git status` on the corresponding Content/ path -- never with the `deleted` flag alone.

params.name: path
params.description: UE long path of the folder to delete, e.g. /Game/Scratch. Must start with '/'. Everything under it goes.

commands.returns: { path: string, already_absent: bool, deleted: bool }

commands.name: deselect_actors
commands.description: Drop specific actors from the editor selection, or clear it entirely with deselect_all. The counterpart of select_actors; use the clear-all form to leave the editor in a known state before a tool that acts on the selection (copy_actors, move_actors_to_level) so it does not pick up leftovers. Editor world only; matches INTERNAL names.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Optional array of internal actor names (GetName) to remove from the selection. One of actor_names or deselect_all=true is required.

params.name: deselect_all
params.description: Optional bool. True clears the whole selection; it wins over actor_names when both are sent.

commands.returns: { deselected_all: bool, deselected_count: int }

commands.name: duplicate_actor
commands.description: Copy one editor-world actor in place through the editor's duplicate path, keeping its component overrides, and return both the new actor's JSON and the original's. Undoable; it changes the editor SELECTION as a side effect. Matches the INTERNAL name only (no editor labels). The clone exists in memory until save_level writes the .umap -- and a save that answers success while `git status` stays clean means the .umap is read-only (e.g. a Git LFS `lockable` file you have not locked), not that the duplicate failed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Editor labels are NOT accepted; resolve one with find_actors_by_name first.

commands.returns: { duplicated_actor: actor JSON (its auto-assigned name lives here), original_actor: actor JSON }

commands.name: end_transaction
commands.description: Close the transaction opened by begin_transaction and COMMIT it, so everything done inside becomes one entry on the editor's undo stack (undo_count grows by one). Pair it with every begin_transaction -- leaving one open makes later edits silently join it. Use cancel_transaction instead when you want the batch thrown away rather than kept. A transaction that holds objects of the running Play-in-Editor session (a widget made with create_widget) is closed without an undo entry, recorded false: the edits stay, and keeping it would close the editor when PIE stops.
commands.returns: { success: bool, transaction_index: int (the one that was closed), recorded: bool (false: no undo entry, see note), undo_count: int after the commit, note?: string }

commands.name: execute_console_command
commands.description: Run a console command through the EDITOR (GEditor->Exec against the editor world): cvars, `stat` overlays, `r.*` toggles, engine commands. WARNING: it does NOT reach a running PIE session's PlayerController, so player cheats like `BugItGo` come back handled:false -- to move or cheat a PIE pawn use execute_python against the anchored PIE world. `handled` is the engine's own "some Exec claimed this string", not proof of an effect: verify with the state (get_cvar, a property read), never with this bool.

params.name: command
params.description: Console command line, e.g. 'stat fps', 'r.ScreenPercentage 50', 'ShowFlag.Grid 0'. Editor-side only.

commands.returns: { command: string, handled: bool (an Exec handler claimed the string -- not evidence the effect happened) }

commands.name: execute_python
commands.description: Execute Python code inside the running Unreal Editor. DO NOT GUESS A FIELD NAME: most of this tool's errors are "object has no attribute" -- and the field usually EXISTS, just not where you reached for it: `HitResult().impact_point` raises, `get_editor_property` cannot find it, and only `to_dict()` returns it (Transform.translation is the reverse). The engine's own stub and Epic's web docs list it either way, so neither settles it -- ask the object (dir(x), x.to_dict(), x.get_editor_property(...)). PIE TRAP -- this tool is the ONE HOLE in the plugin's PIE guard: the commands that compile a Blueprint or write to disk are REFUSED while Play-in-Editor is live (McpPieSafety.gen.h), but arbitrary Python cannot be classified statically, so a script that reaches compile/save through unreal.* (BlueprintEditorLibrary.compile_blueprint, EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset, save_loaded_asset, anything that dirties a Blueprint) RUNS ANYWAY. With PIE live that ends either in a DEAD EDITOR -- the compiler's UREINST_* trampoline retains a world and CheckForWorldGCLeaks is Fatal, taking every unsaved edit with it -- or in a save that reports success without writing a byte (Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0). So: call is_play_in_editor_active FIRST whenever your script compiles, saves, or mutates a Blueprint, and stop PIE before running it. READING the live world during PIE is safe and is exactly what this tool is for -- do not avoid it for that. BEFORE writing a loop, check what already answers it in ONE call: scripts that re-implement something a tool already does fail far more often than scripts doing something genuinely new -- hand-rolled scaffolding is where the errors are, and a bug in the scaffold reads exactly like a finding about the game. enumerate actors of a class -> get_actors_by_class. enumerate them AND read their properties, filtered by class or editor label, drilling into one component, with the answering world STAMPED on the result (this tool cannot tell you which world answered) -> get_actor_properties_by_class. read properties off ONE known object -> get_properties. list an actor's components -> get_actor_components. one line trace -> raycast_scene. sample a property across a whole PIE session ARMED BEFORE BeginPlay -- a window a post-tick callback cannot reach at all -> watch_pie_property. But do NOT read this as "always prefer the specific tool": only a minority of scripts are replaceable end-to-end. Python remains the right answer when the script does what those cannot: several classes in one round trip, walking components AND calling a method, filtering by name substring, correlating two values in the same tick, or anything that mutates. Do not trade one call for twelve. WARNING: `log_output` IS NOT THE LOG OF THE CALL -- it is Python's own prints only (UE fills it from a delegate broadcast solely by unreal.log/log_warning/log_error), so every UE_LOG the ENGINE emits during your script is absent from it. Read `engine_log` instead: it is the GLog slice bracketed to this call, Warning+Error by default. Example: build_meta_human can run, return None, write zero assets and report a clean `log_output` while "LogMetaHumanCoreTechLib: Error: Texture Synthesis has not been initialized" sits in GLog. When a call reports success and NOTHING HAPPENED, `engine_log` is the first place to look; widen with engine_log_level=Log, or pass `log_cursor_before` to get_output_log_lines(since_sequence_id=...) for the unfiltered rest.

params.name: command
params.description: Python code to run (single or multi-line).

params.name: capture_output
params.description: Run as a file and collect captured log (default true)

params.name: mode
params.description: Execution mode: ExecuteFile, ExecuteStatement, or EvaluateStatement (default ExecuteFile)

params.name: engine_log_level
params.description: Minimum severity of ENGINE log to return in `engine_log`: Error, Warning (default), Display, Log/All.

params.name: engine_log_max
params.description: Max lines in `engine_log` (default 50, 0 disables, hard cap 4096).

commands.returns: { command, python_success, execution_mode, command_result, output, log_output, log_line_count, engine_log, engine_log_count, engine_log_truncated, log_cursor_before }

commands.name: execute_python_file
commands.description: Execute a Python (.py) file inside the running Unreal Editor. PIE TRAP: same hole as execute_python -- arbitrary Python is NOT covered by the plugin's PIE guard, so a script that compiles a Blueprint or saves an asset runs even with Play-in-Editor live, where compiling can KILL the editor (UREINST_* retains a world, CheckForWorldGCLeaks is Fatal) and saving reports success without writing (Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0). Check is_play_in_editor_active first when the file compiles, saves or mutates a Blueprint; reading the live world during PIE is safe. WARNING: `log_output` IS NOT THE LOG OF THE CALL -- it is Python's own prints only (UE fills it from a delegate broadcast solely by unreal.log/log_warning/log_error), so every UE_LOG the ENGINE emits during your script is absent from it. Read `engine_log` instead: it is the GLog slice bracketed to this call, Warning+Error by default. Example: build_meta_human can run, return None, write zero assets and report a clean `log_output` while "LogMetaHumanCoreTechLib: Error: Texture Synthesis has not been initialized" sits in GLog. When a call reports success and NOTHING HAPPENED, `engine_log` is the first place to look; widen with engine_log_level=Log, or pass `log_cursor_before` to get_output_log_lines(since_sequence_id=...) for the unfiltered rest.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute path to a .py file accessible from the editor host.

params.name: engine_log_level
params.description: Minimum severity of ENGINE log to return in `engine_log`: Error, Warning (default), Display, Log/All.

params.name: engine_log_max
params.description: Max lines in `engine_log` (default 50, 0 disables, hard cap 4096).

commands.returns: { file_path, python_success, command_result, output, log_output, log_line_count, engine_log, engine_log_count, engine_log_truncated, log_cursor_before }

commands.name: export_assets
commands.description: Export assets to files via IAssetTools::ExportAssets (preferred format, FBX/PNG/EXR first), each written to export_path/<package path without its leading slash>.<extension>, e.g. D:/Exports/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.FBX. What was written is measured per asset on disk: exported lists each asset with its file, and not_exported the ones that did not load, have no exporter or failed to write. Succeeds only when every requested asset was written.

params.name: asset_paths
params.description: Asset object or package paths to export (e.g. ["/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock"]); empty strings are ignored.

params.name: export_path
params.description: Destination directory on disk (e.g. "D:/Exports"), created if missing; each file lands in subfolders named after its package path.

commands.returns: { exported_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, export_path: string, exported: [{ asset_path: string, file: string }], not_exported: [string] }

commands.name: find_actors_by_name
commands.description: Locate actors by a SUBSTRING of their internal name and/or their editor label, returning name, label, class and transform for each hit. This is the one to use when you know what a thing is CALLED but not its class -- get_actors_by_class needs an exact class name, and this one alone can search labels (match='label'), which is where hand-assigned names live. Plain case-INSENSITIVE substring, no wildcards and no regex: 'turret' matches BP_Turret_C_2, and '*' matches literally nothing. Its world selector is the canonical one: 'editor' (default), 'pie'/'game', 'server', 'client' and 'pie:N' all resolve for real, an unrecognised value FAILS instead of falling through to the editor world, and the reply stamps world_package/world_type/net_mode/pie_instance so you can tell which world answered.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Substring to look for, case-insensitive, no wildcards or regex. Cannot be empty.

params.name: match
params.description: Optional 'name' | 'label' | 'both' (default 'both'). 'name' = internal object name only; 'label' = the editor label from the outliner; 'both' = a hit on either. An unknown value is a clean error.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional cap on hits (default 1000); results_truncated says whether the scan stopped early.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'game' (alias of 'pie') | 'server' (the PIE world with authority, GetNetMode() != NM_Client) | 'client' | 'pie:N' (the PIE context whose PIEInstance is N). Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world.

commands.returns: { matching_actors: [ { name, actor_name, label, class, location, rotation, scale, is_loaded } ], matching_actors_count: int, search_pattern: string, match: string, results_truncated: bool, max_results: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (in World Partition the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: find_duplicate_assets
commands.description: Find groups of assets that share the same asset name under a content folder tree (e.g. the same name under both a vendored library tree and a first-party fork), from Asset Registry metadata only: nothing is loaded and contents are not compared, so a group means same name, not same data. Groups come most-duplicated first, each with name, count, classes and every asset's path, package and class. Use it to triage name clashes before cleanup: get_asset_referencers shows who uses each copy, audit_fork_refs checks references between a library and its fork, consolidate_assets merges copies and find_unused_assets finds unreferenced ones. Read-only and idempotent. group_count counts the groups returned, results_truncated says when max_results cut some, total_duplicate_assets counts the extra copies (count - 1 per group) and assets_scanned the assets left after class_filter. No duplicates gives group_count 0, not an error.

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to scan, a package path such as /Game/Characters, default /Game

params.name: recursive
params.description: If true, scan subfolders, default true

params.name: min_group_size
params.description: Minimum number of same-named assets to report as a duplicate group, default 2 (a value below 1 counts as 2)

params.name: class_filter
params.description: Optional list of class short names (e.g. "StaticMesh","Material"); only assets whose AssetClassPath short name case-insensitively matches one of these are considered

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on the number of duplicate GROUPS returned (not raw assets), clamped 1..20000, default 2000

commands.returns: { folder_path, recursive, class_filter, min_group_size, group_count, total_duplicate_assets, assets_scanned, max_results, results_truncated, groups: [{ name, count, classes: [string], assets: [{path, package, class}] }] } (groups sorted by count descending)

commands.name: find_unused_assets
commands.description: Find assets in a folder with zero referencers, and annotate each survivor with the reasons it should be KEPT anyway. "Zero referencers" is not the same as "safe to delete": there are three common ways an asset stays alive with an empty referencer set -- it is explicitly protected, a Config/Default*.ini names it, or it is a fork descending from a vendored base library. Each becomes a keep_reason string on the entry; deletion_candidates lists only the entries with NO keep_reason. Nothing is ever removed from unused_assets by these flags (hiding a genuinely unreferenced asset would be the same lie in the other direction). NOTE: there is deliberately no `is_world` -- it is already visible in class_name ("World").

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Content folder to scan, e.g. /Game/Unused

params.name: recursive
params.description: If true, scan subfolders, default true

params.name: exclude_classes
params.description: Optional list of class name fragments to skip

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Referencer filter: "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive), default "all" (identical behavior to omitting it)

params.name: protect_paths
params.description: Wildcard patterns (FString::MatchesWildcard, case-insensitive, `*` spans '/') matched against the package name and the object path. Default [] . A match adds keep_reason "protected_path".

params.name: include_lineage_reasons
params.description: Default FALSE because it LOADS every candidate Blueprint. When true, a Blueprint whose super chain reaches a class owned by one of base_libraries gets keep_reason "descends_from_base_library" -- the only signal that saves a fork carrying no fork-origin tag (project setting Fork Origin Tag).

params.name: base_libraries
params.description: Vendored-library content roots for the lineage check. Default: the project's Read Only Content Roots (same default as audit_class_purity).

commands.returns: { folder_path, folder_exists, recursive, dependency_type, protect_paths: [string], include_lineage_reasons, base_libraries: [string], unused_assets: [{path, class_name, size_kb, keep_reasons: [string], keep_reason_detail: {...}}], unused_count, total_scanned, deletion_candidates: [string], deletion_candidate_count, assets_with_keep_reason, keep_reason_counts: {protected_path, referenced_by_config, descends_from_base_library}, config_scan: {files_scanned: int, files: [string]}, lineage_scan: {attempted, blueprints_loaded, skipped_non_blueprint, load_failures} }

commands.name: fixup_redirectors
commands.description: Clean up the redirectors a rename/move left behind, under a folder: load each referencing package (which repoints it) and re-save it, optionally force-deleting redirectors whose referencers all saved. Hand-rolled on purpose -- IAssetTools::FixupReferencers HARD-CRASHES on World-Partition/OFPA projects -- and heavily railed: it REFUSES while PIE is active, never writes under readonly_roots (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots), never outside /Game, and never loads or saves map or OFPA packages, handing the resident ones back in skipped_current_world for you to save_level instead. Deletions are DISK-verified (a redirector whose .uasset survives lands in redirectors_delete_failed, not in the count). WARNING: redirectors_found/deleted count OBJECTS: one renamed Blueprint leaves THREE in a single package -- read redirector_packages_found for files.

params.name: path
params.description: Long path to scan, defaults to /Game

params.name: delete_redirectors
params.description: Optional bool (default false). After a successful repoint, force-delete the redirectors whose every non-redirector referencer was saved. Left in place by default (a redirector is ~2 KB and harmless).

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of long-path prefixes that must NEVER be written (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots, i.e. the vendored library roots). Referencers under them are reported in skipped_readonly instead of being saved.

commands.returns: { path: string, redirectors_found: int, redirector_packages_found: int, referencers_repointed: int, packages_saved: int, packages_failed: [{ package: string, error: string }], skipped_readonly: [string], skipped_current_world: [string], redirectors_deleted: int, redirector_packages_deleted: int, redirectors_delete_failed: [{ package: string, reason: string }], redirectors_fixed: int, message: string }

commands.name: get_actors_in_level
commands.description: Dump EVERY actor of a world (name, class, transform), capped by max_results at 5000, with total_actors_in_level and results_truncated so you know if you saw all of it. The unfiltered census: reach for get_actors_by_class when you know the class, find_actors_by_name for a name/label substring, get_actors_in_radius for a place. Its world selector is the canonical one: 'editor' (default), 'pie'/'game', 'server', 'client' and 'pie:N' all resolve for real, an unrecognised value FAILS naming the worlds that exist instead of quietly answering from the editor world, and every reply carries world_package/world_type/net_mode/pie_instance so you can see WHICH world answered rather than assuming.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional cap on returned actors (default 5000). Must be > 0. Truncation is reported, never silent.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'game' (alias of 'pie') | 'server' (the PIE world with authority, GetNetMode() != NM_Client) | 'client' | 'pie:N' (the PIE context whose PIEInstance is N). Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world.

commands.returns: { actors: [actor JSON], actors_count: int, total_actors_in_level: int, results_truncated: bool, max_results: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (in World Partition the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: get_automation_test_results
commands.description: Returns the cached result of the last synchronous test completed through run_automation_test, without running anything: test_name, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings and entries. Skipped or multi-tick tests leave the cache unchanged; fails when no test has completed this editor session.
commands.returns: { test_name, started, completed, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings, entries:[{type,message,context,filename,line}], entry_count }

commands.name: get_current_level
commands.description: Which map a world is sitting on: level_name, its package_name (/Game/... or /Engine/...), the resolved disk filename, whether the package is dirty, and a live actor count. package_name is the discriminator that catches the classic mistake -- if it starts with /Engine/ you are on an engine template (what load_level with default_template=true leaves behind) and a save_level without `filename` would overwrite the ENGINE's own map. Defaults to the EDITOR world; it also takes the standard `world` selector, so during PIE you can ask the play world ('pie'/'server'/'client'/'pie:N') instead of being told about the authoring map and having no way to know it.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default -- the authoring map even while PIE runs) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'game' (alias of 'pie') | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N'. Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world.

commands.returns: { level_name: string, package_name: string (the /Game or /Engine path -- read this one), filename: string, is_dirty: bool, actor_count: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string ("Editor" | "PIE" | ...), net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: get_cvar
commands.description: Read the live value of one console variable of the running editor through IConsoleManager, without changing it: the value as a string and parsed as int, float and bool, its help text, its raw flags and set_by (which layer last set it, such as Constructor, Scalability, ProjectSetting or Console). Use it to read one variable by exact name; to find names by substring or prefix use list_cvars; to change a value use set_cvar (or set_cvars_from_json for many); scalability groups as a whole: get_scalability_levels. A name that is not a registered console variable (including a console command, which has no value) is an error.

params.name: name
params.description: Exact console variable name, e.g. "r.ScreenPercentage" or "t.MaxFPS", as list_cvars returns it (case-insensitive).

commands.returns: { name: string, value: string, string_value: string, int_value: int, float_value: float, bool_value: bool, help: string, flags: int, set_by: string }

commands.name: get_engine_ini_value
commands.description: Read one key from the merged in-memory config (GConfig) of an INI such as Engine or Game. Read-only; returns value and found (false, with an empty value, when the section or key is missing). Pass config_file without .ini. Writer: set_engine_ini_value.

params.name: section
params.description: Section name (e.g. "/Script/Engine.RendererSettings")

params.name: key
params.description: Key inside the section, e.g. "r.DefaultFeature.AntiAliasing".

params.name: config_file
params.description: Config base name without extension, e.g. "Engine" (default), "Game", "Input", "Editor", "Scalability"; "Engine.ini" is not resolved.

commands.returns: { section, key, value, found }

commands.name: get_level_blueprint
commands.description: Get (or, with create=true, bring into being) the current level's Level Blueprint and return the blueprint_path that the graph tools need -- its event graph is always called "EventGraph", so add_graph_node / connect_pins can target it directly with graph_name="EventGraph". This is the entry point for level-specific scripting that does not belong in any actor. Read-only by default: with create=false and no blueprint present it answers exists:false + success:true rather than failing.

params.name: create
params.description: Optional bool (default false). True creates the Level Blueprint if the level has none -- a mutation that dirties the map, so save_level afterwards.

commands.returns: { exists: true, created: bool, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_name: string, event_graph: "EventGraph", level_name: string, success: true }, or, when no blueprint exists and create=false: { exists: false, success: true, level_name: string, note: string }

commands.name: get_media_info
commands.description: Read a media asset by path: class and media_type ("MediaPlayer", "MediaTexture", "FileMediaSource" or "Other"), plus play_on_open and loop for a player, the linked player and auto_clear for a texture, or file_path for a file source. Read-only.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Path of a UMediaPlayer, UMediaTexture or UFileMediaSource asset, e.g. "/Game/Media/MP_Intro"; any other asset reports only its name and class.

commands.returns: { asset_path, asset_name, class, media_type, play_on_open, loop, has_media_player, media_player_path, auto_clear, file_path }

commands.name: get_message_log_entries
commands.description: Read back the messages currently in a named engine Message Log listing (IMessageLogListing::GetFilteredMessages), each resolved back to the actor/component the engine attached to it. The reader that pairs with add_message_log_entry/clear_message_log.

params.name: log_name
params.description: The message log listing name (e.g. "PIE", "MapCheck", or a custom name). Required.

params.name: severity
params.description: Optional severity filter: "Error"|"PerformanceWarning"|"Warning"|"Info" (case-insensitive). Omit for all.

params.name: base_libraries
params.description: Package roots to classify each entry's class against (optional, default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). An explicit [] disables the classification. Reported as data in class_root/class_root_is_base_library; the tool never judges which root is "upstream".

commands.returns: { log_name: string, severity_filter: string|null, base_libraries: [string], entries: [{message: string, severity: string, token_source: string, object_path: string, object_resolved: bool, actor_name: string, actor_label: string, actor_path: string, actor_class: string, actor_guid: string, component_name: string, class_asset_path: string, class_root: string, class_root_is_base_library: bool}], count: int }

commands.name: get_output_log_lines
commands.description: Read the single per-editor-session log buffer UEAgent attaches to GLog (general editor output, not PIE-only -- Serialize() captures every category/verbosity that passes through GLog, regardless of PIE state; usable for PIE Functional Test / wait_for_pie_completion orchestration too). NON-DESTRUCTIVE cursor read (since_sequence_id, same idiom as poll_gameplay_messages), structured entries. Supports all three filters (message text, verbosity level, category).

params.name: count
params.description: Optional int32 cap on the number of entries returned (default 200, max 4096).

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring on the message text.

params.name: level_filter
params.description: Optional exact verbosity name filter (Fatal|Error|Warning|Display|Log|Verbose|VeryVerbose), case-insensitive.

params.name: category_filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring on the log category name.

params.name: since_sequence_id
params.description: Optional int64 cursor; only entries with a higher sequence_id are returned (default 0 = everything currently retained).

commands.returns: { lines: [{sequence_id, ts, level, category, message}], count, held_total, last_sequence_id }

commands.name: get_python_status
commands.description: Reports whether the editor Python plugin is loaded, available, configured and initialized, with the interpreter path and engine version; when Python is initialized it also evaluates sys.version for python_version (empty otherwise). Changes nothing; check it before execute_python or execute_python_file.
commands.returns: { engine_version, module_loaded, python_available, python_configured, python_initialized, interpreter_path, python_version }

commands.name: get_scalability_levels
commands.description: Read the engine's live scalability quality levels (Scalability::GetQualityLevels, the sg.* groups of the editor session) without changing anything: one level per group, 0 Low, 1 Medium, 2 High, 3 Epic, 4 Cinematic, except ResolutionQuality, which is a screen percentage; single_quality_level is the shared level when every group agrees and -1 when they differ (custom). Use it before and after set_scalability_quality, which changes one group or all; for a single sg.* or r.* console variable use get_cvar; for frame rate under those settings use get_fps_info. These are the editor's current settings, not a per-platform device profile or a saved user setting. Takes no parameters and does not fail.
commands.returns: { ResolutionQuality: int, ViewDistanceQuality: int, AntiAliasingQuality: int, ShadowQuality: int, GlobalIlluminationQuality: int, ReflectionQuality: int, PostProcessQuality: int, TextureQuality: int, EffectsQuality: int, FoliageQuality: int, ShadingQuality: int, LandscapeQuality: int, single_quality_level: int }

commands.name: get_selected_actors
commands.description: Read what is selected in the editor viewport/outliner right now: each actor's JSON plus the count and the world it belongs to. Use it to act on "what the user just clicked" without asking for names, and as the read-back for select_actors / deselect_actors. Editor world only, and remember that delete_actor, duplicate_actor, copy_actors and move_actors_to_level all MUTATE the selection as a side effect -- read it before those, not after.
commands.returns: { selected_actors: [actor JSON], selected_count: int, world_name: string }

commands.name: get_struct_members
commands.description: List the members of a user-defined struct (UUserDefinedStruct) with their type, default value, and flags.  The reader that pairs with add_struct_member.

params.name: struct_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UUserDefinedStruct (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyStruct).

commands.returns: { struct_path: string, member_count: int, members: [ { name: string, var_name: string, guid: string, category: string, sub_category?: string, sub_category_object?: string, container_type: string, default_value: string, current_default_value: string, tooltip?: string, edit_on_instance: bool, save_game: bool } ] }

commands.name: get_transaction_history
commands.description: Read the editor's undo buffer as a list, most-recent-first: each entry's title, context, primary object and whether it has already been undone. Use it to answer "what changed the editor recently, and was it me" -- including edits made by the human in the UI -- before you undo anything or blame a tool for a state you did not expect. Pure read; get_undo_state gives the counts-only summary.

params.name: max_entries
params.description: Max entries to return, newest first (default 50, clamped to 1..500).

commands.returns: { count: int, entries: [{ queue_index: int, title: string, context: string, is_transient: bool, primary_object: string, is_undone: bool }] }

commands.name: get_undo_state
commands.description: One call that answers everything you need before touching undo/redo: both counts, both next-entry LABELS, why undo or redo is impossible right now, and whether a transaction is still OPEN (transaction_open -- the thing that silently swallows later edits into someone else's batch). Read it BEFORE undo so you know what you are about to revert.
commands.returns: { can_undo: bool, can_redo: bool, undo_reason?: string (why not, when can_undo is false), redo_reason?: string (why not, when can_redo is false), undo_count: int (entries undo can still revert), redo_count: int (undone entries redo can restore), next_undo: string, next_redo: string, transaction_open: bool, transaction_index: int }

commands.name: get_viewport_state
commands.description: Read the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first) without changing it: realtime (the effective value, an override such as the background throttle included), view mode name and index, camera speed, camera location [x, y, z] and rotation [pitch, yaw, roll], and the Grid, Bounds, Collision, Wireframe and Lighting show flags, a flag this engine lacks left out. view_mode names every engine view mode by its display name without spaces (Lit, CSGWireframe, PlayerCollision...), or ViewMode_<index> for a value the engine does not name; set_viewport_settings takes that name back, but refuses the modes that need a choice made with them. It also reads the perspective FOV, the near clip plane and far clip override, the exposure, the view type (perspective or an orthographic view) and whether cinematic tools may possess the viewport. No viewport is an error; nothing is saved or recorded for undo. Setters: set_viewport_settings.
commands.returns: { realtime: bool, view_mode_index: int, view_mode: string, camera_speed: number, location: [number], rotation: [number], show_flags: object, fov: number (current perspective FOV, degrees), near_clip_plane: number (effective, cm), far_clip_plane_override: number (< 0 when no override is engaged), exposure: { fixed: bool, ev100: number }, view_type: string, view_type_index: int, allows_cinematic_control: bool }

commands.name: import_font_file
commands.description: Import a .ttf/.otf/.ttc/.otc font from disk as a UFontFace, and optionally the companion UFont that a FSlateFontInfo needs to actually render text. This is the only way to get a typeface into the project headlessly: import_texture_file imports images only, and nothing else in the toolset touches fonts. Drives UFontFileImportFactory inline (never IAssetTools::ImportAssets, which asserts when re-entered from the engine tick) and never lets the factory ask: left at its default it pops a MODAL DIALOG asking whether to create the UFont, which would hang the editor on a click that is never coming, so on UE 5.8 BatchCreateFontAsset is set explicitly and on 5.7 the import runs as automated and the UFont is created by the tool. Once imported, point a widget at it with set_widget_property on the dotted path "Font.FontObject" (a UFont) plus "Font.TypefaceFontName", or "Font.Size" for the size.

params.name: source_file_path
params.description: Absolute path on disk to the .ttf/.otf/.ttc/.otc file. A missing file, or any other extension, is a clean error before anything is touched.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: UE long path of the destination content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame/UI/Fonts.

params.name: name
params.description: Optional asset name; defaults to the source file's base name.

params.name: create_font_asset
params.description: Also create the companion UFont asset (default true). A UFontFace alone is a raw typeface: a FSlateFontInfo's FontObject wants a UFont. Pass false to import only the face, e.g. to add it as another typeface entry of an existing font.

commands.returns: { source_file_path, destination_path, imported_object_path, font_face_created, create_font_asset, message }

commands.name: link_media_texture_to_player
commands.description: Bind a UMediaTexture asset to a UMediaPlayer asset (both by asset path) so the texture shows that player's video, in place of any player it was bound to, in one undo step; then save the texture package (the player asset is not modified). The link is written to the texture's saved MediaPlayer property, so it survives a reload; linked confirms both that property and the player the texture now reports (bound_player_path), and a link that did not take is an error with linked false and nothing saved. Idempotent: linking the same pair again writes and saves the same state. A missing texture or player is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Create the assets with create_media_texture and create_media_player (which can also make a linked texture); read back with get_media_info.

params.name: media_texture_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMediaTexture, e.g. "/Game/Media/T_Intro" (the object path form also works).

params.name: media_player_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMediaPlayer to bind, e.g. "/Game/Media/MP_Intro" (the object path form also works).

commands.returns: { media_texture_path, media_player_path, linked, saved, bound_player_path?, save_error? }

commands.name: list_automation_tests
commands.description: List the automation tests registered in this editor without running any: per test its display name, full_test_path, test_name, tags, parameter, source file and line, and participants required. Engine, product and performance tests are listed too, not only smoke tests: the call widens the framework's test filter to every flag and loads the modules that register tests, but changes no asset or level. Tests are returned in registry order up to max_results; total_count counts every registered test, matched_count those the filter matches, and truncated is true when matches were cut off, so narrow the filter or raise max_results. Use it to find the name for run_automation_test; run_smoke_tests runs the smoke set and get_automation_test_results re-reads the last result.

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring matched against the full test path, e.g. 'UEAgent.' or 'Project.Functional'; empty lists every test.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Most tests to return, a positive number (default 500); 0 or a negative value also means 500.

commands.returns: { display_name, full_test_path, test_name, test_tags, test_parameter, source_file, source_file_line, num_participants_required, tests, total_count, matched_count, returned_count, max_results, truncated, filter }

commands.name: list_cvars
commands.description: List the console variables registered in the running editor whose name contains filter and/or starts with prefix, each with its current value as text and its help, without changing anything. Console commands are left out unless include_commands is true (they come with help but no value); with neither filter nor prefix every variable is walked. The list stops at max_results, and truncated plus total_matches tell how many more matched. Use it to discover names; then read one in full (int, float and bool values, flags, set_by) with get_cvar, change it with set_cvar or several at once with set_cvars_from_json, and read the scalability groups with get_scalability_levels. Matching nothing is a success with an empty cvars list.

params.name: filter
params.description: Text the name must contain, case ignored, e.g. "Shadow" (default empty = no filter). Without prefix, space-separated words must all appear and a single character matches as a name prefix; with prefix, a name must start with prefix and contain the whole filter.

params.name: prefix
params.description: Text the name must start with, case ignored, e.g. "r.Shadow." or "t." (default empty = any name).

params.name: include_commands
params.description: true to also list console commands (name and help, no value); default false lists variables only.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Most entries to return, a whole number of at least 1 (default 200); total_matches still counts every match.

commands.returns: { filter: string, prefix?: string, include_commands: bool, cvars: [{name, value?, help}], count: int, total_matches: int, max_results: int, truncated: bool }

commands.name: list_dirty_packages
commands.description: What is UNSAVED in the editor right now: every dirty package with its disk path, split into map / OFPA-external / asset, and -- the reason to run it -- readonly_dirty_count, the single go/no-go number telling you a vendored root like /Game/VendorPack would be REWRITTEN by the next bulk save. Run it before closing the editor, before compiling, and before any save; it also resolves OFPA hashes to actor labels so /__ExternalActors__/AB/CD/EF12 becomes a name. Strictly read-only: never marks dirty, never saves. WARNING: it reports IN-MEMORY state only -- a package clean here can still differ from HEAD on disk, so `git status` stays the disk authority. And do NOT use its pie_active field as the PIE gate: it can answer false with PIE running; the oracle is is_play_in_editor_active.

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of long-path prefixes treated as vendored/upstream (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). Only used to CLASSIFY (under_readonly_root / readonly_dirty_count); nothing is ever written. Pass [] to switch the classification off.

params.name: path_prefix
params.description: Optional long-path prefix filter, e.g. /Game/VendorPack, to ask "is anything of THEIRS dirty". Empty (default) lists everything; what it excluded is counted in filtered_out.

params.name: include_objects
params.description: Optional bool (default false). Also list every object carried by each dirty package. One object-hash walk per package -- a dirty map can hold thousands, so leave it off unless you need the contents.

commands.returns: { dirty_count: int, readonly_dirty_count: int, map_dirty_count: int, external_dirty_count: int, asset_dirty_count: int, filtered_out: int, pie_active: bool, current_world_package: string, path_prefix: string, readonly_roots: [string], readonly_roots_defaulted: bool, packages: [{ package_name: string, file_path: string, exists_on_disk: bool, kind: string, contains_map: bool, newly_created: bool, actor_label: string, actor_name: string, asset_name: string, asset_class: string, under_readonly_root: bool, objects?: [string] }], message: string, note: string }

commands.name: list_engine_ini_sections
commands.description: List the section names of one INI (Engine, Game, Input, Editor, Scalability...) as the running editor holds it in GConfig, the in-memory merge of every config layer, without changing anything. An INI GConfig does not know (a misspelt name, say) is a success with found=false and an empty list. Use it to discover a section before reading one key with get_engine_ini_value or writing one with set_engine_ini_value; for UDeveloperSettings classes use get_project_settings_value. file_path is the saved-config path Saved/Config/<Platform>/<name>.ini built from the name, not a file that was read or checked to exist.

params.name: config_file
params.description: INI base name, e.g. "Engine" (default), "Game", "Input", "Editor", "Scalability"; a trailing ".ini" is dropped.

params.name: include_base
params.description: Ignored: the code reads it but never uses it, so the list is the same whatever you pass.

commands.returns: { count, sections: [string], found: bool, config_file, file_path }

commands.name: load_level
commands.description: Open a map in the editor (by /Game or /Engine package path, or disk .umap), replacing the current world; default_template=true opens the engine's default template level instead (/Engine/Maps/Templates/Template_Default, ~45 actors: floor, PlayerStart, sky and lights), after which a save_level without `filename` would write over the ENGINE's own map (is_engine_template and warning say so). Also the repair for actors that VANISHED from a world in memory after compile_blueprint: reloading the same map brings the placed OFPA instances back with their per-instance config -- never re-place them. REFUSES up front when any other UWorld is still resident in memory, because the engine's world-leak check turns that into a Fatal error that kills the editor process and every unsaved edit with it; the refusal lists the resident worlds and the remedy. Run list_dirty_packages first: a reload discards unsaved work.

params.name: filename
params.description: Disk path to a .umap, OR a long package path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Foo) resolved to the on-disk map file. Required unless default_template is true.

params.name: default_template
params.description: Optional bool (default false): open the engine's default template level (/Engine/Maps/Templates/Template_Default) without naming it in filename; giving both is an error.

params.name: load_as_template
params.description: When true, loads the level as a template; defaults to false

params.name: force
params.description: Skip the resident-world preflight and call LoadMap anyway. With resident worlds alive this PROBABLY KILLS THE EDITOR: the engine raises a Fatal error ("World Memory Leaks"), the process dies and every unsaved in-memory edit is lost. Defaults to false.

commands.returns: { success: bool, error?: string, refused?: bool, load_attempted?: bool, resident_world_count?: int, resident_worlds?: [{ package: string, world_name: string, world_type: string, has_world_context: bool, is_load_target: bool }], remedy?: string, data?: { loaded_filename: string, target_package: string, default_template: bool, level_name?: string, world_name?: string, loaded_package?: string, is_engine_template?: bool, warning?: string (when the loaded map belongs to the engine), resident_world_count: int, forced_past_resident_worlds: bool, resident_worlds?: [...] } }

commands.name: migrate_assets
commands.description: Copy assets, and their dependencies unless ignore_dependencies, into another project's Content folder with IAssetTools::MigratePackages, with no prompt and skipping files that already exist there. The engine first saves every dirty package of this editor, and migrates nothing if one of them fails to save. What was copied is measured from the migration's own package list against the disk: migrated lists each package written (dependencies included), skipped_existing the requested ones the destination already had, failed the requested ones neither written nor skipped. Succeeds when nothing requested failed. destination_path must be a Content folder with a .uproject (or one .uplugin) next to it, or the engine migrates nothing and the call fails.

params.name: asset_paths
params.description: Asset object or package paths to migrate (e.g. ["/Game/Props/SM_Crate"]); each is reduced to its package name.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: Target content folder, e.g. D:/OtherProject/Content

params.name: ignore_dependencies
params.description: When true only the listed packages are copied, without their dependencies (default false).

commands.returns: { migrated_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, destination_path: string, ignore_dependencies: bool, migrated: [{ package: string, file: string }], skipped_existing: [string], failed: [string], note: string? }

commands.name: move_actors_to_level
