commands.description: Relocate existing editor-world actors into another sub-level (persistent or a loaded streaming level) -- it rescues actors that got spawned into the wrong level, which set_current_level only prevents going forward. Idempotent: actors already there come back in already_in_level instead of being touched. WARNING: it is clipboard-backed, so the editor SELECTION is mutated as a side effect, and the destination must be loaded AND unlocked. Both levels' packages get dirty: save_level after.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Array of actor names OR editor labels in the editor world (this one does accept labels, unlike delete_actor/delete_actors).

params.name: target_level
params.description: "persistent" or the short name of a loaded streaming sub-level

params.name: move_all_or_fail
params.description: When true, fail the whole move if any actor cannot be moved; defaults to false

commands.returns: { requested: int, moved_count: int, already_in_level: [string], target_level: string, success: bool, note: string }

commands.name: open_message_log
commands.description: Open or focus the editor Message Log window on one listing (PIE by default), creating the listing empty when it does not exist yet and enabling message log display; no message is changed. opened only says the request was made: without an editor UI nothing shows. module_available says whether the MessageLog module loaded. To read the messages use get_message_log_entries rather than the window; add or empty them with add_message_log_entry and clear_message_log.

params.name: log_name
params.description: Listing to surface (default "PIE").

commands.returns: { opened: bool, log_name: string, module_available: bool }

commands.name: paste_actors
commands.description: Drop whatever copy_actors left on the editor clipboard into the current level (edactPasteSelected), optionally re-centring the whole group on a world location while KEEPING each actor's relative offset -- that is the point of the copy/paste pair versus duplicate_actor. The pasted actors end up selected and are returned with their new names and transforms. Editor world only; they live in memory until save_level writes the .umap.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional world point to centre the pasted group on, ARRAY form only [x, y, z] (the group's average is moved there, each actor's offset preserved). Omit to paste where the originals were; any other value (an object, another length) is an error and nothing is pasted.

commands.returns: { pasted_actors: [actor JSON with the new auto-assigned names], pasted_count: int, success: bool }

commands.name: place_actors_on_terrain
commands.description: Ground many actors on the landscape in one call by sampling the heightmap at each actor's XY (no line trace; scatter without per-point python). Same grounding math as snap_actor_to_landscape, applied per actor.

params.name: actors
params.description: Array of { name (Actor->GetName()) OR label (Actor->GetActorLabel()), z_offset? (per-actor override), align? ('mesh_bbox_bottom'|'actor_origin', per-actor override) }

params.name: align
params.description: Optional default align for entries without their own; 'mesh_bbox_bottom' (default; drops the lowest mesh point) or 'actor_origin'

params.name: z_offset
params.description: Optional default extra world-Z above the sampled ground for entries without their own; defaults to 0

commands.returns: { placed: [ { name, label, previous_z, new_z, landed_z, in_bounds, align, align_used, z_offset } ], failed: [ { name?, label?, error } ], placed_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, landscape_actor_name: string, world_name: string }

retired.how: one snap_actor_to_landscape per actor, with transaction=true for one undo step

commands.name: print_to_output_log
commands.description: Write one line to the editor Output Log under the LogTemp category, at Log, Warning or Error verbosity; verbosity is matched without case, anything else logs at Log, and the reply's verbosity is the level actually used. An empty or missing message is an error. Each call appends another line, so it is not idempotent, and nothing else changes: no asset, no undo step, no Message Log entry; like any UE_LOG line it also reaches the editor log file. Use it to mark a point in the log between other calls; read lines back with get_output_log_lines; a listing in Window > Message Log is add_message_log_entry, an on-screen toast show_notification.

params.name: message
params.description: The text to log; empty is an error.

params.name: verbosity
params.description: UE_LOG verbosity: "Log" (default), "Warning", "Error"; matched without case, and any other value logs at Log.

commands.returns: { logged: bool, message: string, verbosity: string }

commands.name: redo
commands.description: Re-apply the transaction that undo just reverted, or `count` of them, and report what remains, including next_redo. WARNING: `success` is ALWAYS true even with an empty redo stack -- read `applied` instead, and with a count compare actually_redone against requested. Note the redo stack is discarded as soon as any NEW edit is made after an undo, so a redo that answers applied:false usually means something was changed in between, not that the command failed.

params.name: count
params.description: Optional. How many transactions to redo, at least 1 (default 1); stops early when the redo stack runs out. Below 1 is refused.

commands.returns: { applied: bool (THE oracle), requested: int, actually_redone: int (compare against requested), undo_count: int, can_redo: bool, next_redo: string (label of the next redoable entry) }

commands.name: reload_asset_package
commands.description: Re-read already-loaded packages FROM DISK, non-interactively (it never opens the modal that would freeze a headless editor), either preserving or permanently discarding their in-memory edits. This is the repair for the situation list_dirty_packages flags: a vendored package left dirty by a compile cascade is cleaned with on_dirty="discard" (was_dirty:[...] -> still_dirty:[]), so the next bulk save cannot write it. Also the way to throw away a bad in-memory edit without touching disk. It reports before/after evidence per package, and skips what it cannot safely reload (not loaded, OFPA, worlds) instead of pretending. WARNING: on_dirty="discard" is irreversible for unsaved work -- check what is dirty first.

params.name: package_names
params.description: Array of long package names (or object paths) to reload, e.g. ["/Game/VendorPack/.../DT_ItemRows"].

params.name: package_name
params.description: Convenience single-name alias for package_names.

params.name: on_dirty
params.description: Optional "abort" (default) or "discard". "abort" -> EReloadPackagesInteractionMode::AssumeNegative: a package with unsaved in-memory edits is NOT reloaded and its edits are kept. "discard" -> AssumePositive: UPackageTools clears the dirty flag and reloads, PERMANENTLY THROWING AWAY those in-memory edits.

commands.returns: { requested: [string], on_dirty: string, interaction_mode: string, attempted: [string], reloaded: [string], was_dirty: [string], still_dirty: [string], failed: [string], skipped_not_loaded: [string], skipped_ofpa: [string], skipped_world: [object], skipped_invalid: [object], api_returned: bool, api_error: string, verify: { before: [object], after: [object] }, message: string }

commands.name: remove_component_from_actor
commands.description: Detach and destroy one component from an actor PLACED in the level, by component name -- the inverse of add_component_to_actor and, like it, an instance-level edit that does not touch the actor's Blueprint (use remove_component_from_blueprint for the class). Discover the exact component_name with get_actor_components first. Editor world only; dirties the actor's package, so save_level to keep it.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name of the placed actor (editor world).

params.name: component_name
params.description: Exact component name as reported by get_actor_components.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, removed_component: string, component_type: string, success: bool }

commands.name: remove_enum_entry
commands.description: Remove one enumerator from a Blueprint Enum by display name (or internal name).  Idempotent (a missing entry reports already_absent without error); refuses to remove the last remaining entry. The hidden _MAX sentinel is never counted or removable.

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum.

params.name: entry_name
params.description: Enumerator to remove, by display name (or internal name).

commands.returns: { enum_path: string, entry_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, entry_count: int }

commands.name: remove_struct_member
commands.description: Remove one member from a Blueprint user-defined struct, found by display name or else by internal var name (case-insensitive), through the engine's struct editor: one undo step, the struct is recompiled so the Blueprints and DataTable rows that use it lose that field, and the package is marked dirty but not saved (save_asset). Idempotent: a member that is not there changes nothing and answers already_absent true. Removing the last member is refused, since a struct cannot be empty, and nothing changes; a path that does not load as a user-defined struct is an error. Find the names with get_struct_members; inverse: add_struct_member; to keep the data under another name use rename_struct_member instead.

params.name: struct_path
params.description: Asset path of the user-defined struct, e.g. "/Game/Data/S_Item", as get_struct_members takes it.

params.name: member_name
params.description: Member to remove, by its display name as get_struct_members returns it (members[].name) or by its var_name; case-insensitive.

commands.returns: { struct_path: string, member_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, member_count: int }

commands.name: remove_undo_barrier
commands.description: Lift the most recent undo barrier so undo can step past it again -- the counterpart of set_undo_barrier, for when the protected batch is finished -- or, with all=true, every barrier at once (including ones another session or the human placed to protect their work). Nothing is undone; it only lifts the floor. WARNING: `success` is hardcoded true: `removed` is the oracle and comes back false as an honest no-op when there was no barrier.

params.name: all
params.description: Optional bool (default false). true clears ALL undo barriers instead of popping the most recent one.

commands.returns: { success: bool (hardcoded), removed: bool (THE oracle -- false = there was nothing to pop), all: bool (echo), undo_barrier: int now in force, undo_count: int, queue_length: int }

commands.name: rename_enum_entry
commands.description: Rename one enumerator of a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum): resolve the entry by its current display name (or internal name) to its index, then set a new display name via FEnumEditorUtils::SetEnumeratorDisplayName.  Idempotent: renaming an entry to the name it already has is a no-op success (already_named). An unknown current entry is an honest error; so is a new name that is empty/invalid or duplicates another entry's display name (the engine's IsEnumeratorDisplayNameValid rejects it). The hidden _MAX sentinel is never addressable.

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum).

params.name: entry_name
params.description: Enumerator to rename, by its current display name (or internal name).

params.name: new_name
params.description: New display name for the enumerator.

commands.returns: { enum_path: string, entry_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, index: int, entries: [string] }

commands.name: rename_struct_member
commands.description: Rename a member of a user-defined struct by resolving its current display name to its stable VarGuid, then applying the new display name (the same FStructureEditorUtils::RenameVariable path add_struct_member uses to set the initial name).  Idempotent: renaming a member to the name it already has is a no-op success (already_named). An unknown current member, or a new name that collides with another member's name, is an honest error.

params.name: struct_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UUserDefinedStruct.

params.name: member_name
params.description: Member to rename, by its current display name (or internal var name).

params.name: new_name
params.description: New display name for the member.

commands.returns: { struct_path: string, member_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, member: object }

commands.name: reorder_enum_entry
commands.description: Move one enumerator to a new position in a Blueprint Enum, shifting the others (e.g. [A,B,C,D] move B->index 2 = [A,C,B,D]).  to_index is clamped to the user-entry range (the trailing _MAX sentinel is excluded). An unknown entry is an honest error.

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum.

params.name: entry_name
params.description: Enumerator to move, by display name (or internal name).

params.name: to_index
params.description: Target zero-based position among the user entries.

commands.returns: { enum_path: string, entry_name: string, from_index: int, to_index: int, moved: bool, entries: [string] }

commands.name: reset_transaction_buffer
commands.description: IRREVERSIBLE: wipes the editor's ENTIRE undo AND redo history (the human's entries too, not just yours) and drops any open transaction. It does not revert anything -- edits already made stay made, they just stop being undoable. Use only to reclaim memory after a huge batch, or when a corrupt buffer is causing trouble; to undo work use undo (with `count` for several steps). undo_count_before vs after is the evidence.

params.name: reason
params.description: Human-readable reason, logged by the engine so the wipe is traceable. Defaults to 'MCP reset_transaction_buffer'.

commands.returns: { success: bool (hardcoded), undo_count_before: int, undo_count_after: int (0) }

commands.name: run_automation_test
commands.description: Run ONE registered automation test in this editor, synchronously, and return its verdict (pass, fail or skipped) with its errors, warnings and log entries. Find the name first with list_automation_tests; re-read the last result later without running anything with get_automation_test_results; run every smoke test at once with run_smoke_tests. A test that needs several ticks (PIE, a map load, a wait) is not run here but answered verdict skipped with the reason -- drive it with run_functional_test_in_pie -- and so is one that needs an interactive user or a real renderer in a headless editor; an editor busy with a slow task or PIE refuses the start. Marked destructive and not idempotent because the test's own code runs in the editor and can create, change or delete assets and actors as it was written to, so two runs need not do the same; this tool itself saves nothing and adds no undo step for what the test did.

params.name: test_name
params.description: The test's test_name or its full_test_path, exactly as list_automation_tests gives them (e.g. "UEAgent.ClaudeCode")

commands.returns: { test_name, started, completed, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings, entries:[{type,message,context,filename,line}], entry_count, note }

commands.name: run_functional_test_in_pie
commands.description: Place one instance of a Functional Test Blueprint class in the editor level (unless one is already there), then ask the editor to start a Simulate-in-Editor session and, with auto_stop_pie (default), to end it again. It does not wait for the test or read its result: verdict is "pass" whenever a session is running right after the request and "not_run" otherwise, so it is no test verdict -- read the outcome in the output log (get_output_log_lines), or run a registered test with run_automation_test, whose verdict is real. The start request is deferred (and with no level viewport, headless, nothing starts), so on a first call pie_started is usually false and the session starts after the reply without being stopped: end it with stop_play_in_editor. With a session already running it answers pass and, with auto_stop_pie, ends that session. The placed actor stays in the level, unsaved and with no undo step. Create the test first with create_functional_test; a class that is not found, or is not a Functional Test, is an error.

params.name: test_asset_path
params.description: Functional Test Blueprint, as an asset path ("/Game/Tests/BP_FT_PlayerHealth"), object path or generated-class path ("/Game/Tests/BP_FT_PlayerHealth.BP_FT_PlayerHealth_C"); when none loads, the first loaded Functional Test class whose name contains the last path segment is used.

params.name: auto_stop_pie
params.description: Optional bool (default true): request the end of the session right after it is seen running, including a session that was already running before the call.

commands.returns: { test_asset_path, pie_started, verdict: "pass"|"not_run", pie_stopped?, already_in_pie?, spawned?, already_in_world?, note? }

commands.name: run_smoke_tests
commands.description: Runs every registered automation test with the smoke filter, synchronously in the editor, and returns only the aggregate: ran, all_passed and a note. Under a commandlet the engine skips them, so ran and all_passed come back false. For one test with its log entries use run_automation_test.
commands.returns: { ran, all_passed, note }

commands.name: save_asset
commands.description: Write ONE .uasset to disk by package path (a Blueprint, DataTable, material...) and VERIFY the effect: still_dirty_after_save:false plus file_on_disk:true is the oracle, not `saved`. Use save_level for the .umap and reload_asset_package to undo an in-memory edit instead. PIE: this is REFUSED while Play-in-Editor runs (it never stops or touches your session) -- the engine guard Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0 rejects the write before attempting anything, so a save during play would report success without writing a byte. Stop PIE and retry, or pass force=true. WARNING: when it answers success:false with PIE down, a common cause is the file being READ-ONLY on disk (e.g. a Git LFS `lockable` file that has not been `git lfs lock`ed). You do not have to check that by hand: `file_read_only` is measured on every call and the error message states whether a read-only file IS or is NOT the explanation. WARNING: it writes exactly one package, so it cannot stop a compile cascade from dirtying a vendored asset that a LATER bulk save then rewrites -- list_dirty_packages before, `git status` after.

params.name: path
params.description: Full asset path to save, e.g. /Game/MyGame/Core/BP_MyActor (an .Object suffix is tolerated). Must already exist or the call errors.

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of long-path prefixes treated as vendored/upstream (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). A save under one of them is REFUSED by default; see refuse_readonly. Pass [] to disable the classification entirely.

params.name: refuse_readonly
params.description: Optional bool. When true, a save whose package falls under one of readonly_roots is REFUSED (success:false, saved:false, refused_readonly:true) instead of performed. Default = the process-wide switch (mcp_common::IsReadOnlyRootSaveEnforcementEnabled(), true unless `mcp.ReadOnlyRootEnforcement 0`); when false the write happens and is only reported + ledgered.

commands.returns: { path: string, package_name: string, saved: bool, success: bool, under_readonly_root: bool, readonly_root_matched: string, refused_readonly: bool, readonly_roots: [string], readonly_roots_defaulted: bool, still_dirty_after_save: bool, file_on_disk: bool, file_read_only: bool (measured on disk -- true means the file is read-only, e.g. an unlocked Git LFS `lockable` file), verification: object, verification_checks: [object], error?: string }

commands.name: save_level
commands.description: Write the editor's current level (.umap) to disk; it REFUSES while PIE is running (the engine guard rejects the write anyway) and derives `success` from the file being on disk afterwards, never from the save call's own bool. WARNING: it also REFUSES when the target .umap is READ-ONLY on disk, which in an LFS repo means a `lockable` path you have not `git lfs lock`ed: that write cannot succeed, and answering over HEAD's still-untouched bytes would report success:true having written nothing. The refusal names the file and the fix (`git lfs lock <file>`) -- take the lock, do not retry. WARNING: on a file that ALREADY existed, `file_exists_on_disk` alone still cannot tell "I wrote it" from "it was already there": the field that proves the write is `file_mtime_changed`. It is deliberately NOT gating `success`, because a save with nothing dirty to write also leaves the mtime alone and that is not a failure. WARNING: with `filename` this is a SaveAs that DUPLICATES: the editor stays on the old map, the new one becomes a resident world (which then makes load_level refuse), and a SECOND save to the same filename opens a modal that freezes the editor -- treat filename as one-shot per name per session.

params.name: filename
params.description: Optional. A /Game asset path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Foo) or a disk .umap path; both accepted and resolved. Omit it to save the level in place -- that is the branch that just works. Passing one is a SaveAs: duplicate + resident world + the one-shot rule above.

params.name: save_as
params.description: Accepted for wire compatibility and IGNORED: the branch is chosen by whether `filename` was given. It comes back inside `requested` to mark it as your input, not a measurement.

commands.returns: { success: bool, error?: string, data?: { saved_filename?: string, saved_package?: string, saved_disk_path?: string, level_name?: string, file_exists_on_disk: bool, file_size_bytes: int, file_existed_before: bool, file_mtime_changed: bool (the write itself -- see the read-only note above), save_call_returned: bool, rescued_with_save_packages: bool, pie_was_stopped: bool, orphan_world_risk?: bool, requested?: { filename?: string, save_as?: bool } } }

commands.name: select_actors
commands.description: Select actors by name in the editor viewport/outliner, appending to or replacing the current selection, and report which ones were not found. Use it to stage the input for the selection-driven tools (copy_actors with copy_selected, move_actors_to_level) or to show the user what you mean before they look. WARNING: matches INTERNAL names only (no editor labels) and misses are reported in not_found_names instead of failing, so check not_found_count. Editor world only.

params.name: actor_names
params.description: Array of internal actor names (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Editor labels do NOT resolve here; convert them with find_actors_by_name.

params.name: add_to_selection
params.description: Optional bool (default TRUE = append to whatever is already selected). Pass false to clear the selection first and end up with exactly these actors.

commands.returns: { selected_actors: [actor JSON], selected_count: int, not_found_count: int, not_found_names?: [string], add_to_selection: bool }

commands.name: set_actor_transform
commands.description: Move, rotate and/or scale ONE actor (omitted components are left as they are) and return the actor's re-read transform plus the identity of the world that was written. Undoable, and it calls Modify() first -- which matters, because moving an actor from Python does NOT dirty its OFPA package and then save_level reports success while writing nothing. Takes a `world` selector, so it also reaches a LIVE PIE pawn (an editor-only lookup would answer "Actor not found" for an actor that exists in another world). Use execute_batch for many actors, snap_actor_to_landscape to drop one onto the landscape.

params.name: name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel), case-insensitive whole-string match.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional: "editor" (default) | "pie" | "server" | "client" | "pie:N". In co-op the authoritative pawn lives on the server, and a move written to the client world will be corrected by replication.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional new WORLD location, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Absolute, not a delta; any other value (an object, another length) is an error and the actor is not touched.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional new WORLD rotation as the array [pitch, yaw, roll] -- note index 2 is ROLL, not yaw -- or, unambiguously, the object {"pitch":..,"yaw":..,"roll":..}, which is the recommended form.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional new WORLD scale, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Any other value (an object, another length) is an error and the actor is not touched.

commands.returns: { actor JSON via DescribeActorObject, transform RE-READ off the actor after the write }

commands.name: set_actor_transforms
commands.description: Move/rotate/scale MANY actors in a single undoable transaction, each with its own optional location/rotation/scale, reporting success_count, failure_count and the names that did not resolve. Cheaper and atomically undoable versus N set_actor_transform calls. Calls Modify() per actor so their OFPA packages dirty and save_level actually writes them. Takes the same `world` selector as set_actor_transform, so it reaches a live PIE world too. WARNING: resolves the INTERNAL name only (no editor labels, unlike set_actor_transform); a name it cannot find is counted in failure_count, not raised as an error -- read that number.

params.name: actor_transforms
params.description: Array of objects {actor_name: internal GetName; location?: [x,y,z] array only; rotation?: [pitch,yaw,roll] or the safer {pitch,yaw,roll}; scale?: [x,y,z] array only}. Omitted components keep their current value; an entry with no actor_name just increments failure_count, and a malformed vector silently reads as zero.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional: "editor" (default) | "pie" | "server" | "client" | "pie:N". The response stamps which world answered.

commands.returns: { success_count: int, failure_count: int (unresolved or malformed entries -- check it), updated_actors: [actor JSON re-read after the write], failed_actors?: [string], world_name, world_package, ... }

retired.how: one set_actor_transform per actor, with transaction=true for one undo step

commands.name: set_allow_cinematic_control
commands.description: Set whether the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first) may be possessed by cinematic tools such as Sequencer to preview sequences (FEditorViewportClient::SetAllowCinematicControl). It sets the given value rather than toggling; it lasts for this editor session, nothing is saved or undoable, and no viewport is an error. allows_cinematic_control is read back from the viewport. Read the flag without changing it with get_viewport_state (allows_cinematic_control).

params.name: allow
params.description: True to allow cinematic control, false to block it

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: bool, allows_cinematic_control: bool }

commands.name: set_camera_speed
commands.description: Set the camera movement speed of the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first). Affects this editor session only and saves nothing. Returns requested and camera_speed, the value read back from the viewport afterwards.

params.name: speed
params.description: Camera speed as a positive float; 0 or less is an error. Compare camera_speed in the reply to see what the viewport kept.

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: number, camera_speed: number }

commands.name: set_current_level
commands.description: Choose which sub-level of the editor world is CURRENT, i.e. where newly spawned or pasted actors will land. Set it before spawn_actor / paste_actors when a map is split into streaming sub-levels, otherwise everything piles into whichever level happens to be active. Errors honestly if the named streaming level is not loaded/visible; already_current:true when it was already the one. Use move_actors_to_level to relocate actors that ended up in the wrong one.

params.name: level_name
params.description: "persistent" for the persistent level, or the SHORT name of a loaded, visible streaming sub-level (not a /Game path).

commands.returns: { current_level: string, changed: bool, already_current: bool, success: true } -- current_level is the level current after the call; a level that is not found, or not loaded and visible, is an error instead.

commands.name: set_cvar
commands.description: Sets a console variable via IConsoleManager and reads the value back.  Uses IConsoleManager::Get().FindConsoleVariable(name)->Set(value, ECVF_SetByConsole). Honest error if the named cvar does not exist (unlike a raw console Exec which silently no-ops).

params.name: name
params.description: Console variable name, e.g. "r.ScreenPercentage", "r.Shadow.MaxResolution".

params.name: value
params.description: New value (string, number, or bool; coerced to the cvar's type).

commands.returns: { set: bool, requested_value: string, name: string, value: string, string_value: string, int_value: int, float_value: float, bool_value: bool, help: string, flags: int, set_by: string }

commands.name: set_cvars_from_json
commands.description: Set several console variables of the running editor in one call, from a JSON object of name/value pairs, each through IConsoleManager at SetByCode priority. Not atomic: names are applied one by one, an unknown name goes to errors and the others still apply. Unlike set_cvar (one variable, console priority, read back) it reads nothing back, and applied counts every name found, including a set the engine ignores because the variable was last set at a higher priority (by the console or by set_cvar), so confirm values with get_cvar. Find names with list_cvars. The values live in this editor session only: nothing is written to an INI (set_engine_ini_value does that) and nothing is undoable. Text that is not a JSON object is an error and nothing changes. Repeating the call sets the same values again.

params.name: cvars
params.description: A STRING holding a JSON object of exact cvar names to values, e.g. '{"r.ScreenPercentage":"75","t.MaxFPS":"60"}'; names as list_cvars returns them. Give values as text such as "1": a JSON number is passed as its text, and a JSON true/false as the words true/false, which an integer cvar reads as 0.

commands.returns: { applied, requested, errors: [{name, error}] }

commands.name: set_engine_ini_value
commands.description: Write one key into the GConfig copy of an INI (Engine by default), flush it to the saved config under Saved/Config/<Platform>/, and verify by reading it back (applied). It does not edit Config/Default*.ini, and objects that already loaded their config are not reloaded. The value may be text, a bool or a number; with plugin_name it writes a plugin's setting, the section defaulting to the plugin's /Script/<Plugin>.<Plugin>.

params.name: key
params.description: Key inside the section, e.g. "r.DefaultFeature.AntiAliasing"; its current value is replaced.

params.name: value
params.description: Value to write: a string written verbatim (an empty string is allowed), a JSON bool written as GConfig writes one ("True"/"False"), or a JSON number written as its text (an integer without decimals).

params.name: section
params.description: INI section, e.g. "/Script/Engine.RendererSettings"; created when missing; surrounding brackets are dropped. Required unless plugin_name is given.

params.name: config_file
params.description: Config base name without extension, e.g. "Engine" (default), "Game", "Input"; "Engine.ini" is not resolved.

params.name: plugin_name
params.description: Optional plugin, as its .uplugin is named: an unknown one fails with nothing written; a known one adds its identity to the reply and makes section default to /Script/<Plugin>.<Plugin>.

commands.returns: { applied, section, key, value, value_type: "string"|"bool"|"number", readback_value, config_file, config_file_path, plugin_name?, plugin_status?, plugin_version?, plugin_description?, plugin_author?, plugin_category?, plugin_loaded?, plugin_enabled?, plugin_path?, plugin_file? }

commands.name: set_enum_bitflags
commands.description: Turn the "Bitflags" metadata of a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum) on or off, as the enum editor's checkbox does: on, its enumerators can be combined as bit flags, so an integer variable marked Bitmask can use it as its Bitmask Enum. Only this flag changes; build the entries with create_enum, add_enum_entry, rename_enum_entry, reorder_enum_entry or remove_enum_entry, and read them with get_enum_info. One undo step; Blueprints that use the enum are notified, and the enum is marked dirty, not saved (save_asset). Idempotent: the state it already has reports already_set=true, applied=false, and changes nothing. A path that does not load a UUserDefinedEnum (a native C++ enum included) is an error.

params.name: enum_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum, the ".MyEnum" suffix optional), as create_enum returns it or find_assets_by_name finds it.

params.name: bitflags
params.description: Desired state: true to mark as bitflags, false to clear.

commands.returns: { enum_path: string, bitflags: bool, already_set: bool, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_far_clip_plane
commands.description: Override the far clip plane distance, in cm, of the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first, so objects beyond it are culled from the view; no viewport is an error. 0 or a negative distance drops the override and the default far plane applies again. It lasts for this editor session with no undo step and no save, and the previous value is not returned. far_clip_plane is the stored override read back, which is the distance sent, and override_active is true only for a distance above 0. get_viewport_state reads the near plane together with this override (far_clip_plane_override); the near plane is set_near_clip_plane.

params.name: distance
params.description: Far clip distance in cm; 0 or any negative value clears the override and the default far plane applies

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: number, far_clip_plane: number, override_active: bool }

commands.name: set_game_view
commands.description: Turn Game View on or off on the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first (the view the editor's G key toggles); no viewport is an error. Turning it on swaps the viewport's show flags for the game set, hiding editor-only chrome such as sprites, the transform widget and selection outlines, and keeps the editor set to put back when it is turned off. It sets the given state, so a repeat call changes nothing; it lasts for this editor session with no undo step and nothing saved. in_game_view is read back. Single flags are set_show_flag, render modes set_viewport_view_mode; to run the game use start_play_in_editor.

params.name: enabled
params.description: True to enable game view, false to revert to editor view

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: bool, in_game_view: bool }

commands.name: set_near_clip_plane
commands.description: Override the near clip plane distance, in cm, of the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first; no viewport is an error. A negative distance (-1 by convention) drops the override so the engine near plane, GNearClippingPlane, applies again; a distance of at least 0.001, the smallest the editor's Near View Plane control allows, becomes the override. 0 (a degenerate projection), anything else below 0.001 and a value too large for a float are errors before anything changes. It lasts for this editor session with no undo step and no save, and the previous value is not returned. near_clip_plane is the effective near plane read back and override_active says whether an override is now set. get_viewport_state reads both clip planes (near_clip_plane, far_clip_plane_override); the far plane is set_far_clip_plane.

params.name: distance
params.description: Near clip distance in cm, at least 0.001; any negative value (-1 by convention) clears the override and falls back to GNearClippingPlane

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: number, near_clip_plane: number, override_active: bool }

commands.name: set_plugin_enabled
commands.description: Turn a plugin on (or off, with enabled=false) in the .uproject and save the project file to disk. WARNING: `enabled` echoes the requested state once the .uproject write succeeded, and the plugin's MODULES are not loaded or unloaded by this call -- the editor has to be restarted before an enabled plugin's classes, assets or MCP tools actually exist, and a disabled plugin's classes keep working until then. So do not treat a following "class not found", or a still-working feature, as a failure of this command; check project_saved and then restart. A plugin the .uproject already has in that state is a no-op: project_saved=false and nothing saved; a .uproject that cannot be saved makes success false. A name this editor has not discovered as a plugin is an error, and nothing is written to the .uproject. WARNING: disabling a plugin whose assets are referenced leaves those references broken on the next start; check get_plugin_status and the referencers first. Use get_plugin_status to read the current state.

params.name: plugin_name
params.description: Plugin name exactly as in its .uplugin file (e.g. 'PythonScriptPlugin'), not a path.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Optional bool (default true): true enables the plugin, false disables it.

commands.returns: { plugin_name: string (the plugin's own spelling), enabled: bool (the requested state, set when the .uproject write succeeded), project_saved: bool, note: string about the required restart, or that nothing changed }

commands.name: set_scalability_quality
commands.description: Set the running editor's scalability quality, every sg.* group at once (category all, the default) or one group, through Scalability::SetQualityLevels + ApplyCachedQualityLevels, then read all the levels back. It starts from the current levels, so a single-group change leaves the other groups as they were. The change lives in this editor session only: it is not undoable and is not written to GameUserSettings, an INI or a device profile. Check the levels before with get_scalability_levels; for one sg.* or r.* variable use set_cvar instead. An unknown quality word or category is an error and nothing changes; a number outside 0-4 is clamped. set is always true, so compare the returned levels with requested_level. Repeating the call sets the same levels again (idempotent).

params.name: quality
params.description: Level as a number 0-4 (0 Low, 1 Medium, 2 High, 3 Epic, 4 Cinematic; others clamped) or one of "Low", "Medium", "High", "Epic", "Cinematic", case ignored. Required.

params.name: category
params.description: One group, case ignored: "ViewDistance", "AntiAliasing", "Shadows", "GlobalIllumination" (or "GI"), "Reflection", "PostProcess", "Texture", "Effects", "Foliage", "Shading", "Landscape"; or "all" (the default) for every group.

commands.returns: { set: bool, requested_level: int, category: string, ResolutionQuality: int, ViewDistanceQuality: int, AntiAliasingQuality: int, ShadowQuality: int, GlobalIlluminationQuality: int, ReflectionQuality: int, PostProcessQuality: int, TextureQuality: int, EffectsQuality: int, FoliageQuality: int, ShadingQuality: int, LandscapeQuality: int }

commands.name: set_show_flag
commands.description: Set one engine show flag (Grid, Bounds, Collision, Wireframe, Lighting...) on the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first; no viewport is an error. It sets the given state rather than toggling: enabled true turns the flag on, false turns it off, and a repeat call changes nothing. flag_name is matched without case against the engine's show flags and registered custom flags; an unknown name is an error before anything changes. It lasts for this editor session, with no undo step, nothing saved and the earlier value not returned. value is the flag read back and flag_index its engine index. get_viewport_state reads Grid, Bounds, Collision, Wireframe and Lighting back; set_game_view swaps the whole flag set; set_viewport_view_mode changes the render mode.

params.name: flag_name
params.description: Engine show flag name as FEngineShowFlags spells it, e.g. Grid, Bounds, Collision, Wireframe, Lighting; matched without case

params.name: enabled
params.description: True to set the flag, false to clear it

commands.returns: { applied: bool, flag_name: string, flag_index: int, requested: bool, value: bool }

commands.name: set_struct_member_default
commands.description: Set the default value of one member of a Blueprint user-defined struct, found by display name or else by internal var name (case-insensitive), through the engine's struct editor, which checks the value against the member's type and recompiles the struct; one undo step, and the package is marked dirty but not saved (save_asset). Idempotent: a value equal to the stored default text changes nothing and answers already_set true (compared as text, so "1.5" and "1.50" differ). A value invalid for the type, a member that is not found or a path that does not load as a user-defined struct is an error and nothing changes. Read the members and their current defaults with get_struct_members; a new member gets its type from add_struct_member first.

params.name: struct_path
params.description: Asset path of the user-defined struct, e.g. "/Game/Data/S_Item", as get_struct_members takes it.

params.name: member_name
params.description: Member to edit, by its display name as get_struct_members returns it (members[].name) or by its var_name; case-insensitive.

params.name: default_value
params.description: New default as text in the member type's format (e.g. "7", "true", "1.5", "Hello", "(X=1.0,Y=2.0,Z=3.0)" for a Vector); pass "" to clear it.

commands.returns: { struct_path: string, member_name: string, default_value: string, applied_default_value: string, already_set: bool, applied: bool, member: object }

commands.name: set_undo_barrier
commands.description: Drop a floor in the undo stack at the current position so no later undo can cross it -- the way to protect everything done SO FAR (yours or the human's) before starting a risky batch that you may want to unwind. Idempotent: a barrier already sitting at the cursor is not pushed twice (already_existed:true). Lift it with remove_undo_barrier (all=true lifts every barrier).
commands.returns: { success: bool (hardcoded), already_existed: bool (true = nothing new was pushed), undo_barrier: int (cursor it sits at), undo_count: int, queue_length: int }

commands.name: set_view_type
commands.description: Switch the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first, to the perspective camera or one of the six orthographic views; no viewport is an error. type is matched without case, and any other name is an error before anything changes. Switching to an orthographic view unlocks an actor the viewport was piloting, and each projection re-applies the view mode it keeps for itself. It sets the given type, so a repeat call changes nothing; it lasts for this editor session with no undo step and no save. view_type and view_type_index are read back. Read it with get_viewport_state (view_type); render modes are set_viewport_view_mode, the camera position set_viewport_camera.

params.name: type
params.description: View type name. One of: Perspective, Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Front, Back. Matched without case.

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: string, view_type: string, view_type_index: int }

commands.name: set_viewport_camera
commands.description: Place the camera of the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first) at an absolute world location and/or rotation; at least one is required and no viewport is an error. Editor view only, not undoable or saved: a PIE player camera (set_view_target) or a camera actor (set_camera_transform) does not move. location must be an [x, y, z] array of three numbers in cm and rotation three numbers or a roll/pitch/yaw object; anything else is refused before the camera moves. The reply reads location and rotation back, rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll]. Frame an actor with focus_viewport.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation

commands.returns: { applied: bool, location_set: bool, rotation_set: bool, location: [number], rotation: [number] }

commands.name: set_viewport_exposure
commands.description: Set the exposure of the active level editor viewport: fixed at ev100 when fixed is true, automatic eye adaptation when false. Affects the viewport only and saves nothing. Returns applied, fixed and ev100 as read back; get_viewport_state reads them (exposure).

params.name: fixed
params.description: True for fixed exposure (use FixedEV100), false for automatic eye-adaptation

params.name: ev100
params.description: EV100 value to use when fixed=true (any float; typical range -3..20)

commands.returns: { applied: bool, fixed: bool, ev100: number }

commands.name: set_viewport_fov
commands.description: Set the perspective field of view, in degrees, of the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first; no viewport is an error. fov must lie in 5..170, the range of the editor's Field of View control, and a value outside it is an error before anything changes. Like that control it sets both the current view FOV and the stored one that a camera reset or the end of a PIE session restores; fov and stored_fov are read back, and an orthographic view ignores them. There is no undo step and no asset is saved, and the previous FOV is not returned. A viewport piloting a camera actor keeps showing that camera's FOV until it stops piloting it. Read it with get_viewport_state (fov); a camera actor's own FOV is set_camera_fov.

params.name: fov
params.description: Field of view in degrees, from 5 to 170 (the range of the editor's FOV slider)

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: number, fov: number, stored_fov: number }

commands.name: set_viewport_realtime
commands.description: Enable or disable realtime rendering on the active editor viewport

params.name: enabled
params.description: True to turn on realtime updates, false to turn them off

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: bool, realtime: bool, effective_realtime: bool, override_active: bool, override_source: string }

commands.name: set_viewport_settings
commands.description: Change any settings of the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first) in one call: camera location and rotation, field of view, near and far clip planes, exposure, realtime, view mode, show flags, camera speed, perspective or orthographic view type, game view and cinematic control. Pass only the settings to change; each is validated and applied as its own step, in the order listed here, and the call stops at the first one refused (applied lists those already changed). Editor view only: not undoable, nothing saved. get_viewport_state reads every one of them back.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional camera [x, y, z] world location

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional camera world rotation, [pitch, yaw, roll] or {"pitch","yaw","roll"}

params.name: fov
params.description: Optional perspective field of view in degrees

params.name: near_clip
params.description: Optional near clip plane distance in cm

params.name: far_clip
params.description: Optional far clip plane distance in cm; 0 means no far plane

params.name: exposure_fixed
params.description: Optional: true for a fixed exposure at exposure_ev100, false for automatic eye adaptation

params.name: exposure_ev100
params.description: Optional EV100 used when exposure_fixed is true (typical range -3..20); needs exposure_fixed

params.name: realtime
params.description: Optional: realtime rendering on or off

params.name: view_mode
params.description: Optional engine view mode name, e.g. Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, DetailLighting, LightingOnly, ShaderComplexity, Clay

params.name: show_flags
params.description: Optional {flag_name: bool} of engine show flags (Grid, Bounds, Collision, Fog...) set to that state

params.name: camera_speed
params.description: Optional camera movement speed, above 0

params.name: view_type
params.description: Optional: Perspective, Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Front or Back

params.name: game_view
params.description: Optional: game view on (editor-only icons and gizmos hidden) or off

params.name: allow_cinematic_control
params.description: Optional: whether Sequencer may drive this viewport's camera

commands.returns: { applied: { setting: that setting's reply }, failed?: { label, command, error } (when a setting is refused) }

commands.name: set_viewport_view_mode
commands.description: Set the rendering view mode (Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, ShaderComplexity...) of the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first; no viewport is an error. view_mode is matched without case. An unknown name is an error before anything changes, and so is a mode the editor only enters with a choice of what to show (a buffer, a visualization, texture streaming data, a zebra direction): the error says which. The mode is stored for the viewport's current projection only (perspective and orthographic keep separate modes) and lasts for this editor session: no undo step, nothing saved. view_mode and view_mode_index are read back, view_mode as the name get_viewport_state reports and this tool takes back. Show flags: set_show_flag; projection: set_view_type; game view: set_game_view.

params.name: view_mode
params.description: Engine view mode name, matched without case, e.g. Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, CSGWireframe, DetailLighting, LightingOnly, LightComplexity, ShaderComplexity, LightmapDensity, Reflections, PlayerCollision, MeshLODColoration, QuadOverdraw, Clay; each is the engine display name without spaces. BrushWireframe is accepted for Wireframe, ReflectionOverride for Reflections, RandomColor for Random; PathTracing only where ray tracing is allowed.

commands.returns: { applied: bool, requested: string, view_mode_index: int, view_mode: string }

commands.name: show_notification
commands.description: Show a transient toast in the editor through the Slate notification manager: message, an optional completion state icon and a lifetime in seconds, after which it fades on its own. completion_state is matched without case, and anything other than Pending, Success or Fail shows no state; the reply echoes it as sent, not as applied. Each call shows another toast, so it is not idempotent, and nothing else changes: no asset, log line or undo step. shown is false when the notification manager returned no toast, and the call still succeeds. An empty or missing message is an error. For a record that stays use print_to_output_log or add_message_log_entry.

params.name: message
params.description: The text to display in the notification; empty is an error.

params.name: completion_state
params.description: Completion state, case-insensitive: "None" (default), "Pending", "Success" or "Fail"; any other value counts as "None".

params.name: duration
params.description: Notification lifetime in seconds before it fades (default 4.0); the value is not validated.

commands.returns: { shown: bool, message: string, completion_state: string, duration: float }

commands.name: snap_actor_to_ground
commands.description: Drop ONE editor-world actor straight down until its bounds bottom rests on whatever is below -- meshes, BSP or the landscape. It line-traces first and, because headless traces routinely MISS the landscape, falls back to sampling the heightmap so the actor still lands; sampled_from tells you which path answered. Use snap_actor_to_landscape when the ground is definitely the landscape and you want no trace at all, execute_batch for many actors.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name of the actor to snap (editor world).

params.name: trace_distance
params.description: Optional downward trace distance in cm; defaults to 10000

params.name: align_to_surface
params.description: When true, rotate actor to match the surface normal (trace hits only; the heightmap fallback has no normal); defaults to false

params.name: fallback_heightmap
params.description: When true (default) and the downward line trace misses (headless traces routinely miss the landscape), fall back to sampling the landscape heightmap at the actor's XY (same sampler as snap_actor_to_landscape) so the actor still lands. Set false to require a real trace hit.

commands.returns: { actor: actor JSON, hit: bool, landed: bool, sampled_from: 'trace'|'heightmap', hit_actor?: string, hit_distance?: number }

commands.name: snap_actor_to_landscape
commands.description: Ground an actor on the landscape by sampling the heightmap at its XY (no line trace; traces miss the landscape headless). Sets the actor's Z so either its mesh bbox bottom or its origin sits at the sampled height + z_offset.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Internal name of the actor to place (Actor->GetName())

params.name: align
params.description: Optional 'mesh_bbox_bottom' (default; drops the lowest mesh-geometry point onto the ground) or 'actor_origin' (puts the actor origin at the ground)

params.name: z_offset
params.description: Optional extra world-Z added above the sampled ground height; defaults to 0

commands.returns: { actor: actor JSON, landed_z: number (sampled ground world-Z), previous_z: number, new_z: number, sampled_from: 'heightmap', in_bounds: bool, align: string, align_used: string, z_offset: number, landscape_actor_name: string }

commands.name: spawn_actor
commands.description: Place an actor of ANY placeable class -- a built-in short name (StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight, SkyLight, CameraActor, Character), another engine or plugin class by name or path (SkyAtmosphere, ExponentialHeightFog, VolumetricCloud, SceneCapture2D, TextRenderActor, NiagaraActor, /Script/Engine.DecalActor...) or a Blueprint asset path -- into the editor level or a live PIE world, at an optional location/rotation/scale, and set its properties in the same call: properties={"Prop": v} on the actor, {"Component.Prop": v} on a component named so or of a class only one component has (e.g. {"ExponentialHeightFogComponent.FogDensity": 0.05}), written as set_properties writes them. A volume needs a brush: spawn_box_volume places one; an abstract or non-placeable class is refused. Refuses a name an actor already has (omit name to let the engine pick a unique one); the spawn is undoable. A property that cannot be written makes the call fail with properties_failed while the actor stays, so fix it with set_properties or remove it with delete_actor. It creates the actor in MEMORY only -- save_level (with the .umap writable) puts it on disk. WARNING: with 2+ PIE clients world='pie' can land in the CLIENT world, producing an actor the authority never sees -- ask for world='server' instead, and check has_authority and world_package in the reply.

params.name: type
params.description: The actor class: a built-in short name (StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight, SkyLight, CameraActor, Character; a light also as Point, Spot, Directional, Rect or Sky), any other actor class by name or /Script path, or a Blueprint asset path (/Game/BP_Door). Volumes go through spawn_box_volume.

params.name: name
params.description: Optional internal name (and label) for the new actor; must be unused in the target world or the call is refused. When omitted the engine names the actor uniquely and the label is the class default.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional world location, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]; the origin when omitted. Any other value (an object, another length) is an error and nothing is spawned.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional world rotation as the array [pitch, yaw, roll] -- note index 2 is ROLL, not yaw -- or, unambiguously, the object {"pitch":..,"yaw":..,"roll":..}, which is the recommended form. Defaults to zero. Directional, spot and rect lights shine along its forward axis.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional world scale, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Defaults to 1,1,1; any other value (an object, another length) is an error and nothing is spawned.

params.name: static_mesh
params.description: Optional UStaticMesh asset path, only honoured for type=StaticMeshActor (e.g. /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube).

params.name: intensity
params.description: Optional, light types only: the light component's Intensity in the light's units (Directional: lux; Sky: a multiplier); engine default when omitted. Sent for a non-light type it is refused and nothing is spawned.

params.name: color
params.description: Optional, light types only: [r, g, b] linear color, usually 0..1; engine default (white) when omitted. Sent for a non-light type it is refused and nothing is spawned.

params.name: properties
params.description: Optional {"Prop": value, "Component.Prop": value} written after the spawn with set_properties' writer: engine property names, a struct as a JSON object of the fields to change.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector for WHERE the actor is spawned: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'game' (alias of 'pie') | 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- what you want for anything replicated) | 'client' | 'pie:N'. Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent spawn into the editor world.

commands.returns: { actor JSON via DescribeActorObject: name, class, location, rotation, scale, plus world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int, has_authority: bool, local_role: string, light_intensity?: number (light types: the intensity now on the component), light_color?: [r, g, b] (light types: the color now on the component), properties_set?: [string], properties_failed?: [{property, error}] (with properties) }

commands.name: undo
commands.description: Step the editor's undo stack back by one transaction, or by `count` of them, and report what is left, including next_undo (the label of the entry now on top). WARNING: `success` is ALWAYS true, including when there was nothing to undo -- the real oracle is `applied`, and with a count compare actually_undone against requested (the stack ran out, or an undo barrier stopped it); the honest verification is re-reading whatever you changed. Read get_undo_state first to look before you leap.

params.name: count
params.description: Optional. How many transactions to undo, at least 1 (default 1); stops early when the stack runs out or reaches an undo barrier. Below 1 is refused.

commands.returns: { applied: bool (THE oracle -- false means nothing was undone), requested: int, actually_undone: int (compare against requested), undo_count: int, can_undo: bool, next_undo: string (label of the next entry) }

commands.name: add_niagara_data_interface
commands.description: Add a new UNiagaraDataInterface user-parameter binding to a Niagara system, inside an undo transaction, request a recompile and save the system; success requires the save. A user parameter that already has this name and class is left as is (added false, already_exists true, nothing saved); one with this name and any other type is an error. The inverse is remove_niagara_data_interface.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Short name of the new user-parameter (no "User." prefix)

params.name: data_interface_class
params.description: Data interface class name (e.g. "StaticMesh", "Texture"): a loaded data interface class with that name, else /Script/Niagara.NiagaraDataInterface<Name>

commands.returns: { system_path: string, parameter_name: string, data_interface_class: string, data_interface_class_path?: string, offset?: int, added?: bool, already_exists?: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_niagara_emitter_from_template
commands.description: Add a copy of a template emitter to a Niagara system (canonical path).  Loads the template/parent UNiagaraEmitter asset and adds a standalone copy of it to the system via FNiagaraEditorUtilities::AddEmitterToSystem — the same operation the Niagara editor's "Add Emitter" performs. This rebuilds the emitter's nodes and syncs the system overview graph, optionally names the new handle, then requests a compile and saves the system.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. "/Game/Niagara/NS_Example")

params.name: emitter_asset_path
params.description: Asset path of the source UNiagaraEmitter template (e.g. "/Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters/Fountain.Fountain")

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Optional name for the new emitter handle; absent or empty keeps the name the engine generates from the source emitter. The engine sanitizes it and makes it unique among the system's emitters, so read emitter_handle_name for the stored name.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, source_emitter_asset: string, emitter_handle_id: string, emitter_handle_name: string, is_valid: bool, is_enabled: bool, emitters_before: int, total_emitters: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_niagara_event_handler
commands.description: Add an event handler to a Niagara emitter (the writer for event_handler_count).  Constructs an FNiagaraEventScriptProperties (allocating its UNiagaraScript with usage ParticleEventScript, mirroring add_niagara_simulation_stage) and adds it via UNiagaraEmitter::AddEventHandler. Idempotent by source_event_name: if a handler for that event already exists it is returned (already_exists=true) without adding a duplicate. A spawn_number, max_events_per_frame or min_spawn_number that is not a JSON number is an error and nothing changes. The system is saved after modification. The handler's event-script graph is created in a default state -- full event wiring must be completed in the Niagara editor (reported honestly via note); the handler properties are persisted and re-readable.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. "/Game/Niagara/NS_Example").

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle within the system.

params.name: source_event_name
params.description: Name of the source event this handler consumes (its identity key for idempotency).

params.name: execution_mode
params.description: Optional EveryParticle | SpawnedParticles | SingleParticle (default EveryParticle).

params.name: spawn_number
params.description: Optional int particles to spawn per event (SpawnedParticles mode).

params.name: max_events_per_frame
params.description: Optional int cap on events consumed per frame.

params.name: min_spawn_number
params.description: Optional int minimum spawn when random_spawn_number is set.

params.name: random_spawn_number
params.description: Optional bool: spawn a random count in [min_spawn_number, spawn_number].

params.name: source_emitter_id
params.description: Optional GUID of the emitter handle that generates the event (default: this emitter).

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, usage_id: string, source_event_name: string, execution_mode: string, spawn_number: int, max_events_per_frame: int, already_exists: bool, event_handler_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note: string }

commands.name: add_niagara_module_to_stack
commands.description: Insert an engine module script into a Niagara emitter's particle stack.  Loads the module UNiagaraScript and inserts it into the emitter's ParticleSpawn or ParticleUpdate stack via FNiagaraStackGraphUtilities::AddScriptModuleToStack, at the end or at a chosen target_index, then recompiles and saves. Not idempotent: every call adds another module node.  NOTE: only the module's script-default inputs are applied — per-instance input overrides are out of scope (the response reports added_with_defaults=true). Stateless emitters (no editable graph) return a clean error.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle to modify.

params.name: module_script_path
params.description: Asset path of the module UNiagaraScript (e.g. "/Niagara/Modules/Update/Forces/GravityForce.GravityForce")

params.name: script_group
params.description: Optional "spawn" (ParticleSpawnScript) or "update" (ParticleUpdateScript); defaults to "update"

params.name: target_index
params.description: Optional 0-based position in the stack; -1 (INDEX_NONE, the default) and any index past the end append. A value that is not a JSON number is an error.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, module_script_path: string, script_group: string, target_index: int, module_node_name: string, added_with_defaults: bool, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_niagara_renderer
commands.description: Add a new renderer (Sprite / Ribbon / Mesh / Light / Decal) to a Niagara emitter, optionally with its properties seeded in the same call.  Creates a UNiagaraRendererProperties instance of the requested concrete class inside the emitter, as the Niagara editor does, optionally sets the Material UPROPERTY and the supplied properties (the keys set_niagara_renderer_properties takes, converted and clamped by reflection; enum keys fire PostEditChangeProperty), and appends it to the emitter's RendererProperties array, in one undo step. A Light is seeded with affects_translucency and alpha_scales_brightness true (the engine defaults are false), as the dedicated light-renderer tool seeded it; properties overrides either. Then requests a system compile and saves the asset. verified is true when the renderer is in the emitter's list and resolves that emitter; properties reads the stored values back. Each call adds one more renderer. An unknown renderer_type, a material_path that does not load as a material, an unknown key in properties, a numeric property given something other than a JSON number, or a value that does not convert is an error and nothing is created. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the renderer kept in memory.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. "/Game/Niagara/NS_Example").

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Name of the emitter handle (the human-readable name in the system's emitter list).

params.name: renderer_type
params.description: One of "Sprite" / "Ribbon" / "Mesh" / "Light" / "Decal" (case-insensitive).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Optional asset path; sets the renderer's Material property (a class without one, such as Light, ignores it). If omitted, the renderer is added with a null material (still a valid empty renderer).

params.name: properties
params.description: Optional object of renderer properties to seed, with the keys and value forms of set_niagara_renderer_properties, e.g. {"radius_scale": 2, "use_inverse_squared_falloff": false, "color_add": {"X": 1, "Y": 0, "Z": 0}} for a Light (scales clamped at 0; affects_translucency and alpha_scales_brightness default to true) or {"decal_source_mode": "Emitter", "renderer_visibility": 1, "decal_screen_size_fade": 0.1} for a Decal. Keys the renderer class lacks are listed in not_applicable.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, renderer_type: string, renderer_class: string, renderer_index: int, material_path: string, applied: [string], not_applicable: [string], post_edit_fired: bool, properties: object, renderer_count: int, verified: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_niagara_simulation_stage
commands.description: Add a generic simulation stage (UNiagaraSimulationStageGeneric) to one emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, in one undo step, then save the system. The stage gets stage_name as its SimulationStageName, iterates over Particles with execute behavior Always and dispatch type OneD, and runs iteration_count times in a row (default 1), read back in iteration_count; its graph starts in a default state, to be wired in the Niagara editor. An iteration_count that is not a JSON number from 0 to 65535 (the range the runtime honors; 0 skips the stage; a fraction is rounded), or an unknown system or emitter, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the stage kept in memory. Change its other settings with set_niagara_simulation_stage_properties; list stages with get_niagara_simulation_stages.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name for the new simulation stage.

params.name: iteration_count
params.description: Optional number of times the stage runs in a row, from 0 to 65535 (rounded to a whole number); defaults to 1

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, stage_name: string, requested_iteration_count: int, iteration_count: int, total_simulation_stages: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_niagara_system
commands.description: Create an empty UNiagaraSystem asset at package_path/name and save it: its system spawn and update scripts are set up, but it has no emitters. Idempotent: a Niagara System already at that path is returned unchanged with created=false and already_exists=true, and nothing is saved; an asset of another class at that path is an error and nothing is written. Not an undo step. Next, add emitters with add_niagara_emitter_from_template, check the result with get_niagara_system_info or get_niagara_emitter_handles, and place it in a level with spawn_actor (type NiagaraActor). A failed save is an error, the new asset left in memory unsaved.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name, e.g. 'NS_Sparks'; package_path/name must form a valid long package name.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder as a long package path, e.g. '/Game/FX' (default /Game/Niagara); a trailing slash is ignored.

commands.returns: { system_name: string, asset_path: string, created: bool, already_exists?: bool, saved?: bool, save_error?: string, emitter_count: int }

commands.name: duplicate_niagara_emitter_handle
commands.description: Duplicate an emitter handle of a Niagara System asset under a new name, keeping its enabled state, in one undo step, then save the system. The source is found by display name (case-insensitive); an unknown system or source is an error and nothing changes. The stored name can differ from the one asked for, so read new_emitter_name. Returns the actual name and id of the copy plus total_emitters; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the copy kept in memory. Find handle names with get_niagara_emitter_handles; add an emitter asset instead with add_niagara_emitter_from_template; rename the copy with rename_niagara_emitter_handle.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire"; the call fails without it.

params.name: source_emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle to copy (case-insensitive), as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it.

params.name: new_emitter_name
params.description: Name for the copy (default "<source_emitter_name>_Copy").

commands.returns: { system_path: string, source_emitter_name: string, new_emitter_name: string, new_emitter_id: string, is_valid: bool, total_emitters: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: duplicate_niagara_module_in_stack
commands.description: Add another instance of a module to one emitter of a Niagara System asset: the module named module_name (its function name, case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives it) is found on the script_group stack only (spawn or update, any case, default update) and its script is added again to that stack through FNiagaraStackGraphUtilities::AddScriptModuleToStack, in one undo step, then a system compile is requested and the system saved. The new module starts with the default inputs of the script; the input overrides of the source are not copied. Positions are stack positions, as list_niagara_modules reports index: target_index_override sets it (clamped into the stack, -1 appends), else it goes right after the source. inserted_index is read back from the stack, and a module that did not land where asked fails the call. An unknown system, emitter, script_group or module (or a module only on the other stack) is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Inputs: set_niagara_module_input; move: reorder_niagara_modules.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Content path of the UNiagaraSystem asset, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle, as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it.

params.name: module_name
params.description: Function name of the module to duplicate, case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives module_name for that stack, e.g. 'GravityForce'.

params.name: script_group
params.description: Optional "spawn" or "update" (any case), the stack the module is on; defaults to "update"; any other value is an error and nothing changes.

params.name: target_index_override
params.description: Optional stack position for the new module, a JSON number (0 runs first; -1 appends; others are clamped into the stack); defaults to the source's stack index plus one.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, source_module_name: string, source_index: int, new_module_name: string, inserted_index: int, module_count: int, duplicated: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: get_editor_status
commands.description: Prove the Unreal editor is alive and TICKING: a no-argument game-thread liveness/health probe, and the first call to make when the MCP bridge goes quiet. It runs on the GAME THREAD via the bridge's command drain, so a reply proves the game thread is pumping -- unlike a transport-only ping, which a wedged editor still answers. After a "Connection reset" use it to tell an editor CRASH (this errors, the reconnect refuses) from a mere tool TIMEOUT (this returns alive=true); call it twice and diff frame_counter to rule out a deadlock, since a frozen game thread replies once but never advances the frame (frame_count_render_thread is the render thread's own counter). Also reports whether PIE is running (pie_active / is_simulating) and the open editor world, without starting or stopping anything. Read-only and cheap; safe to call any time.
commands.returns: { alive: bool, gis_running: bool, exit_requested: bool, is_editor: bool, frame_counter: number, frame_count_render_thread: number, pie_active: bool, is_simulating: bool, editor_world: string, world_context_count: int }

commands.name: get_engine_info
commands.description: Read the GEngine object (engine_name, engine_class), the live UGameInstance (name, class, object path) and every world context with its world_name, world_type (Editor/PIE/Game/...) and has_game_instance flag. Use it to see how many worlds exist at once -- in co-op PIE the host and each client are SEPARATE world contexts, so this is how you confirm two PIE worlds are up before reading state that must be checked on both sides -- and which GameInstance class a running session picked. A UGameInstance only exists while PIE or a game world runs, so at rest game_instance_exists=false with empty strings is the normal answer, not an error. get_editor_status is the cheaper "is the editor alive" probe. Read-only.
commands.returns: { engine_name: string, engine_class: string, game_instance_exists: bool, game_instance_name: string, game_instance_class: string, game_instance_path: string, world_context_count: int, worlds: [{ world_name, world_type, has_game_instance }] }

commands.name: get_niagara_component_matrix
commands.description: Reads a Matrix (FMatrix4f) override parameter back off a spawned Niagara component — the round-trip reader for set_niagara_component_variable. UNiagaraComponent exposes no GetNiagaraVariableMatrix, so this reads the value straight out of the component's OverrideParameters store (FNiagaraParameterStore) by looking up the Matrix4 FNiagaraVariable; the override is stored as FMatrix44f. Returns found:false with an empty matrix (never a faked identity) when the variable has no local override on the component.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Owner actor identifier (internal name or editor label).

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Niagara variable name to read.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, variable_name: string, variable_type: string, found: bool, matrix: [number x 16] }

commands.name: get_niagara_data_interfaces
commands.description: List the data interfaces bound to a Niagara System's user parameters (the User.* parameters of a data interface type, such as a static mesh or texture DI), or only the one named parameter_name, without changing anything: per binding its user parameter, the DI object and class, and the name and property class of each UPROPERTY (Transient and DuplicateTransient ones skipped; names and types only, no values). This is the system-level list: for the DIs set on module inputs inside one emitter's stacks use get_niagara_emitter_data_interfaces, and for every user parameter, DI or not, get_niagara_system_info. Add a DI with add_niagara_data_interface, point it at an asset with set_niagara_data_interface_asset, set its other fields with set_niagara_data_interface_default. A parameter_name that is not a data interface user parameter of the system, or a system that does not load, is an error; a system with none is a success with count 0. parameter_name in the reply is the short name the other data interface tools take; index is the DI's slot in the system's exposed-parameter store.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset, package or object path, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks' or '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks.NS_Sparks'.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Short name of one data interface user parameter, e.g. 'SourceMesh'; a leading "User." is dropped and case is ignored. Omit it to list every binding.
