commands.returns: { system_path: string, count: int, data_interfaces: [{ index, parameter_name, object_name, data_interface_class, data_interface_class_path, path_name, properties: [{ name, type }], property_count: int }] }

commands.name: get_niagara_effect_type
commands.description: Read which Niagara Effect Type asset a Niagara System asset uses, plus that effect type's settings: update_frequency and cull_reaction (as enum value names), allows_culling (bAllowCullingForLocalPlayers), and the scalability limits of its first system and emitter scalability entries: max_distance and max_instances (system), cull_by_distance (max_distance above 0) and scale_spawn_count (emitter SpawnCountScale). A system with no effect type, or an effect type without those entries, is a success with the defaults: an empty effect_type_path, None for both enums, allows_culling false, max_distance 0, max_instances 0, cull_by_distance false and scale_spawn_count 1. Read-only; an unknown system path is an error. Assign one with set_properties; the system's own flags and fixed bounds: get_properties.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire" (the object path form also works).

commands.returns: { system_path: string, effect_type_path: string, update_frequency: string, cull_reaction: string, allows_culling: bool, max_distance: number, max_instances: int, cull_by_distance: bool, scale_spawn_count: number }

commands.name: get_niagara_emitter_data_interfaces
commands.description: List the data interfaces one emitter of a Niagara System asset uses in its stacks: every data-interface input set on a module (a curve, a color curve, a static mesh, a vector field...), each with its input name, data interface class and object path and the stack it feeds (script_usage: particle_spawn, particle_update, emitter_spawn, emitter_update, particle_event, simulation_stage, or unconnected). Read from the emitter graph, so nothing needs compiling; read-only, it changes nothing. Data interfaces used only inside a module's own script are not listed. The emitter's Emitter Dependencies setting comes back separately as emitter_dependencies (emitter_name, binding_mode Self or Other). For the system's user-parameter data interfaces use get_niagara_data_interfaces (add_niagara_data_interface adds one); list_niagara_modules lists the modules. An emitter with none gives empty lists; a missing system or emitter handle is an error.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Content path of the UNiagaraSystem asset, package or object form, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle, as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it, e.g. 'Fountain'.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, data_interface_count: int, data_interfaces: [{ name, class, data_interface_path, script_usage, script_usages: [string] }], emitter_dependency_count: int, emitter_dependencies: [{ emitter_name, binding_mode }], note?: string }

commands.name: get_niagara_emitter_handles
commands.description: List every emitter handle of a Niagara System asset, or just one chosen by display name or 0-based index, with its display name, id GUID, id name, enabled and valid flags, version GUID and, when it has emitter data, its local-space and deprecated flags, plus emitter_count (all handles of the system). Read-only; the names feed the other emitter tools. A name or index that matches no handle, or an emitter_index that is not a JSON number, is an error.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire"; the call fails without it.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Optional display name of one handle to return (case-insensitive); when non-empty it wins over emitter_index.

params.name: emitter_index
params.description: Optional 0-based position in the emitter list of the system of one handle to return, used only when emitter_name is absent or empty.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_count: int, emitter_handles: [{ index: int, name: string, id: string, id_name: string, is_enabled: bool, is_valid: bool, emitter_version: string, is_local_space?: bool, is_deprecated?: bool }] }

commands.name: get_niagara_emitter_renderers
commands.description: List every renderer of one emitter in a Niagara System asset, in stack order, without changing anything: per renderer its 0-based index, class (Sprite, Mesh, Ribbon, Light, Decal...), object name and material path, the authored fields set_niagara_renderer_properties writes (bIsEnabled, SortOrderHint, MotionVectorSetting, bAllowInCullProxies plus the Sprite, Mesh, Light or Decal fields the class has) and, for a Mesh renderer, its static-mesh slots. Use it to find the renderer_index the renderer tools take; for every property of one renderer use get_niagara_renderer_info. Change a renderer with set_niagara_renderer_properties, set_niagara_renderer_material or set_niagara_mesh_renderer_mesh, add one with add_niagara_renderer, take one out with remove_niagara_renderer. An unknown system or emitter name is an error; an emitter with no renderers is a success with renderer_count 0.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset, package or object path, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle in that system, case ignored, e.g. 'Sparks', as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, renderer_count: int, renderers: [{ index, class, display_name, material_path, properties:{...}, meshes?:[{ slot, mesh_path }] }] }

commands.name: get_niagara_emitter_runtime_summary
commands.description: Read one emitter of a Niagara System asset in a single flat reply: simulation target (CPUSim or GPUComputeSim), bounds mode (Dynamic, Fixed or Programmable) and its fixed box as 'X=.. Y=.. Z=..' strings, particle allocation mode and pre-allocation count, GPU spawn cap per frame (max_gpu_particles), local-space, determinism and persistent-ID flags, how many renderers, event handlers and simulation stages it has, and how many modules each stack holds. Read-only: it changes nothing and compiles nothing. Module counts are per stack, read from the chain that ends at each stack's output node: spawn_module_count and update_module_count for particle spawn and update, emitter_spawn_module_count and emitter_update_module_count, event_module_count over all event handlers and simulation_stage_module_count over all stages; dynamic inputs are not counted, disabled modules are, and graph_function_call_count counts every function-call node of the emitter graph. list_niagara_modules lists modules by name. A missing system or emitter handle is an error. Change these settings with set_niagara_emitter_properties.

params.description: Content path of the UNiagaraSystem asset, package or object form, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle, as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it, e.g. 'Fountain'.

For the emitter's renderers use get_niagara_emitter_renderers, for its simulation stages get_niagara_simulation_stages. An unknown system or emitter name is an error; an emitter with no handlers is a success with event_handler_count 0.

commands.name: get_niagara_system_properties

commands.name: list_niagara_data_interface_classes
commands.description: Enumerate every concrete UNiagaraDataInterface subclass registered in this process via TObjectIterator. Skips Abstract (those are base classes only). Used to discover what data-interface class strings are valid for add_niagara_data_interface.

commands.name: list_niagara_modules
commands.description: List the modules of one stack, or both stacks, of a Niagara emitter in execution order (read-only), optionally just the module with a given name. script_group picks the particle spawn or update stack (default "update"; "all" reads both and also groups them as spawn[] and update[]); a stack's modules are the function-call nodes on its parameter-map chain from its input to its output node, so the other stack's modules and the dynamic inputs feeding module inputs are not listed, while disabled modules are. Each entry: index (its position in its stack, 0 runs first, the index reorder_niagara_modules and add_niagara_module_to_stack take), module_name (GetFunctionName), node_guid, function_script(+class), is_enabled (IsNodeEnabled), is_deprecated, input/output pin counts. Honest-empty modules:[] when the stack has no modules or the graph is not resolvable (a note is returned); a module_name that matches no module is an error.

params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Name of the emitter handle.

params.name: script_group
params.description: Optional "spawn", "update" or "all" (both stacks); defaults to "update".

params.name: module_name
params.description: Optional module name (GetFunctionName, case-sensitive): return only that module; an error when no module of the stack(s) has it.

commands.returns: { count: int, classes: [{class_name, class_path, display_name, abstract, class_flags}] }

commands.name: move_niagara_simulation_stage
commands.description: Move one simulation stage of an emitter of a Niagara System asset to target_index, its 0-based place in the stage list, in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. The stage is found by stage_index (preferred) or stage_name (its SimulationStageName, case-insensitive); one is required. A stage that is not found, a target_index missing or outside the current list, a stage_index or target_index that is not a JSON number, or an unknown system or emitter is an error and nothing changes. Idempotent: a stage already at target_index is a success with moved=false, already_at_target=true and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. List stages with get_niagara_simulation_stages; take one out with remove_niagara_simulation_stage.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle owning the stage.

params.name: target_index
params.description: Required 0-based target index the stage should occupy after the move, a JSON number in [0, total_simulation_stages).

params.name: stage_index
params.description: Optional 0-based index into the emitter's simulation stages, a JSON number; takes precedence over stage_name when both are supplied.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Optional SimulationStageName to match if stage_index is not supplied.

commands.returns: { system_path, emitter_name, stage_index, stage_name, stage_class, target_index, moved, already_at_target, before_index, after_index, total_simulation_stages, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: remove_niagara_data_interface
commands.description: Remove a UNiagaraDataInterface user-parameter binding from a Niagara system by name, inside an undo transaction, request a recompile and save the system; success requires the save. A name with no user parameter, or a user parameter that is not a data interface, is an error and nothing is changed.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Short name of the user-parameter to remove (no "User." prefix)

commands.returns: { system_path: string, parameter_name: string, data_interface_class: string, removed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_niagara_emitter_handle
commands.description: Remove one emitter handle from a Niagara System asset in one undo step, then save the system. The handle is chosen by display name (case-insensitive) or, when emitter_name is absent or empty, by 0-based emitter_index. An unknown system, name or index, or an emitter_index that is not a JSON number, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. Returns the removed name and id and the emitter counts before and after. List handles with get_niagara_emitter_handles; to keep an emitter but stop it, use set_niagara_emitter_properties.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Optional display name of the emitter handle to remove

params.name: emitter_index
params.description: Optional zero-based index; used if emitter_name not provided

commands.returns: { system_path: string, removed_emitter_name: string, removed_emitter_id: string, emitters_before: int, emitters_after: int, removed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_niagara_event_handler
commands.description: Remove an event handler from a Niagara emitter by its usage_id.  Calls UNiagaraEmitter::RemoveEventHandlerByUsageId. Idempotent: if no handler with that usage_id exists it reports already_removed without error. The system is saved after a removal.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle within the system.

params.name: usage_id
params.description: The handler's usage_id (as returned by add_niagara_event_handler / get_niagara_event_handlers).

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, usage_id: string, already_removed: bool, removed: bool, event_handler_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_niagara_module_from_stack
commands.description: Remove one module from a Niagara emitter's particle spawn or update stack, in one undo step: the module and every node that feeds it (its input overrides, dynamic inputs and data-interface inputs) are taken out and the stack's chain is closed over the gap, then a system compile is requested and the system saved. The module is found by function name (case-sensitive) on the script_group stack only, the first one in execution order, as list_niagara_modules lists it. The result is read back: removed is true when the module is off the stack and the stack is one module shorter, chain_intact when the stack still runs from its input to its output node; either false fails the call. An unknown system, emitter, script_group or module (or a module only on the other stack) is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. The inverse is add_niagara_module_to_stack.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Content path of the UNiagaraSystem asset, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle, as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it.

params.name: module_name
params.description: Function name of the module to remove, case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives module_name for that stack, e.g. 'GravityForce'.

params.name: script_group
params.description: Optional "spawn" or "update" (any case), the stack the module is on; defaults to "update"; any other value is an error and nothing changes.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, module_name: string, removed_index: int, removed_node_count: int, module_count: int, chain_intact: bool, removed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_niagara_renderer
commands.description: Take the renderer at renderer_index (0-based, in get_niagara_emitter_renderers order) out of one emitter of a Niagara System asset, in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. renderer_index is required and must be a JSON number of 0 or more; an index out of range, an empty renderer slot, or an unknown system or emitter is an error and nothing changes. The renderers after it move down one index. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. Returns the class of the renderer taken out and the count left. Add one with add_niagara_renderer; change one with set_niagara_renderer_properties.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Name of the emitter handle.

params.name: renderer_index
params.description: 0-based index into the emitter's renderers list, a JSON number (use get_niagara_emitter_renderers to find the index)

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, removed_renderer_index: int, removed_renderer_class: string, renderer_count_after: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_niagara_simulation_stage
commands.description: Remove one simulation stage from an emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by stage_index (0-based, preferred) or stage_name (its SimulationStageName, case-insensitive), in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. One of the two is required, and a stage_index that is not a JSON number is an error. Idempotent: a stage that is not found (an index out of range falls back to stage_name) is a success with removed=false, already_removed=true and saved=false, nothing written. An unknown system or emitter is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. List stages with get_niagara_simulation_stages; reorder them with move_niagara_simulation_stage; add one with add_niagara_simulation_stage.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle owning the stage.

params.name: stage_index
params.description: Optional 0-based index into the emitter's simulation stages, a JSON number; takes precedence over stage_name when both are supplied.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Optional SimulationStageName to match if stage_index is not supplied (matches add_niagara_simulation_stage's name).

commands.returns: { system_path, emitter_name, stage_index, stage_name, stage_class, removed, already_removed, total_simulation_stages, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: remove_niagara_user_parameter
commands.description: Remove one plain user parameter (the User. namespace: a float, int, bool, vector, color...) from a Niagara System asset, in one undo step; the asset is marked dirty, not saved, as set_niagara_user_parameter leaves it (save_asset keeps it). Inverse of set_niagara_user_parameter, which adds the parameter when it is missing. A data interface user parameter is refused (remove_niagara_data_interface removes those), and so is a name the system has no user parameter for, with nothing changed. The reply re-reads the store (still_present). Read: get_niagara_user_parameter.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: User parameter name (without the "User." prefix).

commands.returns: { system_path: string, parameter_name: string, parameter_type: string, removed: bool, still_present: bool }

commands.name: rename_niagara_emitter_handle
commands.description: Rename an emitter handle of a Niagara System asset in one undo step, then save the system. The engine sanitizes the name and makes it unique among the emitters of the system, so read new_name and verified (false when the stored name differs from the request). A name the engine takes as the current one (the same after sanitizing, case-sensitive, ignoring a trailing number) is a success with renamed=false and saved=false, and nothing is written. An unknown system or current_name is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. List names with get_niagara_emitter_handles; copy a handle under a new name with duplicate_niagara_emitter_handle.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire"; the call fails without it.

params.name: current_name
params.description: Current display name of the emitter handle (case-insensitive), as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it.

params.name: new_name
params.description: Requested display name; it may come back sanitized or with a numeric suffix.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, old_name: string, new_name: string, verified: bool, renamed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: reorder_niagara_modules
commands.description: Move one module of a Niagara emitter's particle spawn or update stack to another position in that same stack, changing its execution order: the module, with its input overrides and linked inputs, is taken out of the stack's parameter-map chain and put back at target_index, in one undo step, then a system compile is requested and the system saved. The module is found by function name (case-sensitive) on the script_group stack only; positions count that stack's modules in execution order, exactly as list_niagara_modules reports index. target_index past the last is clamped to it. new_index is read back from the rewired chain. A module already at that position changes nothing: reordered false, saved false and a note. An unknown system, emitter, script_group or module (or a module only on the other stack) is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Insert a new module at a position: add_niagara_module_to_stack with target_index.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Content path of the UNiagaraSystem asset, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle, as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it.

params.name: module_name
params.description: Function name of the module to move, case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives module_name for that stack, e.g. 'GravityForce'.

params.name: target_index
params.description: New position in the stack, a JSON number of 0 or more (0 runs first), counted as list_niagara_modules counts index; clamped to the last; the call fails without it.

params.name: script_group
params.description: Optional "spawn" or "update" (any case), the stack the module is on; defaults to "update"; any other value is an error.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, module_name: string, old_index: int, new_index: int, target_index: int, module_count: int, reordered: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_component_bool
commands.description: Sets a bool override parameter on a spawned Niagara component.  Resolves the UNiagaraComponent on the owner actor and calls SetVariableBool, then reads it back.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Owner actor identifier (internal name or editor label).

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Niagara variable name (override is added locally if needed).

params.name: value
params.description: Bool value to set.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, variable_name: string, variable_type: string, set: bool, verified: bool, value_read_back: bool }

commands.name: set_niagara_component_color
commands.description: Set a LinearColor override (a user parameter value) on the Niagara component of an actor in the editor world, the actor found by internal name or editor label and the first UNiagaraComponent on it used, through UNiagaraComponent::SetVariableLinearColor, which adds the override when needed. color is [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] in numbers within the float range; an omitted alpha is 1 and an omitted color is opaque black. Any other color, a missing actor_name or variable_name, or an actor without a Niagara component is an error and nothing changes. The value is set on the component in memory with no undo step; the level is neither marked dirty nor saved. verified is whether GetVariableColor finds the variable, and value_read_back is what it reads. Four plain components: set_niagara_component_vec4; the asset default: set_niagara_user_parameter.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Owner actor identifier (internal name or editor label).

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Niagara variable name (override is added locally if needed).

params.name: color
params.description: Color as [R, G, B] or [R, G, B, A], numbers within the float range; A is 1.0 when omitted, and an omitted color is opaque black. Any other value is an error.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, variable_name: string, variable_type: string, set: bool, verified: bool, value_read_back: [number, number, number, number] }

commands.name: set_niagara_component_fixed_bounds
commands.description: Set the fixed-bounds override of the Niagara component on a placed actor in the editor world (the first UNiagaraComponent of the actor found by internal name or label) to the local-space box min..max, then read it back. The override is runtime state of that component (UNiagaraComponent::SetSystemFixedBounds): the engine stores it in a member that is not a saved property, in 5.7 and 5.8 alike, and a component has no fixed-bounds field in its details panel, so it is lost when the level reloads and is not carried into PIE; it makes no undo step and does not dirty the level. Repeating the call with the same box gives the same result. An actor that is missing or has no Niagara component is an error and nothing changes. For bounds that persist, write the System asset's Fixed Bounds (bFixedBounds and FixedBounds, with set_properties) or an emitter's with set_niagara_emitter_properties (bounds_mode Fixed); place a Niagara actor with spawn_actor (type NiagaraActor).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Internal name or editor label of an actor in the editor world that has a Niagara component, as get_actors_in_level lists it, e.g. 'NiagaraActor_0'.

params.name: min
params.description: Box minimum corner in the component's local space, [x, y, z] in centimetres, e.g. [-500, -500, 0]; a missing or short array reads as [0, 0, 0], and it is not checked against max.

params.name: max
params.description: Box maximum corner in the component's local space, [x, y, z] in centimetres, e.g. [500, 500, 800]; a missing or short array reads as [0, 0, 0].

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, applied: bool, bounds_valid: bool, min_read_back: [number, number, number], max_read_back: [number, number, number] }

commands.name: set_niagara_component_float
commands.description: Set a float override (a user parameter value) on the Niagara component of an actor in the editor world, the actor found by internal name or editor label and the first UNiagaraComponent on it used, through UNiagaraComponent::SetVariableFloat, which adds the override when the component has none of that name. value is required and must be a JSON number; a missing or mistyped value, a missing actor_name or variable_name, or an actor without a Niagara component is an error and nothing changes. The value is set on the component in memory with no undo step; the level is neither marked dirty nor saved. verified is whether GetVariableFloat finds the variable, and value_read_back is what it reads. Spawn a component with spawn_niagara_component; whole numbers: set_niagara_component_int; the asset default: set_niagara_user_parameter.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Owner actor identifier (internal name or editor label).

params.name: variable_name
params.description: Niagara variable name (override is added locally if needed).

params.name: value
params.description: Float value to set, a JSON number; the call fails without it.

commands.name: set_niagara_component_int

The value is set on the component in memory with no undo step; the level is neither marked dirty nor saved. The component has no public getter for this type, so nothing is read back: verified is always true and note says so. The override is added locally when the component has none for that name. One undo step; nothing is saved (save_level for a placed actor). The fixed bounds of the component are set_niagara_component_fixed_bounds; a parameter's default in the system asset is set_niagara_user_parameter.

commands.name: set_niagara_data_interface_array
commands.description: Replace the contents of a numeric array on an array user-parameter data interface of a Niagara System asset (FloatData by default, IntData on the int32 array DI) with values, in an undo transaction that records the DI, then request a recompile and save the system; success requires the save. Every value must be a finite JSON number; an int array stores it truncated toward zero. A value of another type, an unknown system or data interface, an array_property the DI lacks, or an array of structs (Vector, Color, Position) is an error and nothing changes. There is no no-op check: the same values are written and saved again. The reply reads the stored array back. The DI must exist (add_niagara_data_interface); curve DIs: set_niagara_data_interface_curve; inspect it with get_niagara_data_interfaces.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Short name of the user-parameter array DI (no "User." prefix)

params.name: values
params.description: Array of finite JSON numbers to store (replaces all existing array contents); any other element is an error

params.name: array_property
params.description: Optional array UPROPERTY to set (default "FloatData"; e.g. "IntData" for the int32 array DI)

commands.returns: { system_path: string, parameter_name: string, array_property: string, element_type: string, count: int, values: [number], set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_data_interface_asset
commands.description: Points an object property of a user-parameter data interface on a Niagara system at an asset (e.g. the mesh of a StaticMesh DI, the texture of a Texture DI), inside an undo transaction, reads it back, requests a system recompile and saves the system; success requires the read-back and the save. The DI must already exist (add_niagara_data_interface); property_name picks the property, else the first hard object property in reflection order. The asset must load and be of the property's class, else it is an error and nothing is written. For non-asset fields use set_niagara_data_interface_default.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Short name of the user-parameter DI to mutate

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path of the UObject to assign (must be the right subclass)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional FObjectProperty name on the DI; defaults to the first FObjectProperty

commands.returns: { system_path: string, parameter_name: string, property_name: string, asset_path: string, set: bool (the property reads back the asset), saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_data_interface_curve
commands.description: Replaces all keys of one FRichCurve property on a curve user-parameter data interface of a Niagara system with the given time/value keys (an empty array clears it), rebuilds the DI's lookup table, requests a recompile and saves the system, inside an undo transaction that records the DI; success requires the save. The DI must already exist (add_niagara_data_interface) and curve_property must name an FRichCurve on it: Curve by default, XCurve/YCurve/ZCurve (WCurve too on Vector4) on vector curve DIs, RedCurve/GreenCurve/BlueCurve/AlphaCurve on color curve DIs. Every key must be an object whose time and value are finite JSON numbers, or it is an error and nothing changes. For array DIs use set_niagara_data_interface_array.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Short name of the user-parameter curve DI (no "User." prefix)

params.name: keys
params.description: Array of { time: number, value: number } keys to set (replaces all existing keys on the channel)

params.name: curve_property
params.description: Optional FRichCurve UPROPERTY to author (default "Curve"; e.g. "RedCurve"/"XCurve" on Color/Vector curve DIs)

commands.returns: { system_path: string, parameter_name: string, curve_property: string, key_count: int, keys: [{time,value}], set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_data_interface_default
commands.description: Writes one property of a user-parameter data interface on a Niagara system from text parsed by the property's ImportText, so any type it accepts works ("1.5", "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)", "(R=1,G=0,B=0,A=1)", an enum name), inside an undo transaction, then requests a system recompile and saves the system; success requires the save. A missing DI or property, or text that does not parse, is an error and the DI is left untouched. value echoes the request; value_read_back is the stored value exported as text. List the DI's properties with get_niagara_data_interfaces; for asset references use set_niagara_data_interface_asset.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Short name of the user-parameter DI to mutate

params.name: property_name
params.description: Name of the FProperty on the DI to set

params.name: value
params.description: String representation of the value (parsed by FProperty::ImportText_Direct)

commands.returns: { system_path: string, parameter_name: string, property_name: string, value: string, value_read_back: string, set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_effect_type
commands.description: Assign a Niagara Effect Type asset (the scalability and culling settings) to a Niagara System asset in one undo step, then save the system. effect_type_path is loaded as a UNiagaraEffectType; an unknown system or effect type is an error and nothing changes. A system that already uses that effect type is a success with changed=false and saved=false, and nothing is written. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Read it back, with the effect type's limits, with get_niagara_effect_type.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: effect_type_path
params.description: Asset path of the UNiagaraEffectType to assign.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, effect_type_path: string, success: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_emitter_allocation_mode
commands.description: Set how one emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, sizes its particle buffers (EParticleAllocationMode AutomaticEstimate, ManualEstimate or FixedCount; Automatic, Manual and Fixed also work, case-insensitive) and optionally its PreAllocationCount, in one undo step, then save the system. A negative pre_allocation_count is stored as 0. An unknown mode, a pre_allocation_count that is not a JSON number, or an unknown system or emitter is an error and nothing changes. Values already in place are a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Read back with get_niagara_emitter_runtime_summary; the GPU spawn limit: set_niagara_emitter_max_gpu_particles.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Name of the emitter handle.

params.name: allocation_mode
params.description: One of "AutomaticEstimate", "ManualEstimate", or "FixedCount" (case-insensitive; "Automatic" and "Manual" and "Fixed" also accepted)

params.name: pre_allocation_count
params.description: Optional int, the particle count to allocate up front; a negative one is stored as 0. Only meaningful when not AutomaticEstimate

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, allocation_mode: string, pre_allocation_count: int, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_emitter_bounds
commands.description: Set how one emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, computes its bounds (bounds_mode Dynamic, Fixed or Programmable, case-insensitive, default Fixed) and optionally its fixed box, in one undo step, then save the system. bounds_min and bounds_max are FVector strings like "X=-50 Y=-50 Z=0", not arrays; one alone keeps the other corner. With neither, Fixed resets the box to the engine default (-100 to 100 per axis) and the other modes keep it; min <= max is not checked. An unknown mode, system or emitter, or a corner without X=, Y= and Z=, is an error and nothing changes. A mode and box already in place are a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Read back with get_niagara_emitter_runtime_summary; for a placed Niagara component use set_niagara_component_fixed_bounds.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire" (the object path form also works).

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Emitter handle name as shown in the system, e.g. "Sparks" (case-insensitive).

params.name: bounds_mode
params.description: One of "Dynamic", "Fixed", or "Programmable"; defaults to "Fixed"

params.name: bounds_min
params.description: Optional FixedBounds minimum corner as an FVector string, e.g. "X=-50 Y=-50 Z=0" (the format the reply echoes); all three X=, Y= and Z= keys are needed, so "[x, y, z]" is an error.

params.name: bounds_max
params.description: Optional FixedBounds maximum corner as an FVector string, e.g. "X=50 Y=50 Z=100"; same format and rules as bounds_min.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, bounds_mode: string, bounds_min: string, bounds_max: string, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_emitter_enabled
commands.description: Enable or disable one emitter handle of a Niagara System asset, found by display name (case-insensitive), in one undo step, then save the system. enabled defaults to true. A handle already in that state is a success with state_changed=false and saved=false, and nothing is written. An unknown system or emitter is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. verified compares the state read back with the request. List handles and their states with get_niagara_emitter_handles; take an emitter out for good with remove_niagara_emitter_handle.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Optional bool; defaults to true

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, enabled: bool, state_changed: bool, verified: bool, is_enabled_read_back: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_emitter_max_gpu_particles
commands.description: Set the MaxGPUParticlesSpawnPerFrame override of one emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, in one undo step, then save the system; it limits the particles a GPU emitter spawns per frame and only takes effect when the sim target is GPUComputeSim (effective_for_current_sim says whether it is now). max_gpu_particles is required and must be a JSON number of 0 or more; a negative count, or an unknown system or emitter, is an error and nothing changes. A count already in place is a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Read back with get_niagara_emitter_runtime_summary; switch the sim target with set_niagara_emitter_sim_target.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Name of the emitter handle.

params.name: max_gpu_particles
params.description: Particles the emitter may spawn per frame on the GPU, an integer >= 0; the call fails without it

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, sim_target: string, max_gpu_particles: int, effective_for_current_sim: bool, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_emitter_properties
commands.description: Change any settings of ONE emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, in one call: enabled, simulation target (CPU or GPU), local space, determinism, bounds mode and fixed box, particle allocation mode and pre-allocation count, GPU particle cap and persistent IDs. Pass only the settings to change; each is validated and applied by its own step, in the order listed here, the system recompiled where the setting needs it and saved, and the call stops at the first setting refused, with applied listing those already changed. System-level settings (warmup, effect type, determinism of the system) are properties of the system asset: set_properties with save=true. get_niagara_emitter_info reads an emitter back.

params.description: Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire"

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Emitter handle name as shown in the system (case-insensitive)

params.name: enabled
params.description: Optional: enable or disable the emitter handle

params.name: sim_target
params.description: Optional: "CPUSim" or "GPUComputeSim"

params.name: local_space
params.description: Optional: simulate particles in the emitter's local space (true) or world space (false)

params.name: deterministic
params.description: Optional: the emitter's determinism flag

params.name: bounds_mode
params.description: Optional: "Dynamic", "Fixed" or "Programmable"

params.name: bounds_min
params.description: Optional fixed-bounds minimum corner as an FVector string, e.g. "X=-50 Y=-50 Z=0"

params.name: bounds_max
params.description: Optional fixed-bounds maximum corner as an FVector string, e.g. "X=50 Y=50 Z=100"

params.name: allocation_mode
params.description: Optional: "AutomaticEstimate", "ManualEstimate" or "FixedCount"

params.name: pre_allocation_count
params.description: Optional particle count to allocate up front; needs allocation_mode

params.name: max_gpu_particles
params.description: Optional cap on GPU particles (0 = no cap)

params.name: requires_persistent_ids
params.description: Optional: whether particles carry persistent IDs

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, applied: { setting: that setting's reply }, failed?: { label, command, error } (when a setting is refused) }

commands.name: set_niagara_emitter_requires_persistent_ids
commands.description: Set whether one emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, gives its particles persistent IDs (bRequiresPersistentIDs: a Particles.ID stable across frames, at a small cost), in one undo step, then save the system. requires_persistent_ids is required. A value already in place is a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. A missing param or an unknown system or emitter is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Returns the flag as read back; read it later with get_niagara_emitter_runtime_summary; local space: set_niagara_emitter_sim_target with local_space.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Name of the emitter handle.

params.name: requires_persistent_ids

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, requires_persistent_ids: bool, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.description: Set the simulation target (CPUSim or GPUComputeSim, case-insensitive), the local-space flag (bLocalSpace: particles in the emitter's space, or world space) and the deterministic flag of one emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, in one undo step, then save the system. Each of the three is optional and only the supplied ones are written, but at least one is required. Values already in place are a success with changed=false and saved=false, and nothing is written. An unknown sim_target, system or emitter, or a call with none of the three, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Returns the three as read back. Read them back with get_niagara_emitter_runtime_summary; GPU spawn limit: set_niagara_emitter_max_gpu_particles.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle.

params.name: sim_target
params.description: Optional target type, "CPUSim" or "GPUComputeSim"; omitted keeps the current one.

commands.name: set_niagara_emitter_template_description
commands.description: Set the TemplateAssetDescription text (shown when the emitter is picked as a template) of a standalone Niagara Emitter asset, not an emitter inside a system, in one undo step, then save the asset. description is stored as FText; an empty string clears it. A description the property system already finds identical is a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. An unknown emitter asset or a missing param is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Returns old_description and new_description as read back. Emitters inside a system: get_niagara_emitter_handles; add one from an emitter asset with add_niagara_emitter_from_template.

params.description: Asset path of the UNiagaraEmitter, e.g. "/Game/FX/NE_Sparks" (an emitter asset, not a system path).

params.name: description
params.description: New description text, stored as FText; an empty string clears it.

commands.returns: { emitter_asset_path: string, old_description: string, new_description: string, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_mesh_renderer_mesh
commands.description: Assign a static mesh into a Niagara Mesh renderer's Meshes[] slot.  Resolves (or grows the array to) the slot index, loads the UStaticMesh, and sets the slot's inner .Mesh via reflection on the FNiagaraMeshRendererMeshProperties element. Then requests a system compile and saves; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. add_niagara_renderer type=Mesh leaves Meshes empty (renders nothing); this is the command that makes a Mesh renderer actually draw. A renderer_index or slot that is not a JSON number is an error and nothing changes. Idempotent: re-assigning the same mesh to the same slot does not grow the array, writes nothing and saves nothing (already_assigned=true, saved=false).

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Name of the emitter handle.

params.name: renderer_index
params.description: 0-based index of the Mesh renderer (use get_niagara_emitter_renderers).

params.name: mesh_path
params.description: Asset path of the UStaticMesh to assign (e.g. "/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube").

params.name: slot
params.description: Optional 0-based slot index into Meshes[] (default 0). The array is grown with default elements up to this index if needed.

commands.name: set_niagara_module_enabled
commands.description: Enable or disable one module of a Niagara emitter's particle spawn or update stack (FNiagaraStackGraphUtilities::SetModuleIsEnabled), in one undo step, then request a system compile and save the system; a disabled module stays on the stack but does not run. The module is found by function name (case-sensitive) on the script_group stack only, the first one in execution order. previous_enabled and enabled are read from the node before and after; an enabled state that did not take fails the call. A module already in that state changes nothing: changed false, saved false and a note. An unknown system, emitter, script_group or module (or a module only on the other stack) is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. list_niagara_modules shows each module's is_enabled.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Content path of the UNiagaraSystem asset, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'.

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle, as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it.

params.name: module_name
params.description: Function name of the module to toggle, case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives module_name for that stack, e.g. 'GravityForce'.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Optional bool, the state to set; defaults to true

params.name: script_group
params.description: Optional "spawn" or "update" (any case), the stack the module is on; defaults to "update"; any other value is an error and nothing changes.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, module_name: string, module_index: int, previous_enabled: bool, enabled: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_module_input
commands.description: Override a Niagara module input by writing the rapid-iteration store. Locates the module function-call node (by its module_node_name, as returned by add_niagara_module_to_stack) on the emitter's spawn or update stack, matches the input by its leaf name, and writes the value into the owning group script's RapidIterationParameters store. The system is recompiled and saved. value is required: a JSON number for a float or int input, [x, y, z] for a vector, [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] for a color; a missing or malformed one is an error and nothing changes. HONEST GATE: bool / enum / data-interface / object inputs are not rapid-iteration eligible and return a clean error. The packed value_type must also match the input's actual type or a clean error is returned. Read it back with get_niagara_module_input.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. "/Game/Niagara/NS_Example").

params.name: emitter_name
params.description: Display name of the emitter handle.

params.name: module_node_name
params.description: The module function-call node name (from add_niagara_module_to_stack's module_node_name).

params.name: input_name
params.description: Leaf name of the module input (e.g. "Drag" for "Module.Drag").

params.name: value_type
params.description: One of "float", "int", "vector", or "color"; defaults to "float"

params.name: value
params.description: Required. For float/int: a JSON number. For vector: [x, y, z], numbers within the float range. For color: [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], alpha 1 when omitted. A missing or malformed value is an error.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, emitter_name: string, module_node_name: string, input_name: string, value_type: string, ri_param_name: string, verified: bool, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_renderer_material
commands.description: Set the Material UPROPERTY on a Niagara renderer (Sprite, Ribbon, Mesh or Decal: any renderer class with a Material property).  Loads the material, sets it on the renderer's public Material field, requests a system compile and saves; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. A renderer that already uses that material is a success with changed=false and saved=false, and nothing is written. A renderer_index that is not a JSON number, or a renderer class without a Material property (Light), is an error. Reads back to verify the material path is now bound, and returns the material it replaced.

commands.name: set_niagara_renderer_properties
commands.description: Set properties of one renderer (Sprite, Mesh, Ribbon, Light or Decal) of a Niagara emitter, found by emitter_name and renderer_index, in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. Only supplied fields are written; enum fields (alignment, facing_mode, sort_mode, motion_vector_setting, decal_source_mode) also fire PostEditChangeProperty. Every field is converted before the first write, so a value that does not convert (an unknown enum name, an array for a struct field) or a non-number renderer_index is an error and nothing changes. Values already held: changed=false, saved=false. Keys the renderer class lacks are listed in not_applicable. A failed save makes success false with save_error. commands.name: set_niagara_simulation_stage_properties
commands.description: Set the enum, bool, name and FIntPoint properties of one generic simulation stage (UNiagaraSimulationStageGeneric) of a Niagara emitter, found by stage_index or stage_name, in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. Binding fields (num_iterations, iteration_count, element_count_x|y|z, data_interface) go to not_supported, never written; add_niagara_simulation_stage sets the iteration count. A failed save makes success false with save_error. List: get_niagara_simulation_stages.

commands.name: set_niagara_system_deterministic
commands.description: Set the system-wide determinism flag (bDeterminism, written by reflection) of a Niagara System asset, found by asset path, in one undo step, then save the asset. When true, every instance seeds its random numbers from the system's RandomSeed plus the component's RandomSeedOffset, so runs are repeatable; when false, each instance draws a new seed on reset. deterministic is required. A value the system already holds is a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. A missing param or unknown system is an error; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Read it back with get_niagara_system_info; one emitter's determinism: set_niagara_emitter_sim_target.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: deterministic
params.description: Boolean to assign to bDeterminism

commands.returns: { system_path: string, old_deterministic: bool, new_deterministic: bool, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_niagara_system_properties
commands.description: Set the render and system flags of a Niagara System asset (cast shadow, decals, custom depth/stencil, translucency sort, large world coordinates, current-frame data, fixed bounds) and save it. Use it instead of set_properties for these fields: a render value also turns its bOverride companion on unless that override_ key is sent, the asset is saved, and PostEditChangeProperty is skipped (no scalability refresh); set_properties writes any other UPROPERTY and leaves it unsaved. Only supplied fields are written, in one undo step. Every field and fixed_bounds is checked before the first write: a corner that is not 3 numbers, a number field that is not a JSON number, or a property the engine lacks is an error and nothing changes. Values the system already holds are a success with changed=false and saved=false. A failed save makes success false with save_error. Read back with get_niagara_system_properties.

commands.name: set_niagara_system_warmup_tick_count
commands.description: Recompute the warmup tick count of a Niagara System asset, found by asset path, from its current warmup time and tick delta, in one undo step, then save the asset; it takes no count. The engine stores floor(warmup_time / warmup_tick_delta) and rounds warmup_time down to whole ticks; a delta near zero is reset to 0 with a count of 0, so no warmup runs. Settings that are already consistent are a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. An unknown system is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. For N ticks, set the delta with set_niagara_system_warmup_tick_delta, then N times it with set_niagara_system_warmup_time and check warmup_tick_count; read back with get_niagara_system_info.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, old_warmup_tick_count: int, new_warmup_tick_count: int, warmup_time: number, warmup_tick_delta: number, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

retired.how: object_path=<system>, properties={"WarmupTime":..} or {"WarmupTickDelta":..}, save=true: the engine recomputes WarmupTickCount from them

commands.name: set_niagara_system_warmup_tick_delta
commands.description: Set the warmup tick delta (seconds simulated per warmup tick) of a Niagara System asset in one undo step, then save it. The engine re-derives the tick count as floor(warmup_time / delta) and rounds warmup_time down to a whole number of ticks, so a delta that does not divide the warmup time shortens it and one larger than it zeroes the warmup; the reply does not show this, so read warmup_time and warmup_tick_count back with get_niagara_system_info. A delta that leaves the warmup settings as they are is a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. A missing delta, one that is not a finite JSON number above 0, or an unknown system, is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Set the delta before calling set_niagara_system_warmup_time.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire" (the object path form also works).

params.name: warmup_tick_delta
params.description: Seconds per warmup tick, > 0, e.g. 0.0333 for 30 ticks per second; the call fails without it.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, old_warmup_tick_delta: number, new_warmup_tick_delta: number, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

retired.how: object_path=<system>, properties={"WarmupTickDelta":..}, save=true (the engine recomputes WarmupTickCount)

commands.name: set_niagara_system_warmup_time
commands.description: Set the warmup time in seconds (simulated ahead when the system activates; 0 turns warmup off) of a Niagara System asset in one undo step, then save the asset. The engine re-derives warmup_tick_count as floor(warmup_time / warmup_tick_delta) and rounds the time down to whole ticks, so a time that is not a multiple of the delta comes back shorter in new_warmup_time; with a delta of 0 no warmup runs. A time that is not a finite JSON number of 0 or more, a missing param or an unknown system is an error and nothing changes. A time that leaves the warmup settings as they are is a success with changed=false and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Set the delta first with set_niagara_system_warmup_tick_delta; read back with get_niagara_system_info.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire"; the call fails without it.

params.name: warmup_time
params.description: Warmup time in seconds (>= 0; 0 disables warmup); the call fails without it.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, old_warmup_time: number, new_warmup_time: number, warmup_tick_count: int, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

retired.how: object_path=<system>, properties={"WarmupTime":..}, save=true (the engine recomputes WarmupTickCount)

commands.name: set_niagara_user_parameter
commands.description: Set the default value of one user parameter (the User. namespace) of a Niagara System asset in one undo step, adding the parameter when the system has none of that name and type; the asset is marked dirty, not saved (save_asset keeps it). type picks Float, Vector, Vec2, Vec4, Color, Bool or Int; without it a vector, vec2, vec4 or color key picks that type, else Float. A missing value, or one not of the JSON type the parameter takes, is an error with nothing written. A parameter already holding the value is a success with changed=false and value_set=false, nothing written. verified means the value reads back as sent. Read it with get_niagara_user_parameter; inverse: remove_niagara_user_parameter.

params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: User parameter name (without the "User." prefix).
