params.name: value
params.description: The value of a Float (a number), Int (a whole number) or Bool (true or false) parameter; those types fail without it or with another JSON type

params.name: vector
params.description: [X, Y, Z], 3 numbers, the value of a Vector parameter (required for it; also picks type Vector when type is omitted)

params.name: vec2
params.description: [X, Y], 2 numbers, the value of a Vec2 parameter (required for it)

params.name: vec4
params.description: [X, Y, Z, W], 4 numbers, the value of a Vec4 parameter (required for it)

params.name: color
params.description: [R, G, B] or [R, G, B, A] linear color of a Color parameter, A 1 when omitted (required for it)

commands.returns: { system_path: string, parameter_name: string, parameter_type: string, value_set: bool, changed: bool, value_read_back?: number|bool|[number...], verified: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: spawn_niagara_component
commands.description: Place a Niagara System in the editor level as a new ANiagaraActor (the actor a drag of the system into the viewport makes, through the editor's Niagara actor factory) whose root UNiagaraComponent runs the system, at an optional location and rotation, for previews and set_niagara_component_* calls. For a Niagara component on an actor that already exists use add_component_to_actor (NiagaraComponent) and set its Asset with set_properties. actor_label labels the new actor (default: the system's name, made unique); a label that is "None" or blank, or that another editor-world actor already has as label or internal name, is an error and nothing is spawned, so set_niagara_component_* (actor_name = owner_actor_name or the label) reach this actor. A system the factory refuses (settings requiring an effect type) is an error too. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level keeps it). Editor world only, PIE or not. location and rotation are read back.

params.name: system_path
params.description: Asset path of the Niagara System to place (e.g. /Game/MyGame/NS_Example); one that does not load is an error and nothing is spawned.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional world location [X, Y, Z]; the origin when omitted.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional world rotation, the object {"pitch":..,"yaw":..,"roll":..} or the array [pitch, yaw, roll] (index 2 is ROLL); zero when omitted.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Optional editor label for the new actor; when omitted the factory labels it after the system, made unique. A label that is not a valid actor label ("None", blank), or that another actor of the editor world already has as its label or internal name, is an error and nothing is spawned.

commands.returns: { system_path: string, owner_actor_name: string, owner_actor_label: string, actor_class: string, actor_path: string, component_name: string, is_registered: bool, is_active: bool, location: [number, number, number], rotation: { roll: number, pitch: number, yaw: number } }

commands.name: cancel_render_job
commands.description: Cancels the in-progress movie render, if one is running (honest headless gate).  Movie renders run inside a Play-In-Editor session (UMoviePipelinePIEExecutor), so in a headless / non-interactive editor there is normally no active executor. When an active render exists it is canceled via UMoviePipelineExecutorBase::CancelAllJobs; otherwise this reports was_rendering:false honestly (an expected headless state, not an error).

params.name: job_name
params.description: Optional job name (informational only; cancellation stops the active executor's whole render).

commands.returns: { canceled: bool, was_rendering: bool, note: string }

commands.name: create_render_job
commands.description: Adds a new job for a Level Sequence to this editor session's Movie Render Queue, without rendering: the job points at the sequence, takes map_path as its map when given, and has its default primary configuration. One undo step; the queue lives in memory, so nothing is saved to disk and the job is gone when the editor closes. Works headless. Each call adds another job, even with a job_name the queue already has (tools that take job_name then act on the first match). Next, set resolution, folder and image format with set_render_job_output and render with render_sequence_to_movie, which renders every job in the queue; get_render_queue lists the jobs and delete_render_job takes one out. For a quick render with default PNG output, render_sequence_to_movie alone is enough.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not a path (e.g. "Intro"): the first Level Sequence under /Game with that name, case-insensitive; get_level_sequences lists them.

params.name: job_name
params.description: Optional job name (default "RenderJob_<sequence_name>"), the name set_render_job_output and delete_render_job take; not checked for uniqueness.

params.name: map_path
params.description: Optional object path of the map the job renders in (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap.MyMap"), stored as given and not checked; without it the render plays the level open in the editor.

commands.returns: { job_name: string, sequence_name: string, sequence_path: string, map: string, has_configuration: bool, job_created: bool, queue_job_count: number }

commands.name: delete_render_job
commands.description: Deletes one job, by name, from this editor session's Movie Render Queue, or every job with delete_all true. Only the queued job goes: its sequence, its map and any frames already rendered stay. One undo step; nothing is saved to disk, since the queue lives in memory. Works headless. Idempotent: a job_name the queue does not have succeeds with already_absent true and nothing changes; when several jobs share the name, only the first is deleted. A call with neither job_name nor delete_all is an error. get_render_queue lists the job names, create_render_job and render_sequence_to_movie add jobs, and cancel_render_job stops a render in progress, which this tool does not do.

params.name: job_name
params.description: Name of the job to delete, as get_render_queue lists it (e.g. "RenderJob_Intro"), matched case-insensitively; required unless delete_all is true.

params.name: delete_all
params.description: Optional bool, default false; true deletes every job in the queue and ignores job_name.

commands.returns: { job_name?: string, deleted?: bool, already_absent?: bool, deleted_all?: bool, queue_job_count: number }

commands.name: export_asset_as_text
commands.description: Produce a CANONICAL, STABLE text dump of ANY asset (Blueprint, DataTable, Material, DataAsset, ...) for external diff / VCS snapshot / review, without the volatile bits of the binary .uasset. format='json' (default) gives a deterministic sorted UPROPERTY dump (a UDataTable uses its native GetTableAsJSON writer); format='t3d' gives the engine's UExporter T3D text. Returns the text inline (capped), a whole-text MD5 content hash for change detection, and writes the full dump to Saved/Exports/Text. This is the primitive under the diff tools.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path or /Game package path of the asset to dump.

params.name: format
params.description: 'json' (default; deterministic reflection / DataTable-JSON) or 't3d' (UExporter T3D).

params.name: write_file
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Also write the full dump under Saved/Exports/Text.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, object_path: string, asset_class: string, format: string, text: string, text_length: int, truncated: bool, content_hash: string, export_file_path: string, written: bool, message: string }

commands.name: export_blueprint_data
commands.description: Load a Blueprint asset and write a summary of it to a new file Saved/Exports/Blueprints/<Name>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.json or .txt in the project: parent class, compile status, counts of function graphs, event graphs and variables, function graph names, and member variables (name, pin type, category; JSON adds public and editable flags). No graph nodes; the Blueprint is not modified or compiled. Errors if the asset is missing or not a Blueprint; an unsupported format writes nothing (export_success=false). For an inline reply use get_blueprint_info; for a full dump, export_asset_as_text.

params.name: blueprint_path
params.description: Full path to the blueprint asset (e.g., '/Game/MyBlueprint').

params.name: export_format
params.description: Export format: 'json' or 'txt'.

commands.returns: { blueprint_path: string, export_format: string, export_success: bool, export_message: string, export_file_path: string, export_file_name: string, export_file_size_bytes: int, export_file_size_mb: number, blueprint_class: string, package_name: string, original_file_size_bytes: int, original_file_size_mb: number, export_timestamp: string, export_status: string, export_directory: string }

commands.name: export_level_section
commands.description: Exports the actors of one section of the editor world (name, class, transform) to JSON or TXT. A section is a loaded level (the persistent level or a streaming sub-level, by package name), else an outliner folder (with its subfolders); '*' exports the whole world. An unknown section is an error that lists the loaded levels.

params.name: section_name
params.description: Level package name (e.g. 'L_City_Interiors'), outliner folder path (e.g. 'Lighting' or 'Props/Trees'), or '*' for the whole world.

params.name: export_format
params.description: Export format: 'json' or 'txt'.

commands.returns: { section_name: string, export_format: string, export_success: bool, export_message: string, export_file_path: string, export_file_name: string, export_file_size_bytes: int, export_file_size_mb: number, level_name: string, world_name: string, section_scope: string ('world' | 'level' | 'folder'), actor_count: int, export_timestamp: string, export_status: string, export_directory: string }

commands.name: flush_async_loading
commands.description: Block until all in-flight async package loads finish (::FlushAsyncLoading).
commands.returns: { flushed, async_packages_before, async_packages_after, packages_flushed }

commands.name: generate_asset_report
commands.description: Load an asset and write a property report to a new file Saved/Reports/Assets/<Name>_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.json or .txt in the project: every reflected property of its class (editable or not) with its type and value text, counts of editable and Blueprint-visible properties, and the package file size -- or, with visible_only, just the editable or Blueprint-visible properties as details-panel text. Those statistics go only into the file; the reply carries its path, size and status, and the package file size. The asset is not modified. A missing asset is an error; an unsupported format writes nothing (report_success=false). export_asset_as_text returns a canonical dump inline.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full path to the asset to analyze (e.g., '/Game/MyAsset').

params.name: report_format
params.description: Report format: 'json' or 'txt'.

params.name: visible_only
params.description: Optional bool (default false): write only the editable or Blueprint-visible properties, each as its details-panel text (a JSON `properties` object of name -> text), with report_type "Visible Properties", instead of the full census.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, report_format: string, report_success: bool, report_message: string, report_file_path: string, report_file_name: string, report_file_size_bytes: int, report_file_size_mb: number, asset_class: string, package_name: string, original_file_size_bytes: int, original_file_size_mb: number, report_timestamp: string, report_status: string, report_type: string, report_directory: string }

commands.name: get_render_queue
commands.description: List the jobs in the editor's Movie Render Queue right now (the queue of this editor session, held by the Movie Pipeline Queue subsystem; nothing is read from disk): each job's job_name, sequence and map paths, enabled flag and setting_count (settings on its configuration), plus queue_job_count. Use it to find job names before set_render_job_output, delete_render_job or render_sequence_to_movie, and to confirm what create_render_job added; cancel_render_job stops a render in progress. Read-only and idempotent. An empty queue gives queue_job_count 0, not an error; an editor without the subsystem (Movie Render Queue plugin off) is an error.
commands.returns: { jobs: [{ job_name: string, sequence: string, map: string, enabled: bool, setting_count: number }], queue_job_count: number }

commands.name: get_source_control_status
commands.description: Report the editor revision-control connection, read-only: provider name, whether revision control is enabled and the provider available, and its status_text. Says nothing about individual files or their checkout state, and never connects or changes settings.
commands.returns: { provider, enabled, available, status_text }

commands.name: render_sequence_to_movie
commands.description: Renders a Level Sequence to PNG frames with Movie Render Queue: adds a job named OneShot_<sequence_name> with the engine's default output (1920x1080 into {project_dir}/Saved/MovieRenders/) and starts rendering the whole editor queue, jobs from create_render_job included, in a Play-In-Editor session. Asynchronous: it returns at once without waiting for frames, and render_started only says a render executor was launched, not that frames were written; while a render is already running it starts nothing new. Needs an interactive editor, since it starts its own PIE session; headless, the job is still added. Frames overwrite earlier files of the same name in the output folder, and each call adds another job. For another resolution or format use create_render_job and set_render_job_output first; follow progress with get_render_queue and stop with cancel_render_job.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not a path (e.g. "Intro"): the first Level Sequence under /Game with that name, case-insensitive; get_level_sequences lists them.

params.name: map_path
params.description: Optional object path of the map to render in (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap.MyMap"), stored as given and not checked; without it the render plays the level open in the editor.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, job_name: string, job_created: bool, queue_job_count: number, render_started: bool, render_async: bool, note: string }

commands.name: set_render_job_output
commands.description: Set where and how a Movie Render Queue job writes its frames: resolution, output folder and image format, on the job's configuration. Use it after create_render_job, which makes the job; the queue is rendered by render_sequence_to_movie, which adds a job of its own for a sequence and then renders every job in the queue, this one included; read the queue back with get_render_queue. Each format adds its image-sequence output to the job and none is removed, so calling it with png and then jpg writes both (delete_render_job and create_render_job start the job over). Settings that are not given keep their value; an unknown format, or a resolution with only one side or a side of 0 or less, is refused and nothing changes. exr falls back to png when the EXR output is not available, and format says which was used. The queue lives in this editor session: nothing is saved to disk, and the job is lost when the editor closes.

params.name: job_name
params.description: Name of a job in the editor's render queue, as create_render_job or get_render_queue returns it.

params.name: resolution_x
params.description: Output width in pixels, e.g. 1920; give it together with resolution_y, or neither to keep the current resolution.

params.name: resolution_y
params.description: Output height in pixels, e.g. 1080; give it together with resolution_x.

params.name: output_dir
params.description: Folder the frames are written to, absolute ("D:/Renders/Shot01") or with Movie Render Queue tokens ("{project_dir}/Saved/MovieRenders/"); omit it to keep the current folder.

params.name: format
params.description: Image format of the frames: "png" (default), "jpg" (or "jpeg"), "exr" or "bmp"; any other value is refused.

commands.returns: { job_name: string, format: string, configured: bool, resolution_x: number?, resolution_y: number?, output_dir: string?, settings: [string], image_outputs: [string], setting_count: number }

commands.name: activate_game_feature_plugin
commands.description: Load and activate a Game Feature Plugin by name or URL. ASYNC + honest-headless: the state transition runs on the subsystem's own ticker, so this fires the activation (logging the eventual result) and returns immediately with the current state -- poll get_game_feature_plugin_state until state == "Active". Idempotent: if already active, no-ops with already_active=true.

params.name: plugin_name
params.description: Name of the Game Feature Plugin (resolved to a URL via the subsystem registry). Provide this OR plugin_url.

params.name: plugin_url
params.description: The plugin URL directly (e.g. a file: protocol URL). Takes precedence over plugin_name.

commands.returns: { url: string, already_active: bool, state: string, is_active: bool, is_loaded: bool, is_registered: bool, note: string }

commands.name: deactivate_game_feature_plugin
commands.description: Deactivate an active Game Feature Plugin by name or URL. ASYNC + honest-headless (same fire-and-return pattern as activate): returns immediately with the current state; poll get_game_feature_plugin_state. Idempotent: if not active, no-ops with already_inactive=true.

params.name: plugin_name
params.description: Name of the Game Feature Plugin (resolved to a URL). Provide this OR plugin_url.

params.name: plugin_url
params.description: The plugin URL directly. Takes precedence over plugin_name.

commands.returns: { url: string, already_inactive: bool, state: string, is_active: bool, is_loaded: bool, is_registered: bool, note: string }

commands.name: get_game_feature_plugin_state
commands.description: Read the current lifecycle state of a Game Feature Plugin by name or URL (synchronous). The engine's EGameFeaturePluginState enum is non-reflective, so this is the canonical way to observe/poll a plugin's state after an async activate/deactivate.

params.name: plugin_name
params.description: Name of the Game Feature Plugin (resolved to a URL). Provide this OR plugin_url.

params.name: plugin_url
params.description: The plugin URL directly. Takes precedence over plugin_name. An unknown URL reports state "UnknownStatus".

commands.returns: { url: string, state: string, is_active: bool, is_loaded: bool, is_registered: bool, is_installed: bool, is_in_error_state: bool }

commands.name: list_game_feature_plugins
commands.description: Enumerate every Game Feature Plugin the subsystem knows about (built-in + registered), with each one's current state. Read-only, synchronous.
commands.returns: { plugins: [{ name: string, url: string, loaded_as_built_in: bool, state: string }], count: int }

commands.name: unload_game_feature_plugin
commands.description: Unload a Game Feature Plugin by name or URL (complement of activate/deactivate). ASYNC + honest-headless (same fire-and-return pattern): returns immediately with the current state; poll get_game_feature_plugin_state. Idempotent: if not loaded, no-ops with already_unloaded=true. Note: an active plugin is still loaded, so this unloads it regardless of active state.

params.name: plugin_name
params.description: Name of the Game Feature Plugin (resolved to a URL). Provide this OR plugin_url.

params.name: plugin_url
params.description: The plugin URL directly. Takes precedence over plugin_name.

params.name: keep_registered
params.description: If true, the plugin stays registered after unloading (unwinds to the Registered state instead of fully unregistering). Optional, default false.

commands.returns: { url: string, already_unloaded: bool, keep_registered: bool, state: string, is_active: bool, is_loaded: bool, is_registered: bool, note: string }

commands.name: get_game_mode_info
commands.description: Read which classes a game mode spawns: DefaultPawnClass, HUDClass, PlayerStateClass, GameStateClass, SpectatorClass and PlayerControllerClass from the class default object of an AGameModeBase subclass, native or Blueprint, plus its parent class, is_multiplayer (true when it derives from AGameMode, the match-state subclass) and the GameMode override in the open editor level's World Settings. Read-only. An empty string means that slot or override is unset; a class that does not resolve or is not a game mode is an error. Change the slots with set_game_mode_classes and the level override with set_game_mode_override; the project-wide default is the GlobalDefaultGameMode of GameMapsSettings (get_project_settings_value), and get_world_settings reads the rest of World Settings.

params.name: game_mode_class
params.description: Game mode class by name or path: a native short name with or without the A prefix ('GameModeBase'), a /Script path, or a Blueprint asset or class path, e.g. '/Game/Core/BP_MyGameMode'. One of the two class params is required.

params.name: game_mode_class_path
params.description: Full class path, e.g. '/Script/Engine.GameModeBase' or '/Game/Core/BP_MyGameMode.BP_MyGameMode_C'; tried before game_mode_class.

commands.returns: { game_mode_class: string, parent_class: string, is_multiplayer: bool, default_pawn_class: string, hud_class: string, player_state_class: string, game_state_class: string, spectator_class: string, player_controller_class: string, world_settings_default_game_mode?: string }

commands.name: register_spawn_point
commands.description: Mark an existing actor as a registered spawn point for the project (sets PlayerStartTag + ensures it's a APlayerStart). Useful for tagging generic actors as respawn anchors in lieu of placing APlayerStarts.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the actor to mark as a spawn point.

params.name: player_start_tag
params.description: Optional FName tag (e.g. "Red"/"Blue" for team filtering; "Respawn" for general spawn anchors).

commands.returns: { actor_name, was_player_start, promoted_to_player_start: bool, player_start_tag }

commands.name: set_game_mode_classes
commands.description: Write one or more class slots -- DefaultPawnClass, HUDClass, PlayerStateClass, GameStateClass, SpectatorClass, PlayerControllerClass -- on the class default object (CDO) of an AGameModeBase subclass, picked by game_mode_class_path or else game_mode_class (one is required). Pass at least one slot param; each must resolve to a class deriving from that slot's base, and every one is checked before anything is written, so a bad one writes nothing. A slot that already holds the class is left alone (idempotent). GameModes spawned later (the next PIE) use the new classes. A Blueprint GameMode's CDO is modified and its package marked dirty but not saved: persist it with save_asset (persistable true). A native GameMode class has no savable package, so its values last only until the editor closes (persistable false). Each slot written is read back from the CDO. Read every slot with get_game_mode_info; set_game_mode_override picks the GameMode of the level.

params.name: game_mode_class
params.description: Optional AGameModeBase class name (short or /Script/ path)

params.name: game_mode_class_path
params.description: Optional long /Script/Engine.GameModeBase path (takes precedence)

params.name: pawn_class
params.description: Optional APawn-derivative class for DefaultPawnClass

params.name: hud_class
params.description: Optional AHUD-derivative class for HUDClass

params.name: player_state_class
params.description: Optional APlayerState-derivative class for PlayerStateClass

params.name: game_state_class
params.description: Optional AGameStateBase-derivative class for GameStateClass

params.name: spectator_class
params.description: Optional ASpectatorPawn-derivative class for SpectatorClass

params.name: player_controller_class
params.description: Optional APlayerController-derivative class for PlayerControllerClass

commands.returns: { game_mode_class: string, persistable: bool, default_pawn_class?: string, hud_class?: string, player_state_class?: string, game_state_class?: string, spectator_class?: string, player_controller_class?: string, already_set: bool, slots_written: [string] } -- one read-back field per slot that was passed; already_set is true when every requested slot already held its class (nothing written), and slots_written names the reply fields of the slots that changed.

commands.name: set_game_mode_override
commands.description: Set -- or, with game_mode_class "" or "None", clear -- the GameMode override in the World Settings of the current editor world (AWorldSettings::DefaultGameMode), the GameMode this level uses instead of the project default; a cleared override falls back to the engine's URL/INI DefaultGameMode on the next world load. game_mode_class can be a native class name, a /Script/ path or a Blueprint GameMode asset path, and must derive from AGameModeBase (AGameMode too; is_multiplayer says which). The World Settings actor is modified as part of the call's undo step and the level is marked dirty but not saved: persist it with save_level. Repeating the call leaves the same state (idempotent). An unknown or non-GameMode class, or no editor world, is an error. Read it back with get_game_mode_info; the GameMode's own class slots are set with set_game_mode_classes, and a GameMode Blueprint is made with create_blueprint (parent_class "GameModeBase").

params.name: game_mode_class
params.description: AGameModeBase-derivative class: a native short name (e.g. "GameModeBase"), a /Script/ path, or a Blueprint GameMode asset path (e.g. "/Game/Core/BP_MyGameMode"). An empty string or "None" clears the override.

commands.returns: { world_settings_path: string, world_name: string, default_game_mode: string, previous_default_game_mode: string, reset: bool, is_multiplayer?: bool } -- default_game_mode is "" and reset true when the override was cleared; previous_default_game_mode is the path of the override before the call ("" when there was none); is_multiplayer only when a class was set.

commands.name: spawn_player_start
commands.description: Place a Player Start (where the game mode spawns players) in the editor's current level, with an optional rotation and team tag; when name matches the label or object name of an existing Player Start, that one is moved and retagged instead of adding another. Use it to set where players appear; spawn_actor can also place one (type PlayerStart) but without the tag or the rotation check; to make an actor already in the level a tagged spawn point use register_spawn_point; which pawn spawns there is set_game_mode_classes. Location and rotation are read back from the actor: a mismatch, usually a [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] array sent with the yaw last, answers success false with both values. One undo step; the level is marked dirty but not saved (save_level). Without name every call adds a new Player Start.

params.name: location
params.description: [X, Y, Z] world location in centimetres; put it a little above the floor so the pawn's capsule does not start inside it.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional world rotation. TWO forms: the unambiguous OBJECT form {"roll":R,"pitch":P,"yaw":Y} (RECOMMENDED) or the ambiguous ARRAY form [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] -- note the array order, index 2 is ROLL, not yaw. Default identity.

params.name: player_start_tag
params.description: Optional PlayerStartTag, e.g. "Red", "Blue", "Spectator": the game mode's FindPlayerStart picks starts by this tag (the Portal argument); empty leaves the current tag unchanged.

params.name: name
params.description: Optional actor label, e.g. "PS_RedBase"; an existing Player Start with this label or object name is reused. Without it the engine names the new actor (PlayerStart_N) and every call adds one.

commands.returns: { actor_name, location: [x,y,z] (RE-READ from the actor), rotation: {roll,pitch,yaw} (RE-READ from the actor, axes NAMED), is_spatially_loaded: bool, location_matches_request: bool, rotation_matches_request: bool, player_start_tag, spawned: bool, already_existed: bool, requested: { location, rotation, player_start_tag, name } }

commands.name: activate_ability
commands.description: Try to activate one granted ability on an editor-world actor ability system component with TryActivateAbility; activated is the engine verdict, false when the activation checks of the ability refuse it. Use grant_ability first, and cancel_ability to stop it.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

params.name: ability_name
params.description: Ability to match among the granted specs: the ability_name from get_active_abilities, the class name with or without _C ("GA_Jump"), the asset path ("/Game/Abilities/GA_Jump") or the class path; case-insensitive, first match wins

commands.returns: { actor_name, ability_name, activated }

commands.name: add_attribute_to_set
commands.description: Add one FGameplayAttributeData member variable to an AttributeSet Blueprint, with default_value as its BaseValue and CurrentValue, then compile and save it. A name that is already an attribute of the class is left as it is (added false, already_existed true, nothing saved); a name taken by a variable of another type fails. attribute_present and base_value are read from the compiled class. An add is refused before any edit when a running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk would keep it from being saved, and a failed save undoes it, taking the variable out again and recompiling the Blueprint.

params.name: attribute_set_path
params.description: Full asset path of the AttributeSet Blueprint

params.name: attribute_name
params.description: Name of the new attribute member variable

params.name: default_value
params.description: Initial BaseValue and CurrentValue of the attribute, default 0; not applied to an attribute that already exists.

commands.returns: { attribute_set_path: string, attribute_name: string, default_value: number, added: bool, already_existed: bool, attribute_present: bool, base_value?: number, default_applied?: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: add_gameplay_effect_component
commands.description: Add one empty UGameplayEffectComponent of a standard type to the GEComponents array of a GameplayEffect Blueprint's CDO and save without recompiling. GE components are instanced subobjects of the effect, not actor components, so add_component_to_blueprint and add_component_to_actor cannot add them. Idempotent: an existing component of that type returns already_existed=true. Configure it with the set_gameplay_effect_component_* tools; get_gameplay_effect_components lists them. A running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk fails before any edit, and a failed save undoes the edit.

params.name: gameplay_effect_path
params.description: Asset path of the GameplayEffect Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/GAS/Effects/GE_Damage".

params.name: component_type
params.description: Bare type name, case-insensitive: AssetTags, TargetTags, AdditionalEffects, ChanceToApply, Immunity, TargetTagRequirements, RemoveOther, CustomCanApply, BlockAbilityTags, Abilities or CancelAbilityTags (not the full class name).

commands.returns: { gameplay_effect_path: string, component_type: string, component_class: string, component_count: int, component_added: bool, already_existed: bool }

commands.name: add_gameplay_effect_modifier
commands.description: Append one modifier with a constant magnitude to the Modifiers array on the class default object of a GameplayEffect Blueprint, then save it without recompiling and without an undo entry. attribute_name is looked up across every loaded AttributeSet class; an unknown attribute or modifier_op, a running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk fails before any edit, and a failed save undoes the edit. Each call appends a new entry, even an identical one; modifier_index says where it went. Change its magnitude type with set_gameplay_effect_modifier; remove_gameplay_effect_modifier drops it; get_gameplay_effect_modifiers lists them.

params.name: ge_blueprint_path
params.description: Full asset path of the GE Blueprint

params.name: attribute_name
params.description: Attribute to modify, Health or MySet.Health: the bare name or AttributeSetClass.Attribute, case-insensitive, first match among the loaded AttributeSet classes

params.name: modifier_op
params.description: Add, Multiply, Divide, or Override (case-insensitive)

params.name: magnitude
params.description: Constant magnitude of the modifier, stored as a ScalableFloat without a curve

commands.returns: { ge_blueprint_path: string, attribute_name: string, modifier_op: string, magnitude: number, modifier_index: int, modifier_count: int, magnitude_readback_ok: bool, magnitude_readback: number, added: bool }

commands.name: apply_gameplay_effect
commands.description: Apply a GameplayEffect class to an editor-world actor's ability system component: an outgoing spec at the given level, with a fresh context from that component, applied to self. Duration and infinite effects then show in get_active_effects and come off with remove_gameplay_effect; an instant effect changes base values at once and leaves nothing active. Check the outcome with get_attributes or get_attribute_value; to set one value directly use set_attribute_base_value. applied is the engine's verdict (WasSuccessfullyApplied), true for an instant effect that executed; active says whether an active effect now stands for it, false for an instant one. When the engine refuses the effect (application requirements, an immunity, its chance to apply) applied is false and the call fails, with nothing changed. Not idempotent: each call adds another application or stack. Runtime state only: no undo step, nothing saved. execute_batch of apply_gameplay_effect calls applies a list.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1": the whole name, case-insensitive, no wildcards. get_actors_in_level lists names; find_actors_by_name maps a label to its name

params.name: effect_class
params.description: Class path of a UGameplayEffect subclass, loaded with LoadClass: a Blueprint GE needs its _C class path, e.g. "/Game/Effects/GE_Burn.GE_Burn_C"; a C++ one "/Script/MyGame.GE_Burn". create_gameplay_effect_blueprint makes one; an unloadable path is an error

params.name: level
params.description: Effect level that scalable magnitudes are read at, a number, fractions allowed (e.g. 2.5); default 1.0

commands.returns: { actor_name, effect_class, level, applied, active } -- applied: the engine applied or executed the effect; active: an active effect now tracks it (duration or infinite effects)

commands.name: apply_multiple_gameplay_effects
commands.description: Apply several GameplayEffect classes at one level to an editor-world actor ability system component; each entry is loaded and applied separately, so a bad path does not stop the rest. Returns requested, applied_count, failed_count and the per-entry applied and failed lists.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

params.name: effect_classes
params.description: JSON array of UGameplayEffect class path strings, e.g. ["/Game/Effects/GE_Burn.GE_Burn_C"]; non-string entries go to failed

params.name: level
params.description: GameplayEffect/ability level applied to all effects (default 1.0)

commands.returns: { error, effect_class, applied, active_handle, actor_name, requested, applied_count, failed_count, failed }

commands.name: cancel_ability
commands.description: Stop a running ability on an editor-world actor's ability system component (CancelAbilityHandle) while keeping it granted, reading its spec before and after: was_active, still_active and cancelled. Start it again with activate_ability; to ungrant it use remove_ability instead; get_active_abilities shows which granted abilities are running (is_active). Idempotent: cancelling one that is not running changes nothing and still succeeds with cancelled=false. success is false, with an error, when it is still active afterwards (the ability may not allow cancelling). Runtime state only: no undo step, nothing saved. An unknown actor, a missing component or no matching granted ability is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1": the whole name, case-insensitive, no wildcards. get_actors_in_level lists names; find_actors_by_name maps a label to its name

params.name: ability_name
params.description: Granted ability to cancel: the ability_name get_active_abilities returns, the class name with or without _C ("GA_Jump"), the asset path ("/Game/Abilities/GA_Jump") or the class path; case-insensitive, first matching spec wins

commands.returns: { actor_name, ability_name, was_active, still_active, cancelled } -- read back from the spec: cancelled means was_active and not still_active

commands.name: create_attribute_set_blueprint
commands.description: Create a Blueprint parented to UAttributeSet at package_path/name, compile and save it, or reuse the AttributeSet Blueprint already there (created false, already_existed true; a Blueprint of another class there is an error, and is left untouched); with attributes, add one FGameplayAttributeData variable per entry, then compile and save it. A name the class already has is skipped and listed in skipped_attribute_names; success is false when an added attribute is missing from the compiled class or did not get its default_value. A running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk fails before anything is created or added; a call that adds nothing to an existing set is not refused and saves nothing (saved false). A failed save makes success false, with saved false and save_error, and the added attributes stay in memory only.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without a path, e.g. "AS_Character".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the new asset, e.g. "/Game/GAS/Attributes"; defaults to /Game/Blueprints.

params.name: attributes
params.description: Optional array of {"name": "Health", "default_value": 100} objects; default_value (default 0) becomes the BaseValue and CurrentValue of the compiled default. Entries without a name are ignored; omitted, the set is created empty (add attributes later with add_attribute_to_set).

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_attribute_set: bool, already_existed: bool, attributes_added: int, added_attribute_names: [string], skipped_attribute_names: [string], failed_attribute_names: [string], attributes_applied: bool, created: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_gameplay_ability_blueprint
commands.description: Create a Blueprint parented to UGameplayAbility at package_path/name, compile and save it; returns asset_path, generated_class and is_gameplay_ability. A GameplayAbility Blueprint already at that path is returned untouched (created false, already_existed true); a Blueprint of another class there is an error. Refused during PIE.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without a path, e.g. "GA_Fireball".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the new asset, e.g. "/Game/GAS/Abilities"; defaults to /Game/Blueprints.

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_gameplay_ability: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: create_gameplay_cue_notify
commands.description: Create a GameplayCueNotify Blueprint of the kind notify_type names -- Static (UGameplayCueNotify_Static, non-instanced one-shot, the default), Burst (UGameplayCueNotify_Burst, modern non-instanced one-shot), Actor (AGameplayCueNotify_Actor, a spawned, instanced cue actor) or Looping (AGameplayCueNotify_Looping, modern instanced looping notify) -- at package_path/name, compile and save it, or reuse the one of that class already there (created false, already_existed true); a Blueprint of another class there, or an unknown notify_type, is an error. A registered gameplay_cue_tag is written to the CDO and saved: a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk refuses that write and a failed save undoes it; an unregistered tag only yields cue_tag_set=false. Refused during PIE. Edit it with set_properties (Static, Burst) or set_properties (Actor, Looping).

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without a path, e.g. "GCN_Hit".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the new asset, e.g. "/Game/GAS/Cues"; defaults to /Game/Blueprints.

params.name: notify_type
params.description: Optional kind of notify, any case: Static (default), Burst, Actor or Looping.

params.name: gameplay_cue_tag
params.description: Registered gameplay tag written as GameplayCueTag and GameplayCueName, e.g. "GameplayCue.Hit"; an unregistered tag is skipped (cue_tag_set=false), not an error.

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, notify_type: string, is_gameplay_cue_notify: bool, cue_tag_set: bool, cue_tag_requested: string, cue_tag: string, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: create_gameplay_effect_asset
commands.description: Create a native UGameplayEffect data asset (not a Blueprint, and not a container) at package_path/name with the given duration policy, and save it; no undo transaction. apply_gameplay_effect needs a class, so for an effect you will apply use create_gameplay_effect_blueprint instead; read the result back with get_gameplay_effect_info. Idempotent: a GameplayEffect already at that path, native or Blueprint, is returned untouched with already_existed=true and nothing saved, but the duration_policy in that reply echoes your request, not the asset; an asset of another class there is refused. An unknown duration_policy is an error and nothing is created. A failed save (always while PIE runs) is an error, and the new asset stays in memory unsaved.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without a folder, e.g. "GE_Damage".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder as a long package path, e.g. "/Game/GAS/Effects" (default /Game/GameplayEffects; one trailing slash is dropped).

params.name: duration_policy
params.description: "Instant", "HasDuration" or "Infinite", case ignored (default Instant).

params.name: duration_magnitude
params.description: Duration in seconds as a constant magnitude, e.g. 5.0; used only with HasDuration and ignored otherwise (default 0.0).

commands.returns: { name, asset_path, already_existed, duration_policy, duration_magnitude?, created? }

commands.name: create_gameplay_effect_blueprint
commands.description: Create a Blueprint parented to UGameplayEffect at package_path/name, compile and save it; returns asset_path, generated_class and is_gameplay_effect. A GameplayEffect Blueprint already at that path is returned untouched (created false, already_existed true); a Blueprint of another class there is an error. Refused during PIE.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without a path, e.g. "GE_Damage".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the new asset, e.g. "/Game/GAS/Effects"; defaults to /Game/Blueprints.

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_gameplay_effect: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: create_gameplay_mod_magnitude_calculation_blueprint
commands.description: Create a Blueprint parented to UGameplayModMagnitudeCalculation (a custom magnitude calc class for GE modifiers), compile and save it. A Blueprint of that class already at the path is returned untouched (created false, already_existed true); one of another class there is an error.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name, e.g. MMC_Damage

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Blueprints

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_mod_magnitude_calculation: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: get_ability_asset_tags
commands.description: Read the AssetTags of a GameplayAbility Blueprint from its class default object: ability_tags, asset_tag_count, and ability_name (the default object name). Despite the tool name, no activation data is read: no activation policy, required or blocked tags, cost or cooldown. Read-only and editor-time: it loads the asset and needs no actor or PIE; a path that is not a GameplayAbility Blueprint is an error. set_ability_asset_tags writes these tags; get_ability_info reads an ability granted to an actor.

params.name: ability_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the ability Blueprint asset

commands.returns: { ability_path: string, ability_name: string, ability_tags: [string], asset_tag_count: int }

commands.name: get_ability_info
commands.description: Read one ability granted to an editor-world actor ability system component: ability_class, level, is_active and input_id of the first matching spec. Read-only; an error when no granted spec matches ability_name. Use get_active_abilities to list them all.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

params.name: ability_name
params.description: Ability to match among the granted specs: the ability_name from get_active_abilities, the class name with or without _C ("GA_Jump"), the asset path ("/Game/Abilities/GA_Jump") or the class path; case-insensitive, first match wins

commands.returns: { actor_name, ability_name, ability_class, level, is_active, input_id }

commands.name: get_ability_system_component
commands.description: Read a short census of an editor-world actor's ability system component: component_name, active_abilities_count (every granted spec, running or not) and active_effects_count. Call it first to confirm an actor has a component before grant_ability, apply_gameplay_effect or send_gameplay_event_to_actor; for the entries behind the counts use get_active_abilities, get_active_effects or get_attributes. The component is the actor's IAbilitySystemInterface answer, else its first UAbilitySystemComponent. Read-only and idempotent; it reads the editor world, not a PIE session. A missing actor or component is an error, so has_ability_system is never false.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1": the whole name, case-insensitive, no wildcards. get_actors_in_level lists names; find_actors_by_name maps a label to its name

commands.returns: { actor_name, has_ability_system, component_name, active_abilities_count, active_effects_count }

commands.name: get_ability_tasks
commands.description: List the gameplay tasks the GameplayTasksComponents of an editor-world actor (its ability system component counts) know about, without changing anything: the tasks activated and not yet ended (the component's KnownTasks), plus any queued waiting for task resources. Each has task_name, task_class, task_state (Uninitialized, AwaitingActivation, Active, Paused or Finished), is_ability_task and owner_name (the object that started it, e.g. an ability instance); counts split ability tasks from other gameplay tasks. A task that was created but never activated is not known to the component and is not listed. An actor that is not found, or has no ability system component, is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

commands.returns: { actor_name, task_count, ability_task_count, generic_task_count, tasks: [{ task_name, task_class, task_state, is_ability_task, owner_name }] }

commands.name: get_active_abilities
commands.description: List every ability granted to an editor-world actor ability system component, running or not (all activatable specs, despite the tool name): ability_name (the class default object name), ability_class, level and is_active, plus count. Read-only; get_ability_info reads one.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

commands.returns: { ability_name, ability_class, level, is_active, actor_name, abilities, count }

commands.name: get_active_effects
commands.description: List the gameplay effects currently active on an editor-world actor ability system component: effect_name (the definition object name), effect_class and level for each, plus count. Read-only; effects whose definition is gone are skipped. get_gameplay_effect_info reads one.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

commands.returns: { effect_name, effect_class, level, actor_name, effects, count }

commands.name: get_attribute_meta_on_set_class
commands.description: Read back the FAttributeMetaData DataTable an AttributeSet class is initialized from (read-side of set_attribute_meta_on_set_class): row struct name, row count, and the serialized rows. This reports the AUTHORED defaults on disk, not the live values of any actor -- for those use get_attribute_value / get_attributes.

params.name: attribute_set_class_path
params.description: Full UAttributeSet class path

params.name: data_table_path
params.description: Optional override; default is /Game/UEAgent/AttributeMeta/<ClassName>_Meta

commands.returns: { attribute_set_class, data_table_path, row_struct, row_count, rows }

commands.name: get_attribute_value
commands.description: Read one attribute from the attribute sets registered on an editor-world actor ability system component: value (current, modifiers included), base_value and attribute_set. Read-only; an unknown attribute is not an error but found=false. get_attributes lists every attribute.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

params.name: attribute_name
params.description: Attribute name ("Health") or "SetClass.Attribute" ("MyAttributeSet.Health"), case-insensitive; the first registered attribute that matches wins

commands.returns: { actor_name, attribute_name, found, value, base_value, attribute_set }

commands.name: get_attributes
commands.description: List every attribute of the attribute sets registered on the ability system component of an editor-world actor (its IAbilitySystemInterface answer, else its first UAbilitySystemComponent), each with attribute_name, attribute_set, value (current, modifiers included), base_value and found, plus count. Read-only. A missing actor or component is an error; a component with no registered set gives count 0. Use get_attribute_value for one attribute, set_attribute_base_value to change one.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, attributes: [{ attribute_name: string, attribute_set?: string, value: number, base_value: number, found: bool }], count: int }

commands.name: get_gameplay_cue_notify_info
commands.description: Read the class default object of a GameplayCueNotify Blueprint, loaded by asset path: notify_type (Static, Burst, Actor or Looping), its direct parent_class, GameplayCueTag, GameplayCueName and IsOverride. The lifetime and instancing fields come back only for Actor and Looping notifies; a Static or Burst reply leaves them out. Read-only and editor-time: it writes nothing and needs no PIE or actor. A missing asset or a Blueprint that is not a GameplayCueNotify is an error. Use it to check a notify before or after editing it with set_properties (Static, Burst) or set_properties (Actor, Looping); a new one: create_gameplay_cue_notify.

params.name: cue_notify_path
params.description: Full asset path of the GameplayCueNotify Blueprint (Static/Burst/Actor/Looping), e.g. "/Game/GAS/Cues/GCN_Hit".

commands.returns: { cue_notify_path: string, parent_class: string, notify_type: string, gameplay_cue_tag: string, gameplay_cue_name: string, is_override: bool, auto_destroy_on_remove?: bool, auto_destroy_delay?: number, auto_attach_to_owner?: bool, unique_instance_per_instigator?: bool, unique_instance_per_source_object?: bool, allow_multiple_on_active_events?: bool, allow_multiple_while_active_events?: bool, num_preallocated_instances?: int }

commands.name: get_gameplay_effect_components
commands.description: List the GameplayEffectComponents (the GEComponents array) on the class default object of a GameplayEffect Blueprint without changing it, in array order, each with its class and, for the standard ones, its configured values: target, asset and blocked-ability tags (with their combined tags), chance to apply (read at level 0), application, ongoing and removal require and ignore tags, and granted abilities (class, path, input_id); any other component class comes back with its class only. Use it to check what add_gameplay_effect_component, set_gameplay_effect_component or the set_gameplay_effect_component_* tools wrote, and to find the index remove_gameplay_effect_component takes; for duration, period, stacking and modifiers use get_gameplay_effect_info and get_gameplay_effect_modifiers. A GE with no components gives component_count 0. A path that does not load as a Blueprint, has no generated class, or is not a GameplayEffect Blueprint is an error; a native GameplayEffect asset (create_gameplay_effect_asset) is not read here.

params.name: gameplay_effect_path
params.description: Asset path of the GameplayEffect Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/GAS/GE_Burning", as create_gameplay_effect_blueprint returns it (asset_path).

commands.returns: { gameplay_effect_path: string, components: [object], component_count: int }

commands.name: get_gameplay_effect_info
commands.description: Read the first active gameplay effect on an editor-world actor ability system component whose definition matches effect_name: effect_class and level. Read-only; an error when none matches. For an effect asset that is not applied, use get_gameplay_effect_modifiers instead.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

params.name: effect_name
params.description: Active effect to match by its definition: the effect_name from get_active_effects, the class name with or without _C ("GE_Burn"), the asset path ("/Game/Effects/GE_Burn") or the class path; case-insensitive, first match wins

commands.returns: { actor_name, effect_name, effect_class, level }

commands.name: get_gameplay_effect_modifiers
commands.description: Read the attribute modifiers authored on a GameplayEffect asset (a native UGameplayEffect asset, or a Blueprint GE's class default object): for each, attribute, attribute_set, modifier_op (Additive, Multiplicitive, Division or Override) and magnitude_value_at_level_1; plus duration_policy (Instant, HasDuration or Infinite) and modifier_count. Use it to inspect an effect before apply_gameplay_effect; for an effect already active on an actor use get_gameplay_effect_info, for the asset's components get_gameplay_effect_components, and change modifiers with add_gameplay_effect_modifier, set_gameplay_effect_modifier or remove_gameplay_effect_modifier. Read-only and idempotent. magnitude_type always says ScalableFloat whatever the real type; magnitude_value_at_level_1 is present only for a ScalableFloat magnitude, so its absence means attribute-based, SetByCaller or custom. An unknown path is an error.

params.name: effect_path
params.description: Asset path of the effect, not its _C class path: a Blueprint GE "/Game/Effects/GE_Burn" or a native UGameplayEffect asset "/Game/Effects/GE_Native" (".Name" suffix optional). find_assets_by_name finds it; create_gameplay_effect_blueprint or create_gameplay_effect_asset makes one

commands.returns: { attribute, attribute_set, modifier_op, magnitude_type, magnitude_value_at_level_1, effect_path, duration_policy, modifier_count, modifiers }

commands.name: grant_ability
commands.description: Grant a gameplay ability class to the ability system component of an actor in the editor world (not a PIE session) with GiveAbility at a whole-number level; granted says whether a valid spec handle came back, and false is still a success. Runtime state only: no undo step, nothing saved with the level. Not idempotent: granting the same class again adds another spec. Then run it with activate_ability, list the grants with get_active_abilities, and take one away with remove_ability. To grant it only while an effect is active, use set_gameplay_effect_component (component granted_abilities) on a GameplayEffect Blueprint instead. An unknown actor, an actor without an ability system component, or a class that does not load as a UGameplayAbility is an error and nothing is granted.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1", matched case-insensitively; find_actors_by_name maps labels to names

params.name: ability_class
params.description: Class path of a UGameplayAbility subclass: "/Game/Abilities/GA_Jump.GA_Jump_C" for a Blueprint (note the _C), "/Script/MyGame.MyAbility" for C++; create_gameplay_ability_blueprint makes one.

params.name: level
params.description: Spec level, a whole number, e.g. 3 (default 1).

commands.returns: { actor_name, ability_class, level, granted }

commands.name: poll_gameplay_tag_events
commands.description: Reads fires recorded for a register_gameplay_tag_event subscription since a cursor (non-destructive cursor read, same idiom as poll_delegate_events). Never destructive: call again with next_cursor to keep draining without missing or repeating a fire.

params.name: subscription_id
params.description: subscription_id returned by register_gameplay_tag_event (required)

params.name: cursor
params.description: Optional; only fires with sequence_id > cursor are returned. Defaults to 0 (everything retained).

commands.returns: { subscription_id: number, subscription_exists: bool, events: [{sequence_id: number, timestamp: number, new_count: number}], next_cursor: number }

commands.name: register_gameplay_tag_event
commands.description: Registers a REAL listener on a target actor's UAbilitySystemComponent for a gameplay tag's count changes (UAbilitySystemComponent::RegisterGameplayTagEvent, AbilitySystemComponent.h), binding an actual callback (.AddLambda) and keeping its FDelegateHandle so unregister_gameplay_tag_event can honestly undo it later. Idempotent: re-registering the same (actor, tag, event_type) returns the existing subscription_id instead of stacking a duplicate listener. Poll fires with poll_gameplay_tag_events.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name of the target editor-world actor, or an editor label only one actor has (required)

params.name: event_tag
params.description: FGameplayTag name (e.g. "Gameplay.Event.Hit") (required)

params.name: event_type
params.description: "NewOrRemoved" | "AnyCountChange" (default "NewOrRemoved")

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, event_tag: string, event_type: string, subscription_id: number, registered: bool, already_existed: bool }

commands.name: remove_ability
commands.description: Ungrant one ability from an editor-world actor's ability system component with ClearAbility, the inverse of grant_ability. To only stop a running ability and keep it granted, use cancel_ability instead; get_active_abilities lists what is granted and confirms the result. A running ability is only marked and leaves when it ends (pending_removal=true, still a success); removed=true means the spec is gone now. Only the first matching spec goes, so a class granted twice needs two calls; once none is left a call answers Ability not found. success is false with an error if the spec is still granted afterwards. Runtime state only: no undo step, nothing saved. An unknown actor or missing component is an error and changes nothing.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1": the whole name, case-insensitive, no wildcards. get_actors_in_level lists names; find_actors_by_name maps a label to its name

params.name: ability_name
params.description: Granted ability to remove: the ability_name get_active_abilities returns, the class name with or without _C ("GA_Jump"), the asset path ("/Game/Abilities/GA_Jump") or the class path; case-insensitive, first matching spec wins

commands.returns: { actor_name, ability_name, removed, pending_removal } -- read back: removed means the spec is gone; an active ability is only marked, and leaves when it ends (pending_removal)

commands.name: remove_gameplay_effect
commands.description: Remove one active gameplay effect, with all its stacks, from an editor-world actor's ability system component (RemoveActiveGameplayEffect): the first whose definition matches effect_name. The inverse of apply_gameplay_effect; get_active_effects lists what is active and confirms the result. To change the effect asset itself use remove_gameplay_effect_modifier or remove_gameplay_effect_component instead. Instant effects never stay active, so they cannot be removed here (restore a value with set_attribute_base_value). When several active effects share a definition only the first goes, so call again for each; with none left a call answers Effect not found. removed is the engine answer confirmed by the effect no longer being active; success is false with an error otherwise. Runtime state only: no undo step, nothing saved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the editor-world actor, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_1": the whole name, case-insensitive, no wildcards. get_actors_in_level lists names; find_actors_by_name maps a label to its name

params.name: effect_name
params.description: Active effect to remove, matched by its definition: the effect_name get_active_effects returns, the class name with or without _C ("GE_Burn"), the asset path ("/Game/Effects/GE_Burn") or the class path; case-insensitive, first active match wins

commands.returns: { actor_name, effect_name, removed } -- removed is what the engine reports, confirmed by the effect not being active afterwards

commands.name: remove_gameplay_effect_component
commands.description: Remove a component from a GameplayEffect CDO's GEComponents array by index or by component_type/component_class (inverse of add_gameplay_effect_component), and save; the removed component is left out of the saved asset. A running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk fails before any edit, and a failed save undoes the edit.

params.name: gameplay_effect_path
params.description: Full asset path of the GE Blueprint

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional index into the GEComponents array (call get_gameplay_effect_components to enumerate; 0 = first). Supply this OR component_type

params.name: component_type
params.description: Optional friendly type (AssetTags, TargetTags, AdditionalEffects, ChanceToApply, Immunity, TargetTagRequirements, RemoveOther, CustomCanApply, BlockAbilityTags, Abilities, CancelAbilityTags). Accepts the bare type or the full class name. Supply this OR component_index

params.name: component_class
params.description: Alias of component_type (accepts the full "<Type>GameplayEffectComponent" class name)

commands.returns: { gameplay_effect_path: string, removed_index: int, removed_class: string, component_count: int, removed: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_gameplay_effect_modifier
commands.description: Remove a modifier from a GameplayEffect CDO's Modifiers array by index (the D in add/set CRUD). A running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk fails before any edit, and a failed save undoes the edit.

params.name: ge_blueprint_path
params.description: Full asset path of the GE Blueprint

params.name: modifier_index
params.description: Index into the GE CDO Modifiers array to remove (0 = first; add_gameplay_effect_modifier appends)

commands.returns: { ge_blueprint_path: string, removed_index: int, modifier_count: int, removed: bool }

commands.name: send_gameplay_event_to_actor
commands.description: Send a gameplay event to an editor-world actor's ability system component (UAbilitySystemBlueprintLibrary::SendGameplayEventToActor): it tries to activate every granted ability whose trigger is a GameplayEvent on event_tag or a parent tag, and wakes listeners such as Wait Gameplay Event tasks. Use it for event-driven abilities; to start an ability directly use activate_ability, to change attributes apply_gameplay_effect, and to watch tag count changes register_gameplay_tag_event. Not idempotent: each call fires the event again. Nothing is saved and there is no undo step. sent is measured: a probe listening on the component for exactly event_tag saw the event arrive (the call fails when it did not); asc_resolved says the engine's send path found that same component. Neither says which abilities reacted: check with get_active_abilities (is_active) or get_ability_tasks. An unknown actor, a label several actors share, a missing component or an unregistered tag is an error and sends nothing.

params.name: actor_name

The modifier keeps its attribute and operation, but its previous magnitude is discarded whole (a FinalLookupCurve included), and omitted coefficients take their defaults, not the old values. An unknown, abstract or non-UGameplayModMagnitudeCalculation class, an out-of-range modifier_index, a running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk fails before any edit, and a failed save undoes the edit. Make the class with create_gameplay_mod_magnitude_calculation_blueprint, add a lookup curve with set_gameplay_effect_modifier_custom_curve; other magnitudes: set_gameplay_effect_modifier_attribute_based, set_gameplay_effect_modifier_set_by_caller.

A non-GE Blueprint, a running PIE session, a read-only root or a .uasset read-only on disk fails before any edit, and a failed save undoes the edit. For damage or heal over time also give the effect a duration with set_gameplay_effect_duration; stacking is set_gameplay_effect_stacking.

commands.name: unregister_gameplay_tag_event

Idempotent: an unknown/already-removed subscription_id is a success with removed:false, not an error.

params.description: subscription_id returned by register_gameplay_tag_event (required)

commands.returns: { subscription_id: number, removed: bool, was_registered: bool, engine_unregister_ok: bool }

commands.name: create_behavior_config
commands.description: Get or create a UGameplayBehaviorConfig data asset at package_path/config_name: create it, or load the one already there, set its protected BehaviorClass by reflection when behavior_class resolves (on an existing config this overwrites its class), then save it in every case; no undo step. Use it as the entry point before trigger_behavior_on_actor; to change only the class of a config use set_behavior_class (which errors on a bad class instead of ignoring it), to read one get_behavior_config_info, to find them list_behavior_configs, and to delete one remove_behavior_config. An unresolved behavior_class is ignored without error, so check behavior_class in the reply (empty when unset); created tells new from existing. Idempotent: the same call again leaves the same asset. An asset of another class at that path is an error. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false with saved=false.

params.name: config_name
params.description: Asset name of the config, no folder, e.g. "BC_Patrol".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination content folder as a long package path, e.g. "/Game/AI/Behaviors" (default /Game/MCP).

params.name: behavior_class
params.description: Full path of a loaded UGameplayBehavior subclass, e.g. "/Script/GameplayBehaviorsModule.GameplayBehavior_AnimationBased", or "/Game/AI/GB_Sit.GB_Sit_C" for a Blueprint already loaded; a short name never resolves, and a miss or a non-behavior class is ignored. Omit it to leave the class as it is.

commands.returns: { config_path: string, config_name: string, behavior_class: string, created: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: end_behavior_on_actor
commands.description: Interrupt the gameplay behaviors that the editor world UGameplayBehaviorSubsystem runs on a Pawn found by its label: every running behavior that is a behavior_class (subclasses included), or every one when behavior_class is omitted, gets EndBehavior with interrupted=true. behavior_class must be the full class path of a UGameplayBehavior subclass; a short name, or a path that does not resolve to one, is an error and nothing stops. ended is read back from the subsystem: true once every matching behavior stopped, while still_running counts the ones that did not and makes success false. With none running it succeeds with ended false and a note, so a repeat call is idempotent. Runtime only: nothing is saved or undoable. A missing actor, a non-Pawn or no subsystem is an error. Start one: trigger_behavior_on_actor; subsystem check: get_behavior_subsystem_info.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the Pawn actor in the editor world.

params.name: behavior_class
params.description: Optional full path of the UGameplayBehavior subclass to stop, e.g. "/Script/GameplayBehaviorsModule.GameplayBehavior_AnimationBased"; omitted stops every behavior on the pawn, and a path that does not resolve to such a class is an error

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, behavior_class: string, ended: bool, stopped_count: int, still_running: int, note?: string }

commands.name: get_behavior_config_info
commands.description: Read the protected BehaviorClass of a UGameplayBehaviorConfig asset by reflection: behavior_class (class name), behavior_class_path and has_behavior_class. Read-only; set it with set_behavior_class, or list every config with list_behavior_configs.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Path of the UGameplayBehaviorConfig asset, e.g. "/Game/MCP/BC_Patrol"

commands.returns: { config_path: string, behavior_class: string, behavior_class_path: string, has_behavior_class: bool }

commands.name: get_behavior_subsystem_info
commands.description: Report whether the editor world has a UGameplayBehaviorSubsystem (UGameplayBehaviorSubsystem::GetCurrent): world_name, subsystem_available and, when it exists, subsystem_class. Read-only, no parameters; trigger_behavior_on_actor and end_behavior_on_actor fail without it.
commands.returns: { world_name: string, subsystem_available: bool, subsystem_class: string }

commands.name: list_behavior_configs
commands.description: List the UGameplayBehaviorConfig assets under package_path, recursively, from the Asset Registry, without changing them: each config path and name with the name of its BehaviorClass (empty when unset), plus total. Each match is loaded to read that protected field, so a big folder costs one load per config. Only assets whose class is exactly UGameplayBehaviorConfig are listed: subclass configs such as GameplayBehaviorConfig_Animation or GameplayBehaviorConfig_BehaviorTree, and Blueprint subclasses, are skipped. There is no paging, and no match is total 0, not an error. One config in detail: get_behavior_config_info; create one: create_behavior_config; set its class: set_behavior_class; delete one: remove_behavior_config.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Optional content folder searched recursively (default "/Game"); an empty string also means /Game, so another mount point needs its own path

commands.returns: { package_path, total, configs:[{ config_path, config_name, behavior_class }] }

commands.name: remove_behavior_config
commands.description: Destroy a UGameplayBehaviorConfig data asset (mirror of create_behavior_config). Typed-delete: it loads the asset and REFUSES to delete it if it is not a UGameplayBehaviorConfig, so it cannot wipe the wrong asset the way the generic delete_asset can; that refusal, and a delete the engine does not carry out, make success false with deleted false. Idempotent on missing assets.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Full /Game/... asset path of the config.

commands.returns: { config_path, deleted, already_existed, asset_class?, note? }

commands.name: set_behavior_class
commands.description: Set which UGameplayBehavior class an existing UGameplayBehaviorConfig asset runs (its protected BehaviorClass, written by reflection), then save the asset; no undo step. Use it to repoint a config; create_behavior_config makes a new one (and ignores a bad class instead of failing), get_behavior_config_info reads the class back, list_behavior_configs finds configs. A config that does not load, a class that is not found or is not a UGameplayBehavior subclass is an error and nothing changes. set is true whenever the class resolved, without a read-back, so confirm with get_behavior_config_info. Idempotent: the same class again writes and saves again. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false with saved=false.

params.name: config_path
params.description: UGameplayBehaviorConfig asset as an object or package path, e.g. "/Game/MCP/BC_Patrol", as list_behavior_configs returns it.

params.name: behavior_class
params.description: Full path of a loaded UGameplayBehavior subclass, e.g. "/Script/GameplayBehaviorsModule.GameplayBehavior_AnimationBased", or "/Game/AI/GB_Sit.GB_Sit_C" for a Blueprint already loaded. A bare class name is looked up as given and then with a "U" prefix, but neither form finds a class, so pass the path.

commands.returns: { config_path: string, behavior_class: string, set: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: trigger_behavior_on_actor
commands.description: Start the behavior of a UGameplayBehaviorConfig on a Pawn found by label in the editor world: the config supplies its UGameplayBehavior, whose Trigger runs on the pawn, and the world UGameplayBehaviorSubsystem tracks it until it ends or end_behavior_on_actor stops it. triggered=false means the behavior refused. Runtime only: nothing is saved or undoable. A config without BehaviorClass (see set_behavior_class), no subsystem in the editor world (see get_behavior_subsystem_info), a missing actor or a non-Pawn is an error.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Content path of the UGameplayBehaviorConfig.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the Pawn actor in the editor world to receive the behavior.

commands.returns: { config_path: string, actor_label: string, behavior_class: string, triggered: bool }

commands.name: register_gameplay_debugger_category
commands.description: Register a custom Gameplay Debugger category that prints chosen properties of the selected debug actor, one line per spec (IGameplayDebugger::RegisterCategory); Blueprints cannot author debugger categories, so this is the only way from MCP. Idempotent: a repeat with the same name updates its specs to the new list (already_existed true) and registers nothing new. It lives in memory for this editor session only, nothing is saved; unregister_gameplay_debugger_category is the inverse. It draws only in PIE or a game with a debug actor selected: open the debugger with the apostrophe key or the console command gdt.Toggle; the category starts enabled. A missing name, empty specs or a spec without property_name is an error and nothing is registered, as is a build without the GameplayDebugger module.

params.name: category_name
params.description: Name of the category as the debugger shows it, e.g. 'MyAI'; reusing a name this tool registered updates it.

params.name: specs
params.description: Non-empty array of {property_name, actor_class?, color?, label?}: property_name is a property of the debug actor's class (a missing one prints '<property not found>'); actor_class limits the line to actors of that class by short class name, e.g. 'Character'; color is a debugger text color such as 'white', 'red', 'green', 'yellow' or 'cyan'; label replaces the property name in the line. e.g. [{"property_name": "Health", "color": "green"}]

commands.returns: { category_name: string, spec_count: int, registered: bool, already_existed: bool }

commands.name: unregister_gameplay_debugger_category
commands.description: Unregisters a named GameplayDebugger category created by register_gameplay_debugger_category (GameplayDebugger.h IGameplayDebugger::UnregisterCategory, the exact inverse of RegisterCategory). Also drops the category's stored specs. Idempotent: unregistering a category that register_gameplay_debugger_category did not create is an honest no-op reporting already_absent:true.

params.name: category_name
params.description: Name of the debugger category to unregister (required)

commands.returns: { category_name: string, unregistered: bool, already_absent: bool }

commands.name: add_gameplay_tag_redirect
commands.description: Add an entry to UGameplayTagsSettings::GameplayTagRedirects (the persistent redirect config), then call FGameplayTagRedirectors::RefreshTagRedirects() so the runtime map picks it up. Idempotent (same Old->New pair returns already_present=true). Requires a ConfigRestartRequired=true flag — UGameplayTagsSettings flags it as such; callers should note that the running game still resolves Old to itself until next process restart in Shipping, but in the editor the redirect is live immediately.

params.name: old_tag_name
params.description: Source tag name (FName).

params.name: new_tag_name
params.description: Destination tag name (FName).

commands.returns: { old_tag_name, new_tag_name, added: bool, already_present: bool, total_redirects: int, needs_restart: bool }

commands.name: add_gameplay_tag_to_table
commands.description: Add one tag (with an optional developer comment) as a row in a gameplay tag DataTable, verifying the write by read-back. The team-friendly way to declare tags: it touches only this asset instead of rewriting the shared DefaultGameplayTags.ini the way create_gameplay_tag does. The trade-off is that a tag added here is not registered LIVE, so it may not resolve until the table is reloaded -- if you must use it in the same session, check with get_gameplay_tag_info first.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the gameplay tag data table

params.name: tag
