params.description: The gameplay tag string used as both row Tag and row name

params.name: dev_comment
params.description: Optional developer comment for the row

commands.returns: { table_path: string, tag: string, row_name: string, dev_comment: string, verified: bool, saved: bool, row_count: int, success: bool, message: string }

commands.name: add_tag_to_object
commands.description: Grant a gameplay tag to an object that implements IGameplayTagAssetInterface -- the way to put an actor into a state (stunned, wet, on fire, alerted) so that tag-driven systems react without any of them knowing about each other. Reports already_present and echoes the resulting tag list, so the reply is its own oracle. Register the tag first (get_gameplay_tag_info / create_gameplay_tag): an unregistered string resolves to an empty tag and is added as nothing.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to add the tag to

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the tag to add

commands.returns: { object_path: string, tag_name: string, success: bool, already_present: bool, message: string, tags: [string] }

commands.name: create_gameplay_tag
commands.description: Add a new gameplay tag to the project's DefaultGameplayTags.ini AND register it LIVE in this editor session -- that live half is why you must call this before writing the tag into a DataTable row or a property, since an unregistered tag string is silently reset to None by the importers. But it REWRITES THE WHOLE INI: the list comes back alphabetised, every comment block is deleted, and other tags' DevComments are re-serialised and normalised, so adding one tag can produce a diff full of unrelated insertions and deletions. Copy the ini first; the oracle is `git diff --stat` showing your N insertions and ZERO deletions, and if not, git checkout the ini and re-insert only your line (the tag stays registered live either way -- confirm with get_gameplay_tag_info).

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the gameplay tag to create or check

params.name: dev_comment
params.description: Optional developer comment for the tag

params.name: source_name
params.description: Optional explicit source INI name

commands.returns: { tag_name: string, success: bool, tag_string: string, message: string }

commands.name: create_gameplay_tag_table
commands.description: Create a DataTable of gameplay tags (row struct FGameplayTagTableRow) -- the alternative to declaring tags in DefaultGameplayTags.ini, and the better choice for a large or team-owned tag set: rows merge and diff like data instead of fighting over one ini that the create_gameplay_tag path rewrites end to end. The table must be registered in the project's gameplay tag settings to be loaded. Fill it with add_gameplay_tag_to_table and check it with get_gameplay_tag_table_rows (valid, missing_tags).

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name for the new data table, e.g. GT_MyTags

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/GameplayTags

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, table_path: string, row_struct: string, success: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: find_gameplay_tags
commands.description: Search the registered gameplay tags for everything under a tag -- the discovery call for "what tags exist under Material.Wood" or "is there already a tag for this" -- or, with no query_tag, list EVERY registered tag (the full vocabulary, plugins and vendor content included; projects run to thousands, so prefer a branch). count_only returns just the count: the cheap health probe that the registry loaded, or that create_gameplay_tag registered (compare before and after). Sees the LIVE registry, so a tag added this session by create_gameplay_tag shows up even if the ini was restored, and one that only exists as text in a file does not. A query_tag that is not registered is an error; to test one exact string use get_gameplay_tag_info.

params.name: query_tag
params.description: Optional tag whose branch to list (the tag itself and all of its descendants); omitted or empty lists every registered tag

params.name: count_only
params.description: Optional bool, default false: return count (and manager_valid) without the matching_tags list

commands.returns: { query_tag: string, count: int, manager_valid: bool, matching_tags?: [{ tag_name: string, tag_string: string }] }

commands.name: get_gameplay_tag_info
commands.description: Does this exact tag string exist and resolve right now, and if so its detail: its PARENT tag and where it is defined. found=false is a normal answer, not an error -- the precondition to check BEFORE using a tag anywhere: an unregistered tag is not an error in UE, it silently becomes an empty/None tag, and a query made with an empty tag fails exactly like a valid tag that does not match. The parent is how you walk the hierarchy (Material.Wood.Oak answers to Material.Wood); hierarchy matching is ASYMMETRIC, HasAny(A, B) only succeeds when a tag of A is B or a DESCENDANT of B, so putting a family where a leaf is expected quietly fails. The source says where the tag comes from -- native C++, DefaultGameplayTags.ini, a tag DataTable, or transient (registered live this session and NOT on disk) -- with its comment and native / restricted / explicit flags: whether a tag survives an editor restart, which file to edit to change it, and whether it is YOURS or a vendor's or the engine's before you rename or remove it. Exact lookup: use find_gameplay_tags for a branch.

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the gameplay tag to look up

commands.returns: { tag_name: string, found: bool, tag_string?: string, tag_name_string?: string, parent_tag?: string, source?: string, comment?: string, is_native?: bool, is_restricted?: bool, is_explicit?: bool, allow_non_restricted_children?: bool }

commands.name: get_gameplay_tag_redirects
commands.description: List every entry configured in UGameplayTagsSettings::GameplayTagRedirects (the persistent Old->New redirect config). Read-only reader counterpart of add_gameplay_tag_redirect / remove_gameplay_tag_redirect; does NOT mutate or save.
commands.returns: { redirects: [{ old_tag_name, new_tag_name }], count: int }

commands.name: get_gameplay_tag_table_rows
commands.description: List every tag declared in a gameplay tag DataTable (FGameplayTagTableRow), with its developer comment and whether the live tag manager has it registered -- what this table contributes to the project vocabulary, as opposed to find_gameplay_tags which returns the merged live registry from all sources. valid is false when any row's tag is not registered, and missing_tags names each such tag with its row key, so the table can be fixed or the tags registered. Read-only.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the gameplay tag data table

commands.returns: { table_path: string, row_struct: string, rows: [{ row_name: string, tag: string, dev_comment: string, registered: bool }], row_count: int, valid: bool, missing_count: int, missing_tags: [{ tag_name: string, row_name: string }] }

commands.name: get_object_tags
commands.description: Read the gameplay tags an object currently owns -- what the game believes this actor or asset IS (states, factions, damage types, item categories). Requires the object to implement IGameplayTagAssetInterface; anything else returns nothing, which is a fact about the interface, not about the object's data. Reads the LIVE container, so during PIE tags added at runtime appear here. has_gameplay_tags answers a specific question instead of listing everything.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to get tags from

commands.returns: { object_path: string, tags: [string], tag_count: int }

commands.name: has_gameplay_tags
commands.description: Test the tags an object owns (through IGameplayTagAssetInterface, else its first FGameplayTagContainer property) against a list: match "any" (default, OR) -- the "is it any kind of X" gate: any Damage.*, any Status.*; "all" (AND) -- the multi-condition gate: alive AND armed AND not restrained; "none" -- the blocker/immunity check: not stunned, not already burning (computed as !HasAny, so a true means "clear to proceed", not "has them"). A single tag is a one-element list. Hierarchy matching is ASYMMETRIC and this is where it bites: a requested FAMILY accepts its descendants, a requested LEAF does not accept the family, so swapping the two silently turns an always-true gate into an always-false one. When in doubt request leaf tags, which match either way. owned_tags comes back every time, so a surprising answer is diagnosable in the same call. An unregistered tag name is an error (check it with get_gameplay_tag_info).

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path of the UObject to inspect

params.name: tags
params.description: Non-empty array of tag-name strings (e.g. ["Combat.Hit","Character.State.Alive"])

params.name: match
params.description: Optional "any" (default) | "all" | "none": OR, AND, or the negation of OR

commands.returns: { object_path: string, match: string, result: bool, has_any?: bool, has_all?: bool, has_none?: bool, requested: [string], owned_tags: [string] }

commands.name: remove_gameplay_tag
commands.description: Delete a gameplay tag from its ini source list. Two cautions. Nothing tells you who was using it -- the engine exposes no tag reference count, so audit with find_blueprint_node_references and a binary grep of Content/ first, and add_gameplay_tag_redirect if anything still points at it. And like create_gameplay_tag this rewrites DefaultGameplayTags.ini wholesale, reordering it and dropping comments, so the oracle is `git diff` on the ini, not the success flag.

params.name: tag
params.description: Gameplay tag string to remove, e.g. MyGame.Temp

commands.returns: { tag: string, success: bool, was_present: bool, delete_returned: bool, removed: bool, message: string }

commands.name: remove_gameplay_tag_from_table
commands.description: Remove a gameplay tag row (by tag, the row name) from a FGameplayTagTableRow data table.  Idempotent: a missing row reports already_absent without error.  The remove counterpart of add_gameplay_tag_to_table.

params.name: table_path
params.description: Full asset path of the gameplay tag data table.

params.name: tag
params.description: The gameplay tag string identifying the row to remove (used as the row name).

commands.returns: { table_path: string, tag: string, row_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, row_count: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_gameplay_tag_redirect
commands.description: Delete the gameplay tag redirect(s) that rewrite a given old tag name -- cleanup once every asset has been resaved and nothing references the old name any more. Removing it too early silently breaks whatever still points at the old tag, since an unresolved tag becomes empty rather than an error. If the same old name was rewritten more than once over time there will be several entries: remove_all=true clears them all, and removed_count tells you how many went.

params.name: old_tag_name
params.description: Source tag name to unmap.

params.name: remove_all
params.description: If true (default false), remove every redirect with that OldTagName.

commands.returns: { old_tag_name, removed_count: int, already_absent: bool, total_redirects: int }

commands.name: remove_tag_from_object
commands.description: Take a gameplay tag off an object implementing IGameplayTagAssetInterface -- clearing a state (no longer stunned, no longer burning) so the systems keyed on it stop reacting. The was_present flag distinguishes "removed it" from "it was never there", and the reply echoes the remaining tags. Exact match only: removing a parent tag does not remove its children.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to remove the tag from

params.name: tag_name
params.description: Name of the tag to remove

commands.returns: { object_path: string, tag_name: string, success: bool, was_present: bool, message: string, tags: [string] }

commands.name: add_mesh_primitive
commands.description: Append a Box, Sphere, Cylinder or Cone to the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, keeping the geometry already there: size is the box edge or the diameter and height of the round shapes, centred at location in mesh-local space. Each call adds another copy as one undo step: undo puts the mesh back as it was. Nothing is saved to an asset. An unknown actor or primitive is an error that leaves the mesh as it was; appended is true when the triangle count grew. To merge another actor's mesh use add_mesh_to_dynamic_mesh; to persist the result, copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: primitive
params.description: Box, Sphere, Cylinder, or Cone, default Box

params.name: size
params.description: Dominant dimension in cm, default 100

params.name: location
params.description: Optional local [x, y, z] offset for the primitive

params.name: dimensions
params.description: Fallback alias for size when size is omitted (cm)

params.name: material_id
params.description: Optional MaterialID stamped on the appended triangles (default 0). Non-zero enables the mesh MaterialID attribute first, so a later copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh (bUseSectionMaterials=true) emits this piece as its own section/material slot. This is how one dynamic mesh becomes a multi-slot static mesh.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, primitive: string, size: number, material_id: int, triangle_count: int, triangles_added: int, vertex_count: int, appended: bool }

commands.name: add_mesh_to_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Appends a copy of another DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh to the live dynamic mesh of a target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, keeping the geometry already there: the source vertices, shifted by append_transform, land in the target's mesh-local space, and neither actor's world transform is applied. One undo step puts the target back as it was; the source is not changed, the level is marked dirty and nothing is saved to an asset. Each call adds another copy. An empty source is a success with appended false and a note; an unknown actor, or one without a dynamic mesh, is an error. For a primitive shape use add_mesh_primitive, for a Static Mesh asset copy_static_mesh_to_dynamic_mesh, for a boolean union apply_mesh_boolean_actor_to_actor; keep the result with copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the DynamicMeshActor that receives the geometry, in the editor world.

params.name: source_actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the DynamicMeshActor whose dynamic mesh is copied in; it is read, not changed.

params.name: append_transform
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] translation in cm added to every source vertex before the copy (default [0, 0, 0]); translation only, no rotation or scale.

commands.returns: { actor_name, source_actor_name, triangles_before, triangles_after, triangles_added, vertex_count_after, appended: bool, note?: string } -- appended is false, with a note, when the source mesh has no triangles

commands.name: apply_adaptive_remesh
commands.description: Adaptive-remesh the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, found by label or name, toward max_edge_length, with the edge length scaled per vertex by a weight map and relative_density, as one undo step that restores the mesh; nothing is saved. The engine needs that weight map: without weight_map_name, or with a name the mesh has no weight layer for, it reports an error, remeshed is false and the call fails with the mesh unchanged (weight_map_resolved says whether the name was found). A missing or non-positive max_edge_length or an unknown actor is an error. remeshed is true when the triangle or vertex count changed. For uniform density use apply_uniform_remesh; to only reduce triangles, simplify_mesh. Needs Unreal Engine 5.8 or later.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: max_edge_length
params.description: Target edge length for adaptive remesh (sets TargetType=TargetEdgeLength + TargetEdgeLength). Required.

params.name: min_edge_length
params.description: Soft floor for adaptive edge length (default 1.0). NOTE: FGeometryScriptAdaptiveRemeshOptions has no explicit min field — this is echoed back in the result for traceability but is NOT consulted by the engine call.

params.name: relative_density
params.description: Density adjustment in [-2.0, 2.0] passed to FGeometryScriptAdaptiveRemeshOptions::RelativeDensity (default 0.0).

params.name: weight_map_name
params.description: Name of an existing vertex weight map on the mesh (resolved via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshQueryFunctions::GetWeightMapHandle); the engine's adaptive remesh needs one, so an omitted name or one the mesh has no layer for makes the call fail with the mesh unchanged.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, min_edge_length: number, max_edge_length: number, relative_density: number, weight_map_name: string, weight_map_resolved: bool, target_type: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, remeshed: bool }

commands.name: apply_mesh_boolean
commands.description: Apply a CSG boolean (Subtract by default, Union or Intersect) between the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world and a temporary primitive tool: other_primitive (Sphere by default) of size cm, offset by location in mesh-local space. The target is changed in place as one undo step that restores it, nothing is saved, and each call cuts or merges again. An unknown actor, operation or primitive is an error. When the engine refuses the result (an empty one, such as subtracting from an empty mesh) the mesh is left unchanged, boolean_applied is false and the call fails. To use another actor's mesh as the tool call apply_mesh_boolean_actor_to_actor.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: operation
params.description: Union, Subtract, or Intersect, default Subtract

params.name: other_primitive
params.description: Tool primitive shape, default Sphere

params.name: size
params.description: Tool primitive size in cm, default 100

params.name: location
params.description: Optional tool [x, y, z] offset

params.name: dimensions
params.description: Fallback alias for size when size is omitted (cm)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, operation: string, other_primitive: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, boolean_applied: bool }

commands.name: apply_mesh_boolean_actor_to_actor
commands.description: Apply a CSG boolean using a second DynamicMeshActor as the cutting tool. Unlike apply_mesh_boolean (which builds a transient primitive tool), the tool geometry is the live dynamic mesh of source_actor_name. The target mesh is mutated in place as one undo step that restores it; the source mesh is left untouched. NOT idempotent: re-running keeps cutting/merging the same tool against the already-modified target. When the engine refuses the result (an empty one) the target is left unchanged, boolean_applied is false and the call fails.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor (the receiver, mutated in place)

params.name: source_actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the DynamicMeshActor whose live dynamic mesh is used as the boolean tool

params.name: operation
params.description: Union, Subtract, or Intersect, default Subtract

params.name: use_world_transforms
params.description: Optional bool, default true. When true the tool is positioned by the relative world transform (source relative to target) so the boolean respects the actors' placement; when false the tool is applied at identity (co-located).

params.name: fill_holes
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshBooleanOptions.bFillHoles (default true)

params.name: simplify_output
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshBooleanOptions.bSimplifyOutput (default true)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, source_actor_name: string, operation: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, boolean_applied: bool }

commands.name: apply_mesh_morphology
commands.description: Apply an SDF-based morphology op (dilate/contract/close/open) to the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, found by label or name, replacing the mesh with an SDF-based offset mesh approximation as one undo step that restores the original mesh; nothing is saved. distance is the offset in cm and must be > 0; a missing or unknown operation, a missing distance or an unknown actor is an error checked before anything changes. When the engine reports an error (a result with no triangles, as when a contract erases the whole mesh, or from an empty mesh), morphed is false, the call fails and the mesh is left as it was. Wrap into a solid instead with apply_mesh_solidify; persist the result with copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: operation
params.description: Required. One of: dilate, contract, close, open.

params.name: distance
params.description: Required positive float. Offset distance in cm (SDF-based).

commands.returns: { actor_name, operation, distance, triangle_count, triangle_count_before, vertex_count, morphed }

commands.name: apply_mesh_solidify
commands.description: Voxel-wrap the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, found by label or name: the mesh is replaced by a voxelised-and-meshed approximation on a grid of 64 cells along its longest side, as one undo step that restores the original mesh; nothing is saved. An unknown actor is an error. When the engine reports an error (a result with no triangles, as from an empty mesh), solidified is false, the call fails and the mesh is left as it was. For an offset surface use apply_mesh_morphology; to only fix self-intersections, repair_mesh_self_intersections; persist the result with copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: winding_threshold
params.description: Optional [0..1], default 0.5. Space with generalised winding number above this is considered inside.

params.name: extend_bounds
params.description: Optional positive float, default 1.0. Bounds extension applied to the default input-mesh-based bounds.

params.name: surface_search_steps
params.description: Optional int >= 1, default 3. Marching-cubes vertex search steps.

params.name: thicken_shells
params.description: Optional bool, default false. Thicken open shells into closed solids (expensive on large meshes).

params.name: shell_thickness
params.description: Optional positive float, default 1.0. Offset distance for shell thickening.

commands.returns: { actor_name, triangle_count, triangle_count_before, vertex_count, solidified }

commands.name: apply_uniform_remesh
commands.description: Remesh the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world into evenly sized triangles, aiming at target_edge_length (cm) or target_tri_count: exactly one is required, else an error. The mesh changes in place as one undo step that restores it, and the actor's package is marked dirty, not saved. smoothing_type picks uniform, UV-preserving or mixed smoothing; an unknown value is an error. The reply echoes the settings the engine was given. remeshed is true when the triangle or vertex count changed. For variable density use apply_adaptive_remesh; to only reduce triangles, simplify_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: target_edge_length
params.description: Target uniform edge length in mesh units (sets TargetType=TargetEdgeLength). Mutually exclusive with target_tri_count; at least one is required.

params.name: target_tri_count
params.description: Approximate target triangle count (sets TargetType=TriangleCount). Mutually exclusive with target_edge_length.

params.name: preserve_sharp_edges
params.description: Approximate 'preserve sharp edges' by enabling bPreventNormalFlips on the shared RemeshOptions (default true; UE's FGeometryScriptUniformRemeshOptions has no explicit preserve-sharp flag, so the closest equivalent is the shared RemeshOptions.bPreventNormalFlips).

params.name: smoothing_type
params.description: One of 'uniform' | 'uv_preserving' | 'mixed' (default 'mixed'); maps to EGeometryScriptRemeshSmoothingType on the shared RemeshOptions.

params.name: auto_compact
params.description: Auto-compact the index space after remesh on the shared RemeshOptions (default true).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, target_edge_length: number, target_tri_count: int, preserve_sharp_edges: bool, smoothing_type: string, auto_compact: bool, target_type: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, remeshed: bool }

commands.name: build_mesh_bvh
commands.description: Build a BVH (bounding volume hierarchy) for the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world with BuildBVHForMesh, and read it back with IsBVHValidForMesh. The plugin keeps no BVH between calls: this one is dropped on return, and the spatial-query tools (find_nearest_point_on_mesh, find_nearest_ray_intersection_with_mesh, is_point_inside_mesh) build their own on every call, so they never need this first. It checks that a BVH can be built for the mesh as it is now, which is also the answer to whether a valid BVH exists for it: built (and its alias bvh_rebuilt) is true when the engine reported no error and the BVH reads back as valid (bvh_valid); the call fails otherwise. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: b_only_if_invalid
params.description: Optional bool, default true; it has no effect, since no earlier BVH is kept and every call builds a new one.

commands.returns: { actor_name, built: bool, bvh_rebuilt: bool, b_only_if_invalid: bool, bvh_valid: bool, vertex_count, triangle_count } -- bvh_rebuilt is the same flag as built; actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label; b_only_if_invalid echoes the request; the counts are those of the mesh the BVH was built for.

commands.name: clear_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Empty a DynamicMeshActor's live UDynamicMesh in place (keep the actor, drop the geometry). One undo step restores the geometry; an already empty mesh adds no undo step.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the DynamicMeshActor to clear (required).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, triangle_count_before: int, triangle_count_after: int, vertex_count_before: int, vertex_count_after: int, cleared: bool }

commands.name: compact_mesh
commands.description: Compact a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world (actor found by label or object name): renumber its vertex, triangle and edge IDs into dense ranges, dropping the free ID slots that deletions leave. Geometry and the vertex and triangle counts stay the same, but IDs move, so vertex or triangle IDs read before (select_mesh_triangles, get_mesh_components_detail) are stale afterwards. Idempotent: compacted is true when any ID moved, and one undo step restores the old IDs; an already compact mesh is a success with compacted=false and adds no undo step. Nothing is saved; an unknown actor is an error. Run it after delete_mesh_triangles or remove_unused_vertices, and before the xatlas method of unwrap_mesh_uvs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name of the DynamicMeshActor in the editor world (case-insensitive).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, compacted: bool }

commands.name: copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh
commands.description: Write the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor INTO an EXISTING /Game UStaticMesh asset's LOD via UGeometryScriptLibrary_StaticMeshFunctions::CopyMeshToStaticMesh (7-arg V2, bUseSectionMaterials=true; engine-default options). Editor-only (the engine function is WITH_EDITOR-gated and touches GEditor + FlushRenderingCommands). Idempotent: overwrites the target LOD in place, no duplication. HONEST GATES: the target asset must already exist (create it first, e.g. duplicate_asset of /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube into /Game) and must NOT live under /Engine/ (the engine refuses to modify built-in engine assets). A lod_index outside 0 to 7 (a static mesh has at most 8 LODs) is an error checked before anything changes; one past the asset's last LOD adds the LODs in between, which the engine sets up to be reduced from an earlier LOD.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the source DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: target_static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path of an EXISTING /Game UStaticMesh to overwrite.

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional target LOD index, 0 to 7 (default 0); a negative index or one of 8 or more is refused.

params.name: materials
params.description: Optional ordered list of UMaterialInterface content paths, one per MaterialID (index 0 = MaterialID 0). Supplying it flips bReplaceMaterials on, so the target asset gets exactly these material slots. WITHOUT this the asset keeps its existing slots and a multi-MaterialID mesh collapses into whatever slots already existed — this is the parameter that makes per-triangle MaterialIDs visible on the saved asset.

params.name: material_slot_names
params.description: Optional slot names matching materials 1:1 (default: the engine names them). Ignored when materials is absent.

commands.returns: { actor_name, target_static_mesh_path, lod_index, outcome_success: bool, source_triangle_count, material_count: int, replaced_materials: bool, wrote: bool }. NOTE: this marks the target package dirty (transaction) but does NOT save to disk — persistence requires a separate save (e.g. via save_asset).

commands.name: copy_mesh_uv_channel
commands.description: Copy UV data from one UV channel to another on the same mesh. A dest_channel the mesh does not have yet is added first (the channel count only grows, and channels added in between have no UVs set); a source_channel the mesh does not have, or a dest_channel of 8 or more, is an error checked before anything changes. copied is false, and the call fails, when the engine reports an error; the same channel for both is a no-op that succeeds with copied false and a note. One undo step restores the channels, a failed copy leaves the mesh as it was, and nothing is saved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

params.name: source_channel
params.description: Source UV channel index (required)

params.name: dest_channel
params.description: Destination UV channel index, 0 to 7 (required, added to the mesh when it does not have it yet)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, source_channel: int, dest_channel: int, copied: bool, num_uv_channels_after: int, note?: string } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label; copied is false when source_channel equals dest_channel, and note says so or that the mesh grew new channels to reach dest_channel.

commands.name: copy_static_mesh_to_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Copy the geometry of a UStaticMesh asset INTO the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor via UGeometryScriptLibrary_StaticMeshFunctions::CopyMeshFromStaticMesh (engine-default options: build settings applied, tangents on). Destructive replace of the actor's current mesh. Idempotent-ish: re-running re-extracts the same source geometry. It reads LOD lod_index (default 0) from its source model, or from its render data when that LOD has no source geometry, as a reduced one (read_render_data); a LOD the mesh does not have, or a mesh with no geometry to read, is an error checked before the actor is touched. One undo step restores the previous mesh, a failed copy leaves it as it was, and nothing is saved. Write back to an asset: copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh; query an asset without a copy: get_static_mesh_geometry_stats.

params.name: source_static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path of the source UStaticMesh (e.g. "/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube").

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor whose GetDynamicMesh() receives the geometry.

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional source LOD to read (default 0), from 0 to the mesh's last LOD, echoed as requested_lod_index; a negative one or one the mesh does not have is an error.

commands.returns: { source_static_mesh_path, actor_name, lod_index, requested_lod_index, read_hi_res_source, read_render_data, outcome_success: bool, triangle_count, vertex_count, copied: bool }

commands.name: delete_mesh_triangles
commands.description: Delete the listed triangle IDs (triangle_ids, or a single triangle_id) from a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world; IDs that do not exist are skipped, so compare num_deleted with requested_count (a missing ID is not an error: deleted just comes back false). One undo step restores the triangles, and a call that deletes none adds no undo step; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: triangle_ids
params.description: Non-empty array of non-negative integer triangle IDs, e.g. [0, 5, 12]; any negative or non-numeric entry fails the call. Required unless triangle_id is given.

params.name: triangle_id
params.description: Optional single non-negative triangle ID, read as triangle_ids [triangle_id] when triangle_ids is absent.

commands.returns: { actor_name, num_deleted, requested_count, deleted: bool, triangle_id?: int, triangle_count, previous_triangle_count } -- deleted is num_deleted > 0; triangle_id echoes the single ID when it was given.

commands.name: find_nearest_point_on_mesh
commands.description: Find the nearest point on the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor to a 3D query point via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshSpatial::FindNearestPointOnMesh. Every call builds a fresh BVH from the mesh as it is now (the plugin keeps none), then queries it, so the answer always reflects the latest mesh edits. found is false when no triangle lies within max_distance, or the mesh is empty. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: query_point
params.description: [x, y, z] query point in the mesh's local space.

params.name: max_distance
params.description: Optional float; max search distance (0 = unlimited).

params.name: allow_unsafe_modified
params.description: Optional; maps to bAllowUnsafeModifiedQueries (default false). It has no effect: the BVH is built fresh on every call, so it always matches the mesh.

commands.returns: { actor_name, found: bool, valid: bool, triangle_id, position_x/y/z, bary_coords_x/y/z } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label.

commands.name: find_nearest_ray_intersection_with_mesh
commands.description: Cast a ray against the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor and return the nearest hit via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshSpatial::FindNearestRayIntersectionWithMesh. Every call builds a fresh BVH from the mesh as it is now (the plugin keeps none), so the answer always reflects the latest mesh edits. The engine normalizes ray_direction, so ray_parameter is the distance from ray_origin to the hit. A ray_direction that cannot be normalized (all zeros, a non-finite value, or not an array of three numbers) is refused before anything else runs. hit is false when nothing is hit within max_distance. The mesh is not changed.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: ray_origin
params.description: [x, y, z] origin point of the ray in mesh-local space.

params.name: ray_direction
params.description: [x, y, z] direction of the ray; the engine normalizes it, so its length does not matter, but a zero or non-finite direction is an error.

params.name: max_distance
params.description: Optional float; max search distance (0 = unlimited).

params.name: allow_unsafe_modified
params.description: Optional; maps to bAllowUnsafeModifiedQueries (default false). It has no effect: the BVH is built fresh on every call, so it always matches the mesh.

commands.returns: { actor_name, hit: bool, ray_parameter, hit_triangle_id, hit_position_x/y/z, hit_bary_coords_x/y/z } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label; ray_parameter is a distance along the normalized direction.

commands.name: get_dynamic_mesh_info
commands.description: Read geometry stats off a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world: triangle and vertex counts, whether it is closed, empty or dense (no triangle ID gaps), whether it carries an attribute set, its connected components, open border edges (0 when closed) and extended polygroup layers, and the UV island count of each UV channel. Read-only.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: Optional UV channel index: report the UV islands of that channel only (default every channel). A negative channel is an error; a channel the mesh does not have is reported, not refused, with is_valid_uv_channel=false.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_internal_name: string, component_name: string, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, is_closed: bool, is_empty: bool, is_dense: bool, has_attribute_set: bool, num_connected_components: int, num_open_border_edges: int, num_polygroup_layers: int, uv_channel_count: int, uv_channels: [{ uv_channel: int, num_uv_islands: int, is_valid_uv_channel: bool }] }

commands.name: get_mesh_components_detail
commands.description: Enumerate the connected components (physical pieces) of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh via UE::Geometry::FMeshConnectedComponents, reporting for EACH island its triangle count, its local-space bounding box, its triangle_id range and which MaterialIDs it carries. Read-only (unlike the engine's SplitMeshByComponents, which consumes the mesh). This is the map of a mesh in ONE call, and the tool to reach for BEFORE painting anything: get_mesh_material_ids says how many triangles carry each material, and this says what those triangles physically ARE. HONEST GATE: it names nothing — it gives you sizes and positions, and which island is which part is still a human call; what it prevents is deriving that from a triangle-count assumption.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: max_components
params.description: Cap on how many islands to return (default 64). components_truncated says whether the cap cut the list; component_count is always the real total.

params.name: include_triangle_ids
params.description: Also return each island's full triangle ID list (default false; use the reported id_min/id_max range instead unless the island is non-contiguous).

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_count: int, components_truncated: bool, components: [ { index, triangle_count, id_min, id_max, id_contiguous: bool, material_ids: [int], bounds: { min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x, max_y, max_z, center_x, center_y, center_z, size_x, size_y, size_z }, triangle_ids: [int] } ] }

commands.name: get_mesh_material_ids
commands.description: Read the per-triangle MaterialID distribution of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshMaterialFunctions::GetMaxMaterialID + GetAllTriangleMaterialIDs. Read-only. This is the ORACLE for every MaterialID write: it returns a per-ID triangle histogram, so "did the paint actually land?" is answerable with a read instead of trusting a success flag. IMPORTANT: has_material_ids=false means the mesh has no MaterialID attribute at all, which is exactly the state in which writes are silently dropped by the engine.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

commands.returns: { actor_name, has_material_ids: bool, max_material_id: int, triangle_count: int, distinct_material_ids: int, histogram: [ { material_id: int, triangle_count: int } ] }

commands.name: get_static_mesh_geometry_stats
commands.description: Measure one LOD of a UStaticMesh asset on a transient dynamic-mesh copy with the asset's build settings and build scale applied and degenerate triangles kept, in mesh-local space (cm, no actor transform): surface area (cm^2), signed volume (cm^3) and center of mass; whether it is closed (watertight: triangles and no edge with a single adjacent triangle; an empty mesh is not); the axis-aligned bounding box (min, max, center, and extent as the half-size); triangle and vertex counts with the size of their ID spaces and whether they have gaps; connected components (islands joined through shared edges); open border loops (one per hole or open rim; a chain the engine cannot close counts in open_border_spans, and ambiguous_topology is true with a span or a bowtie vertex); the UV channel count; and the UV-space area of uv_channel (each triangle with UVs adds its unsigned area, so UVs filling the 0-1 square once sum to 1.0). The center and the volume mean something only when is_closed is true, and reversed winding makes the volume negative. From a source model the copy shares one vertex across UV and normal seams, so vertex_count is usually below the render vertex counts of list_uv_channels and get_static_mesh_info. Read-only: the asset is not changed. lod_index picks the LOD (default 0), and one the mesh lacks is an error; a LOD without source geometry, as a reduced one, is read from its render data, split at UV and normal seams (read_render_data). A path that does not load as a static mesh, or a mesh with no geometry to read, is an error. The bounds stored on the asset: get_static_mesh_info; a DynamicMeshActor in the level: get_dynamic_mesh_info.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Content path to the UStaticMesh asset (e.g. "/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube"; the object path form also works).

params.name: lod_index
params.description: LOD to read (default 0), from 0 to the mesh's last LOD, echoed as requested_lod_index; a LOD the mesh does not have is an error and nothing is read.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: Optional UV channel whose UV area is measured (default 0). A negative one is an error; a channel the mesh lacks gives is_valid_uv_channel false and uv_area 0.

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, lod_index, requested_lod_index, read_hi_res_source, read_render_data, surface_area, volume, center_of_mass_x, center_of_mass_y, center_of_mass_z, is_closed, min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x, max_y, max_z, extent_x, extent_y, extent_z, center_x, center_y, center_z, triangle_count, triangle_id_count, has_triangle_id_gaps, vertex_count, vertex_id_count, has_vertex_id_gaps, connected_components, open_border_loops, open_border_spans, ambiguous_topology, uv_channel_count, uv_channel, uv_area, is_valid_uv_channel }

commands.name: is_point_inside_mesh
commands.description: Tests whether a point lies inside the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, with the engine's fast winding number (IsPointInsideMesh), which also gives a sensible answer for meshes with small holes. Every call builds a fresh BVH and winding tree from the mesh as it is now, so the answer reflects the latest edits; nothing is changed or saved. An unknown actor or a missing query_point is an error. Use it for inside/outside tests; for the closest surface point use find_nearest_point_on_mesh, for a ray hit find_nearest_ray_intersection_with_mesh; build_mesh_bvh is never needed first. The point is in mesh-local space: subtract the actor's location (and undo its rotation and scale) to test a world position.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: query_point
params.description: [x, y, z] point in the mesh's local space, in cm (e.g. [0, 0, 50]).

params.name: winding_threshold
params.description: Optional float, default 0.5: the winding number above which the point counts as inside; higher values shrink the inside region, lower ones grow it.

params.name: max_distance
params.description: Optional float; it has no effect on this query, whose winding-number test uses no search distance.

params.name: allow_unsafe_modified
params.description: Optional; maps to bAllowUnsafeModifiedQueries (default false). It has no effect: the BVH is built fresh on every call, so it always matches the mesh.

commands.returns: { actor_name, is_inside: bool, containment_outcome: string } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label.

commands.name: recompute_mesh_normals
commands.description: Recompute the normals of the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, overwriting the values of its existing normal overlay while keeping its hard-edge splits; a mesh without normals first gets per-vertex normals. Face contributions are weighted by area and by corner angle (both on by default; both off gives a plain average). Idempotent, nothing saved: one undo step restores the previous normals, and a recompute that changes nothing adds no undo step. An empty mesh is an error, and recomputed is false (the call fails, leaving the mesh as it was) when the engine reports an error. Use it when shading looks wrong after geometry edits; copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh persists the result.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: angle_weighted
params.description: Weight contributing face normals by corner angle, default true

params.name: area_weighted
params.description: Weight contributing face normals by face area, default true

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, angle_weighted: bool, area_weighted: bool, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, recomputed: bool }

commands.name: recompute_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Re-flatten the UVs of one channel on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world island by island: each existing UV island (or polygroup) keeps its triangles and gets new UVs from the chosen flatten method, as one undo step; the level is marked dirty and nothing is saved. Use it to fix stretched islands while keeping the seams, then repack_mesh_uvs to lay them out in the 0-1 square; unwrap_mesh_uvs cuts new seams over the whole mesh and set_mesh_uvs_from_projection projects instead. An unknown actor, a channel the mesh lacks, an empty mesh, or an unknown island_source or method is an error before anything changes; when the engine refuses (polygroups on a mesh without polygroups) recomputed is false, the call fails and the UVs stay as they were.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, e.g. 'DynamicMeshActor_0'.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel index (default 0); get_dynamic_mesh_info shows the channels the mesh has.

params.name: island_source
params.description: What one island is: "uv_islands" (the channel's existing islands, default) or "polygroups" (one island per polygroup); case-insensitive, any other value is an error.

params.name: method
params.description: Flatten method: "spectral_conformal" (default), "conformal" or "exp_map"; case-insensitive.

commands.returns: { actor_name, uv_channel, island_source, method, recomputed }

commands.name: remap_material_ids
commands.description: Renumber MaterialIDs on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh. Two modes: pass from_material_id + to_material_id to merge one ID into another (UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshMaterialFunctions::RemapMaterialIDs), or pass compact=true with the material list to close gaps left by deleted/merged IDs (CompactMaterialIDs) and get back the compacted list to hand to copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh. Gaps matter: MaterialIDs index into that list positionally, so an unused ID in the middle costs a wasted material slot on the baked asset. The materials list may be shorter than the IDs in use (or absent): the missing entries count as no material. When no triangle carries from_material_id, or from and to are the same ID, the mesh is left unchanged and the call succeeds with applied false, triangles_remapped 0 and a note. Otherwise applied is measured (remap: the triangles that carried from_material_id no longer do; compact: the engine reported no error) and the call fails when it is false, leaving the MaterialIDs as they were. One undo step restores the previous MaterialIDs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: compact
params.description: Compact mode: renumber IDs to be contiguous from 0 (default false).

params.name: from_material_id
params.description: Remap mode: the MaterialID to replace. Required unless compact is true.

params.name: to_material_id
params.description: Remap mode: the MaterialID to replace it with. Required unless compact is true.

params.name: materials
params.description: Compact mode: ordered UMaterialInterface content paths, one per current MaterialID. The compacted list is returned in compacted_materials, in the new ID order.

params.name: remove_duplicate_materials
params.description: Compact mode: also merge IDs that point at the SAME material asset (default false).

commands.returns: { actor_name, mode: string, from_material_id: int, to_material_id: int, triangles_remapped?: int, max_material_id_after: int, distinct_material_ids_after: int, compacted_materials: [string], applied: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_dynamic_mesh_actor
commands.description: Destroy a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, found by label or object name, inside an undoable transaction. Returns the label, internal name and triangle_count_before of the destroyed actor; fails if the name matches no DynamicMeshActor. Create one with spawn_actor.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the DynamicMeshActor to destroy.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_internal_name: string, destroyed: bool, triangle_count_before: int, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_unused_vertices
commands.description: Deletes the orphan vertices (those no triangle uses) of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world and refreshes its render data; triangles and their shape are untouched. Remaining vertex IDs are not renumbered: run compact_mesh afterwards for dense IDs. A mesh without orphan vertices is a success with removed false and adds no undo step; otherwise one undo step restores the mesh. The level is marked dirty, nothing is saved to an asset; an unknown actor or one without a dynamic mesh is an error. Typical after delete_mesh_triangles or apply_mesh_boolean; open seams are closed by weld_mesh_edges, overlaps by repair_mesh_self_intersections, and get_dynamic_mesh_info reads the counts.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world; create one with spawn_actor.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, vertex_count_before: int, vertices_removed: int, removed: bool }

commands.name: repack_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Pack existing UV islands on a UV channel into standard UV space. A channel the mesh does not have, or an empty mesh, is an error checked before anything changes. A channel with no UVs set has no islands to pack: the call succeeds with repacked false and a note, leaving the mesh unchanged. Otherwise repacked is false, and the call fails, leaving the UVs as they were, when the engine reports an error. One undo step restores the previous UVs, nothing saved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV channel index (default 0)

params.name: target_image_width
params.description: target image width in pixels (default 512)

params.name: optimize_island_rotation
params.description: whether to optimize island rotation (default true)

commands.returns: { actor_name, uv_channel, target_image_width, optimize_island_rotation, num_uv_islands, repacked, note? }

commands.name: repair_mesh_self_intersections
commands.description: Boolean-union a DynamicMeshActor's dynamic mesh with itself to repair self-intersections, remove internal/floating geometry and resolve non-manifold overlaps (UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshBooleanFunctions::ApplyMeshSelfUnion). Convergent: the first pass mutates the mesh, but a second pass on the already-cleaned mesh is a no-op (repaired reports false). One undo step restores the mesh, and a pass that changes nothing adds no undo step. NOTE: the engine impl ignores its internal success flag and always returns the target mesh, so success is measured by comparing the triangle count, not by the return value.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor (mutated in place)

params.name: fill_holes
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshSelfUnionOptions.bFillHoles (default true)

params.name: trim_flaps
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshSelfUnionOptions.bTrimFlaps (default true)

params.name: simplify_output
params.description: Optional bool override for FGeometryScriptMeshSelfUnionOptions.bSimplifyOutput (default true)

params.name: winding_threshold
params.description: Optional [0..1] float override for FGeometryScriptMeshSelfUnionOptions.WindingThreshold (default 0.5). Space with generalised winding number above this is considered inside.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, vertex_count: int, is_closed: bool, repaired: bool }

commands.name: rotate_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Rotate all UVs of one channel on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world by an angle in degrees around a UV-space pivot; 0 degrees changes nothing (rotated false) and adds no undo step. One undo step restores the UVs; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel index; a channel the mesh does not have fails the call.

params.name: rotation_angle_deg
params.description: Rotation angle in degrees; 0 leaves the UVs untouched.

params.name: rotation_origin_u
params.description: U coordinate of the rotation pivot (default 0).

params.name: rotation_origin_v
params.description: V coordinate of the rotation pivot (default 0).

commands.returns: { actor_name, uv_channel, rotation_angle_deg, rotation_origin: {u, v}, rotated: bool }

commands.name: scale_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Scale all UVs of one channel on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world by separate U and V factors around the scale origin, as one undo step that restores the UVs; nothing is saved. The factors are checked as the floats the engine uses: a zero factor, or a scale shorter than 0.0001, which the engine would silently replace with 1, 1, is an error and nothing changes. A scale of 1, 1 changes nothing: scaled is false with a note, and no undo step is added. A channel the mesh lacks or an unknown actor is an error. Reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label. Offset UVs: translate_mesh_uvs; rotate them: rotate_mesh_uvs; copy a channel: copy_mesh_uv_channel.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel index; a channel the mesh does not have fails the call.

params.name: scale_u
params.description: Scale factor along U; must be non-zero (1 keeps U unchanged).

params.name: scale_v
params.description: Scale factor along V; must be non-zero (1 keeps V unchanged).

params.name: scale_origin_u
params.description: U coordinate of the point the scaling is centred on (default 0).

params.name: scale_origin_v
params.description: V coordinate of the point the scaling is centred on (default 0).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, uv_channel: int, scale_u: number, scale_v: number, scale_origin: { u, v }, scaled: bool, note: string? }

commands.name: select_mesh_triangles
commands.description: Resolve a region of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh into a triangle selection and report it, with its count and local-space bounding box, without modifying anything (no undo step, nothing dirtied). Read-only companion of set_mesh_material_id scope='region' (and of the region of set_mesh_uvs_from_projection): same region parameters, same resolver, so a region previewed here paints exactly those triangles there. The bounds are what turn a bisection answer ("the piece is somewhere in X>0") into numbers: centre and size. Use it to avoid the failure mode where a mis-specified box selects 0 triangles and the paint call still returns success. Coordinates are LOCAL to the dynamic mesh, not world.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: region
params.description: 'all' (default) | 'box' | 'sphere' | 'plane' | 'normal_angle' | 'material_id' | 'polygroup' | 'connected_component' (one physical PIECE, by the island index that get_mesh_components_detail reports).

params.name: center
params.description: Local [x,y,z] centre. Used by box/sphere, and as the plane origin.

params.name: extent
params.description: Local [x,y,z] HALF-size in cm. Required by region='box'.

params.name: radius
params.description: Radius in cm. Required by region='sphere'.

params.name: normal
params.description: [x,y,z] direction. Plane normal for region='plane', facing direction for 'normal_angle'. Default [0,0,1].

params.name: max_angle_deg
params.description: Max angle from normal in degrees for region='normal_angle' (default 15).

params.name: source_material_id
params.description: MaterialID to select when region='material_id'.

params.name: polygroup_id
params.description: Polygroup to select when region='polygroup'.

params.name: polygroup_layer
params.description: Optional extended polygroup layer index for region='polygroup'.

params.name: component_index
params.description: Island index when region='connected_component'. Get it from get_mesh_components_detail, which reports each piece's size and bounding box.

params.name: min_triangle_points
params.description: How many of a triangle's 3 points must be inside for it to count, 1-3 (default 3 = fully contained).

params.name: invert
params.description: Invert the spatial selection (default false).

params.name: include_triangle_ids
params.description: Also return the resolved triangle IDs (default false; they can be thousands). The returned array is what set_mesh_material_id scope='triangles' consumes.

params.name: max_triangle_ids
params.description: Cap on how many IDs to return when include_triangle_ids is on (default 1000). When the cap truncates, triangle_ids_truncated is true — the count in triangles_selected is still the real one.

commands.returns: { actor_name, region, triangles_selected: int, mesh_triangle_count: int, is_empty: bool, bounds: { min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x, max_y, max_z, center_x, center_y, center_z, size_x, size_y, size_z }, triangle_ids: [int], triangle_ids_truncated: bool } -- bounds are all 0 when the selection is empty.

commands.name: set_dynamic_mesh_material
commands.description: Sets the material of one slot on a DynamicMeshActor's DynamicMeshComponent in the editor world, in one undo step, and refreshes its render state; the level is marked dirty, not saved. applied is the slot read back; the call fails when the slot does not hold the material. Setting the material a slot already has succeeds again (applied true). A missing actor, component or material, or a slot_index outside the component's slots, is an error and nothing changes. Which triangles use a slot is their MaterialID: paint it with set_mesh_material_id and read it with get_mesh_material_ids. For static mesh actors use set_actor_material; get_available_materials lists material paths.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the DynamicMeshActor in the editor world (required).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Object path of a material or material instance (e.g. "/Engine/EngineMaterials/DefaultMaterial.DefaultMaterial"; a path without the .Name suffix also loads), as get_available_materials returns it (required).

params.name: slot_index
params.description: 0-based material slot, less than the component's slot count (slot 0 is always accepted); default 0.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, material_path: string, material_name: string, slot_index: int, applied: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: set_mesh_material_id
commands.description: Stamp a MaterialID onto triangles of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh. scope='all' repaints every triangle (UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshMaterialFunctions::ClearMaterialIDs); scope='triangles' repaints the listed triangle IDs (SetMaterialIDOnTriangles); scope='region' repaints every triangle inside a region resolved like select_mesh_triangles (SetMaterialIDForMeshSelection) -- a box, sphere, plane, normal angle, an existing MaterialID, one polygroup (region='polygroup' with polygroup_id: appended primitives are each their own polygroup, so this is usually the cheapest way to paint a part) or one connected component, the way to address pieces a boolean has fused. Calls EnableMaterialIDs first, because on a mesh without that attribute the engine drops the write. An ID in triangle_ids that is not a triangle, an empty mesh, or a polygroup layer the mesh does not have, is an error checked before anything is painted. A region that selects no triangle succeeds with applied false, triangles_selected 0 and a note, leaving the mesh unchanged. The targeted triangles are read back: applied is true when all of them carry material_id, and the call fails otherwise, leaving the MaterialIDs as they were. One undo step restores the previous MaterialIDs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: material_id
params.description: MaterialID to write (>= 0). Index into the material list later passed to copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: scope
params.description: 'all' | 'triangles' | 'region'. Default 'region' when region is given, else 'all'.

params.name: triangle_ids
params.description: Required when scope='triangles': array of triangle IDs to repaint (e.g. from select_mesh_triangles).

params.name: region
params.description: scope='region' only: 'all' (default) | 'box' | 'sphere' | 'plane' | 'normal_angle' | 'material_id' | 'polygroup' | 'connected_component' (one physical PIECE, by the island index that get_mesh_components_detail reports). Coordinates are LOCAL to the dynamic mesh, not world; preview a region with select_mesh_triangles.

params.name: center
params.description: Region parameter: local [x,y,z] centre. Used by box/sphere, and as the plane origin.

params.name: extent
params.description: Region parameter: local [x,y,z] HALF-size in cm. Required by region='box'.

params.name: radius
params.description: Region parameter: radius in cm. Required by region='sphere'.

params.name: normal
params.description: Region parameter: [x,y,z] direction. Plane normal for region='plane', facing direction for 'normal_angle'. Default [0,0,1].

params.name: max_angle_deg
params.description: Region parameter: max angle from normal in degrees for region='normal_angle' (default 15).

params.name: source_material_id
params.description: Region parameter: the MaterialID to SELECT when region='material_id'. Separate from material_id, which is the one being written, so 'repaint 1 as 2' is expressible.

params.name: polygroup_id
params.description: Region parameter: polygroup to select when region='polygroup'.

params.name: polygroup_layer
params.description: Region parameter: optional extended polygroup layer index for region='polygroup' (default the mesh's default polygroup layer). A layer the mesh does not have is an error.

params.name: component_index
params.description: Region parameter: island index when region='connected_component' (see get_mesh_components_detail).

params.name: min_triangle_points
params.description: Region parameter: how many of a triangle's 3 points must be inside for it to count, 1-3 (default 3 = fully contained). Only used by the spatial regions.

params.name: invert
params.description: Region parameter: invert a box, sphere, plane or normal_angle selection (default false).

commands.returns: { actor_name, material_id, scope, region?: string, triangles_selected?: int, triangles_targeted: int, triangles_painted: int, max_material_id_after: int, distinct_material_ids_after: int, applied: bool, note?: string } -- region and triangles_selected come with scope='region'.

commands.name: set_mesh_uv_element_position
commands.description: Set the (u, v) of one element of a UV channel overlay on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world; an invalid element ID writes nothing, adds no undo step and returns is_valid_element false, not an error. One undo step restores the element; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel index; a channel the mesh does not have fails the call.

params.name: element_id
params.description: ID of the element in the UV overlay of that channel, not a vertex, edge or triangle ID.

params.name: u
params.description: New U coordinate of the element.

params.name: v
params.description: New V coordinate of the element.

commands.returns: { actor_name, uv_channel, element_id, new_position: {u, v}, is_valid_element, set: bool }

commands.name: set_mesh_uvs_from_projection
commands.description: Replace the UVs of one channel on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world with a box, plane or cylinder projection, optionally only inside a region. Box suits plank-and-post geometry (each face takes the axis it faces), plane only flat pieces, cylinder wrapped shapes; projection 'plane' with scale [1,1,1] is a planar projection down mesh-local Z at 1 UV unit per cm. A uv_channel the mesh does not have yet is added first (the channel count only grows, so higher channels such as a lightmap UV1 are kept); uv_channel 8 or more is an error. One undo step restores the previous UVs and channel count. Returns triangles_affected and applied; when the engine reports an error, applied is false, the call fails and the mesh is left as it was.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: projection
params.description: 'box' (default) | 'plane' | 'cylinder'.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV channel to write, 0 to 7 (default 0); a channel the mesh lacks is added.

params.name: location
params.description: Local [x,y,z] origin of the projection shape (default the mesh origin).

params.name: rotation
params.description: [pitch, yaw, roll] of the projection shape (default none). For 'plane', this is what chooses which way the plane faces.

params.name: scale
params.description: [x,y,z] size of the projection shape (default [100,100,100]). THIS IS THE UV DENSITY KNOB: bigger scale = texture repeats fewer times. A tileable material that reads too big or too small is fixed here, not in the material.

params.name: min_island_tri_count
params.description: box only: islands smaller than this are merged into a neighbour (default 2).

params.name: split_angle
params.description: cylinder only: angle in degrees at which the wrap is split (default 45).

params.name: region
params.description: Optional region to limit the projection to; same vocabulary as select_mesh_triangles (default 'all').

params.name: component_index
params.description: Island index when region='connected_component'.

params.name: center
params.description: Region parameter (box/sphere centre, plane origin).

params.name: extent
params.description: Region parameter: box HALF-size.

params.name: radius
params.description: Region parameter: sphere radius.

params.name: normal
params.description: Region parameter: plane/normal_angle direction.

params.name: max_angle_deg
params.description: Region parameter for region='normal_angle'.

params.name: source_material_id
params.description: Region parameter for region='material_id'.

params.name: polygroup_id
params.description: Region parameter for region='polygroup'.

params.name: polygroup_layer
params.description: Region parameter for region='polygroup': extended polygroup layer index (default the mesh's default polygroup layer).

params.name: min_triangle_points
params.description: Region parameter, 1-3.

params.name: invert
params.description: Select the complement of a box, sphere, plane or normal_angle region (default false); the other regions ignore it.

commands.returns: { actor_name, projection, uv_channel, region, triangles_affected: int, uv_channel_count: int, uv_channels_added: int, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, applied: bool, note?: string } -- applied false with a note, and nothing changed, when no triangle is selected.

commands.name: set_num_extended_polygroup_layers
commands.description: Set the number of extended polygroup layers on the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshPolygroupFunctions::SetNumExtendedPolygroupLayers. Idempotent: the engine dedups (only reshapes attributes when the count actually differs from the current one), so re-setting the same count is a no-op. The layer count is read back AFTER the set via GetNumExtendedPolygroupLayers: applied is true when it equals the request, and the call fails, leaving the mesh as it was, when it does not. One undo step restores the previous layers.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: num_layers
params.description: Desired number of extended polygroup layers (>= 0).

commands.returns: { actor_name, requested_num_layers, num_polygroup_layers, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_num_uv_channels
commands.description: Set how many UV channels the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world has: added channels start without UVs, and channels from num_uv_channels upward are discarded with their UVs (note says so). The current count is a no-op (changed false). The engine allows at most 8, so a count above 8 is an error; num_uv_channels is the count read back after the call, and the call fails, leaving the mesh as it was, if it differs from the request. One undo step restores the previous channels with their UVs, nothing saved; reply actor_name is the component name, not the actor label. Fill a channel with copy_mesh_uv_channel or set_mesh_uvs_from_projection; clear_uv_channel works on static mesh assets.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: DynamicMeshActor name (required)

params.name: num_uv_channels
params.description: Desired count, 0 to 8 (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, num_uv_channels: int, previous_num_uv_channels: int, changed: bool, note?: string } -- actor_name is the dynamic mesh component's name, not the actor label; num_uv_channels is read back; note when channels were removed, whose UV data is dropped.

commands.name: simplify_mesh
commands.description: Simplifies the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world down toward target_triangle_count with attribute-aware QEM edge collapse, the shape kept as close as the count allows; the engine stops early when no further collapse is allowed, so triangle_count_after can stay above the target. A target at or above the current count, or an empty mesh, changes nothing (simplified false) and adds no undo step; otherwise one undo step restores the mesh. The level is marked dirty, nothing is saved to an asset. An unknown actor or a target of 0 or less is an error. For evenly sized triangles use apply_uniform_remesh, for density driven by a weight map apply_adaptive_remesh; read counts with get_dynamic_mesh_info and keep the result with copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name of the DynamicMeshActor in the editor world (case-insensitive); create one with spawn_actor.

params.name: target_triangle_count
params.description: Triangle count to simplify down to, greater than 0 (e.g. half of the triangle_count get_dynamic_mesh_info reports); at or above the current count nothing changes.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, target_triangle_count: int, triangle_count_before: int, triangle_count_after: int, vertex_count: int, simplified: bool }

commands.name: spawn_dynamic_mesh_actor
commands.description: Spawn an empty ADynamicMeshActor into the editor world (not PIE) at an optional location and rotation, ignoring collisions, in one undo step -- the editable-mesh actor the GeometryScript tools (add_mesh_primitive, apply_mesh_boolean...) work on; spawn_actor has no such type. Each call adds another actor. Returns its label as actor_name, its internal name and triangle_count (0). Keep a result with copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh; remove it with remove_dynamic_mesh_actor.

params.name: location
params.description: World location [x, y, z] in cm (default the world origin).

params.name: rotation
params.description: World rotation in degrees as [pitch, yaw, roll] (default no rotation).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_internal_name: string, actor_class: string, has_dynamic_mesh_component: bool, has_dynamic_mesh: bool, triangle_count: int, spawned: bool }

commands.name: transform_dynamic_mesh
commands.description: Move, rotate and/or scale every vertex of the live dynamic mesh of a DynamicMeshActor in the editor world about the mesh-local origin with one FTransform via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshTransformFunctions::TransformMesh, baking it into the geometry (the actor transform is not touched; calls accumulate), as one undo step that restores the mesh; pass only location (or translation), rotation or scale to apply just that part. A location, translation or scale that is not three numbers, a rotation that is neither three numbers nor a {pitch, yaw, roll} object, or an empty mesh, is an error. An identity transform succeeds with applied false and a note, leaving the mesh unchanged.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] translation; default (0,0,0)

params.name: translation
params.description: Optional alias of location, read only when location is absent.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] Euler rotation in degrees, or a {pitch, yaw, roll} object; default (0,0,0)

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] scale; default (1,1,1)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, location_x: number, location_y: number, location_z: number, rotation_pitch: number, rotation_yaw: number, rotation_roll: number, scale_x: number, scale_y: number, scale_z: number, applied: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: translate_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Offset every UV of one channel on a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world by (translate_u, translate_v), as one undo step that restores the UVs; the level is marked dirty and nothing is saved. Each call adds its offset again, so a retry shifts twice. A zero offset changes nothing (translated false) and adds no undo step. An unknown actor or a channel the mesh lacks is an error and nothing changes. The reply's actor_name is the component name, not the actor label. Scale or rotate the same channel with scale_mesh_uvs or rotate_mesh_uvs; to lay new UVs instead use set_mesh_uvs_from_projection or unwrap_mesh_uvs; get_dynamic_mesh_info shows the channels the mesh has.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name (case-insensitive) of the target DynamicMeshActor in the editor world, e.g. 'DynamicMeshActor_0'; spawn_actor with type DynamicMeshActor creates one.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel index, e.g. 0; a channel the mesh does not have fails the call.

params.name: translate_u
params.description: Offset added to every U coordinate, in UV units: 1.0 shifts by one full tile, 0.5 by half, negative moves left.

params.name: translate_v
params.description: Offset added to every V coordinate, in UV units: 1.0 shifts by one full tile, 0.5 by half, negative moves down.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, uv_channel: int, translate_u: number, translate_v: number, translated: bool }

commands.name: unwrap_mesh_uvs
commands.description: Compute a real UV UNWRAP for the whole mesh via UGeometryScriptLibrary_MeshUVFunctions::AutoGeneratePatchBuilderMeshUVs or AutoGenerateXAtlasMeshUVs. This is what sits behind the editor's "Auto UV" button. Use it when a projection is not enough (organic or mixed-orientation geometry); for plank-and-post shapes set_mesh_uvs_from_projection with box is usually cleaner and far cheaper. Both methods PACK the result into standard UV space by default, so island layout is handled too. SLOW on dense meshes: this is a solver, not a projection. A UV channel the mesh does not have, or an empty mesh, is an error; applied is false, and the call fails, leaving the UVs as they were, when the solver reports an error (xatlas needs a compact mesh: run compact_mesh first). One undo step restores the previous UVs.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the target DynamicMeshActor.

params.name: method
params.description: 'patch_builder' (default, the editor's Auto UV) or 'xatlas'.

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV channel to write (default 0).

params.name: initial_patch_count
params.description: patch_builder: how many patches to seed (default 100). More patches = less distortion, more seams.

params.name: min_patch_size
params.description: patch_builder: minimum triangles per patch (default 2).

params.name: merging_threshold
params.description: patch_builder: patch merging metric threshold (default 1.5). Higher merges more aggressively, giving fewer islands.

params.name: max_angle_deg
params.description: patch_builder: max angle in degrees between merged patches (default 45).

params.name: respect_polygroups
