params.description: patch_builder: seed patches from the existing polygroups instead of curvature (default false). Useful right after add_mesh_primitive, where each appended face is already its own group.

params.name: auto_pack
params.description: Pack the resulting islands into standard UV space (default true).

params.name: max_iterations
params.description: xatlas: solver iterations (default 2). Higher is slower and slightly tighter.

commands.returns: { actor_name, method, uv_channel, triangle_count: int, uv_channel_count: int, applied: bool }

commands.name: weld_mesh_edges
commands.description: Weld the coincident open boundary edges of a DynamicMeshActor's live dynamic mesh in the editor world (actor found by label or object name), merging boundary edge pairs whose endpoints lie within tolerance so cracks and duplicated seams close. The mesh changes in place as one undo step that restores it, and nothing is saved; a mesh with nothing to weld (closed, or no pair within tolerance) is a success with welded=false and adds no undo step. welded is true when the vertex or triangle count dropped; a failure the engine's welder reports makes success false and leaves the mesh as it was. A negative tolerance or an unknown actor is an error. Count open edges first with get_dynamic_mesh_info (num_open_border_edges); self-intersections: repair_mesh_self_intersections; orphan vertices: remove_unused_vertices; persist the result with copy_dynamic_mesh_to_static_mesh.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name of the DynamicMeshActor in the editor world (case-insensitive).

params.name: tolerance
params.description: Largest distance, in the mesh's local units (cm before actor scale), between the endpoints of two boundary edges for them to be welded; must be >= 0 (default 1e-06).

params.name: only_unique_pairs
params.description: When true (default), weld only edges that have exactly one coincident partner; false also merges ambiguous matches.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, tolerance: number, only_unique_pairs: bool, triangle_count: int, vertex_count: int, welded: bool }

commands.name: get_decal_info
commands.description: Read the decal settings of one ADecalActor in the editor world (not PIE), found by its editor label, without changing anything: DecalSize half-extents in cm (local space, before actor scale), sort order, fade screen size, fade-out and fade-in delays and durations in seconds, destroy-owner-after-fade, DecalColor as r, g, b, a and the decal material's path (empty when none). Use it to check a decal after spawn_decal_actor, or after changing its component with set_properties (object_path "<decal actor path>.DecalComponent", e.g. properties {"SortOrder":2}); for the actor's location and rotation use the actor transform tools. A label with no decal actor (the match is on the label, not the object name), or no editor world, is an error.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the ADecalActor, e.g. "Decal_Blood_01", as spawn_decal_actor set it or the Outliner shows it (case-insensitive, first match).

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, decal_size_x: float, decal_size_y: float, decal_size_z: float, sort_order: int, fade_screen_size: float, fade_start_delay: float, fade_duration: float, fade_in_start_delay: float, fade_in_duration: float, destroy_owner_after_fade: bool, r: float, g: float, b: float, a: float, decal_material: string }

commands.name: set_decal_color
commands.description: Set DecalColor on an editor-world ADecalActor found by label; it only shows if the decal material uses a Decal Color node. A color that is not a 4-number array is ignored (current color kept). A change is one undo step that dirties the level; nothing is saved. Returns the resulting r, g, b, a. An unknown label is an error; read it back with get_decal_info.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the ADecalActor in the editor world.

params.name: color
params.description: Array of exactly 4 numbers [r, g, b, a], a linear color such as [1, 0.5, 0, 1]; missing or another length keeps the current DecalColor.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, r: float, g: float, b: float, a: float }

commands.name: set_decal_fade
commands.description: Set a UDecalComponent's fade fields on a named DecalActor: fade-out timing, fade-in timing, the destroy-owner-after-fade bit and the fade screen size (the screen-size fraction below which the decal fades out).  Writes the EditAnywhere fields directly (mirrors the details panel) so values round-trip exactly, avoiding SetFadeOut's global fade-scale CVar and SetLifeSpan side effect, so no lifespan timer starts in the editor.  Only provided fields change (partial, idempotent); a change is one undo step that dirties the level, nothing is saved. An unknown label, or a fade_screen_size that is not a number of at least 0, is an error before anything is written. Read the values back with get_decal_info.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the ADecalActor in the editor world.

params.name: fade_start_delay
params.description: Optional seconds before fade-out begins (FadeStartDelay; 0 + fade_duration 0 = persistent).

params.name: fade_duration
params.description: Optional fade-out duration in seconds (FadeDuration).

params.name: fade_in_start_delay
params.description: Optional seconds before fade-in begins (FadeInStartDelay).

params.name: fade_in_duration
params.description: Optional fade-in duration in seconds (FadeInDuration).

params.name: destroy_owner_after_fade
params.description: Optional: destroy the owning actor after fully fading out (bDestroyOwnerAfterFade).

params.name: fade_screen_size
params.description: Optional FadeScreenSize, a number >= 0 (typically 0..1; smaller fades the decal only when it gets very small on screen).

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, fade_start_delay: float, fade_duration: float, fade_in_start_delay: float, fade_in_duration: float, destroy_owner_after_fade: bool, fade_screen_size: float, applied_count: int }

commands.name: set_decal_material
commands.description: Assign a material to the UDecalComponent of an ADecalActor in the editor world, found by actor label (not object name), in place of its current one. material_path is loaded as a UMaterialInterface (it renders only with the Deferred Decal material domain) and echoed back as given, not read back. The change is one undo step and dirties the level; nothing is saved. Assigning the material it already has changes nothing and adds no undo step. An unknown label, an actor without a decal component, or a path that does not load as a material is an error. Read back with get_decal_info; spawn_decal_actor can set one at creation; tint: set_decal_color; projection box: set_decal_size.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Actor label of the ADecalActor in the editor world (case-insensitive; the object name does not match).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInterface, e.g. "/Game/Decals/M_Decal_Crack" (the object path form also works); echoed back as given.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, material_path: string }

commands.name: set_decal_size
commands.description: Set the DecalSize half-extents (cm, in the decal's local space, before actor scale) of an ADecalActor's UDecalComponent in the editor world, found by actor label, and refresh its render state. A valid decal_size [x, y, z] wins over size_x, size_y and size_z; without it each given axis changes and the rest keep their value, and a call with none changes nothing. X is the projection depth, Y and Z the footprint. Values are not validated; a change is one undo step that dirties the level, and nothing is saved. An unknown label or an actor without a decal component is an error. Read back with get_decal_info; set it at spawn with spawn_decal_actor; draw order: set_decal_sort_order.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Actor label of the ADecalActor in the editor world (case-insensitive; the object name does not match).

params.name: decal_size
params.description: Optional array of exactly 3 numbers [x, y, z], the half-extents in cm; when valid it overrides size_x, size_y and size_z, and any other length is ignored.

params.name: size_x
params.description: Optional X half-extent in cm (the projection depth); used only without a valid decal_size.

params.name: size_y
params.description: Optional Y half-extent in cm; used only without a valid decal_size.

params.name: size_z
params.description: Optional Z half-extent in cm; used only without a valid decal_size.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, size_x: float, size_y: float, size_z: float }

commands.name: set_decal_sort_order
commands.description: Set the SortOrder of the UDecalComponent of an ADecalActor in the editor world, found by actor label: where decals overlap, a higher sort order draws later, on top of a lower one. sort_order is required; a missing one is an error and nothing is written. A change is one undo step that dirties the level; the order the decal already has changes nothing, and nothing is saved. An unknown label or an actor without a decal component is an error. Read it back with get_decal_info; set the material with set_decal_material and the projection box with set_decal_size.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the ADecalActor in the editor world.

params.name: sort_order
params.description: New sort order value, a whole number (a fraction is rounded); required.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, sort_order: int }

commands.name: spawn_decal_actor
commands.description: Spawn a DecalActor labelled actor_label in the editor world with its DecalSize half-extent and optional material in one call; spawn_actor has no decal type. Idempotent by label: an existing one is REUSED, moved to location/rotation (origin/zero when omitted) and DecalSize reset (default 128,256,256). decal_size must be [x, y, z]; a material_path that does not load is an error and nothing is spawned or moved. No undo; not saved (save_level).

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label for the spawned (or re-used) ADecalActor.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location (default 0,0,0).

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation.

params.name: decal_size
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] half-extent for DecalSize (default 128,256,256).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Optional content path of a UMaterialInterface to assign to the decal; a path that does not load is an error and nothing is spawned or changed.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, reused: bool, decal_size_x: float, decal_size_y: float, decal_size_z: float, decal_material: string }

commands.name: create_hlod_layer
commands.description: Creates and saves a new UHLODLayer (World Partition HLOD layer) asset.  Idempotent on re-run: an HLOD layer already at the path is returned unchanged with created=false, already_exists=true and saved=false, layer_type not applied and nothing saved; an asset of another class there is an error. Sets default streaming-grid cell_size=25600, loading_range=51200. Layer type accepts 'Instancing', 'MeshApproximate' (also 'Custom'/'CustomHLODActor'). Defaults to 'Instancing'. A failed save makes success false with saved=false. Change it later with set_hlod_layer_settings.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new HLOD layer asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder; defaults to /Game/HLOD

params.name: layer_type
params.description: Optional EHLODLayerType string; defaults to "Instancing"

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, layer_type: string, cell_size: int, loading_range: number, created: bool, already_exists?: bool, success: bool, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: get_hlod_layer_actors
commands.description: Enumerate which LOADED actors in the current editor world are assigned to a given UHLODLayer (read-side of set_hlod_layer_actors). Two limits worth knowing before you trust an empty result: it only sees actors currently loaded, and it is WORLD PARTITION ONLY -- on a non-WP world it returns not_applicable=true with a note instead of a list, because there the assignment would not survive a Generate anyway.

params.name: hlod_layer_path
params.description: Full /Game path of the UHLODLayer asset (matches against AActor::HLODLayer::GetPathName()).

commands.returns: { hlod_layer_path, world, is_world_partition, not_applicable, note?, total: int, actors: [{actor_name, actor_path, actor_label}] }

commands.name: get_hlod_layer_info
commands.description: Read one World Partition HLOD layer asset (UHLODLayer): its layer type (Instancing, MeshMerge, MeshSimplify, MeshApproximate, Custom or CustomHLODActor) and its streaming-grid settings, cell_size and loading_range in centimetres and is_spatially_loaded. Read-only: it loads the asset and changes nothing. A path that does not load as an HLOD layer is an error. The grid fields are read by reflection because the engine deprecated them in 5.7; on a build without them they read 0 and false. Find layer paths with get_hlod_layers; change these values with set_hlod_layer_settings, the parent with set_hlod_layer_parent, and list the actors using the layer with get_hlod_layer_actors.

params.name: hlod_layer_path
params.description: Object or package path of the HLOD layer asset, e.g. '/Game/HLOD/HLOD_Instanced' (as get_hlod_layers lists it).

commands.returns: { hlod_layer_path: string, asset_path: string, name: string, layer_type: string, cell_size: int, loading_range: number, is_spatially_loaded: bool }

commands.name: get_hlod_layers
commands.description: List every World Partition HLOD layer asset (UHLODLayer and subclasses) under a content folder and its subfolders, found through the Asset Registry, with each one's name, object path and layer type (Instancing, MeshMerge, MeshSimplify, MeshApproximate, Custom or CustomHLODActor). Each layer asset is loaded to read its type, but nothing is changed or saved. A folder with no layers, or one that does not exist, gives an empty list and count 0, not an error. Use it to find a layer path, then read one layer's grid settings with get_hlod_layer_info or its assigned actors with get_hlod_layer_actors; create_hlod_layer makes a new one and set_hlod_layer_settings changes one.

params.name: path
params.description: Optional content folder searched recursively, as a long package path, e.g. '/Game/HLOD'; default /Game.

commands.returns: { path: string, hlod_layers: [{ name, path, layer_type }], count: int }

commands.name: set_hlod_layer_actors
commands.description: Assign a UHLODLayer to a BATCH of loaded actors in the current editor world -- or clear it from them by passing hlod_layer_path="". WORLD PARTITION ONLY: on a non-WP world it returns not_applicable=true and changes nothing. Idempotent per actor: one that already has that layer is not touched at all and comes back counted as unchanged, so the changed/unchanged/cleared split tells you exactly what really moved.

params.name: actor_paths
params.description: JSON array of actor paths (long package paths or object paths) to assign.

params.name: hlod_layer_path
params.description: Full /Game path of the UHLODLayer asset. Pass empty string ("") to clear.

commands.returns: { hlod_layer_path, world, is_world_partition, not_applicable, note?, requested: int, changed: int, unchanged: int, cleared: int, not_found: [paths], changed_actors: [{actor_path, old_hlod_layer, new_hlod_layer}] }

commands.name: set_hlod_layer_parent
commands.description: Sets (or clears) the parent UHLODLayer of a UHLODLayer and saves it.  The parent chain drives nested HLOD generation (a layer's HLOD becomes an input to its parent's HLOD). Send parent_layer_path="" to clear the parent to null; omit parent_layer_path to leave it untouched. Idempotent: if the parent is already the requested value, nothing is modified/saved (changed_parent=false, saved=false). Validates against self-parent and circular parent chains (the engine's guard is editor-only and does not run headless).

params.name: hlod_layer_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the child HLOD layer asset

params.name: parent_layer_path
params.description: Optional full /Game path to the parent HLOD layer; "" clears to null; absent leaves it untouched

commands.returns: { hlod_layer_path: string, asset_path: string, parent_layer_path: string, has_parent: bool, changed_parent: bool, settings_set: bool, saved: bool, note: string? }

commands.name: set_hlod_layer_settings
commands.description: Sets streaming-grid settings / layer type on a UHLODLayer and saves it.  Partial update: only the fields you send are touched. Sending cell_size or loading_range also enables the layer spatially loaded. Layer type accepts 'Instancing'|'MeshApproximate'|'Custom'|'CustomHLODActor'.

params.name: hlod_layer_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the HLOD layer asset

params.name: cell_size
params.description: Optional streaming-grid cell size

params.name: loading_range
params.description: Optional streaming-grid loading range

params.name: layer_type
params.description: Optional EHLODLayerType string

commands.returns: { hlod_layer_path: string, asset_path: string, layer_type: string, cell_size: int, loading_range: number, changed_cell_size: bool, changed_loading_range: bool, changed_layer_type: bool, settings_set: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: add_input_modifier
commands.description: Reshape the VALUE a key sends before the action sees it: append a modifier (Negate to flip an axis, Swizzle to remap X/Y/Z, DeadZone for stick drift, Scalar for sensitivity) to a key mapping in a mapping context. This is how one Axis2D action serves WASD -- S is W negated, not a second action. Modifiers change the value, triggers change when it fires (add_input_trigger); list_input_types enumerates the classes, remove_input_modifier undoes it by index. The context is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

params.name: context_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputMappingContext.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputAction.

params.name: key
params.description: Key name of the mapping the modifier is attached to.

params.name: modifier_type
params.description: One of "Negate", "Swizzle", "DeadZone", "Scalar".

params.name: context_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Mapping Context

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: key_name
params.description: Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom)

commands.returns: { context_name, action_name, key, modifier_type, modifier_class, index, modifier_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: add_input_trigger
commands.description: Decide WHEN a key fires its action: append a trigger (Down / Pressed / Released / Hold / Tap / Pulse / ChordAction) so a key can mean tap-to-do-X and hold-to-do-Y instead of consuming two keys. Targets either one key mapping inside a mapping context (pass context + key) or, with no context and no key, the InputAction asset's own Triggers array -- the difference decides whether the rule applies to that binding or to the action everywhere, so a key without a context is refused rather than read as the action. The edited asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Tune it afterwards with set_input_action_trigger_behavior; list_input_types enumerates the classes.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputAction.

params.name: trigger_type
params.description: One of "Down", "Pressed", "Released", "Hold", "Tap", "Pulse", "ChordAction".

params.name: context_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputMappingContext. Omit it (and context_path) to append the trigger to the InputAction asset's own Triggers array instead of one of its key mappings.

params.name: key
params.description: Key name of the mapping the trigger is attached to: required with a context, and refused when there is no context.

params.name: context_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Mapping Context, instead of context_name.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: key_name
params.description: Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom)

commands.returns: Context target: { context_name, action_name, key, trigger_type, trigger_class, index, trigger_count, saved, save_error? }; Action target: { action_name, action_path, trigger_type, trigger_class, index, trigger_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: add_mapping_to_context
commands.description: Bind a key to an InputAction in a saved Enhanced Input mapping context, addressing each asset by SHORT ASSET NAME (IMC_Foo / IA_Bar) or by full object path. Returns the mapping index, which is what add_input_trigger / add_input_modifier / get_input_mapping_context (mapping_index) address. A context that already maps that key to that action keeps its mapping (added false, already_mapped true, not saved); a new mapping succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Other actions on the same key are not checked: use find_free_input_key or list_all_input_mappings first.

params.name: context_name
params.description: Short asset name (e.g. IMC_Example) or full object path of the InputMappingContext.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Short asset name (e.g. IA_Example) or full object path of the InputAction.

params.name: key
params.description: Key name to map (e.g. "SpaceBar", "W", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom").

params.name: context_path
params.description: Alias of context_name, read only when context_name is absent.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Alias of action_name, read only when action_name is absent.

params.name: input_action_path
params.description: Second alias of action_name, read only when action_name and action_path are both absent.

params.name: key_name
params.description: Alias of key, read only when key is absent (same FKey names).

commands.returns: { context_name, context_path, action_name, action_path (resolved object path), key, key_name (same as key), index, mapping_count, added, already_mapped, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: create_force_feedback_effect
commands.description: Create a force feedback effect asset (the controller rumble a Play Force Feedback call plays) at package_path/name, with one default channel (all four motors affected, an intensity curve with no keys, so it does not vibrate until the curve is keyed), then save it; there is no undo step. Idempotent: when a force feedback effect already exists at that path it is loaded and returned as it is, with already_existed true, and nothing is saved. An asset of another type at the path, or an invalid name, is an error and nothing changes; a failed save is an error, the new asset staying only in memory. Edit its channels and curves with set_properties (ChannelDetails) on the asset path and read them back with get_properties.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name without folder, e.g. "FFE_Rumble".

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/Input/Feedback" (optional, default "/Game/Gameplay"); a trailing slash is ignored.

commands.returns: { name: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, channel_detail_count: number, is_force_feedback_effect: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: create_input_action
commands.description: Create an Enhanced Input InputAction asset (IA_): the verb half of a keybinding -- what the player does, independent of which key does it. Pick value_type up front (Bool for a button, Axis1D for a trigger/scroll, Axis2D for a stick or WASD, Axis3D), then bind it to a key inside a mapping context with add_mapping_to_context. Changing the type later is set_input_action_value_type; behaviour flags are set_input_action_flags. The asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Name of the new InputAction.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Input).

params.name: path
params.description: Fallback for package_path when package_path is absent.

params.name: value_type
params.description: Value type Bool (default), Axis1D, Axis2D, or Axis3D.

commands.returns: { action_name, action_path, value_type, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: create_input_mapping_context
commands.description: Create an Enhanced Input mapping context asset (IMC_): the container that binds keys to InputActions and can be pushed and popped as a set. Prefer a context per MODE (driving, swimming, building, menu) over one key per verb -- pushing a context re-purposes the existing keys instead of consuming another global one. Empty on creation: fill it with add_mapping_to_context, and check the keys are free first with find_free_input_key. The asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

params.name: context_name
params.description: Name of the new InputMappingContext.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Input).

params.name: path
params.description: Fallback for package_path when package_path is absent.

commands.returns: { context_name, context_path, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: find_free_input_key
commands.description: Which keys are still FREE: lists every input key not bound by any Enhanced Input mapping context or legacy mapping, filterable by category (keyboard / gamepad / mouse / touch) and substring, plus the matching keys that are already bound. The complement of list_all_input_mappings and the tool to run before binding a new keyboard shortcut, since a collision compiles silently and only shows up in play. Also the spelling lookup for any key the engine defines: with bindable_only=false and no category, free_keys + bound_keys together are the full engine key list, each with its exact FKey name ("SpaceBar", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom") and its display name. Trustworthy where the Python route is not: InputMappingContext.mappings is deprecated and returns empty, which makes every taken key look available.

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring matched against the key name or display name.

params.name: category
params.description: Optional key category filter: one of 'keyboard', 'gamepad', 'mouse', 'touch'. Absent = all categories.

params.name: bindable_only
params.description: When true (default), only keys where FKey::IsBindableInBlueprints() is true are considered (skips AnyKey/gestures/etc.). false lists every valid key the engine defines.

commands.returns: { free_keys:[{name (the FKey name binding calls take), key (same), display_name, is_gamepad, is_mouse, is_analog}], free_key_count, bound_keys:[...same shape], bound_key_count (keys bound anywhere, unfiltered), key_count (free_keys + bound_keys listed) }

commands.name: get_input_action
commands.description: Read one Enhanced Input InputAction asset in full: its value type (Bool / Axis1D / Axis2D / Axis3D), its accumulation behaviour, all the consume/pause/reserve flags, and the triggers and modifiers attached to the ACTION itself. The read-back oracle for create_input_action, set_input_action_value_type and set_input_action_flags, and the place to check b_consume_input -- an action left consuming input can swallow a key for the whole game. Triggers listed here are the action's own; the ones on a specific key binding live in the mapping context (get_input_mapping_context, per mapping).

params.name: action_path
params.description: Full path to the InputAction asset (e.g., /Game/Input/IA_Jump).

params.name: action_name
params.description: Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent (short asset name).

commands.returns: { action_path, action_name, value_type, accumulation_behavior, b_consume_input, b_trigger_when_paused, b_consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, b_reserve_all_mappings, trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys, action_description, b_tap, triggers, modifiers }

commands.name: get_input_action_state
commands.description: Read the live Enhanced Input state of one InputAction for a local player in a running PIE or game session: is_tracked, trigger_events, value, last_triggered_world_time and the mapping contexts that carry it, applied or not. It is the oracle for whether an input fired, since inject_key_input and trigger_input_action succeed either way: read it before and after, and an advancing last_triggered_world_time is the proof. is_mapped_in_applied_context false means no applied context maps it (removed on mounting, in a vehicle or a menu); is_tracked false means the engine is not evaluating it, typically an unpossessed pawn. In co-op, world picks which local player is read.

params.name: action
params.description: InputAction to read: full object path or short asset name. Aliases: action_path, action_name.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Local player index (default 0).

params.name: world
params.description: World selector: 'pie' (default) | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game'.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Alias of action, read when action is absent or empty: InputAction object path or short asset name.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Alias of action, read only when action is absent or empty and action_path is absent: InputAction object path or short asset name.

commands.returns: { action_path: string, action_name: string, value_type: string, is_enhanced_input: bool, is_tracked: bool, is_mapped_in_applied_context: bool, trigger_event: number, trigger_events: array, value: array, elapsed_seconds: number, triggered_seconds: number, last_triggered_world_time: number, world_time_seconds: number, contexts_mapping_action: array, contexts_mapping_action_count: number, applied_context_count: number, player_index: number, player_controller: string, player_input_class: string, world: string, note: string }

commands.name: get_input_mapping_context
commands.description: Read ONE Enhanced Input mapping context asset (IMC): every action-to-key mapping it declares, each with its raw Mappings[] index and the triggers attached to that binding (the read-back for add_input_trigger and the trigger_index remove_input_trigger takes); mapping_index narrows the answer to one binding. An IMC asset stores no priority -- that is given when the context is added to a player (AddMappingContext), so it is not reported here. The per-asset reader, and the reliable one -- the Python property InputMappingContext.mappings is deprecated and hands back an EMPTY list without failing, so a scan built on it reports a fully-bound context as empty. Triggers on the InputAction asset itself are in get_input_action. Use list_all_input_mappings for the project-wide "which keys are taken / which conflict" question.

params.name: context_path
params.description: Full path (e.g., /Game/Input/IMC_Default) or short asset name of the InputMappingContext.

params.name: ctx_path
params.description: Alias of context_path, read only when context_path is absent.

params.name: mapping_index
params.description: Optional 0-based index into the context's Mappings[] (the index add_mapping_to_context returns): only that binding is returned, even one without an action. Out of range is an error.

commands.returns: { context_path, context_name, mappings: [{ index, action_name, key (display name), key_name (the FKey name add_mapping_to_context takes), triggers: [{ index, class_name, display_name }], trigger_count }], mapping_count, total_mapping_count }

commands.name: get_input_settings
commands.description: Read the project's LEGACY input mappings from UInputSettings: named action mappings (key + shift/ctrl/alt/cmd modifiers) and axis mappings (key + scale), each with its row count, in one call. Legacy only -- it does NOT see Enhanced Input mapping contexts, so on an Enhanced Input project it can return almost nothing while the game is fully bound. For the complete picture across both systems use list_all_input_mappings; for one Enhanced Input context use get_input_mapping_context.
commands.returns: { action_mappings: [{ action_name, key, shift, ctrl, alt, cmd }], action_mapping_count, axis_mappings: [{ axis_name, key, scale }], axis_mapping_count }

commands.name: get_player_input
commands.description: Read what a player is pressing RIGHT NOW: resolves the PlayerController for a local player index and returns it plus the currently pressed keys. Runtime state, so it needs a live PIE/game session -- an empty pressed_keys outside PIE means nothing. For which keys are BOUND (a static question) use list_all_input_mappings instead; to make an action fire use trigger_input_action.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Player controller index to query (default 0).

commands.returns: { player_controller, pressed_keys }

commands.name: list_all_input_mappings
commands.description: Which keys are already TAKEN, and which ones CONFLICT: aggregates every key-to-action binding across ALL Enhanced Input mapping context assets plus the legacy InputSettings action/axis mappings, and flags any key bound to more than one distinct action. Run it BEFORE claiming a new key -- a keybinding collision does not fail to compile, it surfaces weeks later inside another system. This is the aggregate you can trust: the Python route (InputMappingContext.mappings) is deprecated and returns an EMPTY list, which reads as "every key is free" even when every letter is taken. Use find_free_input_key for the complement (what is still unbound), get_input_mapping_context for one context.

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring on the key name to narrow the returned key_bindings.

params.name: conflicts_only
params.description: When true, return only keys flagged as conflicts (more than one distinct action on the same key). Default false.

commands.returns: { contexts:[{context_path,context_name,mapping_count}], context_count, key_bindings:[{key,display_name,bindings:[{action,source,context_path}],binding_count,distinct_action_count,conflict}], bound_key_count, conflicts:[...], conflict_count, legacy_action_mapping_count, legacy_axis_mapping_count }

commands.name: list_input_types
commands.description: One-call inventory of what Enhanced Input offers in this build: the four InputAction value types (the names create_input_action and set_input_action_value_type take) plus every concrete modifier and trigger subclass, including any the project or a plugin added. Run it before add_input_trigger / add_input_modifier so you pass a class that actually exists instead of guessing a name. Read-only.
commands.returns: { value_types: ["Bool", "Axis1D", "Axis2D", "Axis3D"], value_type_count, modifier_count, trigger_count, modifier_types: [{ class_name, display_name }], trigger_types: [{ class_name, display_name }] }

commands.name: register_input_key_mapping
commands.description: Rebind a player-mappable Enhanced Input mapping to another key for one local player of a running PIE or game session, the way a key-rebinding options menu does (UEnhancedInputUserSettings::MapPlayerKey). It changes that player's user settings in memory only: no asset is edited, nothing is saved, no undo step. To change the key a mapping context asset declares use add_mapping_to_context and remove_mapping_from_context; back to the default key: unregister_input_key_mapping; taken keys: list_all_input_mappings or find_free_input_key. Start PIE first (start_play_in_editor): without a running PIE or game world the call is refused and nothing changes. It also needs Enhanced Input user settings enabled in the project (EnhancedInputDeveloperSettings bEnableUserSettings, before PIE starts) and a context with player-mappable keys applied to that player. A missing mapping_name or an invalid key name is an error before anything changes; when the engine refuses the remap, applied is false, success is false and failure_tags gives its reasons. player_controller and the world fields name the controller and world that were used.

params.name: mapping_name
params.description: Name of the player-mappable key mapping to rebind, as set in its Player Mappable Key Settings, e.g. "Jump" (required).

params.name: new_key
params.description: Unreal key name to bind, e.g. "SpaceBar", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom" or "LeftMouseButton"; must be a valid FKey (required).

params.name: player_controller_name
params.description: Optional object name or actor label of the PlayerController to remap, e.g. "PlayerController_0" (case-insensitive), searched in every running PIE or game world; when given, player_index is ignored.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Local player whose binding changes, in the play world: 0 (default) is the first player controller, any other value matches a local player's controller id.

params.name: slot
params.description: Which of the player's key slots to set: "First" (default), "Second", "Third" or "Fourth"; an unknown name silently means "First".

commands.returns: { applied: bool, mapping_name: string, new_key: string, slot: string, failure_tags: [string], player_controller: string, world_name: string, world_package: string, world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: remove_input_modifier
commands.description: Delete one modifier from a key mapping in an Enhanced Input mapping context, by mapping_index + modifier_index -- e.g. removing a Negate that flipped an axis the wrong way -- and save the context; the call succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Indices shift after a removal, so work from the highest down. add_input_modifier is the inverse.

params.name: ctx_path
params.description: Asset path of the UInputMappingContext

params.name: mapping_index
params.description: 0-based index of the FEnhancedActionKeyMapping

params.name: modifier_index
params.description: 0-based index of the modifier within Mapping.Modifiers

commands.returns: { applied, removed_class_name, remaining_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: remove_input_trigger
commands.description: Delete one trigger from a key mapping in an Enhanced Input mapping context, by mapping_index + trigger_index -- e.g. dropping a Hold so the key fires immediately again -- and save the context; the call succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Get the indices from get_input_mapping_context (mappings[].index, mappings[].triggers[].index); they shift after a removal, so work from the highest down.

params.name: ctx_path
params.description: Asset path of the UInputMappingContext

params.name: mapping_index
params.description: 0-based index of the FEnhancedActionKeyMapping

params.name: trigger_index
params.description: 0-based index of the trigger within Mapping.Triggers

commands.returns: { applied, removed_class_name, remaining_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: remove_mapping_from_context
commands.description: Unbind a key from an InputAction in a saved Enhanced Input mapping context -- how you free a key that list_all_input_mappings flagged as conflicting, or retire a verb. Identified by context + action + key, so only the first mapping of that action to that key goes; the assets themselves survive. The engine moves the context's last mapping into the freed slot, so mapping indexes (add_input_trigger, get_input_mapping_context) can change. The context is saved, and a removal succeeds only when it reaches disk; a mapping that is not there succeeds with removed false and already_absent true, and saves nothing.

params.name: context_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputMappingContext.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Short asset name of the InputAction.

params.name: key
params.description: Key name of the mapping to remove.

params.name: context_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Mapping Context

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: key_name
params.description: Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom)

commands.returns: { context_name, action_name, key, removed, already_absent, mapping_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_input_action_flags
commands.description: Set an InputAction's behaviour flags: consume_input, trigger_when_paused, consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, reserve_all_mappings, the legacy-key consume bitmask, accumulation behaviour and the editor description. Handle consume_input with care -- it is the flag that decides whether OTHER actions on the same key still fire, and turning it on can swallow the game's interaction key entirely, a failure that shows up in an unrelated system days later. Only the fields you pass change, and a call that passes none is an error; the action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Verify with get_input_action.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Input action name

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action

params.name: consume_input
params.description: When set, updates the action's bConsumeInput flag.

params.name: trigger_when_paused
params.description: When set, updates the action's bTriggerWhenPaused flag.

params.name: consumes_action_and_axis_mappings
params.description: When set, updates bConsumesActionAndAxisMappings.

params.name: reserve_all_mappings
params.description: When set, updates bReserveAllMappings.

params.name: trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys
params.description: When set (int32 ETriggerEvent bitmask), updates TriggerEventsThatConsumeLegacyKeys.

params.name: accumulation_behavior
params.description: When set, one of "TakeHighestAbsoluteValue" or "Cumulative".

params.name: action_description
params.description: When set, updates the action's ActionDescription (FText) shown in the editor.

commands.returns: { action_name, action_path, b_consume_input, b_trigger_when_paused, b_consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, b_reserve_all_mappings, trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys, accumulation_behavior, action_description, flags_set, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_input_action_trigger_behavior
commands.description: Tune HOW an input trigger fires on an InputAction: actuation threshold, hold time and one-shot for Hold triggers, tap release window for Tap, time-dilation sensitivity for timed ones -- i.e. how long "hold E to interact" must be held. Address the trigger either by index or by trigger_class (first of that type). Only the fields you pass change; the action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Add the trigger first with add_input_trigger and re-read with get_input_action.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path of the Input Action (or short asset name).

params.name: action_name
params.description: Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent.

params.name: trigger_index
params.description: Index into the action's Triggers array to edit. Mutually exclusive with trigger_class.

params.name: trigger_class
params.description: Select the first trigger of this type (Down|Pressed|Released|Hold|Tap|Pulse|ChordAction) instead of an index.

params.name: actuation_threshold
params.description: When set, the base UInputTrigger::ActuationThreshold (float).

params.name: hold_time_threshold
params.description: When set, UInputTriggerHold::HoldTimeThreshold (float). Hold triggers only.

params.name: is_one_shot
params.description: When set, UInputTriggerHold::bIsOneShot (bool). Hold triggers only.

params.name: tap_release_time
params.description: When set, UInputTriggerTap::TapReleaseTimeThreshold (float). Tap triggers only.

params.name: affected_by_time_dilation
params.description: When set, UInputTriggerTimedBase::bAffectedByTimeDilation (bool). Timed triggers only.

commands.returns: { action_path, action_name, trigger_index, trigger_class, properties_set, trigger, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_input_action_value_type
commands.description: Change an InputAction's value type after the fact (button vs axis: Bool / Axis1D / Axis2D / Axis3D). Not cosmetic -- the type decides what shape of value the bound handlers receive and what trigger_input_action must inject, so switching it can break existing graph pins. Re-read with get_input_action and re-check the handlers. The action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Asset path to the input action

params.name: value_type
params.description: One of "Bool", "Float", "Int", "Vector2D", "Vector", "Rotator", "String", etc.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent.

commands.returns: { action_name, action_path, value_type, value_type_set, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: trigger_input_action
commands.description: Inject a value for an Enhanced Input action into a local player's UEnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem in a running PIE or game session, so the real bound handlers run with the action's own modifiers and triggers (headless key injection never reaches Enhanced Input). dispatched true does not prove a handler fired: compare get_input_action_state before and after.

params.name: action
params.description: Full object path of a UInputAction, or its short asset name (required).

params.name: value_json
params.description: The value to inject, coerced to the action's ValueType: bool (Boolean), number (Axis1D), or a [x,y]/[x,y,z] array or {x,y,z} object (Axis2D/Axis3D). If omitted, Boolean actions default to true (pressed) and axis actions default to zero.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Local player index used to resolve the PlayerController (default 0).

params.name: hold_seconds
params.description: Optional float. When > 0, the value is re-injected every tick for this many seconds (so a movement AXIS actually moves the pawn), then a final neutral/zero value is injected to release. Fire-and-forget: the command returns immediately and the hold runs across the next hold_seconds of PIE. Omit (or 0) for a single one-shot sample.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). With 2+ players the default may drive the OTHER player's pawn.

params.name: action_path
params.description: Alias of action, read when action is absent or empty: InputAction object path or short asset name.

params.name: action_name
params.description: Alias of action, read only when action is absent or empty and action_path is absent: InputAction object path or short asset name.

commands.returns: { dispatched: bool, note: string, action_path: string, value_type: string, injected_value: [x,y,z], player_index: number, hold_seconds: number, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: unregister_input_key_mapping
commands.description: Reset a player-mappable Enhanced Input mapping of one local player of a running PIE or game session back to its default key (UEnhancedInputUserSettings::UnMapPlayerKey), clearing the override register_input_key_mapping made for that slot; the mapping itself stays. It changes that player's user settings in memory only: no asset is edited, nothing is saved, no undo step. Start PIE first (start_play_in_editor): without a running PIE or game world the call is refused and nothing changes. It also needs Enhanced Input user settings enabled in the project (EnhancedInputDeveloperSettings bEnableUserSettings, before PIE starts). To unbind a key in a mapping context asset use remove_mapping_from_context; to see the bound keys use list_all_input_mappings. A missing mapping_name is an error before anything changes; when the engine refuses the reset, applied is false, success is false and failure_tags gives its reasons. player_controller and the world fields name the controller and world that were used.

params.name: mapping_name
params.description: Name of the player-mappable key mapping to reset, as set in its Player Mappable Key Settings, e.g. "Jump" (required).

params.name: player_controller_name
params.description: Optional object name or actor label of the PlayerController to reset, e.g. "PlayerController_0" (case-insensitive), searched in every running PIE or game world; when given, player_index is ignored.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Local player whose binding is reset, in the play world: 0 (default) is the first player controller, any other value matches a local player's controller id.

params.name: slot
params.description: Which of the player's key slots to reset: "First" (default), "Second", "Third" or "Fourth"; an unknown name silently means "First".

commands.returns: { applied: bool, mapping_name: string, slot: string, failure_tags: [string], player_controller: string, world_name: string, world_package: string, world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: can_reset_interchange_actor
commands.description: Check, without changing anything, whether an Interchange reset (restoring an imported actor to what its Interchange scene import produced) can run on one actor of the editor world (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::CanResetActor). can_reset is true only when the Interchange.FeatureFlags.InterchangeReset console variable is on and a component of the actor carries Interchange asset user data (for a Level Instance, its map's world settings do; that map is loaded to check). false is a normal answer, not an error. Use it before reset_interchange_actors, which skips the actors that fail this check without saying which; for a whole map use can_reset_interchange_world and reset_interchange_level_asset; to see what an asset's import recorded, get_interchange_asset_import_data. An actor that is not found is an error.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full object path of the actor (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap.MyMap:PersistentLevel.ActorName_0") or its object name in the persistent level of the editor world (e.g. "StaticMeshActor_3"); labels are not matched.

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, can_reset: bool }

commands.name: can_reset_interchange_world
commands.description: Report, read-only, whether Interchange can reset a world (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::CanResetWorld): the map asset world_path names, loaded if needed, or the current editor world. Returns can_reset, is_editor_world and resolved_world_path. Run the reset with reset_interchange_level_asset.

params.name: world_path
params.description: World asset path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap") or fully-qualified object path. Empty = current editor world.

commands.returns: { world_path: string, can_reset: bool, is_editor_world: bool }

commands.name: can_translate_interchange_source_data
commands.description: Checks whether a translator registered with this editor's Interchange framework can read a source file, judged for most formats by the file extension alone: true means import_interchange_asset can try it, not that the file exists or will import cleanly. Read-only: nothing is imported, loaded or changed. It answers false, not an error, when Interchange import is disabled, the extension is blocked for import in the project, or no translator matches. Use it as a pre-flight check before import_interchange_asset; get_interchange_supported_formats lists every supported extension, and register_interchange_translator adds a reader for a new format.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Path of the source file, absolute on disk (e.g. "C:/Assets/Mesh.fbx", "D:/Scans/room.gltf"); for most translators only its extension is looked at, so the file need not exist yet.

params.name: scene_only
params.description: When true, answer true only when the matching translator is a scene translator (one that imports actors into a level, not only assets). Defaults to false (any translator type).

commands.returns: { file_path: string, scene_only: bool, can_translate: bool }

commands.name: create_interchange_pipeline_asset
commands.description: Create an Interchange pipeline asset of a concrete pipeline class (the generic texture, mesh, material, animation, audio, scenes, groom or assets pipelines, glTF, sparse volume texture, MaterialX). Idempotent: an object of that name already in package_path is returned with already_existed:true.

params.name: pipeline_class_path
params.description: Class path of the concrete (non-abstract) UInterchangePipelineBase subclass to instantiate (e.g. "/Script/InterchangePipelines.InterchangeGenericAssetsPipeline"), loaded via LoadClass.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Name of the new pipeline asset (the object/package name under package_path).

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination UE content folder for the new pipeline asset (e.g. "/Game/Pipelines"). Defaults to "/Game".

commands.returns: { pipeline_path: string, class: string, already_existed: bool, note: string }

commands.name: get_interchange_asset_import_data
commands.description: Read the Interchange import data (UInterchangeAssetImportData) of an asset loaded by package or object path: its source_filenames, display_labels, the pipeline objects stored on it (class, name, object path of each) and whether it holds a node container; with include_node_container, also that container's root_uids and every factory node (uid, display_label and the class of the object that factory produces) -- what an Interchange import produced. An asset imported through the legacy factory path, or never imported, has none: that answers present=false with zeros and empty lists, a normal state and not an error; only a path that does not load is an error. Read-only: it writes nothing and needs no PIE. The legacy UAssetImportData of a factory import (source file and timestamp): get_asset_import_data; replace the pipeline stack: set_interchange_pipelines; reimport from this data: reimport_interchange_asset.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo") or fully-qualified object path ("/Game/Foo/Foo.Foo")

params.name: include_node_container
params.description: Optional bool, default false: add root_uids, factory_node_count and factory_nodes from the import data's node container (empty when there is none)

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, present: bool, pipelines_count: number, pipelines: [{ class: string, name: string, path: string }], has_node_container: bool, source_filenames: [string], display_labels: [string], root_uids?: [string], factory_node_count?: number, factory_nodes?: [{ uid: string, class: string, display_label: string }] }

commands.name: get_interchange_pipeline_properties
commands.description: Read the editable (EditAnywhere) properties of an Interchange pipeline asset by reflection, inherited ones included: each entry gives name, C++ type and, unless class_only is true, the current value as JSON (left out when it cannot be converted). It narrows get_object_info to the EditAnywhere properties and adds a names-only discovery mode; get_properties reads any other UPROPERTY. The values are the in-memory ones, so edits made with set_interchange_pipeline_properties and not yet saved already show. Read-only: it writes nothing and needs no PIE. A path that does not load as a UInterchangePipelineBase is an error. Discover the names with class_only=true, write them with set_interchange_pipeline_properties and persist with save_interchange_pipeline; the pipelines an imported asset used: get_interchange_asset_import_data; a new pipeline asset: create_interchange_pipeline_asset.

params.name: pipeline_path
params.description: Object path of the pipeline asset to read (loaded via LoadObject, must be a UInterchangePipelineBase), e.g. "/Game/Pipelines/MyMeshPipeline.MyMeshPipeline".

params.name: class_only
params.description: When true, return only the EditAnywhere property NAMES and types (no values) for discovery. Defaults to false (includes current values).

commands.returns: { pipeline_path: string, class: string, properties: [{ name: string, type: string, value?: any }], property_count: number }

retired.how: object_path=<pipeline asset>: every property with its type and value

commands.name: get_interchange_project_settings
commands.description: Read the project's Interchange settings, the live class defaults of UInterchangeProjectSettings as Project Settings shows them. For content import: the default pipeline stack, every pipeline stack with its pipeline paths, the per-asset-type default-stack overrides, the import dialog class and the import and reimport dialog flags. For scene import: the default stack, the two dialog flags and only a count of its per-translator dialog overrides. Plus the file picker, generic pipeline and converter default pipeline classes, the static mesh smoothing fallback flag and the Interchange groups. Read-only, with no parameters. Change the default stack with set_interchange_pipeline_stack_default; read one pipeline asset with get_object_info; the formats translators accept: get_interchange_supported_formats.
commands.returns: { content_import_settings: { default_pipeline_stack: string, import_dialog_class: string, b_show_import_dialog: bool, b_show_reimport_dialog: bool, pipeline_stacks: [{ name: string, pipelines: [string] }], pipeline_stacks_count: int, default_pipeline_stack_override: [{ translator_type: string, stack_name: string }] }, scene_import_settings: { default_pipeline_stack: string, b_show_import_dialog: bool, b_show_reimport_dialog: bool, per_translator_dialog_override_count: int }, file_picker_class: string, generic_pipeline_class: string, converter_default_pipeline: string, b_static_mesh_use_smooth_edges_if_smoothing_information_is_missing: bool, interchange_groups: [{ display_name: string, unique_id: string, default_pipeline_stack: string, b_show_import_dialog: bool, b_show_reimport_dialog: bool }], interchange_groups_count: int }

commands.name: get_interchange_supported_formats
commands.description: Report Interchange framework availability and list the file extensions supported by registered Interchange translators of a given type.  Calls UInterchangeManager::GetSupportedFormats(EInterchangeTranslatorType) (InterchangeManager.h, INTERCHANGEENGINE_API) and IsInterchangeImportEnabled(). The 5.8 enum has Invalid / Assets / Actors / Scenes (Scenes = Assets|Actors). Accepts aliases "Assets", "Actors", "Scenes", and "AssetsAndScene" (mapped to Scenes). The registered translator set is private in 5.8, so availability is reported as enabled (= import enabled AND at least one supported asset format) with the per-type format counts.

params.name: translator_type
params.description: Translator type: "Assets" [default], "Actors", "Scenes", or the spec alias "AssetsAndScene"

commands.returns: { translator_type: string, format_count: number, formats: [string], enabled: bool, import_enabled: bool, asset_format_count: number, actor_format_count: number, scene_format_count: number }

commands.name: import_interchange_asset
commands.description: Import a source file synchronously through the Interchange manager: unattended, no dialogs, replacing existing assets unless replace_existing is false. When the InterchangeImport plugin is not loaded the note says so.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Path of the source file to import on disk (e.g. "C:/Assets/Mesh.fbx"). Passed to UInterchangeManager::CreateSourceData.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: Destination UE content folder for the imported asset(s) (e.g. "/Game/Meshes"). Defaults to "/Game/Imported".

params.name: replace_existing
params.description: When true, overwrite an existing asset at the destination (bReplaceExisting). Defaults to true.

commands.returns: { file_path: string, destination_path: string, imported: bool, count: number, imported_objects: [string], note: string }

commands.name: register_interchange_factory
commands.description: Register a factory class -- the Interchange step that creates one kind of asset, such as a texture or a static mesh, from translated data -- with the Interchange manager for this editor session. Nothing is written to disk and the registration ends when the editor closes; the engine registers its own factories on startup, so this is for a class whose plugin did not. The manager keeps one factory per asset class and the first one registered stays: when another factory already makes that asset class the call is refused and names it. Registering the factory that is already active changes nothing and reports already_registered=true, so a repeat call is harmless (idempotent). A class that does not load, is abstract or is not a UInterchangeFactoryBase subclass is refused. The reader of a source file format registers with register_interchange_translator.

params.name: factory_class_path
params.description: Class path of the factory class, e.g. "/Script/InterchangeImport.InterchangeTextureFactory"; loaded with LoadClass.

commands.returns: { factory_class_path, class, asset_class, registered, already_registered }

commands.name: register_interchange_translator
commands.description: Register a translator class -- the Interchange reader of one or more source file formats -- with the Interchange manager for this editor session, so imports and get_interchange_supported_formats pick up its formats. Nothing is written to disk and the registration ends when the editor closes; the engine registers its own translators on startup, so this is for a class whose plugin did not. The class must load and be a concrete UInterchangeTranslatorBase subclass: anything else is refused before it is registered, since the manager would assert on the next format query. A class already registered changes nothing and reports already_registered=true, so a repeat call is harmless (idempotent). A factory, which turns translated data into assets, registers with register_interchange_factory; whether a given file can be read: can_translate_interchange_source_data.

params.name: translator_class_path
params.description: Class path of the translator class, e.g. "/Script/InterchangeImport.InterchangeImageWrapperTranslator"; loaded with LoadClass.

commands.returns: { translator_class_path, class, registered, already_registered?, supported_formats: [string] }

commands.name: reimport_interchange_asset
commands.description: Reimports an asset that was imported through Interchange, from the source file and pipeline stack stored on its Interchange import data, synchronously and without dialogs: the asset's content in memory is overwritten with the file's current content. This tool does not save it (save_asset writes it). An asset without Interchange import data -- a legacy-importer asset, or one never imported -- is an error and nothing changes: use reimport_asset for those. Check which kind an asset has, and its source file, with get_interchange_asset_import_data; change the stored pipelines first with set_interchange_pipelines. A reimport the engine reports as failed still answers success, with reimported false and a note pointing to the editor log, so read reimported.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Package path (e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock") or object path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.SM_Rock") of the asset to reimport; it is loaded if needed.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, reimported: bool, count: number, note: string }

commands.name: reset_interchange_actors
commands.description: Run an Interchange reset (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetActors) on the editor-world actors listed by object path or persistent-level object name; the library skips actors that fail CanResetActor, and the reply does not say which were reset. Returns count, resolved and unresolved_paths. Check first with can_reset_interchange_actor.

params.name: actor_paths
params.description: Actors to reset, each a full object path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap.MyMap:PersistentLevel.ActorName_0") or an object name in the persistent level; labels are not matched, and empty or unknown entries land in unresolved_paths.

commands.returns: { count: number, resolved: number, unresolved_paths: [string], note: string }

commands.name: reset_interchange_level_asset
commands.description: Run an Interchange reset on a level (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetLevelAsset), the map world_path names or the current editor world, only when the Interchange.FeatureFlags.InterchangeReset CVar is on and CanResetWorld is true; otherwise it does nothing and the call fails (reset false, with the reason in note). It does not save. Returns reset, can_reset, cvar_enabled and a note.

params.name: world_path
params.description: World asset path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap") or fully-qualified object path. Empty = current editor world.

commands.returns: { world_path: string, resolved_world_path: string, reset: bool, can_reset: bool, cvar_enabled: bool, note: string }

commands.name: reset_interchange_scene_import_asset
commands.description: Call the Interchange reset of a UInterchangeSceneImportAsset (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetSceneImportAsset); other asset classes are refused. The engine only resets while the Interchange.FeatureFlags.InterchangeReset CVar is 1: with it at 0 the call does nothing and fails (reset false). The reset itself returns nothing, so reset true means it ran, not what it changed. Use reset_interchange_level_asset for a level.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path of the UInterchangeSceneImportAsset (e.g. "/Game/Imports/MyScene.MyScene")

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, reset: bool, cvar_enabled: bool, note: string }

commands.name: save_interchange_pipeline
commands.description: Write the package of an Interchange pipeline asset (a UInterchangePipelineBase loaded by object path) over its .uasset on disk, dirty or not, through the shared asset save; saved false makes success false and save_error carries the measured cause. It is the persist step after create_interchange_pipeline_asset and set_properties, which change memory only; repeating it is idempotent. Like save_asset it refuses during PIE and under a read-only root. A path that does not load as a pipeline is an error.

params.name: pipeline_path
params.description: Object path of the pipeline asset whose package is written to disk (loaded via LoadObject, must be a UInterchangePipelineBase).

commands.returns: { pipeline_path: string, file_path: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_interchange_pipeline_properties
commands.description: Write settings of an Interchange pipeline asset -- what a pipeline does at import, such as whether it imports materials or how it names the assets -- by reflection, from a {name: value} object (a scalar, an object for a struct, an array for a TArray). It is close to set_properties on the same asset path (editable properties only, JSON values); the difference is that it records no undo step and runs one PostEditChange for the whole batch. Values change in memory only: save_interchange_pipeline writes the asset to disk. A name that does not exist, is not editable or does not convert is listed in skipped with the reason, and the others are still written. An empty properties object is refused. Idempotent. Names, types and current values: get_interchange_pipeline_properties; which pipelines an imported asset uses: set_interchange_pipelines.

params.name: pipeline_path
params.description: Object path of the pipeline asset, e.g. "/Game/Pipelines/MyMeshPipeline.MyMeshPipeline"; it must load as a UInterchangePipelineBase.

params.name: properties
params.description: {property_name: value}, with names as get_interchange_pipeline_properties lists them; a struct takes an object of its fields and a TArray an array.

commands.returns: { pipeline_path, applied_count, skipped_count, skipped?: [string], note }

retired.how: object_path=<pipeline asset>, properties with the engine names

commands.name: set_interchange_pipeline_stack_default
commands.description: Choose the named pipeline stack Interchange uses by default for content imports (assets) or scene imports (levels) -- the DefaultPipelineStack that Project Settings > Interchange shows -- and write it to the project's DefaultEngine.ini, so it outlives the editor session. The stack must already exist in that import path's pipeline stacks: an unknown name is refused with the list of the ones there, and so is a read-only DefaultEngine.ini, both before anything changes. The previous default is overwritten and returned in previous_stack_name; choosing the stack that is already the default changes nothing (changed=false), so a repeat call is harmless (idempotent). No undo step is recorded. The content stacks and both current defaults are listed by get_interchange_project_settings; to choose the pipelines of one imported asset instead, use set_interchange_pipelines.

params.name: content_or_scene
params.description: Which default to set: "content" for asset imports (ContentImportSettings) or "scene" for level imports (SceneImportSettings). Case-insensitive.

params.name: stack_name
params.description: Name of an existing pipeline stack of that import path, e.g. "Assets"; matched without case.

commands.returns: { content_or_scene, stack_name, previous_stack_name, changed, config_file, applied }

commands.name: set_interchange_pipelines
commands.description: Replace the UInterchangePipelineBase stack on an asset's UInterchangeAssetImportData.  Loads the asset + its UInterchangeAssetImportData, resolves each path in ``pipeline_paths`` via LoadObject<UObject>, then calls ID->SetPipelines(InPipelines) (InterchangeAssetImportData.h, INTERCHANGEENGINE_API). Idempotent: SetPipelines resets TransientPipelines before applying (impl InterchangeAssetImportData.cpp). Marks the package dirty so the change persists on save.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo")

params.name: pipeline_paths
params.description: Array of fully-qualified pipeline asset paths (UObject* resolved via LoadObject). Entries that fail to resolve are reported in ``unresolved_paths`` but do not abort the call.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, present: bool, pipeline_count: number, unresolved_paths: [string] }

commands.name: add_foliage_instances
commands.description: Place foliage instances of a UFoliageType at explicit transforms in the level's InstancedFoliageActor. DANGER: measured CRASHING the editor process (access violation inside UnrealEditor-FoliageEdit.dll) -- reproducibly, and a single instance crashes just like a thousand, so trimming the count does not help. The reply you see is a "Connection reset", which reads like a network hiccup and is not. Use add_instanced_static_mesh_component + add_instanced_static_mesh_instance instead: an InstancedFoliageActor is itself an actor holding instanced-static-mesh components, so it is the same code path minus the crash. Save your work before calling this at all.

params.name: foliage_type_path
params.description: Full path of the UFoliageType asset

params.name: transforms
params.description: List of [x,y,z] locations or objects with location, rotation, scale

commands.returns: { foliage_type_path: string, foliage_type: string, requested: int, instances_added: int, instance_count_before: int, instance_count: int, placed_instance_count: int, instances_added_ok: bool, foliage_actor: string }

commands.name: add_height_mask_node
commands.description: Drop the nodes of an altitude mask into a material graph: a SmoothStep preset with ConstMin=min_height / ConstMax=max_height in world units, for blending a layer in by height (snow above a line, sand below one). It does NOT build a wired chain despite the name: the SmoothStep Value input is left UNCONNECTED and no world-position node is wired, so you must connect WorldPosition Z into it yourself (connect_material_expressions) or the mask stays constant. Use the reply's expression_id and note to find the pin, then re-read the graph as the oracle.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the target UMaterial

params.name: min_height
params.description: Lower bound (world units) for SmoothStep. Below this the mask is 0.

params.name: max_height
params.description: Upper bound (world units) for SmoothStep. Above this the mask is 1.

params.name: pos_x
params.description: Editor graph X position of the SmoothStep output (default -800)

params.name: pos_y
params.description: Editor graph Y position of the SmoothStep output (default 0)

commands.returns: { material_path, expression_id (the SmoothStep node), min_height, max_height }

commands.name: add_landscape_layer
commands.description: Register a LandscapeLayerInfo asset as a target weight (paint) layer on a landscape, so the terrain can store weight for it and the material's LandscapeLayerBlend can read it. Step 2 of three, between create_landscape_layer_info and paint_landscape_layer -- painting a layer that was never registered writes nothing. Already-registered layers return already_present=true; remove_landscape_layer is the inverse, get_landscape_layers lists what is registered now.

params.name: layer_info_path
params.description: Full path of the ULandscapeLayerInfoObject asset

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, layer_info_path: string, layer_name: string, layer_added: bool, already_present: bool, target_layer_count: int }

commands.name: add_landscape_layer_blend_node
commands.description: Add the LandscapeLayerBlend node that makes a terrain material multi-layered, pre-populated with one input per name in layer_names (weight / alpha / height blend). This is what lets grass, rock, sand and snow coexist on one landscape material, and the layer names must match the ones registered on the terrain with add_landscape_layer or those inputs read zero weight forever. The node is created with its layer inputs but nothing feeding them -- wire each layer's texture chain with connect_material_expressions, then compile_material and check get_material_stats.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the target UMaterial (e.g. /Game/Materials/M_Landscape)

params.name: layer_names
params.description: List of FName layer names to add (in order). Each becomes a FLayerBlendInput with LB_WeightBlend.

params.name: blend_type
params.description: Optional "weight" (default) | "alpha" | "height" for the layer blend enum

params.name: pos_x
params.description: Editor graph X position (default -800)

params.name: pos_y
params.description: Editor graph Y position (default -200)

commands.returns: { material_path, expression_id, layer_count, layers: [{layer_name, blend_type}] }

commands.name: add_landscape_spline_control_point
commands.description: Add a control point to a landscape's spline component -- the first half of laying a road, river bed or path across the terrain (connect consecutive points with add_landscape_spline_segment). Coordinates are LANDSCAPE-LOCAL, not world: subtract the landscape's location (get_landscape_info) before passing them, or the point lands somewhere else entirely. `width` is a HALF-width. The reply's control_point_index is what the segment and edit tools address.

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: location
params.description: [x, y, z] in landscape-local space, default [0,0,0]

params.name: width
params.description: Half-width at this point, default 128

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, control_point_index: int, control_point_count: int, width: number, added: bool, location: [number] }

commands.name: add_landscape_spline_segment
commands.description: Join two existing landscape spline control points with a segment -- the second half of laying a road, river or path: points alone render nothing, the segments between them are the spline. Both indices must already exist (add_landscape_spline_control_point returns them). Chain segments point-to-point for a route; use get_landscape_splines to confirm segment_count grew.

params.name: start_point_index
params.description: Index of the start control point

params.name: end_point_index
params.description: Index of the end control point

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, segment_index: int, segment_count: int, start_point_index: int, end_point_index: int, added: bool }

commands.name: add_slope_mask_node
commands.description: Drop the two nodes of a slope mask into a material graph: a SmoothStep preset with ConstMin=min_slope / ConstMax=max_slope, plus a downstream node whose output is the mask (intended 1 on flat ground, 0 on vertical walls). It does NOT build a wired chain despite the name: no VertexNormalWS node is created and both inputs are left UNCONNECTED, so until you wire VertexNormalWS.B into the SmoothStep Value pin yourself (connect_material_expressions) the mask evaluates to a constant. The reply's expression_id and note tell you which node to wire. Verify by re-reading the graph, not by success.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the target UMaterial

params.name: min_slope
params.description: Lower bound (radians or slope units, depending on convention) for SmoothStep (default 0.0)

params.name: max_slope
params.description: Upper bound for SmoothStep (default 0.5)

params.name: pos_x
params.description: Editor graph X position (default -800)

params.name: pos_y
params.description: Editor graph Y position (default 200)

commands.returns: { material_path, expression_id (the OneMinus output), min_slope, max_slope }

commands.name: add_spline_component
commands.description: Add a USplineComponent to a named editor-world actor (name or label) as an undoable instance component on its root, optionally replacing its default points with your local-space points -- what add_component_to_actor cannot set in the same call. Not idempotent: each call adds a spline, while set_spline_points and get_spline_points act on the actor's FIRST one. An entry that is not [x, y, z] (3 numbers) is an error and nothing is added. Not saved (save_level).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor

params.name: points
params.description: Optional [[x, y, z], ...] spline points in local space; an entry that is not 3 numbers is an error and nothing is added

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, num_points: int, added: bool }

commands.name: add_spline_mesh_component
commands.description: Add a USplineMeshComponent to a named editor-world actor (name or label) as an undoable instance component attached to its root, with a static mesh deformed straight from start to end in local space (SetStartAndEnd, tangent = end - start). Over add_component_to_actor it loads the mesh and sets the deformation in the same call; a mesh that does not load is an error and nothing is added. Not idempotent: each call adds another component. Nothing is saved (save_level).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor
