params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: /Game or /Engine path to the static mesh to deform

params.name: start
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] start point; defaults to (0,0,0)

params.name: end
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] end point; defaults to (100,0,0)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, static_mesh_path: string, mesh_set: bool, start: [number, number, number], end: [number, number, number], added: bool }

commands.name: add_streaming_level
commands.description: Adds a saved level package to the editor world as a streaming sub-level.  Creates a ULevelStreamingDynamic wrapper referencing the given level package and attaches it to the current editor world's StreamingLevels array. The package must already exist on disk (a streaming level references a saved .umap). Idempotent: if the level is already a streaming level, returns its current state with added=false.          (an object path "/Game/Maps/SubLevel.SubLevel" is also accepted).

params.name: level_package_path
params.description: Package path of the level, e.g. "/Game/Maps/SubLevel"

params.name: should_be_loaded
params.description: Desired initial ShouldBeLoaded state (optional, default true)

params.name: should_be_visible
params.description: Desired initial ShouldBeVisible state (optional, default true)

commands.returns: { package_name: string, name: string, streaming_class: string, should_be_loaded: bool, should_be_visible: bool, is_level_loaded: bool, is_level_visible: bool, added: bool, already_present: bool, streaming_level_count: number }

commands.name: assign_actor_to_data_layer_instance
commands.description: Assigns an editor-world actor to a data layer instance.  Uses UDataLayerEditorSubsystem::AddActorToDataLayer against the data layer instance referencing the given asset. Requires a World Partition world; on a non-WP (default) map this returns an honest error (no editor-world swap).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the actor in the editor world.

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the UDataLayerAsset (must be instanced in the world first via create_data_layer_instance).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, data_layer_asset_path: string, instance_name: string, short_name: string, assigned: bool, message: string }

commands.name: attach_actor
commands.description: Attach one editor-world actor to another, both found by internal name or outliner label (first match), optionally at a socket of the parent, keeping the child's world transform, in one undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved. A child that already has a parent moves to the new one, and repeating the same attachment changes nothing (idempotent). attached is the engine's verdict: an attachment it refuses (to the actor itself, into a cycle, a Static child under a non-Static parent) is an error naming the reason, with attached false and no undo step left. The socket name is not checked against the parent. A missing child or parent is an error. Inverse: detach_actor; for a component inside a Blueprint use attach_blueprint_component; to attach over time in a Level Sequence use add_attach_track.

params.name: child_actor_name
params.description: Internal name or outliner label of the child actor to attach (first match in the editor world)

params.name: parent_actor_name
params.description: Internal name or outliner label of the parent actor to attach to (first match in the editor world)

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Optional socket name on the parent, not checked; omitted or empty attaches without a socket

commands.returns: { child: string, parent: string, attached: bool }

commands.name: break_level_instance
commands.description: Breaks an ALevelInstance actor, un-nesting its sub-level content into the current editor level as plain actors and destroying the original level-instance actor.  Canonical headless path: resolve the ALevelInstance by label/name, then ULevelInstanceSubsystem::CanBreakLevelInstance (gate) -> BlockLoadLevelInstance (synchronous load) -> BreakLevelInstance. CanBreakLevelInstance is checked BEFORE BlockLoadLevelInstance on purpose: BlockLoadLevelInstance asserts check(!IsEditing()) and CanBreakLevelInstance rejects the editing/level-script states, so this ordering prevents the assert. BreakLevelInstance returns false when nothing was moved (an empty sub-level is the honest broke=false case, NOT an error). The original actor is destroyed by the engine, so this is a one-shot destructive op: re-running with the same name reports "level instance not found". Requires the editor (GEditor); BreakLevelInstance touches GEditor->GetSelectedActors()/Trans unguarded.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Required. Label or name of the ALevelInstance actor to break (matched via GetActorNameOrLabel).

params.name: levels
params.description: Optional, default 1. How many nested levels deep to break (passed to BreakLevelInstance Levels).

params.name: keep_folders
params.description: Optional, default false. When true, preserve the source actor folders (ELevelInstanceBreakFlags::KeepFolders) instead of flattening them.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, broke: bool, moved_actor_count: number, moved_actors: [string], levels: number, keep_folders: bool, was_loaded_forced: bool, note: string }

commands.name: build_lighting
commands.description: Start an asynchronous static lighting build of all levels in the editor world (not only the current one) and return started without waiting for the result. Side effect: writes the quality and OnlyBuildCurrentLevel=false into LightingBuildOptions of the editor per-project settings.

params.name: quality
params.description: Preview, Medium, High or Production (case-insensitive); any other value silently builds at Preview. Default Preview.

commands.returns: { quality: string, started: bool, note: string }

commands.name: capture_pie_screenshot
commands.description: Write a PNG of what the running game shows: the PIE game viewport, or the active editor viewport when there is no game viewport (with PIE not running, saved_to_pie_active=false and a note says so). It reads the pixels synchronously, so the file holds the 3D scene without the UMG/Slate HUD, and an existing file at output_path is overwritten. With include_ui=true during PIE it also queues an engine screenshot that a later frame crops to the game viewport, HUD included, and writes over the same file (ui_overwrite_next_frame=true): re-read the file after the call. Use it to SHOW a play-test result; for the editor viewport with a fresh redraw, resizing or base64 use capture_viewport, for a supersampled image capture_high_res_screenshot, and for actor state instead of pixels capture_pie_state. Start PIE with start_play_in_editor first. No viewport, a zero-size viewport or a failed write is an error. Changes nothing in the level; every call writes the file again.

params.name: output_path
params.description: File path of the PNG, absolute or relative to the editor's working directory, e.g. "D:/Shots/hud.png"; folders are created. Omit it to auto-name <Project>/Saved/MCP/PIE_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss UTC>.png.

params.name: include_ui
params.description: true to also write the HUD version over output_path on a later frame (PIE with rendering only, SDR only, abandoned after 8 s, e.g. with an HDR editor display); default false keeps only the scene-only PNG.

commands.returns: { saved_to_pie_active, output_path, width, height, bytes_written, includes_ui, ui_overwrite_next_frame, ui_note?, note? }

commands.name: commit_level_instance
commands.description: Closes the in-place edit opened by edit_level_instance: the engine commits (or discards) the edits, saves the sub-level .umap back to disk, and re-collapses the streaming level into the instanced ALevelInstance.  Canonical headless path: resolve the ALevelInstance by label/name, then ULevelInstanceSubsystem::CanCommitLevelInstance (gate) -> CommitLevelInstance. When the instance is NOT being edited, CanCommitLevelInstance returns false with reason "not currently being edited" — that is reported honestly as { committed:false, was_editing:false } and is a SUCCESS (a no-op close), NOT an error, so this is safe to call unconditionally to guarantee no dangling edit-mode. CommitLevelInstance returns whether the sub-level package save succeeded (committed:false on an honest save failure). Optional discard (default false) throws the edits away instead of saving. Requires the editor (GEditor); CommitLevelInstance touches GEditor->Trans / selection unguarded. Under -unattended the commit's save dialogs do not block.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Required. Label or name of the ALevelInstance actor whose edit to commit (matched via GetActorNameOrLabel).

params.name: discard
params.description: Optional, default false. When true, discard the in-place edits instead of saving them back to the sub-level .umap.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, committed: bool, was_editing: bool, discarded: bool, note: string }

commands.name: copy_landscape_region
commands.description: Clone a rectangle of terrain relief: copy a heightmap region between two landscapes (or within one, by omitting the source name), resampling automatically when the source and destination rectangles differ in size. Regions are in VERTEX coordinates, not world units -- get the ranges from get_landscape_info (min_x/max_x, size_x). Use it to duplicate an island or reuse sculpted relief; use import_landscape_heightmap when the source is a file instead.

params.name: source_region
params.description: Required [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] in source vertex coords

params.name: dest_region
params.description: Required [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] in destination vertex coords

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional destination landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: source_landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional source landscape actor name, defaults to destination

commands.returns: { source_landscape_actor_name: string, dest_landscape_actor_name: string, applied: bool, resampled: bool, source_width: int, source_height: int, dest_width: int, dest_height: int, source_region: [int], dest_region: [int] }

commands.name: create_data_layer_asset
commands.description: Create a UDataLayerAsset (the World Partition data layer definition) at package_path/name with its type and debug color, and save it. This is only the asset: put it in a map with create_data_layer_instance and add actors with assign_actor_to_data_layer_instance. data_layer_type is matched without case and anything but Runtime gives Editor; a debug_color missing or shorter than 3 numbers gives the default color. A data layer asset already at that path is returned unchanged (created=false, already_exists=true, saved=false; type and color are not applied) and nothing is saved, so repeat calls are idempotent; another asset class there, an external data layer asset included, or an invalid path, is an error. No undo step is recorded; a failed save, as during PIE, makes success false. Later changes: set_data_layer_type or set_data_layer_debug_color; read back: get_data_layer_assets with data_layer_asset_path; list them: get_data_layer_assets.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new data layer asset, also its package name under package_path.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/DataLayers")

params.name: data_layer_type
params.description: Data layer type: "Editor" or "Runtime" (optional, default "Editor"); matched without case, any other value gives Editor

params.name: debug_color
params.description: Optional [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] integers 0-255 (defaults to [0, 128, 255, 255]); rounded and clamped, alpha 255 when omitted, a shorter array is ignored

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, data_layer_type: string, is_runtime: bool, debug_color: [number, number, number, number], created: bool, already_exists: bool, success: bool, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: create_data_layer_instance
commands.description: Instances a UDataLayerAsset into the editor world's World Partition.  Uses UDataLayerEditorSubsystem::CreateDataLayerInstance. Requires the editor world to be a World Partition world; on the default non-WP map this returns an honest "requires world partition" error (no editor-world swap is done).

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the UDataLayerAsset to instance.

commands.returns: { data_layer_asset_path: string, instance_name: string, short_name: string, full_name: string, data_layer_type: string, is_runtime: bool, asset_path: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool }

commands.name: create_foliage_type
commands.description: Create and save a FoliageType asset (UFoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh) wrapping a static mesh, so it can be placed as foliage and tuned with set_properties. Creating the asset is safe; note that the tools that PLACE instances of it (add_foliage_instances, scatter_foliage_in_box, scatter_foliage_on_layer) can crash the editor, so plan to scatter via instanced-static-mesh components or PCG. For landscape GRASS driven by the terrain material use create_landscape_grass_type instead.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name, e.g. FT_Grass

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Full path of the source StaticMesh

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Foliage

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, static_mesh: string, foliage_class: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool, mesh_set: bool, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: create_landscape
commands.description: Create a new terrain: spawn an ALandscape actor in the editor world sized by section_size x sections_per_component x component_count, filled with a FLAT heightmap at `height`. This is step 1 of two -- the relief comes from a following import_landscape_heightmap onto this actor, and going through this pair instead of the editor's New Landscape dialog is the point: the dialog treats its Location field as the terrain CENTRE (not the corner) and can fill only part of the components on import, silently. Verify the result with get_landscape_info (location, size_x/size_y, component_count), never with what you typed.

params.description: Vertices per section, default 63 (rounded up to power of two)

params.name: sections_per_component

params.name: component_count_y
params.description: Components on Y axis, default 8

params.name: height
params.description: Initial uint16 height value, default 32768

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_path: string, section_size: int, subsection_size_quads: int, sections_per_component: int, component_count_x: int, component_count_y: int, quads_per_component: int, size_x: int, size_y: int, vertex_count: int, height_midpoint: int, imported: bool, landscape_created: bool, location: [number] }

commands.name: create_landscape_grass_type
commands.description: Create and save a LandscapeGrassType asset, optionally seeding its first grass variety with a mesh. This is landscape grass, not foliage: instances are generated by the terrain MATERIAL through a LandscapeGrassOutput node, so the asset alone renders nothing until it is wired there -- and unlike the foliage scatter tools, this path does not crash the editor. Idempotent (an existing asset comes back unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, nothing saved). Tune it with set_landscape_grass_type_properties; the honest check that the wiring resolved is ULandscapeComponent.get_grass_types_bp(), since counting grass instances headless reads 0 even when the player sees grass.

params.name: package_path

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, grass_class: string, variety_count: int, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: create_landscape_layer_info
commands.description: Create and save the LandscapeLayerInfo asset that a terrain paint layer needs before it can hold weight (grass, rock, sand, snow...). Step 1 of three: create the asset here, register it on the terrain with add_landscape_layer, then paint weight with paint_landscape_layer. Idempotent-ish -- an existing asset comes back with already_exists=true.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name, e.g. LI_Grass

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Landscape

params.name: layer_name

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, layer_name: string, layer_info_class: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, message: string }

commands.name: create_level_instance
commands.description: Spawns an ALevelInstance actor in the editor world and binds it to a saved map (.umap).  Uses the canonical headless-safe path: SpawnActor<ALevelInstance> + ALevelInstance::SetWorldAsset (NOT the editor-interactive ULevelInstanceSubsystem::CreateLevelInstanceFrom). The referenced .umap MUST already exist on disk; validated before binding so no actor is left with a broken WorldAsset. The sub-level is streamed in deferred/async, so loaded is always false here (binding != synchronous load). Idempotent: an existing ALevelInstance referencing the same world asset at the same location is returned with already_exists=true.

params.name: world_asset_path
params.description: Package/object path of the saved map to reference (e.g. "/Game/Maps/Foo").

params.name: location
params.description: Optional spawn location [x, y, z] (default [0,0,0]).

params.name: name
params.description: Optional actor label for the spawned level instance.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, world_asset_path: string, world_asset_set: bool, world_asset_valid: bool, loaded: bool, location: [number,number,number], already_exists: bool, note: string }

commands.name: create_world_partition_map
commands.description: Creates and saves a new World Partition-enabled UWorld map asset on disk.  The editor world is NOT swapped: a new Inactive UWorld is created inside a /Game package with World Partition enabled and saved by the editor's map save as a .umap, with the actor files World Partition creates for it under __ExternalActors__. A map already at the path is returned unchanged with created=false, already_exists=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved; its world_partition_enabled says whether it has World Partition. An asset of another class there is an error. With Play-in-Editor running, or a path under a read-only content root, a new map is refused before anything is created: success false with save_error. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Read a map's state with get_world_partition_info once it is open.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the new map.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination /Game folder (default /Game/Maps).

params.name: enable_streaming
params.description: bool, enable World Partition streaming (default true).

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, map_path: string, world_partition_enabled: bool, runtime_hash_type: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, message: string, note: string }

commands.name: detach_actor
commands.description: Detach an editor-world actor from the actor it is attached to, keeping its world transform (it does not move), in one undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level keeps it). Its own attached children stay with it. The inverse of attach_actor, which also moves an actor to a new parent directly, so detaching first is not needed for that. Idempotent: an actor with no parent is a success with was_attached=false and detached=false, and nothing changes. detached is read back after the call (former_parent names the old parent), so was_attached=true with detached=false means the engine kept the attachment, still answered as a success. An actor that is not found is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Internal name or outliner label of the editor-world actor, e.g. "SM_Lamp_3" or "Lamp"; get_actors_in_level or find_actors_by_name list them.

commands.returns: { actor: string, was_attached: bool, detached: bool, former_parent: string }

commands.name: does_foliage_type_exist
commands.description: Yes/no guard: does this FoliageType asset path exist and load? Cheap precondition check before a create/scatter/tune call so a typo in the path fails here instead of deep inside another tool. Asks about the ASSET only -- get_foliage_instance_count (has_instances) answers whether anything of it is placed in the level.

params.name: foliage_type_path
params.description: Asset path (e.g. /Game/Foliage/BP_Tree)

commands.returns: { exists: bool, asset_path: string }

commands.name: edit_level_instance
commands.description: Enters in-place edit mode on an ALevelInstance: the engine unloads the instanced sub-level and re-loads it as an editable streaming level so its actors can be modified in the current editor world, then closed by commit_level_instance.  Canonical headless path: resolve the ALevelInstance by label/name, then ULevelInstanceSubsystem::CanEditLevelInstance (gate) -> EditLevelInstance. CanEditLevelInstance is checked BEFORE EditLevelInstance on purpose: EditLevelInstanceInternal opens with check(CanEditLevelInstance(LI)) — a HARD ASSERT — so this ordering turns an un-editable instance into an honest error (with the engine's Reason) instead of a crash. Idempotent: an instance already in edit mode is a no-op (already_editing:true, editing:true). DEFENSIVE CRASH GUARD: on a World-Partitioned map the edit path calls FModuleManager::GetModuleChecked("LevelInstanceEditor") which asserts if that module is not loaded; when the world is partitioned AND the LevelInstanceEditor module is not loaded we fail honestly instead of proceeding. (create_level_instance produces non-partitioned maps, so the normal flow passes this guard.) Requires the editor (GEditor); EditLevelInstance touches GEditor->Trans / selection unguarded. The edit resets the undo stack and streams the world asynchronously (deferred world-swap), so the edit MUST be closed by a matching commit_level_instance.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Required. Label or name of the ALevelInstance actor to open for edit (matched via GetActorNameOrLabel).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, editing: bool, already_editing: bool, note: string }

commands.name: export_landscape_heightmap
commands.description: Dump the landscape heightmap (or a vertex sub-region) to a PNG or 16-bit .r16 file on disk -- THE oracle for any question about the whole terrain: whether an import really landed, where the real min/max heights are, whether a region is unfilled. Prefer it over sampling points with get_landscape_height_at when the question covers the whole surface: a handful of probes has repeatedly suggested flips and offsets that did not exist, while comparing the exported array against the source closes it in one step. An .r16 is exactly width*height*2 bytes, so a short file is itself a failure signal. Use get_landscape_height_at instead for a single world XY.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute filesystem path for the exported heightmap

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: region
params.description: Optional [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] vertex region, defaults to whole landscape

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, file_path: string, export_width: int, export_height: int, exported: bool, file_exists: bool, file_size: number, export_warning: string }

commands.name: flatten_landscape_in_box
commands.description: Level the terrain under a footprint: snap every heightmap vertex inside a world-space box to ONE absolute height, so a base, road or building pad sits flat. Give the height either as target_z in world units (converted using the landscape scale) or as a raw uint16 target_height (0..65535, where 32768 is the midpoint). Absolute, unlike set_landscape_height_in_box which adds a delta; follow with smooth_landscape_in_box to blend the hard rim it leaves. vertices_modified = 0 means the box never touched the terrain.

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: target_height
params.description: Optional uint16 heightmap value 0 to 65535

params.name: target_z
params.description: Optional target world Z, converted to uint16 using landscape scale

params.name: box_min
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world-space box minimum

params.name: box_max
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world-space box maximum

params.name: center
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] box center (alternative to box_min/box_max)

params.name: extent
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] box half-extents (alternative to box_min/box_max)

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, target_height: int, applied: bool, vertices_modified: int, region_width: int, region_height: int, region: [int] }

commands.name: focus_viewport
commands.description: Move the camera of every level editor viewport to frame one actor of the editor world, found by internal name or outliner label (first match), or, when actor_name is omitted, the actors currently selected. Only the viewport cameras change: nothing in the level, no undo entry, nothing saved, and the selection stays as it is. An actor_name that matches nothing, or no actor_name with an empty selection, is an error. The reply has focused_actor (the internal name) in actor mode or focused_count in selection mode, never both. To place the camera at an exact location and rotation use set_viewport_settings, read it back with get_viewport_state, and select actors first with select_actors.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Optional internal name or outliner label of the actor to frame; omitted, the current selection is framed

commands.returns: { focused_actor?: string, focused_count?: int }

commands.name: get_absolute_transform
commands.description: Read the absolute (world-space) location/rotation/scale flags of an EDITOR-world actor's root SceneComponent. The read-back oracle for set_absolute_transform, and the first thing to check when an attached actor inherits an unexpected offset or scale from its parent. An actor with no RootComponent answers has_root:false instead of failing.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel); exact match, editor world only.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, has_root: bool, absolute_location?: bool, absolute_rotation?: bool, absolute_scale?: bool }

commands.name: get_actor_blueprint
commands.description: Tell whether a placed actor comes from a Blueprint and, if so, name its generated class and source asset. Cheap one-actor answer to "what BP is this thing?" -- for the reverse (all actors of a class) use get_actors_by_class. World-aware: world='editor' (default) | 'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N', so a RUNTIME-SPAWNED actor -- which never exists in the editor world, where it reads as a flat "Actor not found" -- can be identified too; the reply stamps world_name/world_package/net_mode/pie_instance.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel); exact match.

An unrecognised value FAILS naming the worlds that exist; it never falls back to another world in silence.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_class: string, world: string, is_blueprint: bool, blueprint_class?: string, blueprint_asset?: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.description: List every component on one actor in the editor OR the live PIE world: name, class, is_active, plus mesh/light details. Accepts world='editor'|'pie'|'server'|'client'|'pie:N' ('server' = the PIE world with authority, 'client' = the other one) and stamps world_name/world_package/net_mode/pie_instance so a co-op reading says WHICH world it came from. Use this to discover component names; then get_component_properties (also world-aware) for their values -- reading with the default world='editor' returns the pre-BeginPlay archetype, not the running actor.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel); exact match, not a substring.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie').

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_class: string, world: string, components: [{ name: string, class: string, is_active: bool, is_editable: bool, type?: string, mesh_name?: string, intensity?: number, light_color?: string }], components_count: number, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_actor_folder
commands.description: Read an actor's outliner folder path (reader twin of set_actor_folder)

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor name or label in the world outliner

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, folder_path: string }

commands.name: get_actor_label
commands.description: Read an actor's display label from the level (reader twin of set_actor_label)

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor name or label in the world outliner

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_label: string }

commands.name: get_actor_lock_location
commands.description: Read whether an EDITOR-world actor is location-locked in the viewport (AActor::IsLockLocation). The read-back oracle for set_actor_lock_location, and the thing to check first when a transform command reports success but the actor has not moved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel); exact match, editor world only.

commands.returns: { actor_name, locked }

commands.name: get_actors_by_class
commands.description: Census of one class in a chosen world: names + locations of every actor whose class name matches EXACTLY (no subclasses; a Blueprint needs its runtime name with the _C suffix, e.g. BP_Foo_C), capped at 1000. The co-op workhorse -- world='editor'|'pie'|'server'|'client'|'pie:N' ('server' = the PIE world with authority, 'client' = the other), and the reply stamps world_name/world_package/net_mode/pie_instance so actors_count:0 is readable as "not in THIS world" instead of "does not exist". Use find_actors_by_name for substring/label search, get_actors_in_radius for proximity. Two false zeros: with 2+ PIE clients a bare world='pie' resolves to only ONE of the two worlds; and after compile_blueprint the placed OFPA instances vanish from BOTH editor and PIE worlds in memory (git shows them intact on disk -- the fix is load_level of the same map, never re-placing them).

params.name: class_name
params.description: Whole UClass name, e.g. 'StaticMeshActor' or 'BP_MyTurret_C'. Compared case-insensitively but WHOLE-string: not a path, not a substring, and never matched against parent classes.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie').

commands.returns: { class_name: string, world: string, actors: [{ name: string, class: string, location: { x: number, y: number, z: number } }], actors_count: number, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_actors_in_radius
commands.description: Spatial query: every actor whose ORIGIN (not its bounds) lies within radius cm of a world point, with each one's distance and location. Pick this over get_actors_by_class when the question is "what is near here" instead of "where are the X". World-aware: world='editor' (default) | 'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N', so actors SPAWNED AT RUNTIME -- which the editor world never contains -- are reachable, and the reply stamps world_name/world_package/net_mode/pie_instance so actors_count:0 reads as "nothing near here IN THIS WORLD" instead of "nothing near here".

params.name: radius
params.description: Search radius in centimetres (Unreal units), measured to each actor's origin.

params.name: center
params.description: World-space center, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Omitted, it is the origin [0,0,0], which reads exactly like "nothing is near there"; any other value (an object, another length) is an error.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). An unrecognised value FAILS naming the worlds that exist; it never falls back to another world in silence.

commands.returns: { center_x: number, center_y: number, center_z: number, radius: number, world: string, actors: [{ name: string, class: string, distance: number, location: { x: number, y: number, z: number } }], actors_count: number, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_data_layer_assets
commands.description: Lists the UDataLayerAsset assets (subclasses included) under a content folder and all its sub-folders, found through the Asset Registry, or reads exactly one with data_layer_asset_path; each entry carries name, object path, type (Editor, Runtime or Unknown), the runtime flags and the debug color. Every match is loaded to read them; nothing is modified and the list is not paginated. These are layer assets, not the layers of the open World Partition map: list those with get_data_layer_instances.

params.name: path
params.description: Content path to search (optional, default "/Game", recursive). Ignored when data_layer_asset_path is given.

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Optional full path of ONE data layer asset to read instead of searching; an asset that does not load as a UDataLayerAsset is an error.

commands.returns: { path: string, data_layer_asset_path?: string (echo, single-asset mode), data_layer_assets: [{ name: string, path: string, type: string, is_runtime?: bool, is_private?: bool, supports_actor_filters?: bool, debug_color?: [number, number, number, number] }], count: number }

commands.name: get_data_layer_instances
commands.description: Lists the data layer instances of the level open in the editor (the editor world, not PIE): each with its object name, short and full name, type (Editor or Runtime), runtime flag and the Data Layer asset it instances. Read-only: loads and changes nothing. A map without World Partition succeeds with an empty list and is_world_partition_enabled false, which is the expected answer, not an error. asset_path is the data_layer_asset_path that assign_actor_to_data_layer_instance, set_data_layer_type, set_data_layer_initial_runtime_state and remove_data_layer_instance take. To list the Data Layer assets in the content folders, instanced or not, use get_data_layer_assets; to instance one, create_data_layer_instance; for the map's overall World Partition state, get_world_partition_info.
commands.returns: { world_name: string, is_world_partition_enabled: bool, data_layer_instances: [{instance_name, short_name, full_name, data_layer_type, is_runtime, asset_path}], count: int, note: string }

commands.name: get_foliage_in_radius
commands.description: List the actual foliage instances of one FoliageType inside a world-space sphere, with each one's location, rotation, scale and instance_index. Use it to check what is standing on a spot before building there, or as a dry run before remove_foliage_instances with the same center and radius. Capped by max_results (default 100, hard cap 1000), so a full count must come from get_foliage_instance_count, not from len(instances).

params.name: foliage_type_path
params.description: Asset path of the UFoliageType to query

params.name: radius
params.description: Radius in world units

params.name: center_x
params.description: X component of the world-space center of the query sphere

params.name: center_y
params.description: Y component of the world-space center of the query sphere

params.name: center_z
params.description: Z component of the world-space center of the query sphere

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum entries returned (default 100, hard cap 1000)

commands.returns: { count, instances: [{location, rotation, scale, instance_index}] }

commands.name: get_foliage_instance_count
commands.description: Count how many instances of one FoliageType are placed across the level's InstancedFoliageActors. The cheapest oracle for "did that scatter place anything / did the removal clear it" -- one number, no transform payload. has_instances is the plain yes/no. Use get_foliage_in_radius when you need WHERE they are.

params.name: foliage_type_path
params.description: Full path of the UFoliageType asset

commands.returns: { foliage_type_path: string, foliage_type: string, has_instances: bool (instance_count > 0), instance_count: int, placed_instance_count: int, foliage_actor_count: int }

commands.name: get_foliage_type_properties
commands.description: Read a FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh asset's authored tunables in one call -- density, radius, scale and z-offset ranges, cull distances, mobility, align-to-normal, random yaw, world collision, shadow and indirect-lighting flags -- under the names set_foliage_type_properties takes. A curated view with nothing computed; get_properties reads any other UPROPERTY on the asset. Actor foliage types are not found. Describes the ASSET, not what is placed in the level: for that use get_foliage_instance_count / get_foliage_in_radius.

params.name: foliage_path
params.description: Asset path of the UFoliageType

commands.returns: { asset_path, foliage_class, density, density_adjustment_factor, radius, scale_x:{min,max}, scale_y, scale_z, z_offset, cull_distance:{min,max}, mobility, align_to_normal, random_yaw, collision_with_world, cast_shadow, affect_dynamic_indirect_lighting }

retired.how: object_path=<foliage type>, property_names=["Density","Radius","ScaleX","CullDistance",...], or get_object_info for all of them

commands.name: get_foliage_types
commands.description: List every FoliageType actually present in the level's InstancedFoliageActors, with the instance counts each carries. The level-side inventory ("what vegetation is in this map, and how much"), as opposed to get_properties which describes one asset. Nothing here means nothing has been placed, even if the FoliageType assets exist in Content.
commands.returns: { foliage_types: [object], foliage_type_count: int, foliage_actor_count: int }

commands.name: get_landscape_grass_type_properties
commands.description: Read one grass variety (variety_index, default 0) of a LandscapeGrassType asset: mesh, density, placement jitter, start/end cull distance, min LOD, scaling mode and scale ranges, rotation/alignment and shadow flags, under the names set_landscape_grass_type_properties takes. Use it instead of get_properties, which can only return the whole GrassVarieties array, not one element; per-platform values report their Default only. Two units that mislead: grass_density is instances per TEN square metres (25 means 2.5/m2), and start_cull_distance only fades if the mesh's material uses a PerInstanceFadeAmount node -- otherwise clusters pop at end_cull_distance and the start value does nothing.

params.name: grass_path
params.description: Asset path of the ULandscapeGrassType

params.name: variety_index
params.description: Optional index of the FGrassVariety to read, default 0 when omitted; an index outside the grass type's varieties is an error

commands.returns: { asset_path, grass_class, variety_index, variety_count, grass_mesh, grass_density, placement_jitter, start_cull_distance, end_cull_distance, min_lod, scaling, scale_x:{min,max}, scale_y, scale_z, random_rotation, align_to_surface, use_grid, cast_dynamic_shadow, receives_decals, keep_instance_buffer_cpu_copy }

commands.name: get_landscape_height_at
commands.description: How high is the ground here: sample the terrain surface height (world Z) at one world (x, y) -- the tool for placing an actor on the terrain, checking a spawn point is above water, or proving a region is not flat. Reads the heightmap texture directly (FHeightmapAccessor + bilinear interpolation), so unlike raycast_scene it needs NO collision, NO PIE and no cooked physics: it answers in the editor world where a line trace just misses the landscape. Honest at the edges -- outside the extent it clamps to the nearest vertex and says in_bounds=false, and it reports the (col,row) vertex it sampled so you can verify the pixel-to-world mapping. Use export_landscape_heightmap instead when the question is about the WHOLE terrain (min/max, unfilled regions, did an import land): a handful of probes has repeatedly suggested flips and offsets that were not there.

params.name: x
params.description: World-space X coordinate to sample

params.name: y
params.description: World-space Y coordinate to sample

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name or label, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, x: number, y: number, height: number, vertex: [int, int], in_bounds: bool }

commands.name: get_landscape_info
commands.description: Find the terrain and read its geometry: every ALandscape actor in the editor world with its world location and scale, vertex extent (min_x/min_y/max_x/max_y, size_x/size_y) and component layout (component_count, component_size_quads, subsection_size_quads, num_subsections). The first call of any landscape task -- it gives you the actor name the other landscape tools need, and the numbers to convert a world XY into a heightmap vertex. Also the ONLY trustworthy check of where the terrain actually is: the editor's New Landscape dialog treats its Location field as the CENTRE, so a terrain can sit half a world away from the corner you typed; read `location` here afterwards instead of believing the input. Note it lists ALandscape actors only, not the LandscapeStreamingProxy actors a World-Partition map renders through.
commands.returns: { landscapes: [{ actor_name, actor_path, location: [x,y,z], scale: [x,y,z], component_size_quads, subsection_size_quads, num_subsections, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y, size_x, size_y, component_count }], landscape_count: int }

commands.name: get_landscape_layers
commands.description: List which paint/weight layers are registered on a landscape (name plus its LandscapeLayerInfo asset). The cheap check before painting: a layer missing from this list will silently absorb any paint_landscape_layer call. Use it to discover the layer names a terrain material expects.

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, layers: [object], layer_count: int }

commands.name: get_landscape_material
commands.description: Read which material the terrain is currently using: the landscape's assigned render material and hole material as asset paths (direct UPROPERTY read, null when unset). The read-back oracle for set_landscape_material. It reports the ALandscape actor only -- on a World-Partition map the LandscapeStreamingProxy actors carry their own copy, so to prove the whole terrain is dressed also read landscape_material on the proxies.

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, material_path: string|null, hole_material_path: string|null }

commands.name: get_landscape_nanite_status
commands.description: Report a landscape's Nanite flags (enabled / built / up-to-date / out-of-date) without triggering a build. Read-only, editor-only. TRUST ONLY nanite_enabled: the built/up-to-date flags can CONTRADICT each other (nanite_built=false alongside nanite_up_to_date=true and out_of_date=false) and stay at built=false while the editor is visibly building the meshes -- they do not distinguish "not built" from "built and current". For "is the Nanite mesh actually built", count the "Built static mesh ...LandscapeNaniteMesh" lines in Saved/Logs/ instead.

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name/label, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, nanite_enabled: bool, nanite_built: bool, nanite_up_to_date: bool, nanite_out_of_date: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: get_landscape_spline_control_point
commands.description: Read ONE landscape spline control point by index: its landscape-local location and rotation, half-width, side/end falloff, and how many segments connect to it. The per-point reader that pairs with set_landscape_spline_control_point; get_landscape_splines only gives component-level counts, so this is the only way to see where a road or river point actually sits. connected_segment_count = 0 marks a dangling point that draws nothing.

params.name: control_point_index
params.description: Index into the splines component's ControlPoints (required)

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, control_point_index: int, control_point_count: int, location: [number], rotation: [number], width: number, side_falloff: number, end_falloff: number, connected_segment_count: int }

commands.name: get_landscape_splines
commands.description: Summary of a landscape's spline component: whether it has one at all, plus the control point and segment counts. The quick "is there a road/river network on this terrain, and how big" check, and the count oracle after adding or removing points. For an individual point's position and width use get_landscape_spline_control_point -- this returns no per-point data.

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, has_splines_component: bool, control_point_count: int, segment_count: int }

commands.name: get_level_instance_info
commands.description: List every Level Instance actor (ALevelInstance, Packed Level Actors included) in the editor world, live from the world's actors, without changing anything: per actor its label (or name when unlabeled), the .umap it references, whether that reference is valid, whether its level has finished loading (false right after binding, as loading is deferred) and its location. Use it to find the actor the other level-instance tools take: create_level_instance places one, edit_level_instance and commit_level_instance edit its content in place, break_level_instance turns it into plain actors, pack_level_actors bakes a map into a packed Blueprint. Classic streaming sub-levels are listed by get_streaming_levels instead, and other actors by get_actors_in_level. A map with no level instances is a success with an empty list and count 0. Reads the editor world, not a PIE session.
commands.returns: { world: string, level_instances: [{ actor_name: string, world_asset_path: string, world_asset_valid: bool, is_loaded: bool, location: [number,number,number] }], count: number }

commands.name: get_lighting_in_area
commands.description: Light-only spatial query: every actor carrying a LightComponent within radius cm of a world point, reporting light_type, intensity, color and distance. Use it to answer "why is this spot dark / blown out" without walking the whole outliner (get_actors_in_radius returns everything and no light data). World-aware: world='editor' (default) | 'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N', which is what lets you see lights attached to actors that only exist at runtime (a torch on a spawned character, a muzzle flash), and the reply stamps world_name/world_package/net_mode/pie_instance so lights_count:0 is readable as "not in THIS world".

params.name: radius
params.description: Search radius in centimetres (Unreal units), measured to each light actor's origin.

params.name: center
params.description: World-space center, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Omitted, it is the origin [0,0,0], which reads exactly like "there are no lights here"; any other value (an object, another length) is an error.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). An unrecognised value FAILS naming the worlds that exist; it never falls back to another world in silence.

commands.returns: { center_x: number, center_y: number, center_z: number, radius: number, world: string, lights: [{ actor_name: string, light_type: string, intensity: number, light_color: string, distance: number, location: { x: number, y: number, z: number } }], lights_count: number, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_navigation_data
commands.description: Inventory of navigation in a chosen world: every ANavigationData actor (the RecastNavMesh included) with its class, every NavMeshBoundsVolume with its location, and whether the world is flagged whole-world-navigable. The first thing to read when AI will not path -- no bounds volume, or a volume with an empty brush, means zero navmesh tiles. Errors honestly if the world has no navigation system at all. World-aware: world='editor' (default) | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'pie'. WARNING: The navmesh is SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE: asking a client answers "Navigation System not found" while the server's navmesh is perfectly alive, so anchor world='server' -- and the reply stamps world_name/world_package/net_mode/pie_instance so you can prove which one you asked.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- the ONLY one that owns a navmesh) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'pie' (ambiguous) | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). An unrecognised value FAILS naming the worlds that exist; it never falls back to another world in silence.

commands.returns: { world: string, navigation_data: [{ name: string, class: string }], navigation_data_count: number, nav_bounds_volumes: [{ name: string, location_x: number, location_y: number, location_z: number }], nav_bounds_volumes_count: number, navigation_system_available: bool, is_whole_world_navigable: bool, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_spline_points
commands.description: Reads the control points of a named actor's USplineComponent (reader twin of set_spline_points). Returns each point's index and local-space location (the same space set_spline_points writes in), plus the total count and closed-loop flag.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, count: int, closed_loop: bool, points: [{ index: int, location: [number, number, number] }] }

commands.name: get_streaming_levels
commands.description: List every streaming sub-level of the current editor world (UWorld::GetStreamingLevels) without changing anything: per sub-level its package, wrapper object name and streaming class, the requested should-be-loaded and should-be-visible flags, and whether it is actually loaded and visible now, plus world_package (the persistent map). A world with no sub-levels is a success with an empty list; a World Partition map normally has none, since its cells stream at runtime (get_world_partition_info, list_world_partition_actors). Use it to find the level_package_path the other tools take: add_streaming_level adds one, set_streaming_level_loaded and set_streaming_level_visible change the requests, remove_streaming_level detaches one. For Level Instance actors use get_level_instance_info; for the map you are on get_current_level. Reads the editor world, not a PIE session.
commands.returns: { streaming_levels: [{ package_name: string, name: string, streaming_class: string, should_be_loaded: bool, should_be_visible: bool, is_level_loaded: bool, is_level_visible: bool }], streaming_level_count: number, world_package: string }

commands.name: get_world_partition_info
commands.description: Reads the editor world's World Partition state: data layer count, runtime hash class, streaming, the number of GENERATED streaming grids (0 until a cook/build generates them; edit-time grid settings live in the map's World Settings) and whether a minimap texture already exists (a minimap is built only by the WorldPartitionMiniMapBuilder commandlet with -AllowCommandletRendering or Build > Build Minimap). REAL read: works on any map, also during PIE. Returns is_world_partition_enabled=false on the default (non-WP) editor map, which is the correct result.
commands.returns: { world_name: string, is_world_partition_enabled: bool, num_data_layers: int, runtime_hash_type: string, is_streaming_enabled: bool, num_streaming_grids: int (generated runtime grids of a spatial hash; 0 otherwise), has_minimap: bool (a WorldPartitionMiniMap actor holds a texture), note: string }

commands.name: get_world_settings
commands.description: Read a world's framework wiring: default GameMode plus the pawn / PlayerController / HUD / spectator classes it hands out, and gravity, time dilation and paused state. Use this to check WHICH GameMode+PC a map will spawn. It also reads the physics/bounds side: the authored GlobalGravityZ, its override switch and the effective gravity, KillZ and its damage type, whether world-bounds checks are on (KillZ does nothing without them), WorldToMeters and bForceNoPrecomputedLighting -- the read-back of set_world_gravity and set_kill_z, which write the editor world. World-aware: with the default world='editor' there is no live GameMode, so the classes come from the DefaultGameMode CDO -- i.e. what the map INTENDS; ask for world='server' and GetAuthGameMode() returns the GameMode a running PIE ACTUALLY instantiated, which is the read that settles a set_player_controller_class that looks applied and is not. WARNING: world_type is stamped by the canonical world evidence, so it can read 'PIE', not only Game/Editor/Other.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- the only one with a live AuthGameMode) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). An unrecognised value FAILS naming the worlds that exist; it never falls back to another world in silence.

commands.returns: { world: string, world_name: string, world_type: string, default_game_mode: string, default_pawn_class: string, player_controller_class: string, hud_class: string, spectator_class: string, world_gravity_enabled: bool (the effective gravity Z is non-zero), world_gravity_overridden: bool (Override World Gravity), world_gravity_z: number, global_gravity_z: number (the authored override value), global_gravity_set: bool (Override World Gravity), effective_gravity_z: number (WorldSettings GetGravityZ), kill_z: number, kill_z_damage_type: string, enable_world_bounds_checks: bool, world_to_meters: number, force_no_precomputed_lighting: bool, time_dilation: number, paused: number, world_package: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: import_landscape_heightmap
commands.description: Load a PNG or 16-bit .r16 heightmap file from disk and stamp it onto an existing landscape: this is the reliable route to terrain relief, and the reason to prefer it over the editor's Import from File dialog, which can fill only part of the components and drop the peak with no warning at all. It does not negotiate resolution -- create the landscape at the file's own vertex size first (create_landscape) so resampled comes back false. success/applied is an acknowledgement, not proof: the oracle is export_landscape_heightmap plus an array compare against the source file, or get_landscape_height_at probes.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute filesystem path or /Game asset path of the heightmap

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: flip_y
params.description: Optional, flip the Y axis on import

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, file_path: string, source_width: int, source_height: int, dest_width: int, dest_height: int, resampled: bool, applied: bool }

commands.name: inject_analog_input
commands.description: Feed an analog axis value (gamepad stick, trigger) to a running PIE session's PlayerController -- how you actually MOVE or LOOK headless, where inject_key_input only does digital keys. NOTE: A single axis sample decays to zero within a tick, so sustained motion needs hold_seconds, which re-injects every tick for that long and then neutralises with a 0.0; it is fire-and-forget and returns immediately. Requires an active PIE session and a genuinely analog key (a digital one is a clean error).

params.name: key
params.description: Required analog key name, e.g. "Gamepad_LeftX", "Gamepad_LeftTriggerAxis". Rejected with a clean error if the key is not analog.

params.name: value
params.description: Required float axis value; roughly -1..1 for sticks, 0..1 for triggers.

params.name: pie_client_index
params.description: Optional int (default 0). Which PIE client window to target -- 0 is the server/host window in a ListenServer session, 1 the first client.

params.name: hold_seconds
params.description: Optional float. When > 0, the analog value is re-injected every tick for this many seconds (a single axis sample decays to zero, so sustained motion needs re-feeding), then a final 0.0 is injected to neutralize. Fire-and-forget: returns immediately and the hold runs across the next hold_seconds of PIE. Omit (or 0) for a single sample.

commands.returns: { injected: bool, key: string, value: number, pie_client_index: int, hold_seconds: number }

commands.name: inject_key_input
commands.description: Press or release a keyboard/gamepad key at a running PIE session's PlayerController, so an agent can drive the game headless -- jump, interact, open a menu. Press and release are SEPARATE calls: a tap is two of them, a hold is press now and release later. Requires an active PIE session; use inject_analog_input for sticks and triggers (with its hold_seconds for sustained movement) and inject_mouse_button for clicks. WARNING: `injected` only means the event reached the controller: whether the game DID anything is a state read, and in co-op read the right world.

params.name: key
params.description: Required key name as Unreal spells it, e.g. "SpaceBar", "W", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom". An unknown name is a clean error, never a silent no-op.

params.name: event
params.description: Optional "Pressed" (default), "Released" or "Repeat". Remember the matching Released, or the game keeps thinking the key is down.

params.name: pie_client_index
params.description: Optional int (default 0). Which PIE client window to target -- 0 is the server/host window in a ListenServer session, 1 the first client.

params.name: amount_depressed
params.description: Optional float (default 1.0). Only meaningful on the controller route.

params.name: route
params.description: Optional "controller" (default), "slate" or "both". NOTE: THIS IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN DRIVING THE GAME AND DRIVING THE UI: the controller route goes through PlayerController::InputKey, which is the gameplay input layer -- it moves the character and fires Enhanced Input actions but NEVER moves UI focus. The slate route goes through FSlateApplication::ProcessKeyDownEvent, which is the only one that moves FOCUS, so it is the only way to test a menu's gamepad navigation headless. They are not interchangeable; "both" sends to each.

commands.returns: { injected: bool, key: string, event: string, pie_client_index: int, route: string, controller_injected: bool, slate_injected: bool, slate_handled: bool, slate_note? } -- NOTE: slate_handled is Slate's own verdict on whether anything consumed the key: false usually means nothing had focus, which is the useful signal (not a failure of the call).

commands.name: inject_mouse_button
commands.description: Fire a simulated mouse click at a running PIE session's PlayerController: fire/aim/interact without a human at the mouse. Press and release are SEPARATE calls, so a click is two of them and a hold is press now, release later. It injects the button only -- it does not move the cursor, so aim with set_control_rotation first. Requires an active PIE session; use inject_key_input for keyboard/gamepad buttons and click_pie_widget for UMG buttons, which this does NOT reach.

params.name: button
params.description: Optional "Left"|"Right"|"Middle" (default "Left"); anything else is a clean error.

params.name: event
params.description: Optional "Pressed" (default) or "Released". A full click needs both, in two calls.

params.name: pie_client_index
params.description: Optional int (default 0). Which PIE client window to aim at -- 0 is the server/host window in a ListenServer session, 1 the first client.

commands.returns: { injected: bool (the event was delivered to the controller, NOT that the game reacted -- verify with state), button: string, event: string, pie_client_index: int }

commands.name: is_play_in_editor_active
commands.description: THE oracle for "is the game running right now": asks ULevelEditorSubsystem::IsInPlayInEditor and returns is_pie_active plus status 'Playing'/'Stopped' and the current level name. Cheap, read-only, no params. Use it to confirm start_play_in_editor / stop_play_in_editor (both answer from before the async transition finishes) and as the gate before any save -- saving with PIE up is refused by the engine. WARNING: Do NOT use the pie_active field of list_dirty_packages for this: it can report false with PIE running and answering.
commands.returns: { is_pie_active: bool, current_level: string (the EDITOR's current level, not the PIE world), status: 'Playing'|'Stopped' }

commands.name: list_orphaned_ofpa_actors
commands.description: Finds __ExternalActors__ (OFPA) packages with no registered World Partition descriptor -- actors invisible to get_actors_by_class/list_world_partition_actors because their package fell out of sync with the level's registered actor set (e.g. after a bad delete+save). Three enumeration layers, most-to-least authoritative: (1) raw filesystem scan of the level's external-actors folder (catches AssetRegistry blind spots); (2) AssetRegistry GetAssetsByPath (bIncludeOnlyOnDiskAssets=true, zero-load class info via AssetClassPath); (3) IF map_path is the CURRENTLY OPEN editor world with an initialized World Partition, a live cross-check against the real descriptor set. When map_path is a DIFFERENT map (the recommended procedure: clean up orphans with the editor on another map), layer 3 is skipped and disk-and-registry-both-present candidates are reported as candidate_unconfirmed rather than a false-confident confirmed_orphan. Read-only: never loads a package, never opens/swaps to map_path.

params.name: map_path
params.description: Long package name of the level to inspect (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Maps/MainMap); does NOT need to be the open editor world (that only enables the stronger layer-3 cross-check).

params.name: filter_generated_class
params.description: Optional substring (case-insensitive) matched against each candidate's generated_class_name (the AssetClassPath, resolved with zero loading); also tried as a UClass IsChildOf when the string resolves to a real class.

commands.returns: { map_path, external_actors_path, disk_count, asset_registry_count, live_registered_count (nullable), live_cross_check_available, confirmed_orphan_count, candidate_unconfirmed_count, candidates: [{ path, generated_class_name, is_loaded, on_disk, in_asset_registry, classification }], note }

commands.name: list_world_partition_actors
commands.description: Lists the editor world's World Partition actors by walking their DESCRIPTORS without loading any actor package.  Unlike get_actors_by_class (which only sees LOADED AActors via TActorIterator), this reads FWorldPartitionActorDescInstance for every actor known to World Partition, INCLUDING spatially-unloaded / streamed-out ones (solving "get_actors_by_class only sees loaded actors"). Editor-world read only (WP actor descriptors are editor-only data); honest empty list on a non-WP (default) map.

params.name: filter_class
params.description: Optional. Class filter: resolved to a UClass (full path, /Script name, Blueprint asset path, or bare A/U name) and matched against each descriptor's native class via IsChildOf; ALSO matched as a case-insensitive substring against the descriptor's native and base class paths (so Blueprint class names like 'BP_Foo_C' or partial names work).

params.name: name_contains
params.description: Optional. Case-insensitive substring matched against the actor's label, object name, and soft path.

params.name: folder
params.description: Optional. Case-insensitive substring matched against the actor's editor folder path.

params.name: limit
params.description: Optional int cap on the number of actors returned (default 2000); total_matched reports the full match count regardless of the cap.

commands.returns: { world: string, is_world_partition: bool, is_initialized: bool, count: int, total_matched: int, truncated: bool, actors: [{ path: string, name: string, label: string, native_class: string, base_class: string, display_class: string, is_spatially_loaded: bool, is_loaded: bool, editor_only: bool, folder: string, runtime_grid: string, editor_bounds: {valid,origin,extent}, runtime_bounds: {valid,origin,extent}, data_layers: [string] }], note: string }

commands.name: load_world_partition_region
commands.description: Load the World Partition actors inside a box of the editor world into memory and keep them there, as the editor's Load Region does, so get_actors_by_class, get_properties and the other actor tools can see actors that were unloaded. Use it on a World Partition map before reading or editing actors far from what is loaded; release them with unload_world_partition_region and the same label. It edits, spawns and saves nothing, but it is not idempotent: each call registers one more region under its label (unload releases them all). A map without World Partition, or one not initialized, and a zero-volume box are errors and nothing loads; a box that touches no cell answers loaded false. num_loaded_actors counts the loaded actors of the whole world, not only this box.

params.name: min
params.description: [x,y,z] one corner of the box, in centimetres (world units); min and max may come in either order, they are sorted per axis.

params.name: max
params.description: [x,y,z] the opposite corner of the box, in centimetres; it must differ from min so the box has volume.

params.name: label
params.description: Name for the region, used later by unload_world_partition_region (default "MCP Load Region"); use one label per region to release them separately.

commands.returns: { world: string, is_world_partition: bool, loaded: bool, region_min: [x,y,z], region_max: [x,y,z], label: string, num_loaded_actors: int, note: string }

commands.name: pack_level_actors
commands.description: Bakes a saved map (.umap) into a reusable APackedLevelActor Blueprint headless: the source level's static-mesh actors are merged into ISM components on the generated Blueprint so it streams as one cheap actor.  Uses FPackedLevelActorBuilder::CreateDefaultBuilder + CreateOrUpdateBlueprint with bCheckoutAndSave=false on purpose — that builder save path is silently cancelled under -unattended (FileHelpers PR_Cancelled) and would falsely report success; instead the Blueprint package is persisted explicitly via UEditorLoadingAndSavingUtils::SavePackages and its REAL result is returned as `saved`. The build runs in the builder's own FPreviewScene (no editor-world swap, no PIE, no render). Requires the editor (GEditor). Idempotent: an existing Blueprint at blueprint_path is updated in place (the engine early-outs via PackedHash when the source is unchanged), never duplicated.

params.name: world_asset_path
params.description: Package/object path of the saved source map to pack (e.g. "/Game/Maps/Foo"). Must exist on disk.

params.name: blueprint_path
params.description: Destination package path for the APackedLevelActor Blueprint (e.g. "/Game/Maps/BPP_Foo").

params.name: save
params.description: Optional, default true. Persist the Blueprint package to disk and report the real save result in `saved`.

commands.returns: { blueprint_path: string, source_world_asset: string, blueprint_created: bool, packed: bool, packed_hash: number, saved: bool, note: string }

commands.name: paint_landscape_layer
commands.description: Paint terrain texture layers headless: write ONE uniform weight (0-255) into a landscape weightmap over a vertex region, or the whole terrain if you omit region. Blunt by design -- it fills a rectangle, it does not brush or blend, so build variety by painting several layers over different rectangles. The layer must already be registered with add_landscape_layer or nothing is stored. Region coordinates are VERTICES, not world units: get the ranges from get_landscape_info. Check vertices_painted and paint_warning rather than the success flag.

params.name: layer_info_path
params.description: Full path of the ULandscapeLayerInfoObject asset

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: weight
params.description: 0 to 255 weight value, default 255

params.name: region
params.description: Optional [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] vertex region, defaults to the whole landscape

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, layer_info_path: string, layer_name: string, weight: int, painted: bool, vertices_painted: number, region: [int], paint_warning: string }

commands.name: possess_pawn
commands.description: Make the first PlayerController of a running PIE session possess a pawn of that PIE world (AController::Possess), so input and camera go to it; the pawn it controlled before is unpossessed and stays in the world. Requires PIE: start it with start_play_in_editor; with no PIE session for pie_client_index, or a name that is not a pawn in that world, it is an error and nothing changes. Then drive it with inject_key_input or inject_analog_input, or aim it with set_control_rotation. Runtime only: nothing is saved and there is no undo. A pawn the controller already has is a success with already_possessed=true and no call. The engine's authority gate silently skips the possession on a pure client's PlayerController (Standalone and ListenServer have authority): then possessed=false, had_authority=false and a note, still a success, so always read possessed.

params.name: pawn_actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the pawn actor in the PIE world, e.g. "BP_Vehicle_C_0" or "Truck"; find_actors_by_name or get_actors_in_level with world="pie" list them.

params.name: pie_client_index
params.description: Which PIE instance, a whole number from 0 (default 0: the first, the server in a ListenServer session); 1, 2... for further clients.

commands.returns: { possessed: bool, already_possessed: bool, had_authority: bool, pawn_actor_name: string, pie_client_index: int, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_actor_from_data_layer_instance
commands.description: Removes an editor-world actor from a data layer instance (inverse of assign_actor_to_data_layer_instance).  Uses UDataLayerEditorSubsystem::RemoveActorFromDataLayer against the data layer instance referencing the given asset. Requires a World Partition world; on a non-WP (default) map this returns an honest error (no editor-world swap). Idempotent: removed=false means the actor was not in the layer (not an error).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or name of the actor in the editor world.

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the UDataLayerAsset (the instance referencing it must exist in the world).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, data_layer_asset_path: string, instance_name: string, short_name: string, removed: bool, message: string }

commands.name: remove_data_layer_instance
commands.description: Removes a data layer instance from the editor world's World Partition (inverse of create_data_layer_instance).  Uses UDataLayerEditorSubsystem::DeleteDataLayer (void), verified by read-back: after delete GetDataLayerInstance(asset) must be null. Requires a World Partition world; on a non-WP (default) map this returns an honest error (no editor-world swap). Idempotent: already_deleted=true when no instance referenced the asset before the call.

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the UDataLayerAsset whose instance should be removed from the world.

commands.returns: { data_layer_asset_path: string, deleted: bool, already_deleted: bool, instance_name?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: remove_foliage_instances
commands.description: Delete the placed instances of one FoliageType from all InstancedFoliageActors in the level: EVERY instance by default -- the bulk undo for a scatter that went wrong -- or, with a radius, only those inside a world-space sphere, the way to carve a building site, road or clearing out of existing vegetation without wiping the whole type. Preview a sphere with get_foliage_in_radius first. The FoliageType asset itself is untouched. Undoable. Check remaining (and remaining_in_radius for a sphere) in the reply, not just removed_count.

params.name: foliage_type_path
params.description: Full path of the UFoliageType asset

params.name: center_x
params.description: Optional X of the world-space center of the removal sphere (default 0); needs radius.

params.name: center_y
params.description: Optional Y of the world-space center of the removal sphere (default 0); needs radius.

params.name: center_z
params.description: Optional Z of the world-space center of the removal sphere (default 0); needs radius.

params.name: radius
params.description: Optional radius of the removal sphere in world units, > 0. When given only instances inside the sphere are removed; when omitted every instance of the type is.

commands.returns: { foliage_type_path: string, foliage_type: string, removed_count: int, remaining: int (instances of the type left anywhere), foliage_actors_affected: int, removed_all: bool (remaining == 0), requested_radius?: number (sphere mode), remaining_in_radius?: int (sphere mode: instances left inside the sphere, 0 when it worked) }

commands.name: remove_landscape_layer
commands.description: Unregister a target weight (paint) layer from a landscape -- the inverse of add_landscape_layer. Identify it either by layer_info_path or by layer_name. This detaches the layer from the terrain; it does not delete the LandscapeLayerInfo asset, and any material that still blends that layer will now read zero weight for it.

params.name: layer_info_path
params.description: Full path of the ULandscapeLayerInfoObject asset; if omitted, resolved by layer_name via the landscape info

params.name: layer_name
params.description: Optional layer FName; defaults to the layer info's own GetLayerName()

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, layer_info_path: string, layer_name: string, layer_removed: bool, already_absent: bool, target_layer_count: int }

commands.name: remove_landscape_spline_control_point
commands.description: Delete a landscape spline control point by index, and with it every segment attached to it (segments_removed says how many) -- so removing a mid-route point BREAKS the road or river in two rather than healing it; re-join the neighbours with add_landscape_spline_segment. Remaining indices shift, so delete from the highest index down when removing several.

params.name: control_point_index
params.description: Index into the splines component's ControlPoints

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, control_point_index: int, removed: bool, control_point_count: int, segments_removed: int, segment_count: int }

commands.name: remove_landscape_spline_segment
commands.description: Delete ONE landscape spline segment by index, unlinking its two endpoint control points but keeping them -- the way to cut a road or river without losing the route's points (remove_landscape_spline_control_point destroys the point and all its segments instead). Segment indices shift after a removal, so work from the highest index down.

params.name: segment_index
params.description: Index into the splines component's Segments

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, segment_index: int, removed: bool, segment_count: int, control_points_unlinked: int }

commands.name: remove_orphaned_ofpa_actors
commands.description: Honest-gated deletion of __ExternalActors__ (OFPA) orphan packages. Every entry in actor_paths is RE-VERIFIED against a fresh 3-layer scan (never trusts the caller's list, e.g. from a stale list_orphaned_ofpa_actors call) -- only a definitive classification='confirmed_orphan' is eligible for deletion; anything else (candidate_unconfirmed / registered / registered_no_file / unknown) is refused regardless of dry_run/force_save. dry_run DEFAULTS TO TRUE (deliberate deviation from a delete-by-default signature: editor crashes around OFPA + World Partition actor deletion are documented, and this tool is unexercised) and is ALWAYS forced to true -- no override parameter exists for this -- when map_path is the CURRENTLY OPEN editor world; open a different map first to actually delete (the recommended cleanup procedure). Deletion (when dry_run=false) is raw file removal of the .uasset (+ sibling .uexp/.ubulk), NOT ObjectTools::ForceDeleteObjects on a bare AActor package -- that path is untested here for a standalone-loaded actor with no owning level, and is plausibly part of why in-editor OFPA actor deletion crashes; a package still loaded in memory is refused unless force_save=true.

params.name: map_path
params.description: Long package name of the level whose orphans to remove (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Maps/MainMap).

params.name: actor_paths
