params.description: Array of external-actor PACKAGE path strings to remove (the 'path' field from list_orphaned_ofpa_actors).

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Default true. When true (or forced true by the active-world gate), nothing is deleted; would_delete reports what WOULD be removed. Pass false to actually delete.

params.name: force_save
params.description: Default false. Only meaningful when dry_run=false: permits deleting a candidate that is currently loaded in memory (is_loaded=true). Never overrides the confirmed_orphan re-verification requirement or the active-world gate.

commands.returns: { map_path, requested_count, refused_active_world, dry_run, would_delete: [{path, generated_class_name, is_loaded}], deleted: [{path, deleted, error?}], refused_not_orphan: [{path, classification, reason}], refused_loaded: [{path, reason}], deleted_count, note }

commands.name: remove_streaming_level
commands.description: Detach a streaming sub-level from the current editor world: a loaded one is unloaded and taken out with UEditorLevelUtils::RemoveLevelFromWorld (unsaved edits in it are lost), an unloaded one has its streaming wrapper dropped with UWorld::RemoveStreamingLevel; method says which. The sub-level's .umap stays on disk; the persistent map is marked dirty, not saved (save_level keeps the change), and the change is wrapped in an undo transaction, but add_streaming_level is the reliable way back. To only hide or unload it while keeping it in the world, use set_streaming_level_visible or set_streaming_level_loaded instead. removed is re-checked by listing the world's sub-levels again; success stays true even when removed=false, so read removed. A level that is not a sub-level of the editor world is an error and nothing changes; a second call on the same level is therefore an error (not idempotent).

params.name: level_package_path
params.description: Package path of an existing streaming sub-level, e.g. "/Game/Maps/Arena_Lighting", as get_streaming_levels returns it; an object path or the bare level name ("Arena_Lighting") also matches, case ignored.

commands.returns: { package_name: string, removed: bool, method: string, streaming_level_count: number }

commands.name: scatter_foliage_in_box
commands.description: Scatter N seeded-random foliage instances of a type inside a world-space box (same seed = same layout). DANGER: measured CRASHING the editor process, the identical access violation as add_foliage_instances (UnrealEditor-FoliageEdit.dll) because both end in the same FFoliageInfo::AddInstance path -- lowering count does not help and the failure arrives disguised as "Connection reset". Use add_instanced_static_mesh_component + add_instanced_static_mesh_instance to scatter instead, or PCG for rule-driven placement. Save your work before calling this at all.

params.name: foliage_type_path
params.description: Full path of the UFoliageType asset

params.name: count
params.description: Optional number of instances to scatter, default 8 when omitted; a negative count is taken as 0

params.name: seed
params.description: Seed for the random stream, default 1337

params.name: center
params.description: [x, y, z] box center in world space, default [0,0,0]

params.name: extent
params.description: [x, y, z] box half-extents, default [500,500,0]

params.name: align_to_ground
params.description: If true, place at the box top instead of random Z

commands.returns: { foliage_type_path: string, foliage_type: string, requested: int, seed: int, align_to_ground: bool, instances_added: int, instance_count_before: int, total_instance_count: int, placed_instance_count: int, instances_added_ok: bool, center: [number], extent: [number], foliage_actor: string }

commands.name: scatter_foliage_on_layer
commands.description: Scatter foliage only where a landscape PAINT LAYER is strong enough: samples seeded candidates in a box, keeps those whose layer weight clears layer_weight_threshold, and rejects the rest -- so trees land on the forest layer and not on rock. The rule-driven sibling of scatter_foliage_in_box. DANGER: it reaches the same FFoliageInfo::AddInstance path that can crash the editor from its two sibling tools, so treat it as unsafe and prefer add_instanced_static_mesh_component + add_instanced_static_mesh_instance (query the layer weight yourself) or a PCG graph. Save your work before calling it.

params.name: foliage_type_path
params.description: Asset path of the UFoliageType (e.g. /Game/Foliage/BP_Tree)

params.name: landscape_name_or_label
params.description: Actor label (or name) of the target ALandscape

params.name: layer_name
params.description: FName of the landscape paint layer (e.g. "Grass", "Forest")

params.name: center
params.description: Optional [x,y,z] world center of the scatter box (default 0,0,0)

params.name: extent
params.description: Optional [x,y,z] half-extent of the scatter box (default 500,500,0)

params.name: count
params.description: Number of candidate positions to sample (default 16)

params.name: layer_weight_threshold
params.description: Minimum layer weight [0,1] for placement (default 0.5)

params.name: seed
params.description: Random seed for deterministic scatter (default 1337)

params.name: align_to_ground
params.description: When true, candidates placed at box-top Z so ground snap is meaningful

commands.returns: { applied, requested_count, instances_added, instances_rejected }

commands.name: set_absolute_transform
commands.description: Make an EDITOR-world actor's root SceneComponent use ABSOLUTE (world-space) location/rotation/scale instead of inheriting from its parent -- for an attached actor that drifts or shears when its parent moves or is scaled. At least one of the three flags must be supplied (otherwise clean error), and the reply re-reads all three off the component. Read them back with get_absolute_transform; this does NOT call Modify(), so pair it with another dirtying edit or the save may skip the actor.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel); exact match, editor world only. Errors if the actor has no RootComponent.

params.name: absolute_location
params.description: Optional bool. True = keep world location regardless of the parent; omitted = leave the flag untouched.

params.name: absolute_rotation
params.description: Optional bool. True = keep world rotation regardless of the parent; omitted = leave untouched.

params.name: absolute_scale
params.description: Optional bool. True = ignore parent scale (stops inherited squash/stretch); omitted = leave untouched.

commands.returns: { applied: bool, actor_name: string, absolute_location: bool, absolute_rotation: bool, absolute_scale: bool (all three re-read off the root component) }

commands.name: set_actor_component_collision
commands.description: Sets collision on a PLACED actor's UPrimitiveComponent (the placed-actor twin of set_blueprint_component_collision). Resolves the actor by name/label then its primitive component (by name, or the root primitive when component_name is omitted) and applies, in order: SetCollisionProfileName (expands the profile into the FBodyInstance response array), SetCollisionEnabled, then per-channel SetCollisionResponseToChannel. Channel keys accept a friendly display name ("Pawn", "Visibility", or a project CUSTOM trace/object channel) OR an ECC_* token; this is how you block a custom game channel that the BlockAll profile leaves at Ignore. After applying, collision-enabled is toggled off/on to force the FBodyInstance to rebuild its filter data, and Actor->Modify() marks the (OFPA) package dirty so save_level persists the change.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target actor

params.name: component_name
params.description: Primitive component name; defaults to the actor's root primitive component when omitted

params.name: profile
params.description: Optional collision profile name to apply first (e.g. "BlockAll", "OverlapAllDynamic", a custom preset)

params.name: collision_enabled
params.description: Optional NoCollision/QueryOnly/PhysicsOnly/QueryAndPhysics

params.name: responses
params.description: Optional { channel: response } map; channel = friendly name or ECC_* token, response = Ignore/Overlap/Block

params.name: world
params.description: absent/"editor" (default; the world save_level persists) | "server" (the PIE world with authority) | "client" | "pie:N" | "pie" (ambiguous) | "game" (alias of "pie")

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, profile: string, collision_enabled: string, responses_applied: [{ channel: string, response: string }], collision_enabled_effective: string, rebuilt: bool, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: set_actor_folder
commands.description: Move an editor-world actor, found by internal name or label (first match), into an outliner folder; an empty folder_path moves it back to the root. Undoable, marks the level dirty, not saved; returns the internal actor_name and folder_path as given. get_actor_folder reads it back.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Current actor name or label in the world outliner

params.name: folder_path
params.description: Outliner folder path with "/" between levels, e.g. "Lighting/Sky"; an empty string moves the actor to the root.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, folder_path: string }

commands.name: set_actor_label
commands.description: Set the outliner label of an editor-world actor found by internal name or current label (first match). The engine trims it and keeps the old label when the new one is invalid, for example empty, so check label in the reply. Marks the level dirty without an undo entry.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Current actor name or label in the world outliner

params.name: new_label
params.description: Display label to set, e.g. "Lamp_Kitchen"; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, label: string }

commands.name: set_actor_lifetime
commands.description: Schedules an actor in the active world (a running PIE/game world if one exists, otherwise the editor world) for automatic destruction after N seconds via FTimerManager::SetTimer. Idempotent: re-running cancels the previous timer and resets the countdown. Used for transient effects (damage numbers, FX) that should auto-cleanup. Runtime/cooked-build safe: resolves the world via GEngine's world contexts, not GEditor, so it also works in packaged builds.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target actor (required)

params.name: seconds
params.description: Seconds until the actor is destroyed (required, >0)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, seconds: number, scheduled: bool, replaced_previous_timer: bool }

commands.name: set_actor_lock_location
commands.description: Lock or unlock an actor in the EDITOR world so viewport dragging cannot move it by accident (AActor::SetLockLocation). Pin landmarks -- PlayerStart, landscape, hand-placed props -- before a batch transform pass. Calls Modify(), so it dirties the actor's package and needs a save_level to persist. Read the flag back with get_actor_lock_location. Does not affect runtime/PIE movement.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel); exact match, editor world only.

params.name: locked
params.description: True to lock, false to unlock

commands.returns: { applied, actor_name, locked }

commands.name: set_actor_material
commands.description: Set a component-level override material on one slot of an editor-world actor (found by name or label): on its first StaticMeshComponent, else its first other mesh component. The mesh asset and other slots are untouched. Errors when the actor, a mesh component or the material is missing. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved. A slot_index outside the component's material slots is refused. For the mesh asset use set_static_mesh_material_slot; for a tweakable runtime copy, create_dynamic_material_on_actor.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the target actor

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UMaterialInterface

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Material slot index, from 0 to the component's slot count minus 1, default 0

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, material: string, slot_index: int }

commands.name: set_actor_spatially_loaded
commands.description: Sets whether an actor of the editor world is spatially loaded by World Partition: true streams it in and out with the grid cell it sits in, false keeps it always loaded. One undo step; the actor's package (its external actor file on a World Partition map) is marked dirty, not saved: persist with save_level. A value the actor already has succeeds with changed false. Actors the engine pins as always loaded (Info actors such as World Settings, directional lights, unbound post-process volumes) cannot change: the call still succeeds with applied false, can_change false and nothing changed. An unknown actor is an error. On a map without World Partition the flag is stored but has no effect. Read the flags of all actors with list_world_partition_actors (is_spatially_loaded); assign data layers with assign_actor_to_data_layer_instance, and bring unloaded actors into the editor with load_world_partition_region.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label or object name of the actor in the editor world (case-insensitive), e.g. "SM_Rock_12"; list_world_partition_actors gives labels even for unloaded actors, but the actor must be loaded.

params.name: is_spatially_loaded
params.description: Required bool: true = streamed with its grid cell, false = always loaded.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_path: string, requested: bool, is_spatially_loaded: bool, applied: bool, can_change: bool, changed: bool, note: string }

commands.name: set_control_rotation
commands.description: Set a Controller's control rotation (AController::SetControlRotation) in the active PIE session -- aims the view and, for a possessed pawn, its control-driven facing. Targets the named pawn's controller, a named controller, or (no target_name) the PIE session's PlayerController. PIE-gated: clean error if no PIE session.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Required number. Control rotation pitch (degrees).

params.name: yaw
params.description: Required number. Control rotation yaw (degrees).

params.name: roll
params.description: Required number. Control rotation roll (degrees).

params.name: target_name
params.description: Optional. Name/label of the possessed pawn (uses its controller) or a controller; default = the PIE session's PlayerController.

params.name: pie_client_index
params.description: Optional int (default 0).

commands.returns: { applied: bool, target: string, control_rotation: [pitch, yaw, roll], pie_client_index: int }

commands.name: set_data_layer_debug_color
commands.description: Set the debug color of a World Partition data layer asset (UDataLayerAsset), the color the Data Layers outliner and the World Partition debug views show for that layer, in one undo step, then save the asset and read the color back (color_set). Setting the color it already has writes and saves it again with the same result. A path that does not load as a data layer asset or a color that is not an array of 3 or 4 numbers is an error and nothing changes; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory. Find layer assets with get_data_layer_assets; create one with its color in one call with create_data_layer_asset; change its Editor or Runtime type with set_data_layer_type.

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Object or package path of the data layer asset, e.g. '/Game/DataLayers/DL_Interiors'.

params.name: color
params.description: [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] in 0-255, e.g. [255, 128, 0]; values are rounded and clamped to 0-255, and alpha defaults to 255.

commands.returns: { data_layer_asset_path: string, asset_path: string, debug_color: [number, number, number, number], data_layer_type: string, color_set: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_data_layer_initial_runtime_state
commands.description: Authors the initial runtime state ("Unloaded"|"Loaded"|"Activated") of a runtime data layer's instance in the current World Partition map, creating the instance from the asset if missing.  Headless authoring (no PIE); the state takes effect when the level streams in. Requires a World Partition map (honest error otherwise).

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the (runtime) data layer asset.

params.name: initial_runtime_state
params.description: "Unloaded", "Loaded" or "Activated".

params.name: create_instance_if_missing
params.description: Create the data layer instance from the asset if none exists yet (optional, default true).

commands.returns: { data_layer_asset_path: string, initial_runtime_state: string, is_runtime: bool, already_existed: bool, state_set: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_data_layer_parent
commands.description: Sets (or clears) the parent of a data layer instance in the editor world's World Partition (twin of create_data_layer_instance).  Uses UDataLayerEditorSubsystem::SetParentDataLayer, verified by read-back (GetParent() must equal the requested parent). Both instances are resolved from their UDataLayerAsset paths (create the instances first via create_data_layer_instance). Pass parent_data_layer_asset_path empty/omitted to detach (reparent to root). Requires a World Partition world; on a non-WP (default) map this returns an honest error (no editor-world swap). Idempotent: already_parented=true when the instance already had the requested parent. Note: SetParentDataLayer returns false (parented=false) when the engine rejects the relationship (CanBeChildOf()==false, e.g. a runtime child under an editor parent or a cycle); the read-back reports the honest result.

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the child UDataLayerAsset (its instance must exist in the world).

params.name: parent_data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the parent UDataLayerAsset (its instance must exist in the world). Omit or pass empty to clear the parent (reparent to root).

commands.returns: { data_layer_asset_path: string, parent_data_layer_asset_path: string, instance_name: string, parent_instance_name: string, parented: bool, already_parented: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: set_data_layer_runtime_state
commands.description: Sets the LIVE runtime state ("Unloaded"|"Loaded"|"Activated") of a runtime data layer in a running World Partition game (PIE).  Requires a World Partition map; outside PIE this is an honest gate (applied:false + note pointing to set_data_layer_initial_runtime_state) rather than a failure.

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the (runtime) data layer asset.

params.name: runtime_state
params.description: "Unloaded", "Loaded" or "Activated".

params.name: is_recursive
params.description: Also apply to child data layers (optional, default false).

commands.returns: { data_layer_asset_path: string, runtime_state: string, applied: bool, success: bool, note: string }

commands.name: set_data_layer_type
commands.description: Sets the EDataLayerType ("Editor" or "Runtime") of a UDataLayerAsset and saves it.  Editor-only authoring on the data asset itself (no world required); mirrors set_data_layer_debug_color.

params.name: data_layer_asset_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the data layer asset.

params.name: data_layer_type
params.description: "Editor" or "Runtime".

commands.returns: { data_layer_asset_path: string, asset_path: string, data_layer_type: string, is_runtime: bool, type_set: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: set_foliage_type_properties
commands.description: Set tunables of a FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh asset in one call, only the fields you pass, then save it. Over set_properties it takes the scale, z-offset and cull ranges as {"min","max"} objects and saves in the same call, but records no undo step. Returns the read-back values with applied_count and saved. An invalid mobility, or a range that is not such an object with a number bound, fails the call before anything is written. Edits the asset only: instances already placed keep their transforms. Read: get_foliage_type_properties.

params.name: foliage_path
params.description: Asset path of a UFoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh, e.g. "/Game/Foliage/FT_Example"; actor foliage types are not found.

params.name: density
params.description: Instances per 1000 x 1000 uu area (10 m by 10 m) when painting.

params.name: density_adjustment_factor
params.description: Density multiplier used when reapplying: above 1 adds instances, below 1 removes them.

params.name: radius
params.description: Minimum distance in cm between foliage instances.

params.name: scale_x
params.description: X scale range as a JSON object {"min":0.8,"max":1.2}, either bound optional; anything else (not an object, no number bound, another key) fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: scale_y
params.description: Y scale range as a JSON object {"min":0.8,"max":1.2}, either bound optional; anything else fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: scale_z
params.description: Z scale range as a JSON object {"min":0.8,"max":1.2}, either bound optional; anything else fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: z_offset
params.description: Z location offset range in cm as a JSON object {"min":-5,"max":0}; either bound may be left out; anything else fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: cull_distance
params.description: Integer interval {"min":start,"max":end} in cm: instances fade from min (only with a PerInstanceFadeAmount material node) and clusters cull beyond max; 0 disables. Anything but such an object fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: mobility
params.description: Component mobility: Static, Stationary or Movable, case-insensitive; any other value fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: align_to_normal
params.description: Tilt instances to the normal of the surface they are placed on.

params.name: random_yaw
params.description: Give each instance a random yaw around its vertical axis.

params.name: collision_with_world
params.description: Test for overlap with world geometry before placing each instance.

params.name: cast_shadow
params.description: Whether the foliage components cast shadows.

params.name: affect_dynamic_indirect_lighting
params.description: Whether the foliage injects light into dynamic indirect lighting; used only when cast_shadow is true.

commands.returns: { asset_path, foliage_class, density, density_adjustment_factor, radius, scale_x:{min,max}, scale_y, scale_z, z_offset, cull_distance:{min,max}, mobility, align_to_normal, random_yaw, collision_with_world, cast_shadow, affect_dynamic_indirect_lighting, applied_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_kill_z
commands.description: Set the KillZ death plane on the EDITOR world's WorldSettings: any actor falling below this world Z is destroyed, provided the world's bounds checks are enabled (read that flag with get_world_settings, enable_world_bounds_checks -- with it off, KillZ does nothing and the fall looks like a bug). Optionally sets the damage type applied on the kill. Values come back RE-READ off WorldSettings, not echoed. Undoable, but it dirties the MAP: save_level to keep it.

params.name: kill_z
params.description: World-space Z height (cm) below which actors get destroyed. Put it under the lowest playable geometry, not at 0.

params.name: kill_z_damage_type
params.description: Optional UDamageType class name or full path (e.g. 'DamageType' or '/Script/Engine.DamageType'). Resolved BEFORE anything is written, so a bad name is a clean error and KillZ is left untouched.

commands.returns: { applied_kill_z: number, kill_z: number (both re-read off WorldSettings), kill_z_damage_type: string ('None' if unset), success: bool (hardcoded) }

commands.name: set_landscape_grass_type_properties
commands.description: Set fields of one grass variety (variety_index) of a LandscapeGrassType asset, only those you pass, and save it. set_properties cannot address one FGrassVariety element of the asset's array; this also writes only the per-platform Default of density and cull distances, refreshes the state hash, and appends a variety for index 0 when the list is empty. No undo step. A grass_mesh that does not load, an invalid scaling or a scale range that is not a {"min","max"} object fails the call with nothing changed, not even the appended variety. Read: get_landscape_grass_type_properties.

params.name: grass_path
params.description: Asset path of the LandscapeGrassType, e.g. "/Game/Foliage/GT_Field".

params.name: variety_index
params.description: Index of the FGrassVariety to edit, default 0 (appends if the array is empty)

params.name: grass_mesh
params.description: Path of the StaticMesh for this variety, e.g. "/Game/Foliage/SM_Grass"; a path that does not load as a StaticMesh fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: grass_density
params.description: Instances per 10 square metres (25 means 2.5 per m2), so a wrong guess is a 10x error in the instance budget.

params.name: placement_jitter
params.description: Jitter of the grid placement from 0 to 1; only used when use_grid is true.

params.name: start_cull_distance
params.description: Distance in cm where instances start to fade, an integer; it does nothing unless the grass material uses a PerInstanceFadeAmount node, and 0 disables it.

params.name: end_cull_distance
params.description: Distance in cm beyond which a whole grass cluster is culled, an integer.

params.name: min_lod
params.description: Smallest mesh LOD to render, from -1 to 8; -1 uses the MinLOD of the static mesh asset.

params.name: scaling
params.description: Scale mode: Uniform, Free or LockXY, case-insensitive; any other value fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: scale_x
params.description: X scale range as a JSON object {"min":0.8,"max":1.2}, also used for every axis with Uniform scaling; anything else (not an object, no number bound, another key) fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: scale_y
params.description: Y scale range as a JSON object {"min":0.8,"max":1.2}, used only with Free scaling; anything else fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: scale_z
params.description: Z scale range as a JSON object {"min":0.8,"max":1.2}, used with Free or LockXY scaling; anything else fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: random_rotation
params.description: Give each instance a random rotation instead of a shared one.

params.name: align_to_surface
params.description: Tilt instances to the landscape normal instead of keeping them vertical.

params.name: use_grid
params.description: Place instances on a jittered grid instead of a Halton sequence.

params.name: cast_dynamic_shadow
params.description: Whether instances cast shadows with non-precomputed (dynamic) shadowing.

params.name: receives_decals
params.description: Whether the grass instances receive decals.

params.name: keep_instance_buffer_cpu_copy
params.description: Keep a CPU copy of the instance buffer, which the overlap-count queries of the grass component need.

commands.returns: { asset_path, grass_class, variety_index, variety_count, grass_mesh, grass_density, placement_jitter, start_cull_distance, end_cull_distance, min_lod, scaling, scale_x:{min,max}, scale_y, scale_z, random_rotation, align_to_surface, use_grid, cast_dynamic_shadow, receives_decals, keep_instance_buffer_cpu_copy, applied_count, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: set_landscape_height_in_box
commands.description: Raise or lower terrain: add delta_z world units to every heightmap vertex inside a world-space box (give box_min/box_max, or center/extent). A RELATIVE edit -- to force a region to one absolute height use flatten_landscape_in_box, and to soften the seams afterwards use smooth_landscape_in_box. Check vertices_modified in the reply: a zero means the box missed the terrain, which is what a wrongly-signed world coordinate looks like.

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: delta_z
params.description: World Z delta to apply to every vertex in the region

params.name: box_min
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world-space box minimum

params.name: box_max
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world-space box maximum

params.name: center
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] box center (alternative to box_min/box_max)

params.name: extent
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] box half-extents (alternative to box_min/box_max)

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, delta_z: number, delta_steps: int, applied: bool, vertices_modified: int, region_width: int, region_height: int, region: [int] }

commands.name: set_landscape_material
commands.description: Dress the terrain: assign the landscape's render material (and optionally its hole material) by asset path. Does MORE than the name suggests and that is the point -- it PROPAGATES to every LandscapeStreamingProxy, which is what actually renders on a World-Partition map, so you do not have to walk the proxies by hand. Consequence to budget for: it dirties one package per proxy plus the landscape. Idempotent (re-assigning the same material returns already_set), and the shader recompile is async even though the assignment is immediate. Do not trust material_assigned as the oracle -- re-read with get_landscape_material and spot-check a proxy's own landscape_material.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInterface (e.g. "/Engine/EngineMaterials/WorldGridMaterial")

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: hole_material_path
params.description: Optional asset path of the UMaterialInterface used for components with holes

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, material_path: string, material_assigned: bool, already_set: bool, hole_material_path?: string, hole_material_assigned?: bool, note: string }

commands.name: set_landscape_spline_control_point
commands.description: Move, rotate or re-width one existing landscape spline control point by index -- how you adjust a road or river route without rebuilding the spline. Only the fields you pass change (applied_count reports how many landed). Location is LANDSCAPE-LOCAL, not world, and width is a HALF-width. Read the current values first with get_landscape_spline_control_point.

params.name: control_point_index
params.description: Index into the splines component's ControlPoints

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] in landscape-local space; only applied if provided

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll]; only applied if provided

params.name: width
params.description: Optional half-width at this point; only applied if provided

commands.returns: { landscape_name: string, control_point_index: int, control_point_count: int, applied_count: int, location: [number], rotation: [number], width: number, updated: bool }

commands.name: set_pie_window_size
commands.description: Set the size of the Play-In-Editor window, so a UI can be checked at more than whatever resolution the window happens to have. start_play_in_editor takes no size parameter, so without this the classic UI bug -- fine at 1920x1080, overlapping at 1280x720 -- cannot be reproduced headless. Writes ULevelEditorPlaySettings, the same setting the editor's Play dropdown edits, and it applies to the NEXT PIE session: one already running keeps its window. For a single Widget Blueprint you do not need PIE at all -- render_widget_preview takes width/height/scale directly.

params.name: width
params.description: Window width in pixels (clamped to 160..7680).

params.name: height
params.description: Window height in pixels (clamped to 120..4320).

params.name: center
params.description: Center the new window on screen (default true).

commands.returns: { width: int, height: int, center: bool, applies_to: string, pie_currently_active: bool } -- applies_to is always "next PIE session"; WARNING: pie_currently_active:true is the warning that what is on screen RIGHT NOW is not what you just set.

commands.name: set_player_controller_class
commands.description: Point the world's GameMode at a PlayerController class, writing the live GameMode instance if one exists and otherwise the defaults of the world's Blueprint GameMode (refused when the GameMode is a native class, or when the world has none: those defaults are process-wide and never saved). success is read back from the slot written. WARNING: It does NOT compile or save the GameMode Blueprint, so a later PIE can still instantiate the OLD class from the already-compiled BlueprintGeneratedClass (three reads can agree on the new class while PIE spawns the engine default). Always follow with compile_blueprint on the GameMode and then save_asset, and verify in PIE by the SPAWNED controller's full class path -- never by re-reading this slot.

params.name: player_controller_class
params.description: Class name or full path (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/Core/BP_MyPlayerController.BP_MyPlayerController_C'); rejected if it is not a child of APlayerController.

commands.returns: { player_controller_class: string, game_mode_class: string, written_to: string ('live_game_mode' | 'game_mode_defaults'), success: bool (the written slot reads back the class; still not a PIE oracle) }

commands.name: set_spline_points
commands.description: Replace every control point of the first spline component on an editor-world actor with the given local-space positions, in order, in one undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level). The new points get the default auto-curve tangents, and closed_loop, when given, also sets whether the last point joins the first. An empty points array leaves the spline with no points. Idempotent: the same points again give the same spline. Read the result with get_spline_points (same local space); give an actor a spline first with add_spline_component; to bend a mesh along a spline use add_spline_mesh_component. An unknown actor, an actor without a spline component, or a points entry that is not 3 numbers is an error and nothing changes.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor, e.g. "Road_Spline"

params.name: points
params.description: [[x, y, z], ...] positions in cm in the spline component's local space (relative to the component, not the world), e.g. [[0,0,0],[500,0,0],[500,500,100]]; an entry that is not 3 numbers is an error and nothing is changed

params.name: closed_loop
params.description: Optional bool: true joins the last point back to the first, false leaves the spline open; omitted keeps the current setting

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, num_points: int, closed_loop: bool, points_set: bool }

commands.name: set_streaming_level_loaded
commands.description: Set the should-be-loaded request flag of a streaming sub-level of the editor world (ULevelStreaming::SetShouldBeLoaded), found by package path, object path or short name (case-insensitive), inside an undo transaction that marks the map dirty without saving. It is a request: this call streams nothing in or out itself, so is_level_loaded may not change. Only a sub-level class that stores the flag honors it, such as ULevelStreamingDynamic (what add_streaming_level creates); an always-loaded sub-level keeps reporting should_be_loaded true, so asking to unload it gives applied false (applied compares ShouldBeLoaded with loaded). Repeating it leaves the same state, though each call still adds an undo step. An unknown level is an error. Visibility: set_streaming_level_visible; current state: get_streaming_levels; detaching a sub-level: remove_streaming_level.

params.name: level_package_path
params.description: Package path of an existing streaming sub-level, e.g. "/Game/Maps/SubLevel"; an object path or the bare level name also matches.

params.name: loaded
params.description: Desired should-be-loaded state; required.

commands.returns: { package_name: string, name: string, streaming_class: string, should_be_loaded: bool, should_be_visible: bool, is_level_loaded: bool, is_level_visible: bool, requested_loaded: bool, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_streaming_level_visible
commands.description: Set the game-time should-be-visible request flag (ULevelStreaming bShouldBeVisible) of a streaming sub-level of the editor world, found by package path or short name, inside an undo transaction. It is a request, not an immediate change, and the editor viewport follows the level's separate editor-visibility flag, so is_level_visible may not change. Marks the map dirty without saving; an unknown level is an error. applied compares the flag with visible. Loading: set_streaming_level_loaded; current state: get_streaming_levels; adding a sub-level: add_streaming_level.

params.name: level_package_path
params.description: Package path of an existing streaming sub-level.

params.name: visible
params.description: Desired should-be-visible state.

commands.returns: { package_name: string, name: string, streaming_class: string, should_be_loaded: bool, should_be_visible: bool, is_level_loaded: bool, is_level_visible: bool, requested_visible: bool, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_view_target
commands.description: Point the active PIE session's PlayerController camera at an actor (APlayerController::SetViewTargetWithBlend). blend_time=0 cuts instantly; >0 blends linearly. PIE-gated: clean error if no PIE session. Frames captures without spawning a camera by hand.

params.name: target_actor_name
params.description: Required. Name/label of the actor to view through (its camera/eyes) in the PIE world.

params.name: blend_time
params.description: Optional number (default 0). Seconds to blend from the current view target.

params.name: pie_client_index
params.description: Optional int (default 0).

commands.returns: { applied: bool, view_target: string, blend_time: float, pie_client_index: int, note?: string }

commands.name: set_world_gravity
commands.description: Set an exact global gravity on the EDITOR world's WorldSettings, or one from a named preset (Earth -980, Moon -163, Mars -371, Zero, Low -490, High -1960, Enabled -980, Disabled 0): writes GlobalGravityZ and the "Override World Gravity" flag, then RE-READS GetGravityZ() into the reply so gravity_z is a measurement rather than an echo, next to the previous values and a census of the world's physics components with an impact rating. Earth is about -980 with the default centimetre unit. Undoable (wrapped in a transaction) but it dirties the MAP -- save_level to keep it, and check the .umap is not read-only or the save writes nothing. Read it back with get_world_settings.

params.name: gravity_z
params.description: Custom gravity along Z in cm/s^2 (negative = downward; Earth is about -980). Required unless preset is given; sending both is refused.

params.name: preset
params.description: Optional preset NAME instead of gravity_z, in any capitalisation: 'Earth' (-980), 'Moon' (-163), 'Mars' (-371), 'Zero' (0), 'Low' (-490), 'High' (-1960), 'Enabled' (-980), 'Disabled' (an override of 0). An unknown name is refused and nothing is written.

params.name: enable_override
params.description: Optional bool (default true). True makes the world use the gravity; false disables the override so the project default applies again.

commands.returns: { applied_gravity_z: number (what landed in GlobalGravityZ), enable_override: bool, gravity_z: number (re-read GetGravityZ, the effective value), previous_gravity_z: number (effective gravity before the write), previous_override: bool (Override World Gravity before the write), preset?: string (echo), world_name: string, world_physics_component_count: int (actors with a primitive component), world_simulate_physics_component_count: int, world_dynamic_physics_component_count: int (Movable), gravity_impact: number, gravity_impact_rating: string, gravity_recommendations: [string], success: bool (hardcoded) }

commands.name: smooth_landscape_in_box
commands.description: Soften terrain: run a 3x3 box blur over the heightmap inside a world-space box, 1 to 5 iterations. The finisher for the other two sculpt tools -- flatten_landscape_in_box and set_landscape_height_in_box leave a hard rim, and a couple of iterations here blends it. It only averages what is there; it cannot add relief.

params.name: landscape_actor_name
params.description: Optional landscape actor name, defaults to first found

params.name: iterations
params.description: Number of smoothing iterations 1 to 5

params.name: box_min
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world-space box minimum

params.name: box_max
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world-space box maximum

params.name: center
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] box center (alternative to box_min/box_max)

params.name: extent
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] box half-extents (alternative to box_min/box_max)

commands.returns: { landscape_actor_name: string, iterations: int, applied: bool, vertices_smoothed: int, region_width: int, region_height: int, region: [int] }

commands.name: spawn_level_streaming_volume
commands.description: Spawn an ALevelStreamingVolume in the editor world with a real box brush (half-extent extent) and bind it to an existing streaming sub-level, setting its usage, editor_pre_vis_only and disabled flags, in one undo step. Over spawn_box_volume(volume_class='LevelStreamingVolume') it adds the binding: the volume is appended to the sub-level's EditorStreamingVolumes, which no other tool writes. Each call spawns a NEW volume; an extent axis of 0 or less becomes 100; an unknown usage or sub-level is an error before anything spawns. Not saved (save_level). WARNING: Treat every call as an operation that CAN KILL THE EDITOR: any UWorld/UPackage handle left in an execute_python global keeps the PIE world rooted and the engine aborts with "Object ... from PIE level still referenced" -- purge the __main__ namespace and gc.collect() BEFORE calling. commands.name: audit_class_purity
commands.description: Project-wide "fork purity" audit of INHERITANCE lineage (complements audit_fork_refs, which audits a fork's INTERNAL refs). Walks every Blueprint UClass under class_root, ascends each parent chain to the point where it leaves class_root, and flags any project class whose chain crosses DIRECTLY into an upstream base library (base_libraries, e.g. /Game/VendorPack) WITHOUT going through a declared thin fork -- a class carrying the fork-origin metadata tag (project setting Fork Origin Tag) that fork_class_chain writes. Catches a new asset that inherits straight from a vendored library instead of via a project fork. Read-only: classes are loaded to resolve the chain (like audit_replication) but never saved. Returns a summary plus the full per-class classification and the actionable violation list inline. NOTE: matches exact UBlueprint assets (as audit_replication/audit_fork_refs do); Widget/Anim blueprints are out of scope for v1. A legit fork created without the fork-origin tag reports as a violation -- back-fill it with set_asset_metadata_tag. The tag is also CHECKED FOR TRUTH, not just for presence: the class it names must really be in the fork point's ancestor chain (the full chain, so declaring a grandparent is fine). A class that declares a fork origin it does not actually descend from -- a copy-sibling rather than a child, or a stale tag left behind by a re-parent -- reports verdict fork_origin_mismatch, whatever its boundary looks like; that also catches copies parented straight to a native class, which the boundary check alone would wave through as native_rooted.

params.name: class_root
params.description: Own content tree to audit. Defaults to the project setting Project Content Root ("/Game" unless configured).

params.name: base_libraries
params.description: Array of upstream roots a project class must not inherit from directly. Defaults to the project's Read Only Content Roots.

params.name: recursive
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Recurse into subfolders.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Cap on classes processed (clamped 1..100000). Defaults to 5000.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Max parent-chain steps to ascend within class_root (clamped 1..256). Defaults to 32.

commands.returns: { class_root: string, base_libraries: [string], summary: { class_count: int, pure_fork_count: int, native_rooted_count: int, other_parent_count: int, violation_count: int (missing_fork_tag + fork_origin_mismatch; == violations.length), missing_fork_tag_count: int, fork_origin_mismatch_count: int, distinct_impure_fork_points: int }, classes: [{ class, package, immediate_parent, fork_point, boundary_parent, boundary_kind, boundary_library, is_declared_fork, fork_origin, fork_origin_in_chain: bool, fork_origin_matched_ancestor: string, fork_origin_exists: bool, verdict: "pure_fork"|"native_rooted"|"other_parent"|"violation"|"fork_origin_mismatch" }], violations: [{ class, kind: "missing_fork_tag"|"fork_origin_mismatch", fork_point, boundary_parent, boundary_library, declared_fork_origin?, actual_immediate_parent?, fork_origin_exists?, actual_ancestor_chain?: [string], detail? }], message: string }

commands.name: audit_fork_refs
commands.description: Audit a fork subtree for references that still point at the SOURCE tree it was copied from (duplicate_asset / duplicate_directory by script do NOT remap internal refs, so a copy keeps pointing at the original -- e.g. a MaterialInstance Parent still under /Game/VendorPack). Reports, per fork asset, the source dependencies (authoritative, from the AssetRegistry) and, best-effort, the exact PROPERTY holding each source object ref. With fix=true it FArchiveReplaceObjectRefs each source object to a same-named counterpart found inside the fork and saves the asset.

params.name: fork_root
params.description: Fork content path to audit, e.g. '/Game/MyGame/Environment/AutoLandscape'.

params.name: source_root
params.description: Origin tree the refs should not point at (optional; defaults to the project's Read Only Content Root when exactly one is configured).

params.name: include_properties
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Load each offending asset and report which property holds each source ref (best-effort; the dependency list is authoritative).

params.name: fix
params.description: Optional bool (default false). Remap source object refs to a same-named fork counterpart via FArchiveReplaceObjectRef and save the asset.

params.name: max_assets
params.description: Max fork assets to scan (optional, default 2000; clamped 1..20000).

params.name: dependency_type
params.description: Optional string, one of "hard"|"soft"|"all" (case-insensitive, default "all"). Scopes the per-asset dependency scan: "hard" surfaces only load-bearing refs into source_root (e.g. a MaterialInstance Parent, a hard object property) -- the correctness-critical case this audit exists for; "soft" surfaces only soft/lazy refs (TSoftObjectPtr, FSoftObjectPath); "all" (default) leaves the scan unscoped.

commands.returns: { fork_root: string, source_root: string, fix: bool, dependency_type: string, assets_scanned: int, offending_count: int, total_source_dependencies: int, offenders: [{asset, package, source_dependencies:[string], properties:[{property, ref}], remapped:int}], fixed_assets: int, refs_remapped: int, unresolved_counterparts: [string], message: string }

commands.name: delete_asset
commands.description: Force-delete one asset with no confirmation or undo: references to it are nulled, the object is purged and its .uasset/.umap file removed from disk. Check get_asset_referencers first. Succeeds only when the file is gone from disk and the object from memory: a file left behind (read-only, or held open by another process) fails the call with file_still_exists true, and the asset comes back when the editor restarts. With expected_class it is a typed delete: an asset of any other class is refused and nothing is deleted, and a path with no asset is a no-op success.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset to delete, as an object path ("/Game/Props/SM_Box.SM_Box") or a bare package path ("/Game/Props/SM_Box")

params.name: expected_class
params.description: Optional class the asset must be, or a list of classes it may be any one of, as short names ("AnimSequence") or /Script/ paths ("/Script/Engine.StaticMesh"). A Blueprint asset also passes when its generated class derives from one ("Subsystem" accepts a subsystem Blueprint). Another class is refused with success false, deleted false, expected_class_matched false, its asset_class (and generated_class_name for a Blueprint) and a note, and nothing is deleted. With it, a path that names no asset is a no-op: success, deleted false, already_existed false. A name that resolves to no class is an error.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, object_path: string, asset_class: string (class path), asset_class_name: string (short class name of the asset), generated_class_name?: string, expected_class_matched?: bool, package_name: string, original_file_size_bytes: number, original_file_size_mb: number, delete_success: bool, delete_message: string, asset_verified_deleted: bool, file_still_exists: bool, deleted: bool, already_existed: bool, note?: string, deletion_timestamp: string? }

commands.name: duplicate_asset
commands.description: Duplicates an asset to a new name, in the same directory or in destination_path, then PERSISTS the copy to disk immediately (unless Play-In-Editor is active -- see the "saved"/"save_error" note on the save step below; a duplicate is very often used AS a safety net before a risky edit, so leaving it memory-only defeats the point). A target name already taken, in memory or on disk, is refused with nothing touched, unless if_exists='return' hands back an existing asset of the source's class with created=false; a destination outside the project's writable content (engine content, a read-only root, no mounted root) is refused, and so is a source that is not of expected_class when one is given. By default (remap_internal_refs absent/false) this is otherwise a plain copy: like EditorAssetLibrary.duplicate_asset, any internal references the copy holds still point at the ORIGINAL (not remapped). Set remap_internal_refs=true to run the SAME 2nd-pass reference remap that duplicate_directory uses (FArchiveReplaceObjectRef mapping original->copy) so the copy's own self-references point at the copy, before that save. repoint_parents_within additionally re-applies a MaterialInstance parent via SetParentEditorOnly when the parent maps into the copied set (for a single asset this only fires if the copy's parent is the original itself).

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full asset path to duplicate (e.g. /Game/Assets/MyAsset); engine content such as /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube can be copied into the project with destination_path

params.name: new_asset_name
params.description: Name for the duplicated asset

params.name: destination_path
params.description: Optional folder for the copy, a long package path (/Game/MyMeshes, a project plugin mount) or a folder relative to /Game; default the source asset's own folder

params.name: if_exists
params.description: Optional "error" (default: a taken target name is refused) or "return" (an asset of the source's class already at the target is returned untouched with created=false; one of another class is still refused)

params.name: expected_class
params.description: Optional class the SOURCE asset must be, or a list of classes it may be any one of, short names ("SkeletalMesh") or /Script/ paths; a Blueprint also passes when its generated class derives from one. Any other source is refused and nothing is duplicated; a name that resolves to no class is an error.

params.name: remap_internal_refs
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When true, remap the copy's internal refs (original->copy) before the save; adds { new_path, refs_remapped } to the result.

params.name: repoint_parents_within
params.description: Optional bool (default false). When true (and remap_internal_refs true), also re-apply MaterialInstanceConstant parents that map into the copied set via SetParentEditorOnly.

commands.returns: { original_asset_path: string, new_asset_name: string, new_asset_path: string, destination_path: string, created: bool, duplication_success: bool, duplication_message: string, new_asset_class: string, new_package_name: string, asset_verified: bool, new_file_size_bytes: number?, new_file_size_mb: number?, original_asset_class: string, original_package_name: string, new_path: string?, refs_remapped: int?, saved: bool?, save_error: string? }

commands.name: duplicate_directory
commands.description: Recursively copy a content folder to a new path, REMAPPING references among the copied assets so the new subtree points at its own copies (true graph isolation) while references to assets OUTSIDE the set stay shared with the originals (the "copy what you modify, share the rest" policy). Unlike EditorAssetLibrary.DuplicateDirectory / duplicate_asset (which copy without remapping, so copies keep pointing at the originals), this duplicates every asset then runs a second reference-replacement pass with the full old->new map, and saves the copies. Intended for material/instance/texture/data-asset libraries; Blueprints may need a recompile and maps (UWorld) are not handled specially.
