params.description: Optional array of content roots that must never be written (checked on source AND destination). Absent => the project's Read Only Content Roots. An EXPLICIT [] disables the guard. (Read through mcp_common::ParseReadonlyRoots, so the type hint is what puts it in the catalog.)

params.name: check_cdo_references
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Scan native CDOs for a hard reference to the asset and refuse instead of letting the engine open a modal.

commands.returns: { original_asset_path: string, new_folder_path: string, new_asset_path: string, move_success: bool, move_message: string, new_asset_class: string, new_package_name: string, asset_verified: bool, new_file_size_bytes: number?, new_file_size_mb: number?, original_file_exists: bool?, original_asset_class: string, original_package_name: string, new_object_resolves: bool?, new_file_on_disk: bool?, new_file_path: string?, redirector_left: bool?, verification: object?, verification_checks: [object]?, would_block_on_modal: bool?, cdo_referencing_class: string?, cdo_soft_reference_check: string? }

commands.name: remove_primary_asset_rule
commands.description: Remove every PrimaryAssetTypesToScan entry of one type from the Asset Manager project settings and write DefaultGame.ini; an unknown type is an error. Returns removed_count, type_count_after and saved. The running Asset Manager is not refreshed, so its scanned data for the type remains.

params.name: primary_asset_type
params.description: Name of the primary asset type to remove, e.g. "Item".

commands.returns: { primary_asset_type, removed_count, type_count_after, saved }

commands.name: rename_asset
commands.description: Renames an asset to a new name in its current directory. GUARDED (both guards are shared with move_asset, and both come from the AssetRenameManager source -- see the comment block on AnyNativeCdoHardReferences): (1) refuses to touch anything under a read-only root (readonly_roots, default: the project's Read Only Content Roots -- the upstream tree is never mutated in place); (2) refuses BEFORE calling the engine when a native class' CDO hard-references the asset, because FAssetRenameManager would open an FMessageDialog there and block the game thread (which kills the MCP session). And it does not trust IAssetTools::RenameAssets' return value: the result is READ BACK (new object resolves + new package on disk + redirector left at the original path), because the engine silently drops packages that failed to save unless UE source control is connected (with plain git it never is).

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full asset path to rename

params.name: new_asset_name
params.description: New name for the asset

params.name: readonly_roots
params.description: Optional array of content roots that must never be written. Absent => the project's Read Only Content Roots. An EXPLICIT [] disables the guard. (Read through mcp_common::ParseReadonlyRoots, so the type hint is what puts it in the catalog.)

params.name: check_cdo_references
params.description: Optional bool (default true). Scan native CDOs for a hard reference to the asset and refuse instead of letting the engine open a modal. Set false to skip the scan (faster, but a modal can then hang the editor).

commands.returns: { original_asset_path: string, new_asset_name: string, new_asset_path: string, rename_success: bool, rename_message: string, new_asset_class: string, new_package_name: string, asset_verified: bool, new_file_size_bytes: number?, new_file_size_mb: number?, original_file_exists: bool?, original_asset_class: string, original_package_name: string, new_object_resolves: bool?, new_file_on_disk: bool?, new_file_path: string?, redirector_left: bool?, verification: object?, verification_checks: [object]?, would_block_on_modal: bool?, cdo_referencing_class: string?, cdo_soft_reference_check: string? }

commands.name: run_external_project_script
commands.description: Spawn a SEPARATE headless UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe to run a python script against an EXTERNAL project and capture its stdout. Needed because another project's /Game packages collide with the live project's (they cannot be loaded side by side), so reading data from content outside this project needs an isolated editor. Give it an existing .uproject OR a module_dir (a minimal engine-only .uproject is cloned in place, with any 'disable_plugins' turned off, then deleted); it launches `<uproject> -run=pythonscript -script=<script> -unattended -nullrhi -NoLiveCoding -stdout`, blocks until exit or timeout, and returns stdout. HEAVY: spawns a full editor process (tens of seconds) and BLOCKS the editor for the duration -- run with confirmation. The engine binary is resolved from THIS editor's install (FPaths::EngineDir); no path is assumed.

params.name: script
params.description: Absolute path to the .py file to run (the -script argument).

params.name: uproject
params.description: Path to an existing external .uproject to run against (optional; provide this OR module_dir).

params.name: module_dir
params.description: Directory of a content folder or project whose Content to load; a temporary engine-only .uproject is cloned here and cleaned up (optional; provide this OR uproject).

params.name: disable_plugins
params.description: Optional list of plugin names to disable in the CLONED .uproject (e.g. custom plugins that hang headless startup). Only applies when module_dir is used.

params.name: extra_args
params.description: Optional list of extra command-line tokens appended to the launch.

params.name: timeout_seconds
params.description: Max seconds to wait before terminating the child (optional, default 300; clamped 30..3600).

commands.returns: { exe: string, uproject_used: string, cloned: bool, script: string, params: string, launched: bool, exit_code: int, success: bool, timed_out: bool, duration_seconds: number, stdout: string, stdout_length: int, stdout_file: string, cleaned_up: bool, message: string }

commands.name: scan_primary_assets
commands.description: Synchronously rescan the directories and specific assets of every PrimaryAssetTypesToScan rule (or only primary_asset_type) so the Asset Manager registers their primary assets; rules without paths are skipped. Returns num_assets_found, types_scanned and per-type scanned_types. Run it after add_primary_asset_rule.

params.name: primary_asset_type
params.description: Configured type name to scan alone, e.g. "Item"; omitted or empty scans every rule, and an unknown name scans nothing (types_scanned=0).

commands.returns: { type, num_assets_found, num_paths, scanned, types_scanned, scanned_types }

commands.name: set_primary_asset_cook_rule
commands.description: Set the CookRule of an existing PrimaryAssetTypesToScan rule in the Asset Manager project settings, plus ChunkId and bApplyRecursively when given, then write DefaultGame.ini (no undo); a failed write makes success false. An unknown type (add it with add_primary_asset_rule) or cook_rule is an error before any change. Priority is not touched here; add_primary_asset_rule sets it. Nothing is rescanned. Read the rules back with get_primary_asset_types (primary_asset_type); the reply's cook_rule is the short name of the stored rule.

params.name: primary_asset_type
params.description: Name of the primary asset type (e.g. "Item").

params.name: cook_rule
params.description: One of "Unknown" / "Never" / "Development" / "DevelopmentAlways" / "Always", case-insensitive; "Development" stores ProductionNeverCook, and the EPrimaryAssetCookRule names (e.g. "AlwaysCook", "DevelopmentAlwaysProductionUnknownCook") are accepted too.

params.name: chunk_id
params.description: Optional chunk ID override for the rule

params.name: apply_recursively
params.description: Optional flag to apply the rule recursively

commands.returns: { primary_asset_type, cook_rule, priority, chunk_id, apply_recursively, saved }

commands.name: add_mass_tag_to_entity
commands.description: Add an FMassTag (a tag, not a trait or fragment, despite the name) to a Mass entity of the editor world (not PIE) by archetype migration. Caveat: EVERY entity sharing that archetype gets the tag, not only this one. Returns old_archetype_id, new_archetype_id and changed; inverse: remove_mass_tag_from_entity.

params.name: entity_handle
params.description: Entity handle as "Index:SerialNumber", two integers such as "12:3" (no braces); a no-longer-valid entity is an error

params.name: tag
params.description: Reflected name of an FMassTag struct without the F prefix, as list_mass_tag_types returns it (e.g. "MassOffLODTag"); /Script paths do not resolve

commands.returns: { entity_handle, old_archetype_id, new_archetype_id, tag, changed }

commands.name: add_mass_trait
commands.description: Adds a trait (a concrete UMassEntityTraitBase subclass) to a UMassEntityConfigAsset and saves the config. Idempotent: if the config already holds a trait of exactly that class, itself or through its parent config chain, nothing is added or saved and the reply has added=false, already_existed=true and that trait's trait_path. trait_class takes a reflected name with or without its U prefix, or a /Script path; an unknown or non-trait class is an error, but an abstract one is not refused: the engine creates it behind an ensure and warns it is nulled out on save. Edit it with set_mass_trait_property; remove_mass_trait is the inverse; add_mass_tag_to_entity tags a live entity instead.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Asset path to the UMassEntityConfig

params.name: trait_class
params.description: Trait class name to add (e.g. UMassMovementTrait)

commands.returns: { config_path, trait_class, trait_path, trait_count, added, already_existed, saved }

commands.name: create_mass_entity_config
commands.description: Create a UMassEntityConfigAsset (an empty list of Mass traits) at package_path/config_name and save it; an existing config there is loaded and re-saved instead (created:false). Returns config_path, trait_count and saved. Add traits with add_mass_trait, then link it with set_mass_spawner_entity_types.

params.name: config_name
params.description: Name of the UMassEntityConfig asset

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP)

commands.returns: { config_path, config_name, trait_count, created, saved }

commands.name: create_mass_spawner_actor
commands.description: Spawn an AMassSpawner actor into the editor world at location (zero rotation) and label it; the level is not saved. config_path is only echoed, not linked (config_linked:false): link configs with set_mass_spawner_entity_types. Use a unique label, since the spawner tools take the first match.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label for the new spawner actor

params.name: config_path
params.description: Optional entity config asset path (echoed; not linked)

params.name: location
params.description: Optional spawn location [X, Y, Z] in world units (cm), default the origin; ignored unless it holds exactly 3 numbers

commands.returns: { actor_label, actor_name, config_path, config_linked, note }

commands.name: delete_mass_entity
commands.description: Destroy a single Mass entity by its handle (Index:SerialNumber), or with all=true every Mass entity in the editor world (not a PIE world), archetype by archetype; no undo either way. Give exactly one of entity_handle and all. To despawn what one spawner made use despawn_mass_entities.

params.name: entity_handle
params.description: "{Index}:{SerialNumber}" string returned by spawn/query. Provide this OR all.

params.name: all
params.description: Optional bool, default false: true destroys every entity of the editor world's entity manager instead of one. Provide this OR entity_handle.

commands.returns: { entity_handle?: string, destroyed?: bool, already_destroyed?: bool, all?: bool, destroyed_count?: int, before_count?: int, after_count?: int }

commands.name: despawn_mass_entities
commands.description: Trigger entity despawning on a AMassSpawner (DoDespawning from the FTSTicker path, outside Mass processing); inverse of spawn_mass_entities. Reports the global Mass entity-count delta; no-op (was_empty) when this spawner spawned nothing.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the AMassSpawner actor

commands.returns: { actor_label, entity_count_before, entity_count_after, despawned, was_empty, note }

commands.name: fire_mass_signal
commands.description: Raise a named Mass signal through the UMassSignalSubsystem of the editor world (not a PIE world) for one entity, or for every live entity when entity_handle is left out; the signal processors subscribed to that name react the next time Mass processing runs in that world, which is the only side effect (nothing is saved and there is no undo step). Use it to trigger signal-driven logic (for example StateTree re-evaluation) without waiting for gameplay. The signal name is NOT validated: a name no processor listens to is accepted and does nothing, and dispatched_count still counts the entities signalled. An entity_handle that does not parse or names no live entity (check it with get_mass_entity_info) is an error and nothing is signalled; so is a world without the Mass signal or entity subsystem. Count the live entities with list_mass_archetypes or get_mass_entity_count.

params.name: signal
params.description: Signal name, as the receiving processors subscribe to it, e.g. "StateTreeActivate" (case-insensitive FName); any name is accepted.

params.name: entity_handle
params.description: Optional handle "Index:SerialNumber" of one live entity, e.g. "12:3" (Index above 0, SerialNumber not 0). Leave it out to signal every live entity of the editor world.

commands.returns: { signal, dispatched_count: int, broadcast: bool }

commands.name: get_mass_config_parent
commands.description: Read the parent config path of a UMassEntityConfigAsset (inverse of set_mass_config_parent).

params.name: config_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMassEntityConfigAsset

commands.returns: { config_path, parent_config_path, has_parent, config_class }

commands.name: get_mass_entity_count
commands.description: Count entities matching a fragment/tag requirement. Requires "fragment" (UScriptStruct path or name) and optional "presence" ("All"|"Any"|"None" — default "All"). For tag-only queries use "tag" (UScriptStruct path).

params.name: fragment
params.description: Script struct path or name (e.g. "/Script/MassMovement.MassMovementFragment" or "FMassMovementFragment").

params.name: tag
params.description: Optional. Same format as fragment. Use to require an FMassTag marker.

params.name: presence
params.description: "All" (default), "Any", or "None".

commands.returns: { matching_count: int, fragment, tag, presence }

commands.name: get_mass_entity_info
commands.description: Inspect one Mass entity of the editor world (not PIE) by handle, read-only: valid, built, archetype_id and the fragment types of its archetype. A destroyed or unknown handle returns valid:false rather than an error; a malformed handle is an error.

params.name: entity_handle
params.description: Entity handle as "Index:SerialNumber", two integers such as "12:3" (no braces)

commands.returns: { entity_handle, valid, built, archetype_id, fragment_count, fragment_types: [string] }

commands.name: get_mass_spawner_info
commands.description: Read an AMassSpawner actor of the editor world, found by actor label (first match), read-only. Returns actor_name, count (the spawn count set_mass_spawner_count writes) and entity_types [{entity_config, proportion}] (what set_mass_spawner_entity_types writes) with entity_type_count; the entities it spawned are counted by list_mass_archetypes instead.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the AMassSpawner actor

commands.returns: { actor_label, actor_name, count, entity_type_count, entity_types: [{ entity_config, proportion }] }

commands.name: get_mass_trait_property
commands.description: Read a property (name or dotted path) of a trait on a Mass entity config, picked by trait_class, as ExportText plus its C++ type. Use it because a trait is an instanced object inside the config that get_properties cannot address by class. Write: set_mass_trait_property.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Asset path to the UMassEntityConfigAsset

params.name: trait_class
params.description: Trait class name; the trait must be on the config

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property name or dotted path

commands.returns: { config_path, trait_class, property_name, value, type }

commands.name: list_mass_archetypes
commands.description: Census the Mass entities of the editor world (not a PIE world), read-only: every archetype with its live-entity and fragment counts. Returns archetype_count, total_entities (the sum over the archetypes), total (the entity manager's own count) and archetypes [{archetype_id, entity_count, fragment_count}]; get_mass_entity_info names the fragments of one entity, get_mass_entity_count counts by fragment or tag.
commands.returns: { archetype_count: int, total_entities: int, total: int, archetypes: [{ archetype_id: string, entity_count: int, fragment_count: int }] }

commands.name: list_mass_tag_types
commands.description: Lists the Mass tag types loaded in this editor: every struct derived from FMassTag, the zero-size markers an entity carries or not (e.g. MassOffLODTag), each with its reflected name and path, in no particular order. Abstract tag structs are left out unless include_abstract is true; nothing else is filtered. Read-only reflection: changes nothing. The name is what add_mass_tag_to_entity and remove_mass_tag_from_entity take as tag. Tags are not traits: the traits an entity config holds are listed with list_mass_traits and added with add_mass_trait; live entities and their archetypes come from list_mass_archetypes and get_mass_entity_info.

params.name: include_abstract
params.description: Optional bool, default false; true also lists tag structs marked Abstract (bases that are not meant to be set on entities).

commands.returns: { count, traits: [{ name, path }] } -- traits holds the tag types (name without the F prefix, e.g. "MassOffLODTag"; path is the /Script path)

commands.name: list_mass_traits
commands.description: List the traits a UMassEntityConfigAsset holds itself (not those inherited from its parent config), read-only, in config order. Returns config_path, trait_count and traits [{class, name}]; edit them with add_mass_trait, remove_mass_trait and set_mass_trait_property.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Asset path to the UMassEntityConfig

commands.returns: { class, name, config_path, trait_count, traits }

commands.name: remove_mass_tag_from_entity
commands.description: Remove an FMassTag from a Mass entity of the editor world (not PIE) by archetype migration; inverse of add_mass_tag_to_entity. Caveat: the tag is removed from EVERY entity sharing that archetype, not only this one. Returns old_archetype_id, new_archetype_id and changed (false when nothing moved).

params.name: entity_handle
params.description: Entity handle as "Index:SerialNumber", two integers such as "12:3" (no braces); a no-longer-valid entity is an error

params.name: tag
params.description: Reflected name of the FMassTag struct to remove, without the F prefix, as list_mass_tag_types returns it (e.g. "MassOffLODTag"); /Script paths do not resolve

commands.returns: { entity_handle, old_archetype_id, new_archetype_id, tag, changed }

commands.name: remove_mass_trait
commands.description: Remove one trait from the trait list of a Mass entity config asset (UMassEntityConfigAsset), picked by index or by class, then save the asset; there is no undo step. Inverse of add_mass_trait. It only reaches traits the config holds itself, as list_mass_traits shows them: a trait inherited from the parent config (set_mass_config_parent) stays. Not idempotent: once the trait is gone, a repeat call is an error (no matching class, or index out of range), and so are both or neither selector, a config that does not load and an unknown or non-trait class; nothing changes then. Later traits shift down one index. A failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the removal only in memory. To untag one live entity instead use remove_mass_tag_from_entity.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Asset path of the Mass entity config, e.g. "/Game/Mass/DA_CrowdAgent", as create_mass_entity_config returns it (config_path).

params.name: trait_index
params.description: 0-based position in the config's own trait list, as list_mass_traits reports it (traits[] order); give this or trait_class, not both.

params.name: trait_class
params.description: Trait class name, with or without its U prefix, or a /Script path, e.g. "MassMovementTrait"; removes the first own trait whose class is that class or a subclass of it. Give this or trait_index, not both.

commands.returns: { config_path, removed, removed_trait_class, removed_index, trait_count, saved }

commands.name: set_mass_config_parent
commands.description: Set the parent config of a Mass entity config asset (UMassEntityConfigAsset), so the child inherits every trait of the parent chain on top of its own, replacing any parent it had, then save the child; there is no undo step. Use it to share a base trait set between configs instead of repeating add_mass_trait on each. Read it back with get_mass_config_parent; the child's own traits stay as list_mass_traits shows them. A repeat call with the same parent sets and saves again (set stays true). There is no way to clear the parent here. A config or parent that does not load, or a config given as its own parent, is an error and nothing changes; longer cycles (A under B under A) are not checked. A failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the change only in memory.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Asset path of the child config to change, e.g. "/Game/Mass/DA_Soldier", as create_mass_entity_config returns it (config_path).

params.name: parent_config_path
params.description: Asset path of the config to inherit from, e.g. "/Game/Mass/DA_BaseAgent"; must be a different UMassEntityConfigAsset.

commands.returns: { config_path, parent_config_path, parent, set, saved }

commands.name: set_mass_spawner_count
commands.description: Set how many entities an AMassSpawner actor in the editor world spawns (its protected Count property, written by reflection); spawn_mass_entities spawns this count, scaled by the spawner's SpawningCountScale and the scalability spawn density. No undo step, and the level is neither marked dirty nor saved (save_level). Use it before spawn_mass_entities; set the types with set_mass_spawner_entity_types; read the current count with get_mass_spawner_info. Idempotent: the same count again gives the same result. set is true when the count read back equals the requested one. A missing actor_label or count, or no spawner with that label, is an error and nothing changes; the count is not range-checked.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the AMassSpawner actor, e.g. "CrowdSpawner"; matched case-insensitively, first match in the editor world (not PIE).

params.name: count
params.description: Number of entities to spawn, an integer such as 100 (a fraction is truncated).

commands.returns: { actor_label, count, set }

commands.name: set_mass_spawner_entity_types
commands.description: Replace the entity types of an AMassSpawner actor in the editor world (its protected EntityTypes list, written by reflection) with the given Mass entity configs, each at proportion 1.0. It replaces, never appends: the old list is cleared first, and an empty array leaves the spawner with no types. Paths that do not load as a UMassEntityConfigAsset are skipped silently, so compare linked with the number you passed. No undo step, and the level is neither marked dirty nor saved (save_level). Place the spawner first with spawn_actor (type "MassSpawner"); set how many it spawns with set_mass_spawner_count; read back with get_mass_spawner_info; spawn with spawn_mass_entities. A missing actor_label or config_paths, or no spawner with that label, is an error and nothing changes. Idempotent: the same list gives the same result.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the AMassSpawner actor, e.g. "CrowdSpawner"; matched case-insensitively, first match in the editor world (not PIE).

params.name: config_paths
params.description: Array of Mass entity config asset paths, e.g. ["/Game/Mass/DA_CrowdAgent"], as create_mass_entity_config returns them (config_path); [] clears the list.

commands.returns: { actor_label, entity_type_count, linked, set }

commands.name: set_mass_trait_property
commands.description: Set one property (name or dotted struct path) of a trait on a Mass entity config asset from import text, as one undo step, and save it. set_properties needs the trait's object path; this finds it by trait_class (add it: add_mass_trait). The trait gets PostEditChange as after a Details-panel edit; there is no edit gate, and a value that does not import is refused with nothing changed. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Read: get_mass_trait_property.

params.name: config_path
params.description: Asset path to the UMassEntityConfigAsset

params.name: trait_class
params.description: Trait class name; the trait must already be on the config (e.g. MassVelocityRandomizerTrait)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property name or dotted path (e.g. MaxSpeed, or Movement.HighResSpeed)

params.name: value
params.description: String value parsed by FProperty::ImportText_Direct

commands.returns: { config_path, trait_class, property_name, value, set, saved, save_error? }

commands.name: spawn_mass_entities
commands.description: Run DoSpawning on an editor-world AMassSpawner found by actor_label and report the global Mass entity-count delta -- it spawns entities, not an actor (spawn_actor places the spawner). All configured types spawn at the spawner's own count (set_mass_spawner_count); a count that differs from it is an error and nothing is spawned. spawned can be 0. Inverse: despawn_mass_entities.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the AMassSpawner actor

params.name: count
params.description: Optional; must equal the spawner's own count (set_mass_spawner_count), which is what DoSpawning spawns. Any other value is an error and nothing is spawned.

commands.returns: { actor_label, entity_count_before, entity_count_after, spawned, spawner_count, note }

commands.name: add_collection_parameter
commands.description: Add a scalar or vector (RGBA color) parameter with a new GUID to a Material Parameter Collection asset and save it; a new parameter changes the collection layout, so the engine recompiles the materials that use the collection. An existing parameter of that name and kind only gets its default overwritten (already_existed=true). The kind is param_type, or inferred from default_value: an [r, g, b, a] array means a vector, anything else a scalar. Returns the count before and after for that kind, the default and the id. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the change kept in memory. Change a default later with set_collection_parameter_default; read back with get_collection_info.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the MPC asset

params.name: param_name
params.description: Name of the new parameter

params.name: param_type
params.description: Optional "scalar" or "vector"; default inferred from default_value (an array -> vector, else scalar). Any other value is an error

params.name: default_value
params.description: Scalar: default float value, default 0. Vector: [r, g, b, a] floats, default [0, 0, 0, 1]; a shorter array keeps 0 for missing color channels and 1 for alpha. An existing parameter of that name gets this value too, even when it is omitted

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, param_name: string, param_type: string, param_added: bool, already_existed: bool, scalar_count_before?: int, scalar_count?: int, default_value?: number (scalar), vector_count_before?: int, vector_count?: int, default?: {r,g,b,a}, default_rgba?: [number] (vector), id: string, saved: bool }

commands.name: add_material_attribute_layers_node
commands.description: Adds a new MaterialAttributeLayers expression to a UMaterial asset, turns on bUseMaterialAttributes (the separate pins such as Base Color stop driving the material), wires the node into MaterialAttributes, recompiles and saves. Not idempotent: each call adds another node. Fails when the save fails; returns connected_material_attributes and num_expressions. Unwire: disconnect_to_material_output output_property=MaterialAttributes.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Object path to the UMaterial, e.g. /Game/MyGame/M_Example

params.name: node_name
params.description: Label echoed back in the reply only; it does not name or find any node in the graph

commands.returns: { material_path: string, expression_added: bool, expression_class: string, connected_material_attributes: bool, use_material_attributes: bool, num_expressions: int, recompiled: bool, saved: bool, node_name: string, save_error: string }

commands.name: add_material_function_call
commands.description: Insert a call to a UMaterialFunction into a UMaterial graph: a MaterialFunctionCall node bound to the function, so the function's inputs and outputs become the node's pins. Refused, with the node removed again, when the function cannot be called from this material.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UMaterial (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/M_Example')

params.name: function_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UMaterialFunction to call (e.g. '/Game/Functions/MF_Foo.MF_Foo')

params.name: node_name
params.description: Optional name for the new node; a name another object of the material already has gets a unique variant

commands.name: add_material_function_output
commands.description: Add a FunctionOutput node, the output pin named output_name, to a UMaterialFunction asset loaded from function_path, then recompile the function (loaded materials that use it recompile too) and mark it dirty, without saving and without an undo transaction. Each call adds another node, so it is not idempotent, and output_name is stored as given: a name another output already has is not made unique. The new output starts unwired, placed right of the graph below the existing outputs, and node_id is its handle; added confirms the output count rose by one. A function that does not load is an error. Wire it with connect_material_function_pins, edit it with set_material_function_output_props, and its inverse is delete_material_function_output; inputs are add_material_function_input; list pins with get_material_function_info; persist with save_asset.

commands.returns: { function_path: string, output_name: string, node_id: string, num_outputs: number, added: bool }

commands.name: compile_material

GATED by Substrate: when Substrate is disabled this returns a clear error ("Substrate disabled: cannot connect slab to Front Material...") because the Front Material input is only meaningful with Substrate enabled. When enabled, connects via ConnectMaterialProperty(MP_FrontMaterial) and recompiles. Unwire: disconnect_to_material_output output_property=FrontMaterial.

params.description: Content path to the UMaterial holding the slab node

commands.description: Wire one output of an expression node into a main input of a UMaterial asset (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal...). The edit stays in memory: no recompile, no dirty flag, no save, so follow with compile_material and save_asset. Node-to-node wiring is connect_material_expressions.

commands.name: copy_material_instance_dynamic_parameters
commands.description: Copy parameter values from a source material or material instance into a transient Material Instance Dynamic (MID), found by object path or name as create_material_instance_dynamic returns it. The MID's current overrides are cleared first, then every non-static parameter the MID exposes takes the source's value where the source has that parameter; static switches are not copied. Takes effect at once, nothing saved, no undo. Refused, with the MID untouched, when the source is the MID itself or has none of its parameters. copied is measured: every copyable parameter read back on the MID with the source's value. For saved Material Instance Constant assets use copy_material_instance_parameters.

params.name: mid_object_path
params.description: Object path of the MID

params.name: source_material_path
params.description: Content path to the source material to copy from

commands.returns: { mid_object_path, source_material_path, source_material_name, params_in_source, params_copied, params_not_in_source, mismatched_params, copied }

commands.name: copy_material_instance_parameters
commands.description: Bulk-copy every scalar, vector and texture OVERRIDE from one material instance to another -- the way to clone a calibration onto a sibling instance instead of re-setting parameters one by one. Copies overrides only, so anything the source inherited untouched is not carried, and STATIC SWITCHES are not copied at all (set those with set_material_instance_parameter). Read the copied counts in the reply and verify with get_material_parameters; diff_material_instances shows what still differs.

params.name: source_path
params.description: Content path of the source UMaterialInstanceConstant.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: Content path of the destination UMaterialInstanceConstant.

commands.returns: { source_path: string, destination_path: string, scalars_copied: int, vectors_copied: int, textures_copied: int }

commands.name: create_dynamic_material_on_actor
commands.description: Give one material slot of a mesh component on an editor-world actor its own Material Instance Dynamic (UPrimitiveComponent::CreateDynamicMaterialInstance), which replaces the slot's material with the MID, in one undo step that marks the level dirty; no asset is created or saved. The actor is matched by object name or label (first match), the component is its first StaticMeshComponent, else its first mesh component. Without parent_material_path the MID wraps the slot's current material, and a slot already holding a MID returns that same MID with created false, changing nothing; with it, the slot is first set to that material. Pass mid_object_path to set_material_instance_dynamic_parameter, or to get_material_parameters as material_instance_path; verified confirms the slot holds the MID. A missing actor, mesh component or material, or an out-of-range element_index, is an error. Unowned MID: create_material_instance_dynamic; saved asset: create_material_instance.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name or label of the actor in the editor world; the first actor whose object name or label matches is used

params.name: element_index
params.description: Material slot index on the mesh component (default 0); must be below the component's slot count

params.name: parent_material_path
params.description: Optional source material for the MID (default slot's current material); when given it is assigned to the slot before the MID is made from it

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_label, component_name, element_index, mid_object_path, mid_name, parent_material_path, verified, created, note? }

commands.name: create_material
commands.description: Create a new base material asset (UMaterial) -- the graph-owning master whose parameters and static switches every instance of it inherits. Prefer create_material_instance when you only need a re-skin of something that exists: an instance costs no new shader permutations and leaves the original updatable. After creating, build the graph with create_material_expression + connect_material_expressions, then verify with get_material_stats (compile_errors empty and stats_valid true) -- compile_material only acknowledges, it does not report errors, and a landscape material that fails to compile silently falls back to the default material.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Content FOLDER the material is created in (e.g., '/Game/Materials')

params.name: material_name
params.description: Name of the material asset to create

commands.returns: { material_path: string (object path of the new material, '/Game/Materials/M_X.M_X'), material_name: string, package_path: string, success: bool } -- an existing asset of that name is an error, never overwritten

commands.name: create_material_expression
commands.description: Add ONE node to a material graph -- or to a material function's internal graph -- by expression class path (e.g. /Script/Engine.MaterialExpressionConstant, ...TextureSample, ...ScalarParameter), at a graph position. The building block of headless material authoring: create the nodes, then wire them with connect_material_expressions and connect_to_material_output (inside a function: connect_material_function_pins, then recompile_material_function). The node arrives UNCONNECTED, so nothing renders differently until it is wired -- verify with get_material_graph_info and get_material_stats, not with the success flag. Inverse: delete_material_expression (with material_function_path inside a function).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full path to the material (e.g., '/Game/Materials/MyMaterial.MyMaterial'); a UMaterialFunction path is accepted too and creates the node inside that function

params.name: expression_class_name
params.description: Material expression class name (e.g., '/Script/Engine.MaterialExpressionConstant')

params.name: material_function_path
params.description: Alias of material_path that addresses a UMaterialFunction (or material layer): the node is created inside the function's graph

params.name: node_pos_x
params.description: Optional graph editor X position; defaults to 0

params.name: node_pos_y
params.description: Optional graph editor Y position; defaults to 0

commands.returns: { material_path: string, material_function_path?: string (the function's object path, when the node went into a function), expression_class_name: string, expression_name: string, node_pos_x: int, node_pos_y: int, success: bool }

commands.name: create_material_function
commands.description: Create an empty material function asset named name in package_path -- a plain UMaterialFunction through the editor factory, or with usage MaterialLayer / MaterialLayerBlend a material layer or layer blend function, the way the editor's factories make them -- exposed to the material function library, with the optional description stored as its tooltip, then save it. Idempotent: an existing material function at that path, whatever its class or usage, is returned untouched with already_exists=true, already_existed=true, created=false and saved=false, and nothing is saved (description is ignored then and comes back as the function's own); another asset class there, or an invalid package path, is an error. A failed save (PIE running, read-only file) makes success false with created=true, saved=false and save_error, the function kept in memory. Then add pins with add_material_function_input and add_material_function_output and nodes with create_material_expression (material_function_path); read it back with get_material_graph_info; a variant with overrides: create_material_function_instance; use it in a material: add_material_function_call (a layer or blend: set_material_layer_stack); inverse: delete_asset.

params.name: package_path
params.description: /Game package directory, e.g. '/Game/MyGame'; a trailing slash is ignored

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name for the new material function

params.name: description
params.description: Text stored as the function Description, the tooltip shown wherever the function is used; default empty. Ignored when the function already exists.

params.name: usage
params.description: Optional "Default" (a plain UMaterialFunction, the default), "MaterialLayer" (a UMaterialFunctionMaterialLayer) or "MaterialLayerBlend" (a UMaterialFunctionMaterialLayerBlend), any case. Any other value is an error

commands.returns: { function_path: string, asset_path: string, name: string, package_path: string, class: string, usage: string, description: string, num_inputs: number, num_outputs: number, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, already_exists?: bool }

commands.name: create_material_function_instance
commands.description: Create a UMaterialFunctionInstance asset named instance_name in package_path through the editor factory, parented to the material function or function instance at parent_function_path, then save it. package_path is any long package path, such as /Game/Materials or a plugin's /MyPlugin/Funcs; a relative folder is read under /Game, a missing folder is made, and an unmounted or malformed path is an error. Idempotent: an instance already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true, created=false and saved=false, its own parent in parent_function_path (the requested one is ignored) and nothing saved; another asset class there is an error. A parent that does not load is an error and nothing, not even the folder, is created; a failed save (PIE running, read-only file) makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the new instance kept in memory. Re-parent later: set_material_function_instance_parent; a new base function: create_material_function.

params.name: parent_function_path
params.description: Asset path of the parent UMaterialFunctionInterface

commands.name: create_material_instance
commands.description: Create a material instance (MIC) from a parent material -- the cheap, non-destructive way to re-skin a vendor or engine material: the parent stays untouched and updatable while only your overrides are stored, and no new shader is compiled -- optionally applying a dict of parameter overrides in the same call. Idempotent (already_exists=true when it is already there; parameter_overrides are then not applied and note says so). The parent may be omitted (a parentless instance) and may be given as a bare material NAME instead of a path; resolve an ambiguous name first. Check applied_overrides_count against what you sent and re-read with get_material_parameters: a name the parent does not expose is simply not applied. Tune it later with set_material_instance_parameter, and remember static switches inherit from the parent and are set separately.

params.name: instance_name
params.description: Name of the material instance to create

params.name: instance_path
params.description: Content folder for the material instance (e.g., '/Game/Materials'); defaults to /Game/MCP. The asset is created at <instance_path>/<instance_name>

params.name: package_path
params.description: Alias of instance_path

params.name: name
params.description: Alias of instance_name

commands.name: create_material_instance_dynamic
commands.description: Create a Material Instance Dynamic (MID) of a parent material in the transient package: a runtime-only object that is never saved, belongs to no actor and has no undo step. The plugin keeps a reference to every MID it makes this way, so garbage collection does not free it; no tool releases one, so each lives until the editor closes. Set its parameters with set_material_instance_dynamic_parameter, which takes its mid_object_path, or use create_dynamic_material_on_actor to have a mesh component own a MID it renders. A name another MID holds gets a numbered suffix, so keep mid_name and mid_object_path from the reply; each call creates another MID. A parent that cannot be loaded, or a name held by an object of another class, is an error. Read its values with get_material_parameters (material_instance_path = its mid_object_path); a saved, reusable instance asset: create_material_instance.

params.description: Optional name for the MID (default auto-generated from MID_ and the parent's name)

A failed save makes success false with saved=false. Returns collection_path, scalar_count, vector_count and saved. commands.name: delete_material_expression
commands.description: Delete ONE node from a material graph -- or from a material function's internal graph -- by name. Deliberately one at a time, and that is the safe way to empty a graph: the engine's bulk delete_all_material_expressions can leave half the nodes behind with no error, and a rebuild on top then produces duplicate parameter names that no parameter listing reveals (duplicates collapse by name). Loop this instead, re-reading get_material_graph_info until its expression_count reaches 0. The underlying engine call also returns false while having done the work, so count the nodes rather than trusting the flag. Inside a function (material_function_path, or a function path in material_path) the links into the node are broken, the node leaves the function's expressions and the reply re-reads them (deleted, expression_count); the change stays in memory until recompile_material_function saves it. Inverse of create_material_expression; a node that is not there is an error and nothing changes.

Idempotent: an already-absent node_id returns { deleted:false, already_absent:true } as success, not an error.

params.name: function_path

commands.returns: { function_path: string, node_id: string, deleted: bool, already_absent: bool, num_inputs: number, num_outputs: number }

commands.description: Diff two Material Instance Constants: what side B overrides differ from side A (parent + scalar/vector/texture/static-switch overrides + material layer stack). Answers "what did this fork change vs its parent (or the original)". Read-only; nothing is saved. Editor-only.

Inside a function the change stays in memory until recompile_material_function saves it.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full path to the material (e.g., '/Game/Materials/MyMaterial.MyMaterial'); a UMaterialFunction path is accepted too and disconnects inside that function

params.name: to_expression_name
params.description: Name of the destination material expression whose input is disconnected

params.name: to_input_name

params.name: material_function_path

commands.returns: { material_path: string, material_function_path?: string, to_expression_name: string, to_input_name: string, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, success: bool }

commands.name: disconnect_to_material_output
commands.description: Disconnect a material output property (inverse of connect_to_material_output).  Idempotent: an already-disconnected property returns already_disconnected=true (still success — the output slot always resolves to a valid input, so false is unambiguously "nothing was connected", never an error).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Material asset path.

(same strings as connect_to_material_output), FrontMaterial (the Substrate slab wire connect_substrate_slab_to_material makes) and MaterialAttributes (the wire add_material_attribute_layers_node makes) included

commands.returns: { material: string, output_property: string, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool }

commands.name: duplicate_material_expression
commands.description: Copy one expression node of a UMaterial asset into the same material, optionally renamed, then recompile the material and mark it dirty without saving. The copy keeps the source position and settings (a parameter keeps its name) and its output is unwired. Returns duplicate_node and expression_count.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full asset path of the UMaterial.

params.name: node_id
params.description: Object name of the expression to copy, as listed by get_material_graph_info (nodes[].name).

params.name: new_node_name
params.description: Object name for the copy; when taken, a unique variant is used (read duplicate_node). Default: a name the engine picks.

commands.returns: { material_path: string, source_node: string, duplicate_node: string, duplicate_class: string, expression_count: number }

commands.name: duplicate_material_parameter_collection
commands.description: Copy a Material Parameter Collection asset to package_path/new_name, with every scalar and vector parameter's name, Id and default value, then save the copy; the source is not changed and there is no undo step. Use it to start a variant of an existing collection; for an empty one use create_material_parameter_collection, and for any other asset type duplicate_asset. An asset already at the target path is refused, so a repeat call fails and nothing changes; a source that does not load as a collection, or an invalid target name, is an error too. A failed save makes success false, with saved false, save_error and the copy only in memory. Read the copy with get_collection_info; rename its parameters with rename_collection_parameter.

params.name: source_path
params.description: Collection to copy, as an asset path, e.g. "/Game/MPC/MPC_A", or the object path "/Game/MPC/MPC_A.MPC_A".

params.name: new_name
params.description: Asset name of the copy without folder, e.g. "MPC_B"; must be a valid, non-empty asset name.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target folder, e.g. "/Game/MPC"; default is the folder of source_path when it is an object path with a dot ("/Game/MPC/MPC_A.MPC_A"), else "/Game/MaterialCollections".

commands.returns: { source_path: string, collection_path: string, asset_path: string, name: string, package_path: string, scalar_count: int, vector_count: int, duplicated: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: get_collection_info
commands.description: Read the parameters of a Material Parameter Collection asset: scalar_params (name, default, id, index), vector_params (name, id, default object, default_rgba, index), scalar_count, vector_count and total_count. Read-only. Narrow it to one parameter with param_name and/or one kind with param_type: the lists then hold only the matches, found says whether the name matched, and the counts stay the collection's totals. index is the parameter's position in its scalar or vector array. The live per-world values: get_material_parameter_collection_instance_info.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the MPC asset

params.name: param_name
params.description: Optional: list only the parameter with this name, and report found

params.name: param_type
params.description: Optional "scalar" or "vector": list only that kind. Any other value is an error

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, collection_name: string, collection_class: string, scalar_params: [{name, default, id, index}], vector_params: [{name, id, default, default_rgba, index}], scalar_count: int, vector_count: int, total_count: int, found?: bool (with param_name) }

commands.name: get_material_function_info
commands.description: Describe a material function asset -- a plain function, a material layer, a layer blend or a function instance -- without changing it: its class and usage ("Default", "MaterialLayer" or "MaterialLayerBlend"), is_layer / is_blend, the input and output pin counts it exposes (num_inputs, num_outputs; an instance reports its parent's) and num_expressions, plus, for a UMaterialFunction, its FunctionInput and FunctionOutput nodes: node_id, name, type, description, sort priority and preview value for inputs; name, description and sort priority for outputs (a function instance has no nodes of its own, so its lists are empty). For the whole node graph use get_material_graph_info.

params.name: material_function_path
params.description: Asset path of the material function, layer, layer blend or function instance, e.g. "/Game/Materials/MF_Blend".

params.name: layer_path
params.description: Alias of material_function_path

commands.returns: { material_function_path: string, asset_path: string, class: string, usage: string, is_layer: bool, is_blend: bool, num_inputs: number, num_outputs: number, num_expressions: number, input_count: number, output_count: number, inputs: [{ node_id: string, input_name: string, input_type: string, description: string, sort_priority: number, use_preview_value: bool, preview_value: {x,y,z,w} }], outputs: [{ node_id: string, output_name: string, description: string, sort_priority: number }] }

commands.name: get_material_graph_info
commands.description: Read the expression graph of a UMaterial asset -- or of a UMaterialFunction / material layer's internal graph -- without changing it: every expression node with its object name (the node_id other material tools take), class, class path and description, its inputs by index, and the node-to-node connections flattened into connections[], each with the source output index. Only wiring between expressions is listed -- what feeds the material's main outputs (BaseColor, Normal...) is not -- and node positions and property values are not read. input_name and to_input are each input's name as the node reports it (GetInputName, e.g. A, B, Alpha), and node_count counts the nodes listed. expression_count counts every expression object the asset owns, including orphan_nodes its expression collection does not list (a partial bulk delete or a duplicate leaves them behind, and duplicate parameter names hide there): it is the count to watch when deleting nodes one by one until 0. A material instance or a path that does not load is an error. Shader stats: get_material_stats; wiring: connect_material_expressions, connect_to_material_output, connect_material_function_pins.

params.name: material_path
params.description: UMaterial asset path, e.g. "/Game/Materials/M_Rock" or "/Game/Materials/M_Rock.M_Rock"; a UMaterialFunction path is read as a function graph; a material instance is not accepted

params.name: material_function_path
params.description: Alias of material_path that addresses a UMaterialFunction (or material layer / layer blend)

commands.returns: { material_path?: string (a material), material_name?: string, material_function_path?: string (a function), expression_count: number, orphan_count: number, orphan_nodes: [{ name: string, class: string }], node_count: number, nodes: [{ name: string, class: string, class_path: string, description: string, inputs: [{ index: number, input_name: string, source?: string, source_output_index?: number }], input_count: number }], connection_count: number, connections: [{ from: string, from_output_index: number, to: string, to_input: string }] }

commands.name: get_material_instance_info
commands.description: One-call overview of a material instance (constant, or any other UMaterialInstance): parent material path, name and class, COUNTS of scalar/vector/texture overrides, base property overrides, static switches and static component masks, and the base property overrides themselves -- blend mode, two-sided, shading model and opacity mask clip value, each with its own bOverride_ flag. The flag matters as much as the value: an override that is false means the parent's setting wins whatever value is stored, and a material that looks wrong despite correct parameters is often a blend-mode override. A triage read for parameters -- counts, not values, so it can say "there are 14 static switches here" but never which ones are on: for parameter values use get_material_parameters (parameter_type all includes the static switches). set_material_instance_parent and set_properties write what it reports.

params.name: material_instance_path
params.description: Content path to the material instance (UMaterialInstanceConstant, or any UMaterialInstance).

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, material_instance_class: string, parent_material_path: string, parent_material_name: string, parent_material_class: string, scalar_param_count: int, vector_param_count: int, texture_param_count: int, base_override_count: int, static_switch_count: int, static_component_mask_count: int, override_blend_mode: bool, blend_mode: string, override_two_sided: bool, two_sided: bool, override_shading_model: bool, shading_model: string, override_opacity_mask_clip_value: bool, opacity_mask_clip_value: float, asset_registry_path: string }

commands.name: get_material_instance_parameter_overridden
commands.description: Is this parameter set on the INSTANCE, or just inherited from the parent? Returns the override flag for one named parameter -- the discriminator that a plain value read cannot give you, since an inherited value and a locally-set identical value read the same. Use it to confirm a write actually landed on the child (and, in a read-only vendor material, to prove you edited your instance and not the library asset). Editor-only.

params.name: material_instance_path
params.description: Content path to the UMaterialInstanceConstant.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Name of the parameter to query.

params.name: association
params.description: Optional EMaterialParameterAssociation: "Global" (default), "Layer", or "Blend".

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, parameter_name: string, association: string, overridden: bool }

commands.name: get_material_layer_stack
commands.description: Read a material's layer stack: the layer functions and blend functions it uses, in order, with has_layers telling you whether the material is layered at all. Check this before any set_material_instance_parameter call -- on a non-layered material the layer indices mean nothing, and here is where you learn which index is which surface.

params.name: material_instance_path
params.description: Content path to the material

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, layers: [{name, function_path}], blends: [{name, function_path}], layer_count: int, blend_count: int, has_layers: bool }

commands.name: get_material_parameter_collection_instance_info
commands.description: Read the live per-world values of a Material Parameter Collection (its transient instance on one world) without changing any value: current_value per scalar and current_rgba per vector, each with readback_ok (false when the instance lacks that parameter, the value then being the asset default), plus parent_collection_path and is_valid. The world is the editor world by default, or the Play-in-Editor world world_label selects; the world fields and pie_instance (-1 outside PIE) say which one answered. Use it to check set_material_parameter_collection_instance_value or reset_material_parameter_collection_instance; for the saved defaults use get_collection_info. The engine lookup creates the instance at the defaults when the world has none, so instance_exists is true in practice, and scalar_override_count and vector_override_count are only the parameter counts, not overrides. A collection that does not load, or a world_label no live world matches, is an error.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the collection, e.g. "/Game/MPC/MPC_Global", as get_collection_info takes it.

params.name: world_label
params.description: Which world: empty or "editor" for the editor world (the default), even while Play-in-Editor runs; "pie" (alias "game") for the running PIE world, "server" or "client" for that PIE world, "pie:N" for PIE instance N. any other value names a live world by its object name (the editor world is checked first, so a map name selects it) or by its package name (UEDPIE_N_ and the map name for a PIE world), and a value no world has fails and lists the worlds present

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, world_name: string, world_package: string, world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int, instance_exists: bool, is_valid: bool, parent_collection_path: string, scalar_override_count: int, vector_override_count: int, scalars: [object], vectors: [object] }

commands.name: get_material_parameters
commands.description: What can I tune on this material without recompiling it: EVERY parameter the material or its parent exposes, each with its EFFECTIVE value (the instance's own override, else what it inherits), whether this instance overrides it, its layer association and layer index. This is the contract -- untouched parameters are listed too, with the value they inherit. Works on a base material, a material instance, or a live Material Instance Dynamic found by object path or name. By default it lists scalar, vector and texture parameters; parameter_type static_switch, static_component_mask or all adds the STATIC parameters, the switches and channel masks that decide whether whole shader branches run at all. Narrow it to one parameter with parameter_name (found tells a misspelled name from a value; when exactly one entry matches its value and overridden are also copied to the top level), to one layer slot with association + layer_index, and to the instance's own overrides with overridden_only. orphaned_overrides lists overrides an instance still stores for parameters its parent no longer exposes: they are kept on the asset and apply to nothing.

params.name: material_instance_path
params.description: Content path to the material (a base material or an instance), or the object path or name of a live Material Instance Dynamic (as create_material_instance_dynamic returns it)

params.name: parameter_type
params.description: Optional kind filter: "scalar", "vector", "texture", "static_switch", "static_component_mask", or "all" for every kind. Omitted: scalar, vector and texture. Any other value is an error

params.name: param_type
params.description: Alias of parameter_type

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Optional: list only the parameter(s) with this name (case-insensitive) and report found

params.name: param_name
params.description: Alias of parameter_name

params.name: association
params.description: Optional association filter: "Global", "Layer" or "Blend". Any other value is an error

params.name: layer_index
params.description: Optional layer index filter (a Layer/Blend parameter's slot; Global parameters have -1)

params.name: overridden_only
params.description: Optional bool (default false): list only the parameters this instance overrides itself

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, object_path: string, parent_material: string (parent's object path, "None" for a base material), parent_material_name: string, mid_name?: string (when the target is a Material Instance Dynamic), parameters: [{name, type, association, layer_index, value?, overridden}], parameter_count: int, orphaned_overrides: [{name, type, association, layer_index, value}], orphaned_override_count: int, found?: bool (with parameter_name), value?: number|{r,g,b,a}|string|bool, overridden?: bool }

commands.name: get_material_physical_material
commands.description: Which physical material a material is linked to -- what decides footstep sounds, impact effects, friction and surface type when something hits this surface. Reads the RAW field with no engine-default fallback, so an empty path means "nothing authored here" and the engine default applies at runtime; that distinction is exactly what you want when auditing why a surface sounds wrong. set_material_physical_material writes it.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full path to the material (e.g., '/Game/Materials/MyMaterial.MyMaterial')

commands.returns: { material_path: string, physical_material_path: string, success: bool }

commands.name: get_material_referencers
commands.description: What would I break if I changed this material: every asset that references it, bucketed by kind (static mesh, skeletal mesh, blueprint, level, other) with counts, plus the material's own blend mode and two-sided / masked / translucent / opaque flags. The impact check before editing or deleting a shared material. Note it takes a material NAME, not a path, so an ambiguous name can resolve to the wrong asset -- confirm with resolve_asset_by_name first. Nothing to do with get_material_usage_flag, which is about permitted geometry types.

params.name: material_name
params.description: Name of the material asset

commands.returns: { material_name: string, material_class: string, material_category: string, material_tooltip: string, material_display_name: string, usage: [{package_name, asset_name, asset_class, asset_path, usage_type, usage_category, asset_category, asset_tooltip, asset_display_name}], usage_count: int, static_mesh_usage_count: int, skeletal_mesh_usage_count: int, blueprint_usage_count: int, level_usage_count: int, other_usage_count: int, material_has_referencers: bool, material_is_two_sided: bool, material_is_masked: bool, material_is_translucent: bool, material_is_opaque: bool, blend_mode: string }

commands.name: get_material_stats
commands.description: Read PER-ASSET shader complexity for a material or material instance (instruction counts, sampler/texture-sample counts) -- the numbers the Material Editor's Stats panel shows, unlike get_shader_info (project-wide/global). Read-only: does not Modify()/dirty the asset. Render-adjacent: forces synchronous shader compilation on the FIRST call for a given material (UMaterialEditingLibrary::GetStatistics blocks on FMaterialResource::FinishCompilation); subsequent calls are fast once the shader map is cached. Works for both UMaterial and UMaterialInstance (UMaterialInterface's GetMaterialResource is virtual/overridden on both).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full path to the material or material instance (e.g., '/Game/Materials/MyMaterial.MyMaterial')

commands.returns: { material_path, material_class, num_vertex_shader_instructions, num_pixel_shader_instructions, num_samplers, num_vertex_texture_samples, num_pixel_texture_samples, num_virtual_texture_samples, num_uv_scalars, num_interpolator_scalars, compile_errors: string[], stats_valid: bool }

commands.name: get_material_usage_flag
commands.description: Is this material allowed to be used on that kind of geometry? Reads one EMaterialUsage flag (SkeletalMesh, InstancedStaticMeshes, Niagara, SplineMesh, ...) on a base material. The check to make when a material renders fine on a static mesh and comes out as the default grey checker on a skeletal mesh or an instanced mesh -- a missing usage flag is exactly that symptom. Accepts the name with or without the MATUSAGE_ prefix; set_material_usage_flag enables it (and forces a shader recompile).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full path to the material (e.g., '/Game/Materials/MyMaterial.MyMaterial')

params.name: usage
params.description: Usage flag name, with or without the MATUSAGE_ prefix (e.g., 'SkeletalMesh' or 'MATUSAGE_SkeletalMesh')

commands.returns: { material_path: string, usage: string, enabled: bool, success: bool }

commands.returns: { substrate_enabled: bool, r_substrate_cvar: int, note?: string, detected: bool }

commands.name: recompile_material_function
commands.description: Recompile a material function, layer or function instance (UpdateMaterialFunction): loaded materials using it recompile and dependent function instances are marked dirty but not saved, then the function itself is saved; success requires that save. recompiled is always true, not a shader-error report.

params.name: material_function_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialFunctionInterface (function, layer or function instance), e.g. "/Game/Materials/MF_Blend".

commands.returns: { material_function_path: string, function_class: string, recompiled: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: regenerate_collection_parameter_id
commands.description: Assign a new random FGuid Id to one parameter of a Material Parameter Collection asset and save it; returns new_id. It searches only the array param_type selects (default scalar) and errors when the name is not there.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the MPC asset

params.name: param_name
params.description: Name of the parameter to regenerate the id for

params.name: param_type
params.description: Which array to search: "scalar" or "vector", any case; omitted or anything else means scalar

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, param_name: string, param_type: string, new_id: string, regenerated: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: remove_collection_parameter
commands.description: Remove one parameter from a Material Parameter Collection asset by name and save it, or with all=true clear every parameter of a kind (or both kinds) at once. Errors when param_name is not in the array param_type selects. Reports the scalar and vector counts before and after.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Full /Game path to the MPC asset

params.name: param_name
params.description: Name of the parameter to remove. Required unless all is true, and must be omitted with all=true

params.name: param_type
params.description: Which array: "scalar" or "vector" (default scalar); with all=true also "all" (the default then) for both arrays. Other values: scalar without all, an error with all=true

params.name: all
params.description: Optional bool (default false): clear every parameter of param_type instead of one

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, param_name?: string, param_type: string, removed?: bool, cleared?: bool (all=true), scalar_count_before: int, vector_count_before: int, scalar_count: int, vector_count: int, saved: bool }

commands.name: rename_collection_parameter
commands.description: Rename one scalar or vector parameter of a Material Parameter Collection asset, keeping its Id so the materials that read it keep resolving it, in one undo step, then save the asset. Use it rather than remove_collection_parameter plus add_collection_parameter, which gives the parameter a new Id that those materials do not know; to give it a new Id on purpose use regenerate_collection_parameter_id. A new_name already used in the same array, the parameter's own name included (names compare case-insensitively), is refused, so repeating a rename fails; a param_name that is not in the array param_type selects is an error; nothing changes in either case. A collection that does not load is an error; a failed save makes success false, with saved false, save_error and the rename only in memory. List the names with get_collection_info.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the collection, e.g. "/Game/MPC/MPC_Global" or the object path "/Game/MPC/MPC_Global.MPC_Global".

params.name: param_name
params.description: Current name of the parameter, as get_collection_info lists it (scalar_params[].name or vector_params[].name); case-insensitive.

params.name: new_name
params.description: New parameter name, e.g. "WindStrength"; must not be used by another parameter of the same kind (compared case-insensitively).

params.name: param_type
params.description: Which array to search: "scalar" or "vector", any case; omitted or anything else means scalar

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, param_name: string, new_name: string, param_type: string, renamed: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: reset_material_parameter_collection_instance
commands.description: Reset the Material Parameter Collection Instance (MPCI: the transient per-world values of a collection asset) of one collection on a world to the collection's default values by dropping all its scalar and vector overrides. The world is the editor world by default, or the Play-in-Editor world world_label selects; world_package and world_type say which one was reached. Runtime only: nothing is saved, no undo. A world with no instance for the collection gets a fresh one at the defaults (created=true, already_existed=false), so this is also how to give a world its instance; is_valid says whether the instance is bound to a valid collection. scalars_reset_to_default and vectors_reset_to_default count parameters now reading their default. For a Material Instance Constant asset use set_material_instance_parameter_override with all=true and override=false.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Full /Game path of the parent MPC

params.name: world_label
params.description: Which world: empty or "editor" for the editor world (the default), even while Play-in-Editor runs; "pie" (alias "game") for the running PIE world, "server" or "client" for that PIE world, "pie:N" for PIE instance N. any other value names a live world by its object name (the editor world is checked first, so a map name selects it) or by its package name (UEDPIE_N_ and the map name for a PIE world), and a value no world has fails and lists the worlds present

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, world_name: string, world_package: string, world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int, scalar_count: int, vector_count: int, scalars_reset_to_default: int, vectors_reset_to_default: int, cleared: bool, is_valid: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }

commands.name: set_collection_parameter_default
commands.description: Change the default value stored in a Material Parameter Collection asset for one existing parameter, in one undo step, then save the asset; every material reading the collection sees the new default. A scalar parameter takes scalar_value, a vector parameter takes vector [r, g, b, a]; the value is read back from the asset into the reply. This edits the asset; to override the value only in a running world use set_material_parameter_collection_instance_value. Add a parameter first with add_collection_parameter; list names, kinds and current defaults with get_collection_info; rename with rename_collection_parameter. Idempotent: the same value again rewrites it and saves. A collection that does not load, a name that is neither a scalar nor a vector parameter, or a missing value for the parameter's kind is an error and nothing changes; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the change only in memory.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the Material Parameter Collection, e.g. "/Game/Materials/MPC_Weather", as create_material_parameter_collection returns it.

params.name: param_name
params.description: Exact name of an existing parameter, e.g. "WindStrength", as get_collection_info lists it.

params.name: scalar_value
params.description: New float default for a scalar parameter, e.g. 0.75; required when the parameter is scalar, ignored for a vector one.

params.name: vector
params.description: New linear color default for a vector parameter, as a JSON array [r, g, b, a] of floats, e.g. [1, 0.5, 0, 1]; alpha is 1 when only three values are given. Required when the parameter is a vector.

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, param_name: string, param_type: string, default_set: bool, saved: bool, default_value: number, scalar_value: number, default: object, default_rgba: [number] }

commands.name: set_material_domain
commands.description: Set the material domain (EMaterialDomain) of a UMaterial asset, then recompile it and mark its package dirty, without saving and without an undo transaction. domain is matched without case and also accepts spellings such as post_process, decal or light function; an unknown domain is an error before the material loads, and a material instance or a path that does not load is an error (Material not found). Setting the domain it already has still recompiles. previous_domain and domain are read back, and domain_set confirms the change took. Persist with save_asset; a new post-process material is create_post_process_material; a recompile alone is compile_material.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full path to the material, e.g. '/Game/MyGame/M_Example.M_Example'; a UMaterial, not a material instance

params.name: domain
params.description: One of 'Surface', 'PostProcess', 'UI', 'DeferredDecal', 'LightFunction', 'Volume', matched without case; post_process, userinterface, decal, deferred_decal and light_function (or the same words with spaces) work too

commands.returns: { material: string, material_path: string, previous_domain: string, requested_domain: string, domain: string, domain_set: bool }

commands.name: set_material_expression_property
commands.description: Write one property of an expression node of a UMaterial asset (not an instance), found by its object name node_id. param_name names the property on every node type (R on Constant, DefaultValue or SliderMax on ScalarParameter, Constant on Constant3Vector and Constant4Vector, DefaultValue on VectorParameter...); ParameterName renames a parameter node through its own SetParameterName. Over set_properties on the node it also runs PostEditChange on the material and accepts "[r,g,b,a]" or "r,g,b" for a linear color. A value that does not parse for the property is refused and nothing is written. No undo, no save: it marks the material dirty (persist with save_asset). value_after is the property read back. Instances: set_material_instance_parameter.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Material asset path

params.name: node_id
params.description: Id of the target expression in the material

params.name: param_name
params.description: Name of the property to set (e.g. "ParameterName", "R", "DefaultValue")

params.name: value
