commands.name: set_material_instance_dynamic_parameter
commands.description: Set a scalar, vector (color) or texture parameter override on a transient Material Instance Dynamic (MID), found by object path or name as create_material_instance_dynamic or create_dynamic_material_on_actor return it; it takes effect at once and is never saved. param_type picks the kind, or it is inferred from value: a number is a scalar, an {r,g,b,a} object a vector, a string a texture path. param_name must be a global parameter of that kind of the MID's material (as get_material_parameters lists it for the MID); any other name is refused and nothing is written. set is the read-back of the new value.

params.name: mid_object_path
params.description: Object path of the MID (from create_material_instance_dynamic)

params.name: param_name
params.description: Name of a parameter of the MID's material, of the kind written

params.name: mid_path
params.description: Alias of mid_object_path

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Alias of param_name

params.name: param_type
params.description: Optional "scalar", "vector" or "texture"; default inferred from value (number -> scalar, object -> vector, string -> texture). Any other value, or one that does not match the value's shape, is an error

params.name: value
params.description: New value: a float for a scalar, a color object {r, g, b, a} for a vector (a missing component is 0, a missing a is 1), a texture content path for a texture. Required unless texture_path is given

params.name: texture_path
params.description: Alias of value for a texture parameter (a texture content path)

commands.returns: { mid_object_path, param_name, param_type, old_value, new_value (numbers for a scalar, {r, g, b, a} for a vector), old_texture_path?, new_texture_path?, requested_texture_path? (texture), set }

commands.name: set_material_instance_parameter
commands.description: Set a parameter override on a Material Instance Constant asset and re-read it: a scalar, vector or texture global parameter (set comes from the re-read, as the engine setter always returns false, plus value_after and overridden_after; the package is marked dirty, not saved), a static switch or static component mask (its static permutation rebuilt and the instance saved), or, with layer_index, a scalar, vector or texture parameter of one layer of a layered instance. Malformed vectors are rejected. set_material_instance_parameter_override toggles or clears overrides; set_material_instance_dynamic_parameter writes a transient MID.

params.name: instance_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInstanceConstant, e.g. "/Game/Materials/MI_Rock".

params.name: param_name
params.description: Parameter name as defined in the parent material, e.g. "BaseTint"; only global parameters are reached, not layer parameters.

params.name: value
params.description: Value. Scalar: a number (JSON number or numeric string). Vector: '(R=..,G=..,B=..,A=..)', '[r,g,b,a]', '[r,g,b]', 'r,g,b,a', 'r,g,b', or a real JSON array of 3-4 numbers; anything else is REJECTED (never written as black). Texture: an asset path. Static switch: a bool or 'true'/'false'.

params.name: association
params.description: Optional, static switch or component mask: GlobalParameter (default), LayerParameter or BlendParameter

params.name: layer_index
params.description: Optional: the zero-based layer of a layered instance; with a scalar, vector or texture param_type it writes that layer's parameter

params.name: param_type
params.description: "scalar" | "vector" | "texture" | "static_switch" | "static_component_mask" (a value [r, g, b, a] of bools) (optional, inferred from the value: a JSON array => vector, a JSON bool => static_switch, a JSON number => scalar, a string starting with '/' => texture, with '(' or '[' => vector, else scalar. A bool passed AS A STRING still reads as scalar, so pass param_type explicitly in that case)

commands.returns: { instance: string, instance_path: string, param_name: string, param_type: string, value_format?: string, set: bool, value_after: number|object|string|bool|null, overridden_after: bool, value_requested: number|object|string|bool, requested: {...} }

commands.name: set_material_instance_parameter_override
commands.description: Toggle the per-parameter override flag on a Material Instance Constant (any of the 11 parameter types, including static switch), or with all=true clear EVERY parameter override at once. bOverride=true keeps/enables the local override; bOverride=false REVERTS the parameter to the parent material's value (removes the override). Runs UpdateMaterialInstance and persists. Returns honestly: success=false when the parameter is not found on the instance. all=true with override=false resets every scalar, vector and texture value to what the parent gives (ClearParameterValuesEditorOnly) and persists, reporting cleared. Editor-only.

params.name: material_instance_path
params.description: Content path to the UMaterialInstanceConstant.

params.name: override
params.description: Bool: true = keep local override; false = revert to parent (remove the value). Must be false with all=true.

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Name of the parameter whose override flag to toggle. Required unless all is true.

params.name: association
params.description: Optional EMaterialParameterAssociation: "Global" (default), "Layer", or "Blend".

params.name: all
params.description: Optional bool (default false): with override=false, clear every parameter override of the instance instead of one; parameter_name is then not used and must be omitted.

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, parameter_name?: string, association?: string, requested_override: bool, applied?: bool, overridden?: bool, cleared?: bool (all=true), saved: bool }

commands.name: set_material_instance_parent
commands.description: Re-parent a material instance onto a different base material -- how you swap an instance from a vendor master to your own without recreating it and re-pointing every referencer. Overrides whose parameter names do not exist on the new parent become orphaned and silently stop applying, so re-read with get_material_parameters afterwards and expect to re-check the static switches, whose defaults come from the new parent.

params.name: material_instance_path
params.description: Content path to the UMaterialInstanceConstant.

params.name: new_parent_path

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, old_parent: string, new_parent: string, changed: bool }

commands.name: set_material_instance_static_component_mask
commands.description: Set a static component-mask (R/G/B/A bools) parameter override on a Material Instance Constant, rebuild the static permutation and persist. Reads back via GetParameterValue. Editor-only.

params.name: material_instance_path

commands.description: Set a static-switch (static bool) parameter override on a Material Instance Constant, then rebuild the static permutation and persist. Reads the value back via the getter (the engine value-setter wrapper always returns false, so its return is never trusted). Editor-only.

commands.description: Write a scalar / vector / texture parameter scoped to ONE layer of a layered material instance (addressed by zero-based layer_index), so each layer of a blend keeps its own tiling, tint or texture. Different from set_material_instance_parameter_override, which targets the Global association and would hit the wrong slot on a layered material. Do not trust the success flag -- the engine's setters are known to report failure while doing the work; re-read with get_material_parameters (parameter_name, association Layer, layer_index).

params.name: material_instance_path
params.description: Content path to the MIC, e.g. /Game/MyGame/MI_Example

params.description: For scalar: a float. For vector: dict {r, g, b, a}. For texture: a content path string.

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, parameter_name: string, layer_index: int, success: bool }

commands.description: Define which material-layer and blend functions a layered material instance stacks, in order -- how you compose a surface (base + dirt + snow) out of reusable layer functions instead of editing the base material graph. Read the result back with get_material_layer_stack.

params.name: layers

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, layer_count: int, blend_count: int, success: bool }

commands.name: set_material_parameter_collection_instance_value
commands.description: Override one scalar or vector (color) parameter on the Material Parameter Collection Instance (MPCI: the transient per-world values) of a collection asset on one world, creating the instance when needed, and push the value to the renderer. A scalar takes value; a vector takes rgba or r/g/b/a (r/g/b/a override the matching rgba entries, and channels given by neither are 0, alpha 1, not the current value) -- the color form is used when any of those is given or when parameter_name is a vector of the collection. The world is the editor world by default, or the Play-in-Editor world world_label selects; world_package and world_type say which one was reached. Runtime only: the asset is untouched, nothing is saved, no undo, and the override is lost when the instance is rebuilt. A missing value or color, a collection that does not load, an unmatched world, or a parameter_name that is not a parameter of that kind in the collection is an error; readback_value / readback_rgba is what the instance holds afterwards, and one that differs from what was written makes success false with readback_ok=false. Saved default: set_collection_parameter_default; drop every override: reset_material_parameter_collection_instance; read values: get_material_parameter_collection_instance_info.

params.name: collection_path
params.description: Full /Game path of the parent MPC

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Name of the scalar or vector parameter to override

params.name: value
params.description: New float value for a scalar parameter. Required unless a color (rgba or r/g/b/a) is given for a vector parameter

params.name: rgba
params.description: Optional [r, g, b, a] color for a vector parameter

params.name: r
params.description: Optional red channel for a vector parameter, alternative to rgba

params.name: g
params.description: Optional green channel

params.name: b
params.description: Optional blue channel

params.name: a
params.description: Optional alpha channel

params.name: world_label
params.description: Which world: empty or "editor" for the editor world (the default), even while Play-in-Editor runs; "pie" (alias "game") for the running PIE world, "server" or "client" for that PIE world, "pie:N" for PIE instance N. any other value names a live world by its object name (the editor world is checked first, so a map name selects it) or by its package name (UEDPIE_N_ and the map name for a PIE world), and a value no world has fails and lists the worlds present

commands.returns: { collection_path: string, parameter_name: string, param_type: string ("scalar" or "vector"), value?: number, readback_value?: number (scalar), value_rgba?: [number], readback_rgba?: [number] (vector), readback_ok: bool, world_name: string, world_package: string, world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }

commands.name: set_material_physical_material
commands.description: Link (or clear) the UPhysicalMaterial on a UMaterial asset and persist it to disk.  Idempotent: re-setting the same phys-mat returns already_set=true.  An empty/omitted physical_material_path CLEARS the link (sets it to null).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Full path to the material (e.g., '/Game/Materials/MyMaterial.MyMaterial')

params.name: physical_material_path

commands.returns: { material_path: string, physical_material_path: string, already_set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, success: bool }

commands.name: set_material_usage_flag
commands.description: Turn one usage flag (EMaterialUsage: SkeletalMesh, InstancedStaticMeshes, NiagaraSprites, SplineMesh...) on or off on a base UMaterial asset, which recompiles its shaders for that usage, then save the material. Use it when get_material_usage_flag shows the flag off for geometry that renders the material as the default checker; it works on base materials only, so set it on the parent of a material instance. Idempotent: when the flag already has that value the engine setter does nothing (already_set=true), though the material is still saved. Not an undo step. An unknown usage name or a path that does not load as a UMaterial is an error and nothing changes. A failed save (a read-only file, say) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, and leaves the flag set in memory only.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Object or package path of the base material, e.g. '/Game/Materials/M_Base.M_Base' or '/Game/Materials/M_Base'.

params.name: usage
params.description: EMaterialUsage name with or without the MATUSAGE_ prefix, e.g. 'SkeletalMesh', 'InstancedStaticMeshes' or 'MATUSAGE_Nanite'; any other name is an error.

params.name: enabled
params.description: true (default) turns the flag on, false turns it off.

commands.returns: { material_path: string, usage: string, enabled: bool (read back from the material), already_set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_substrate_slab_scalar
commands.description: Drives one input pin of the Substrate Slab BSDF node of a material with a constant: adds a NEW Constant expression holding value to the material graph and wires it into the named pin of the material's first Slab node, replacing whatever fed that pin, then saves the material. Each call adds another Constant node, even for the same pin and value; a constant that fed the pin before stays in the graph, unwired. Not recorded for undo, and the save result is not checked. Works whether Substrate is enabled or not (substrate_enabled reports it). The material needs a Slab node from create_substrate_slab_node; connect_substrate_slab_to_material wires the slab to the output. An unknown pin name is an error, but the Constant created before the failed wire stays in the graph. To change a constant already wired, use set_material_expression_property on its constant_node_id; delete stray nodes with delete_material_expression.

params.name: material_path
params.description: Package or object path of the UMaterial holding the slab node (e.g. "/Game/Materials/M_Substrate").

params.name: pin_name
params.description: Slab input pin to drive, by its input name: e.g. "Roughness", "Anisotropy", "F0" or "DiffuseAlbedo" (a color pin receives the scalar on all channels).

params.name: value
params.description: Scalar the Constant node holds (e.g. 0.35 for Roughness); not range-checked.

commands.returns: { material_path: string, slab_node_id: string, constant_node_id: string, pin_name: string, value: number, connected: bool, substrate_enabled: bool, r_substrate_cvar: int, note?: string }

commands.name: swap_material_layer_parameters
commands.description: Exchange two layer slots on a layered material instance -- reorder which surface sits above which without rebuilding the whole stack with set_material_layer_stack. Every per-layer parameter moves with the slot, so any index you recorded earlier now points at the other layer; re-read get_material_layer_stack afterwards.

params.name: material_instance_path
params.description: Content path to the MIC

params.name: original_index
params.description: The original layer parameter index

params.name: new_index
params.description: The new layer parameter index to swap with

commands.returns: { material_instance_path: string, original_index: int, new_index: int, success: bool }

commands.name: clear_procedural_mesh
commands.description: Empty the geometry of one section, or drop every section, of a UProceduralMeshComponent on an editor-world actor found by label, then rebuild its bounds and collision. A single cleared section keeps its slot (remaining_sections unchanged); with section_index omitted or -1 all sections go. Transient: nothing is marked dirty, saved or undoable. A missing actor or component_index is an error, and so is a section_index past the end or below -1. remove_procedural_mesh_component deletes the component itself.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the PMC

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional 0-based PMC index on the actor; defaults to 0

params.name: section_index
params.description: Optional 0-based section to empty; omit it, or pass -1, to drop all sections

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, section_cleared: int, remaining_sections: int }

commands.name: create_procedural_box_mesh
commands.description: Generate a box mesh via UKismetProceduralMeshLibrary::GenerateBoxMesh and push it into a procedural mesh component as a single section: section_index replaces an existing section, or equals the section count to append a new one. A negative section_index, or one past the section count, is an error checked before anything changes.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the PMC

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional 0-based PMC index on the actor; defaults to 0

params.name: section_index
params.description: Optional target section index, 0 to the current section count (which appends a new section); defaults to 0

params.name: box_radius
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] half-extents; defaults to (50, 50, 50)

params.name: create_collision
params.description: Optional bool; defaults to false

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, section_index: int, vertex_count: int, triangle_count: int, total_sections: int }

commands.name: create_procedural_grid_mesh
commands.description: Build a flat welded grid of num_x by num_y vertices spaced grid_spacing apart, centred on the component origin in its XY plane with 0-1 UVs and +Z normals, and write it into section_index of a UProceduralMeshComponent on an editor-world actor found by label, replacing that section if it exists, or appending a new one when section_index equals the section count. A missing actor or component, or a section_index that is negative or past the section count, is an error checked before anything changes. num_x * num_y is capped at 1,000,000 vertices (1000 x 1000) because each grid vertex costs about 300 bytes across the generated arrays, the section copy and the render buffers, so one call stays near 300 MB with every index far inside int32; a larger grid, or a count outside int32, is an error too. Transient: nothing is marked dirty, saved or undoable. Add the component with create_procedural_mesh_component first; create_procedural_box_mesh builds a box.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the PMC

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional 0-based PMC index on the actor; defaults to 0

params.name: section_index
params.description: Optional target section index, 0 to the current section count (which appends a new section); defaults to 0

params.name: num_x
params.description: Optional vertex count along X (the grid has num_x - 1 cells; below 2 there is no geometry); defaults to 10; num_x * num_y at most 1000000

params.name: num_y
params.description: Optional vertex count along Y (the grid has num_y - 1 cells; below 2 there is no geometry); defaults to 10; num_x * num_y at most 1000000

params.name: grid_spacing
params.description: Optional grid cell size in world units; defaults to 16.0

params.name: create_collision
params.description: Optional bool; defaults to false

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, section_index: int, vertex_count: int, triangle_count: int, total_sections: int }

commands.name: create_procedural_mesh_component
commands.description: Spawn a bare AActor labelled actor_label in the editor world with a new UProceduralMeshComponent as its root, the target the procedural-mesh tools find by label; spawn_actor has no bare actor, and add_component_to_actor adds a PMC to an existing one. The new actor stands at location (the origin when omitted; a location that is not 3 numbers is refused) and the PMC is an instance component, so save_level keeps both; one undo step, the level marked dirty, not saved. Idempotent: an actor already labelled actor_label that has a PMC is returned with reused:true and is not moved (location in the reply is where it stands). A label held by an actor WITHOUT a PMC is an error, since the procedural-mesh tools would find that actor first, and so is a label that is "None" or blank; nothing is spawned then.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label for the new actor; the procedural-mesh tools find the actor by it. An actor that already carries it is reused when it has a PMC and refused when it has none (those tools would find it first); a label that is not a valid actor label ("None", blank) is refused. Nothing is spawned on a refusal.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location of a new actor; defaults to (0,0,0). A reused actor is not moved.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_index: int, section_count: int, reused: bool, location: [number, number, number] }

commands.name: get_procedural_mesh_info
commands.description: Read a summary of one procedural mesh component on an editor-world actor, without changing it: the section count, two collision settings (use_complex_as_simple_collision, use_async_cooking) and, per section, its index, vertex and triangle counts, whether it is visible and whether it has collision. Use it to find the section_index the section tools take, and to check that geometry landed after create_procedural_box_mesh, create_procedural_grid_mesh or set_procedural_mesh_section_vertices; for the raw positions, normals and UVs of one section use get_procedural_mesh_section_data. An actor with no such label, or one with no procedural mesh component at component_index, is an error. Editor world only, not PIE.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the component (whole label, case-insensitive; the object name is not matched), as create_procedural_mesh_component set it, e.g. "ProcMeshActor".

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional 0-based index among the actor's procedural mesh components, in component order (default 0); most actors have only one.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, num_sections: int, use_complex_as_simple_collision: bool, use_async_cooking: bool, sections: [{ index: int, vertex_count: int, triangle_count: int, visible: bool, collision_enabled: bool }] }

commands.name: get_procedural_mesh_section_data
commands.description: Read back the raw geometry (vertices, triangles, normals, UV0, tangents, colors) of a single procedural mesh section. A negative or missing section is an error.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the PMC

params.name: section_index
params.description: Required target section index (>= 0)

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional 0-based PMC index on the actor; defaults to 0

commands.returns: { actor_label, section_index, vertex_count, triangle_count, vertices, triangles, normals, uv0, tangents, colors, local_box, collision_enabled, visible }

commands.name: remove_procedural_mesh_component
commands.description: Destroy the UProceduralMeshComponent on a named actor in the editor world (inverse of create_procedural_mesh_component). It removes only the FIRST such component it finds, so an actor carrying several needs one call each; the response says whether one was found at all, and whether it was the actor's root.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the component

commands.returns: { actor_label, removed, component_name?, was_root? }

commands.name: set_procedural_mesh_material
commands.description: Assign a material to one slot of the first UProceduralMeshComponent on an editor-world actor (found by label or object name) with SetMaterial, marking the actor package dirty without saving. Returns the loaded material_path, element_index and previous_material_path when the slot had a material. element_index may name a slot the component has (one per section, or an existing override) or the next one past them; a negative one, or one further past, is an error checked before anything changes. A slot that already holds the material succeeds with material_set false and a note, touching nothing; otherwise material_set is read back from the slot and the call fails when it is false.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label or object name of the actor; the first actor matching either is used

params.name: material_path
params.description: Material or material instance asset path, e.g. "/Game/Materials/M_Rock"

params.name: element_index
params.description: Material slot index, usually the section index; default 0; from 0 up to the larger of the section count and the override count

commands.returns: { actor_label, material_path, element_index, material_set, previous_material_path?, note? }

commands.name: set_procedural_mesh_section_vertices
commands.description: Move the vertices of an existing section of a UProceduralMeshComponent on an editor-world actor found by label: vertices sets every position in order, while triangles, normals, UVs, colors and tangents stay as they were (normals are not recomputed). When the section has collision its collision vertices follow, and the component bounds are rebuilt. Sending the same positions again leaves the section as it was, so the call is idempotent. A missing actor or component, a negative or nonexistent section, an empty vertices array or a count different from the section's is an error before anything changes. Transient: nothing is marked dirty, saved or undoable. New geometry or topology: create_procedural_box_mesh, create_procedural_grid_mesh; read the section back: get_procedural_mesh_section_data; counts: get_procedural_mesh_info.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the PMC

params.name: vertices
params.description: Required [[x, y, z], ...] array in component space with the same vertex count as the existing section; an entry that is not a 3-element array is skipped before the count is compared

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional 0-based PMC index on the actor; defaults to 0

params.name: section_index
params.description: Optional target section index (>= 0); defaults to 0

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, section_index: int, vertex_count: int }

commands.name: set_procedural_mesh_section_visible
commands.description: Toggle the visibility of a single section on a procedural mesh component. Idempotent: sets the section's bSectionVisible flag directly.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the PMC

params.name: visible
params.description: Required bool; new visibility for the section

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional 0-based PMC index on the actor; defaults to 0

params.name: section_index
params.description: Target section index; defaults to 0

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, section_index: int, visible: bool, total_sections: int }

commands.name: slice_procedural_mesh
commands.description: Slice a procedural mesh in place with a plane, optionally spawning the other half as a new PMC on the same actor. NOT idempotent: mutates the mesh destructively; re-running slices the already-sliced result.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the PMC

params.name: component_index
params.description: Optional 0-based PMC index on the actor; defaults to 0

params.name: plane_position
params.description: [x,y,z] world-space point on the slice plane

params.name: plane_normal
params.description: [x,y,z] slice plane normal (must be non-zero); geometry on the positive side is kept

params.name: create_other_half
params.description: Optional bool; if true, the sliced-off half is spawned as a new PMC on the same actor

params.name: cap_option
params.description: Optional "NoCap" | "CreateNewSectionForCap" | "UseLastSectionForCap"; defaults to "NoCap"

params.name: cap_material_path
params.description: Optional /Game path to a UMaterialInterface for the cap

commands.returns: { actor_label, sliced, total_sections, other_half_created, other_half_component_name?, other_half_sections? }

commands.name: execute_batch
commands.description: Run SEVERAL commands back-to-back inside the SAME game-thread pass, with no intermediate MCP round-trips -- the way to cut N calls to 1 when you are authoring in bulk. Any command the bridge dispatches can go in the list. By default every item runs even if an earlier one failed, and each result is reported individually; set stop_on_error to abort at the first failure, and transaction to make the whole run a single undo step.

params.name: commands
params.description: [{command_type: string, params?: object}, ...] (required, non-empty)

params.name: stop_on_error
params.description: Stop after the first failing sub-command (default false)

params.name: transaction
params.description: Wrap the whole run in one undo transaction, so a single undo reverts all of it (begin_transaction / end_transaction). When stop_on_error trips on an error, cancel_transaction closes it instead and rolls back what the run had recorded, items reported ok included: transaction_rolled_back says whether it did. Default false.

commands.returns: { success: bool, results: [{index: int, command_type: string, ok: bool, payload?: any, error?: string}], stopped_early: bool, transaction_rolled_back?: bool (with transaction, when stop_on_error tripped) }

commands.name: add_eqs_generator
commands.description: Adds a UEnvQueryGenerator subclass to a UEnvQuery option. If the option has no generator yet, this becomes it; otherwise replaces. option_index names an existing option, or equals the option count to append one new empty option; a negative option_index, or one past the option count, is an error checked before anything changes.

params.name: query_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required)

params.name: generator_class
params.description: Generator class name (e.g. "ActorsOfClass", "SimpleGrid", "PathingGrid") or full path (e.g. "/Script/AIModule.EnvQueryGenerator_ActorsOfClass")

params.name: option_index
params.description: Optional option index to target (default 0); the current option count appends a new option, a larger index is refused

commands.returns: { query_path, option_index, generator_class, generator_name, replaced, saved }

commands.name: add_eqs_option
commands.description: Append a new empty option (no generator, no tests) after the existing options of the UEnvQuery asset at query_path and return its option_index, always the last one. Each call adds another option (not idempotent). The asset is only marked dirty, not saved (save_asset), and the append is one undo step; a query that does not load is an error. An option without a generator is skipped, with an error log, when the query runs: give it one with add_eqs_generator (which can also append the option itself when option_index equals the option count), then add tests with add_eqs_test. Inspect with get_eqs_query_info; inverse: remove_eqs_option; a new query: create_eqs_query.

params.name: query_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required)

commands.returns: { query_path, option_index, option_count }

commands.name: add_eqs_test
commands.description: Add a test of test_class to an option of a UEnvQuery asset, after the option's existing tests. Idempotent per class: if the option already has a test of that class, that one is returned (already_existed=true) and nothing is added, so an option holds at most one test per class. option_index names an existing option, or equals the option count to append one new empty option; a negative option_index, or one past the option count, is an error checked before anything changes. Undoable as one editor transaction; marks the asset dirty without saving (save_asset). Valid classes: list_eqs_test_types; configure the test with set_eqs_test_scoring; remove_eqs_test is the inverse.

params.name: query_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required)

params.name: test_class
params.description: Test class name (e.g. "Distance", "Trace", "Pathfinding", "Dot") or full path

params.name: option_index
params.description: Optional option index to target (default 0); the current option count appends a new option, a larger index is refused

commands.returns: { query_path, option_index, test_class, test_name, test_index, test_count, already_existed } — idempotent by test class within the option

commands.name: create_eqs_query
commands.description: Create an empty Environment Query System asset (UEnvQuery) named name in package_path (default /Game/EQS), with no options yet, and save it. Idempotent: a query already at that path is returned as it is, with already_exists=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved; an asset of another class there is an error. A failed save (PIE running, read-only file) makes success false with saved=false, the new query kept in memory. Then give it an option and a generator with add_eqs_generator and tests with add_eqs_test, tune them with set_eqs_test_scoring, inspect it with get_eqs_query_info and run it with run_eqs_query.

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name for the new UEnvQuery

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/EQS)

commands.returns: { name, package_path, asset_path, asset_class, query_name, has_options, option_count, already_exists, saved, success, message }

commands.name: diagnose_navmesh
commands.description: One-call navmesh diagnosis: reports every ANavMeshBoundsVolume (brush validity + world extent — detects the EMPTY brush = 0 bounds that yields 0 tiles), inclusion/total nav bounds, bWholeWorldNavigable, invoker-only generation + registered invokers, the RecastNavMesh MaxTiles / built (active) tile count / RuntimeGeneration, and is_spatially_loaded per volume, the nav system state (supported agents by name, nav data count, dirty flag; a world without a navigation system reports zeros, not an error), plus an actionable `diagnosis` list. Read-only.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) | 'server' (**the one you want in PIE**: the navmesh is SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE, so only the authoritative world has a nav system and a RecastNavMesh) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context -- may well land on the CLIENT) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie').

commands.returns: { world, has_authority, nav_system_present, whole_world_navigable, generate_only_around_invokers, supported_agent_count, supported_agents:[string], nav_data_count, is_navigation_dirty, nav_bounds_volume_count, nav_bounds_volumes:[{actor_name, actor_label, is_spatially_loaded, brush_present, brush_empty, bounds_valid, bounds_extent:{x,y,z}, brush_poly_count, note}], registered_nav_bounds_count, total_nav_bounds:{valid, min:{x,y,z}, max:{x,y,z}, extent:{x,y,z}}, invoker_component_count, invoker_location_count, invoker_seed_bounds_count, recast_navmesh_present, recast:{name, runtime_generation, supports_runtime_generation, max_tiles, active_tile_count, tile_size_uu, is_spatially_loaded}, diagnosis:[string], success, world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode, pie_instance }. On a CLIENT world (has_authority=false) the heuristics are suppressed and `diagnosis` says so first: a client with no nav system / no RecastNavMesh is EXPECTED, and rebuild_navigation is NEVER recommended from there.

commands.name: diff_collision_channels
commands.description: Aligns this project's custom collision channels with another project's config BY NAME and reports index shifts (which ECC_GameTraceChannelN slot / TraceTypeQueryN a same-named channel moved to). Diagnoses the migration hazard where custom channels don't travel and traces silently stop hitting. Reads the other project's DefaultEngine.ini straight from disk (not loaded). Read-only.

params.name: other_project_config_dir
params.description: Path to the OTHER project's Config directory (containing DefaultEngine.ini); the project root also works (Config/DefaultEngine.ini is tried as a fallback)

commands.returns: { other_ini_path, other_ini_found, aligned_by, this_channel_count, other_channel_count, shifted_count, matched:[{name, is_trace_type, channel_this, channel_other, channel_shifted, query_this, query_other, query_shifted}], only_in_this:[{name, channel, query_type}], only_in_other:[{name, channel, query_type}], success }

commands.name: dump_collision_channels
commands.description: Dumps this project's custom collision channels (from config): each ECC_GameTraceChannelN / object channel -> friendly name, whether it's a trace or object channel, and its TraceTypeQueryN / ObjectTypeQueryN index (the value a raycast/overlap passes). Read-only. Read from GConfig [/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile] DefaultChannelResponses.
commands.returns: { source, builtin_trace_count, builtin_object_count, count, channels:[{channel, channel_value, name, is_trace_type, is_static_object, is_custom_game_slot, default_response, query_type, query_index, query_number}], success }

retired.how: each custom channel carries is_trace_type, query_type, query_index and query_number

commands.name: get_eqs_query_info
commands.description: Reports the composition of an Environment Query (UEnvQuery) asset without running it: each option with its index, its generator class (absent when the option has none) and its tests in order, each with index and class. Read-only: loads the asset, changes and saves nothing; an asset that does not load as a UEnvQuery is an error, and a query without options returns option_count 0. Use it to get the option_index and test_index that add_eqs_generator, add_eqs_test, set_eqs_test_scoring, set_eqs_generator_properties, remove_eqs_test and remove_eqs_option take, and to check their result. To see what the query actually selects in the level, run it with run_eqs_query; the classes to add come from list_eqs_generator_types and list_eqs_test_types.

params.name: query_path
params.description: Asset path of the UEnvQuery (required), e.g. "/Game/EQS/EQ_FindCover" (the ".EQ_FindCover" object suffix is optional), as create_eqs_query or find_assets_by_name gives it.

commands.returns: { query_path, option_count, options:[{index, generator_class?, generator_path?, test_count, tests:[{index, class, path}]}] }

commands.name: get_recast_navmesh_settings
commands.description: Read the generation settings of the editor world's default RecastNavMesh: agent_radius, agent_height, agent_max_slope (degrees) and agent_max_step_height, tile_size_uu (resolved) and tile_size_uu_raw (the property), cell_size and cell_height at Default resolution, merge_region_size, min_region_area and the simplification values; lengths in cm. The read side of set_recast_navmesh_settings: call it before and after that tool. Whether the navmesh is actually built (bounds, tile counts) is diagnose_navmesh's job, and get_navigation_data lists the nav actors of any world. Read-only and idempotent; never creates a navmesh; editor world only. With no RecastNavMesh yet (no NavMeshBoundsVolume, or never built) it answers recast_navmesh_present=false and success=true with a note, not an error.
commands.returns: { recast_navmesh_present, navmesh_name, agent_radius, agent_height, agent_max_slope, agent_max_step_height, tile_size_uu, tile_size_uu_raw, cell_size, cell_height, merge_region_size, min_region_area, max_simplification_error, simplification_elevation_ratio, note, success }

commands.name: list_eqs_context_types
commands.description: Lists the concrete EQS context classes (UEnvQueryContext subclasses, such as EnvQueryContext_Querier or EnvQueryContext_Item) loaded in this editor, sorted by name, each with its name and class path; abstract and deprecated classes are left out. Read-only reflection: takes no parameters, loads and changes nothing. Blueprint contexts appear only once their Blueprint is loaded. A context class says what a generator or test is measured from: pass its path to a context property, such as SearchCenter, with set_eqs_generator_properties. For generator classes use list_eqs_generator_types, for test classes list_eqs_test_types; get_eqs_query_info shows what a query already uses.
commands.returns: { base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }

commands.name: list_eqs_generator_types
commands.description: Lists all concrete UEnvQueryGenerator subclasses usable as EQS generators. Read-only reflection (GetDerivedClasses).
commands.returns: { base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }

commands.name: list_eqs_test_types
commands.description: Lists all concrete UEnvQueryTest subclasses usable as EQS tests. Read-only reflection (GetDerivedClasses).
commands.returns: { base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }

commands.name: rebuild_navigation
commands.description: Rebuild all navigation data of the editor world (UNavigationSystemV1::Build): regenerate every navmesh tile inside the NavMeshBoundsVolumes, spawning a missing RecastNavMesh, and block until the build finishes (seconds on a large map). Call it after moving geometry or nav volumes, or after set_recast_navmesh_settings (or pass rebuild=true there). Diagnose first, and check the result after, with diagnose_navmesh (active_tile_count) or get_navigation_data; place bounds with spawn_box_volume (volume_class=NavMeshBoundsVolume). rebuilt=true only means the build ran: with no bounds volume, or a locked build, the engine builds nothing. A world with no navigation system is not an error: rebuilt=false, nav_system_present=false. A repeat call rebuilds again. No undo step; the level is not saved (save_level). Editor world only, never a PIE session.
commands.returns: { rebuilt, nav_system_present, message, success, nav_data_count }

commands.name: remove_eqs_generator
commands.description: Remove the generator from one option of a UEnvQuery asset, keeping the option and its tests. The inverse of add_eqs_generator; to swap generators just call add_eqs_generator, which replaces it; to drop the whole option with its tests use remove_eqs_option, and one test remove_eqs_test. get_eqs_query_info shows each option's generator before and after. An option left without a generator is skipped, with an error log, when the query runs. One undo step; the asset is marked dirty, not saved (save_asset). Idempotent: an option that already has no generator answers removed=false and nothing changes. A query that does not load, or an option_index out of range, is an error and nothing changes.

params.name: query_path
params.description: Asset path of the UEnvQuery, e.g. "/Game/EQS/EQ_FindCover" (the ".EQ_FindCover" object suffix is optional), as create_eqs_query or find_assets_by_name gives it (required)

params.name: option_index
params.description: 0-based index of the option whose generator goes, as get_eqs_query_info lists the options (default 0); out of range is an error

commands.returns: { query_path, option_index, removed }

commands.name: remove_eqs_option
commands.description: Remove the option at option_index from a UEnvQuery asset loaded by asset path, together with its generator and all its tests; the options after it shift down one index, and option_count is what remains. One undo step puts it back. The asset is marked dirty, not saved: persist it with save_asset. A query that does not load, or an option_index out of range, is an error and nothing changes. Not idempotent: repeating the call removes the option that moved into that index, so read the indices with get_eqs_query_info first. Inverse: add_eqs_option; keep the option but drop its generator: remove_eqs_generator; a single test: remove_eqs_test.

params.name: query_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required)

params.name: option_index
params.description: Index of the option to remove (required)

commands.returns: { query_path, option_index, removed, option_count }

commands.name: remove_eqs_test
commands.description: Remove the test at test_index from the option at option_index (default 0) of a UEnvQuery asset loaded by asset path; the tests after it shift down one index, and test_count is what the option keeps. One undo step puts the test back. The asset is marked dirty, not saved: persist it with save_asset. A query that does not load, or an option or test index out of range, is an error and nothing changes. Not idempotent: repeating the call removes the test that moved into that index, so read the indices with get_eqs_query_info first. Inverse: add_eqs_test; retune a test instead: set_eqs_test_scoring; a whole option: remove_eqs_option; the generator: remove_eqs_generator.

params.name: query_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required)

params.name: test_index
params.description: Index of the test to remove within the option (required)

params.name: option_index
params.description: 0-based index of the query option that holds the test (default 0).

commands.returns: { query_path, option_index, test_index, removed, test_count }

commands.name: run_eqs_query
commands.description: Run a UEnvQuery once, synchronously, in the editor world (UEnvQueryManager::RunInstantQuery) and return status, num_items, item_type and up to max_items scored items, each with score, location and, for actor items, the actor. Use it to test a query built with create_eqs_query, add_eqs_generator and add_eqs_test; get_eqs_query_info shows its composition without running it. It changes no asset or actor and saves nothing; editor world only, never a PIE session. Generators/tests needing navigation data (SimpleGrid/PathingGrid/Pathfinding/Project/Trace) need a built navmesh (rebuild_navigation, checked with diagnose_navmesh); without it, or without a querier for Querier-relative contexts, status is not Success while success and ran stay true, with a note. No EQS manager, or a query with no usable option, answers ran=false with a note. An unknown query_path, querier_actor or run_mode is an error and the query does not run.

params.name: query_path
params.description: Asset path of the UEnvQuery, e.g. "/Game/EQS/EQ_FindCover" (the ".EQ_FindCover" object suffix is optional), as create_eqs_query or find_assets_by_name gives it (required)

params.name: querier_actor
params.description: Optional object name or editor label of the editor-world actor used as the query Querier (drives EnvQueryContext_Querier and Querier-relative generators), whole name, case-insensitive, first match wins, e.g. "BP_Guard_C_0"; omitted: the query asset itself, which has no location

params.name: run_mode
params.description: "SingleResult" (the best item) | "RandomBest5Pct" | "RandomBest25Pct" (one random item scoring within 5% or 25% of the best) | "AllMatching" (every passing item, best first); case-insensitive, default "AllMatching", any other value is an error

params.name: max_items
params.description: Optional cap on how many items are serialized into items, a whole number (default 50; negative counts as 0); the query still evaluates all and num_items counts them

commands.returns: { query_path, ran, eqs_manager_present, status, is_successful, num_items, item_type, run_mode, items:[{index, score, location:{x,y,z}, actor?}], note? }

commands.name: set_eqs_generator_properties
commands.description: Set properties of the generator of one option (option_index) of a UEnvQuery asset by reflection, in one undo step; only the named properties change. Use it over set_properties, which needs the generator's object path: here a class property (SearchedActorClass, SearchCenter) takes a class path such as /Script/Engine.Pawn, checked against its base class, and an FAIDataProvider value (SearchRadius, GenerateOnlyActorsInRadius) takes {"DefaultValue": number or bool}; others take their JSON value. A property that is unknown or rejects the value lands in failed without failing the call; applied echoes each stored value. A query that does not load, an option_index out of range or an option with no generator (add_eqs_generator) is an error. Marked dirty, not saved (save_asset). Scoring: set_eqs_test_scoring; classes: list_eqs_generator_types; composition: get_eqs_query_info.

params.name: query_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required)

params.name: properties
params.description: JSON object { PropertyName: value, ... } applied to the generator, keys as named on its class (value formats in the description)

params.name: option_index
params.description: Zero-based option index whose generator is edited (default 0); out of range is an error

commands.returns: { query_path, option_index, generator_class, set:[name], failed:[{name, error}], applied:{name: stored_value_text} }

commands.name: set_eqs_test_scoring
commands.description: Set the scoring and filter settings of test test_index in option option_index of a UEnvQuery asset, in one undo step: TestPurpose, FilterType, ScoringEquation, the FloatValueMin and FloatValueMax bounds and, only when given, ScoringFactor. The first five are written on every call, so one left out goes back to its default (Score, Range, Linear, 0, 1); the reply reads the stored values back. Values equal to the stored ones are a no-op: changed=false, a note, nothing written. A changed asset is marked dirty, not saved: persist it with save_asset. An enum name the param does not list (the error names the accepted ones), a query that does not load or an index out of range is an error, and nothing changes. Add the test with add_eqs_test; read the indices with get_eqs_query_info; generator settings: set_eqs_generator_properties.

params.name: query_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required)

params.name: option_index
params.description: Option index (default 0)

params.name: test_index
params.description: Test index within the option (default 0)

params.name: test_purpose
params.description: "Filter" | "Score" | "FilterAndScore" (default "Score")

params.name: filter_type
params.description: "Minimum" | "Maximum" | "Range" | "Match" (default "Range")

params.name: scoring_equation
params.description: "Linear" | "Square" | "InverseLinear" | "SquareRoot" | "Constant" (default "Linear")

params.name: scoring_factor
params.description: Optional weight multiplier applied after the equation (ScoringFactor.DefaultValue); only applied when provided

params.name: float_value_min
params.description: Optional min for FloatValueMin (default 0)

params.name: float_value_max
params.description: Optional max for FloatValueMax (default 1)

commands.returns: { query_path, option_index, test_index, test_name, changed, test_purpose, filter_type, scoring_equation, scoring_factor, float_value_min, float_value_max, note? }

commands.name: set_recast_navmesh_settings
commands.description: Change generation settings of the editor world's default RecastNavMesh: agent size, slope and step height, tile and cell size, region and simplification values. Only the params passed are written, each clamped first, and applied echoes the stored values, so a repeat call changes nothing more. Read current values with get_recast_navmesh_settings. Existing tiles keep the old settings until a rebuild: pass rebuild=true (synchronous, seconds on a large map) or call rebuild_navigation, then check tiles with diagnose_navmesh. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level). Editor world only. Without a RecastNavMesh (no NavMeshBoundsVolume yet: spawn_box_volume with volume_class=NavMeshBoundsVolume, then rebuild_navigation) nothing changes and it answers recast_navmesh_present=false, success=true, with a note.

params.name: agent_radius
params.description: Optional float, cm; ARecastNavMesh::AgentRadius, e.g. 34 (>= 0; negatives become 0). When the navmesh registers again (a map reload) the navigation system's Supported Agents config writes its own radius back

params.name: agent_height
params.description: Optional float, cm; ARecastNavMesh::AgentHeight, e.g. 144 (>= 0); like agent_radius, the Supported Agents config writes its own value back when the navmesh registers again

params.name: agent_max_slope
params.description: Optional float degrees; ARecastNavMesh::AgentMaxSlope, e.g. 44 (clamped to 0..89)

params.name: agent_max_step_height
params.description: Optional float, cm; SetAgentMaxStepHeight(Default, v), the highest step agents climb, e.g. 35 (>= 0)

params.name: tile_size_uu
params.description: Optional float, cm; ARecastNavMesh::TileSizeUU, the edge of one navmesh tile, e.g. 1000 (clamped to >= 300)

params.name: cell_size
params.description: Optional float, cm; SetCellSize(Default, v), voxel width: smaller is finer and slower to build, e.g. 19 (clamped 1..1024)

params.name: cell_height
params.description: Optional float, cm; SetCellHeight(Default, v), voxel height, e.g. 10 (clamped 1..1024)

params.name: merge_region_size
params.description: Optional float; ARecastNavMesh::MergeRegionSize, regions smaller than this merge with neighbours, e.g. 400 (>= 0)

params.name: min_region_area
params.description: Optional float; ARecastNavMesh::MinRegionArea, isolated regions smaller than this are dropped, e.g. 0 (>= 0)

params.name: max_simplification_error
params.description: Optional float; ARecastNavMesh::MaxSimplificationError, how far simplified edges may stray from the voxel outline, e.g. 1.3 (>= 0)

params.name: simplification_elevation_ratio
params.description: Optional float; ARecastNavMesh::SimplificationElevationRatio, e.g. 0 (>= 0)

params.name: rebuild
params.description: Optional bool (default false); true calls UNavigationSystemV1::Build() synchronously after writing so the change takes effect now; false leaves requires_rebuild=true

commands.returns: { recast_navmesh_present, navmesh_name, applied:{field:value}, requires_rebuild, rebuilt, note, success }

commands.name: spawn_nav_link_proxy
commands.description: Spawn an ANavLinkProxy actor (with its class-default point link) in the editor world at location through the editor actor subsystem, in one undo step, and label it with its internal name so label lookups find it. spawn_actor has no nav-link type. Each call adds a new actor (not idempotent); the link endpoints are not set here -- write its PointLinks with set_properties. The level is not saved (save_level) and this call does not rebuild navigation (rebuild_navigation). During PIE the editor refuses the spawn and the call is an error, as it is without an editor world. Move it with set_actor_transform; inverse: delete_actor. An area that changes path cost or blocks: spawn_nav_modifier_volume; the navmesh bounds: spawn_navmesh_bounds_volume.

params.name: location
params.description: [x, y, z] world location for the nav link proxy in cm; missing spawns at the origin, and any other value is an error and nothing is spawned

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_label, actor_path, actor_class, success }

commands.name: spawn_nav_modifier_volume
commands.description: Spawn an ANavModifierVolume in the editor world at location, give it a real box brush of half-extent extent (a spawned volume has none) and optionally set its nav area class, in one undo step, then label it with its internal name so label lookups find it. Over spawn_box_volume(volume_class='NavModifierVolume') it sets the area class in the same call; spawn_box_volume instead re-reads the bounds against the request. area_class names a UNavArea subclass already loaded (e.g. NavArea_Null or NavArea_Obstacle; a Blueprint area by its _C name); a name that does not resolve is not an error: area_class_applied comes back false and the default area stays. An extent axis of 0 or less becomes 100. Each call adds a new actor. Not saved (save_level); this call does not rebuild navigation (rebuild_navigation). Refused during PIE. Navmesh bounds: spawn_navmesh_bounds_volume; links: spawn_nav_link_proxy.

params.name: location
params.description: [x, y, z] world location for the volume in cm; missing spawns at the origin, and any other value is an error and nothing is spawned

params.name: area_class
params.description: Optional UNavArea subclass name to apply via SetAreaClass, e.g. NavArea_Null; unresolved names are ignored with area_class_applied false

params.name: extent
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] box half-extent in cm (default 100,100,100, a 200 cm box); a component of 0 or less becomes 100

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_label, actor_path, actor_class, brush_built, area_class_applied, area_class, success }

commands.name: get_dedicated_server_status
commands.description: Polls the state of the most recent launch_dedicated_server job: running / finished / canceled, with elapsed time and a tail of captured process output. Honest has_server:false if no server was ever launched this editor session.
commands.returns: { has_server: bool, running?: bool, finished?: bool, canceled?: bool, exit_code?: int, command_line?: string, elapsed_seconds?: number, output_tail?: string }

commands.name: get_network_info
commands.description: Read a network snapshot of the editor world, never a PIE world: its net mode (with its code and the server/client flags); whether it has a net driver, and the driver's class, tick rates and client connection count; every replicating actor with its class, local and remote role and dormancy, optionally only those with one local role; when they exist, the GameState (class, player count, each player) and the first PlayerController; and the session keys of the [OnlineSubsystem] engine config. The editor world normally has no net driver, GameState or PlayerController, so net_driver_info comes back empty and those two blocks are left out. Nothing is written; without an editor world it is an error. One actor in detail: get_actor_replication_info; a whole-project Blueprint sweep: audit_replication.

params.name: role_filter
params.description: Optional local role to keep in replicated_actors: Authority, SimulatedProxy, AutonomousProxy or None (case-insensitive); omitted lists every replicating actor. Any other value is an error.

commands.returns: { world_name: string, world_valid: bool, net_mode: string, net_mode_code: int, is_server: bool, is_client: bool, has_net_driver: bool, net_driver_info: { class?: string, max_net_tick_rate?: number, net_server_max_tick_rate?: number, connection_count?: number }, replicated_actors: [{ name: string, class: string, local_role: string, remote_role: string, is_replicated: bool, net_dormancy: string }], replicated_actor_count: number, role_filter?: string, has_game_state: bool, game_state_info?: { class: string, player_count: number, is_valid: bool, players: [{ player_name: string, player_id: number, is_valid: bool, player_class: string }] }, player_controller_info?: { class: string, is_valid: bool, is_local_player: bool }, config_settings: { default_platform_service?: string, default_identity_interface?: string, max_players: number, use_dedicated_server: bool } }

commands.name: launch_dedicated_server
commands.description: Relaunches the CURRENT editor binary with "-server -log": a real, non-rendering, network-listening game instance (GIsServer=true/GIsClient=false/GIsEditor=false -- confirmed via UE 5.8 source: StaticDedicatedServerCheck/SetIsRunningAsDedicatedServer in LaunchEngineLoop.cpp, FApp::CanEverRender()==false whenever IsRunningDedicatedServer()). This is honestly NOT a Server.Target.cs shipping build (still the full editor binary, WITH_EDITOR=1) -- it closes only the TESTABLE half of the dedicated-server gap; real server packaging is out of scope. Async, like start_package_build: returns immediately once the process is launched, poll get_dedicated_server_status for output/exit; the server never exits on its own, so call stop_dedicated_server to terminate it. Refuses to launch a second server while one is already running (honest, not silently queued/clobbered).

params.name: extra_args
params.description: Optional raw extra command-line arguments appended verbatim after "-server -log" (e.g. "-port=8888").

commands.returns: { server_started: bool, already_running: bool, command_line: string, note: string }

commands.name: set_actor_replication
commands.description: Configure the replication of an editor-world actor found by object name or label: movement (bReplicateMovement) and lifecycle (bReplicates: the actor is spawned and destroyed on clients). Only the settings sent are applied, inside one undoable transaction, and each is read back: a call that sends neither replicate_movement nor replicate_lifecycle changes nothing and is an error. Physics has no switch of its own in the engine -- a simulating root's state travels with movement replication -- so replicate_physics is reported in not_applied. Only that placed instance changes, not its class defaults; nothing is saved. Read every replication setting with get_actor_replication_info.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the actor in the editor world (first match)

params.name: replicate_movement
params.description: Optional: whether to replicate movement (bReplicateMovement); applied only when sent

params.name: replicate_physics
params.description: Optional; NOT applied, see the description; listed in not_applied when sent

params.name: replicate_lifecycle
params.description: Optional: whether the actor replicates at all, i.e. exists on clients (bReplicates, set through AActor::SetReplicates); applied only when sent. Movement replication does nothing without it.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, replication_configured: bool, message: string, previous_settings: { replicate_movement: bool, replicate_lifecycle: bool }, new_settings: { replicate_movement?: bool, replicate_lifecycle?: bool }, actual_settings: { replicate_movement: bool, replicate_lifecycle: bool }, not_applied?: [string], actor_valid: bool, actor_class: string }

commands.name: set_network_authority
commands.description: Set the local net role (AActor::SetRole) of an editor-world actor, found by object name rather than label, to Authority, SimulatedProxy, AutonomousProxy or None (case-insensitive; any other value is an error before anything changes). Only that placed instance's in-memory Role changes: RemoteRole and replication settings stay as they are, there is no undo entry and the level is not marked dirty. authority_set compares the role read back with the request. Read roles with get_actor_replication_info (one actor) or get_network_info (every replicated actor, filterable by role); choose what replicates with set_properties.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name of the editor-world actor (case-insensitive); labels are not matched

params.name: authority
params.description: The network authority role to set; valid values: Authority, SimulatedProxy, AutonomousProxy, None

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, authority_set: bool, previous_authority: string, requested_authority: string, actual_authority: string, actor_valid: bool, actor_class: string }

commands.name: stop_dedicated_server
commands.description: Terminates the in-progress dedicated server, if one is running (honest no-op otherwise). FMonitoredProcess::Cancel(true) kills the whole process tree.
commands.returns: { stopped: bool, was_running: bool }

commands.name: analyze_asset_performance
commands.description: Grade one asset Good, Fair or Poor against fixed thresholds, without changing it: the path is looked up in the asset registry and the asset loaded synchronously. Static meshes are graded on triangles summed over all render LODs (above 50k Fair, above 100k Poor), Texture2D on resolution (above 2K, above 4K), materials and instances on parameter count (above 25, above 50); fewer than 2 LODs or mips, a mesh or texture package over 50 MB and over 10 texture parameters only add performance_issues. Other classes get performance_rating Unknown. suggestions is fixed advice per class, not derived from the numbers; texture_sample_count counts texture parameters and instruction_count is always 0. A path missing from the registry or failing to load is an error. Many assets: execute_batch; a verdict: check_asset_optimization; shader stats: get_material_stats; memory: get_asset_memory_usage.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.SM_Rock") or package path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock") of an asset the asset registry knows

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, asset_class: string, file_size_bytes: number, file_size_mb: number, optimization_type: string, lod_count?: number, triangle_count?: number, vertex_count?: number, section_count?: number, performance_rating: string, performance_issues: [string], suggestions: [string], width?: number, height?: number, mip_count?: number, compression_settings?: string, pixel_format?: string, parameter_count?: number, texture_sample_count?: number, instruction_count?: number }

commands.name: analyze_assets_performance_batch
commands.description: Batch version of analyze_asset_performance. Resolves and analyzes multiple assets by path in one call (avoids callers looping analyze_asset_performance one-by-one). Forces a synchronous load per asset, so max_results defaults conservatively.

params.name: asset_paths
params.description: Required array of asset paths to analyze.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional cap on how many of asset_paths to process (default 200, clamped 1..2000). Entries beyond the cap are not processed.

commands.returns: { requested_count: number, processed_count: number, results_truncated: bool, results: [{ asset_path: string, found: bool, asset_class?: string, file_size_bytes?: number, file_size_mb?: number, optimization_type?: string, performance_rating?: string, performance_issues?: [string], suggestions?: [string], ...same per-asset fields as analyze_asset_performance's data payload, error?: string }] }

commands.name: check_asset_optimization
commands.description: Check one asset against fixed optimization thresholds and return a verdict, without changing it; the asset is found in the asset registry and loaded. Static meshes: LOD count (under 2 severe, under 3 mild), triangles over all render LODs (above 100k, above 50k) and package size (above 50 MB, above 10 MB). Texture2D: resolution (above 4K, above 2K), mips (under 2, under 4), package size and an advisory note for the TC_Default preset. Materials and instances: parameters (above 50, above 25) and texture parameters (above 10, above 5). Other classes: package size only. is_optimized turns false on any severe finding, optimization_status is the worst tier (Good, Fair, Poor), and issues pair one to one with recommendations. A path missing from the registry or failing to load is an error. Graded stats: analyze_asset_performance; more advice: suggest_asset_optimizations; fixes: set_asset_lod_settings, set_asset_compression.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.SM_Rock") or package path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock") of an asset the asset registry knows

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, asset_class: string, file_size_bytes: number, file_size_mb: number, is_optimized: bool, optimization_status: string, issues: [string], recommendations: [string], lod_count?: number, triangle_count?: number, vertex_count?: number, width?: number, height?: number, mip_count?: number, compression_settings?: string, pixel_format?: string, parameter_count?: number, texture_sample_count?: number }

commands.name: get_asset_compression
commands.description: Read a TEXTURE's compression settings (inverse of set_asset_compression): TC_* enum names plus pixel format and LOD group. Accepts UTexture2D / UTexture2DArray / UTextureCube / UTextureRenderTarget2D; hand it anything else and it does not error -- it answers is_texture=false and reports asset_class, so check that flag before reading the rest.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full /Game/... asset path

commands.returns: { asset_path, asset_class, is_texture, compression_settings?, pixel_format?, lod_group?, source_format?, srgb?, never_stream?, note? }

commands.name: get_asset_lod_settings
commands.description: Read a mesh's LOD config (inverse of set_asset_lod_settings): per-LOD triangle count, vertex count and screen size for UStaticMesh or USkeletalMesh, plus LODGroup, which exists on StaticMesh only. There is NO lod-bias field in the response -- see the note below before you go looking for it.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full /Game/... asset path

commands.returns: { asset_path, asset_class, lod_count, lod_group?, lods:[{ lod_index, screen_size?, triangle_count, vertex_count }] }

commands.name: get_asset_memory_usage
commands.description: Estimate the memory one asset needs from simple formulas, not a measurement, without changing it; the asset is found in the asset registry and loaded. Static meshes count 24-byte vectors, three per triangle plus one per vertex, over all render LODs; Texture2D 4 bytes per texel over the whole mip chain, whatever the compression; materials and instances 1 KB per parameter; any other class reports its package size. memory_usage bands the estimate per class (Low, Medium, High, Very High; Unknown for other classes) and optimization_tips is one fixed line per class. file_size_bytes is the package file on disk, 0 when there is none. A path missing from the registry or failing to load is an error. The disk size alone is get_asset_file_info, a graded report analyze_asset_performance, the whole editor's memory get_memory_usage.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.SM_Rock") or package path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock") of an asset the asset registry knows

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, asset_class: string, file_size_bytes: number, file_size_mb: number, memory_type: string, lod_count?: number, triangle_count?: number, vertex_count?: number, section_count?: number, estimated_memory_usage_bytes: number, estimated_memory_usage_mb: number, memory_usage: string, optimization_tips: string, width?: number, height?: number, mip_count?: number, compression_settings?: string, pixel_format?: string, parameter_count?: number, texture_sample_count?: number }

commands.name: get_asset_streaming_config
commands.description: Read the streaming knobs (inverse of set_asset_streaming_config). Works at two levels: with NO asset_path it reports the GLOBAL texture-streaming pool size (only when the editor runs a render-asset streaming manager -- an editor started with -nullrhi has none, and then streaming_manager_available is false and the pool size is omitted); with one, it adds that asset's NeverStream flag (which applies to any UStreamableRenderAsset -- textures AND static meshes) plus the texture-only LODGroup and VirtualTextureStreamingPriority. There is NO `streaming_priority` field -- see the note below.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Optional /Game/... asset path; if omitted, returns global streaming config only

commands.returns: { streaming_manager_available: bool, global_pool_size?: int, asset_path?, asset_class?, is_streamable?: bool, never_stream?: bool, lod_group?: string, lod_group_int?: number, use_virtual_texture_streaming_priority?: bool, note? }

commands.name: set_asset_compression
commands.description: Sets the REAL texture compression quality (UTexture::CompressionQuality) on a texture asset and saves it to disk. Only UTexture targets are supported (no engine-level "compression" concept exists for meshes/materials); non-texture assets fail honestly with success:false.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: The path to the asset in the asset registry.

params.name: compression_type
params.description: The compression quality to apply: 'High', 'Medium', or 'Low' (case-insensitive). Maps to TCQ_High / TCQ_Medium / TCQ_Low. Any other value is a hard error.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, compression_type: string, asset_type: string, original_file_size_bytes: number, original_file_size_mb: number, is_texture: bool, compression_quality_applied?: string, current_compression_settings?: string, pixel_format?: string, width?: number, height?: number, mip_count?: number, saved: bool, success: bool, message: string, error?: string }

commands.name: set_asset_lod_settings
commands.description: Sets the REAL LOD count on a UStaticMesh (adds/removes FStaticMeshSourceModel entries via AddSourceModel/RemoveSourceModel, rebuilds via PostEditChange, saves to disk). SkeletalMesh LOD-count mutation is NOT supported (would require the FLODUtilities mesh-reduction subsystem, out of scope) -- read-only LOD info is still reported honestly. Non-mesh assets fail with success:false.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: The path to the asset in the asset registry.

params.name: lod_count
params.description: The desired number of LOD levels (1-8). Must be an integer. Only mutates for UStaticMesh; reported but not applied for SkeletalMesh/other.

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, requested_lod_count: number, asset_type: string, current_lod_count?: number, total_triangles?: number, total_vertices?: number, lod_data?: [object], saved?: bool, success: bool, message: string, error?: string, final_lod_count: number, lod_efficiency?: number, lod_recommendations?: [string] }

commands.name: set_asset_streaming_config
commands.description: Sets the REAL NeverStream flag (UStreamableRenderAsset::NeverStream) on a texture or static mesh and saves it to disk. enable_streaming=true clears NeverStream (asset streams on demand); enable_streaming=false sets it (asset stays fully resident). Assets with no such knob (e.g. Material) fail honestly with success:false.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: The path to the asset in the asset registry.

params.name: enable_streaming
params.description: Whether to enable streaming for the asset (maps to NeverStream = !enable_streaming).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, enable_streaming: bool, asset_type: string, file_size_bytes: number, file_size_mb: number, is_streamable: bool, never_stream?: bool, saved?: bool, success: bool, message: string, error?: string }

commands.name: suggest_asset_optimizations
commands.description: List optimization advice for one asset, without changing it; the asset is found in the asset registry and loaded. critical_suggestions come from thresholds: a static mesh with fewer than 2 render LODs or over 100k triangles across them, a Texture2D above 4K or with fewer than 2 mips, a material or instance with over 50 parameters or over 10 texture parameters, and any package over 50 MB. performance_suggestions and memory_suggestions are fixed advice per class plus package-size notes above 10 MB, and suggestions joins all of them with eight generic lines every asset gets; other classes get a not-analyzed note instead of class advice. A path missing from the registry or failing to load is an error. For a pass/fail verdict use check_asset_optimization, for graded stats analyze_asset_performance.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.SM_Rock") or package path ("/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock") of an asset the asset registry knows

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, asset_class: string, file_size_bytes: number, file_size_mb: number, suggestions: [string], critical_suggestions: [string], performance_suggestions: [string], memory_suggestions: [string], lod_count?: number, triangle_count?: number, vertex_count?: number, width?: number, height?: number, mip_count?: number, compression_settings?: string, pixel_format?: string, parameter_count?: number, texture_sample_count?: number }

commands.name: cancel_package_build
commands.description: Stop the package build that start_package_build launched in this editor session, if it is still running: the whole process tree is killed (UAT and the UnrealBuildTool and cooker processes it spawned), so its partial output stays as it is and the build has to be started again from the beginning. A build launched outside this editor session is not seen. Idempotent: with no build running, or none started this session, nothing happens and canceled and was_running are false. canceled true means the kill was requested; the processes end asynchronously, so confirm with get_package_build_status (canceled true, running false) before starting a new build with start_package_build.
commands.returns: { canceled: bool, was_running: bool }

commands.name: get_package_build_status
commands.description: Polls the state of the most recent start_package_build job: running / finished / canceled / launch-failed, with elapsed time and a tail of captured UAT output. Honest has_build:false if no build was ever started this editor session.
commands.returns: { has_build: bool, running?: bool, finished?: bool, canceled?: bool, launch_failed?: bool, exit_code?: int, success?: bool, platform?: string, configuration?: string, elapsed_seconds?: number, output_tail?: string }

commands.name: start_package_build
commands.description: Starts an asynchronous project package build (BuildCookRun) via UAT (FSerializedUATProcess), for the current .uproject. Runs RunUAT BuildCookRun -project=<this project> -noP4 -utf8output -platform=<platform> -clientconfig=<configuration> -cook -allmaps -build -stage -pak -archive -archivedirectory=<dir>. This is a real external process that can take minutes (it builds the target, then cooks); the call returns immediately once launched -- poll get_package_build_status for progress/outcome. Refuses to start a second build while one is already in flight (honest, not silently queued).

params.name: platform
params.description: Optional target platform (UAT platform name, e.g. "Win64"). Defaults to "Win64".

params.name: configuration
params.description: Optional build configuration ("Debug"|"DebugGame"|"Development"|"Test"|"Shipping"). Defaults to "Development".

params.name: archive_directory
params.description: Optional output directory for the archived build. Defaults to <ProjectSavedDir>/Packages/<platform>.

params.name: extra_args
params.description: Optional raw extra UAT arguments appended verbatim (e.g. "-distribution -iostore").

commands.returns: { build_started: bool, already_running: bool, platform: string, configuration: string, archive_directory: string, command_line: string, note: string }

commands.name: add_trace_bookmark
commands.description: Emit a TRACE_BOOKMARK into the active .utrace at the current frame. The bookmark channel must be enabled in the trace (default start_trace channels include it). The text is dynamic via printf-style formatting, but the Format token itself is a TEXT() literal as required by the macro's static_assert.

params.name: text
params.description: The bookmark text. Becomes the bookmark label in UnrealInsights.

commands.returns: { bookmarked: bool, text: string, frame: int, note: string }

commands.name: assign_runtime_virtual_texture_to_landscape
