commands.description: Add a URuntimeVirtualTexture to the landscape's RuntimeVirtualTextures array (slot-index based) AND propagate it to every ALandscapeStreamingProxy of that landscape, because in World Partition the proxies are the actors that render. Every proxy is re-read after the write; `applied` and the envelope `success` are DERIVED from that re-read (proxies_with_rvt == proxies_total), never asserted.

params.name: landscape_name_or_label
params.description: Actor label/name of the target ALandscape

params.name: rvt_asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the RVT asset

params.name: slot_index
params.description: 0-based index into LandscapeProxy::RuntimeVirtualTextures (default 0)

params.name: propagate_to_proxies
params.description: Optional bool, default TRUE. Opt-out that writes the landscape actor alone. NOTE: with it false the proxies stay empty and nothing writes to the RVT cache, so `applied` will still report false (plus a `warning`) unless the proxies already carried the RVT -- the opt-out exists to reproduce that write, not to bless its result.

commands.returns: { applied, slot_index, rvt_asset_path, landscape, landscape_has_rvt, propagate_to_proxies, proxies_total, proxies_updated, proxies_with_rvt, proxies_missing: [string], proxies_missing_truncated: bool, proxy_enumeration, warning?, requested: {...} }

commands.name: create_runtime_virtual_texture
commands.description: Create a URuntimeVirtualTexture asset at directory_path/asset_name with the given material type, tile count and tile size (both exponents, clamped silently), and save it; the save result is not checked. Returns asset_path, tile_count, tile_size and size in texels. Then use create_runtime_virtual_texture_volume and assign_runtime_virtual_texture_to_landscape.

params.name: asset_name
params.description: Name of the new RVT asset (e.g. "RVT_Landscape"), without a folder.

params.name: directory_path
params.description: Content folder as a long package path (e.g. "/Game/VirtualTextures"), not a relative one (default /Game).

params.name: material_type
params.description: One of "BaseColor_Normal_Specular", "BaseColor_Normal_Roughness" or "WorldHeight", case-insensitive (default "BaseColor_Normal_Specular"); any other value, BaseColor_YCoCg included, is refused.

params.name: tile_count
params.description: Exponent of the size in tiles: 2^n tiles, clamped to 0..12 (default 8 = 256 tiles); a texel value such as 256 is clamped to 12.

params.name: tile_size
params.description: Exponent of the tile size: 2^(n+6) texels, clamped to 0..4 (default 2 = 256 texels).

params.name: continuous_update
params.description: When true, already mapped pages are re-rendered round-robin (bContinuousUpdate); default false.

commands.returns: { asset_path, material_type, tile_count, tile_size, size }

commands.name: create_runtime_virtual_texture_volume
commands.description: Spawn an ARuntimeVirtualTextureVolume (the RVT producer that registers the runtime virtual texture into the scene and defines its world-space region) bound to an RVT asset. Without a volume, assign_runtime_virtual_texture_to_landscape only wires the landscape as a writer -- nothing produces the RVT. Optionally fits the volume bounds to an actor (usually the landscape) in the same call. Headless-safe: spawns with a null VirtualTexture (no render-state) then binds a valid RVT. Idempotent: returns the existing volume if one already targets this RVT.

params.name: rvt_asset_path
params.description: Required. /Game path to the URuntimeVirtualTexture asset (create_runtime_virtual_texture).

params.name: bounds_align_actor
params.description: Optional. Name/label of an actor (usually the ALandscape) to fit the volume bounds to; runs the engine "Set Bounds" after binding.

params.name: volume_name
params.description: Optional. Actor label for the spawned volume.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x,y,z] spawn location (default [0,0,0]; overridden by the bounds-align when bounds_align_actor is given).

commands.returns: { volume_name, rvt_asset_path, bounds_aligned, bounds_align_actor?, already_existed }

commands.name: end_timing_region
commands.description: Close an open named region and return its duration in ms. Removes the region from the active set; subsequent end_timing_region with the same name returns an error.

params.name: name
params.description: Region identifier. Must match an open region.

commands.returns: { ended: bool, name: string, duration_ms: float, duration_s: float }

commands.name: get_fps_info
commands.description: Read a one-call frame-rate snapshot of the editor without changing anything: current_fps from the editor world's last tick (0 while paused or before the first tick, and the editor world even while PIE runs), target_fps (the engine max-FPS cap, or 60 when uncapped) and their difference, the engine-wide rolling averages GAverageFPS and GAverageMS, frame pacing (r.VSync, smoothing, max and min FPS), the r.ScreenPercentage in use, the live UObject count, process physical memory in bytes and MB, and the world's name and net mode. Use it for a quick is-it-fast-enough check; for per-thread times and a CPU/GPU bottleneck verdict use get_frame_timing, for a memory breakdown (scene, GPU, system) get_memory_usage, for quality presets get_scalability_levels, and for a profile over time start_trace. The values are instantaneous: an unfocused editor is throttled, so call it twice and compare. Errors only when there is no editor world.
commands.returns: { current_fps: float, target_fps: float, fps_variance: float, average_fps: float (GAverageFPS), average_ms: float (GAverageMS), engine_version: string, is_editor: bool, is_dedicated_server: bool, performance_settings: {vsync_enabled (r.VSync), smooth_frame_rate, max_fps (0 = uncapped), min_fps (lower bound of frame-rate smoothing; 0 without it)}, screen_percentage: float (r.ScreenPercentage within the scalability range), object_count: int, memory: { used_physical_bytes, peak_used_physical_bytes, available_physical_bytes, total_physical_bytes, used_physical_mb, peak_used_physical_mb, available_physical_mb }, world_name: string, net_mode: string }

commands.name: get_frame_timing
commands.description: Read the current frame's Game/Render/GPU/RHI thread times plus a CPU-vs-GPU bottleneck verdict with an actionable hint.
commands.returns: { frame_ms: float, game_thread_ms: float, render_thread_ms: float, rhi_thread_ms: float, game_thread_wait_ms: float, render_thread_wait_ms: float, gpu_ms: float, cpu_busy_ms: float, verdict: "GPU-bound"|"CPU-bound (game thread)"|"CPU-bound (render thread)"|"VSync/present bound"|"balanced"|"no-data", hint: string, null_rhi: bool, note: string } -- cpu_busy_ms is game + render + rhi; null_rhi is true with -nullrhi or in a commandlet, where the timings read 0 (verdict "no-data" when they all do) and note warns of it; otherwise note is empty.

commands.name: get_memory_usage
commands.description: Read a snapshot of memory use for the whole editor process without changing anything, in four blocks: process_memory (used, peak, available and total physical, used and peak virtual, in whole MB), scene_memory (a walk of every actor of the editor world, not a PIE world: actors, components, and on StaticMeshActors only the meshes, distinct materials and the distinct textures those materials use, plus every UTexture2D resident in memory process-wide), gpu_memory (dedicated, shared and total video memory, present only when the RHI reports them, and streaming and non-streaming texture memory) and system_info (platform, CPU brand, cores, threads). Use it to see where memory goes overall; for one asset's own size use get_asset_memory_usage, for byte-precise process memory next to the frame rate get_fps_info. The scene walk visits every actor, so it costs more on big levels. Errors only when there is no editor world.
commands.returns: { process_memory: {used_physical_memory_mb, peak_used_physical_memory_mb, available_physical_memory_mb, total_physical_memory_mb, used_virtual_memory_mb, peak_used_virtual_memory_mb}, scene_memory: {actor_count, component_count, static_mesh_count, material_count (distinct), material_slot_count, texture_count (distinct textures the scene's materials use), resident_texture_count (every UTexture2D in memory)}, gpu_memory: {gpu_memory_available, gpu_memory_status, rhi_name, dedicated_video_memory_mb?, shared_system_memory_mb?, total_graphics_memory_mb?, streaming_texture_memory_mb, non_streaming_texture_memory_mb}, system_info: {platform, cpu_brand, cpu_cores, cpu_threads} }

commands.name: get_runtime_virtual_texture_info
commands.description: Read a URuntimeVirtualTexture asset without changing it: material_type (full enum name, e.g. "ERuntimeVirtualTextureMaterialType::WorldHeight"), tile_count in tiles, tile_size and size in texels (not the exponents create_runtime_virtual_texture takes), and continuous_update.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Object or package path of the RVT asset (e.g. "/Game/VirtualTextures/RVT_Landscape").

commands.returns: { asset_path, material_type, tile_count, tile_size, size, continuous_update }

commands.name: get_trace_status
commands.description: Reports whether Unreal Insights tracing is available in this build, whether a trace is recording right now, and to which file or server. Read-only and instant: it starts and stops nothing. Call it before start_trace to see whether a trace is already running (for example one started with -trace on the command line, which start_trace would not replace), or after stop_trace to confirm the recording ended. list_traces lists the recorded .utrace files on disk, and list_timing_regions the open timers of start_timing_region, which are not traces.
commands.returns: { system_status: "not_available"|"available"|"tracing_to_file"|"tracing_to_server"|"tracing_to_secure_network"|"tracing_to_custom_relay"|"unknown", compile_time_enabled: bool, connected: bool, destination: string, elapsed_s: float } -- compile_time_enabled is false only when system_status is not_available (tracing compiled out, as in Shipping); destination is empty and elapsed_s 0 when not connected, and elapsed_s is also 0 for a trace start_trace did not start.

commands.name: list_timing_regions
commands.description: Read-side of start_timing_region: the named timing regions still OPEN in this bridge instance, each with how long it has been running. Use it to spot a region you forgot to close, or to read an elapsed time without ending the region. Entries disappear when end_timing_region closes them, one name at a time; the state is per bridge instance and does not survive a restart.
commands.returns: { total, regions:[{ name, started_at_s, elapsed_s }] }

commands.name: list_traces
commands.description: Enumerate .utrace files in <ProjectDir>/Saved/Profiling/, returning their path, size and modification time.
commands.returns: { directory: string, count: int, traces: [{ path, name, size_bytes, modified_iso }] } -- directory is the resolved profiling folder; only its own files are listed, not subfolders.

commands.name: set_runtime_virtual_texture_volume_bounds
commands.description: Fit an existing ARuntimeVirtualTextureVolume's bounds to an actor -- the engine "Set Bounds" button (RuntimeVirtualTexture::SetBounds). Sets the volume's BoundsAlignActor and recomputes its transform to cover that actor (a landscape uses its complete bounds) plus any primitives writing to the volume's RVT. The volume must already have its RVT bound (create_runtime_virtual_texture_volume). Optional landscape texel-snap + bounds expansion.

params.name: volume_name
params.description: Required. Actor name/label of the ARuntimeVirtualTextureVolume.

params.name: bounds_align_actor
params.description: Required. Name/label of the actor (usually the ALandscape) to fit the bounds to.

params.name: snap_to_landscape
params.description: Optional bool. Snap virtual-texture texels to landscape vertices (only meaningful when the align actor is a landscape).

params.name: expand_bounds
params.description: Optional float >= 0. Amount to expand the computed bounds.

commands.returns: { volume_name, bounds_align_actor, snap_to_landscape, expand_bounds, applied }

commands.name: start_timing_region
commands.description: Starts a named wall-clock timer in this editor session, to measure how long a stretch of work (several tool calls, a PIE run) takes; end_timing_region with the same name stops it and returns the elapsed time in ms. It needs no Insights trace and writes nothing to a trace or to disk: the start time is kept in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts. Idempotent: a name that is already open keeps its original start time and returns already_started true with started false. list_timing_regions shows the open timers; for engine-level profiling use start_trace with add_trace_bookmark instead.

params.name: name
params.description: Required timer name, any non-empty string (e.g. "import_pass"); pass the same name to end_timing_region (names match case-insensitively).

commands.returns: { started: bool, already_started: bool, name: string, started_at_s: float, note?: string } -- started_at_s is the editor's platform clock in seconds; note only when the region was already open

commands.name: start_trace
commands.description: Starts recording an Unreal Insights trace of this editor process to a new .utrace file, for profiling CPU, GPU and frame timing with the chosen channels. Idempotent: while any trace is active, including one started with -trace on the command line, it starts nothing and returns already_tracing true with the current destination; call stop_trace first for a new recording. The engine will not write over an existing file: an output_path that already exists makes the call fail with nothing started. Only the trace file is written; assets and levels are untouched. Flow: start_trace, reproduce the problem, mark moments with add_trace_bookmark, stop_trace to flush, list_traces to find the file; get_trace_status tells whether a trace is running. For a quick reading without a file use get_frame_timing or get_fps_info.

params.name: channels
params.description: Comma-separated Insights channels to enable (default "cpu,frame,bookmark"; others: gpu, region, memtag, counters, log, screenshot), e.g. "cpu,gpu,frame,bookmark".

params.name: output_path
params.description: Path of the .utrace file to create, absolute (e.g. "D:/Traces/run1.utrace") or relative to <ProjectDir>/Saved/Profiling; another extension is changed to .utrace and the folder is created. Default <ProjectDir>/Saved/Profiling/MCP_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.utrace.

commands.returns: { tracing: bool, already_tracing: bool, destination: string, channels?: string, started_at_s?: number, connection_type?: string, elapsed_s?: number, note: string } -- channels and started_at_s for a new trace; connection_type (file, server, custom_relay...) and elapsed_s when a trace was already active

commands.name: stop_trace
commands.description: Stop the active Unreal Insights trace and return its destination, duration and file size. Idempotent — calling stop_trace when no trace is active returns was_tracing:false with a note instead of failing.
commands.returns: { stopped: bool, was_tracing: bool, destination?: string, duration_s?: float, size_bytes?: int, note: string } -- with no trace running only stopped:false, was_tracing:false and note; when the engine's Stop() refuses because the trace is already stopping, stopped is false and size_bytes is absent; after a stop, note says to open the .utrace in Unreal Insights. duration_s is 0 for a trace start_trace did not start.

commands.name: unassign_runtime_virtual_texture_from_landscape
commands.description: Inverse of assign_runtime_virtual_texture_to_landscape: clears ONE slot of a landscape's RuntimeVirtualTextures array, breaking the binding without leaving a dangling entry behind. It unbinds only -- the RVT asset itself survives (delete_asset with expected_class "RuntimeVirtualTexture" destroys that). Reports the asset path that was in the slot, so the operation is reversible.

params.name: landscape_name
params.description: Actor name (or label) of the ALandscape actor (omit for first landscape in world)

params.name: slot_index
params.description: 0-based index to clear (default 0)

commands.returns: { cleared, slot_index, previous_rvt_asset_path?, landscape }

commands.name: add_field_node
commands.description: Author a field command node into a UFieldSystem and persist it.  Builds a transient authoring field U-node (selected by node_type), resolves the physics target to an EFieldPhysicsType, constructs the runtime FFieldSystemCommand via FFieldObjectCommands::CreateFieldCommand, appends it to UFieldSystem.Commands, and saves the asset.  node_type accepts "RadialFalloff", "PlaneFalloff", "BoxFalloff", "WaveScalar", "UniformScalar", "NoiseField", "UniformInteger", "RadialIntMask", "UniformVector", "RadialVector", "RotatedRadialVector", "RandomVector". Vector nodes pair with vector targets (LinearVelocity/LinearForce); scalar with strain/threshold; integer with state (DynamicState).  target is a physics target attribute name like "LinearVelocity", "ExternalClusterStrain", "DynamicState".  falloff_type accepts "Inverse", "Squared", "Logarithmic", or "None". Defaults to "Linear".

params.name: field_system_path
params.description: Asset path of the UFieldSystem (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/FS_Example")

params.name: node_type
params.description: One of "RadialFalloff", "PlaneFalloff", "BoxFalloff", "WaveScalar", "UniformScalar", "NoiseField", "UniformInteger", "RadialIntMask", "UniformVector", "RadialVector", "RotatedRadialVector", "RandomVector". RotatedRadialVector needs UE 5.8.

params.name: target
params.description: Physics target attribute name, e.g. "LinearForce", "LinearVelocity", "ExternalClusterStrain", "DynamicState"

params.name: magnitude
params.description: Optional scalar magnitude; defaults to 1.0

params.name: radius
params.description: Optional falloff / mask radius; defaults to 100.0

params.name: position
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world / center position

params.name: direction
params.description: Optional [x, y, z]; uniform-vector direction, plane normal (PlaneFalloff), or rotation axis (RotatedRadialVector)

params.name: falloff_type
params.description: Optional EFieldFalloffType; defaults to "Linear"

params.name: min_range
params.description: Optional remap lower bound for falloff/noise nodes; defaults to 0.0

params.name: max_range
params.description: Optional remap upper bound for falloff/noise nodes; defaults to 1.0

params.name: default_value
params.description: Optional out-of-range value for falloff nodes; defaults to 0.0

params.name: distance
params.description: Optional plane distance limit for PlaneFalloff; defaults to 0.0

params.name: wavelength
params.description: Optional WaveScalar wavelength; defaults to 10000.0

params.name: period
params.description: Optional WaveScalar period; defaults to 1.0

params.name: wave_function
params.description: Optional WaveScalar function "Cosine", "Gaussian", "Falloff", "Decay"; defaults to "Cosine"

params.name: interior_value
params.description: Optional RadialIntMask interior integer; defaults to 1

params.name: exterior_value
params.description: Optional RadialIntMask exterior integer; defaults to 0

params.name: mask_condition
params.description: Optional RadialIntMask condition "Always", "MergeInterior", "MergeExterior"; defaults to "Always"

params.name: angle
params.description: Optional RotatedRadialVector rotation angle in degrees; defaults to 0.0. Needs UE 5.8.

commands.returns: { field_system_path: string, node_type: string, target: string, physics_type_name: string, command_count: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_geometry_collection_source
commands.description: Append an additional StaticMesh source to an existing geometry collection, then save it. Succeeds only when the package reaches disk; a failed save leaves the change in memory only (saved false, save_error).

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UGeometryCollection

params.name: source_mesh_path
params.description: Asset path to the UStaticMesh to append

params.name: transform
params.description: Optional {location, rotation, scale} for the source mesh placement

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, source_mesh_path: string, num_sources: int, num_materials: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: add_impulse_to_actor
commands.description: Kick a physics body: apply an impulse (or, with vel_change, a mass-independent velocity change) to an actor's primitive component, optionally at a world location for torque via AddImpulseAtLocation, or on a named skeletal bone. Acts on the EDITOR world, where nothing is simulating unless the component has simulate_physics on -- so on a resting editor actor this is a no-op that still reports applied:true; verify with a transform re-read, and for gameplay-time forces drive it in PIE.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor (required)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional primitive component name (defaults to the actor's RootComponent)

params.name: impulse
params.description: [x, y, z] impulse vector in world units (required)

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location for AddImpulseAtLocation (omit to use AddImpulse)

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Optional skeletal bone name to apply the impulse to

params.name: vel_change
params.description: Optional; if true, impulse is treated as a velocity change (mass-independent)

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, applied: bool }

commands.name: add_instanced_static_mesh_component
commands.description: Attach an InstancedStaticMeshComponent (ISM) with an optional static mesh to a placed editor-world actor (name or label), in one undo step, to scatter copies of one mesh through it with add_instanced_static_mesh_instance. Over add_component_to_actor it only saves the separate mesh write, and it is idempotent: an existing ISM (a HISM counts) is returned with already_existed=true and its mesh left as it is (static_mesh in the reply says which). Without static_mesh_path the new ISM has no mesh; a path that does not load is an error and nothing is added. Not saved (save_level). The working alternative to the foliage scatter tools, which crash the editor in this build.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor (required)

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Optional /Game/... path to a UStaticMesh asset; without it the ISM has no mesh. A path that does not load is an error and nothing is added; on an existing ISM it is not applied.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, num_instances: int, static_mesh: string (the ISM's mesh path, empty when none), already_existed: bool }

commands.name: add_instanced_static_mesh_instance
commands.description: Place one more instance of an InstancedStaticMeshComponent's mesh at a world transform -- the cheap way to scatter many copies of a mesh (rocks, props, vegetation) without spawning an actor each. Pair it with add_instanced_static_mesh_component to create the component first. Prefer this route over the foliage tools: scatter_foliage_in_box and add_foliage_instances both CRASH the editor in this build, and an ISM is the same code path a foliage actor and PCG use anyway.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the actor carrying the ISM component (required)

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional ISM component name (defaults to the first one on the actor)

params.name: location
params.description: [x, y, z] world-space translation (required)

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation (defaults to zero)

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] scale (defaults to [1,1,1])

params.name: world_space
params.description: Optional; if true, transform is interpreted in world space (default true)

commands.returns: { instance_index: int, num_instances: int }

commands.name: add_physics_asset_body
commands.description: Add a body for one bone to a UPhysicsAsset (FPhysicsAssetUtils::CreateNewBody) with ONE collision primitive, in one undo step, then save the asset. Without radius, length or extent the primitive is FITTED to the preview mesh's vertices weighted to that bone, as the Physics Asset editor's Add Body does (FPhysicsAssetUtils::CreateCollisionsFromBones): a capsule, sphere, box or convex hull. With any of them it is a primitive of that size centred on the bone instead -- a capsule (radius, length), a sphere (radius) or a box (extent [x,y,z]); a convex hull is fitted only, so it refuses sizes. A bone with no vertices weighted to it cannot be fitted: that is an error naming the explicit-size way, and nothing is kept; so is a convex without a preview mesh. With no preview mesh and no sizes the primitive gets the default sizes (fitted=false, and a note says so). No constraint is made: joint it with add_physics_asset_constraint, tune it with set_physics_body_properties. A bone that already has a body is a success with already_existed=true and nothing changed or saved; a bone the preview mesh's skeleton does not have is an error. Inverse: remove_physics_asset_body; read: get_physics_asset_info. A failed save makes success false with save_error.

params.name: physics_asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the UPhysicsAsset.

params.name: bone_name
params.description: Bone the body follows (one body per bone; get_physics_asset_info lists skeleton_bones).

params.name: primitive
params.description: "capsule" (default), "sphere", "box" or "convex" (fitted only).

params.name: radius
params.description: Capsule or sphere radius in cm; giving it makes an explicit-size primitive instead of a fitted one (default 10 when another size is given).

params.name: length
params.description: Capsule length in cm between the two sphere centres; giving it makes an explicit-size primitive (default 20).

params.name: extent
params.description: Box size [x, y, z] in cm; giving it makes an explicit-size primitive (default [20, 20, 20]).

commands.returns: { physics_asset_path: string, bone_name: string, body_index: int, primitive: string, fitted: bool, added: bool, already_existed: bool, primitive_count: int, body_count: int, bone_in_skeleton: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: add_physics_asset_constraint
commands.description: Author a ragdoll constraint (joint) inside a UPhysicsAsset between two bones.  Creates a UPhysicsConstraintTemplate via FPhysicsAssetUtils::CreateNewConstraint (idempotent by name — re-using a name returns the existing joint), sets the child/parent bones and a Limited swing+twist cone, and snaps the joint frames to the bones' default relative transform when BOTH bones exist in the preview-mesh skeleton (skipped honestly otherwise, since the engine fatal-checks an unknown bone).  Refine motions/limits afterwards with set_physics_asset_constraint_limits.

params.name: physics_asset_path
params.description: /Game path to the UPhysicsAsset to add the constraint to.

params.name: child_bone
params.description: Name of the child bone/body (ConstraintBone1, the moving end).

params.name: parent_bone
params.description: Name of the parent bone/body (ConstraintBone2, the anchor end).

params.name: constraint_name
params.description: Optional joint name (defaults to child_bone); re-using an existing name is idempotent (no duplicate).

commands.returns: { physics_asset_path: string, constraint_name: string, constraint_index: int, child_bone: string, parent_bone: string, already_existed: bool, child_in_skeleton: bool, parent_in_skeleton: bool, child_body_index: int, parent_body_index: int, frames_snapped: bool, collision_disabled: bool, constraint_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string, constraint: object }

commands.name: add_static_mesh_simple_collision
commands.description: Appends one simple collision element to a UStaticMesh and saves the mesh: a primitive (Box, Sphere or Capsule) sized to the mesh bounds, or a K-DOP hull (NDOP10_X / NDOP10_Y / NDOP10_Z bevel the four edges along that axis, NDOP18 every edge, NDOP26 every edge and corner) fitted around the LOD0 vertices as the Static Mesh Editor's Add K-DOP action does. A mesh outside /Game is first copied to dest_path under /Game, reusing a copy already there (duplicated: this call created it). An unknown shape is an error naming the accepted ones, checked before any copy. Not idempotent: each call adds one more element, existing collision is kept (clear it with remove_static_mesh_collision; convex decomposition is set_static_mesh_convex_collision). A K-DOP subsystem failure, as under PIE, makes success false with collision_changed and the new copy's saved; a failed save makes success false with save_error.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Path to the source UStaticMesh.

params.name: dest_path
params.description: Path under /Game to copy a mesh that is not under /Game into before editing (required then; an existing mesh there is reused and edited)

params.name: shape
params.description: Box (default), Sphere, Capsule, NDOP10_X, NDOP10_Y, NDOP10_Z, NDOP18 or NDOP26, case-insensitive. Any other value is refused.

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, shape, box_count, sphere_count, capsule_count, element_count, collision_added, duplicated_to_game, duplicated, added_index (K-DOP shapes), simple_collision_count (K-DOP shapes), saved, save_error?, collision_changed? }

commands.name: cluster_geometry_collection
commands.description: Runs auto-clustering on all transforms of a UGeometryCollection asset, targeting site_count clusters ("Small" doubles it, "Large" halves it, any other method keeps it) with connectivity enforced, then saves it. Returns the cluster count used and the transform counts before and after; the call fails when no cluster was added (a collection that is not fractured into several pieces has nothing to group) or when the save fails.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UGeometryCollection

params.name: cluster_size_method
params.description: Small, Medium, or Large, default Medium

params.name: site_count
params.description: Target cluster count before cluster_size_method scales it, minimum 1, default 10

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, cluster_size_method: string, site_count: int, num_transforms_before: int, num_transforms_after: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: compute_geometry_collection_proximity
commands.description: Rebuilds the proximity (adjacency) graph of a UGeometryCollection asset in place and saves it; undoable. Returns proximity_pairs (unordered pairs of neighboring pieces, from a precise proximity pass), transform_count, success and saved; fails when the save fails. Afterwards get_geometry_collection_hierarchy reports proximity_computed true.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the UGeometryCollection

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, proximity_pairs: int, transform_count: int, success: bool, saved: bool }

commands.name: create_field_system_asset
commands.description: Create a UFieldSystem asset -- an empty list of Chaos field commands -- at package_path/field_system_name (default folder /Game/MCP), register it with the Asset Registry and save it; no undo step. Idempotent: a field system already at that path is loaded and returned unchanged in the same shape, with saved=false and a message, nothing saved; command_count tells how many commands it already holds. An invalid package name, or a name taken by an asset of another class, is an error; a failed save of the new asset gives success false with saved=false and save_error. field_system_path is the package path (e.g. /Game/MCP/FS_Example). Add commands with add_field_node, read them with get_field_system_info, place the asset in the level with spawn_actor.

params.name: field_system_name
params.description: Asset name (e.g. "FS_Example")

params.name: package_path
params.description: Optional content folder; defaults to /Game/MCP

commands.returns: { field_system_path: string, field_system_name: string, command_count: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, message?: string }

commands.name: create_geometry_collection
commands.description: Creates a UGeometryCollection asset at package_path/name, optionally filled from one StaticMesh, and saves it. An existing collection there is RESET first (all geometry and sources discarded; created false, rebuilt true). A source_mesh_path that does not load as a StaticMesh is an error, checked before anything is touched. Succeeds only when the package reaches disk; a failed save leaves the collection in memory only (saved false, save_error).

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder for the asset, e.g. /Game/Chaos/Collections; a path without a leading slash is placed under /Game/

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the geometry collection asset, e.g. GC_Wall

params.name: source_mesh_path
params.description: Optional StaticMesh to convert and append, e.g. /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube

commands.name: create_physics_asset
commands.description: Create a UPhysicsAsset at package_path/name by generating bodies and constraints from a skeletal mesh with the engine's default settings (FPhysicsAssetUtils::CreateFromSkeletalMesh), set that mesh as its preview mesh and save it, with no undo transaction; the mesh itself is not pointed at the new asset (assign_skeletal_mesh_physics_asset does that). Idempotent: a physics asset already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, nothing generated or saved and skeletal_mesh_path not read, while another asset class there is an error before any mesh loads. A generation failure is not an error: the asset is still saved, with bodies_generated=false and generation_message. A failed save, refused while PIE runs, makes success false with save_error. Inspect it with get_physics_asset_info; tune bodies with set_physics_body_properties and joints with add_physics_asset_constraint.

params.name: name

commands.name: cut_geometry_collection_with_planes
commands.description: Cut every piece of a UGeometryCollection asset with num_planes flat planes placed at random (seeded) inside its bounds, with no noise on the cut surfaces, in one undo step, then save it. The cut pieces stay in the hierarchy as parents of the new ones, so each call adds pieces on top of the earlier ones; it is not idempotent. Choose it for a few long straight cuts (planks, slabs); for a regular grid of cuts use slice_geometry_collection, for organic Voronoi shards fracture_geometry_collection, and to group pieces afterwards cluster_geometry_collection. Make the collection first with create_geometry_collection; check the result with get_geometry_collection_hierarchy or get_geometry_collection_info. new_fracture_count is the number of transforms the cut added; the call fails when it added none (an empty collection, or planes that miss every piece) even though the asset is still saved, and when the save fails (for example while PIE runs). A path that does not load as a geometry collection is an error and nothing changes.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Asset path of the UGeometryCollection, e.g. "/Game/Destruction/GC_Wall", as create_geometry_collection returns it (asset_path).

params.name: num_planes
params.description: Number of random cutting planes, an integer of at least 1 (smaller values become 1), default 3.

params.name: random_seed
params.description: Integer seed for plane placement, default 1337; the same seed on the same collection gives the same planes.

params.name: grout
params.description: Width of the gap left between cut pieces, in cm, e.g. 0.5 (default 0, no gap).

params.name: split_islands
params.description: true (default) turns every disconnected part of a cut piece into its own piece; false keeps them together.

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, num_planes: int, new_fracture_count: int, transform_count: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: find_scene_overlaps
commands.description: Sphere / box / capsule overlap query against the world: "what is inside this volume?", returning one JSON entry per overlapping actor+component instead of export-text, so no Python is needed to parse it. Use it over raycast_scene when the question is proximity/containment rather than line of sight -- e.g. is the pawn actually inside a water body's real collision, is anything blocking a build spot. Accepts the same `world` selector (editor / server / client / pie:N): an editor-world query does NOT see World-Partition/OFPA actor collision, so pass a live PIE world, and in co-op say WHICH one or an empty result is uninterpretable.

params.name: half_height

params.name: trace_channel

params.name: world

commands.returns: { overlaps: [{actor_path, actor_name, component_name, item_index, blocking}], count: int, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: fracture_geometry_collection
commands.description: Applies Voronoi fracturing to all transforms of a UGeometryCollection asset, using num_sites random sites in its bounds, then saves it. num_fractures is the number of new pieces, measured as the transforms the fracture added; the call fails when it added none (an empty collection, or a chance_to_fracture that skipped every piece) or when the save fails. Re-fracturing grows a collection geometrically and can stall the editor; fracture a fresh one from create_geometry_collection.

params.name: geometry_collection_path
params.description: Full asset path to the UGeometryCollection

params.name: num_sites
params.description: Number of random Voronoi sites to generate, minimum 1, default 20

params.name: random_seed
params.description: Seed for the random site positions and the per-transform fracture chance, default 0

params.name: chance_to_fracture
params.description: Chance from 0 to 1 that each selected transform is fractured, default 1

params.name: grout
params.description: Width of the gap left between cut pieces, in cm (default 0)

params.name: split_islands
params.description: Optional, split resulting islands, default false

commands.returns: { geometry_collection_path: string, num_fractures: int, transform_count: int, num_sites: int, random_seed: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }

commands.name: get_actor_bounds
commands.description: Measure how BIG an actor really is: its aggregate world-space bounding box (origin, half-extent, min, max) in the EDITOR world. The size oracle for placement and footprint questions, and the honest test for "did that volume/brush actually get built" -- a spawned volume whose extent comes back (0,0,0) has no geometry no matter what the spawning tool reported. Its `components` filter is the reason to prefer it over reading a component property: "all" (default, AActor::GetActorBounds -- inflated by interaction/trigger shapes), "colliding" (only collision-enabled components) or "mesh"/"rendered" (UMeshComponent geometry ONLY, so trigger spheres/boxes are excluded and the box hugs what you actually see). Editor world only -- for a PIE-world footprint use find_scene_overlaps/raycast_scene with a `world` selector.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor name or editor label

params.name: components
params.description: Which components contribute: "all" (default; everything, trigger shapes included) | "colliding" (collision-enabled only) | "mesh" | "rendered" (UMeshComponent geometry only)

params.name: include_child_actors
params.description: Include child-actor components' bounds. Defaults to false.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, components: string, valid: bool, component_count: int, origin: {x,y,z}, extent: {x,y,z}, min: {x,y,z}, max: {x,y,z} } -- valid=false with a zero extent means no contributing geometry was found

commands.name: get_collision_info
commands.description: Read ONE placed primitive component's collision setup and physics state: collision enabled mode, per-channel responses (WorldStatic / WorldDynamic / Pawn / PhysicsBody), overlap and hit event flags, simulate-physics, mobility, and the physical material with its friction / restitution / density. The tool to answer "why does this not block / not overlap" without writing Python. Two limits from the code: it searches by component NAME across the world's actors but only inspects each actor's FIRST primitive component, so a secondary component (a second collider, a trigger next to a mesh) reports "not found" even though it exists; and it reads the component's live responses, NOT the profile definition -- for the profile itself use get_collision_profile (which is blind to +EditProfiles overrides), and prove a channel really blocks with raycast_scene.

params.name: component_name

commands.name: get_field_system_info

A path that does not load as a physics asset is an error. Edit bodies with set_physics_body_properties, joints with add_physics_asset_constraint, set_physics_asset_constraint_limits or set_physics_asset_constraint_drives; a world constraint actor is get_physics_constraint_info. Read-only complement of spawn_physics_constraint / set_physics_constraint_limits / set_physics_constraint_drives; returns the serialized template, not live simulation state (no motor torque/broken/force values, which are 0 outside PIE).

commands.name: get_physics_settings
commands.description: One-shot physics census of the current world: UPhysicsSettings substepping/delta-time values, world gravity_z, and a walk of every actor counting collision-enabled vs disabled, simulating bodies, mobility split and mass totals, plus a heuristic quality label and a recommendations list. Use it for a broad "what is the physics state of this level" sweep instead of hand-writing the actor loop in Python; for ONE component's collision use get_collision_info, and to change gravity use set_world_gravity (this world) or set_project_settings_value (the project default). Read the numbers with three caveats visible in the code: physics_engine is a hardcoded "PhysX" literal (UE5 actually runs Chaos), the walk takes only the FIRST primitive component per actor so multi-component actors are undercounted, and generate_hit_events is always 0 (never populated).

commands.name: get_scene_bounds
commands.description: How big is the LEVEL: one world-space bounding box aggregated over every level-bounds-relevant actor in the editor world (persistent level plus any loaded streamed levels), or over an explicit subset if you pass actor_names. Use it for map extents / where-is-everything questions; use get_actor_bounds for a single actor. Note it only sees LOADED actors, so on a World-Partition map an unloaded region contributes nothing and the box reads smaller than the map.

params.description: Optional subset of actor names/labels; omit for every loaded actor in the world

commands.name: raycast_scene
commands.description: Line trace / raycast the world and get a REAL JSON hit result -- what actor and component was hit, impact point, normal and distance -- instead of the UE export-text FHitResult blob that call_function on a line-trace UFUNCTION returns, so no Python parsing is needed. Accepts a `world` selector (editor / server / client / pie:N), which matters twice: an EDITOR-world trace does not hit World-Partition/OFPA actor collision (only cooked in the PIE physics scene) and reads as a clean miss, and in co-op a miss on the client world looks identical to a missing collider -- pass "server" or "pie:N" so a hit:false is interpretable. Also the honest way to prove a custom collision CHANNEL blocks: trace the same segment on a known-good channel (Visibility) and on the new one and compare actor/component/Z/distance, because get_collision_profile does not see +EditProfiles overrides.

params.name: end
params.description: World-space [x, y, z] trace end

params.name: trace_channel
params.description: Collision channel, canonical ("ECC_Visibility") or friendly ("Visibility", "Camera", or a custom channel name). Defaults to "Visibility". A channel created THIS session is not in the live profile table yet -- restart the editor before trusting a trace on it.

params.name: trace_complex
params.description: Test against complex (per-poly) collision instead of simple. Defaults to false.

params.name: ignore_actors
params.description: Actor names/labels to exclude from the trace.

params.name: return_physical_material
params.description: Populate physical_material in the result. Defaults to false.

params.name: world
params.description: Which world to trace: absent/"editor" (default) | "server" (the PIE world with authority) | "client" | "pie:N" | "pie" (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | "game" (alias of "pie"). Editor-world traces do NOT hit World-Partition/OFPA actors, so pass a live world to verify obstacle collision; with 2+ PIE instances prefer "server"/"pie:N".

A bone with no body, or an index out of range, is an honest no-op (removed=false, already_absent=true, nothing saved). A failed save makes success false with save_error. params.description: /Game path to the UPhysicsAsset.

Idempotent: an already-absent constraint returns removed:false/already_absent:true with success (no mutation, no save).

commands.description: Clear ALL simple/convex collision primitives from a UStaticMesh's BodySetup (the 'clear' half of the collision CRUD).  Calls UBodySetup::RemoveSimpleCollision (InvalidatePhysicsData + AggGeom.EmptyElements), rebuilds the physics meshes and saves; a failed save makes success false with save_error.  Reuses the same duplicate-first logic as add_static_mesh_simple_collision so a read-only /Engine source is copied into dest_path first (an existing copy there is reused); duplicated is true when this call created that copy.  Idempotent: clearing an already-empty BodySetup (or a mesh with no BodySetup) is a no-op reported via already_empty:true, where saved reports only the save of a copy this call created and is false, with nothing saved, when there is none.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Path to the source UStaticMesh.

params.name: dest_path
params.description: /Game path to duplicate a read-only /Engine source mesh into first (required only when the source is not under /Game).

commands.name: set_actor_physical_material
commands.description: Override the physical material (friction, restitution, surface type) of one placed actor's collision body in the editor world, through UPrimitiveComponent::SetPhysMaterialOverride on a single component: the StaticMeshComponent of a StaticMeshActor, otherwise the actor's first primitive component. One undo step; the level is marked dirty but not saved (save_level), and neither the mesh asset nor other actors change. verified is true when the override read back from the component's body is that material. Create the material with create_physical_material; for another component of the actor set its BodyInstance through set_component_property; read the actor's components with get_actor_components. Idempotent: the same material again changes nothing new. There is no way to clear the override here. Over add_component_to_actor it assigns the graph via UPCGComponent::SetGraph, which set_properties cannot (the graph lives in a read-only GraphInstance). Idempotent: an actor that already has one (an APCGVolume does) gets it back, graph re-assigned. It generates within the actor's BOUNDS, so a volume with no brush geometry yields zero instances with no error -- check get_actor_bounds first. Then generate_pcg_component and get_pcg_component_info. Not saved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Display label or internal name of the target editor-world actor (required)

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Optional /Game/... path of a UPCGGraph to assign to the component

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, already_existed, graph_path, graph_assigned }

commands.name: add_pcg_graph_parameter
commands.description: Expose a tunable on a PCG graph (bool / int / float / double / string) so density, radius or a toggle can be driven from outside instead of being welded into a node. Idempotent (already_existed when the name is taken). Only worth doing on graphs you own -- adding one to a library graph means editing that asset. Set a value with set_pcg_graph_parameter and list them with get_pcg_graph_parameters; inverse: remove_pcg_graph_parameter.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UPCGGraph (required)

params.name: name
params.description: Parameter name (required)

params.name: type
params.description: "bool" | "int" | "float" | "double" | "string" (required)

commands.returns: { pcg_graph_path, name, type, added, already_existed, parameter_count }

commands.name: add_pcg_node
commands.description: Add one unconnected node of a PCG settings class (the node type: surface sampler, static mesh spawner, filter...) with its default settings to a PCG graph asset, in one undo step, then save the graph. Each call adds another node, so a repeat call makes a duplicate. Get valid node_type names from list_pcg_node_types; wire the new node with connect_pcg_nodes using the node_name it returns, set its fields with set_pcg_node_properties, and check the graph with get_pcg_graph_info. To embed a whole graph use add_pcg_subgraph_node instead; inverse: remove_pcg_node; make the graph first with create_pcg_graph. A graph that does not load, or a node_type that is not a concrete PCG settings class, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false, with saved false, save_error and the node only in memory.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example"), as create_pcg_graph returns it.

params.name: node_type
params.description: A concrete UPCGSettings subclass, as list_pcg_node_types returns it (types[].name or types[].path): e.g. "PCGSurfaceSamplerSettings", "PCGStaticMeshSpawnerSettings", or "/Script/PCG.PCGSurfaceSamplerSettings"; the U prefix is optional.

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_title: string, node_name: string, settings_class: string, node_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_pcg_subgraph_node
commands.description: Embed one PCG graph inside another as a Subgraph node -- how you reuse a scatter or filter recipe across biomes instead of duplicating nodes, and how you consume a library graph without editing it. Check first with get_pcg_graph_info that the target graph actually USES its input node (a graph with no edges from its default input cannot be fed filtered data and will ignore whatever you wire in), and with get_pcg_graph_parameters whether it exposes anything tunable.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the host UPCGGraph (required)

params.name: subgraph_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UPCGGraph to embed as a subgraph (required)

commands.returns: { graph_name, asset_path, node_name, node_title, subgraph_path, subgraph_set, node_count, saved }

commands.name: cleanup_pcg_component
commands.description: Wipe a PCG component's generated output synchronously -- and the step you must not skip after editing a graph: a plain generate_pcg_component with force reuses the CACHED result, so the world keeps the STALE meshes and settings while every flag reads generated:true. Call this with remove_components=true FIRST, then generate, then verify by re-reading the actor's spawned components rather than the generated flag. Also the way to clear procedural content before moving or resizing the volume.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor holding the UPCGComponent (required)

params.name: remove_components
params.description: Optional; also remove spawned managed components (default false)

commands.returns: { actor_name, cleaned, generated }

commands.name: connect_pcg_nodes
commands.description: Connects two PCG nodes by adding a directed edge from an output pin to an input pin.  Node names come from get_pcg_graph_info; the implicit graph endpoints are addressable as "Input"/"Output". from_pin/to_pin default to the node's "Out"/"In" pin (else its first pin); the resolved labels are echoed in the response. Idempotent: an existing edge reports already_connected without error. The graph is re-saved after a new edge is added.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

params.name: from_node
params.description: Upstream node: a node_name from get_pcg_graph_info, or the token "Input" for the graph's implicit input node.

params.name: to_node
params.description: Downstream node: a node_name, or the token "Output" for the graph's implicit output node.

params.name: from_pin
params.description: Optional output-pin label on from_node (default the node's "Out" pin, else its first output pin).

params.name: to_pin
params.description: Optional input-pin label on to_node (default the node's "In" pin, else its first input pin).

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, from_node: string, from_pin: string, to_node: string, to_pin: string, already_connected: bool, connected: bool, edge_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: create_pcg_graph
commands.description: Create an empty UPCGGraph asset at package_path/name and save it, or return the UPCGGraph already there unchanged (created=false, already_exists=true, nothing saved), so repeat calls are idempotent. A fresh graph holds only its implicit Input and Output nodes, which node_count leaves out (0). Another asset class at that path, or an invalid path, is an error; a failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error. No undo step is recorded. Requires the PCG plugin. Next: add nodes with add_pcg_node (types from list_pcg_node_types), wire them with connect_pcg_nodes, expose tunables with add_pcg_graph_parameter, read back with get_pcg_graph_info, and use it in the level through spawn_box_volume or add_pcg_component.

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the PCG Graph asset to create; the object path becomes package_path/name.name.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination /Game folder (default /Game/PCG); a trailing slash is ignored.

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, created: bool, already_exists?: bool, node_count: int, saved?: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: disconnect_pcg_nodes
commands.description: Remove the one directed edge from an output pin of one node to an input pin of another in a PCG graph asset, in one undo step, then save the graph; both nodes and every other edge stay. Pin labels default to the node's "Out" or "In" pin (else its first pin), and the labels used are echoed back. Inverse of connect_pcg_nodes; to drop a node with all its edges use remove_pcg_node; to see nodes, pins and edges first use get_pcg_graph_info. Components already generated from the graph keep their old output until cleanup_pcg_component and generate_pcg_component run. Idempotent: when no such edge exists nothing is changed or saved and already_disconnected is true; disconnected is read back after the call. A graph, node or pin that cannot be resolved is an error before anything changes. A failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved false and save_error, the edge gone only in memory.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph, e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example", as create_pcg_graph returns it.

params.name: from_node
params.description: Upstream node name as get_pcg_graph_info lists it (node_name, case-insensitive), or the token "Input" for the graph's input node.

params.name: to_node
params.description: Downstream node name as get_pcg_graph_info lists it (node_name, case-insensitive), or the token "Output" for the graph's output node.

params.name: from_pin
params.description: Optional output-pin label on from_node (default the node's "Out" pin, else its first output pin).

params.name: to_pin
params.description: Optional input-pin label on to_node (default the node's "In" pin, else its first input pin).

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, from_node: string, from_pin: string, to_node: string, to_pin: string, already_disconnected: bool, removed: bool, disconnected: bool, edge_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: generate_pcg_component
commands.description: Triggers PCG generation on an actor's UPCGComponent. Generation is ASYNCHRONOUS (scheduled on the PCG subsystem, resolved over subsequent editor ticks) — this returns the scheduled task id, NOT a finished result. Poll get_pcg_component_info / get_pcg_generated_data for completion (honest).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor holding the UPCGComponent (required)

params.name: force
params.description: Optional; force regeneration even if already generated (default true)

commands.returns: { actor_name, scheduled, task_id, is_generating, generated, note }

commands.name: get_pcg_component_info
commands.description: Read an actor's PCG component: which graph it runs, its seed, whether it is generating or already generated, activated, partitioned, and its generation trigger. Read-only. Use it to find which graph is driving an actor and to confirm a seed for deterministic scatter -- but NOT as proof the world matches the graph: generated:true is satisfied by a cached result, so after editing a graph the flag says done while the spawned meshes are stale. The real check is the actor's spawned components (get_pcg_generated_data / get_components_by_class), after cleanup_pcg_component + generate_pcg_component.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor holding the UPCGComponent (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name, has_component, graph_path, is_generating, generated, seed, activated, is_partitioned, generation_trigger }

commands.name: get_pcg_generated_data
commands.description: Report what the PCG component of an editor-world actor produced in its last generation, without changing anything: per output item its pin, tags and data class (e.g. PCGPointData). Generation is asynchronous, so the list is empty, with a note, until a generate_pcg_component run has completed: poll this or get_pcg_component_info after triggering it. An actor without a PCG component answers has_component false and an empty list rather than an error; an actor that is not found is an error. For the component's graph, seed and generating state use get_pcg_component_info; for the graph's nodes get_pcg_graph_info; to clear the output cleanup_pcg_component.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor holding the PCG component (an APCGVolume or an actor given one by add_pcg_component), by object name or editor label, e.g. "PCGVolume_0" (required)

commands.returns: { actor_name, has_component, output_data_count, data:[{index, pin, data_class, tags:[...]}], note? }

commands.name: get_pcg_graph_info
commands.description: Reads the structure of a UPCGGraph: node count, per-node titles and pin labels, and every directed edge.  Pin labels and the input_node_name/output_node_name feed connect_pcg_nodes / disconnect_pcg_nodes; the implicit graph endpoints are also addressable by the tokens "Input"/"Output".

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_count: int, nodes: [{node_name, title, settings_class, input_pins: [string], output_pins: [string]}], has_input_node: bool, has_output_node: bool, input_node_name: string, output_node_name: string, edges: [{from_node, from_pin, to_node, to_pin}], edge_count: int }

commands.name: get_pcg_graph_parameters
commands.description: List a PCG graph's user parameters with name, type and current value -- and the read that decides whether a THIRD-PARTY graph can be reused without editing it. An empty list means nothing is exposed: meshes, densities and exclusions are welded inside, so the only way to change them is to edit the asset, which is not an option for a read-only library graph. Read-only. Note it accepts a PCGGraph asset, not a PCGGraphInstance -- overriding a parameter on an instance has no headless route and must be ticked in the details panel.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UPCGGraph (required)

commands.returns: { pcg_graph_path, parameter_count, parameters:[{name, type, value}] }

commands.name: get_pcg_node_properties
commands.description: Read the reflected properties of one PCG node's settings object (UPCGSettings), serialized to JSON, the node found by its node_name from get_pcg_graph_info or the "Input"/"Output" tokens. Use it instead of get_properties, which would need the settings subobject's path. Read-only; write with set_pcg_node_properties.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

params.name: node_name
params.description: The node_name from get_pcg_graph_info of the node to read (the tokens "Input"/"Output" address the implicit endpoints).

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_name: string, settings_class: string, properties: object }

commands.name: list_pcg_node_types
commands.description: Enumerate every PCG node type available in this build (all concrete PCGSettings subclasses, including plugin- and project-added ones), with class names and paths. Run it before add_pcg_node so you pass a class that exists instead of guessing a name from documentation that may not match this engine version. Read-only reflection.
commands.returns: { base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }

commands.name: remove_pcg_graph_parameter
commands.description: Remove a user parameter from a PCG graph asset, in one undo step, and delete the Get Parameter nodes that read it, as the PCG editor does when a parameter goes (getter_nodes_removed); the graph is marked dirty, not saved, as add_pcg_graph_parameter leaves it. Inverse of add_pcg_graph_parameter. A name the graph has no parameter for is an honest no-op (removed=false); a graph that does not load is an error (a PCGGraphInstance is not accepted, as for set_pcg_graph_parameter). The reply re-reads the parameters (parameters). Generated output is not refreshed: cleanup_pcg_component then generate_pcg_component. Read: get_pcg_graph_parameters.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UPCGGraph (required)

params.name: name
params.description: Parameter name to remove (required)

commands.returns: { pcg_graph_path, name, removed, getter_nodes_removed, parameter_count, parameters: [string], note? }

commands.name: remove_pcg_node
commands.description: Removes a user-added node from a PCG graph by name.  Uses UPCGGraph::RemoveNode, which auto-breaks the node's edges and notifies its neighbours; the graph is re-saved after the mutation. The implicit Input/Output endpoint nodes cannot be removed (doing so would silently corrupt the graph) and are rejected with an honest error. Idempotent: a node that is not present reports already_removed without error.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

params.name: node_name
params.description: The node_name from get_pcg_graph_info of the node to remove. The tokens "Input"/"Output" (and the endpoints' real names) are rejected: the implicit graph endpoints cannot be removed.

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_name: string, removed: bool, already_removed: bool, node_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: set_pcg_component_properties
commands.description: Write UPROPERTYs (Seed, bActivated, GenerationTrigger, ...) on the PCG component of an editor-world actor found by label or name, reading each stored value back. Over set_properties: no component path and no edit gate, but no PostEditChange is sent, so the component is not refreshed -- run generate_pcg_component. Nothing is saved.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Actor holding the UPCGComponent (required)

params.name: properties
params.description: JSON object { PropertyName: value, ... } applied to the component

commands.returns: { actor_name, set:[name], failed:[{name, error}], applied:{name: stored_value_text} }

retired.how: object_path="<actor>.PCGComponent", properties with the engine names

commands.name: set_pcg_graph_parameter
commands.description: Write the value of an existing PCG graph user parameter (bool / int / float / double) and read the stored value back, so the reply is its own oracle -- how you tune scatter density or a rule threshold without opening the graph. The parameter must already exist (add_pcg_graph_parameter) and the value type must match. IMPORTANT: it accepts a PCGGraph ASSET only and answers "PCG graph not found" for a PCGGraphInstance -- per-instance overrides have no headless route and must be ticked in the details panel. Changing a parameter does not update the world: cleanup_pcg_component then generate_pcg_component, or the cached output is reused.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: /Game/... path to the UPCGGraph (required)

params.name: name
params.description: Parameter name (must already exist; add with add_pcg_graph_parameter) (required)

params.name: value
params.description: New value; its type must match the parameter's declared type (required)

commands.returns: { pcg_graph_path, name, type, set, value }

commands.name: set_pcg_node_properties
commands.description: Write fields of one PCG node's settings object, picked by node_name in a PCG Graph asset, then save the graph and read the settings back. Use it instead of set_properties, which needs the settings object's path: this also clamps numbers to ClampMin/ClampMax and runs PostEditChange, invalidating the node's cached CRC and rebuilding its pins. Only keys in properties are written, in one undo step; keys match property names case-insensitively. An empty object, a key that names no property (the error lists them), a deprecated or instanced one, a null value, or a value of the wrong kind or that does not convert is an error and nothing changes. A call that changes no value still runs PostEditChange and re-saves. "Input"/"Output" address the endpoints. Read: get_pcg_node_properties.

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Asset path of the PCG Graph (e.g. "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example" or fully-qualified "/Game/PCG/PCG_Example.PCG_Example").

params.name: node_name
params.description: The node_name from get_pcg_graph_info of the node to author (the tokens "Input"/"Output" address the implicit endpoints).

params.name: properties
params.description: Object of UPCGSettings fields to merge, keyed by property name (matched case-insensitively) (e.g. for a SurfaceSampler: bApplyDensityToPoints(bool), PointsPerSquaredMeter(float>=0), Looseness(float)); absent keys untouched. An empty object, a key that names no property of the settings class (or a deprecated one, or one holding instanced subobjects), a null value or a value that does not convert is an error and nothing is changed.

commands.returns: { graph_name: string, asset_path: string, node_name: string, settings_class: string, applied_keys: [string], properties: object, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: spawn_pcg_volume
commands.description: Spawn an APCGVolume in the editor world with a REAL cube brush of half-extent extent and optionally assign a PCG graph, in one undo step. Over spawn_box_volume(volume_class='PCGVolume') it adds the graph (UPCGComponent::SetGraph), a rotation and a name (used only when free); add_pcg_component sets a graph on an existing actor. Bounds, scale and brush are RE-READ, never echoed. Without extent the volume is brush-less (kept for compatibility) and the reply warns: null bounds generate 0 instances in total silence. Not saved (save_level).

params.name: location
params.description: World location [X, Y, Z] for the volume.

params.name: extent
params.description: Cube HALF-size [x, y, z] in unreal units, each > 0 (same convention as spawn_box_volume / spawn_navmesh_bounds_volume). STRONGLY RECOMMENDED: omitting it leaves the volume with extent (0,0,0) and the PCG component generates 0 instances with no error and no warning.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation for the volume (default 0,0,0).

params.name: pcg_graph_path
params.description: Optional content path of a UPCGGraph to assign to the spawned volume's PCG component.

params.name: name
params.description: Optional explicit name (skipped if already used in the current level to avoid Rename-onto-occupied crash).

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, actor_label: string, actor_class: string, has_pcg_component: bool, pcg_graph_path: string, graph_assigned: bool, location: [float], bounds_extent_actual: [float], bounds_origin_actual: [float], actor_scale: [float], has_brush_geometry: bool, brush_poly_count: int, brush_requested: bool, scale_normalized: bool, warning?: string, requested: {...} }

retired.how: volume_class="PCGVolume", location, extent; then add_pcg_component(graph) on it, which reuses the volume's PCG component

commands.name: call_function
commands.description: Invoke a UFUNCTION and get its return value and out-params back typed. The target is any UObject named by object_path -- a level actor, component archetype, class default object, asset, or a LIVE PIE subobject when `world` picks a live world (the response stamps which world ran it) -- or, with class_name instead, that class's Class Default Object (the way to reach UKismetSystemLibrary, UGameplayStatics or any Blueprint Function Library when there is no instance), or, with component_class, the FIRST component of that class on the actor object_path names (no hand-built component path; in co-op, world='server' is where authoritative component state lives). Arguments go in the `parameters` dict, keyed by parameter name (an unknown key is a hard error, so read the signature with get_function_info first). Marshals scalars, ENUM by entry name, Blueprint STRUCTs as JSON objects, ARRAY/set as JSON arrays, FGameplayTag (validated against the registry), FGuid, and OBJECT/class arguments by path (resolved in the target's own world first, then as an asset; a path that resolves to nothing is a hard error, never a silent null). Only BlueprintCallable+Public or BlueprintEvent functions are callable; pass transact=true to make the write undoable and actually dirty an OFPA package.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function to call, exactly as declared (a Blueprint graph named "Add Item" keeps its spaces)

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the target object: full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" (first segment: the actor's internal name in the editor world, internal name OR editor label in a live world). With component_class it names the ACTOR whose component is called. Required unless class_name is given.

params.name: actor
params.description: Alias of object_path.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Optional, instead of object_path: a class NAME (bare/native e.g. "KismetSystemLibrary", /Script path, or a Blueprint asset path -- a Blueprint path yields its GeneratedClass); the function runs on that class's Class Default Object, with no `world`.

params.name: component_class
params.description: Optional component CLASS (bare/native name, /Script path, or Blueprint asset path) to locate on the actor object_path names; the FIRST component of (or derived from) that class is the target. Must derive from UActorComponent.

params.name: function
params.description: Alias of function_name.

params.name: parameters
params.description: Optional {param_name: value} dict. Scalars map directly; pass an ENUM by its entry name as a string (e.g. "Harvest"); pass a STRUCT param as a JSON object {Field: val, ...} and an ARRAY/set as a JSON array (nativized via FJsonObjectConverter — nested structs + enum-by-name inside structs supported; JSON keys match the field's authored name); FGameplayTag as {"TagName":"A.B"}; FGuid as a hex/braced string. A UE-format text string (e.g. "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)") is also accepted for structs.

params.name: args_json
params.description: Alias of parameters; like parameters it also takes the dict as JSON text.

params.name: params
params.description: Alias of parameters.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector (takes precedence over use_pie_world): absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Anything other than absent/'editor' resolves object_path in that live world; an unrecognised value is an error naming the worlds that exist. Ignored with class_name.

params.name: use_pie_world
params.description: Optional (default false). Resolve object_path in the running PIE world instead of the editor world. Equivalent to world='pie'; `world` wins when both are given.

params.name: transact
params.description: Optional (default false). When true, wrap the invocation in an FScopedTransaction and Modify() the target (and, for a component, its owner) BEFORE calling, so whatever the function writes is undoable AND marks the owning package dirty. Without this, a CallInEditor-style function that fills state on a World Partition (OFPA) actor leaves the package clean and save_level reports success while writing nothing. REFUSED for pure/const functions and for PIE-world targets (both would only produce a false-positive dirty flag).

commands.returns: { object_path: string, function_name: string, success: bool, message: string, return_value: any (typed: bool/number/string natively, struct/map as object, array/set as array, object-ref as path string), out_params: object (same typed values), world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number, class_name?: string, class_path?: string, actor?: string, component_class?: string, component_path?: string, transaction?: { requested, modified: [path], saved_to_transaction_buffer, is_package_external, package_name, package_file, package_file_exists, package_dirty_before, package_dirty_after }, verification?: object (only when transact=true) } -- object_path echoes the request (with class_name, the class default object's path); class_name/class_path with class_name; actor/component_class/component_path with component_class.

commands.name: compare_objects
commands.description: Diff TWO LIVE objects property by property at the same instant, using the ENGINE's own equality (FProperty::Identical + PPF_DeepComparison) rather than exported text, so FText localization identity and object-outer differences are classified as `noise` instead of being reported as real differences. Use it for "instance vs its CDO", "fork vs original", "this actor vs that one". Accepts `world`, which resolves BOTH paths in the SAME world (e.g. two live actors inside the server world); to compare the same actor ACROSS worlds — server vs client — use capture_object_snapshot + diff_object_snapshots, which is what a replication check needs. list_instance_overrides diffs a placed actor against its archetype and also tells you which package carries the override; diff_blueprints diffs the AUTHORED graphs instead of live values.

params.name: object_path_1
params.description: Path or name of the first object (full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" by internal name; in a live world the first segment also matches the editor LABEL)

params.name: object_path_2
params.description: Path or name of the second object, same resolution as object_path_1 and in the SAME world

params.name: equality_predicate
params.description: Optional 'identical' (DEFAULT, FProperty::Identical + PPF_DeepComparison — what the engine itself calls equal) or 'export_text' (raw ExportTextItem_Direct(Defaults=nullptr, PPF_None) string compare, kept only for callers that depend on its over-reporting behavior).

params.name: include_noise
params.description: Optional (default false). With equality_predicate='identical', also emit under `noise[]` the properties the engine considers EQUAL but whose exported text differs (FText localization identity, object outer). They are ALWAYS counted in `noise_counts` whether or not this is set.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector applied to BOTH paths: absent/'editor' (default) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). It cannot straddle two worlds — one selector, both objects; an UNRECOGNIZED value is an error naming the worlds that exist, never a silent fallback.

commands.returns: { object_path_1: string, object_path_2: string, same_class: bool, same_type: bool, equality_predicate: string, differences: [{property, difference, kind, value_1?: typed_value, value_2?: typed_value, export_text_1?, export_text_2?, note?}], difference_count: int, noise_counts: object, noise_count: int, noise?: [...], world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: find_classes_implementing_interface
commands.description: Find every class loaded in memory that implements an interface (a native UInterface or a Blueprint Interface), directly or through a parent class, without changing anything: per class its name, path, is_blueprint and implemented_by_k2 (the interface was added in a Blueprint). The engine keeps no reverse index, so it sweeps every loaded class (scanned_class_count) and returns the whole list, never truncated; deprecated and replaced classes are skipped. A Blueprint that is not loaded is missed: for a base class rather than an interface use list_derived_classes, which also reads unloaded Blueprints from the Asset Registry. An interface that does not resolve, or a class that is not an interface, is an error. One class's interfaces: get_class_hierarchy; add an interface to a Blueprint: implement_interface.

params.name: interface
params.description: Interface to search for: bare reflected name (e.g. "Interactable" or "UInteractable"), a /Script/Module.Name path, or a Blueprint Interface asset path (e.g. "/Game/BPI/BPI_Use.BPI_Use"), resolved like list_derived_classes' base_class.

params.name: include_blueprints
