params.description: true (default) also returns Blueprint-generated classes; false returns native C++ classes only.

commands.returns: { interface: string, classes: [{class_name, path, is_blueprint, implemented_by_k2}], count: int, scanned_class_count: int }

commands.name: get_actor_properties_by_class
commands.description: Find placed actors by CLASS (IsA) and/or editor label and read chosen properties of each in one call, as { path, props } per instance, in a live PIE world by default or in the editor world with world='editor' (no PIE needed). Pick it when you have no object path, or want the same properties across many actors; for one object you can name, get_properties reads it typed and reports a misspelled name in not_found[], where this tool silently drops it. Filter with class_name and/or actor_label, drill into one `component`, list the `properties` to read, and compare world='server' with 'client' to separate the authoritative value from the replicated one; the reply stamps the world that answered. It replaces an execute_python loop over GetAllActorsOfClass + get_editor_property. Read-only.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Class filter: bare UClass name resolved with FindFirstObject (e.g. "BP_MyActor_C", "StaticMeshActor"), NOT an asset path. Matches every actor that IsA(class_name). REQUIRED unless actor_label is given.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor-label filter; matches actors whose GetActorLabel() equals this EXACTLY (no substring, no case-folding). REQUIRED unless class_name is given — the call errors when both are missing.

params.name: component
params.description: Optional component name to drill into on each matched actor (reads that component's props instead of the actor's). WARNING: actors that have no component with this name are DROPPED from `instances` entirely, so a short list can mean "wrong component name", not "no such actor".

params.name: properties
params.description: Optional property names to read. Names the target does not have are skipped SILENTLY (no not_found list — cross-check the spelling with get_object_info or get_class_properties). Omit it to read every BlueprintVisible property, which on a Character is a very large payload.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default, ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'editor' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). THIS is the parameter that separates a server reading from a client one.

commands.returns: { instances: [{ path: string, props: object (typed values) }], instance_count: int, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_class_functions
commands.description: List every UFUNCTION a class exposes — the ones it DECLARES plus every inherited one, each tagged with owner_class and is_inherited, and counted separately in declared_function_count / inherited_function_count so "does this class add a function of its own?" is answerable WITHOUT reading the array (declared_only=true returns just those) — with its signature and the flags that decide whether MCP can call it: is_blueprint_callable, is_public, is_static, is_blueprint_pure, is_blueprint_event, is_call_in_editor, category, tooltip and the parameter names/types. This is the lookup to run BEFORE call_function, which refuses anything that is not BlueprintCallable+Public or a BlueprintEvent. WARNING: ZERO own functions is NOT "no Blueprint API": components and data classes usually expose theirs as PROPERTIES (get_class_properties), and a plugin's runtime API often lives in a separate static "*BlueprintLibrary" class rather than on the type itself — both traps show up on MetaHumanComponentBase, whose creator API is in MetaHumanCharacterInstanceBlueprintLibrary. get_function_info drills into ONE function (and separates return values from inputs); get_blueprint_functions lists the graphs a Blueprint AUTHORED rather than the compiled class surface.

params.name: class_name
params.description: UClass identifier, resolved with ResolveClass: bare FName ("Character"), /Script/Module.Class, a Blueprint asset path, or a generated class ("BP_MyActor_C"). WARNING: the REGISTERED FName can differ from the C++ type name and from the name the Python bindings expose — UMetaHumanCharacterInstance is registered as "MetaHumanInstance" — so a failure here is NOT evidence the class is absent; the error names the near misses instead. The response echoes what it resolved to in resolved_class_name / resolved_class_path.

params.name: declared_only
params.description: Optional bool (default false). true = ONLY the UFUNCTIONs this class declares, skipping every inherited one.

commands.returns: { class_name: string, resolved_class_name: string, resolved_class_path: string, declared_only: bool, functions: [{name, owner_class, is_inherited, is_blueprint_callable, is_blueprint_event, is_public, is_static, is_blueprint_pure, is_call_in_editor, category?, tooltip?, parameters: [{name, type}]}], function_count: int, declared_function_count: int, inherited_function_count: int }

commands.name: get_class_hierarchy
commands.description: Walk the full inheritance chain of a class from itself up to UObject, one record per level with its path, is_native flag, class flags/metadata and implemented interfaces — the answer to "is X a Y?" and "where does the native code stop and the Blueprint chain start?". For a USubsystem class it also names the subsystem lifetime (Engine, Editor, GameInstance, World or LocalPlayer), at the top and per level. get_blueprint_parent returns only the IMMEDIATE parent of a Blueprint ASSET; this returns every ancestor of a compiled CLASS. list_derived_classes goes the other direction (descendants).

params.name: class_name
params.description: UClass identifier, resolved with ResolveClass: bare FName ("Character"), /Script/Module.Class, a Blueprint asset path, or a generated class ("BP_MyActor_C"). WARNING: the REGISTERED FName can differ from the C++ type name and from the name the Python bindings expose — UMetaHumanCharacterInstance is registered as "MetaHumanInstance" — so a failure here is NOT evidence the class is absent; the error names the near misses instead.

commands.returns: { class_name: string, lifetime?: string, hierarchy: [{name, path, is_native, lifetime?, is_abstract, is_deprecated, is_placeable, config_name, implemented_interfaces: [{interface, implemented_by_k2}], class_group?, is_blueprintable?, is_blueprint_type?, display_name?, tooltip?}] } -- lifetime only on a USubsystem class and on its levels that are USubsystem classes ("Unknown" for the abstract USubsystem bases).

commands.name: get_class_properties
commands.description: List every property VISIBLE on a class — the ones it DECLARES plus every inherited one, each tagged with owner_class and is_inherited so "does this class add anything of its own?" is a FIELD (declared_property_count) and not an eyeball diff against a remembered list of engine members. declared_only=true returns just this class's own. WARNING: a component or data class usually exposes its Blueprint API as PROPERTIES, not functions: get_class_functions coming back with nothing of its own does NOT mean the class has no API — ask here too (e.g. MetaHumanComponentBase: 0 own functions, 12 own properties). Full typed descriptor per property — kind, cpp_type, editable, edit_const, blueprint_visible, replicated, save_game, config, clamp min/max, enum entries, struct fields, tooltip, edit_condition — plus the class's own flags, config name and implemented interfaces. Schema only: NO instance values. Use get_object_info (include_property_metadata=true) for the same descriptors WITH the current values of a live object, get_properties when you already know the names, and get_blueprint_variables for just the variables a Blueprint itself authored.

params.name: class_name
params.description: UClass identifier, resolved with ResolveClass: bare FName ("Character"), /Script/Module.Class, a Blueprint asset path, or a generated class ("BP_MyActor_C"). WARNING: the REGISTERED FName can differ from the C++ type name and from the name the Python bindings expose — UMetaHumanCharacterInstance is registered as "MetaHumanInstance" — so a failure here is NOT evidence the class is absent; the error names the near misses instead. The response echoes what it resolved to in resolved_class_name / resolved_class_path.

params.name: declared_only
params.description: Optional bool (default false). true = ONLY the properties this class declares, skipping every inherited one. The cheap way to ask "what does this class add?", and what keeps a big class's response from being offloaded for size (get_class_properties("MetaHumanComponentBase") is 44 KB inherited-heavy, 12 properties declared).

commands.returns: { class_name: string, resolved_class_name: string, resolved_class_path: string, declared_only: bool, declared_property_count: int, inherited_property_count: int, is_abstract, is_deprecated, is_placeable, is_native, config_name, implemented_interfaces: [{interface, implemented_by_k2}], class_group?, is_blueprintable?, is_blueprint_type?, display_name?, tooltip?, properties: [<typed descriptor: name, owner_class, is_inherited, kind, cpp_type, editable, edit_const, blueprint_visible, save_game, replicated, config, deprecated, disable_edit_on_instance, enum_values?, fields?, object_class?, inner?, clamp_min/max?, tooltip?, edit_condition?, categories?, units?, display_name?, allow_private_access>], property_count: int }

commands.name: get_component_events
commands.description: List the events (dynamic multicast delegate properties, such as OnComponentHit or OnComponentBeginOverlap) that one component of an actor in the editor world exposes, read from its class by reflection, inherited ones included: per event its name, declaring class, whether it is inherited, its signature and parameters (name, C++ type, is_out), whether Blueprints can bind it (blueprint_assignable) and whether anything is bound to it on this component now. Also facts about the component: class with its category, tooltip and display-name metadata, active and registered state, owner and creation method. Read-only. A name it lists is what subscribe_to_delegate takes to record fires, and what add_component_bound_event binds in a Blueprint; get_class_properties lists every property of a class. An actor or component not found is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the label) of the actor in the editor world, compared without case, e.g. 'StaticMeshActor_0'.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Object name of one of that actor's components, compared without case, e.g. 'StaticMeshComponent0'; get_actor_components lists them.

commands.returns: { actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, component_category: string, component_tooltip: string, component_display_name: string, events: [{name, owner_class, is_inherited, blueprint_assignable, blueprint_callable, signature, parameters: [{name, type, is_out}], parameter_count, is_bound}], events_count: int, declared_events_count: int, component_is_active: bool, component_is_registered: bool, component_owner: string, component_creation_method: string }

commands.name: get_enum_info
commands.description: Read an enum's definition — native or Blueprint (UUserDefinedEnum) — listing every entry (the _MAX sentinel excluded) with index, internal_name, display_name and numeric value. WARNING: the two names DIVERGE on a Blueprint enum: the editor shows the display_name ("Snowy") while the authored entry is the opaque internal_name ("NewEnumerator5"), and the INTERNAL name is what set_properties / set_component_property / call_function's enum-by-name marshaling accept. Read it here before writing an enum, or the write imports nothing.

params.name: enum_name
params.description: Bare enum name resolved with FindFirstObject (e.g. "ECollisionEnabled", "E_MyEnum"); an asset path is NOT accepted here

commands.returns: { enum_name: string, enum_path: string, is_user_defined: bool, values: [{index, name, internal_name, display_name, value}] }

commands.name: get_function_info
commands.description: Inspect ONE UFUNCTION on a class and get its exact call contract: input parameters and RETURN/out values split into separate lists (get_class_functions lumps them together), plus is_blueprint_callable / is_public / is_static / is_blueprint_pure / is_call_in_editor, category and tooltip. Run it to learn the PARAMETER NAMES to put in call_function's `parameters` — that dict is keyed by name and an unknown key is a hard error.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Bare UClass name resolved with FindFirstObject (e.g. "KismetSystemLibrary", "BP_MyActor_C"); an asset path is NOT accepted here

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function to inspect, exactly as the class declares it (a Blueprint graph named "Add Item" keeps its spaces)

commands.returns: { class_name: string, function_name: string, is_blueprint_callable: bool, is_blueprint_event: bool, is_public: bool, is_static: bool, is_blueprint_pure: bool, is_call_in_editor: bool, category?, tooltip?, parameters: [{name, type}], returns: [{name, type}] }

commands.name: get_object_info
commands.description: Portrait of ONE object when you do not know its property names yet: identity (name, class, class path, super class, is_valid), class flags, metadata and implemented interfaces, EVERY reflected property as { name: typed_value }, and for an actor its live components with their classes. Once you know the names, get_properties is far cheaper; get_class_properties gives the property descriptors of a class with no instance, get_class_hierarchy its ancestor chain, and get_actor_components the components alone. include_properties=false makes it the cheap "what IS this thing?" probe (identity and class only); include_property_metadata=true adds each property's editor metadata (type, editable, edit_const, blueprint_visible, replicated, save_game, clamp, tooltip, enum entries) next to its value. Accepts `world`, so the portrait can be the live server or client instance -- useful when a class is swapped at runtime -- and the reply stamps which world answered. Read-only.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object to inspect. In the editor world: full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" whose first segment is the actor's INTERNAL name. In a live world: a fully-qualified PIE path or the same dotted form (first segment matches internal name OR editor label).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default: the editor/asset instance) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Anything other than absent/'editor' portrays the LIVE instance in that world; an UNRECOGNIZED value is an error naming the worlds that exist, never a silent fallback to another world.

params.name: include_properties
params.description: Optional bool (default true). false skips the properties and the components list, leaving identity and class only.

params.name: include_property_metadata
params.description: Optional bool (default false). true returns properties as an ARRAY of typed descriptors (see get_class_properties) each with its current `value`, instead of the { name: typed_value } map.

commands.returns: { object_path: string, object_name: string, class_name: string, class_path: string, super_class: string, is_valid: bool, is_abstract, is_deprecated, is_placeable, is_native, config_name, implemented_interfaces: [{interface, implemented_by_k2}], class_group?, is_blueprintable?, is_blueprint_type?, display_name?, tooltip?, properties?: {prop_name: typed_value} | [<typed descriptor + value>], property_count?: int, components?: [{name, class}], world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number } -- properties/property_count/components only with include_properties; properties is the array form with include_property_metadata; super_class is "None" for UObject.

commands.name: get_package_info
commands.description: Inspect a package that is ALREADY LOADED IN MEMORY: its long name, its is_dirty flag, and every UObject it contains with that object's class. Answers "what actually lives inside this .uasset, besides the asset named after it?" and "does this package have unsaved changes?". WARNING: it resolves with FindFirstObject over loaded UPackages — a package that is on disk but not loaded is reported as not found; use get_asset_by_name / resolve_asset_by_name for on-disk existence, and list_dirty_packages to sweep every dirty package at once.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Long package name of a LOADED package (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/Systems/Foo/BP_Foo"), matched against loaded UPackage objects

commands.returns: { package_path: string, package_name: string, is_dirty: bool, objects: [{name, class}], object_count: int }

commands.name: get_properties
commands.description: Read one or several named properties off ONE object you can already name -- an asset path, a live object's full path, a CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" whose first segment is the actor's internal name -- typed rather than stringified, as { name: typed_value } plus each property's FProperty class and not_found[] for names the class does not declare. Pick it when you have the object and the names: get_object_info when you do not know the names yet, get_actor_properties_by_class when you have no path and want instances by class or label (it drops misspelled names; this reports them), get_component_properties to list every property of one component or of a Blueprint component template. property_name reads one; property_names batches several. Accepts `world` (editor, server, client, pie:N), so the same read on server and client is the cheapest proof that a value replicated; the reply stamps which world answered. Read-only.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Path or name of the object instance. In the editor world: full object path, asset path, CDO/archetype, or a dotted "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" whose first segment is the actor's INTERNAL name (editor labels are not matched here). In a live world: a fully-qualified PIE path or the same dotted form (first segment matches internal name OR editor label).

params.name: property_names
params.description: Optional names of the properties to read; every name that the class does not declare comes back in not_found[]. Required unless property_name is given.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional single property to read, added to property_names.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default: the editor/asset instance) | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Anything other than absent/'editor' reads the LIVE instance in that world; an UNRECOGNIZED value is an error naming the worlds that exist, never a silent fallback to another world.

commands.returns: { object_path: string, class_name: string, values: object (typed: bool/number/string natively, struct/map as object, array/set as array, object-ref as path string), property_types: object ({name: FProperty class name}), not_found: [string], world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: get_struct_info
commands.description: Read the definition of a UScriptStruct (native or Blueprint-authored): its path and every member property as a typed descriptor. Use it to learn the FIELD NAMES before passing a struct as a JSON object to call_function / set_properties, or to read the row layout behind a DataTable. get_struct_members is the Blueprint-struct-authoring view of the same asset; get_enum_info is the enum equivalent.

params.name: struct_name
params.description: Bare struct name resolved with FindFirstObject (e.g. "Vector", "S_ItemStructure"); an asset path is NOT accepted here

commands.returns: { struct_name: string, struct_path: string, properties: [<typed property descriptor>] }

commands.name: list_derived_classes
commands.description: Enumerate every class derived from a base class (native + Blueprint, Widget and Anim Blueprints included) in any UObject hierarchy -- "what breaks if I change this base class?", or every subsystem of a lifetime family (base_class GameInstanceSubsystem, WorldSubsystem, EditorSubsystem...). The base may be a native class or a Blueprint asset. With loaded_only=false (default) it also surfaces not-yet-loaded Blueprint subclasses from the asset registry without loading them (loaded=false: no is_abstract/module/parent_class/lifetime, native_parent from the registry tag). include_native=false and package_path narrow it to the Blueprint assets under a content folder.

params.name: base_class
params.description: Name/path of the base class (resolved via ResolveClass: bare name, /Script/ path, or Blueprint class/asset path); a name ResolveClass does not know is looked up as a Blueprint asset name under /Game, and when that name matches more than one asset the others are listed in ambiguous_matches.

params.name: include_blueprints
params.description: Include Blueprint-generated (non-native) subclasses (default true)

params.name: include_native
params.description: Include native C++ subclasses (default true); false lists only Blueprint classes

params.name: include_abstract
params.description: Include classes flagged CLASS_Abstract (default false)

params.name: loaded_only
params.description: If false (default), also queries the asset registry for Blueprint subclasses not currently loaded in memory

params.name: package_path
params.description: Optional content folder (e.g. "/Game" or "/Game/Characters"): keep only Blueprint classes whose package lies under it. Native classes are not filtered by it.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Optional cap on classes returned, 1..100000 (absent: no cap); results_truncated says whether any were left out

commands.returns: { base_class: string, base_class_path: string, ambiguous_matches?: [string], classes: [{class_name, path, is_blueprint, is_abstract?, module?, loaded, parent_class?, native_parent?, lifetime?, asset_name?, asset_path?, package?}], count: int, native_count: int, blueprint_count: int, results_truncated: bool, max_results?: int } -- asset_name/asset_path/package name the Blueprint ASSET of a Blueprint class (its generated "_C" class stripped); native_parent is the first native ancestor; lifetime (Editor, Engine, GameInstance, World, LocalPlayer or Unknown) only for a loaded USubsystem class.

commands.name: list_enums
commands.description: List the enum types (UEnum) loaded in memory, native C++ and Blueprint user-defined, with their entries, without changing anything: per enum its name, path, owning module (C++ enums only) and entries [{name, value}], leaving out the _MAX sentinel and entries tagged Hidden. Unfiltered it returns every loaded enum with all its entries, a very large reply, so pass name_pattern or module_filter. module_filter matches C++ enums only, since a Blueprint enum has no module, and a Blueprint enum asset that is not loaded is not listed. No match gives count 0, not an error. For one enum's display names, which differ from the internal names on a Blueprint enum, use get_enum_info; structs: list_structs; author enums with create_enum and add_enum_entry.

params.name: module_filter
params.description: Optional plain substring of the owning module name, case-insensitive, no wildcards, e.g. "Engine" or "StateTreeModule"; matches C++ enums only.

params.name: name_pattern
params.description: Optional plain substring of the enum name, case-insensitive, no wildcards, e.g. "Collision"; omitted or empty keeps every name.

commands.returns: { enums: [{enum_name, path, module?, entries:[{name, value}]}], count: int }

commands.name: list_instance_overrides
commands.description: List the property values a placed actor, and each of its components, holds as per-instance overrides in the level -- every property that differs from its archetype (the class defaults for the actor, the Blueprint's component template for a component) -- each with the archetype value beside it, plus the package that stores the actor (for a World Partition actor its own external .uasset) and whether that package is dirty. Use it to confirm that a write such as set_properties really landed on the instance (it catches an empty "()" stored where a gameplay tag was meant); to read named properties of any object use get_properties, and for every property of one component get_component_properties. Read-only: it compares the loaded actor in the editor world, so with a dirty package the result is unsaved state (caveat says which). Properties the engine counts as equal but exports differently are counted in noise_counts and listed only with include_noise. An actor not found in the editor world, or one without an archetype, is an error.

params.name: actor
params.description: Actor to audit: internal object name, editor label, or full object path, e.g. "BP_Door_C_3" or "Door_Main". Resolved in the EDITOR world, since a per-instance override is an editor/on-disk value, not a runtime one.

params.name: include_components
params.description: Optional (default true). Also compare every component of the actor with its own archetype, the Blueprint's component template rather than the Blueprint class defaults (which hold no components).

params.name: require_edit
params.description: Optional (default true). Only consider properties flagged CPF_Edit, i.e. what a human could actually have authored in the details panel. false widens to every reflected property.

params.name: include_transient
params.description: Optional (default false). Include CPF_Transient / DuplicateTransient / NonPIEDuplicateTransient / Deprecated properties. They are never saved, so they are noise in an override audit.

params.name: include_noise
params.description: Optional (default false). Also list, under `noise[]`, the properties the engine considers EQUAL but whose exported text differs (FText localization identity, object outer). They are ALWAYS counted in `noise_counts` regardless.

commands.returns: { actor_path, actor_name, actor_label, actor_class, archetype_path, archetype_class, archetype_is_cdo, is_package_external, package_name, package_file, package_file_exists, package_dirty, overrides: [{property, kind, value, archetype_value, declaring_class, property_type, note, ...}], override_count, components: [{component, component_class, creation_method, archetype_path, archetype_is_cdo, overrides, override_count, noise?}], components_examined, component_override_count, total_override_count, properties_examined, skipped: {transient, not_edit, no_baseline}, noise_counts: object, noise_count: int, noise?: [...], caveat: string }

commands.name: list_modules
commands.description: List the C++ modules the editor's module manager knows (FModuleManager::QueryModules) -- engine, editor, project and plugin modules, loaded or not -- each with name, file_path (its binary on disk), is_loaded and is_game_module, plus count; optionally only names containing name_pattern, or only loaded ones. Use it to check that a module's code is present and loaded before relying on its classes; for a plugin's enabled state use get_plugin_status, and for the types a module defines list_derived_classes, list_structs or list_enums (Niagara stack modules are list_niagara_modules, a different thing). Read-only and idempotent: it loads or unloads nothing. No match gives count 0, not an error.

params.name: name_pattern
params.description: Optional plain substring of the module name, case-insensitive, no wildcards, e.g. "Niagara"; omitted or empty lists every module

params.name: loaded_only
params.description: true keeps only the modules loaded right now (default false)

commands.returns: { modules: [{name, file_path, is_loaded, is_game_module}], count: int }

commands.name: list_objects_of_class
commands.description: Enumerate live instances of a class currently in memory, complementing get_actors_by_class (actors only) with any UObject-derived type. Accepts `world` to SCOPE the sweep to one world — 'server' vs 'client' is what separates an authoritative census from a replicated one, and without it a PIE session returns the instances of EVERY world mixed together (host and client both), which reads as duplicates. The response stamps the world that answered, so count:0 means "not in THIS world" instead of "does not exist".

params.name: class_name
params.description: Name/path of the class to enumerate instances of (resolved via ResolveClass)

params.name: world_only
params.description: Only include objects that resolve a UWorld via GetWorld() (default true). Ignored when `world` is given, which is already a stricter filter.

params.name: include_default
params.description: Include each class's Class Default Object (default false). A CDO has no world, so passing `world` excludes CDOs regardless of this flag.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector that SCOPES the sweep: absent (default: every loaded instance, across all worlds) | 'editor' | 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Only objects whose GetWorld() IS that world are returned; an UNRECOGNIZED value is an error naming the worlds that exist, never a silent fallback to another world.

commands.returns: { class_name: string, objects: [{object_path, name, class, outer}], count: int, world: string ('any' when no selector was given), world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: list_structs
commands.description: List the struct types (UScriptStruct) loaded in memory, native C++ and Blueprint user-defined, without changing anything: per struct its name, path, owning module (C++ structs only) and is_user_defined. Unfiltered it returns every loaded struct, thousands of them, so pass name_pattern or module_filter. module_filter matches C++ structs only, since a Blueprint struct has no module, and a Blueprint struct asset that is not loaded is not listed. No match gives count 0, not an error. Read one struct's fields with get_struct_info (by the struct_name given here) or a Blueprint struct's members with get_struct_members (by its asset path); enums: list_enums; author a struct with create_struct.

params.name: module_filter
params.description: Optional plain substring of the owning module name, case-insensitive, no wildcards, e.g. "CoreUObject" or "StateTreeModule"; matches C++ structs only.

params.name: name_pattern
params.description: Optional plain substring of the struct name (no F prefix), case-insensitive, no wildcards, e.g. "Vector"; omitted or empty keeps every name.

commands.returns: { structs: [{struct_name, path, module?, is_user_defined}], count: int }

commands.name: poll_delegate_events
commands.description: Return the fires a subscribe_to_delegate subscription has recorded after cursor, oldest first, each with its sequence_id, a timestamp in seconds (FPlatformTime::Seconds) and the delegate's parameters as payload. It does not wait for new fires and does not consume what it returns, so the same cursor gives the same events again; pass next_cursor back to read only newer ones. Only the latest 512 fires per subscription are kept. subscription_active false means the target object is gone: recorded fires still come back, but no new ones will arrive. An unknown subscription_id is an error. unsubscribe_delegate ends the subscription; poll_gameplay_tag_events is the same reader for register_gameplay_tag_event.

params.name: subscription_id
params.description: The subscription_id that subscribe_to_delegate returned, e.g. 3.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Optional sequence_id: only fires with a higher one are returned; pass the previous reply's next_cursor. Default 0 returns every fire still kept.

commands.returns: { events: [{sequence_id, ts, payload}], next_cursor: int, subscription_active: bool }

commands.name: set_properties
commands.description: Write one or several properties on ONE object -- an asset, a CDO/archetype, a placed actor, or one of its components as "Actor.Component" -- in the EDITOR world, as an edit in the Details panel: each write runs Modify/PreEditChange/PostEditChange (undoable, package dirtied, the component re-registered), and the reply lists set[] and failed[{property,error}] per name. This is the tool for any editable setting of a light, fog, sky, cloud, decal, camera, post-process volume, capture, replication flag, sound, Niagara system, physical material, montage, foliage type or other asset: pass the engine's property names (get_object_info lists them), a struct as a JSON object of only the fields to change, a color as {"R","G","B","A"}. The actor is found by its internal name or by a label only it has; the component by its name or by a class only one of its components has ("Sun.DirectionalLightComponent", "Fog.ExponentialHeightFogComponent"). A key inside a struct that names no field is refused, and nothing is written to that property. clamp=true keeps numbers inside the property's ClampMin/ClampMax, as the Details panel does, and lists what it clamped; save=true saves the asset's package (refused for a level object: save_level). A blend space is resampled after the write. Use set_component_property for a component in a live PIE world, set_blueprint_component_properties for a Blueprint's component template, set_widget_property inside a Widget Blueprint, call_function for the object's own setter. Unregistered gameplay tags are refused. No Blueprint is compiled.

params.name: object_path
params.description: The object, resolved in the EDITOR world: an asset path, a full object path, a CDO/archetype, or "Actor[.Component[.Subobject]]" where Actor is an internal name or a unique label and Component a component name or a class only one component has.

params.name: properties
params.description: Optional dict of {property_name: value}; values can be scalar, nested object, or array (UE-format text like "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)" is also accepted for structs). Required unless property_name + value is given; both together write properties{} first.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional single property to write (must be CPF_Edit and not EditConst, or it lands in failed[] with the reason). Needs value.

params.name: value
params.description: Optional new value for property_name: string, number, boolean, JSON object (struct), JSON array (array/set/tag container), or a UE-format text string like "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)"

params.name: save
params.description: Save the asset's package after the writes (default false); refused, before anything is written, for an object in a level

params.name: clamp
params.description: Clamp each number written to the ClampMin/ClampMax of its property, struct fields and array elements included (default false)

commands.returns: { object_path: string, resolved_path: string, set: [string], failed: [{property, error}], clamped?: [string] ("name=value", with clamp), saved?: bool, save_error?: string (with save), success: bool }

commands.name: subscribe_to_delegate
commands.description: Start recording a dynamic multicast delegate (an event such as OnComponentHit or a Blueprint event dispatcher, with any number of parameters) of a live object: a rooted observer is bound to it and every fire is kept with its parameters as text, the latest 512 per subscription. It is the first of three steps: read the fires with poll_delegate_events (subscription_id plus a cursor), and stop with unsubscribe_delegate, which frees the observer; the subscription otherwise stays until the editor closes, and stops recording when the object goes away. Find event names with get_component_events, or get_event_dispatchers for a Blueprint; for gameplay tag count changes use register_gameplay_tag_event instead. It observes only: nothing in the object or level changes, and nothing is saved. Idempotent per the exact (object_path, delegate_name) text: the same pair returns the existing subscription_id with already_existed=true (a different spelling of the same object makes a second subscription, and a target that no longer exists is subscribed afresh). An object that is not found, or a delegate_name that is not a multicast delegate of its class, is an error.

params.name: object_path
params.description: Object owning the delegate: a full object path (an asset, or a live object's path, including a PIE actor's), the internal name of an editor-world actor ("BP_Door_C_1"), or "Actor.Component" for one of its components ("BP_Door_C_1.TriggerBox"). Bare names search the editor world only.

params.name: delegate_name
params.description: Exact name of the dynamic multicast delegate property on that object's class, e.g. "OnComponentBeginOverlap" or "OnDoorOpened", as get_component_events or get_event_dispatchers list it.

commands.returns: { subscription_id: int, signature: string, already_existed: bool }

commands.name: unsubscribe_delegate
commands.description: Remove a subscription: unbinds the observer from the delegate and frees it. Idempotent (removing an unknown/already-removed subscription_id is a no-op success, not an error).

params.name: subscription_id
params.description: The id returned by subscribe_to_delegate

commands.returns: { removed: bool }

commands.name: get_actor_replication_info
commands.description: Read every replication setting of an actor placed in the editor world, found by object name or label (first match): replicates, replicate_movement, replicate_physics (whether the root simulates physics, whose state travels with movement), net_load_on_client, net_use_owner_relevancy, always_relevant, both net update frequencies, the net cull distance (squared as stored, and in cm), dormancy, net priority and the local and remote roles (name and number). Read-only; it reads the placed instance, not a PIE server or client copy, so the roles are the authoring-time ones. Writers: set_properties (replicates, movement), set_properties, set_network_authority (local role).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name or label of the actor in the editor world (first match).

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Alias of actor_name.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, class_name: string, replicates: bool, replicate_movement: bool, replicate_physics: bool, net_load_on_client: bool, net_use_owner_relevancy: bool, always_relevant: bool, net_update_frequency: float, min_net_update_frequency: float, net_cull_distance_squared: float, net_cull_distance_cm: float, net_dormancy: string, net_dormancy_int: int, net_priority: float, role: string, local_role: int, local_role_name: string, remote_role: int, remote_role_name: string }

commands.name: set_actor_net_cull_distance
commands.description: Set the net cull distance of an actor placed in the editor world, found by label (first match): distance is the linear radius in cm, squared before AActor::SetNetCullDistanceSquared stores it (15000, the engine default, stores 225000000). Past that distance from a client's viewer the actor is no longer relevant for replication to that client, unless it is always relevant. Only that placed instance changes, not its class defaults, with no undo step, no dirty mark and no save, and a PIE copy is never touched. distance echoes the request, not a read-back: get_actor_replication_info returns both stored forms (net_cull_distance_squared, net_cull_distance_cm). A missing label or distance is an error; no range check is made. Update rate: set_actor_net_update_frequency; every replication setting at once: get_actor_replication_info.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the actor in the editor world (first match).

params.name: distance
params.description: Net cull distance in cm (will be squared before being set); a negative value squares to the same distance.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, distance: float }

commands.name: set_actor_net_dormancy
commands.description: Set NetDormancy on an editor-world actor found by label (AActor::SetNetDormancy). Only that placed instance changes; it is not marked dirty and nothing is saved. dormancy in the reply is the parsed enum name (e.g. DORM_DormantAll), not a read-back: use get_actor_replication_info.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the actor in the editor world.

params.name: dormancy
params.description: ENetDormancy value, case-insensitive, with or without a DORM_ or DORMANT_ prefix: Never, Awake, DormantAll (or All), DormantPartial (or Partial), Initial; e.g. "DORM_DormantAll".

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, dormancy: string }

commands.name: set_actor_net_priority
commands.description: Write NetPriority, the relative replication priority when bandwidth is short, on an editor-world actor found by label. Only that placed instance changes; it is not marked dirty or saved. priority is read back after the write; get_actor_replication_info reads it as net_priority. Engine defaults: 1.0 for actors, 3.0 for pawns.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label of the actor in the editor world (matched against labels, not object names); first match.

params.name: priority
params.description: New NetPriority as a float, written as given with no clamping; higher makes the actor more likely to replicate when bandwidth is saturated.

commands.returns: { actor_name, priority }

commands.name: set_actor_net_update_frequency
commands.description: Set how often an actor placed in the editor world is considered for replication: frequency goes to NetUpdateFrequency and, when given, min_frequency to MinNetUpdateFrequency, both in updates per second, through the AActor setters. The actor is found by label (first match); only that placed instance changes, not its class defaults, with no undo step, no dirty mark and no save, and a PIE copy is never touched. Leaving out min_frequency keeps the current minimum. The reply echoes the requested numbers (min_frequency only when given), not a read-back: read them with get_actor_replication_info. A missing label or frequency is an error; neither value is range-checked. Culling by distance: set_actor_net_cull_distance; priority when bandwidth is short: set_actor_net_priority; dormancy: set_actor_net_dormancy.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the actor in the editor world (first match).

params.name: frequency
params.description: Net update frequency in Hz (updates per second), written as given; required.

params.name: min_frequency
params.description: Optional minimum net update frequency in Hz, the floor adaptive net update frequency may drop to; omitted leaves it unchanged.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, frequency: float, min_frequency: float? }

commands.name: delete_save_game
commands.description: Delete the save file of a slot with DeleteGameInSlot; the data is gone for good. success is false, with an error, when the engine refuses, usually because the slot does not exist (check with get_save_game_slot_info). Returns slot_name, user_index and message.

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Save slot name to delete

params.name: user_index
params.description: Platform user index for the save system; default 0 (the generic desktop save system ignores it)

commands.returns: { slot_name: string, user_index: int, success: bool, message: string }

commands.name: get_save_game_slot_info
commands.description: Read the file facts of one save slot without loading or changing it: exists (UGameplayStatics::DoesSaveGameExist) and, for an existing slot, save_path (the generic desktop Saved/SaveGames/<slot>.sav) plus file_size, modified_iso and modified_ticks when that file is on disk. Use it to check one slot before load_game or delete_save_game, or after save_game to confirm the write; to discover slot names use list_save_games; to read the saved object's contents use load_game. A missing slot is a success with exists=false and an error field saying so, and then no save_path, size or time.

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Exact save slot name, e.g. "Slot1", as list_save_games returns it; on desktop it is the file name without .sav.

params.name: user_index
params.description: Platform user index, a whole number (default 0); the generic desktop save system ignores it.

commands.returns: { slot_name: string, user_index: int, exists: bool, save_path?: string, file_size?: int, modified_iso?: string, modified_ticks?: int, error?: string }

commands.name: list_save_games
commands.description: List the save slots the platform's save system knows for a user index: on desktop, the .sav files at the root of Saved/SaveGames, each with slot_name and, when that file exists, file_path and file_size. Use it to find slot names for load_game, get_save_game_slot_info (one slot, with its modified time) or delete_save_game; save_game writes a slot. A save system can also keep a slot as a FOLDER of .sav files, which is not a slot here: those folders are reported apart in slot_folders (count does not include them), so an empty list is only proof of no save when slot_folders is empty too. Read-only and idempotent; no PIE needed. No saves at all gives count 0, not an error.

params.name: user_index
params.description: Optional user index, default 0. Passed to the platform's save system; the generic desktop one keeps every user's slots in one folder, so there it changes nothing.

commands.returns: { user_index: int, save_directory: string, save_games: [{ slot_name, file_path?, file_size? }], count: int, slot_folders: [{ folder, sav_files }] (subfolders of save_directory holding .sav files, searched recursively) }

commands.name: load_game
commands.description: Load the SaveGame stored in a slot with LoadGameFromSlot and report the transient object: save_game_instance, save_game_class and save_game_path. success is false when the slot is empty or unreadable, or holds a class other than save_game_class; get_save_game_slot_info (exists) tells missing from corrupt. It only reads: the slot file is not changed and the object is transient. Write a slot with save_game.

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Save slot name to load from

params.name: user_index
params.description: Platform user index for the save system; default 0 (the generic desktop save system ignores it)

params.name: save_game_class
params.description: Optional SaveGame subclass the slot is expected to hold. A slot file records its own class and is rebuilt as that; when the loaded object is not this class (or a child of it) the load is reported as failed. An unknown class name is an error.

commands.returns: { slot_name: string, user_index: int, success: bool, save_game_instance: string, save_game_class: string, save_game_path: string, expected_class?: string, error: string }

commands.name: load_game_from_memory
commands.description: Deserialize a SaveGame from a base64 blob (the memory_base64 of save_game_to_memory) with LoadGameFromMemory; returns the transient object save_game_instance, save_game_class and save_game_path. Invalid base64 is an error; success is false when the blob is corrupt, truncated or from another SaveGame class. It only reads: nothing is written to disk and the object is transient. Make a blob with save_game_to_memory; to read a slot file use load_game.

params.name: memory_base64
params.description: Base64 text of a serialized SaveGame, as returned in memory_base64 by save_game_to_memory

commands.returns: { success: bool, memory_size: int, save_game_instance: string, save_game_class: string, save_game_path: string, error: string }

commands.name: restore_actor_state
commands.description: Restore the transform + properties a previous serialize_actor_state wrote, addressed by the SAME key it was saved under. Idempotent: restoring twice in a row re-applies the same values both times. It restores only what was captured -- if serialize_actor_state was called without property_names, this puts back the transform and nothing else.

params.name: actor_name_or_stable_key
params.description: Required. The stable_key used at serialize time (or the actor_name, when no explicit stable_key was passed to serialize_actor_state). The actor to restore ONTO is then resolved from the actor_name stored inside the saved payload, looked up in the current world.

commands.returns: { restored: bool, properties_restored: [string], transform_restored: bool }

commands.name: save_game
commands.description: Write a NEW SaveGame object holding its class defaults, of save_game_class (default UMCPSaveGame), to a slot with SaveGameToSlot, overwriting whatever the slot held. It captures no live game or level state, so use it to create or reset a slot, e.g. to test a load path. On desktop the file is Saved/SaveGames/<slot>.sav. Read it back with load_game, check it with get_save_game_slot_info or list_save_games, delete it with delete_save_game; for bytes that never touch disk use save_game_to_memory. The old file is not backed up and there is no undo step. An unknown, non-SaveGame or abstract class is an error and nothing is written; success is false, with an error, when the engine refuses the write.

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Save slot name, e.g. "Slot1"; on desktop it is the file name Saved/SaveGames/<slot_name>.sav. list_save_games shows the slots that exist

params.name: user_index
params.description: Platform user index for the save system; default 0 (the generic desktop save system ignores it)

params.name: save_game_class
params.description: Name of a loaded, concrete USaveGame subclass, e.g. "MySaveGame", or "BP_MySave_C" for a Blueprint one already loaded (found with FindFirstObject, never loaded from disk); default UMCPSaveGame

commands.returns: { slot_name: string, user_index: int, success: bool, message: string }

commands.name: save_game_to_memory
commands.description: Serialize a NEW SaveGame object holding its class defaults, of save_game_class (default UMCPSaveGame), with SaveGameToMemory and return the bytes as memory_base64 with memory_size. Despite the save verb it writes nothing: no slot, file or asset, and the object is transient and dropped. Use it to see a SaveGame class's default serialized form, or to get a blob for load_game_from_memory, which round-trips it; to write a slot on disk use save_game. No live game state is captured. An unknown, non-SaveGame or abstract class is an error; success is false, with an error and no memory_base64, when the engine fails to serialize.

params.name: save_game_class
params.description: Name of a loaded, concrete USaveGame subclass, e.g. "MySaveGame", or "BP_MySave_C" for a Blueprint one already loaded (found with FindFirstObject, never loaded from disk); default UMCPSaveGame

commands.returns: { success: bool, save_game_class: string, memory_size: int, memory_base64: string }

commands.name: serialize_actor_state
commands.description: Save an actor's transform plus an EXPLICIT set of properties into a SaveGame slot, keyed by an identity YOU choose (stable_key, defaulting to actor_name). Nothing is captured implicitly: name the properties you want in property_names or you get the transform and only the transform. Idempotent -- re-serializing the same key overwrites that slot, it never duplicates. Pair with restore_actor_state, which takes the same key.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Required. Object name or editor label of the actor to serialize (resolved via mcp_common::FindActorByName).

params.name: stable_key
params.description: Optional. Identity used as the persistence key; defaults to actor_name. The caller owns this key on purpose: AActor::GetActorGuid() is editor-only and not documented as stable across level reloads, so no GUID key is auto-generated for you.

params.name: property_names
params.description: Optional array of UPROPERTY names to capture in addition to the transform. If omitted, ONLY the transform is saved -- it never silently saves "everything" via CPF_SaveGame, which no native property here sets and which, on a Blueprint variable, depends on whether that Blueprint ticked the SaveGame checkbox (get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info reports it): a filter this command cannot assume for you.

commands.returns: { slot_id: string, saved: bool, property_count: int }

commands.name: add_smart_object_definition_default_behavior
commands.description: Add a definition-level default behavior, a new instance of the class named by behavior_class, to a USmartObjectDefinition asset, in one undo step, then save it: slots without a behavior of their own use the defaults. The private DefaultBehaviorDefinitions array is reached through reflection. The class is a short native name or a /Script path and must derive from USmartObjectBehaviorDefinition; an unknown, abstract or unrelated class is an error before anything changes. Every call adds another default. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Inverse: remove_smart_object_definition_default_behavior; per slot: add_smart_object_slot_behavior_definition.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: behavior_class
params.description: Behavior class: short native name or /Script path; must derive from USmartObjectBehaviorDefinition

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, behavior_class: string, default_behavior_count: int, added: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_smart_object_slot
commands.description: Append a named activity slot, enabled, to a USmartObjectDefinition asset, in one undo step, then save it. Idempotent on name: when a slot named slot_name is already there, nothing is added, written or saved (already_existed true, changed false, saved false), and activity_tag is not applied to it. activity_tag (default Default) is added to the new slot only when it is a registered gameplay tag, though the reply echoes it either way, so read the slot back with get_smart_object_slots_detail. A missing definition is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Inverse: remove_smart_object_slot; its tags: set_smart_object_slot_activity_tags.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Unique name for the new slot

params.name: activity_tag
params.description: Optional FGameplayTag to attach to the slot; defaults to "Default"

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_name: string, activity_tag: string, slot_count: int, added?: bool, already_existed?: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: add_smart_object_slot_behavior_definition
commands.description: Add a behavior definition, a new instance of the class named by behavior_class, to the behaviors of the slot at slot_index in a USmartObjectDefinition asset, in one undo step, then save it. The class is a short native name or a /Script path and must derive from USmartObjectBehaviorDefinition, e.g. GameplayBehaviorSmartObjectBehaviorDefinition; an unknown, abstract or unrelated class is an error before anything changes. Every call adds another behavior, even of a class the slot already has. A behavior on every slot, or a default one, is what register_smart_object_actor needs. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Inverse: remove_smart_object_slot_behavior_definition; for all slots: add_smart_object_definition_default_behavior.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Index of the slot to attach the behavior to

params.name: behavior_class
params.description: Behavior class: short native name (e.g. "GameplayBehaviorSmartObjectBehaviorDefinition") or full /Script path

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_index: int, behavior_class: string, behavior_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotation
commands.description: Add an entrance annotation (an entry and/or exit point) to the slot at slot_index in a USmartObjectDefinition asset, with its offset, rotation, tags and navigation and trajectory fields, in one undo step, then save it. A field not given keeps the engine default, and every call adds another entrance. An invalid selection_priority, a missing definition or an invalid slot_index is an error before anything changes; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. entrance_count counts the slot's entrances and data_count all its definition data. Read them back with get_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotations; inverse: remove_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotation.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Index of the slot to add the entrance to

params.name: offset
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] local-space offset of the entrance

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] local-space rotation (degrees)

params.name: is_entry
params.description: Optional: entrance can be used to enter the slot (default true)

params.name: is_exit
params.description: Optional: entrance can be used to exit the slot (default true)

params.name: tags
params.description: Optional gameplay tag names identifying the entrance

params.name: trace_ground_location
params.description: Optional: adjust ground location with a line trace (default true).

params.name: check_transition_trajectory
params.description: Optional: check collisions on the transition from nav location to slot (default false).

params.name: selection_priority
params.description: Optional entrance selection priority: Lowest|Lower|Low|BelowNormal|Normal|AboveNormal|High|Higher|Highest (default Normal).

params.name: trajectory_start_height_offset
params.description: Optional height offset at the start of the transition check (default 80).

params.name: trajectory_slot_height_offset
params.description: Optional height offset at the slot for the transition check (default 40).

params.name: transition_check_radius
params.description: Optional radius of the transition trajectory check (default 10).

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_index: int, entrance_count: int, data_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: claim_smart_object
commands.description: Reserve the first free slot of the Smart Object component of an editor-world actor (USmartObjectSubsystem::MarkSlotAsClaimed, Normal priority, no user), so other users see it taken; claim_handle and slot_id identify it. To claim and mark the slot occupied in one call use use_smart_object; to find objects by area find_smart_objects. The component must be registered with the subsystem first (register_smart_object_actor; get_smart_object_component_definition shows registered), and the definition needs a behavior or it never registers. The claim is runtime subsystem state: not saved, no undo step. Each call claims another free slot, and once all are claimed the call is an error. Release goes through release_smart_object with actor_label, which unregisters the whole component and frees all its claims; the claim_handle string cannot be passed back. success is false, with an error, when the claim does not read back valid.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label (not the object name) of the editor-world actor carrying the USmartObjectComponent, e.g. "SO_Bench_1", as register_smart_object_actor set it; whole label, case-insensitive, first match wins

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Optional path to the definition; only echoed back in the reply, never loaded or checked

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, definition_path: string, claim_handle: string, slot_id: string, is_claimed: bool, success: bool }

commands.name: create_smart_object_definition
commands.description: Create a USmartObjectDefinition asset at package_path/definition_name, or load the one already there, add default slots (enabled, no tags) until it has num_activity_slots, then save it. Slots already there are kept and never taken away; created says whether the asset is new. A definition that already has at least that many slots changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false), so a repeat call is idempotent. A name taken by another asset class, or a path that is not an asset path, is an error; a failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Slots added to an existing definition are one undo step; a new asset is not undoable. Named slots: add_smart_object_slot; slot fields: set_smart_object_slot_activity_tags or set_smart_object_slot_enabled; a behavior, which register_smart_object_actor needs: add_smart_object_definition_default_behavior or add_smart_object_slot_behavior_definition; read back: get_smart_object_definition_summary.

params.name: definition_name
params.description: Name for the new Smart Object definition, also its asset name

params.name: package_path
params.description: Content folder; defaults to /Game/MCP

params.name: num_activity_slots
params.description: Slot count to reach, default 1: slots are added until the definition has this many, none are taken away

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, definition_name: string, num_slots: int, created: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: find_smart_objects
commands.description: Spatially query the SmartObject subsystem for slots within a box centered on a point (USmartObjectSubsystem::FindSmartObjects). HONEST GATE: the spatial index only populates once the subsystem runtime is initialized (BeginPlay/PIE); in the editor/headless world it is empty, so this returns success with an empty results list and a note rather than fabricating hits.

params.name: center
params.description: [x, y, z] world-space center of the search box

params.name: radius
params.description: Half-extent (uu) of the AABB search box around center

params.name: include_claimed
params.description: Optional: also return already-claimed slots (default false)

params.name: include_disabled
params.description: Optional: also return disabled slots (default false)

commands.returns: { center: [number, number, number], radius: number, results: [{ object_handle: string, slot_handle: string, actor_label: string }], count: int, note?: string }

commands.name: get_smart_object_component_definition
commands.description: Read which USmartObjectDefinition the USmartObjectComponent of an editor-world actor references (definition, as an object path; has_definition=false and an empty string when none) and whether the component is registered with the editor world's SmartObjectSubsystem (registered, a valid handle), which claim_smart_object and use_smart_object need. The read side of set_smart_object_component_definition; register_smart_object_actor spawns an actor with one. To read the definition asset itself use get_smart_object_definition_summary or get_smart_object_slots_detail. Read-only and idempotent. A label no actor has, or an actor without the component, is an error.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label (not the object name) of the editor-world actor carrying the USmartObjectComponent, e.g. "SO_Bench_1"; whole label, case-insensitive, first match wins. find_actors_by_name with match='label' finds labels

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, definition: string, has_definition: bool, registered: bool }

commands.name: get_smart_object_definition_summary
commands.description: Read the object-level state of a USmartObjectDefinition asset without changing it: its activity tags with their merging policy, the user-tag filtering policy and whether the object-level user filter is empty, the slot count, the default behavior count, and bounds around every slot in the object local space (slot offsets plus the default slot size, not world space). It also runs the engine Validate() pass: is_valid, and validation_errors with the messages of every severity. It also gives slot_activity_tags, the union of the activity tags of every slot (object-level activity_tags excluded), and registered_actor_count, how many smart object components registered with the editor-world SmartObjectSubsystem use this definition (0 without that subsystem). A missing definition_path, or one that does not load, is an error. Per-slot fields: get_smart_object_slots_detail; entrances: get_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotations; edit the object level with set_smart_object_definition_activity_tags or set_smart_object_definition_user_tag_filter.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Object path of the USmartObjectDefinition asset, e.g. /Game/AI/SO_Bench.SO_Bench

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_count: int, activity_tags: [string], slot_activity_tags: [string], registered_actor_count: int, merging_policy: string, filtering_policy: string, user_filter_is_empty: bool, bounds: { min: [number, number, number], max: [number, number, number] }, is_valid: bool, validation_errors: [string], default_behavior_count: int }

commands.name: get_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotations
commands.description: List a slot's entrance annotations with all their fields (round-trip reader for add_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotation, including the navigation/trajectory fields).

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset.

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Index of the slot to read.

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_index: int, entrance_count: int, entrances: [ { offset: [float], rotation: [float], is_entry: bool, is_exit: bool, tags: [string], trace_ground_location: bool, check_transition_trajectory: bool, selection_priority: string, trajectory_start_height_offset: float, trajectory_slot_height_offset: float, transition_check_radius: float } ] }

commands.name: get_smart_object_slots_detail
commands.description: List every slot of a USmartObjectDefinition asset with its index, name, enabled flag, offset [x, y, z] in cm and rotation [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees relative to the owner, activity_tags, whether its user tag filter is empty, its behavior classes and counts, data_count and entrance_count. Use it to find the slot_index the set_smart_object_slot_* and remove_smart_object_slot tools take, and to read back their edits; for object-level state (tags, policies, bounds, validation) use get_smart_object_definition_summary, and for entrance fields get_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotations. Read-only and idempotent; reads the asset, not a placed actor. A definition with no slots gives slot_count 0. A missing or unloadable definition_path is an error.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Object path of the USmartObjectDefinition asset, e.g. "/Game/AI/SO_Bench.SO_Bench" (the package path "/Game/AI/SO_Bench" also loads); create_smart_object_definition makes one

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_count: int, slots: [{ index: int, name: string, enabled: bool, offset: [number, number, number], rotation: [number, number, number], activity_tags: [string], user_filter_is_empty: bool, behavior_count: int, behavior_classes: [string], data_count: int }] }

commands.name: register_smart_object_actor
commands.description: Spawn an empty actor in the editor world, attach a USmartObjectComponent pointing at the given definition, and register it with USmartObjectSubsystem. Note: the definition must already have a behavior definition (per-slot or default) or the subsystem silently rejects the handle (see handle_valid).

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label for the new actor

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location; defaults to (0,0,0)

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, definition_path: string, has_component: bool, registered: bool, handle_valid: bool }

commands.name: release_smart_object
commands.description: Release a Smart Object claim. The only headless-safe path is to pass actor_label so the subsystem can unregister the component (which releases any claim it holds). FSmartObjectUserHandle is private in UE 5.7, so a claim_handle-only path is not possible without a C++ extension.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Optional editor label of the actor whose component to unregister (releases all its claims)

params.name: claim_handle
params.description: Optional canonical claim string; documented limitation: round-trip is not public in 5.7

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, released: bool } | (error: "release_smart_object: ...")

commands.name: remove_smart_object_definition_default_behavior
commands.description: Remove one definition-level default behavior (the ones slots without a behavior of their own use), found by its index in the private DefaultBehaviorDefinitions array, from a USmartObjectDefinition asset loaded by path, then save it. The array is reached through reflection, later entries shift down one index, and the removal is one undo step. A behavior_index outside the array is a success with removed=false, already_absent=true and saved=false, nothing touched, and an omitted one is an error; a repeat call with an index still in range removes the next default. default_behavior_count is what is left. A missing definition is an error; a failed save gives success false, saved=false and save_error, with the removal kept in memory. Add one: add_smart_object_definition_default_behavior; count them: get_smart_object_definition_summary; per-slot behaviors: remove_smart_object_slot_behavior_definition.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: behavior_index
params.description: Index into DefaultBehaviorDefinitions to remove

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, behavior_index: int, default_behavior_count: int, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_smart_object_slot
commands.description: Remove the slot at slot_index from a USmartObjectDefinition asset, together with its behaviors, tags and annotations; later slots shift down one index, so re-read indices with get_smart_object_slots_detail. Saves the asset; a failed save returns an error with the removal kept in memory. An invalid slot_index is an error. Undoable (one editor transaction). To turn a slot off while keeping indices stable use set_smart_object_slot_enabled; add_smart_object_slot appends one.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Index of the slot to remove

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_index: int, slot_count: int, removed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_smart_object_slot_behavior_definition
commands.description: Remove one behavior definition, found by its position in the slot's BehaviorDefinitions, from the slot at slot_index of a USmartObjectDefinition asset loaded by path, in one undo step, then save it; later behaviors shift down one index. slot_index must name a slot: an omitted or invalid one is an error. A behavior_index outside the array is a success with removed=false, already_absent=true and saved=false, nothing touched; an omitted one is an error. Because indices shift, repeating a call with an index still in range removes the next behavior: re-read the counts with get_smart_object_slots_detail between calls. A missing definition is an error; a failed save gives success false, saved=false and save_error, with the removal kept in memory. Add one: add_smart_object_slot_behavior_definition; definition-wide defaults: remove_smart_object_definition_default_behavior; the whole slot: remove_smart_object_slot.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset.

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Index of the slot to edit.

params.name: behavior_index
params.description: Index into the slot's BehaviorDefinitions to remove.

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_index: int, behavior_index: int, behavior_count: int, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotation
commands.description: Remove one entrance annotation (an entry or exit point) from the slot at slot_index of a USmartObjectDefinition asset loaded by path, in one undo step, then save it. entrance_index counts only the entrance annotations in the slot's DefinitionData, numbered as add_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotation and get_smart_object_slot_entrance_annotations number them; other annotations are skipped and kept. slot_index must name a slot: an omitted or invalid one is an error. An entrance_index matching no entrance is a success with removed=false, already_absent=true and saved=false, nothing touched, and an omitted one is an error; a repeat call with an index still in range removes the next entrance. entrance_count and data_count are what is left. A failed save gives success false, saved=false and save_error, with the removal kept in memory. The whole slot: remove_smart_object_slot.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: slot_index
params.description: Index of the slot to edit

params.name: entrance_index
params.description: Index among the slot's entrance annotations to remove (0-based; entrances only, not all definition data)

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, slot_index: int, entrance_index: int, entrance_count: int, data_count: int, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_smart_object_component_definition
commands.description: Set the USmartObjectDefinition that the USmartObjectComponent of an actor in the editor world references, found by actor_label, in one undo step when the component is transactional. The level is marked dirty and nothing is saved. A component that already references that definition is left as it is (changed false). A component bound to the Smart Object simulation is refused before anything changes, since the engine ignores the change then: unregister it with release_smart_object and actor_label first. set is read back from the component's reference and makes success false when it did not take. A missing actor, component or definition is an error. Read back with get_smart_object_component_definition; spawn one with register_smart_object_actor.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor carrying the USmartObjectComponent

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset to assign

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, definition_path: string, definition: string, registered: bool, set: bool, changed: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: set_smart_object_definition_activity_tags
commands.description: Replace the object-level activity tags of a USmartObjectDefinition asset with activity_tags, optionally set its activity-tag merging policy and user-tag filtering policy, in one undo step, then save it. The whole tag container is written: an omitted or empty list empties it, and names that are not registered gameplay tags are skipped silently (compare activity_tags in the reply); an omitted policy keeps its value. A missing definition or an unknown policy name is an error checked before anything is written, so the definition stays as it was. A call that leaves tags and policies as they were changes and saves nothing (changed false), and a failed save, as during PIE, makes success false. Per-slot tags: set_smart_object_slot_activity_tags; object-level user filter: set_smart_object_definition_user_tag_filter; read back: get_smart_object_definition_summary.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: activity_tags
params.description: Gameplay tag names for the definition's object-level activity tags; the list replaces the current tags whole

params.name: merging_policy
params.description: Optional activity-tag merging policy: "Combine" (default) or "Override"; Combine merges slot and object tags, Override lets non-empty slot tags take their place; omitted keeps the current policy

params.name: filtering_policy
params.description: Optional user-tag filtering policy: "NoFilter", "Combine", or "Override"; how the object and slot user filters apply to a request; omitted keeps the current policy

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, activity_tags: [string], merging_policy: string, filtering_policy: string, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_smart_object_definition_user_tag_filter
commands.description: Replace the object-level user tag filter of a USmartObjectDefinition asset (the gameplay tag query a user must pass to use the object) with one built from user_tags and match (any, all or none of the tags), in one undo step, then save it. Unregistered tag names are skipped (the reply lists the tags kept); a list of only such names, or any other match, is an error before anything changes. An empty or omitted user_tags clears the filter (cleared true): an empty filter refuses no user. A call that leaves the filter as it was saves nothing (changed false). A missing definition is an error; a failed save, as during PIE, makes success false. How it combines with slot filters: filtering_policy of set_smart_object_definition_activity_tags; per-slot filter: set_smart_object_slot_user_tag_filter; read back: get_smart_object_definition_summary.

params.name: definition_path
params.description: Path to the USmartObjectDefinition asset

params.name: user_tags
params.description: Gameplay tag names the filter query matches against; unregistered names are skipped, and an empty list clears the filter

params.name: match
params.description: Match mode: "any" (default), "all", or "none"; any other value is an error

commands.returns: { definition_path: string, user_tags: [string], match: string, filter_is_empty: bool, changed: bool, cleared: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_smart_object_slot_activity_tags
commands.description: Set the activity tags of the slot at slot_index in a USmartObjectDefinition asset (which activities the slot supports), in one undo step, then save it. The list is written whole: an omitted or empty list empties the tags, and names that are not registered gameplay tags are skipped silently, so compare activity_tags in the reply. A slot that already has exactly those tags changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false).
