commands.name: get_subsystem_instance_info
commands.description: Find the live instance of a subsystem class by its lifetime and read its exposed properties (EditAnywhere or Blueprint-visible, inherited included, Transient skipped), each with name, C++ type, property class, edit and blueprint_visible flags, and its value exported as text (empty when it cannot be exported); include_properties=false skips the property walk for a cheap "is it there, and what is it called" lookup. lifetime picks the host: world reads the world the world selector picks, the editor world by default; gameinstance and localplayer read the game instance of that world, the running Play-in-Editor world by default, since the editor world never has one (without PIE they fail saying so). The reply names the world it read (world_package, world_type). A missing host or instance is an error. Read-only. To enumerate use list_subsystem_instances or list_local_player_subsystems.

params.name: subsystem_class
params.description: Class of the subsystem to inspect: short reflected name (with or without the U prefix), /Script path, or a Blueprint subsystem's class path. Must derive from USubsystem.

params.name: lifetime
params.description: Which host resolves the instance: one of engine | gameinstance | world | editor | localplayer (case-insensitive).

params.name: class_name
params.description: Alias of subsystem_class.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Local player index, used only when lifetime is "localplayer" (default 0).

params.name: include_properties
params.description: Optional bool (default true). false returns the instance's identity only, with no properties walk.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector for the world, gameinstance and localplayer lifetimes, ignored by the others: editor, pie (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context), game (alias of pie), server (the PIE world with authority), client or pie:N. Absent means editor for world and pie for gameinstance and localplayer. An unrecognised value fails naming the worlds that exist

commands.returns: { subsystem_class: string, lifetime: string, subsystem_name: string, subsystem_path: string, instance_name: string, instance_path: string, property_count?: int, properties?: [{ name, cpp_type, class, edit, blueprint_visible, value }], world?: string, world_name?: string, world_package?: string, world_type?: string, net_mode?: string, pie_instance?: int } -- instance_name/instance_path repeat subsystem_name/subsystem_path; property_count and properties only with include_properties; the world fields only for the world, gameinstance and localplayer lifetimes

commands.name: list_local_player_subsystems
commands.description: Enumerate every live ULocalPlayerSubsystem-derived instance across all local players of the game instance of a Play-in-Editor world, the running PIE world by default (world picks another; world_package and world_type say which one was read). Local players exist only while PIE runs: without PIE, or for a world with no game instance such as the editor world, it is an error that says so. Read-only.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent or pie (the default, ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context), game (alias of pie), server (the PIE world with authority), client, pie:N, or editor (which has no game instance, so it fails). An unrecognised value fails naming the worlds that exist

commands.returns: { world: string, world_name: string, world_package: string, world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int, local_player_count: int, subsystem_count: int, subsystems: [{ player_index, player_name, subsystem_class, subsystem_name, subsystem_path }] }

commands.name: activate_external_subsystem
commands.description: Externally activate a Blueprint-authored USubsystem via FSubsystemCollectionBase::ActivateExternalSubsystem. Refuses to toggle native / abstract / base classes.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Short class name or /Script/ path of a Blueprint-derived USubsystem

commands.returns: { class_name: string, activated: bool }

commands.name: deactivate_external_subsystem
commands.description: Tear down a Blueprint-authored subsystem (a non-native, non-abstract USubsystem class) in every live subsystem collection of its family (engine, editor, game instance, world or local player), through the engine's external-subsystem switch: its Deinitialize runs and its runtime state is lost. Runtime only: nothing is saved and there is no undo, and a world or game instance created later builds it again. The inverse is activate_external_subsystem; check what is live with list_subsystem_instances (with class_name it answers active true or false), and find candidate classes with list_derived_classes. Native engine subsystems, the subsystem base classes and abstract classes are refused, since tearing them down can crash the editor; a class that is not found or is not a subsystem is an error. Idempotent: a repeat call, or one for a subsystem that is not active, changes nothing. deactivated is always true, since the engine call reports nothing, so confirm with list_subsystem_instances.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Blueprint subsystem class, by its Blueprint asset path (e.g. "/Game/Systems/BP_ScoreSubsystem"), generated class path, or loaded generated class name (e.g. "BP_ScoreSubsystem_C"); a native /Script/ class resolves but is refused.

commands.returns: { class_name: string, deactivated: bool }

commands.name: list_subsystem_instances
commands.description: Enumerate the USubsystem instances live right now, with each one's class path and lifetime (class default objects are skipped); with class_name it answers the yes/no question for ONE class instead -- active is whether that class (or a subclass) has any live instance, across every lifetime. A LocalPlayer subsystem only exists while a PIE session has a local player, so a headless editor lists Engine / Editor / GameInstance / World ones; list_local_player_subsystems reads a PIE player's.

params.name: lifetime
params.description: Optional filter: "Engine"|"Editor"|"GameInstance"|"World"|"LocalPlayer" (case-insensitive)

params.name: class_name
params.description: Optional USubsystem class (short name or /Script/ path): keep only the instances of that class or a subclass. A name that does not resolve to a USubsystem class is an error.

commands.returns: { total: int, instance_count: int, active: bool, lifetime_filter?, class_name?, lifetime?, instances:[{ class_name, class_path, lifetime, instance_name, instance_path }] } -- total and instance_count are the same number and active is total > 0; class_name and lifetime (the class's own lifetime category) appear when class_name was given.

commands.name: check_blueprint_errors
commands.description: Quick static check of one Blueprint without compiling it: the cached status of its last compile (an error status adds one generic line, never the compiler messages; a never-compiled Blueprint reads Unknown) plus structural findings: no parent class, a component template without a class, a variable without a name or type, an empty function or one without an entry node, and pin-less nodes. Read-only: it compiles, saves and changes nothing, so its answer can be stale after edits. error_status is Clean, Warnings Only or Errors Found. For the real compiler errors and their nodes use compile_blueprint (it recompiles); for graph bugs that compile clean, lint_blueprint_graph; for a whole folder, audit_blueprint_health. A name matching no Blueprint, or several, is an error.

params.name: blueprint_path
params.description: Object path, package path or bare short name of the Blueprint, e.g. '/Game/Blueprints/BP_Door' or 'BP_Door'; a short name several Blueprints share is an error listing the candidates.

commands.returns: { blueprint_path: string, resolved_object_path: string, blueprint_class: string, is_blueprint: bool, error_status: string, error_message: string, errors: [string], warnings: [string], error_count: int, warning_count: int, blueprint_compiled: bool, compilation_status: string, is_static_analysis: bool, recompiled_blueprint: bool, orphaned_node_heuristic: string }

commands.name: get_blueprint_debug_info
commands.description: Read a Blueprint's structure, metadata and complexity in one static report: cached compile status, file size, function/event/variable/component/node counts, function names, variables, components, a heuristic complexity score with its level, a performance rating and advice; with function_name, one function graph's node and pin counts; with include_graph_listing, every graph's nodes listed. An asset that resolves but is not a Blueprint is not an error: the reply is its identity with is_blueprint false. Read-only: nothing is compiled (compile_blueprint compiles), and nothing is executed or traced at runtime: observe runtime with set_blueprint_breakpoint (+ PIE) or watch_pie_property; the cached compile errors and structural problems are check_blueprint_errors.

params.name: blueprint_path
params.description: Object path, package path, or bare short name of the blueprint (resolved via mcp_common::ResolveAssetFlexible; ambiguity errors out listing candidates)

params.name: function_name
params.description: Optional name of one of the Blueprint's own function graphs (case-insensitive) to analyze statically: adds function_name and function_exists and, when it exists, function_node_count, function_pin_count, function_rating (Good, Moderate over 20 nodes, Complex over 50) and function_issues. The function is never executed; an unknown name is function_exists false, not an error.

params.name: include_graph_listing
params.description: Optional (default false): add a static listing of every function and event graph with its nodes, in array order rather than execution order: execution_flow, function_calls (function graph names), event_calls (event graph names), graphs_analyzed, includes_composite_subgraphs and limitations.

params.name: include_composites
params.description: Optional (default false), used with include_graph_listing: also descend into collapsed composite subgraphs (UEdGraph::SubGraphs). Macro-instance graphs are never followed.

commands.returns: { blueprint_path: string, resolved_object_path: string, blueprint_class: string, is_blueprint: bool, debug_status: string, debug_level: string, debug_message: string, file_size_bytes: int, file_size_mb: number, function_count: int, event_count: int, variable_count: int, component_count: int, total_nodes: int, parent_class: string, blueprint_compiled: bool, compilation_status: string, function_names: [string], variable_info: [{ name, type, category, is_public, is_editable }], component_info: [{ name, class, is_root }], complexity_score: number, complexity_level: string, performance_rating: string, recommendations: [string], function_name?: string, function_exists?: bool, function_node_count?: int, function_pin_count?: int, function_rating?: string, function_issues?: [string], execution_flow?: [string], function_calls?: [string], event_calls?: [string], graphs_analyzed?: int, includes_composite_subgraphs?: bool, limitations?: [string] }

commands.name: list_validators
commands.description: List the editor data validators the DataValidation subsystem has enabled (ForEachEnabledValidator): class_name, class_path and enabled for each, plus validator_count. Read-only; errors when the DataValidation plugin subsystem is unavailable. validate_asset runs them on one asset.
commands.returns: { validators: [{ class_name: string, class_path: string, enabled: bool }], validator_count: number }

commands.name: remove_blueprint_breakpoint
commands.description: Remove a debugging breakpoint from a specific node within a blueprint graph via FKismetDebugUtilities::RemoveBreakpointFromNode. Idempotent (already_absent when none exists).

params.name: blueprint_path
params.description: Object path, package path, or bare short name of the blueprint (resolved via mcp_common::ResolveAssetFlexible; ambiguity errors out listing candidates)

params.name: node_name
params.description: Name or title of the graph node to remove the breakpoint from (title-contains match)

commands.returns: { blueprint_path: string, node_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, found_in_graph: bool, node_class?: string, node_title?: string }

commands.name: run_map_check
commands.description: Run the editor's Map Check (the MAP CHECK console command) on the level open in the editor and report error, warning and info counts plus up to 200 messages, each resolved back to the actor or component the engine attached to it. Use it to find level problems such as missing meshes, actors with invalid settings or lighting that needs a rebuild; for assets use validate_asset or validate_assets_in_path, for Blueprints check_blueprint_errors. It changes no actor or asset and saves nothing, but it replaces the contents of the editor's Map Check message log (no window opens); get_message_log_entries rereads it. Severity numbers: 1 error, 2 performance warning, 3 warning, 4 info. The counts cover every message and messages_truncated says when the list was capped. Editor world only, not a PIE session; success is false when the editor did not run the command, and the counts are then stale.

params.name: check_deprecated_only
params.description: When true, runs MAP CHECKDEP: only the deprecated-class checks (optional, default false)

params.name: base_libraries
params.description: Package roots, e.g. ["/Game/Marketplace"], to classify each message's class against (optional, default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). An explicit [] disables the classification. Reported as data in class_root/class_root_is_base_library; the tool never judges which root is "upstream".

commands.returns: { world: string, map_check_ran: bool, check_deprecated_only: bool, base_libraries: [string], error_count: number, warning_count: number, info_count: number, total_messages: number, messages_truncated: bool, messages: [{ severity: number, text: string, token_source: string, object_path: string, object_resolved: bool, actor_name: string, actor_label: string, actor_path: string, actor_class: string, actor_guid: string, component_name: string, class_asset_path: string, class_root: string, class_root_is_base_library: bool }] }

commands.name: set_blueprint_breakpoint
commands.description: Add an enabled Blueprint debugger breakpoint on one node of a Blueprint's function or event graphs, found by its title, so execution pauses there in the editor's Blueprint debugger the next time Play-in-Editor reaches it. It changes editor debug state only: the asset is not modified or saved, and there is no undo step. Idempotent: a node that already has a breakpoint answers already_existed true. The first node whose title contains node_name is used (function graphs first, then event graphs; macro graphs are not searched), so pass a distinctive part of the title; no matching node answers found_in_graph false and breakpoint_set false rather than an error. Inverse: remove_blueprint_breakpoint; find node titles with get_graph_nodes. A Blueprint that does not resolve, an asset that is not a Blueprint, or a bare name matching several Blueprints is an error.

params.name: blueprint_path
params.description: Blueprint to debug: object path, package path (e.g. "/Game/BP/BP_Door") or bare asset name (e.g. "BP_Door"); a bare name matching several Blueprints is an error that lists them.

params.name: node_name
params.description: Part of the node title as the graph shows it, e.g. "Print String" or "Event BeginPlay"; matched case-insensitively against node titles (not object names), first match wins.

commands.returns: { blueprint_path: string, node_name: string, breakpoint_set: bool, already_existed: bool, found_in_graph: bool, node_class?: string, node_title?: string }

commands.name: validate_asset
commands.description: Run the editor's enabled data validators (the Data Validation plugin, in its Script use case) on one asset and report the verdict, without changing or saving it (the asset gets loaded): validation_result is Valid, Invalid or NotValidated (no validator applies to that asset), is_valid is false only for Invalid, and errors and warnings carry the validators' messages. Use it to check one asset after editing it, e.g. before a commit or a cook; for a whole folder use validate_assets_in_path, to see which validators exist list_validators, and for a level's actors run_map_check. validators_run counts the enabled validators, not the ones that applied to this asset, so a NotValidated result is the sign that none did. An asset the Asset Registry cannot find, or the Data Validation plugin being off, is an error.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Asset to validate, as an object path ("/Game/MyGame/M_Example.M_Example") or a package path ("/Game/MyGame/M_Example", which names its primary asset).

commands.returns: { asset_path: string, resolved_object_path: string, validation_result: string, is_valid: bool, errors: [string], warnings: [string], error_count: number, warning_count: number, validators_run: number }

commands.name: validate_assets_in_path
commands.description: Run the enabled editor data validators (Script use case, as validate_asset does) on every asset under a content path, recursively by default, up to max_results assets; truncated tells when more were found. Loads each asset but changes and saves nothing. Per asset: validation_result (Valid, Invalid or NotValidated), is_valid (NotValidated counts as valid), errors and warnings; totals in num_valid, num_invalid and num_not_validated. A path with no assets returns zero counts, not an error. Use validate_asset for one asset, list_validators to see which validators run.

params.name: path
params.description: Package path to scan, e.g. "/Game/MyGame".

params.name: recursive
params.description: Whether to scan sub-paths (optional, default true)

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum number of assets to validate (optional, default 1000, valid 1-100000)

commands.returns: { path: string, recursive: bool, num_assets: number, num_valid: number, num_invalid: number, num_not_validated: number, total_found: number, truncated: bool, results: [{ asset_path: string, asset_name: string, asset_class: string, validation_result: string, is_valid: bool, error_count: number, warning_count: number, errors: [string], warnings: [string] }] }

commands.name: watch_pie_property
commands.description: Sample one or SEVERAL properties across a PIE session, arming BEFORE PIE starts so a write that happens in BeginPlay is still observable. Answers "what did this value do during play", NOT "who wrote it": it SAMPLES rather than intercepting writes, so `identifies_writer` is always false and a transient A->B->A between two samples is invisible. THE ORDER MATTERS: action="start" arms and returns immediately (it cannot block the game thread), THEN you start PIE, and afterwards action="status" returns the recorded samples. Arming while PIE is ALREADY running is honoured but flagged (`armed_while_pie_running`) -- the BeginPlay window has already passed for that session, which is precisely the failure this tool exists to avoid, so stop PIE, arm, then start PIE. It self-disarms on duration_seconds or max_samples (it can never leak a ticker) and the recorded samples survive until action="clear".

params.name: action
params.description: Optional: "start" (default) | "status" | "stop" | "clear" | "list".

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property to sample on the matched object. Required for "start" unless `properties` is given.

params.name: properties
params.description: Optional array of property names sampled TOGETHER, in the SAME tick, as one ROW. This is what answers correlation questions ("movement_mode changed in the same tick immersion crossed the threshold"), which N separate watches cannot: each would dedupe on its own clock and the columns would not line up. The row is the dedup unit -- if ANY field changes the whole row is recorded -- and each sample carries a `values` object with the per-property breakdown. With one property there is no `values` object.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Optional actor class filter (exact UClass name; a Blueprint class needs the "_C" suffix). At least one of class_name / actor_label is required for "start".

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Optional actor filter, matched against the editor label OR the object name.

params.name: component
params.description: Optional component name: sample the property on that component of the matched actor instead of on the actor.

params.name: sample_interval_seconds
params.description: Optional periodic sampling interval (default 0.1, min 0.01).

params.name: duration_seconds
params.description: Optional auto-disarm after this many real seconds (default 300; 0 = no time cap, disarms only on max_samples or an explicit stop).

params.name: max_samples
params.description: Optional hard cap on recorded samples (default 400).

params.name: watch_id
params.description: Target watch for "status" / "stop" / "clear" (omit = all of them).

commands.returns: { action: string, watch_id?: int, armed?: bool, watches: [{ watch_id, property_name, class_name, actor_label, component, sample_interval_seconds, duration_seconds, max_samples, active, saw_pie_world, armed_while_pie_running, sample_count, elapsed_real_seconds, stop_reason, distinct_objects_seen, samples?: [{ phase, object_path, actor_label, value_text, value, elapsed_real_seconds, world_time_seconds, world, changed_from_previous }] }], identifies_writer: bool, sampling_only: bool, armed_pre_pie?: bool, pie_running?: bool, class_resolved?: bool, hint?: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }. The five world_* / net_mode / pie_instance fields identify the PIE world the ticker is sampling AT THE MOMENT OF THE CALL (all null / pie_instance -1 when no PIE session is running, which is the normal state right after arming).

commands.name: add_attach_track
commands.description: Add a Sequencer 3D-Attach track on a binding so it follows another binding (e.g. a prop attached to a character's hand socket) over the section's range.  The attachee binding owns a UMovieScene3DAttachTrack; AddConstraint creates an attach section pointing at the target binding.  Idempotent by (target_binding_guid, start_frame). Inverse: remove_sequence_track with binding_guid.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding to attach (the attachee; this binding owns the attach track).

params.name: target_binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding to attach TO (the parent/target).

params.name: start_frame
params.description: Optional start frame of the attach section (default: the sequence playback range start).

params.name: duration
params.description: Optional duration in frames (default: the playback range size).

params.name: socket_name
params.description: Optional socket name on the target to attach to (default: none -> target root).

params.name: component_name
params.description: Optional component name on the target to attach to (default: none).

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, target_binding_guid: string, track_added: bool, already_exists: bool, start_frame: int, duration: int, socket_name: string, component_name: string, section_count: int, track_class: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_audio_section
commands.description: Adds (or reuses) a root audio track on a Level Sequence and optionally a section.  Finds an existing root UMovieSceneAudioTrack or adds one. If sound_path loads a USoundBase, a sound section is placed at the playback range start. Inverse: remove_section without binding_guid, track_type=audio.

params.name: sequence_name

params.name: sound_path

commands.name: add_camera_cut
commands.description: Adds a camera cut section bound to a camera binding over a frame range, creating the camera cut track if it does not yet exist, then saves the sequence. The binding must exist in the sequence (get_sequence_bindings lists them), or nothing is added. Inverse: remove_section without binding_guid, track_type=cameracut.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence (first asset under /Game with that name), or its full /Game path.

params.name: camera_binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the camera binding the cut switches to.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Alias of sequence_name.

params.name: start_frame
params.description: Optional inclusive start frame in tick resolution (default 0).

params.name: end_frame
params.description: Optional exclusive end frame (default start_frame + 1); must be > start_frame.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, sequence_path: string, camera_binding_guid: string, start_frame: int, end_frame: int, track_class: string, section_class: string, section_index: int, section_count: int, section_added: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_camera_cut_track
commands.description: Add the camera cut track of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), the root track whose sections pick the camera the sequence shows, in one undo step, then save the sequence. A movie scene holds at most one: when it already has one, nothing is added, written or saved (track_added false, changed false, saved false), so a repeat call is idempotent, and a camera cut track of another class there is an error. A new track has no section. A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Cuts: add_camera_cut; a camera with its cut: create_cine_camera_in_sequence. Inverse: remove_sequence_track track_name=CameraCut.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_count: int, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: add_component_material_track
commands.description: Adds a component material parameter track for one indexed material slot to an object binding of a Level Sequence (first asset-name match under /Game), or reuses the binding's existing track for that slot, and saves the sequence. With parameter_name it keys that scalar parameter at frame (a tick-resolution frame) and reads the key back: success requires it, and a key the engine would skip (locked section, read-only sequence) is refused before anything is written; without it, it only adds a section spanning the playback range when the track has none. The slot index is not checked against the bound component, which is not resolved. An unknown binding_guid or a material_index that is not a whole number >= 0 is an error. For a Material Parameter Collection use add_material_parameter_collection_track; for other animated properties use add_property_track. Inverse: remove_sequence_track with binding_guid.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence

params.name: binding_guid

params.name: material_index

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Optional scalar material parameter name to key

params.name: value
