params.name: frame
params.description: Optional frame number for the key (default 0)

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, material_index: int, material_type: string, parameter_name: string, value: number, key_added: bool (read back from the track), section_added: bool (the track gained a section, keying included), scalar_channel_count: int, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_event_track_section
commands.description: Append a new UMovieSceneEventSection to the existing UMovieSceneEventTrack on the sequence. Inverse: remove_section without binding_guid, track_type=event.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path of the Level Sequence.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: start_frame
params.description: Inclusive start frame for the new event section (default 0).

params.name: end_frame
params.description: Exclusive end frame for the new event section (default = start_frame + 1).

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, track_class: string, section_index: int, section_count: int, start_frame: int, end_frame: int, section_class: string, section_added: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_event_track_to_sequence
commands.description: Add a new root event track (UMovieSceneEventTrack) to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), in one undo step, then save the sequence. Every call adds another track, even when the sequence already has one, and the new track has no sections (section_count 0). Add trigger sections with add_event_track_section, which appends to the first event track of the sequence. A sequence that is not found is an error; a failed save (for example during PIE) makes success false with saved=false and save_error. List root tracks with get_sequence_tracks; the inverse is remove_sequence_track; for a fade track use add_fade_track_to_sequence.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, track_class: string, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_fade_track_to_sequence
commands.description: Add the root fade track of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), with a fade section spanning the playback range, in one undo step, then save the sequence. A fade track already there is reused and gets a section only when it has none, so a repeat call is idempotent: a fade track that already has a section is left as it is, with nothing written or saved (track_added and section_added false, changed false, saved false). A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. List root tracks with get_sequence_tracks; inverse: remove_sequence_track.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, section_class: string, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: add_keyframe_to_property_track
commands.description: Adds a keyframe to a property track's section channel(s) at the given time, in one undo step, then saves the sequence. The property track must already exist (call add_property_track first); property_name picks which one when the binding has several tracks of that type. The value is keyed onto every channel of the section. By default a key already at that tick frame is updated in place; interp_mode (float/vector/color tracks only) instead INSERTS a key with that interpolation -- linear, constant, or cubic with explicit broken arrive_tangent/leave_tangent -- even on an occupied frame. Read keys back with get_channel_keyframes, retime one with move_keyframe.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding owning the property track.

params.name: property_type
params.description: One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility".

params.name: time_seconds
params.description: Time (seconds, >= 0) at which to place the key; rounded to the nearest tick frame.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional name or path of the property whose track takes the key, case ignored; omitted, the first track of property_type on the binding. A name no track of that type animates is an error that lists the ones it does.

params.name: value
params.description: Key value. For Float: a scalar. For Bool/Visibility: a bool. For Vector/Color: a list of numbers (Vector/Color). Defaults to 0 / [] if omitted.

params.name: interp_mode
params.description: Optional, float channels only: "cubic", "linear" or "constant". When given the key is inserted with that interpolation instead of updating one at that frame.

params.name: arrive_tangent
params.description: Optional tangent for interp_mode "cubic" (default 0).

params.name: leave_tangent
params.description: Optional tangent for interp_mode "cubic" (default 0).

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, property_type: string, property_name: string, time_seconds: float, key_frame: int, keys_added: int, channel_count: int, key_index: int, key_count: int, interp_mode?: string, arrive_tangent?: float, leave_tangent?: float, saved: bool, save_error?: string } -- key_index and key_count describe the section's first channel; property_name is the property of the track that took the key.

commands.name: add_level_visibility_track
commands.description: Add a root level-visibility track (UMovieSceneLevelVisibilityTrack) to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, or reuse the one it has, give it a section spanning the playback range when it has none, and set that section's streamed-level visibility, in one undo step, then save the sequence. Idempotent: a repeat call reuses the track and its first section and overwrites their visibility, and their level names when level_names is non-empty, with the values passed; visible defaults to true, so omitting it sets an existing section back to Visible. A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. For an actor's own visibility use add_property_track (property_type=Visibility, property_name=bVisible); list root tracks with get_sequence_tracks; the inverse is remove_sequence_track.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case.

params.name: visible
params.description: Optional bool, default true (levels Visible); false makes them Hidden. Written on every call.

params.name: level_names
params.description: Optional array of streamed-level short names the section controls, e.g. ["Sublevel_Interior"]; a non-empty array overwrites the section's list, an empty or omitted one keeps it.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, section_class: string, visibility: string, level_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_marked_frame
commands.description: Adds a marked frame (a labelled marker on the Sequencer timeline) at a tick-resolution frame of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, in one undo step, and saves the sequence; is_determinism_fence turns the same mark into an evaluation fence. Idempotent per frame: an existing mark at that frame is updated instead of duplicated, its label replaced when one is given and both flags overwritten with the values passed (false when omitted); already_existed says which. When the mark already has both flags and the label given (or no label is given), the call changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false). Read marks with get_marked_frames, delete one with remove_marked_frame.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: frame
params.description: Tick frame number to mark.

params.name: label
params.description: Optional human-readable label (auto-generated if empty).

params.name: is_determinism_fence
params.description: Optional bool (default false): treat the mark as an evaluation fence (cannot be crossed in one evaluation).

params.name: is_inclusive
params.description: Optional bool (default false): when a determinism fence, how the previous/next ranges are dissected ((X,Y]->(Y,Z] vs (X,Y)->[Y,Z]).

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, frame: int, mark_index: int, label: string, is_determinism_fence: bool, is_inclusive: bool, already_existed: bool, marked_frame_count: int, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: add_material_parameter_collection_track
commands.description: Add a Material Parameter Collection root track bound to an existing MPC asset to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, or reuse its MPC track already bound to that collection, in one undo step, then save the sequence. With parameter_name it keys that scalar parameter at frame (a tick-resolution frame) with value, and key_added is read back: a key the engine skips (locked section, read-only sequence) leaves key_added false without failing the call. Without parameter_name it only gives the track a playback-range section when it has none. The parameter name is not checked against the collection. A missing sequence or MPC is an error; a failed save makes success false. Component material slot: add_component_material_track; a new collection parameter: add_collection_parameter.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case.

params.name: mpc_path
params.description: Object path of an existing UMaterialParameterCollection asset (e.g. /Game/MyGame/MPC_X)

params.name: parameter_name
params.description: Optional scalar parameter name to key on the MPC track; not checked against the collection. Omit it to add only the track and a section.

params.name: value
params.description: Optional scalar value for the keyed parameter (default 0.0)

params.name: frame
params.description: Optional key frame in the sequence's tick resolution, not display-rate frames (default 0); fractions are truncated.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, mpc_path: string, mpc_name: string, parameter_name: string, value: number, key_added: bool, section_added: bool, scalar_channel_count: int, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_property_track
commands.description: Adds a typed property track + section to a Level Sequence binding.  The track animates a named property on the bound object (e.g. property_type Float with "Intensity", Visibility with "bVisible"). A section spanning the movie scene's playback range is created so keys evaluate. Inverse: remove_sequence_track with binding_guid.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence (found by AssetName under /Game), or its full /Game path.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of an existing binding (possessable or spawnable).

params.name: property_type
params.description: One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility".

params.name: property_name
params.description: Name of the animated property (e.g. "RelativeLocation", "Intensity", "bHidden"). Used as both the property name and path.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, property_type: string, property_name: string, track_class: string, section_class: string, section_created: bool, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_sequence_folder
commands.description: Create a Sequencer outliner folder on a Level Sequence's movie scene (root folder, or a child of a named parent), inside an undo transaction, and save the sequence; success requires the save. Idempotent by name: a folder that already exists succeeds with already_existed true and saved false (nothing is written).

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Asset path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: folder_name
params.description: Name of the folder to create.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: parent_folder
params.description: Optional name of an existing parent folder; if given, the new folder is nested under it instead of at the root.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, folder_name: string, parent_folder: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, root_folder_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_shot_section
commands.description: Adds a cinematic shot section (UMovieSceneCinematicShotSection) to the shot track and saves the sequence.  Creates the cinematic shot track if it does not exist yet. The inner shot sequence is shot_sequence_path, or <target name>_Shot in the target's folder when omitted; it is loaded when it exists, else created and saved as a new asset (inner_sequence_created says which). An inner shot sequence that cannot be loaded, created or saved (a new one that fails to save stays in memory only), that is the target itself or that already plays it at any depth is an error and nothing is added. success is false, with save_error, when the save of the target fails. Inverse: remove_section without binding_guid, track_type=shot.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: shot_sequence_path
params.description: Optional content path of the inner shot Level Sequence. If omitted, an inner shot Level Sequence is created and persisted.

params.name: start_frame
params.description: Inclusive start frame for the shot section (default 0).

params.name: duration
params.description: Section duration in tick frames (default 150).

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, inner_sequence_created: bool (true only when this call created the inner sequence), shot_name: string, shot_sequence_path: string, start_frame: int, duration: int, section_count: int, section_class: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_shot_track
commands.description: Make sure a Level Sequence has its cinematic shot track (UMovieSceneCinematicShotTrack), the root track that holds shot sections, adding it when missing, in one undo step, then save the sequence. Idempotent: a sequence that already has one keeps it (track_added=false; section_count counts its shots), though the sequence is saved again either way. add_shot_section also creates this track when missing, so call this one only to get an empty shot track; list tracks with get_sequence_tracks; remove_sequence_track is the inverse. The sequence must already exist (create_level_sequence). An unknown sequence is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the track kept in memory.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path, e.g. "/Game/Cinematics/LS_Intro", OR bare asset name "LS_Intro" (the first Level Sequence under /Game with that name); get_level_sequences lists them.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_skeletal_animation_track
commands.description: Adds a skeletal-animation track to a Level Sequence binding.  If anim_path loads a UAnimSequenceBase (a UAnimMontage qualifies), a section is added starting at the playback range start; otherwise just the empty track. Inverse: remove_sequence_track with binding_guid; one section: remove_section.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of an existing binding (typically a SkeletalMeshActor).

params.name: anim_path
params.description: Optional content path of a UAnimSequenceBase or UAnimMontage, e.g. "/Game/Anims/MyAnim".

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, anim_loaded: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, anim_path: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_slomo_track
commands.description: Add the root time-dilation (slomo) track of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), with a section spanning the playback range, and key dilation at frame, in one undo step, then save the sequence. A slomo track already there is reused with its first section; the key overwrites a key at that tick frame whole, interpolation included, or is added. A track whose section already holds that very key at that frame changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false), so a repeat call is idempotent. This is asset data, not the PIE player play rate. A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Change the key's interpolation with set_keyframe_interpolation.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence

params.name: dilation
params.description: Optional time-dilation multiplier (default 1.0; <1 slower, >1 faster)

params.name: frame
params.description: Optional frame number for the dilation key (default 0)

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, section_class: string, dilation: number, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: add_spawnable_to_sequence
commands.description: Add a spawnable binding to a Level Sequence asset: the sequence itself spawns an actor of class_name while it plays and despawns it after, so no level actor is needed or created now and no open Sequencer is needed. To animate an actor already placed in the level use bind_actor_to_sequence (a possessable) instead; for a keyed camera with its camera cut use create_cine_camera_in_sequence. Each call adds another binding (not idempotent). One undo step, then the sequence is saved. Pass the returned binding_guid to add_transform_track_to_binding and the other binding tools; list bindings with get_sequence_bindings; remove_sequence_binding is the inverse. An unknown sequence or a class that is not an AActor subclass is an error and nothing is added; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the binding kept in memory.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name (not a path) of the target Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro": the first Level Sequence under /Game with that name, case-insensitive; get_level_sequences lists them, create_level_sequence makes one.

params.name: class_name
params.description: AActor subclass to spawn: "CineCameraActor" (default), "StaticMeshActor", "PointLight", another native class by short name (e.g. "SkeletalMeshActor"), or a path such as "/Script/Engine.SkyLight" or a Blueprint's "/Game/BP_Door.BP_Door_C".

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, class_name: string, spawnable: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_subcomponent_possessable
commands.description: Adds a component possessable as a child of an existing binding (possessable or spawnable) of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, in an undo transaction, and saves the sequence; each call adds a new one, named possessable_name or else the component_class text. It records name, class and parent only: no component object is bound to it. To possess an actual component of an editor-world actor use bind_component_to_sequence; for whole actors use bind_actor_to_sequence or add_spawnable_to_sequence. An unknown parent GUID, an unresolvable class, or a class that is not an ActorComponent is an error.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the level sequence asset.

params.name: parent_binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the parent binding (spawnable or possessable).

params.name: component_class
params.description: Component class name (e.g. 'StaticMeshComponent', 'SpotLightComponent').

params.name: possessable_name
params.description: Optional override name for the new possessable.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, possessable_guid: string, component_class: string, parent_guid: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_subsequence_track
commands.description: Nests one Level Sequence in another: finds the target's first root track of exactly the subsequence class (never a cinematic shot track or another subclass) or adds one, adds a sub section playing the inner sequence from start_frame for duration tick-resolution frames, and saves the target. The inner sequence is sub_sequence_path, or <target name>_Sub in the target's folder when omitted; it is loaded when it exists, else created and saved as a new asset (inner_sequence_created says which). Each call adds another section. An inner sequence that cannot be loaded, created or saved (a new one that fails to save stays in memory only), that is the target itself, or that already plays the target at any depth is an error and nothing is added. success is false, with save_error, when the save of the target fails. For cinematic shots use add_shot_track. One sub-sequence section: remove_section without binding_guid, track_type=sub; the whole track: remove_sequence_track.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/SUBSEQ_Example") OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: sub_sequence_path
params.description: Optional content path of the sub Level Sequence to nest. If omitted, a sibling inner Level Sequence is created and persisted.

params.name: start_frame
params.description: Inclusive start frame for the sub section (default 0).

params.name: duration
params.description: Section duration in tick frames (default 150).

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, inner_sequence_created: bool (true only when this call created the inner sequence), start_frame: int, duration: int, section_count: int, sub_sequence_path: string, sub_sequence_name: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_transform_keyframe
commands.description: Adds one transform keyframe (9 double channels) at a time on a binding's transform section.  Requires a transform track to already exist (call add_transform_track_to_binding first).

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding.

params.name: time_seconds
params.description: Time of the key in seconds (>= 0). Converted to ticks via tick resolution.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] scale (default 1,1,1).

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, time_seconds: float, key_frame: int, keys_added: int, channel_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_transform_track_to_binding
commands.description: Give one binding of a Level Sequence a 3D transform track (location, rotation, scale) with a section over the playback range, so the bound actor can be animated. Use it before add_transform_keyframe, which needs it; the binding comes from add_spawnable_to_sequence or bind_actor_to_sequence (get_sequence_bindings lists them). Other track kinds on a binding: add_property_track, add_skeletal_animation_track, add_attach_track. Idempotent: a binding that already has a transform track keeps it and its first section (track_added and section_created false); a track with no section gets one. An unknown sequence, a malformed GUID or a GUID that is not a binding of the sequence is an error and nothing changes. One undo step, then the sequence is saved; a failed save answers success false with the change kept in memory. Remove it with remove_sequence_track (track_name "MovieScene3DTransformTrack" and the same binding_guid).

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not a path, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the one with that name under /Game is used.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding, e.g. "8E2F14A64B7D5C3E9A1B2C3D4E5F6071", as add_spawnable_to_sequence, bind_actor_to_sequence or get_sequence_bindings return it.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_created: bool, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: bind_actor_to_sequence
commands.description: Adds a possessable binding to a Level Sequence for an existing editor-world actor, and with property_name + property_type also adds a typed property track (with a section spanning the playback range) to it -- the bind+animate flow in one call. Idempotent per actor: an actor the sequence already possesses keeps its binding (binding_created false), and without a property to add nothing changes or is saved.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label (or name) of the actor in the current editor world to possess.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional property of the actor to animate (e.g. "bHidden"); needs property_type. Used as both the property name and path.

params.name: property_type
params.description: Optional, with property_name: one of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility".

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, actor_name: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, possessable: bool, binding_created: bool, property_name?: string, property_type?: string, track_class?: string, section_class?: string, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string } -- the property fields only when a track was added.

commands.name: bind_component_to_sequence
commands.description: Adds a possessable binding for an actor's component to a Level Sequence, and with property_name + property_type also adds a typed property track (with a section spanning the playback range) to that new binding. Resolves the actor by label in the current editor world, finds the named component (by component name, class name, or "root"), adds a possessable for the component class, binds the component, and parents the component binding to the actor's binding when the actor is already possessed. Every call makes a NEW component possessable; when the track step fails the new binding stays.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Label (or name) of the actor in the current editor world.

params.name: component_name
params.description: Component object name, component class name, or "root".

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: property_name
params.description: Optional component property to animate (e.g. "Intensity"); needs property_type. Used as both property name and path, and not checked against the component.

params.name: property_type
params.description: Optional, with property_name: one of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility".

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, parent_binding_guid?: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, component_bound: bool, parented_to_actor: bool, possessable_count: int, property_name?: string, property_type?: string, track_class?: string, section_class?: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string } -- the property fields only when a track was added.

commands.name: create_cine_camera_in_sequence
commands.description: Adds a keyed camera to an existing Level Sequence in one call: a new spawnable CineCameraActor binding, a transform track whose section spans the playback range with location, rotation and scale 1 keyed at frame 0, and a camera cut bound to that camera over the whole playback range (the camera cut track is added when missing). One undo step; then saves the sequence, and success requires the save. Each call adds another camera and cut; on a sequence that already has cuts the engine re-sorts them and the new cut overlaps them. The sequence must exist (create_level_sequence; get_level_sequences lists names). For another spawnable class use add_spawnable_to_sequence, for a cut to an existing binding add_camera_cut, for more keys add_transform_keyframe; get_sequence_bindings reads the result.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not a path (e.g. "Intro"): the first Level Sequence under /Game with that name, case-insensitive.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] world location in cm for the camera's key at frame 0 (default [0, 0, 0]).

params.name: rotation
params.description: Optional rotation in degrees for the key at frame 0: object {"pitch": P, "yaw": Y, "roll": R} (missing axes 0) or array [pitch, yaw, roll]; default all 0.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, class_name: string, spawnable: bool, transform_keyed: bool, camera_cut_added: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: create_level_sequence
commands.description: Creates a Level Sequence asset at package_path/sequence_name and saves it, with playback range [0, duration) and frame_rate, truncated to whole fps, as both tick resolution and display rate; the end frame is duration times that whole rate, to the nearest frame. If that asset already exists it is loaded and those settings are overwritten, its keys, sections and ranges migrated to the new rate so nothing moves in time; sequence_created tells a new asset from an existing one. Not undoable; another asset class at the path, or a duration shorter than one frame, is an error. To retime an existing sequence use set_sequence_frame_rate or set_sequence_settings (duration); list sequences with get_level_sequences.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the new sequence to create

params.name: package_path
params.description: Target content path, defaults to /Game/Sequences

params.name: duration
params.description: Playback duration in seconds, above 0 and at most 3600, default 10

params.name: frame_rate
params.description: Frame rate in fps, at least 1 and at most 120, truncated to whole fps, default 30

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, package_path: string, duration: number, frame_rate: number, sequence_created: bool (false when the asset already existed), saved: bool, asset_path: string, playback_range_set: bool, tick_rate_set: bool, actual_start_frame: int, actual_end_frame: int }

commands.name: duplicate_keyframe
commands.description: Copy the value of one existing key to another time on a property track of a Level Sequence binding, in one undo step, then save the sequence. The sequence is found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match); property_type picks the binding's first track of that type (first section) and channel_index the channel, one per component for Vector and Color. Both times are seconds rounded to tick frames, and the source key must sit exactly on its frame or the call is an error. Only the value is copied, not interpolation or tangents; a key at the destination is overwritten, one equal to the copy is a no-op (changed false, saved false), so a repeat is idempotent. A failed save gives success false, saved=false and save_error. Move instead: move_keyframe; drop: remove_keyframe; list: get_channel_keyframes; fix the copy's interpolation: set_binding_channel_keyframe_interpolation.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding owning the property track.

params.name: property_type
params.description: One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility".

params.name: source_time_seconds
params.description: Time (seconds) of the source key to copy.

params.name: dest_time_seconds
params.description: Destination time (seconds) for the cloned key.

params.name: channel_index
params.description: Index of the channel to read/write (default 0).

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, property_type: string, source_time_seconds: float, dest_time_seconds: float, source_frame: int, dest_frame: int, channel_index: int, duplicated_value: string, keys_written: int, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: get_audio_section_properties
commands.description: Read the playback settings of one audio section of a Level Sequence (path or bare name): the first root audio track, section by section_index. Use it instead of get_properties because it evaluates what no UPROPERTY holds directly: volume and pitch sampled at frame 0, the key counts of the animated volume/pitch channels, and looping via IsRepeating(); it also reports sound, start offset and attenuation override. Pure reader (no transaction, no save); write with set_audio_section_properties.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the Level Sequence that owns the (root) audio track.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: section_index
params.description: Index of the section on the resolved root audio track (default 0).

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, section_class: string, section_index: int, sound_path: string, start_offset: int, volume: number, pitch: number, volume_key_count: int, pitch_key_count: int, looping: bool, play_until_finished?: bool (needs UE 5.8), suppress_subtitles: bool, override_attenuation: bool, attenuation_path: string }

commands.name: get_channel_keyframes
commands.description: Lists every key of one channel of one section of a Level Sequence: index, tick-resolution frame, time in seconds and value, plus interpolation, tangent mode and tangents for double and float channels (bool keys have none). The section is resolved like get_section_info (binding_guid, track_type or track_index, section_index; a root track without binding_guid); channel_type and channel_index pick the channel. Read-only: nothing is modified or saved; an empty channel returns key_count 0, and a missing sequence, track, section or channel is an error. Use it to find the index or frame that move_keyframe, remove_keyframe, duplicate_keyframe and set_binding_channel_keyframe_interpolation take, and to check add_transform_keyframe or add_keyframe_to_property_track; get_section_info reads the section's range and settings.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game object path (e.g. "/Game/Cinematics/Intro.Intro") or bare asset name ("Intro") of the Level Sequence; a bare name, or a path that does not load, resolves to the first Level Sequence under /Game with that asset name.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path, read when sequence_path is absent or empty; same formats.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding whose section to read, as get_sequence_bindings returns it. Omit it (and binding_name_or_guid) for a section of a ROOT track -- shot, camera cut, audio, event, sub-sequence, fade: track_type or track_index then pick among the root tracks in get_sequence_tracks order, camera cut last.

params.name: track_type
params.description: Optional track kind; the first track of exactly that kind wins, else the first subclass: transform, float, bool, vector, color, visibility, audio, event, fade, skeletalanimation, sub, cameracut, shot, slomo, property, attach. An unrecognised value is ignored and track_index is used.

params.name: track_index
params.description: 0-based index into the binding's tracks, or into the root tracks without binding_guid, in get_sequence_tracks order (default 0); used when track_type is omitted.

params.name: section_index
params.description: 0-based index of the section on the resolved track (default 0); out of range is an error.

params.name: channel_type
params.description: Channel value kind: "double" (default; transform tracks) | "float" (float, color and other property tracks) | "bool" (bool and visibility tracks). Aliases transform, scalar, color, boolean, visibility are accepted; anything else is an error.

params.name: channel_index
params.description: 0-based index among the section's channels of that kind (default 0); on a transform section 0-2 = location X/Y/Z, 3-5 = rotation roll/pitch/yaw, 6-8 = scale X/Y/Z.

params.name: binding_name_or_guid
params.description: Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, channel_index: int, channel_type: string, key_count: int, keyframes: [{ index: int, frame: int, time_seconds: number, value: number|bool, interp_mode: string, tangent_mode: string, arrive_tangent: number, leave_tangent: number }] }

commands.name: get_level_sequence_status_runtime
commands.description: Read the playback state of a runtime Level Sequence player in a PIE or game world, found by the player_key play_level_sequence_runtime returned, without changing it: status (Playing, Paused or Stopped), the playing, paused and reversed flags, current_time and duration in seconds, frame_rate in frames per second and playback_progress as a percentage (0 to 100; 0 for a zero-length sequence). Use it to check the effect of pause_level_sequence_runtime, resume_level_sequence_runtime or set_level_sequence_time_runtime; for a sequence asset's length and frame rates without any player use get_timeline_info instead. A key that was never issued, was released by stop_level_sequence_runtime, or whose player was destroyed (ending PIE destroys them all) is an error saying to call play_level_sequence_runtime first.

params.name: player_key
params.description: The player_key string play_level_sequence_runtime returned in this editor session; keys do not survive the end of PIE.

commands.returns: { player_key: string, status: string, is_playing: bool, is_paused: bool, is_reversed: bool, current_time: number, duration: number, frame_rate: number, playback_progress: number }

commands.name: get_level_sequences
commands.description: List the Level Sequence assets under a content folder and its subfolders (default /Game) from the asset registry, without loading or changing anything: per sequence its name, package_path, asset_path and class. Use it to find the sequence_name or path that get_timeline_info, get_sequence_tracks, play_timeline, set_timeline_time and play_level_sequence_runtime take; for any asset type use find_assets_by_name; to make one use create_level_sequence. At most max_results entries come back, in registry order: total_count is the number of sequences found, returned_count the number listed, and truncated is true when total_count is larger, so narrow package_path or raise max_results. A folder with none gives an empty list; a max_results outside 1 to 10000 is an error.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Long package path of the folder to search, subfolders included, e.g. "/Game/Cinematics" (default "/Game"; plugin content needs its own root such as "/MyPlugin").

params.name: max_results
params.description: Maximum number of sequences to return, an integer from 1 to 10000 (default 1000).

commands.returns: { sequences: [object], total_count: int (found under package_path), returned_count: int (listed, at most max_results), max_results: int, truncated: bool }

commands.name: get_marked_frames
commands.description: Lists the user marked frames (labelled timeline markers) of a Level Sequence in stored order, each with its index, tick-resolution frame, label and determinism-fence flags, plus whether the marks are locked. Read-only: loads the sequence, changes and saves nothing; a sequence without marks returns an empty list and count 0, an unknown name is an error. Use it to get the index, frame or label that remove_marked_frame takes, and to check add_marked_frame, which adds or updates a mark; lock marks with set_sequence_settings (marked_frames_locked). Sequence names come from get_level_sequences; tracks and sections are read with get_sequence_tracks.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not a path (e.g. "Intro"): the first Level Sequence under /Game with that name, case-insensitive.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, marked_frames: [{index, frame, label, is_determinism_fence, is_inclusive}], marked_frame_count: int, marked_frames_locked: bool }

commands.name: get_section_info
commands.description: Read the settings of one section of a Level Sequence: start_frame and end_frame (tick-resolution frames, end exclusive; 0 for an open, infinite bound), ease-in and ease-out lengths and whether they are manual, completion_mode (keep_state, restore_state or project_default), blend_type (absolute, additive, relative, additive_from_base, override, or invalid when unset), is_locked, is_active and, for a 3D-attach section, its six attach_rules. The section is found by binding_guid (none for a root track such as a shot, camera cut or audio track), then track_type or track_index, then section_index: get_sequence_tracks lists tracks with section counts, get_sequence_bindings the bindings. The read side of set_section_properties, set_section_range and set_attach_section_rules. Read-only and idempotent; reads the asset, no open Sequencer needed. An unknown sequence, an invalid GUID, a binding without tracks, a track_type with no such track, or an index out of range is an error.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path, e.g. "/Game/Cinematics/LS_Intro", OR bare asset name "LS_Intro" of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding whose section to inspect, as get_sequence_bindings or get_sequence_tracks gives it. Omit it (and binding_name_or_guid) for a section of a ROOT track -- shot, camera cut, audio, event, sub-sequence, fade: track_type or track_index then pick among the root tracks in get_sequence_tracks order, camera cut last.

params.name: track_type
params.description: Optional kind of track, case-insensitive: "transform"|"float"|"bool"|"vector"|"color"|"visibility"|"audio"|"event"|"fade"|"skeletalanimation"|"subsequence"|"cameracut"|"shot"|"slomo"|"property"|"attach"; the first track of that kind wins and none is an error; any other value is ignored and track_index picks.

params.name: track_index
params.description: Index into the binding's tracks (0 = first track, default 0), in get_sequence_tracks order. Without binding_guid it indexes the root tracks.

params.name: section_index
params.description: Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0); get_sequence_tracks gives each track's section_count.

params.name: binding_name_or_guid
params.description: Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, section_index: int, start_frame: int, end_frame: int, ease_in_frames: int, ease_out_frames: int, manual_ease_in: bool, manual_ease_out: bool, completion_mode: string, blend_type: string, blend_type_valid: bool, is_locked: bool, is_active: bool, is_attach_section: bool, attach_rules: object? }

commands.name: get_sequence_bindings
commands.description: Lists the object bindings of a Level Sequence, the first asset under /Game whose name matches sequence_name (case-insensitive), with each binding's bound class, parent GUID, spawn ownership and tracks (class, display name, section count, is_empty); read-only, needs no open Sequencer. kind narrows it to possessables or spawnables, binding_guid to one binding. spawnable is true when the binding has a spawn track (a spawnable is recorded as a possessable plus a spawn track) and possessable otherwise; possessable_count and spawnable_count are the movie scene's own counts and can disagree with those flags. Root tracks are not listed: use get_sequence_tracks. Change a spawnable's ownership with set_spawn_ownership; one section's range, easing and blend come from get_section_info.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: kind
params.description: Optional 'all' (default), 'possessable' or 'spawnable' (case-insensitive): which bindings to list.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: Optional GUID of one binding to list alone; an invalid GUID, or one the sequence has no binding for, is an error.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, kind: string, binding_guid?: string, bindings: [{guid, name, spawnable, possessable, class, parent_guid, spawn_ownership, track_count, tracks: [{class, display_name, section_count, is_empty}]}], binding_count: int, possessable_count: int, spawnable_count: int } -- class is the bound (or spawned) actor class, "null" when unknown; parent_guid is "" for a top-level binding; spawn_ownership (InnerSequence, RootSequence or External) is "" unless the binding is a spawnable custom binding.

commands.name: get_sequence_folders
commands.description: Reads the Sequencer outliner folder tree of a Level Sequence: each root folder with its child folders nested to any depth, the root tracks it holds (class and track name) and the object-binding GUIDs it holds. Read-only: nothing is modified or saved; a sequence without folders returns an empty list, and a sequence that cannot be found is an error. Use it to check add_sequence_folder, remove_sequence_folder and move_track_to_folder, and to get the folder_name they take. Tracks and bindings outside every folder are not listed here: get_sequence_tracks and get_sequence_bindings give the full flat lists.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game object path (e.g. "/Game/Cinematics/Intro.Intro") or bare asset name ("Intro") of the Level Sequence; a bare name, or a path that does not load, resolves to the first Level Sequence under /Game with that asset name. get_level_sequences lists them.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path, read when sequence_path is absent or empty; same formats.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, root_folder_count: int, folders: [{ name: string, child_folders: [...recursive...], child_tracks: [{class, name}], child_bindings: [guid_string] }] }

commands.name: get_sequence_tracks
commands.description: Lists the tracks of a Level Sequence, given as a bare asset name (the first asset under /Game whose name matches, case-insensitive) or a /Game path: root (master) tracks, the camera cut track included, with display name, track name, class and section count, then each object binding (guid, display name) with its own tracks nested, plus totals -- track counts, section count and a per-class breakdown. Read-only; needs no open Sequencer. total_track_count is the number of tracks listed: root tracks plus every binding's tracks. For spawnable/possessable flags and one binding's tracks use get_sequence_bindings.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target level sequence, or its /Game path

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Alias of sequence_name

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, sequence_path: string, master_tracks: [{display_name, track_name, class, section_count}], bindings: [{guid, display_name, tracks: [{display_name, track_name, class, section_count}]}], master_track_count: int, binding_count: int, binding_track_count: int, total_track_count: int, total_section_count: int, distinct_class_count: int, class_breakdown: [{class, count}] } -- class_breakdown counts every listed track by class, most frequent first.

commands.name: get_timeline_info
commands.description: Reads the timeline summary of a Level Sequence asset (first asset-name match under /Game); needs no open Sequencer and changes nothing. Returns asset_path, start_frame and end_frame in ticks (the playback range), duration in seconds, tick_resolution and display_rate each with numerator and denominator, and track, binding, possessable and spawnable counts. master_track_count counts the root tracks, the camera cut track included, as get_sequence_tracks lists them.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path (e.g. "LS_Intro"); the first match under /Game is used

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, asset_path: string, start_frame: int, end_frame: int, duration: number, tick_resolution: number, tick_resolution_numerator: int, tick_resolution_denominator: int, display_rate: number, display_rate_numerator: int, display_rate_denominator: int, master_track_count: int, binding_count: int, possessable_count: int, spawnable_count: int } -- start_frame/end_frame are tick-resolution frames, not display frames; tick_resolution is the rate set_sequence_frame_rate changes together with display_rate.

commands.name: move_keyframe
commands.description: Move one key of a channel of one section on an object-binding track of a Level Sequence to new_frame, keeping its value, interpolation and tangents, in one undo step, then save the sequence. The key is found by index, or by frame within tolerance; channel_type (double, float or bool) and channel_index pick the channel, and the section is resolved like get_section_info. Another key already at new_frame is removed, so a repeat call is idempotent. A key already alone at new_frame changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false), with moved false. A missing key or channel is an error before anything changes. Remove a key: remove_keyframe; list keys: get_channel_keyframes.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: new_frame
params.description: Destination frame number for the key.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding whose section to edit. Omit it (and binding_name_or_guid) for a section of a ROOT track -- shot, camera cut, audio, event, sub-sequence, fade: track_type or track_index then pick among the root tracks in get_sequence_tracks order, camera cut last.

params.name: track_type
params.description: Optional class filter (see set_section_properties) selecting the track on the binding.

params.name: track_index
params.description: Index into the binding's tracks (default 0; used when track_type omitted). Without binding_guid it indexes the root tracks.

params.name: section_index
params.description: Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0).

params.name: channel_type
params.description: Channel value kind: "double" (default) | "float" | "bool".

params.name: channel_index
params.description: Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0).

params.name: index
params.description: Index of the key to move (mutually exclusive with frame).

params.name: frame
params.description: Frame of the key to move (resolved via FindKey; provide index OR frame).

params.name: tolerance
params.description: Optional FindKey frame tolerance when locating by frame (default 0).

params.name: binding_name_or_guid
params.description: Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, channel_index: int, channel_type: string, old_frame: int, new_frame: int, key_index: int, moved: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: move_track_to_folder
commands.description: Moves one root (master) track, picked by class, or one object binding, picked by GUID, into an existing Sequencer outliner folder of a Level Sequence, taking it out of any other folder, in one undo step, then saves the sequence; success requires the save. Only the outliner grouping changes: sections, keys and playback stay as they were. Idempotent: a track or binding already in that folder succeeds with already_present true and saved false (nothing is written). Refused with nothing changed when the folder is missing (create it with add_sequence_folder), the GUID is not a binding of the sequence, no track or several tracks of that class match (pass track_name), or both or neither of track_class and binding_guid are given. Check the result with get_sequence_folders; level actors go in folders with set_actor_folder instead.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game object path (e.g. "/Game/Cinematics/Intro.Intro") or bare asset name ("Intro") of the Level Sequence; a bare name, or a path that does not load, resolves to the first Level Sequence under /Game with that asset name.

params.name: folder_name
params.description: Name of the destination folder, as get_sequence_folders lists it; searched depth-first through all folders, the first with that name wins.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path, read when sequence_path is absent or empty; same formats.

params.name: track_class
params.description: Class name of the root track to move, without the U prefix, case-insensitive (e.g. "MovieSceneCameraCutTrack", "MovieSceneAudioTrack"; get_sequence_tracks lists each root track's class). Mutually exclusive with binding_guid.

params.name: track_name
params.description: Optional track name (as get_sequence_tracks lists it) to pick one when several root tracks share the class.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of an object binding to move with all its tracks, as get_sequence_bindings returns it. Mutually exclusive with track_class.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, folder_name: string, track_class: string, track_name: string, binding_guid: string, moved: bool, already_present: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: pause_level_sequence_runtime
commands.description: Pauses, at its current position, the runtime ULevelSequencePlayer whose player_key play_level_sequence_runtime returned. Players live in the PIE or game world and stop resolving once it ends. Returns player_key, paused, playing and current_time in seconds; read it later with get_level_sequence_status_runtime. Inverse: resume_level_sequence_runtime.

params.name: player_key
params.description: Player key returned from play_level_sequence_runtime

commands.returns: { player_key: string, paused: bool, playing: bool, current_time: number }

commands.name: pause_timeline
commands.description: Pause the editor Sequencer's preview playback on a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, first opening that sequence in the Sequencer when another one (or none) is shown; the playhead stays where it is. Editor preview only: to pause a sequence playing in PIE or a game use pause_level_sequence_runtime. Changes no asset; pausing a sequence that is not playing does nothing and still succeeds. playing and paused are read right after the call (paused is simply not playing). A sequence that is not found, or no Sequencer that can show it, is an error. Start again with play_timeline; move the playhead with set_timeline_time.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path, e.g. "LS_Intro" (case-insensitive; the first match under /Game is used), as get_level_sequences returns it (sequences[].name).

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, playing: bool, paused: bool }

commands.name: play_level_sequence_runtime
commands.description: Spawn an ALevelSequenceActor with a ULevelSequencePlayer for a Level Sequence in a running PIE or game world, start it with default playback settings, and return the player_key the other runtime tools take. Every call makes a new player and actor with its own key, even for a sequence already playing; nothing in the editor level or on disk changes. No PIE or game world, a world selector naming the editor world, or no sequence of that name under /Game is an error and nothing is spawned. The key stops resolving when PIE ends. Then: pause_level_sequence_runtime, set_level_sequence_time_runtime, get_level_sequence_status_runtime, and stop_level_sequence_runtime to release the player and destroy its actor; to scrub in the editor without PIE, play_timeline or set_timeline_time.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path, e.g. "LS_Intro"; matched case-insensitively, and the first match under /Game is used.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Runtime playback needs a PIE/Game world (an editor world has no movie-scene tick manager and would assert), so an editor world is refused here.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, player_key: string, playing: bool, current_time: number, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: play_timeline
commands.description: Starts playback in the editor's Sequencer on a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, first opening it there when it is not the sequence shown. Editor preview only, no PIE or game player (use play_level_sequence_runtime for that). Returns at once and changes no asset; calling it while playing keeps playing. playing is read right after the call. Errors when the sequence is missing or no Sequencer can show it. Pause with pause_timeline; move the playhead with set_timeline_time.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target level sequence

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, playing: bool }

commands.name: remove_keyframe
commands.description: Delete one key from one channel of a section of a Level Sequence, found by its index or by its frame. Read the keys first with get_channel_keyframes, which takes the same locator and lists each key's index, frame and value; to move a key use move_keyframe, to copy one duplicate_keyframe, to change its value or tangents set_binding_channel_keyframe_interpolation, and to drop the whole section remove_section. The section is found like set_section_properties: binding_guid with track_type or track_index and section_index, or no binding for a root track; channel_type and channel_index pick the channel (transform location x, y, z are double channels 0-2, rotation 3-5, scale 6-8). A key that does not exist (index out of range, or no key within tolerance of frame) is an error and nothing changes. Not idempotent: repeating a call with the same index removes the key that took its place. One undo step, then the sequence is saved; a failed save answers success false with the change kept in memory.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding whose section to edit. Omit it (and binding_name_or_guid) for a section of a ROOT track -- shot, camera cut, audio, event, sub-sequence, fade: track_type or track_index then pick among the root tracks in get_sequence_tracks order, camera cut last.

params.name: track_type
params.description: Optional class filter (see set_section_properties) selecting the track on the binding.

params.name: track_index
params.description: Index into the binding's tracks (default 0; used when track_type omitted). Without binding_guid it indexes the root tracks.

params.name: section_index
params.description: Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0).

params.name: channel_type
params.description: Channel value kind: "double" (default) | "float" | "bool".

params.name: channel_index
params.description: Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0).

params.name: index
params.description: Index of the key to remove (mutually exclusive with frame).

params.name: frame
params.description: Frame of the key to remove (resolved via FindKey; provide index OR frame).

params.name: tolerance
params.description: Optional FindKey frame tolerance when locating by frame (default 0).

params.name: binding_name_or_guid
params.description: Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, channel_type: string, channel_index: int, removed_frame: int, key_index: int, removed: bool, key_count_after: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: remove_marked_frame
commands.description: Removes one user marked frame from a Level Sequence, by index, frame, or label -- or, with all=true, every marked frame -- inside an undo transaction, and saves the sequence; success requires the save. A selector that matches no mark, or all=true on a sequence without marks, succeeds with already_removed true and saved false (nothing is written).

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: index
params.description: Optional mark index to delete. Takes precedence over frame/label.

params.name: frame
params.description: Optional tick frame number to resolve the mark to delete (FindMarkedFrameByFrameNumber).

params.name: label
params.description: Optional label to resolve the mark to delete (FindMarkedFrameByLabel).

params.name: all
params.description: Optional bool (default false): delete EVERY marked frame (DeleteMarkedFrames) instead of one; index, frame and label are then refused.

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, removed_index: int, removed_count: int, already_removed: bool, already_empty?: bool, marked_frame_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string } -- removed_index is -1 with all=true or when nothing matched; already_empty only with all=true.

commands.name: remove_section
commands.description: Deletes one section, by index, from a track of a Level Sequence in one undo step, then saves the sequence; success requires the save. The section is resolved like get_section_info: with binding_guid, a track of that object binding; without it, a root track (shot, camera cut, audio, event, sub-sequence, fade). track_type picks the first track of that kind, else track_index; section_index picks the section. A missing sequence, binding, track or section index is an error and nothing changes. The track itself stays, even when left empty: remove_sequence_track deletes a whole track, remove_keyframe a single key. A repeat call deletes whatever section now sits at that index, so re-read indexes first with get_sequence_tracks or get_section_info. Inverse of add_audio_section, add_shot_section, add_event_track_section and add_camera_cut.

params.description: Alias for sequence_path, read when sequence_path is absent or empty; same formats.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding whose section to remove, as get_sequence_bindings returns it. Omit it (and binding_name_or_guid) for a section of a ROOT track -- shot, camera cut, audio, event, sub-sequence, fade: track_type or track_index then pick among the root tracks in get_sequence_tracks order, camera cut last.

params.description: Optional track kind; the first track of exactly that kind wins, else the first subclass: transform, float, bool, vector, color, visibility, audio, event, fade, skeletalanimation, sub, cameracut, shot, slomo, property, attach. An unrecognised value is ignored and track_index is used.

params.name: track_index
params.description: 0-based index into the binding's tracks, or into the root tracks without binding_guid, in get_sequence_tracks order (default 0); used when track_type is omitted.

params.name: section_index
params.description: 0-based index of the section to delete on the resolved track (default 0); out of range is an error.

params.name: binding_name_or_guid
params.description: Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved.

The binding itself stays (remove_sequence_binding removes it). No match, a bad GUID or a binding the sequence does not have is an error and nothing changes. commands.name: set_audio_section_properties
commands.description: Set playback properties of one section (section_index) on a root audio track (audio_track_index) of a Level Sequence, in one undo step, then save the sequence: sound, looping, play until finished (UE 5.8), subtitle suppression, attenuation override and asset, volume, pitch and start offset. Use it rather than set_properties: volume and pitch are keyed channels, not plain properties, the start offset is converted to tick-resolution frames, and the section's own setters run (setting a sound re-derives looping). Only fields you pass change; a sound or attenuation path that does not load, or an offset outside the frame range, is an error before anything changes. volume/pitch without time_seconds become one constant key at frame 0; with time_seconds a linear key is ADDED at that time, rounded to a tick, even over an existing key. When nothing changes, nothing is saved and no undo step is left (changed false). Read: get_audio_section_properties; add: add_audio_section.

params.description: StartFrameOffset in tick frames (omit to leave unchanged).

params.name: end_frame_offset
params.description: EndFrameOffset in tick frames (omit to leave unchanged).

params.name: first_loop_start_frame_offset
params.description: FirstLoopStartFrameOffset in tick frames; only meaningful when can_loop is true (omit to leave unchanged).

params.name: hierarchical_bias
params.description: HierarchicalBias (int; default engine value 100; omit to leave unchanged).

params.name: can_loop
params.description: bCanLoop; gates the loop offsets (omit to leave unchanged).

params.name: time_scale
params.description: Constant playback time scale (double; must be non-zero -- ~0 is a FixedTime warp, not a play rate; omit to leave unchanged).

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, section_class: string, section_index: int, start_frame_offset: int, end_frame_offset: int, first_loop_start_frame_offset: int, hierarchical_bias: int, can_loop: bool, time_scale: double|null, set: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: set_timeline_time
commands.description: Move the editor Sequencer's playhead on a Level Sequence, found by asset name under /Game, to a time in seconds (a jump: nothing plays in between), first opening that sequence in the Sequencer when another one (or none) is shown. Editor preview only: to seek a sequence playing in PIE or a game use set_level_sequence_time_runtime. Changes no asset: the actors the sequence binds are only previewed at that time, as the Sequencer does. The same time again lands on the same frame. actual_frame is where the playhead landed, in display-rate frames, read back after the jump; time_set only says the jump was issued. A negative time, a sequence that is not found, or no Sequencer that can show it is an error and nothing moves. See the sequence length first with get_timeline_info; play or pause with play_timeline and pause_timeline.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path, e.g. "LS_Intro" (case-insensitive; the first match under /Game is used), as get_level_sequences returns it (sequences[].name).

params.name: time
params.description: Playhead position in seconds from the sequence start, e.g. 2.5; must be 0 or more (a time past the end is not refused).

commands.returns: { sequence_name: string, requested_time: number, actual_frame: int, time_set: bool }

commands.name: set_transform_section_mask
commands.description: Set which channels of one 3D transform section on an object-binding track of a Level Sequence are animated (UMovieScene3DTransformSection::SetMask), in one undo step, then save the sequence. channels names the channels to enable, as an array or a comma-separated string; every other channel is masked off, and an unknown token is an error before anything changes. Existing keys are kept: the mask only filters evaluation and display. The section is resolved like get_section_info; one that is not a 3D transform section is an error. The mask is read back as channels and channel_mask, and a section that already has that mask changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false). Quaternion rotation: set_transform_section_quaternion_interpolation.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: channels
params.description: Channels to ENABLE: a JSON array (e.g. ["TranslationX","Rotation"]) OR a comma-separated string. Tokens: TranslationX/Y/Z, Translation, RotationX/Y/Z (Roll/Pitch/Yaw), Rotation, ScaleX/Y/Z, Scale, Weight, AllTransform, All, None.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding whose transform section to edit. Omit it (and binding_name_or_guid) for a section of a ROOT track -- shot, camera cut, audio, event, sub-sequence, fade: track_type or track_index then pick among the root tracks in get_sequence_tracks order, camera cut last.

params.name: track_type
params.description: Optional class filter (default resolves the transform track; see set_section_properties).

params.name: track_index
params.description: Index into the binding's tracks (default 0). Without binding_guid it indexes the root tracks.

params.name: section_index
params.description: Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0).

params.name: binding_name_or_guid
params.description: Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, section_index: int, channels: string[], channel_mask: int, set: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, note: string, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_transform_section_quaternion_interpolation
commands.description: Turns quaternion (slerp) rotation interpolation on or off for one 3D transform section of a Level Sequence binding, in one undo step, and saves the sequence; keys are kept. The section is section_index on the binding's first track of track_type, or on its track_index-th track when track_type is omitted or unrecognised; a section that is not a 3D transform section is an error, and one already in the requested state changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false). For the section's blend type use set_section_properties; to enable or disable channels use set_transform_section_mask.

params.name: sequence_path
params.description: Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence.

params.name: use_quaternion
params.description: Desired quaternion-interpolation state.

params.name: sequence_name
params.description: Alias for sequence_path.

params.name: binding_guid
params.description: GUID of the binding whose transform section to edit. Omit it (and binding_name_or_guid) for a section of a ROOT track -- shot, camera cut, audio, event, sub-sequence, fade: track_type or track_index then pick among the root tracks in get_sequence_tracks order, camera cut last.

params.name: track_type
params.description: Optional track kind, e.g. "transform": picks the binding's first track of that kind. Omitted or unrecognised, track_index picks the track instead.

params.name: track_index
params.description: Index into the binding's tracks (default 0). Without binding_guid it indexes the root tracks.

params.name: section_index
params.description: Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0).

params.name: binding_name_or_guid
params.description: Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved.

commands.returns: { sequence_path: string, section_index: int, use_quaternion_interpolation: bool, set: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: stop_level_sequence_runtime
commands.description: Stops the runtime ULevelSequencePlayer whose player_key play_level_sequence_runtime returned, forgets the key and destroys the ALevelSequenceActor hosting it, so the key is invalid afterwards. Returns player_key, stopped (true when a playing or paused player was stopped, read back after Stop) and playing as read just after Stop. A player that had already stopped (it reached its end, say) is still released: success with stopped false and a note. A player still playing or paused after Stop is an error, and the key and its actor are kept. Use pause_level_sequence_runtime to keep the player.

params.name: player_key
params.description: Player key returned from play_level_sequence_runtime

commands.returns: { player_key: string, stopped: bool, playing: bool, note?: string }

commands.name: create_trigger
commands.description: Creates a trigger actor (TriggerBox or TriggerSphere) at a specified location. These two shapes only -- for a brush-based ATriggerVolume use spawn_box_volume(volume_class="TriggerVolume") instead.

params.name: trigger_name
params.description: Name label for the trigger actor

params.name: trigger_type
params.description: Trigger class: "TriggerBox" (default) or "TriggerSphere". "TriggerVolume" is deliberately REJECTED here -- ATriggerVolume derives from AVolume/ABrush and needs a real UModel brush built for it, so spawning it through this path would hand you a success-shaped actor with no real collision; use spawn_box_volume(volume_class="TriggerVolume"), which builds that brush.

params.name: location
params.description: World [x, y, z] location to spawn the trigger (default 0,0,0)

commands.returns: { trigger_name, trigger_type, actor_name, actor_path, success }

commands.name: get_actors_in_trigger
commands.description: List and count the actors that a TriggerBox, TriggerSphere or TriggerVolume in the editor world (not PIE) currently reports as overlapping (AActor::GetOverlappingActors), without changing anything. Returns actor_count and actors [{actor_name, actor_class}], plus the trigger's own object name and class. The first actor whose object name or editor label matches is used; when it is not a trigger the call fails.

params.name: trigger_name
params.description: Object name or editor label of the trigger actor, such as the actor_name returned by spawn_actor.

commands.returns: { trigger_name, actor_name (the trigger's object name), actor_class (the trigger's class), actors: [{actor_name, actor_class}], actor_count }

commands.name: get_trigger_events
commands.description: Read the overlap-event configuration of an actor's primitive component: collision profile, whether overlap events are enabled at all, and which begin/end overlap handlers are actually bound. Read-only inverse of set_trigger_events -- it changes nothing, so it is the way to check a trigger is really armed before blaming the gameplay code.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name of the actor (must have a primitive/collision component).

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, collision_profile, overlap_events_enabled, begin_overlap_bound, end_overlap_bound, callback_bound }

commands.name: get_trigger_info
commands.description: Read what kind of trigger an editor-world actor is and where it reaches: actor_class, is_trigger_box, is_trigger_sphere, and the world-space bounds of its root collision shape as bounds_origin and bounds_extent (half-size, cm, as "X=.. Y=.. Z=.." text; left out when the root is not a primitive). Use get_actors_in_trigger for what it overlaps now, get_trigger_events for its overlap and collision settings, get_volume_info for other volumes; resize with set_trigger_box_extent or set_trigger_sphere_radius. Read-only and idempotent; editor world only, not PIE. An unknown name, or an actor that is not a TriggerBox, TriggerSphere or TriggerVolume, is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name (not the editor label) of the trigger actor in the editor world, e.g. "TriggerBox_0", as spawn_actor returns it; whole name, case-insensitive. find_actors_by_name maps a label to its name

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_class, is_trigger_box, is_trigger_sphere, bounds_origin, bounds_extent }

commands.name: get_volume_info
commands.description: Read a volume actor (any AVolume: BlockingVolume, KillZVolume, PainCausingVolume, PostProcessVolume, TriggerVolume, NavMeshBoundsVolume...) in the editor world without changing it: its class, a flag for each of four common kinds (blocking, kill-Z, pain-causing, post-process) and, when it has a brush component, the world-space bounds of that brush as bounds_origin and bounds_extent (half-size, cm, as "X=.. Y=.. Z=.." text) plus has_brush (whether brush geometry is assigned; without it the volume encloses nothing). Use it to check a volume made by spawn_box_volume; for a TriggerBox or TriggerSphere use get_trigger_info, for overlap settings get_trigger_events, for kind-specific settings get_properties; delete one with remove_volume. Editor world only, not PIE. An unknown name, or an actor that is not a volume, is an error.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name of the volume actor in the editor world, e.g. "BlockingVolume_0", as spawn_box_volume returns it; its editor label is not matched (find_actors_by_name maps a label to its name).

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_class, is_blocking_volume, is_killz_volume, is_pain_causing_volume, is_post_process_volume, bounds_origin?, bounds_extent?, has_brush? }

commands.name: remove_trigger
commands.description: Delete one shape trigger -- a TriggerBox, TriggerSphere or TriggerCapsule -- from the editor world. The actor is found by its object name and its class is checked first: any other class, a TriggerVolume included, is refused and nothing is destroyed. The deletion records no undo step and does not save the level (save_level does). A name that matches no actor is a success with deleted=false, so a repeat call is harmless (idempotent). For a brush volume use remove_volume; to delete any actor with undo, delete_actor.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: The trigger's object name, not its editor label (e.g. TriggerBox_0, as get_actors_in_trigger reports it in actor_name); matched without case.

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_class, deleted (false when nothing was destroyed), already_existed (false when no actor had that name), note? }

commands.name: remove_volume
