commands.description: Destroy a volume ACTOR in the world -- any AVolume subclass: BlockingVolume, PainCausingVolume, PostProcessVolume, TriggerVolume and the rest. Typed: it verifies the actor really is an AVolume before deleting, so pointing it at a non-volume actor is refused rather than obeyed (success false, deleted false, nothing destroyed). This is the counterpart of spawn_box_volume; for a TriggerBox, TriggerSphere or TriggerCapsule use remove_trigger instead.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Name of the AVolume actor.

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_class, deleted, already_existed, note? }

commands.name: set_trigger_box_extent
commands.description: Resize a TriggerBox in the editor world by setting the unscaled half-extent of its box collision component and updating its overlaps, in one undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level). For a TriggerSphere use set_trigger_sphere_radius; a brush volume such as a TriggerVolume has no resize tool. Read the result with get_trigger_info (bounds, which include the actor scale) and what now overlaps with get_actors_in_trigger. Idempotent: the same extent again reports changed=false, though the level is still marked dirty. An extent of 0 or less or a missing one, an unknown name, an actor that is not a TriggerBox, or one without a box collision component is an error and nothing changes.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name of the TriggerBox actor in the editor world, e.g. "TriggerBox_0", as spawn_actor returns it; its editor label is not matched (find_actors_by_name maps a label to its name).

params.name: extent_x
params.description: Half-extent along local X in cm, greater than 0, e.g. 200; the box is twice as long, and the actor scale multiplies it in the world.

params.name: extent_y
params.description: Half-extent along local Y in cm, greater than 0.

params.name: extent_z
params.description: Half-extent along local Z in cm, greater than 0.

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, previous_extent: {x, y, z}, new_extent: {x, y, z}, changed }

commands.name: set_trigger_events
commands.description: Configure overlap-event generation on a trigger/volume's root primitive component: applies the built-in 'Trigger' collision profile (QueryOnly with overlap responses) and toggles SetGenerateOverlapEvents. Honesty note: this configures the component to FIRE overlap events, but binding an actual OnComponentBeginOverlap / OnActorBeginOverlap callback requires a Blueprint or native C++ class on the actor -- the cmd reports callback_bound=false to make that explicit.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Trigger/volume actor name (required)

params.name: generate_overlap_events
params.description: Whether the component generates overlap events (default true)

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, collision_profile, overlap_events_enabled, message, callback_bound, success }

commands.name: set_trigger_sphere_radius
commands.description: Resize a TriggerSphere in the editor world by setting the unscaled radius of its sphere collision component and updating its overlaps, in one undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level). Returns previous_radius, new_radius and changed. For a TriggerBox use set_trigger_box_extent; for a brush volume such as a TriggerVolume there is no resize tool. Read the result with get_trigger_info (bounds, which include the actor scale) and what now overlaps with get_actors_in_trigger. Idempotent: the same radius again reports changed=false, though the level is still marked dirty. A radius of 0 or less, an unknown name, an actor that is not a TriggerSphere, or one without a sphere collision component is an error and nothing changes.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Object name of the TriggerSphere actor in the editor world, e.g. "TriggerSphere_0", as spawn_actor returns it; its editor label is not matched.

params.name: radius
params.description: New unscaled sphere radius in cm, greater than 0, e.g. 250; the actor scale multiplies it in the world.

commands.returns: { actor_name, component_name, previous_radius, new_radius, changed }

commands.name: spawn_box_volume
commands.description: Spawn ANY AVolume-derived actor (default BlockingVolume) in the editor world AND build a real cube brush for it from a half-extent, so the volume actually encloses space: spawn_actor has no volume types, and a volume spawned without a brush has zero bounds -- 0 nav tiles, no overlap. It then normalizes the residual scale some actor factories stamp on placement (PCGVolume: 25,25,10) and RE-READS the brush bounds, so `success` means the volume matches the extent you asked for, not that the call returned. One more step finishes the typed volumes: add_pcg_component(graph) on a PCGVolume, set_properties {"AreaClass": ...} on a NavModifierVolume, {"bUnbound": true} on an unbound PostProcessVolume; spawn_level_streaming_volume binds a sub-level. Called with no class and no extent it gives a 200 cm BlockingVolume cube. One undo step; refused during PIE; the level is not saved.

params.name: volume_class
params.description: Optional volume class (default "BlockingVolume"): short reflected name ('BlockingVolume', 'KillZVolume', 'PainCausingVolume', 'PostProcessVolume', 'TriggerVolume', 'NavMeshBoundsVolume', 'PhysicsVolume', 'PCGVolume', case-insensitive, with or without a leading 'A') or a full object path ('/Script/Engine.TriggerVolume'). Must be a concrete AVolume subclass; anything else is an error.

params.name: location
params.description: World [x, y, z] location to spawn the volume (default 0,0,0)

params.name: extent
params.description: Optional [x, y, z] in unreal units, each component > 0; default [100, 100, 100] (a 200 cm cube). !!! THIS IS THE SEMI-AXIS (HALF-size), NOT the full edge length !!! extent=[500,500,200] builds a 1000 x 1000 x 400 cube and, with the scale normalized, gives world bounds of +/-500 / +/-200 around `location`. Check `bounds_extent_actual` against what you asked for. A value that is not an array is an error.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Optional editor label for the spawned actor

params.name: is_spatially_loaded
params.description: Optional World Partition spatial-loading flag. Applied only when passed and the actor allows changing it (spatial_flag_applied); omitted, the actor keeps its class default. Reported RE-READ from the actor.

params.name: normalize_scale
params.description: Default TRUE: resets the actor scale to (1,1,1) after building the brush, so the world bounds equal the requested `extent`. It matters because some actor factories stamp a default scale during placement -- APCGVolume is spawned at (25, 25, 10) -- and since brush polys are authored in LOCAL space that scale MULTIPLIES your extent. Set it false only if you deliberately want the factory's scale; `spawn_scale` always reports what it was. Be aware that with normalize_scale=false and a factory scale != 1 the real bounds are NOT the requested extent, so `extent_matches_request` and therefore `success` come back FALSE -- that is the honest answer, not a bug, and `actor_scale` says why they differ.

commands.returns: { actor_name, actor_path, actor_class, volume_class, world_bounds_extent: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, GetActorBounds -- kept for compatibility), bounds_extent_actual: [x,y,z] (RE-READ from the BRUSH component's world bounds; this is the volume itself, with no stray editor sprite in the box), bounds_origin_actual: [x,y,z], actor_scale: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, after normalization), spawn_scale: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, as the actor factory left it), scale_normalized: bool (true only when a correction was actually needed), extent_matches_request: bool, bounds_tolerance_uu: number, has_brush_geometry, brush_built, is_spatially_loaded (RE-READ), spatial_flag_applied, success, requested: { volume_class, location, extent, actor_label, is_spatially_loaded, normalize_scale } }

commands.name: add_list_view
commands.description: Construct a list-type view -- a UListView, a UTileView (view_type=Tile) or a UTreeView (view_type=Tree) -- named list_view_name in the tree of a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, with EntryWidgetClass from entry_widget_class when given, under the panel parent_widget_name or else the root canvas or panel, then compile and save the Blueprint in one undo step. In an empty tree it becomes the root; a parent or root that is not a panel, or a full single-child panel, is an error. Idempotent by name: a view of the requested class already called list_view_name is left untouched (already_existed=true, widget_added=false, saved=false, a note, its own entry_widget_class), nothing compiled or saved; that name held by anything else is an error, and so is a missing Blueprint, an unknown view_type or a non-UUserWidget entry class. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the edit kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Authoring only: a tree view's items and their children are supplied at runtime; fill a list or tile view in PIE with set_pie_list_view_items. Inverse: remove_widget_from_blueprint.

params.name: widget_blueprint_name
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/UI/WBP_Inventory"

params.name: list_view_name
params.description: FName of the new view widget in the tree; also the idempotency key

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Alias of list_view_name, read only when list_view_name is absent

params.name: entry_widget_class
params.description: Optional entry widget class for each row, tile or tree node (asset path such as "/Game/UI/WBP_ItemTile", or a /Script path)

params.name: view_type
params.description: Optional "List" (default, UListView), "Tile" (UTileView) or "Tree" (UTreeView), case-insensitive; anything else is an error

params.name: parent_widget_name
params.description: Optional name of an existing panel widget (UPanelWidget) in the tree to insert the new view under; omitted = the root canvas or panel (in an empty tree the view becomes the root)

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_name, list_view_name, list_view_class, view_type, already_existed, entry_widget_class, parent_widget_name?, widget_added, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: add_viewmodel
commands.description: Add a view-model context named context_name, of class view_model_class, to the MVVM view of a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, then compile and save the Blueprint, in one undo step. creation_type says how the widget gets its instance at runtime: CreateInstance by default, PropertyPath from source_property_path, GlobalViewModelCollection by global_identifier, or Manual (supplied at runtime, e.g. by set_viewmodel_field). Idempotent by context_name: a context of that name and class is kept as it is, answered with its own creation_type, already_existed=true, saved=false and a note, nothing changed, compiled or saved; one of another class is an error. A Blueprint without MVVM support fails with a note; a bad class or creation_type is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the edit kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Undo it with remove_viewmodel; bind fields with bind_widget_to_viewmodel.

params.name: widget_blueprint_name
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset, e.g. "/Game/UI/WBP_HUD".

params.name: view_model_class
params.description: View model class: asset path (/Game/...) or /Script/<Module>.<ClassName>

params.name: context_name
params.description: FName identifying this context (idempotency key)

params.name: creation_type
params.description: Optional (default "CreateInstance"): one of "CreateInstance" | "PropertyPath" | "GlobalViewModelCollection" | "Manual" (EMVVMBlueprintViewModelContextCreationType).

params.name: source_property_path
params.description: Optional: only used when creation_type="PropertyPath" (required in that case). Sets FMVVMBlueprintViewModelContext::ViewModelPropertyPath.

params.name: global_identifier
params.description: Optional: only used when creation_type="GlobalViewModelCollection" (required in that case). Sets FMVVMBlueprintViewModelContext::GlobalViewModelIdentifier.

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_name, view_model_class, context_name, creation_type, source_property_path?, global_identifier?, already_existed, view_model_count, has_mvvm_extension, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: add_widget_animation
commands.description: Add a UWidgetAnimation called animation_name to a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, as the editor's New Animation button does: an inner UMovieScene at 20 fps with a 0 to 5 s playback range, the display label set to animation_name and the animation registered as a Blueprint variable, then compile and save the Blueprint. object_name can differ from animation_name when a stale object already holds that name. Idempotent: an animation whose object name or display label equals animation_name (ignoring case) is returned with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, nothing compiled or saved. A missing Blueprint is an error; a failed save makes success false with save_error, the animation kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Animate it with add_widget_animation_track and add_widget_animation_keyframe; list: get_widget_animations; inverse: remove_widget_animation.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: name/display label for the new animation

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, object_name: string, display_name: string, added: bool, already_existed: bool, has_movie_scene: bool, animation_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: add_widget_animation_keyframe
commands.description: Add a keyframe to an existing widget-animation property track's section (call add_widget_animation_track first). Converts time_seconds to an FFrameNumber via the MovieScene's tick resolution, extends the section's range to cover the key if needed, then adds the key on the matching channel(s) via the requested interpolation (AddLinearKey | AddCubicKey | AddConstantKey for float/color's FMovieSceneFloatChannel(s); bool channels have no interpolation concept and always use UpdateOrAddKey). Read: get_widget_animation_tracks; inverse: remove_widget_animation_keyframe.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the target animation

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the animated widget

params.name: property_path
params.description: the SAME property_path used in add_widget_animation_track

params.name: time_seconds
params.description: time (seconds, >= 0) at which to place the key

params.name: value
params.description: key value: a number for float, a bool for bool, or a [R,G,B,A] (A optional, defaults 1.0) array for color

params.name: interpolation
params.description: Optional "linear" (default) | "cubic" | "constant" (float/color only; ignored for bool)

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, widget_name: string, property_path: string, track_type: string, time_seconds: float, key_frame: int, keys_added: int, interpolation: string, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: add_widget_animation_track
commands.description: Add (or reuse) a MovieScene property track for a widget's property inside a UWidgetAnimation: finds/creates a UMovieScenePossessable bound to the named widget (+ matching FWidgetAnimationBinding), resolves property_path to a top-level reflected property on the widget's class, and adds the matching typed track (UMovieSceneFloatTrack | UMovieSceneColorTrack | UMovieSceneBoolTrack) with a full-playback-range section. track_type="auto" infers from the property's reflected type (FFloatProperty/FDoubleProperty->float; FLinearColor or FSlateColor struct->color; FBoolProperty->bool). Call add_widget_animation_keyframe afterward to place keys. Single-level property_path only (not dotted sub-paths). Read: get_widget_animation_tracks; inverse: remove_widget_animation_track.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the target animation

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget (in the SAME WidgetBP's tree) to animate

params.name: property_path
params.description: name of a top-level reflected property on the widget's class (e.g. "RenderOpacity", "ColorAndOpacity")

params.name: track_type
params.description: Optional "auto" (default) | "float" | "color" | "bool"

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, widget_name: string, property_path: string, track_type: string, possessable_guid: string, binding_reused: bool, track_class: string, track_reused: bool, section_class: string, section_created: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: add_widget_property_binding
commands.description: Bind a widget PROPERTY to a function of the Widget Blueprint -- the Designer's "Bind" dropdown, headless. The property then recomputes every frame from that function instead of holding a fixed value (a health bar's Percent, a label's Text, a panel's Visibility). TWO RULES, both enforced by the ENGINE'S OWN validator (FDelegateEditorBinding::IsBindingValid, the same code the UMG compiler runs -- this tool does not second-guess it): the property is bindable only if its widget declares a companion delegate named "<Property>Delegate" (Text -> TextDelegate), and the function must have a COMPATIBLE SIGNATURE (same return type, NO parameters) and be PURE (BlueprintPure or const), because it is called while painting. A refusal names which of the two failed and, when the property is not bindable at all, lists the ones that are. Create the function first with add_blueprint_function + set its return type; one property can hold only ONE binding, so re-binding the same property REPLACES it (reported in replaced_existing).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget in the tree whose property gets bound (must be a direct variable of the UserWidget)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Property to bind, e.g. "Text" on a TextBlock, "Percent" on a ProgressBar, "Visibility" on any widget. Must have a companion "<property_name>Delegate" on the widget's class.

params.name: function_name
params.description: Name of the function ON THIS Widget Blueprint that supplies the value. Must be pure and take no parameters, returning the property's type.

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true). The compile is what turns the editor binding into the runtime one, so a false here leaves the binding authored but not live.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, property_name: string, function_name: string, bound: bool, valid: bool, replaced_existing: bool, member_guid: string, validation_messages: [string], bindable_properties?: [string], saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: add_widget_to_blueprint
commands.description: Add a widget to the tree of a Widget Blueprint asset as the last child of the panel parent_name (default the root, which must then be a panel), register it as a variable, then compile and save the blueprint; no undo step. widget_type takes the curated palette of list_widget_types (TextBlock, Button, ProgressBar, Slider, ScrollBox...), any native widget class path, or a Widget Blueprint to nest, which must not contain this one. Idempotent by name: a widget already called widget_name with the same class is returned as is (already_existed true), and the blueprint is compiled and saved only when it has unsaved changes (otherwise saved=false, nothing saved); another class under that name, an unknown widget_type or a bad parent is an error. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error. Inspect: get_widget_blueprint_tree; inverse: remove_widget_from_blueprint (remove_widget is the runtime tool).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_type
params.description: one of TextBlock, Button, Image, VerticalBox, CanvasPanel, ProgressBar, Slider, CheckBox, ComboBoxString, ScrollBox, Border, Overlay, SizeBox, WidgetSwitcher, HorizontalBox, EditableTextBox, Spacer, GridPanel, RichTextBlock, EditableText, MultiLineEditableText, ComboBox, SpinBox, ScaleBox, SafeZone, UniformGridPanel, WrapBox, MenuAnchor (the curated names; see list_widget_types), OR any other native widget class path (e.g. /Script/UMG.Throbber, /Script/UMG.ListView), OR a UserWidget-derived Widget Blueprint to embed as a nested instance, by its /Game asset path (e.g. /Game/UI/WBP_HealthBar) or generated-class path (/Game/UI/WBP_HealthBar.WBP_HealthBar_C)

params.name: widget_name
params.description: unique name for the new widget

params.name: parent_name
params.description: Optional name of a panel widget to host the new child; defaults to the root widget.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, added_widget_name: string, widget_type: string, widget_class: string, parent_name: string, slot_class: string, added: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string, note: string? }

commands.name: apply_widget_style_preset
commands.description: Apply ONE block of style properties to EVERY widget of a Widget Blueprint that matches a filter, in a single pass with ONE compile + ONE save -- the multi-widget companion to set_widget_property's multi-path form. Selection is target_widgets (explicit names, wins over everything) OR target_class (matched with IsA, so subclasses count) AND/OR name_pattern (wildcard). At least one selector is required: to hit every widget in the tree say so explicitly with name_pattern="*". Every value goes through the same honest applier, so the per-widget report distinguishes what landed from what was ignored; dry_run=true resolves the match and reports it WITHOUT writing, which is the cheap way to check a filter before it touches 40 widgets.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: preset
params.description: Dict of {"<property or dotted path>": <value>} applied to each matched widget, e.g. {"WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor":"#1B1B1BFF"}. Optional when the source_* params are used; when both are given the inline values WIN, so you can say "the theme, but this one in red". A path that does not exist on a given matched widget lands in that widget's ignored[] instead of failing the whole call.

params.name: source_bp_path
params.description: THEME MODE: /Game path of a Widget Blueprint holding a REFERENCE widget to copy the style from, instead of writing the values inline. This is what makes one widget the single source of truth rather than scattering the same colour across 40 calls.

params.name: source_widget_name
params.description: Name of the reference widget inside source_bp_path. Required with source_bp_path.

params.name: source_property_paths
params.description: Which paths to copy off the reference widget, e.g. ["WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor","WidgetStyle.NormalPadding"]. A path that does not resolve on the REFERENCE is an error, not a silent skip: an incomplete theme that says nothing is worse than a refusal. Use audit_widget_style with the same reference + paths to find what has drifted before fixing it.

params.name: target_class
params.description: Class filter matched with IsA: a curated name (Button, TextBlock), a native class path (/Script/UMG.Button) or a Widget Blueprint asset path. Subclasses match too.

params.name: name_pattern
params.description: Wildcard on the widget's name (Btn_*, *_Title, or * for every widget). Combined with target_class as AND.

params.name: target_widgets
params.description: Explicit widget names. When present, target_class and name_pattern are IGNORED and only these are touched (reported in selector_used).

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Resolve the match and report it without writing anything (default false).

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true; a dry run never saves).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, selector_used: string, matched: [string], matched_count: int, dry_run: bool, results: [{widget_name, widget_class, applied, ignored, errors, failed_paths, applied_count, all_applied}], widgets_fully_applied: int, widgets_with_failures: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: bind_widget_to_viewmodel
commands.description: Add a binding to the MVVM view of a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, from a view-model property (source_path) to a widget property (destination_path), then compile and save the Blueprint in one undo step. Both paths are resolved by reflection, written through UMVVMEditorSubsystem as the MVVM editor does, and read back: a write that did not stick is rolled back and is an error, with nothing saved. Not idempotent: each call adds another binding. An unknown binding_mode, context, widget or property, or a path that is not Context.Property, is an error before anything changes; a Blueprint without MVVM support fails with a note. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the binding kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Add the context with add_viewmodel; inverse: unbind_widget_from_viewmodel.

params.name: widget_blueprint_name
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: source_path
params.description: "ViewModel.Property" (exactly one dot): ViewModel = an existing viewmodel context name (added via add_viewmodel), Property = a reflected property on that viewmodel's class. Multi-segment ("A.B.C") is NOT supported.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: "Widget.Property" (exactly one dot): Widget = a widget name in this Widget BP's WidgetTree, Property = a reflected property on that widget's class. Multi-segment is NOT supported.

params.name: binding_mode
params.description: optional: "OneWay" (default), "TwoWay", "OneTime", "OneWayToSource"

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_name, source_path, destination_path, binding_mode, created, binding_count, binding_id, source_path_verified, destination_path_verified, has_mvvm_extension, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: click_pie_widget
commands.description: Fire a LIVE UMG widget's event in the running PIE session (game thread): resolve a UWidget by name among the active viewport UserWidgets (reusing the list_pie_widgets walk) and BROADCAST its named BlueprintAssignable multicast delegate (default OnClicked). Unlike list_pie_widgets (read-only) this MUTATES runtime state -- it runs the exact bound handlers a real click would, including the client->server RPC path, so equip/inventory/craft UI flows can be driven headless instead of by a human (driving them via call_function bypasses that RPC path and yields false negatives). Errors clearly if no Play-In-Editor session is running or the widget/event is not found.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Required. Name of the target UWidget in the live tree (as reported by list_pie_widgets), e.g. "ConfirmButton". Matches a widget inside an active viewport UserWidget's WidgetTree, or a top-level UserWidget by its own name.

params.name: event
params.description: Optional (default "OnClicked"): BlueprintAssignable multicast delegate to fire (e.g. "OnClicked", "OnPressed", "OnReleased").

params.name: child_name
params.description: Optional: after resolving widget_name, drill into a descendant widget with this name (the resolved widget's own WidgetTree if it is a UserWidget, else a named child in its subtree) and fire the event on THAT widget instead.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional (default 0): when set, only consider viewport UserWidgets owned by the local player with this index (single-player PIE resolves globally).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD.

commands.returns: { success: bool, widget_name, resolved_widget, resolved_class, event, is_bound: bool, fired: bool, player_index, child_name?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number } -- is_bound is false when the delegate exists but has no bound handlers (broadcast is still a safe no-op).

commands.name: create_common_ui_stack
commands.description: Make a UCommonActivatableWidgetStack the root of the empty tree of a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, then compile and save the Blueprint in one undo step. root_class picks the UCommonActivatableWidgetStack subclass to construct; one that does not resolve, or is not such a subclass, falls back to the base class with root_class_resolved=false and root_class_note. The stack is named CommonActivatableWidgetStack, made unique when an object of the tree holds that name. Idempotent: a root that is already a stack is kept as it is (already_existed=true, root_changed=false, saved=false, a note), nothing compiled or saved. Any other root, or a missing Blueprint, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the edit kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Screens go on the stack at runtime: push_common_ui_widget and pop_common_ui_widget; read it with list_pie_widgets. Inverse: remove_widget_from_blueprint.

params.name: widget_blueprint_name
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint

params.name: root_class
params.description: Optional. Asset path (/Game/...) or /Script/<Module>.<ClassName> of a UCommonActivatableWidgetStack subclass. Omitted = base UCommonActivatableWidgetStack.

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_name, root_class?, already_existed, stack_class, root_class_requested, root_class_resolved, root_class_note?, root_changed, root_widget, root_widget_class, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: create_menu_screen_widget
commands.description: Build a styled menu screen: create or reuse the Widget Blueprint at package_path/name with a centred panel, optional title and one button per entry bound to an event-graph OnClicked handler, then compile and save. Re-runs reuse widgets and bindings. Returns contrast_ratio_normal_text; the default colors pass audit_widget_accessibility. Layout is not measured (long labels can clip) and text is inline, not String Table.

params.name: package_path
params.description: /Game folder for the new Widget Blueprint (e.g. /Game/MyGame/UI).

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name, e.g. WBP_OptionsMenu.

params.name: entries
params.description: REQUIRED, the buttons top to bottom. Each item is either a plain string (the label) or an object {label, handler_name?}. handler_name names the generated event-graph function; omitted, it becomes On<Label>Clicked. Order is preserved.

params.name: title
params.description: Optional heading text above the buttons. Omitted or empty = no title widget at all (not an empty one).

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Parent UUserWidget subclass (default "UUserWidget"). Pass a CommonUI activatable class here to scaffold a screen for a CommonUI stack.

params.name: background
params.description: Draw the background panel (default true). false leaves the buttons floating on nothing -- which is what makes contrast unjudgeable, so it also drops contrast_ratio_normal_text from the payload.

params.name: panel_color
params.description: Background panel colour. "#RRGGBBAA", [r,g,b,a] (LINEAR 0..1) or {R,G,B,A}. Default is a near-black panel.

params.name: button_color
params.description: Button resting colour, same formats. If you override this, you own the contrast: the returned ratio tells you what you got.

params.name: text_color
params.description: Label colour for title and buttons, same formats. Default white.

params.name: title_font_size
params.description: Title text size in Slate font points, truncated to a whole number; default 36. Unused when title is empty.

params.name: button_font_size
params.description: Button label size in Slate font points, truncated to a whole number; default 20. It also sets the contrast floor checked (3:1 at 18 or more, else 4.5:1); under 12 is what audit_widget_accessibility flags as small_text.

params.name: panel_width
params.description: Panel width in pixels (default 480).

params.name: panel_height
params.description: Panel height in pixels (default 560).

params.name: bind_events
params.description: Wire each button's OnClicked to a handler in the event graph (default true). false builds the visuals only.

params.name: theme_source_bp
params.description: Optional /Game path of a Widget Blueprint holding a reference Button whose style is copied onto every generated button INSTEAD of the built-in defaults (same idea as apply_widget_style_preset's theme mode: one widget is the single source of truth).

params.name: theme_source_widget
params.description: Name of the reference Button inside theme_source_bp. Required with it.

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save when done (default true).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path, asset_path, created, already_existed, root_widget, panel_widget, box_widget, title_widget, entries: [{label, button_widget, text_widget, handler_name, bound, already_bound, error}], entry_count, buttons_bound, colors: {panel, button, text}, contrast_ratio_normal_text, contrast_required, contrast_passes, contrast_note, theme_source, compiled, saved, save_error }

commands.name: create_widget
commands.description: Create a runtime UUserWidget instance of a concrete UserWidget class in a running PIE world (the default while PIE runs) or the editor world, owned by that world's first local PlayerController when there is one, and optionally AddToViewport it. Nothing is saved, and an unreferenced widget is garbage-collected. In the editor world add_to_viewport never adds (no PlayerController): read added_to_viewport. A taken name gets a unique variant, reported in widget_name; a class that does not load, is abstract or is not a UserWidget is an error. To change the asset use add_widget_to_blueprint; remove_widget searches the same worlds.

params.name: widget_class_path
params.description: Full path to widget class, e.g. '/Game/UI/MyWidget.MyWidget_C'

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name to assign to the created widget instance (a name another widget already has gets a unique variant, which widget_name in the response reports)

params.name: add_to_viewport
params.description: If true, AddToViewport the widget (optional, default false). It only ever really adds when the target world has a local PlayerController -- check added_to_viewport in the response, and see target_world for when that is possible at all.

params.name: target_world
params.description: Optional: "editor" | "pie" | "server" (the PIE world with authority) | "client" | "pie:N" | "game" (alias of "pie"). Defaults to "pie" when a Play-In-Editor session is running, else "editor". IMPORTANT: "editor" NEVER has a PlayerController, because GEditor's world is not a game world, so add_to_viewport can never really add there -- that is reported honestly (added_to_viewport stays false), never simulated. "pie" resolves the running PIE world and its first local PlayerController, so add_to_viewport there performs a REAL AddToViewport().

commands.returns: { widget_name: string, widget_class_path: string, widget_class_name: string, target_world: string, added_to_viewport: bool, add_to_viewport_note?: string, widget_valid: bool, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: create_widget_blueprint
commands.description: Create a UWidgetBlueprint at package_path/name with the editor Widget Blueprint factory, parented to parent_class (a class path such as /Game/UI/WBP_Base.WBP_Base_C, or a short class name), give it a CanvasPanel root named RootCanvas when the factory made no root, then compile and save it. Idempotent by path: a Widget Blueprint already there is returned untouched (created=false, already_existed=true, saved=false), nothing compiled or saved; that reply gives the parent_class it really has, with a note when it is not the requested one. A parent that is not a UUserWidget subclass, an invalid path, or another kind of asset at that path is an error. A failed save makes success false with save_error and keeps the new asset in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Then add widgets with add_widget_to_blueprint and read the tree with get_widget_blueprint_tree; an Editor Utility Widget is create_editor_utility_widget_blueprint.

params.name: package_path
params.description: /Game folder to create the asset in (e.g. /Game/UI)

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name (no extension), e.g. "WBP_MainMenu"; with package_path it gives the asset path.

params.name: parent_class
params.description: Parent UUserWidget subclass (default "UUserWidget").

commands.returns: { name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, parent_class: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, root_created?: bool, root_widget: string, root_widget_class: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: duplicate_widget
commands.description: Duplicate a widget (DuplicateObject<UWidget> outered to the WidgetTree) and add the clone under a target parent panel, copying the source's slot property values onto the new slot when the slot classes match. Refuses (clear error, no partial/broken result) to duplicate a panel widget that currently has children -- UE's object duplication would leave the clone's slots aliasing the SAME original child widgets rather than deep-copying them (see FDuplicateDataWriter); duplicate leaf widgets, or rebuild the panel's children individually with add_widget_to_blueprint. Name collisions on new_name are a clear error (not a silent alias of the pre-existing widget at that name).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget to duplicate (must not be a panel widget with children)

params.name: new_name
params.description: unique name for the duplicate

params.name: target_parent_name
params.description: Optional name of the panel widget to host the duplicate; defaults to the source widget's own current parent (sibling placement).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, source_widget_name: string, new_widget_name: string, widget_class: string, target_parent_name: string, slot_class: string, slot_class_matched_source: bool, slot_properties_copied: int, duplicated: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: get_level_widget_properties
commands.description: Read the live state of a UUserWidget hosted on a UWidgetComponent in the current editor level, found by the widget's object name (list_level_widget_components gives the names): class, validity, visibility, enabled and focus, the hosting component's draw size and relative transform, parent, and the direct children of its root panel (one level). Use it for this runtime state, which no UPROPERTY read gives; get_object_info reads the widget's raw properties. A running PIE session is never searched: use list_pie_widgets for live game UI.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget to query

commands.returns: { widget_name: string, widget_class: string, widget_valid: bool, widget_visible: bool, visibility: string, size?: { width: number, height: number }, position?: { x: number, y: number, z: number }, rotation?: { pitch: number, yaw: number, roll: number }, scale?: { x: number, y: number, z: number }, parent_widget?: string, parent_class?: string, child_count: number, children: [{ name: string, class: string, depth: number (1), valid: bool, enabled: bool, visibility: string }], is_enabled: bool, has_focus: bool }

commands.name: get_pie_focused_widget
commands.description: Report which UMG widget currently has FOCUS in the running PIE session -- the assertion that makes gamepad navigation testable instead of eyeballed. Resolves FSlateApplication's focused SWidget and maps it back to the UMG UWidget that created it, by walking up to the owning SObjectWidget and matching cached widgets: the same route the engine's own navigation component uses, and it has to walk up because the widget holding focus is usually an internal SButton, not the one that maps 1:1 to a UWidget. Pair it with inject_key_input route="slate", the only input path that moves focus at all: press Down, read this, assert. Returns has_focus:false as an honest success (not an error) when nothing is focused -- which is itself the finding when a menu opens with no focus and every navigation key then appears to do nothing.

params.name: user_index
params.description: Optional Slate user index (default 0). Local co-op players are separate Slate users, so player 2 is user 1.

commands.returns: { has_focus: bool, slate_widget_type: string, widget_name: string, widget_class: string, owning_user_widget: string, owning_user_widget_class: string, resolved_to_umg: bool, note? } -- resolved_to_umg:false together with has_focus:true means something in Slate holds focus but it is not a UMG widget (the viewport, a native Slate panel); slate_widget_type still names it.

commands.name: get_widget_animation_tracks
commands.description: Read what one UWidgetAnimation of a Widget Blueprint animates: every widget it binds (widget_name, possessable_guid, is_root_widget, widget_in_tree) with its tracks (track_class, track_type float|color|bool, the animated property) and, per section, its range in seconds and every key of every channel (frame, time_seconds, value). Read-only. It reads what add_widget_animation_track and add_widget_animation_keyframe write, and gives the widget_name, property_path and time_seconds that remove_widget_animation_track and remove_widget_animation_keyframe take; get_widget_animations lists the animations. A missing Blueprint or animation is an error.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the animation (get_widget_animations lists them)

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, object_name: string, tick_resolution: number, playback_start_seconds: number, playback_end_seconds: number, binding_count: int, track_count: int, key_count: int, bindings: [{widget_name, possessable_guid, is_root_widget, widget_in_tree, slot_widget_name?, tracks: [{track_class, track_type, property_name, property_path, sections: [{section_index, start_seconds, end_seconds, channels: [{channel_type, channel_index, key_count, keys: [{frame, time_seconds, value}]}]}]}]}] }

commands.name: get_widget_animations
commands.description: Lists the animations (UWidgetAnimations) authored in a Widget Blueprint asset, each with its object name, display name and whether it has a movie scene, plus animation_count and the resolved asset_path. Read-only: loads the asset, changes and saves nothing; a path that does not exist or is not a Widget Blueprint is an error, and a Blueprint without animations returns an empty list. Use it to get the animation_name that play_widget_animation, stop_widget_animation, remove_widget_animation, get_widget_animation_tracks and add_widget_animation_track take (either name works). add_widget_animation creates one; get_widget_animation_tracks shows what one animates.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: Asset path of the Widget Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu" (package or object path); it must exist and be a Widget Blueprint.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, asset_path: string, animations: [{name, display_name, has_movie_scene}], animation_count: int }

commands.name: get_widget_blueprint_tree
commands.description: Return a Widget Blueprint's widget tree as nested {name, class, children[]} AND, on request, the actual VALUES of its widgets and slots -- which is what makes verifying a style a cheap read instead of a PIE session. Off by default (a bare tree is what name-only callers want); three switches turn it on: property_paths reads exact dotted paths ("WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor") on every node whether or not they still hold the default -- this is the oracle that closes a set_widget_property; include_properties reports only what DIFFERS from each widget's archetype, i.e. what this Widget Blueprint actually changed, instead of the ~120 inherited properties nobody reads; include_slot adds each widget's UPanelSlot class plus its own non-default values (position, anchors, padding, row/column). Values come back as TYPED JSON, not UE export-text. widget_name dumps one subtree instead of the whole asset.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Optional: dump only this widget and its descendants instead of the whole tree.

params.name: property_paths
params.description: Optional list of property names or dotted paths read on EVERY node, emitted under "properties" even when the value is still the default. A path that does not exist on a given widget is listed in that node's "unresolved_property_paths" (normal: a WidgetStyle has no meaning on a TextBlock), never silently dropped.

params.name: include_properties
params.description: Emit each widget's editable properties that DIFFER from its archetype, under "non_default_properties" (default false).

params.name: include_slot
params.description: Emit each widget's UPanelSlot class and its non-default slot values under "slot" (default false).

params.name: include_navigation
params.description: Emit each widget's six gamepad/keyboard navigation directions under "navigation" (default false). A widget with no authored navigation reports all six as Escape with has_authored_navigation:false -- which is what it will actually do in game, rather than an empty object the caller has to interpret. Author them with set_widget_navigation.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Optional recursion limit (-1 = unlimited, the default). A panel cut off by the limit reports "children_omitted" instead of passing for a leaf.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, asset_path: string, widget_count: int, root_widget: string, dumped_root: string, include_properties: bool, include_slot: bool, include_navigation: bool, property_paths: [string], tree: {name, class, properties?, unresolved_property_paths?, non_default_properties?, slot?, children: [...], children_omitted?} }

commands.name: list_level_widget_components
commands.description: CALL THIS FIRST to discover valid widget_name values instead of guessing: it enumerates ALL UWidgetComponents on ALL actors of the current EDITOR level, which is the EXACT population that get_level_widget_properties / set_level_widget_visibility search by widget_name (remove_widget searches it too). It reads GEditor's world and never a running PIE session (use list_pie_widgets for that), and it lists every widget component on an actor, not just the first. WARNING: THIS POPULATION IS NOT WIDGET BLUEPRINTS, and that is the trap the name does not warn you about: these are world-space UWidgetComponents hosted on actors. To author the CONTENT of a Widget Blueprint asset -- its tree, styles or layout -- you want get_widget_blueprint_tree / set_widget_property / set_slot_properties instead. In particular ANCHORS live on a UCanvasPanelSlot inside a Widget Blueprint's tree and have no meaning at all on a level UWidgetComponent: set them with set_slot_properties(widget_bp_path, widget_name, anchors=[min_x,min_y,max_x,max_y]).

params.name: actor_name_filter
params.description: Optional substring filter on the owning actor's name (Contains match)

commands.returns: { components: [{ actor_name: string, widget_component_name: string, widget_name: string|null, widget_class: string|null }], component_count: number, actor_name_filter: string|null }

commands.name: list_pie_widgets
commands.description: Read LIVE UMG from the running PIE session (game thread): enumerate the active UUserWidgets added to the viewport and walk each widget tree, emitting name/class plus optional visibility/hover/text/value/geometry as a parent/child tree.  Reads only game-thread-safe widget-tree state (never the render thread). Errors clearly if no Play-In-Editor session is running.  DESCENDS INTO NESTED WIDGET BLUEPRINTS: an AAA screen is a Widget Blueprint composed of Widget Blueprints, so everything interesting sits one level below the first. Cycles are handled with a visited set plus max_depth, and a subtree that IS cut says so in subtree_omitted instead of looking like a leaf. Rich text is read too (URichTextBlock does not derive from UTextBlock). Not implemented: include_bindings, which is accepted and flagged in bindings_note.

params.name: root_filter
params.description: Optional case-sensitive substring; only top-level UserWidgets whose object name contains it are returned.

params.name: include_text
params.description: Optional bool (default true): include UTextBlock text.

params.name: include_visibility
params.description: Optional bool (default true): include visibility, is_hovered and has_keyboard_focus per widget. has_keyboard_focus is what tells you whether a navigation key will do anything at all: with nothing focused every key is a no-op, which reads exactly like broken navigation.

params.name: include_bindings
params.description: Optional bool (default false): NOT implemented in this subset; sets bindings_note when true.

params.name: include_values
params.description: Optional bool (default false): include is_enabled + widget-type-specific value (Slider.value / ProgressBar.percent / CheckBox.is_checked / ComboBoxString.selected_option).

params.name: include_geometry
params.description: Optional bool (default false): include GetCachedGeometry()-derived absolute_position/absolute_size, render_opacity, and render_transform.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Optional recursion limit (-1 = unlimited, the default). Counts every level including the descent into a nested Widget Blueprint's own tree. A subtree cut by the limit reports subtree_omitted rather than passing for a leaf.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD.

commands.returns: { widgets: [{ widget_name, class, is_any_animation_playing, visibility?, is_hovered?, children: [{ widget_name, class, visibility?, is_hovered?, text?, is_enabled?, value?, percent?, is_checked?, selected_option?, geometry?, children: [...] }] }], widget_count: int, scanned_viewport_widgets: int, include_text: bool, include_visibility: bool, include_bindings: bool, include_values: bool, include_geometry: bool, bindings_note?: string, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: list_widget_property_bindings
commands.description: List the UMG PROPERTY BINDINGS of a Widget Blueprint -- the "Bind" dropdown next to a property in the Designer's details panel, which makes that property recompute every frame by calling a function instead of holding a fixed value. These live in UWidgetBlueprint::Bindings, NOT in the widget tree and NOT in the event graph, so no other reader sees them; and UWidgetBlueprint::Bindings is NOT exposed to Python either (get_editor_property("bindings") throws), so this is the only headless way to read them. Each entry is re-validated live with the engine's own FDelegateEditorBinding::IsBindingValid, so a binding whose function was renamed or made non-pure comes back valid:false WITH the compiler's reason -- that is the difference between "there is a binding" and "there is a binding that works".

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: include_bindable_properties
params.description: Also list, per widget in the tree, which properties ACCEPT a binding at all (default false). A property is bindable only if its widget declares a companion delegate named "<Property>Delegate" -- this saves guessing.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, binding_count: int, bindings: [{ widget_name, property_name, function_name, kind, member_guid, source_property, valid, validation_messages: [string] }], bindable_properties?: {widget_name: [string]} }

commands.name: list_widget_types
commands.description: List the CURATED widget_type names accepted by add_widget_to_blueprint, with each entry's resolved /Script/UMG.<Name> class path and whether LoadObject actually resolves it in this build (should always be true; reported for honesty rather than assumed). This list is a convenience shortlist, NOT the full set of accepted values -- add_widget_to_blueprint also accepts any native widget class path (/Script/Module.ClassName) and any UserWidget-derived Widget Blueprint's /Game asset path (embeds a nested instance); see custom_class_note in the response.
commands.returns: { widget_types: [{ widget_type: string, class_path: string, resolvable: bool }], count: int, custom_class_note: string }

commands.name: play_widget_animation
commands.description: Plays an animation of a Widget Blueprint on a live instance of that widget in a running Play-In-Editor session (UUserWidget::PlayAnimation): the first on-screen instance of the Blueprint's class in the PIE world that world selects. Without a PIE session, or without such an instance, nothing plays and the call still succeeds with played false, headless true, requires_pie true and a note: start PIE with start_play_in_editor and get the widget on screen first. It changes only the running widget, never the asset (saved is always false), and played true means PlayAnimation was called, not read back; a repeat call starts the animation again. An animation name the Blueprint does not have is an error. Names come from get_widget_animations; stop playback with stop_widget_animation; list_pie_widgets shows which widgets are on screen.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: Asset path of the Widget Blueprint (e.g. "/Game/UI/WBP_HUD"); it must exist.

params.name: animation_name
params.description: Object name or display label of the animation, as get_widget_animations lists it (case-insensitive).

params.name: start_at_time
params.description: Optional time in seconds into the animation to start from (default 0).

params.name: num_loops
params.description: Optional whole number of times to play (default 1); values below 1 play once, so the engine's endless loop (0) is not available.

params.name: play_mode
params.description: Optional "Forward" (default) | "Reverse" | "PingPong", case-insensitive; any other value plays Forward.

params.name: playback_speed
params.description: Optional speed multiplier (default 1.0; 2.0 plays twice as fast).

params.name: restore_state
params.description: Optional bool: restore the pre-animation state on finish (default false).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, animation_exists: bool, played: bool, headless: bool, requires_pie: bool, note: string, saved: bool, live_widget_name?: string, live_animation_name?: string, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: pop_common_ui_widget
commands.description: Pop the ACTIVE screen off a live CommonUI stack, or clear the whole stack -- the inverse of push_common_ui_widget and the other half of driving a menu state machine headless (open, go deeper, come back, assert what is on top). WARNING: RUNTIME ONLY, same as the push: with no PIE session there is nothing on any stack. Popping an empty stack is an honest success with popped:false, not an error.

params.name: stack_widget_name
params.description: Name of the live activatable container in the running session.

params.name: clear_all
params.description: Remove EVERY widget instead of just the active one (default false).

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional local player index whose viewport widgets are searched (default 0).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N'.

commands.returns: { stack_widget_name, popped: bool, popped_widget: string, cleared_all: bool, widget_count: int, active_widget: string } -- widget_count and active_widget are read AFTER the operation; popped:false with widget_count:0 means the stack was already empty.

commands.name: push_common_ui_widget
commands.description: Push a screen onto a LIVE CommonUI activatable stack in the running PIE session -- the operation that lets a menu state machine be driven to a specific state and then asserted. create_common_ui_stack only puts the stack in place; its contents are populated at runtime with AddWidget, which this calls headless, so "open the pause menu, then the options page, now check the back button" is reproducible. WARNING: RUNTIME ONLY: the container's widget list and its widget pool are Transient, so with no PIE session there is genuinely nothing to push onto and this says so rather than pretending. The pushed widget is activated by the stack itself; read the result with get_common_ui_stack or list_pie_widgets, and move focus into it with set_pie_widget_focus.

params.name: stack_widget_name
params.description: Name of the live UCommonActivatableWidgetStack (or any activatable container) in the running session. Resolved like click_pie_widget, nested Widget Blueprints included.

params.name: widget_class
params.description: The UCommonActivatableWidget class to push: a /Game Widget Blueprint path, its generated-class path, or a native class path.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional local player index whose viewport widgets are searched (default 0).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N'.

commands.returns: { stack_widget_name, pushed_class, pushed_widget: string, widget_count: int, active_widget: string } -- widget_count and active_widget are read off the stack AFTER the push, so they are evidence rather than an echo.

commands.name: remove_viewmodel
commands.description: Remove the view-model context named context_name from the MVVM view of a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, then compile and save the Blueprint in one undo step; view_model_count is what the view keeps. Idempotent: a name that matches no context, or a Blueprint with no MVVM view at all (has_mvvm_extension=false), is a success with removed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is changed or saved. A missing Blueprint is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Inverse: add_viewmodel; drop a single binding instead: unbind_widget_from_viewmodel.

params.name: widget_blueprint_name
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset (string)

params.name: context_name
params.description: FName identifying the context to remove (idempotency key)

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_name, context_name, already_existed, removed, view_model_count, has_mvvm_extension, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: remove_widget
commands.description: Detach a runtime UserWidget, found by object name, from the viewport or panel holding it with RemoveFromParent. It searches the worlds create_widget uses: the one target_world names, or without it the running PIE world first and then the editor world; in each, the first widget hosted by a level UWidgetComponent, then any other UserWidget of that world. The object is not deleted, no asset changes and there is no undo. was_in_viewport and had_parent are measured before the call: both false means nothing was detached, as for a component-hosted widget. It never edits a Widget Blueprint asset: remove_widget_from_blueprint deletes a widget from one.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Object name of the runtime widget to detach (case-insensitive), as list_level_widget_components or create_widget report it

params.name: target_world
params.description: Optional world to search, with the values create_widget takes (editor, pie, server, client, pie:N, game). Omitted: the PIE world while PIE runs, then the editor world.

commands.returns: { widget_name: string, target_world: string, was_in_viewport: bool, had_parent: bool, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: remove_widget_animation
commands.description: Remove a UWidgetAnimation from a Widget Blueprint.  Inverse of add_widget_animation: finds the animation by object name or display label, removes it from WidgetBP->Animations, unregisters it as a blueprint variable (OnVariableRemoved), then compiles and saves. If no such animation exists it is an honest no-op (removed:false, already_existed:false, no save).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the animation to remove

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, object_name: string, removed: bool, already_existed: bool, animation_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: remove_widget_animation_keyframe
commands.description: Remove the key at time_seconds (or the key_index-th key) from every channel of the track that animates property_path of widget_name in one UWidgetAnimation of a Widget Blueprint -- the four channels of a color track at once -- then compile and save the Blueprint; no undo step. Inverse of add_widget_animation_keyframe, which rounds time_seconds to a tick frame the same way, so the time given there finds its key here. The key is matched within tolerance seconds (default 0: the same tick). A time or key_index that matches no key is an error listing the key times, and nothing changes; so is a missing Blueprint, animation, binding or track. The section keeps its range. Refused during PIE unless force=true; a failed save makes success false with save_error. Read keys: get_widget_animation_tracks; the whole track: remove_widget_animation_track.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the animation

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the animated widget

params.name: property_path
params.description: the SAME property_path given to add_widget_animation_track

params.name: time_seconds
params.description: time of the key to remove, in seconds; give it or key_index

params.name: key_index
params.description: index of the key among the first channel's keys (in time order); give it or time_seconds

params.name: tolerance
params.description: how far from time_seconds a key may be and still match, in seconds (default 0)

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, widget_name: string, property_path: string, track_type: string, removed_frame: int, removed_time_seconds: number, keys_removed: int, key_count_after: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: remove_widget_animation_track
commands.description: Remove the track that animates property_path of widget_name inside one UWidgetAnimation of a Widget Blueprint, with its sections and keys, then compile and save the Blueprint; no undo step. Inverse of add_widget_animation_track: when it was the widget's last track, the widget's binding (its possessable and FWidgetAnimationBinding) goes too, and binding_removed says so. widget_name is matched against the animation's bindings, so the binding of a widget already deleted from the tree can be cleaned too. A widget or property with no such track is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing compiled or saved); a missing Blueprint or animation is an error. Refused during PIE unless force=true; a failed save makes success false with save_error. Read first: get_widget_animation_tracks; one key only: remove_widget_animation_keyframe; the whole animation: remove_widget_animation.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the animation

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the animated widget, as get_widget_animation_tracks reports it

params.name: property_path
params.description: the property the track animates, the SAME property_path given to add_widget_animation_track (e.g. "RenderOpacity")

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, widget_name: string, property_path: string, removed: bool, track_class: string, binding_removed: bool, tracks_left_on_binding: int, saved: bool, save_error: string, note: string? }

commands.name: remove_widget_from_blueprint
commands.description: Delete widgets from the tree of a Widget Blueprint ASSET, children included, as the Designer's Delete does: their property bindings, the graph nodes that read their variables and the variables themselves go too; then compile and save the Blueprint. The removal is one undo step (compile and save are not undone). Inverse of add_widget_to_blueprint, add_list_view and create_common_ui_stack; remove_widget is the runtime tool and never edits an asset. Give widget_name or widget_names: every name is resolved first, and one unknown name fails the call with nothing changed. The reply re-reads the tree: removed_with_children lists every widget that left it. A widget animation that still binds a removed widget keeps its binding (remove_widget_animation_track drops it). Refused during PIE unless force=true; a failed save makes success false with save_error. Read the tree: get_widget_blueprint_tree.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget to delete (get_widget_blueprint_tree lists them); give it or widget_names

params.name: widget_names
params.description: several widget names to delete in one call, with one compile and one save

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, removed: string[], removed_with_children: string[], removed_count: int, widget_count: int, root_widget: string, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: remove_widget_property_binding
commands.description: Remove a UMG property binding (the Designer's "Bind" dropdown set back to none), so the property goes back to holding its authored fixed value. Inverse of add_widget_property_binding and idempotent: a property that was not bound is an honest success with removed:false, never an error.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget whose binding to drop

params.name: property_name
params.description: The bound property, e.g. "Text". Matching is on widget_name + property_name, which is exactly how UMG identifies a binding (one binding per property, max).

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, property_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, remaining_binding_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: rename_widget
commands.description: Rename the widget old_name in the tree of a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, with the Designer's F2 rename: its variable, graph references, bindings and navigation links follow, then the Blueprint is compiled and saved in one undo step. Characters an object name cannot hold are dropped from the name but kept in the display label; resolved_name is the name the widget got, with a note when it differs. An empty, too-long or taken name (another widget or Blueprint member), a BindWidget name of the wrong type, or a missing Blueprint or old_name is an error, and nothing changes. A new_name identical to the current name renames nothing (renamed=false, saved=false, a note); a case change is a rename. A failed save makes success false with save_error. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Move it: reparent_widget; read the tree: get_widget_blueprint_tree.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: old_name
params.description: current name of the widget in the tree

params.name: new_name
params.description: desired new name

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, old_name: string, new_name: string, resolved_name: string, renamed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }

commands.name: render_widget_preview
commands.description: Render a Widget Blueprint to a PNG on disk WITHOUT running the game: builds the widget with the editor's own designer flags, draws it through FWidgetRenderer into a render target and writes the file. This is what turns "does this style look right?" from a PIE session someone has to watch into a static read plus one image to LOOK at. HONEST SCOPE: it is a DESIGN preview, the same thing the UMG Designer shows -- not the live HUD. Anything that only exists while the game runs (text filled in NativeConstruct, property bindings, ViewModel data, anything behind an IsDesignTime() guard) renders at its default/empty value. Use list_pie_widgets or capture_pie_screenshot for the running session. Returns rendered:false with a reason (never a blank image) when the editor has no RHI (-nullrhi/headless), because FWidgetRenderer cannot draw there.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset to render

params.name: output_path
params.description: Optional output file. A bare name lands under <ProjectSaved>/MCP/WidgetPreviews/, an absolute path is used verbatim, and .png is appended when missing. Defaults to the asset's name.

params.name: width
params.description: Optional render width in pixels. Omit BOTH width and height to render at the widget's own desired size (a Slate prepass measures it).

params.name: height
params.description: Optional render height in pixels. Omit BOTH width and height to render at the widget's own desired size.

params.name: scale
params.description: Optional draw scale applied by the renderer (default 1.0), the equivalent of DPI scaling in the Designer.

params.name: opaque_background
params.description: Optional (default false). Force every pixel's alpha to 255 so the PNG is not transparent where the widget did not paint -- the same trick capture_viewport uses. Leave false to keep real transparency.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, rendered: bool, file_path: string, width: int, height: int, scale: number, drew_at_desired_size: bool, byte_size: int, designer_flags: string, preview_note: string, error?: string }

commands.name: reorder_widget_child
commands.description: Change a widget's index among its parent panel's children via UPanelWidget::ShiftChild (clamps new_index internally; safe with any int). For a CanvasPanel parent, visual stacking is governed by each child's CanvasPanelSlot ZOrder (set_slot_properties z_order), NOT child index -- the index shift is still applied and reported honestly, with a note.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget to reorder

params.name: new_index
params.description: desired index among its parent's children (clamped to [0, child_count])

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, parent_name: string, old_index: int, requested_index: int, resolved_index: int, child_count: int, reordered: bool, parent_is_canvas_panel: bool, note?: string, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: reparent_widget
commands.description: Move a widget to a new parent panel (optionally at a specific child index), via FWidgetBlueprintOperationUtils::MoveWidget -- the same primitive backing the Designer's drag-and-drop reparent. Validates the new parent is a panel widget and refuses to create a cycle. Optional slot_properties are applied to the widget's NEW slot afterward via the shared reflection setter (e.g. {"Row":1,"Column":2} for a GridSlot). THIS IS ALSO HOW YOU FILL A NAMED SLOT: a UNamedSlot is a UContentWidget (hence a panel), so add one with add_widget_to_blueprint widget_type="NamedSlot" and reparent the content into it -- there is no separate SetContentForSlot tool and none is needed (it answers reparented:true, new_slot_class:PanelSlot).

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget to move

params.name: new_parent_name
params.description: name of the panel widget to become the new parent

params.name: target_index
params.description: Optional int child index to insert at (default: append at the end)

params.name: slot_properties
params.description: Optional object of {PropertyName: value} applied to the resulting slot via reflection (best-effort; per-field errors are reported, not fatal)

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, old_parent_name: string, new_parent_name: string, new_slot_class: string, resolved_child_index: int, reparented: bool, slot_properties_applied: int, slot_property_errors?: [string], saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: set_box_slot_properties
commands.description: Configure a widget's box-family slot layout (alignment/padding/size) in a Widget Blueprint, found by the child widget's name, then compile and save the Widget Blueprint. Applies under a HorizontalBox/VerticalBox/Overlay/Border/SizeBox/ScrollBox, dispatching by slot type through the slot's own setters; set_properties would need the slot object's path and neither compiles nor saves. A padding that is not 1, 2 or 4 numbers, or an unknown alignment or size_rule, fails the call before anything is written. Size only applies to Horizontal/Vertical/ScrollBox slots -- on the others it comes back as a note. No undo step. CanvasPanel child: set_widget_slot_properties; GridPanel child: set_grid_slot_properties.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the child widget whose box slot to edit

params.name: horizontal_alignment
params.description: Optional alignment: Fill | Left | Center | Right

params.name: vertical_alignment
params.description: Optional alignment: Fill | Top | Center | Bottom

params.name: padding
params.description: Optional [Left, Top, Right, Bottom] floats (also accepts [uniform] or [horizontal, vertical]); any other shape, or an entry that is not a number, fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: size_rule
params.description: Optional Fill | Auto (Horizontal/Vertical/ScrollBox slots only).

params.name: size_value
params.description: Optional float fill weight (used with size_rule = Fill; default 1.0).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, slot_type: string, settings_applied: object, applied_count: int, notes: [string], saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_grid_slot_properties
commands.description: Configure the UGridSlot of a widget under a GridPanel in a Widget Blueprint, found by the child widget's name: row, column, spans, alignment, padding, layer, nudge. Over set_properties it needs no slot object path, uses the slot's own setters, and compiles and saves the Widget Blueprint; no undo step. A padding that is not 1, 2 or 4 numbers, a nudge that is not exactly 2, or an unknown alignment fails the call before anything is written. Idempotent. GridPanel: add_widget_to_blueprint widget_type="GridPanel"; other panels: set_box_slot_properties, set_widget_slot_properties.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the child widget whose grid slot to edit

params.name: row
params.description: Optional int row index of the cell

params.name: column
params.description: Optional int column index of the cell

params.name: row_span
params.description: Optional int number of rows this slot spans

params.name: column_span
params.description: Optional int number of columns this slot spans

params.name: horizontal_alignment
params.description: Optional alignment: Fill | Left | Center | Right

params.name: vertical_alignment
params.description: Optional alignment: Fill | Top | Center | Bottom

params.name: padding
params.description: Optional [Left, Top, Right, Bottom] floats (also accepts [uniform] or [horizontal, vertical]); any other shape, or an entry that is not a number, fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: layer
params.description: Optional int draw/hit-test layer offset (positive draws on top).

params.name: nudge
params.description: Optional [X, Y] content offset; anything but an array of exactly 2 numbers fails the call and nothing is changed.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, slot_type: string, settings_applied: object, applied_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: set_level_widget_visibility
commands.description: Set the Slate visibility of a UUserWidget hosted on a UWidgetComponent in the current editor level, found by the widget's object name (list_level_widget_components gives the names; a running PIE session is never searched). visibility is matched without case, and an invalid value is an error before the lookup; a widget not found is an error too. The change goes to the live widget instance only: no undo step, nothing marked dirty or saved, and a widget the component rebuilds, after a level reload for instance, starts from its class default again. A repeat call changes nothing. previous_visibility and actual_visibility are read around the write, and visibility_set compares the result with the request. Read it with get_level_widget_properties; live PIE UI is list_pie_widgets; a Widget Blueprint's own widgets are set_widget_property.

params.name: widget_name
