params.description: Object name of the UUserWidget a UWidgetComponent in the editor level hosts, as list_level_widget_components reports it in widget_name

params.name: visibility
params.description: Target visibility state: Visible, Collapsed, Hidden, HitTestInvisible, or SelfHitTestInvisible (matched without case)

commands.returns: { widget_name: string, visibility_set: bool, previous_visibility: string, requested_visibility: string, actual_visibility: string, widget_valid: bool }

commands.name: set_named_slot_content
commands.description: Put a widget into a NAMED SLOT of a NESTED Widget Blueprint instance -- the "template screen with holes" pattern. reparent_widget already fills a UNamedSlot that belongs to your own tree (it is a UContentWidget, so it is just a panel), but the slot of an embedded instance is not a panel in your tree at all: it is an entry in that instance's NamedSlotBindings, and no other tool writes it. WARNING: the engine's SetContentForSlot returns nothing and SILENTLY DROPS the binding when the slot name does not exist, so this re-reads it with GetContentForSlot afterwards and reports the RE-READ, never the call. List what a given instance offers with available_slots in the response, or pass no slot_name at all to just enumerate them.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the OUTER Widget Blueprint (the one that owns both the nested instance and the content).

params.name: host_widget_name
params.description: Name of the nested Widget Blueprint instance in the outer tree -- the widget that OWNS the slot.

params.name: slot_name
params.description: Name of the named slot to fill. Omit to only enumerate what the host offers (nothing is written, available_slots is still returned).

params.name: content_widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget in the OUTER tree to place in the slot. It must already exist there (add_widget_to_blueprint creates it). Omit together with clear=true to empty the slot.

params.name: clear
params.description: Empty the slot instead of filling it (default false). Mutually exclusive with content_widget_name.

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path, host_widget_name, host_class, available_slots: [string], slot_name, content_widget_name, filled: bool, verified_content: string, saved, save_error } -- verified_content is what GetContentForSlot returns AFTER the write: empty when the engine dropped the binding, which is the only way to tell that from a success.

commands.name: set_pie_list_view_items
commands.description: Populate a LIVE UListView/UTileView in the running PIE session. Resolves widget_name (optionally drilling into child_name) among the active viewport UserWidgets using the same walk click_pie_widget uses, resolves each entry in items[] to a UObject* (an actor name/label in the PIE world, else a /Game asset path via FSoftObjectPath::TryLoad), then calls SetListItems (or AddItems when append=true). Companion to add_list_view (view_type List or Tile), which only constructs an EMPTY view.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Required. Name of the target UListView/UTileView in the live tree (as reported by list_pie_widgets), resolved the same way click_pie_widget resolves widget_name.

params.name: items
params.description: Required array of strings. Each entry is either an actor name/label to resolve in the PIE world, or a /Game asset path to load via FSoftObjectPath::TryLoad.

params.name: child_name
params.description: Optional: after resolving widget_name, drill into a descendant widget with this name and populate THAT widget instead.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional (default 0): restrict widget resolution to viewport UserWidgets owned by this local player index (single-player PIE resolves globally).

params.name: append
params.description: Optional (default false). false = SetListItems (replaces the current item list). true = AddItems (appends).

params.name: refresh
params.description: Optional (default true). Accepted for API symmetry: UListView::SetListItems/AddItems call UListViewBase::RequestRefresh() UNCONDITIONALLY, so refresh=false cannot honestly suppress it -- see refresh_note in the response rather than a silent no-op.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default) | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session each client owns its own widgets.

commands.returns: { success, widget_name, resolved_widget, resolved_class, child_name?, player_index, requested_items, resolved_count, unresolved_items[], append, refresh, refresh_note, item_count_after, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: set_pie_widget_focus
commands.description: Give keyboard/gamepad FOCUS to a live UMG widget in the running PIE session, so navigation has somewhere to start from. Menus routinely open with nothing focused, and then every navigation key does nothing -- which reads exactly like broken navigation and sends you to debug rules that were fine. Resolves the widget the same way click_pie_widget does (widget_name, optionally drilling in with child_name, nested Widget Blueprints included), then calls UWidget::SetKeyboardFocus. Verify with get_pie_focused_widget and drive from there with inject_key_input route="slate".

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of a live UserWidget added to the viewport, or of a widget inside one.

params.name: child_name
params.description: Optional: after resolving widget_name, drill into this descendant by name (nested Widget Blueprints included).

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional local player index whose viewport widgets are searched (default 0).

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector, same rules as list_pie_widgets: absent/'pie' | 'server' | 'client' | 'pie:N'.

commands.returns: { focused: bool, widget_name: string, widget_class: string, has_keyboard_focus: bool } -- has_keyboard_focus is RE-READ off the widget after the call, so it is evidence and not an echo: false means Slate refused the focus, and the usual cause is that the widget is not focusable (check IsFocusable and its Visibility -- a HitTestInvisible widget cannot take focus).

commands.name: set_pie_widget_value
commands.description: Set a LIVE PIE input widget's REAL value (companion to click_pie_widget, which only broadcasts a delegate with zero-init params and never touches Slider/CheckBox/EditableTextBox/ComboBoxString state first). Resolves the widget exactly like click_pie_widget (same widget_name/child_name/player_index rules), then calls the widget's real setter: USlider::SetValue, UCheckBox::SetIsChecked, UEditableTextBox::SetText/UEditableText::SetText, UComboBoxString::SetSelectedOption, or UProgressBar::SetPercent. fire_event genuinely gates a manual OnCheckStateChanged/OnTextChanged(+OnTextCommitted) broadcast for CheckBox/EditableText(Box); Slider/ComboBoxString auto-broadcast on the engine side whenever the value actually changes (fire_event cannot suppress that -- see event_fired_note); ProgressBar has no change event at all. Errors clearly if no PIE session is running, the widget is not found, or its class is not one of the supported input types.

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Required. Name of the target UWidget in the live tree (as reported by list_pie_widgets).

params.name: value
params.description: Required object: {"type":"float"|"bool"|"string", "value": <matching JSON type>}.

params.name: child_name
params.description: Optional: drill into a descendant widget with this name after resolving widget_name.

params.name: player_index
params.description: Optional (default 0): filter to viewport UserWidgets owned by this local player index.

params.name: fire_event
params.description: Optional bool (default true): broadcast the widget's change event where the engine does not already do so unconditionally (CheckBox / EditableTextBox / EditableText).

params.name: commit_type
params.description: Optional "Default" | "OnEnter" | "OnUserMovedFocus": when present (EditableTextBox/EditableText only, and fire_event is true), also broadcasts OnTextCommitted with this commit type.

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD.

commands.returns: { widget_name, resolved_widget, resolved_class, value_type, value, set: bool, event_fired: bool, player_index, child_name?, event_fired_note?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: set_slot_properties
commands.description: Set ANY property of a widget's UPanelSlot BY REFLECTION, whatever the concrete slot class is -- including the 9 of UMG's 17 slot types that no shortcut covers (UButtonSlot, which is every widget inside a Button; UUniformGridSlot, UWrapBoxSlot, UStackBoxSlot, UWidgetSwitcherSlot, USafeZoneSlot, UScaleBoxSlot, UBackgroundBlurSlot, UWindowTitleBarAreaSlot) and any slot type a future engine version adds. Accepts dotted paths into nested slot structs ("Padding.Left", "Size.SizeRule") and reports field by field what landed, same honest contract as set_widget_property: the oracle is applied[]/ignored[]/errors[], not success. It covers the common slots too, with the engine's names and formats: a CanvasPanel slot's LayoutData {Anchors, Offsets {Left, Top, Right, Bottom}}, ZOrder and bAutoSize; a box, overlay, border, size-box or scroll-box slot's HorizontalAlignment/VerticalAlignment (HAlign_Center, VAlign_Fill...), Padding {Left, Top, Right, Bottom} and Size {SizeRule, Value}; a grid slot's Row, Column, RowSpan, ColumnSpan, Layer and Nudge {X, Y}.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget whose slot to edit (its PARENT panel decides the slot class; read it from get_widget_blueprint_tree include_slot=true)

params.name: properties
params.description: {"<property or dotted path>": <value>, ...} written onto the slot object, e.g. {"Padding":[8,4,8,4],"HorizontalAlignment":"HAlign_Center"}. Enums accept the short name; FMargin accepts a scalar, [h,v] or [l,t,r,b].

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, parent_name: string, slot_class: string, requested_paths: [string], applied: [string], ignored: [string], errors: [{path, error}], failed_paths: [string], applied_count: int, all_applied: bool, current_values: object, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: set_viewmodel_field
commands.description: Create a fresh instance of view_model_class and give it to a live UUserWidget through UMVVMView::SetViewModelByClass, which fills the view-model context of the widget whose class matches; context_name does not pick it. The widget is the one a UWidgetComponent shows: on the first actor whose label matches widget_instance_name, or, when the name contains a slash, on the first actor whose component uses that widget class, searched across every open world, PIE included. Runtime state only: nothing is compiled or saved, and each call swaps in a new instance. set and assigned_context are read back: if no context took it (none or several match, or it is not settable), success is false with the reason. A widget without an MVVM view, a class that is abstract or not a UMVVMViewModelBase, or no matching widget is an error. Authoring-time contexts: add_viewmodel; bindings: bind_widget_to_viewmodel.

params.name: widget_instance_name
params.description: Label of an actor that has a widget component, matched case-insensitively, or, when it contains a slash, the widget class its component uses, e.g. "/Game/UI/WBP_Nameplate".

params.name: view_model_class
params.description: VM class: asset path or /Script/<Module>.<ClassName>

params.name: context_name
params.description: Name of the view-model context meant; echoed back, since the context is chosen by the class of view_model_class (assigned_context says which took it).

commands.returns: { widget_instance_name, view_model_class, context_name, set, assigned_context, instance_class, error?, note? }

commands.name: set_widget_drag_drop
commands.description: Set DragDropOperationClass on a widget found by name in the tree of a Widget Blueprint, then compile and save the Blueprint in one undo step (set=true, changed=true, property_set); a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the class kept in memory. A widget already holding that class is left as it is (changed=false, saved=false, a note), nothing compiled or saved. Only list, tile and tree views (UListViewBase) have that property; any other widget gets set=false and a note, nothing written: its drag and drop is the OnDragDetected and OnDrop events of a User Widget graph, authored with build_blueprint_graph after list_overridable_functions. operation_class defaults to /Script/UMG.DragDropOperation; a class that does not load or is no UDragDropOperation, or a missing Blueprint or widget, is an error, nothing written. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Make the view with add_list_view (view_type List, Tile or Tree).

params.name: widget_blueprint_name
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/UI/WBP_Inventory".

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget in the tree of that Blueprint, e.g. "ItemTiles"; only a list, tile or tree view can take the class.

params.name: operation_class
params.description: Class path of a UDragDropOperation subclass, e.g. "/Script/UMG.DragDropOperation" or "/Game/UI/DDO_Item.DDO_Item_C"; defaults to /Script/UMG.DragDropOperation.

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_name, widget_name, operation_class, set, changed, has_drag_drop_property, operation_class_loaded, property_set?, saved?, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: set_widget_navigation
commands.description: Author a widget's GAMEPAD/KEYBOARD navigation rules -- what gets focus when the player pushes up, down, left, right, Tab or Shift+Tab off this widget. Without this a menu cannot be driven with a pad, and it is NOT reachable through set_widget_property: UWidget::Navigation is an Instanced SUBOBJECT that starts null, so there is no asset path a reflection setter could point at and a dotted path fails on a null segment. Follows the editor's own flow, including the two details that matter: the subobject is created RF_Transactional with template flags propagated, and if all six directions end up on Escape the subobject is DISCARDED (that is what tells "no navigation authored" apart from "navigation authored that happens to be the default", and it is what the Designer does). Read the result back with get_widget_blueprint_tree include_navigation=true.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Name of the widget in the tree whose navigation to author

params.name: rules
params.description: Dict of {direction: rule}. Direction is Up|Down|Left|Right|Next|Previous (Next/Previous are Tab/Shift+Tab). The value is either a rule name string ("Wrap", "Stop", "Escape") or an object {"rule":"Explicit","widget_to_focus":"Btn_Confirm"} when the rule needs a target. Rules: Escape (default -- let the search continue outward), Stop (movement dies here), Wrap (cycle inside the container), Explicit (jump to widget_to_focus).

params.name: all_directions
params.description: Optional rule name applied to ALL SIX directions before `rules` is processed, so you can say "Stop everywhere, except Down" in one call. Explicit is refused here: it would need six different targets.

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true).

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path, widget_name, applied: [{direction, rule, widget_to_focus}], current_navigation: {Up:{rule,widget_to_focus}, ...}, navigation_discarded: bool, saved, save_error } -- navigation_discarded:true means every direction ended on Escape so the subobject was dropped, exactly as the Designer does; current_navigation is then all-Escape.

commands.name: set_widget_property
commands.description: Set ONE or MANY reflected properties on a widget of a Widget Blueprint, addressing NESTED STYLE FIELDS by dotted path ("WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor", "Items[0].Label") and reporting FIELD BY FIELD what landed, then compile and save it (save=false defers). Use it instead of set_properties for widgets: it finds the widget by name in the tree, writes leaf fields inside structs, takes color/margin/brush shorthands and compiles; set_properties takes only top-level names and compiles nothing. Two calling shapes over one write path: property_name+value, or a properties map under ONE Modify + ONE compile + ONE save (a FButtonStyle is ~30 leaf fields -- one call, not 30 recompiles). WARNING: the oracle is applied[]/ignored[]/errors[], NOT success: a key matching no reflected field lands in ignored[] and all_applied goes false. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true. Read back with get_widget_blueprint_tree(property_paths=[...]); slot layout: set_slot_properties.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget in the tree (get_widget_blueprint_tree lists them)

params.name: property_name
params.description: Single reflected property name ("Text") OR a dotted path into nested structs ("WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor"); array indices are supported ("Items[0].Label"). Requires `value`. Omit when using `properties`.

params.name: value
params.description: New value for property_name: string, number, bool, JSON object (struct, applied field by field) or JSON array. Colors accept {"R":1,"G":0,"B":0,"A":1}, [r,g,b,a] or "#RRGGBBAA"; FMargin accepts a scalar, [h,v] or [l,t,r,b]; an FSlateBrush accepts a texture/material path string; enums accept the short name ("Box").

params.name: properties
params.description: Batch form: {"<dotted path>": <value>, ...}. Every path is written against the SAME widget under one Modify/compile/save. Combinable with property_name+value (both end up in the same map).

params.name: save
params.description: Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true). Pass false to chain several calls and save once at the end -- the asset stays dirty in memory until something saves it.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, widget_class: string, requested_paths: [string], applied: [string], ignored: [string], errors: [{path, error}], failed_paths: [string], applied_count: int, all_applied: bool, current_values: object, saved: bool, save_error: string }

commands.name: set_widget_slot_properties
commands.description: Set the CanvasPanelSlot layout of a widget inside a CanvasPanel of a Widget Blueprint asset -- anchors, offsets, position, size, z_order and auto_size, only those passed -- then compile and save the blueprint; the reply reads the whole slot back. Use it rather than set_slot_properties for canvas layout: it takes plain arrays ([MinX,MinY,MaxX,MaxY], [L,T,R,B], [X,Y]) instead of LayoutData.* paths. position and size write the same fields as offsets (Left/Top and Right/Bottom) and are applied after it, so they win when both are given. An anchors or offsets that is not exactly 4 numbers, or a position or size that is not exactly 2, fails the call before anything is written, compiled or saved. A widget not under a CanvasPanel, or a call with none of the six fields, is an error. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true. For other slot types use set_box_slot_properties, set_grid_slot_properties or set_slot_properties.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: widget_name
params.description: name of the widget whose canvas slot to edit

params.name: anchors
params.description: Optional [MinX, MinY, MaxX, MaxY] anchor floats; anything but an array of exactly 4 numbers fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: offsets
params.description: Optional [Left, Top, Right, Bottom] offset floats; anything but an array of exactly 4 numbers fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: position
params.description: Optional [X, Y] position; anything but an array of exactly 2 numbers fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: size
params.description: Optional [X, Y] size; anything but an array of exactly 2 numbers fails the call and nothing is changed.

params.name: z_order
params.description: Optional int draw/hit-test order (higher draws on top); use with reorder_widget_child's note for CanvasPanel stacking.

params.name: auto_size
params.description: Optional bool: when true, the slot sizes itself to the widget's desired size instead of `size`.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, anchors_set: bool, offsets_set: bool, position_set: bool, size_set: bool, z_order_set: bool, auto_size_set: bool, current_anchors: [float], current_offsets: [float], current_position: [float], current_size: [float], current_z_order: int, current_auto_size: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }

commands.name: stop_widget_animation
commands.description: Stop a widget animation. REAL stop (UUserWidget::StopAnimation) when a live PIE instance of this WidgetBP is found in the viewport's active UUserWidgets: stopped is true when the animation was playing before the call and is not after it; one that was not playing (stopped or paused) succeeds with stopped:false and a note, and one still playing after the call is an error. Falls back to an honest headless gate (stopped:false, headless:true, requires_pie:true) otherwise.

params.name: widget_bp_path
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: animation_name
params.description: object name OR display label of the animation to stop

params.name: world
params.description: Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) | 'server' (the PIE world with authority) | 'client' | 'pie:N' | 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD.

commands.returns: { widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, animation_exists: bool, stopped: bool, headless: bool, requires_pie: bool, note: string, saved: bool, live_widget_name?: string, live_animation_name?: string, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }

commands.name: unbind_widget_from_viewmodel
commands.description: Remove one binding from the MVVM view of a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, picked by binding_index or, when no index is given, by binding_id, then compile and save the Blueprint in one undo step; binding_count is what the view keeps. A binding that is not there (an index out of range, an id no binding has, or a Blueprint with no MVVM view: has_mvvm_extension=false) is a success with removed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is changed or saved. By index a repeat call removes the binding that moved into that index. Neither identifier, a binding_id that is not a GUID, or a missing Blueprint is an error. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Inverse: bind_widget_to_viewmodel; a whole context: remove_viewmodel.

params.name: widget_blueprint_name
params.description: /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset

params.name: binding_index
params.description: int index of the binding to remove (primary identifier; one of binding_index / binding_id required)

params.name: binding_id
params.description: optional GUID string of the binding to remove (alternative to binding_index)

commands.returns: { widget_blueprint_name, binding_index?, binding_id?, already_existed, removed, binding_count, has_mvvm_extension, saved, save_error?, note? }

commands.name: add_usd_internal_reference
commands.description: Add an internal reference composition arc (references another prim inside the SAME stage; no asset_path needed).

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Prim that owns the reference (the consumer).

params.name: target_prim_path
params.description: Prim inside the same stage to reference.

params.name: position
params.description: List position (same vocabulary as add_usd_reference). Default "BackOfPrependList".

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, prim_path: string, target_prim_path: string, added: bool, position: string, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: add_usd_payload
commands.description: Add a payload composition arc to a prim (load-on-demand; payloads are NOT loaded by the stage unless an explicit Load rule says so), composing the prim prim_path_for_target of the layer at asset_path, or that layer's defaultPrim when prim_path_for_target is empty (uses_default_prim). The arc is authored on the stage's current edit target layer and stays in memory until save_usd_stage; no undo step. added=false, with the USD messages in errors, when USD rejects the arc; an unregistered stage or a missing prim is an error. Read it back with get_usd_prim_metadata (key "payload"). Inverse: clear_usd_payloads (one payload with asset_path).

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Prim that owns the payload.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Identifier of the layer containing the payload.

params.name: prim_path_for_target
params.description: Absolute path of the prim inside the payload layer to compose, e.g. "/Chair". Empty (default) authors an empty target path, which USD resolves to that layer's defaultPrim.

params.name: position
params.description: List position (same vocabulary as add_usd_reference). Default "BackOfPrependList".

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, prim_path: string, asset_path: string, prim_path_for_target: string, uses_default_prim: bool, added: bool, position: string, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: add_usd_reference
commands.description: Add an external reference arc to a prim of a registered USD stage, so prim_path composes the prim prim_path_for_target of the layer file at asset_path, or that layer's defaultPrim when prim_path_for_target is empty (uses_default_prim). For a prim of the same stage use add_usd_internal_reference, for a load-on-demand arc add_usd_payload; clear_usd_references is the inverse, and get_usd_prim_info or list_usd_prims shows the composed result. The arc is authored on the stage's current edit target layer (set_usd_edit_target; list_usd_stage_layers shows the stack) and stays in memory until save_usd_stage. No undo step. added=false, with the USD messages in errors, when USD rejects the arc; an unregistered stage_name or a prim that does not exist is an error (success=false) and nothing is authored.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage (list_usd_stages shows it), e.g. "Shot010".

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the existing prim that receives the reference, e.g. "/World/Chair"; define_usd_prim creates one.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Identifier of the layer to reference: an absolute file path such as "C:/Assets/chair.usda", or a path relative to the layer being edited such as "./chair.usda".

params.name: prim_path_for_target
params.description: Absolute path of the prim inside the referenced layer to compose, e.g. "/Chair". Empty (default) authors an empty target path, which USD resolves to the referenced layer's defaultPrim; a layer without one composes nothing there.

params.name: position
params.description: "FrontOfPrependList" | "BackOfPrependList" | "FrontOfAppendList" | "BackOfAppendList", case-insensitive; prepended arcs are stronger than appended ones. Default BackOfPrependList, which is also what any other string means (the reply then echoes the string sent).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, prim_path: string, asset_path: string, prim_path_for_target: string, uses_default_prim: bool, added: bool, position: string, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: add_usd_variant
commands.description: Add a new variant to an existing variant set at the requested list position; idempotent (returns already_existed:true when the variant is already present). Inverse: remove_usd_variant.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: SdfPath of the prim that authors the variant set

params.name: variant_set_name
params.description: Variant set that will receive the new variant

params.name: variant_name
params.description: Name of the variant to add

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Stage cache key

params.name: position
params.description: One of FrontOfPrependList / BackOfPrependList / FrontOfAppendList / BackOfAppendList (default BackOfPrependList)

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, variant_set_name: string, variant_name: string, added: bool, already_existed: bool, position: string }

commands.name: add_usd_variant_set
commands.description: Author a new (empty) variant set on a prim at the requested list position; idempotent (returns already_existed:true when the set is already present). Inverse: remove_usd_variant_set.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: SdfPath of the prim that will author the variant set

params.name: variant_set_name
params.description: Name of the variant set to create

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Stage cache key

params.name: position
params.description: One of FrontOfPrependList / BackOfPrependList / FrontOfAppendList / BackOfAppendList (default BackOfPrependList, matching the USD wrapper default)

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, variant_set_name: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, position: string }

commands.name: apply_usd_prim_schema
commands.description: Apply a USD API schema (e.g. "MaterialBindingAPI") to an existing prim of a registered USD stage, on the current edit target. Checks CanApplyAPI first: a schema that cannot apply returns applied=false with the USD reason in why_not instead of an error. Not saved to disk.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: schema_name
params.description: Schema identifier (not the C++ class name), e.g. "MaterialBindingAPI", "GeomModelAPI"

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { applied: bool, schema_name: string, why_not?: string }

commands.name: clear_usd_attribute
commands.description: Clear authored values of a USD attribute on a prim of an open stage: with time, only the sample at that time code; without it, the default value and every time sample. Edits the stage in memory; save_usd_stage writes it. Returns present and cleared, present false when the attribute is missing.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Name of the attribute to clear, e.g. "size".

params.name: time
params.description: Time code of the single sample to clear (ClearAtTime); omit it to clear the default value and all samples (Clear).

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attr_name: string, cleared: bool, present: bool, time: number? }

commands.name: clear_usd_payloads
commands.description: Remove the payload arcs of a prim: every payload (UsdPayloads::ClearPayloads), or with asset_path the one payload to that layer and target prim (RemovePayload). Inverse of add_usd_payload, which clear_usd_references does not touch; the edit lands on the stage's current edit target layer, as the add did. Irreversible, like every USD composition edit here (no undo). had_payloads and has_payloads are the prim read before and after (UsdPrim::HasAuthoredPayloads). A stage or prim that does not resolve is an error; a prim with no payload is an honest no-op (cleared=false). Save the layer with save_usd_stage.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Prim whose payloads should be removed.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Optional identifier of the payload's layer: only the payload to that layer (and prim_path_for_target) goes.

params.name: prim_path_for_target
params.description: With asset_path, the prim inside that layer the payload targets, as given to add_usd_payload. Empty (default) means the default-prim payload add_usd_payload authors when it is given none.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, prim_path: string, asset_path?: string, had_payloads: bool, cleared: bool, has_payloads: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: clear_usd_references
commands.description: Remove every reference arc of a prim of a registered USD stage, external and internal alike (UsdReferences::ClearReferences); payloads stay (clear_usd_payloads removes those). The inverse of add_usd_reference and add_usd_internal_reference; no tool removes a single reference. Only the edits on the stage's current edit target layer go, so references authored on other layers still compose (switch layers with set_usd_edit_target; list_usd_stage_layers shows the stack); check the result with get_usd_prim_info. Irreversible: no undo step. The change stays in memory until save_usd_stage. A repeat call leaves the list empty again. An unregistered stage_name or a prim that does not exist is an error (success=false); USD complaints come back in errors.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage (list_usd_stages shows it), e.g. "Shot010".

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the existing prim whose references are cleared, e.g. "/World/Chair"; list_usd_prims lists prim paths.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, prim_path: string, cleared: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: clear_usd_variant_selection
commands.description: Clear the selected variant of one variant set on a prim of a cached USD stage, so no variant of that set is selected there; the set and its variants stay. It first moves the stage's edit target to the strongest layer that defines the prim and clears the selection on that layer, so a selection authored on another layer can still apply: check with list_usd_variant_sets. The edit stays in memory until save_usd_stage and has no undo step. A repeat call changes nothing more; cleared is the engine's answer. An unknown stage, an invalid or missing prim, or a variant set the prim does not have is an error and nothing is written. To pick another variant instead use set_usd_variant_selection; to delete the set itself, remove_usd_variant_set.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the existing prim that has the variant set, e.g. "/World/Car"

params.name: variant_set_name
params.description: Variant set whose selection is cleared, as list_usd_variant_sets reports it, e.g. "color"

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage (list_usd_stages shows it), or the end of a cached stage's root layer identifier, case-insensitive, e.g. "Shot010"

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, variant_set_name: string, cleared: bool }

commands.name: close_usd_stage
commands.description: Close a USD stage by its LLM-facing stage_name.  Removes the stage from the LLM-facing UEAgent::UsdRegistry::GStageNameCache AND calls UnrealUSDWrapper::EraseStageFromCache on it — this is the ONLY way to release a memory stage (memory stages are never closed automatically, even on editor shutdown). If stage_name is not in the cache the call returns success with a note rather than an error (idempotent — closing an already-closed stage is a no-op). The 'removed_from_cache' field reports whether the stage was actually present in the UnrealUSDWrapper stage cache at close time.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under via open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, closed: bool, was_in_cache: bool, removed_from_cache: bool, note: string? }

commands.name: create_usd_attribute
commands.description: Create an attribute of a given USD type on a prim of an open stage, or return the existing one with created false. Edits the stage in memory; save_usd_stage writes it. Returns name, type_name, cpp_type and created; author its value with set_usd_attribute_value.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Attribute name (e.g. "size", "displayColor")

params.name: type_name
params.description: USD type name (e.g. "float", "float3", "token", "asset")

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, name: string, type_name: string, cpp_type: string, created: bool }

commands.name: create_usd_stage
commands.description: Create a new USD stage (either on-disk or in-memory).  When file_path is provided, UnrealUSDWrapper::NewStage(FilePath) creates a root layer file at that path and opens it as a stage. When file_path is omitted or empty, NewStage() (no args) creates a memory-only stage — this is the only way to author a USD stage that is NOT persisted to disk; the only way to clean it up is close_usd_stage. The new stage is always added to the LLM-facing UEAgent::UsdRegistry::GStageNameCache under stage_name (default "Untitled"), so subsequent calls can refer to it by name. The returned identifier is the root layer's USD identifier (real path for on-disk; an anonymous "anon:0x..." handle for memory stages).

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute path for the new USD root layer file (.usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz). Omit or empty for a memory-only stage (optional).

params.name: stage_name
params.description: LLM-facing name to register the new stage under (optional, default "Untitled").

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, file_path: string, memory: bool, identifier: string, real_path: string, dirty: bool, is_valid: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: create_usd_stage_actor
commands.description: Spawn an AUsdStageActor, the actor that displays a USD file live in the level, into the editor world (not a PIE world), or return the one already there: the tool keeps one stage actor per world, so when any exists it changes nothing and returns already_existed true with that actor's actor_path, whatever name you pass. The level is not saved (save_level). The new actor shows nothing until set_usd_stage_actor_root_layer gives it a USD file; then inspect it with get_usd_stage_actor_info, get_usd_generated_component and get_usd_generated_assets. To author a USD file without an actor use create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage instead; remove the actor with delete_actor. A new actor gets scale [1, 1, 1]; scale is the actor's scale read back after the call (change it with set_actor_transform). No editor world is an error (the editor must be running with a level open).

params.name: name
params.description: Object name for a new actor, e.g. "UsdStageActor" (the default); a numeric suffix is added when taken, so read the real name from the reply. Ignored when a stage actor already exists.

params.name: location
params.description: World [x, y, z] location in cm for a new actor, e.g. [0, 0, 100] (default [0, 0, 0]); missing trailing numbers stay 0.

params.name: rotation
params.description: World [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees for a new actor, e.g. [0, 90, 0] (default [0, 0, 0]).

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, already_existed: bool, name: string, scale: [x, y, z] }

commands.name: define_usd_prim
commands.description: Define a prim (specifier def) of type_name at prim_path on a registered USD stage, at its current edit target, defining missing ancestors as typeless prims. On an existing prim of another type it replaces the type, so leaving type_name out retypes it to Xform. The requested specifier is then authored at the edit target (specifier_set_ok); specifier reports it only when that write succeeded, and a failed write fails the call. An unknown specifier is refused before anything is authored. In memory only: save_usd_stage writes it. override_usd_prim authors an over instead; set_usd_prim_metadata with key "typeName" changes only the type.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath, e.g. /World/Cube

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under

params.name: type_name
params.description: USD type name (Xform, Mesh, Cube, Scope, Camera, DistantLight...). Default: Xform

params.name: specifier
params.description: "Def" | "Over" | "Class", case-insensitive; anything else is refused. Default: Def

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, type_name: string, specifier?: string, is_valid: bool, specifier_set_ok: bool, requested?: object }

commands.name: flatten_usd_stage
commands.description: Export a flattened copy of the stage to a .usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz file (the file writer is chosen by the extension).  Wraps UE::FUsdStage::Export(OutputPath, bAddSourceFileComment, FileFormatArguments) — does NOT alter the in-memory stage. When add_source_file_comment is true (default) the flattened file includes a comment header noting the source file (useful for provenance). The returned 'exported' field reports pxr::'s bool return — false means the file writer could not write the requested path (e.g. invalid extension, permission denied). Realistic gotcha: stage.Export() requires the stage NOT be in a restricted-edit state — under headless cov this is not an issue, but in-editor it can be during PIE.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under, OR an absolute file path to auto-open.

params.name: output_path
params.description: Absolute path of the flattened file to write. The file extension picks the writer (.usda=text, .usdc=binary, .usdz=archive).

params.name: add_source_file_comment
params.description: Include the source-file comment header in the flattened file (default true).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, resolution: string, output_path: string, exported: bool, add_source_file_comment: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: get_usd_attribute_time_samples
commands.description: List the time codes, in ascending order, at which one attribute of a prim on a USD stage this server has open has authored time samples; the values themselves are not returned (read one with get_usd_attribute_value at that time). Read-only: the stage is not changed. Returns time_samples, count and present; an attribute the prim does not have is not an error but present false with an empty list, while a stage that is not open or a missing prim is an error. Use list_usd_prim_attributes first to see which attributes have samples (time_sample_count); set_usd_attribute_value writes a sample and clear_usd_attribute removes one.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube", as list_usd_prims returns it.

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Full attribute name including any namespace, as list_usd_prim_attributes returns it, e.g. "xformOp:translate".

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attr_name: string, time_samples: [number], count: int }

commands.name: get_usd_attribute_value
commands.description: Read the composed value of one attribute on a prim of a registered USD stage, at the time code in time, else at the default time (the static default, not a sample), possibly a schema fallback (has_value true, has_authored_value false). value is {type, value}: a scalar as a boolean, number or string; a pathExpression as its text; a vector, color or point as an array of numbers; a quaternion as [x, y, z, w], real part last; a matrix as an array of rows; an array attribute as a JSON array of those plus length and truncated, cut at 600 numbers or strings (fewer long strings). Another type, or no value, gives null with a note. A missing attribute is present=false; a missing stage or prim is an error. Read-only. Every attribute: list_usd_prim_attributes; sampled times: get_usd_attribute_time_samples; author a value: set_usd_attribute_value.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Attribute name to read, e.g. "size"

params.name: time
params.description: Optional USD time code to read at, e.g. 24; when omitted the default time is read (the static default value, not a sample)

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attr_name: string, present: bool, has_value?: bool, has_authored_value?: bool, type?: string, type_name?: string, time?: number, value?: { type: string, value: any, length?: number, truncated?: bool, note?: string } | null, note?: string }

commands.name: get_usd_generated_assets
commands.description: Resolve the transient assets (UStaticMesh, USkeletalMesh, UMaterial, etc.) generated by the stage actor for a given prim path.  Wraps AUsdStageActor::GetGeneratedAssets(prim_path). Returns an empty assets array (count:0) when the prim has no generated assets — NOT an error. A prim may produce multiple assets (e.g. a skinned mesh produces USkeletalMesh + USkeleton + UPhysicsAsset).

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full actor path (or short name) of the AUsdStageActor.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Full prim path, e.g. "/root_prim/my_mesh".

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, prim_path: string, assets: [string], count: int }

commands.name: get_usd_generated_component
commands.description: Find the scene component an AUsdStageActor generated in the level for one prim of its open USD stage (AUsdStageActor::GetGeneratedComponent), without changing anything: its component_path and component_class when present. Use it to reach the Unreal component behind a prim, for example to read its transform with the component tools; for the meshes, materials and other assets a prim produced use get_usd_generated_assets; for the actor's stage and load state get_usd_stage_actor_info. The components are transient: they exist only while the stage is loaded (set_usd_stage_actor_root_layer with OpenedAndLoaded) and are rebuilt when it reloads. present false is not an error: the prim path does not exist, has no component of its own (it was collapsed into a parent prim, so query the parent), or the stage is not loaded. An actor_path that matches no stage actor in the editor world, or a missing prim_path, is an error.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: The stage actor: its full path as create_usd_stage_actor returns it (actor_path), or its object name or editor label, e.g. "UsdStageActor".

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute USD prim path in the actor's stage, starting with "/", e.g. "/Root/Geom/Chair".

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, prim_path: string, present: bool, component_path?: string, component_class?: string }

commands.name: get_usd_prim_info
commands.description: Read one prim of a registered USD stage: name, type_name, active, parent_path, direct children_count, applied_schemas, variant_sets and an is_a map for nine common types (Xform, Mesh, Cube, Scope, Camera, four lights). A missing prim returns is_valid=false with a note, not an error. Read-only.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the prim to read, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { name: string, prim_path: string, type_name: string, active: bool, is_valid: bool, is_pseudo_root: bool, parent_path: string, children_count: number, applied_schemas: [string], variant_sets: [string], is_a: { Xform, Mesh, Cube, Scope, Camera, DistantLight, SphereLight, RectLight, MeshLight: bool } }, or { prim_path, is_valid: false, note } when the prim does not exist

commands.name: get_usd_prim_metadata
commands.description: Read the metadata of a prim on a registered USD stage as USD resolves it: one key (present plus value as {type, value}) or, with no key, all entries (authored and fallback) plus count; composition arcs such as references are read by key only, as their strongest opinion. Values read as get_usd_attribute_value reads them, an Sdf enum such as specifier as its number; a dictionary (customData, with the schema's fallback entries) as an object of {type, value} entries; a list op as {explicit} or {prepended, appended, deleted, ordered?, added?} arrays of item texts (numbers for an integer list op), apiSchemas, inactiveIds and other non-arc list ops composed into one explicit list; both with length and truncated. One reply holds about 30000 characters of values: past that, values are cut and further entries listed in omitted_keys. Above 100 entries only count and a note return. Read-only. Author with set_usd_prim_metadata; prim summary: get_usd_prim_info.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

params.name: key
params.description: Metadata field to read, e.g. "documentation"; empty or omitted (default) returns all entries.

commands.returns: { present: bool, key: string, value: { type: string, value: any, length?: number, truncated?: bool, note?: string }, metadata: object, count: number, truncated?: bool, omitted_keys?: [string], note?: string }

commands.name: get_usd_stage_actor_info
commands.description: Reads the live state of a USD stage actor (AUsdStageActor) in the editor world: the root layer identifier and file path of the stage it displays (the isolated stage while isolate_usd_layer is active), its load state (stage_state 0 = Closed, 1 = Opened, 2 = OpenedAndLoaded, with its name), whether it has generated a Level Sequence for animated prims, how many scene components it holds, and whether a layer is isolated. Read-only: changes, loads and saves nothing; with no stage open, root_layer and real_path are empty. An actor_path that matches no stage actor is an error. Use it after create_usd_stage_actor and set_usd_stage_actor_root_layer to check the stage loaded; for one prim's component or assets use get_usd_generated_component or get_usd_generated_assets. Stages opened by the stage tools, not by an actor, are read with get_usd_stage_info and list_usd_stages.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: The stage actor: its full path as create_usd_stage_actor returns it (actor_path), or its object name or editor label, e.g. "UsdStageActor".

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, root_layer: string, real_path: string, stage_state: int, stage_state_name: string, has_level_sequence: bool, generated_component_count: int, has_isolated_stage: bool } -- actor_path is the resolved full path; generated_component_count counts every scene component the actor owns, its own root included

commands.name: get_usd_stage_info
commands.description: Read metadata about a USD stage: root layer identifier, real path, dirty flag, timecode range (start/end), frames-per-second, total prim count (recursive) and layer-stack depth (includes session layers when include_session_layers is true).  Resolves stage_name via the LLM-facing UEAgent::UsdRegistry::GStageNameCache first, then falls back to treating stage_name as a file path and auto-opening it (LoadAll, use cache). Returns 'resolution' as one of "cache_hit" / "auto_opened" so the caller knows which path served the stage.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under, OR an absolute file path to auto-open.

params.name: include_session_layers
params.description: Include session layers when computing the layer-stack depth (default true).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, resolution: string, identifier: string, real_path: string, dirty: bool, start_time: number, end_time: number, frames_per_second: number, prim_count: int, layer_stack_count: int, has_start_time: bool, has_end_time: bool, has_fps: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: insert_usd_sublayer
commands.description: Add a sublayer path to the root layer of a registered USD stage, so that layer's opinions compose into the stage, then save the root layer to disk (Save without force: the whole root layer, including any other unsaved edits on it). Read the stack and its indices with list_usd_stage_layers, take a sublayer out by index with remove_usd_sublayer, and to author into the new layer point set_usd_edit_target at it. The path is not checked to exist; USD complaints come back in errors. No undo step. success means the root layer was saved, so read inserted and already_present: a path already in the list changes nothing (already_present=true, nothing saved) and answers success=false, and an in-memory stage (anonymous root layer, nothing to save to) answers success=false even with inserted=true. Idempotent in effect: a repeat adds nothing. An unregistered stage_name is an error.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Exact name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage (a stage only in the USD cache is not found here).

params.name: sublayer_path
params.description: Path or USD identifier of the layer to insert, e.g. "D:/USD/props.usda" or "./props.usda" (resolved relative to the root layer); compared with the existing entries as text, case ignored.

params.name: index
params.description: 0-based position in the root layer's sublayer list, where 0 is the strongest; -1 (default) appends as the weakest. The reply's index echoes this value, not the resulting position.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, sublayer_path: string, index: int, inserted: bool, already_present: bool, new_count: int, saved: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: isolate_usd_layer
commands.description: Enter isolated mode by replacing the actor's displayed stage with a new stage rooted at one of the sublayers of the current layer stack.  Wraps AUsdStageActor::IsolateLayer(Layer, b_load_usd_stage). The layer_index selects into Stage.GetLayerStack(true) — index 0 is the root layer, >0 are sublayers. When b_load_usd_stage is true (default) assets, actors and components are regenerated from the isolated stage; when false the isolation is structural only.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full actor path (or short name) of the AUsdStageActor.

params.name: layer_index
params.description: Index into the actor's stage layer stack (default 0 = root layer).

params.name: b_load_usd_stage
params.description: Load assets/components from the isolated stage (default true).

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, layer_index: int, isolated_layer: string, b_load_usd_stage: bool }

commands.name: list_usd_file_formats
commands.description: List the USD file format extensions the engine supports, with optional human-readable descriptions -- also the probe of whether the USDCore plugin loaded: native_present / supported_present false (a zero count) means it did not.  Always returns the native set ("usd"/"usda"/"usdc"/"usdz", UnrealUSDWrapper::GetNativeFileFormats) and the full supported set (native + third-party USD plugin extensions like "abc" from usdAbc, GetAllSupportedFileFormats). When include_descriptions is true, also calls AddUsdImportFileFormatDescriptions to populate the human-readable per-extension description strings (e.g. "usdc; Universal Scene Description binary files").

params.name: include_descriptions
params.description: Also return the per-extension import description strings from UnrealUSDWrapper::AddUsdImportFileFormatDescriptions (optional, default false).

commands.returns: { native_formats: [string], supported_formats: [string], native_count: int, supported_count: int, native_present: bool, supported_present: bool, descriptions: [{format: string, description: string}]? }

commands.name: list_usd_prim_attributes
commands.description: List every attribute of one prim on a USD stage this server has open, with each one's name, USD type, C++ type, whether it has a value (fallback values count) or an authored opinion, and how many time samples it has. Read-only: the stage is not changed. Use it to find an attribute name; then read one value with get_usd_attribute_value, its sample times with get_usd_attribute_time_samples, or write it with set_usd_attribute_value. For the prim's own type, specifier and schemas use get_usd_prim_info; to find prim paths use list_usd_prims. A stage that is not open (open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage first) or a prim that does not exist is an error.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube", as list_usd_prims returns it.

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attributes: [{name, type_name, cpp_type, has_value, has_authored_value, time_sample_count}], count: int }

commands.name: list_usd_prims
commands.description: List the prims under one prim (default the pseudo root "/") of a registered USD stage without changing anything, each with prim_path and type_name, plus count: its direct children, or with recursive=true its whole subtree in depth-first order (each parent before its children, siblings in stage order). Only active, loaded, defined, non-abstract prims appear (so active is always true here), and instance proxies are not traversed: a deactivated prim, an over-only prim or a Class prim needs get_usd_prim_info by path. Use it to discover prim paths before get_usd_prim_info (one prim's schemas and variant sets), list_usd_prim_attributes or the authoring tools; list_usd_stages shows which stages are open and get_usd_stage_info the total prim count. An unregistered stage_name, a malformed prim_path_prefix or a prim that does not exist is an error; a prim without children is a success with count 0.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

params.name: prim_path_prefix
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the prim whose children are listed, e.g. "/World"; it must exist (it is a parent path, not a text prefix). Default "/" (the pseudo root).

params.name: recursive
params.description: false (default) lists the direct children only; true lists every descendant, each parent before its children.

commands.returns: { prims: [{ prim_path, type_name, active }], count: number }

commands.name: list_usd_stage_layers
commands.description: List the layer stack of a USD stage opened with open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage, read-only: each layer's index, identifier, real_path, is_root, is_session, is_edit_target, is_muted, dirty and sublayer paths, plus root_layer_index, session_layer_count, edit_target_index, count and any captured USD errors; with layer_index only that layer. The indices are the ones set_usd_edit_target takes: the full stack, the stage's session layer and its sublayers first (every stage these tools open or create has an anonymous session layer), then the root layer and its sublayers, so the root is usually index 1. An unregistered stage_name, a layer_index outside the stack or an invalid layer at it is an error.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under via open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage.

params.name: include_session_layers
params.description: When true (default) the session layers are listed too; false leaves them out of layers without renumbering the rest, so the root keeps its index. layer_index ignores it.

params.name: layer_index
params.description: Optional 0-based index into the full stack, as set_usd_edit_target counts it (root_layer_index gives the root); report only that layer

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, include_session_layers: bool, root_layer_index: int, session_layer_count: int, edit_target_index: int (-1 when the edit target is outside the stack), count: int, layers: [{ index: int, identifier: string, real_path: string, is_root: bool, is_session: bool, is_edit_target: bool, is_muted: bool, dirty: bool, sub_layer_paths: [string], sub_layer_count: int }], layer_index?: int, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: list_usd_stages
commands.description: Enumerate every stage currently in the UnrealUSDWrapper stage cache (shared across C++ + Python).  Returns one entry per cached stage with the root layer identifier, real path and dirty flag. It reads the engine's stage cache directly, so it also lists the stages opened outside these tools (Python USD scripts, the editor's USD importer). Each entry's 'stage_name' is the name the stage was opened under through these tools; it is empty for a stage they did not open.
commands.returns: { stages: [{stage_name: string, identifier: string, real_path: string, dirty: bool}], count: int }

commands.name: list_usd_variant_sets
commands.description: List the variant sets a prim of a cached USD stage has, without changing anything: their names, each set's variant names (variants) and the selected variant of each set that has one (selections, empty when none is authored). With variant_set_name only that set is reported, also as variant_set_name, current_selection (empty when none) and variant_count, and a set the prim does not have is an error. Use it before set_usd_variant_selection or clear_usd_variant_selection, which take these names; author sets and variants with add_usd_variant_set and add_usd_variant, delete them with remove_usd_variant_set and remove_usd_variant. An unknown stage, an invalid prim path or a prim that does not exist is an error; open a stage first with open_usd_stage.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the existing prim to inspect, e.g. "/World/Car"

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage (list_usd_stages shows it), or the end of a cached stage's root layer identifier, case-insensitive, e.g. "Shot010"

params.name: variant_set_name
params.description: Optional name of the one variant set to report, e.g. "color"; omitted or empty reports every set

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, names: [string], selections: object, variants: object (set name -> [variant name]), count: int, variant_set_name?: string, current_selection?: string, variant_count?: int }

commands.name: mute_usd_layer
commands.description: Mute and unmute layers of a registered USD stage in one atomic call (UsdStage::MuteAndUnmuteLayers): a muted layer's opinions drop out of composition until it is unmuted. Muting is stage state held in memory: no layer file changes and save_usd_stage does not record it. Read layer identifiers, and confirm is_muted afterwards, with list_usd_stage_layers; to send edits to a layer use set_usd_edit_target instead, and to show one layer alone on a stage actor isolate_usd_layer. muted and unmuted echo the identifiers sent, not a read-back. Muting a layer already muted changes nothing, so a repeat call is harmless. An unregistered stage_name is an error (success=false); USD complaints come back in errors. No undo step.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage (list_usd_stages shows it), e.g. "Shot010".

params.name: mute_paths
params.description: Layer identifiers to mute, as list_usd_stage_layers reports them, e.g. ["C:/Shots/lighting.usda"]; non-string or empty entries are skipped. Empty/missing is allowed (no-op on the mute side).

params.name: unmute_paths
params.description: Layer identifiers to unmute, same form as mute_paths. Empty/missing is allowed (no-op on the unmute side).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, muted: [string], unmuted: [string], errors: [string]? }

commands.name: open_usd_stage
commands.description: Open an existing USD stage from a file path.  Wraps UnrealUSDWrapper::OpenStage with caching and force-reload controls. When use_stage_cache is true (default) and the file is already open in the UnrealUSDWrapper stage cache, the existing stage is returned. When force_reload is true, all local layers are forced-reloaded from disk (useful when the file was modified by another tool since the last open). The opened stage is added to the LLM-facing UEAgent::UsdRegistry::GStageNameCache under either the explicit stage_name or a derived one (basename without extension). The stage_id returned is the root layer's USD identifier — a stable string handle useful as a unique reference across follow-up commands.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Absolute path to the .usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz file (or a USD layer identifier).

params.name: stage_name
params.description: LLM-facing name to register the opened stage under. Defaults to the file basename without extension (optional).

params.name: initial_load_set
params.description: "LoadAll" (default; loads payloads) or "LoadNone" (faster; inspect without loading payloads).

params.name: use_stage_cache
params.description: Use UnrealUSDWrapper's stage cache (default true). When false the stage is re-read and not added to the cache.

params.name: force_reload
params.description: Force-reload all local layers from disk, bypassing the layer registry (default false).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, stage_id: string, identifier: string, real_path: string, from_cache: bool, file_path: string, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: override_usd_prim
commands.description: Author an over (specifier over, no type) at prim_path on a registered USD stage, at its current edit target, with overs for missing ancestors, to add opinions to a prim without defining it. A prim that already exists there is returned untouched (already_existed true, no specifier reported, since nothing was authored); specifier Over comes back only for an over this call authored. is_valid=false means USD refused; a missing stage or a bad path is an error. In memory only: save_usd_stage writes it. define_usd_prim creates a typed def; set_usd_prim_specifier changes the specifier of an existing prim.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath to author the over at, e.g. "/World/Cube"

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, is_valid: bool, already_existed: bool, specifier?: string }

commands.name: remove_usd_attribute
commands.description: Remove one attribute from a prim on a registered USD stage by deleting its scene description in the current edit target layer only, so opinions from other layers or references can keep it composed. Idempotent: an absent attribute gives present=false and removed=false, not an error, and a relationship of that name counts as absent. A stage not registered under stage_name or a missing prim is an error. In memory only: save_usd_stage writes it. To keep the attribute and drop its values use clear_usd_attribute.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Name of the attribute to remove, e.g. "size"

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attr_name: string, removed: bool, present: bool }

commands.name: remove_usd_prim
commands.description: Remove a prim and its subtree from the current edit target layer of a registered USD stage, returning removed. Opinions in other layers or references can keep it composed; set_usd_prim_metadata with key "active" and value false is the reversible way to hide a prim. Not saved to disk.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the prim to remove, e.g. "/World/Cube"; its descendants go with it.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { removed: bool, prim_path: string }

commands.name: remove_usd_prim_schema
commands.description: Remove an applied API schema (e.g. "MaterialBindingAPI") from an existing prim of a registered USD stage, on the current edit target. A schema the prim does not have returns removed=false and was_applied=false instead of an error. Not saved to disk; inverse of apply_usd_prim_schema.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: schema_name
params.description: Schema identifier as listed in applied_schemas by get_usd_prim_info, e.g. "MaterialBindingAPI".

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { removed: bool, schema_name: string }

commands.name: remove_usd_sublayer
commands.description: Remove a sublayer by index from the stage's root layer's composition stack.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under.

params.name: sublayer_index
params.description: 0-based index into GetSubLayerPaths() of the root layer.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, sublayer_index: int, removed: bool, new_count: int, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: remove_usd_variant
commands.description: Delete one variant from a variant set of a prim of a cached USD stage: on every spec of the prim in the stage's local layer stack the variant spec goes (with the opinions authored inside it), and a selection of that variant is cleared. Inverse of add_usd_variant. Opinions on a layer outside the local stack (a reference or payload) are left as they are and counted in specs_skipped. A set the prim does not have is an error; a variant the set does not have is an honest no-op (removed=false). Irreversible, like every USD composition edit here (no undo); save with save_usd_stage. Read: list_usd_variant_sets; the whole set: remove_usd_variant_set.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: SdfPath of the prim that authors the variant set

params.name: variant_set_name
params.description: Variant set that holds the variant

params.name: variant_name
params.description: Name of the variant to delete

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Stage cache key

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, variant_set_name: string, variant_name: string, removed: bool, specs_edited: int, specs_skipped: int, still_present: bool, variant_names: [string] }

commands.name: remove_usd_variant_set
commands.description: Delete a variant set from a prim of a cached USD stage, as the variant set editor does: on every spec of the prim in the stage's local layer stack (root, sublayers, session layer) the variant set with all its variants goes, with its name in the variant set list and its selection. Inverse of add_usd_variant_set; clear_usd_variant_selection only clears the selection. Opinions authored on a layer outside the local stack (one brought in by a reference or payload) are left as they are and counted in specs_skipped, so the set can still show (still_present). A prim that does not author the set is an honest no-op (removed=false); a missing stage or prim is an error. Irreversible, like every USD composition edit here (no undo); save with save_usd_stage. Read: list_usd_variant_sets.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: SdfPath of the prim that authors the variant set

params.name: variant_set_name
params.description: Name of the variant set to delete

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Stage cache key

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, variant_set_name: string, removed: bool, specs_edited: int, specs_skipped: int, still_present: bool }

commands.name: save_usd_stage
commands.description: Save a USD stage's file layers to disk: the root layer and every sublayer of its stack (UE::FSdfLayer::Save on each), each one only when it is dirty unless force is set. layers reports every layer with was_dirty, saved, dirty after and, for one left alone, skipped ("clean", or "anonymous" for an in-memory layer, which has no file); layers_saved counts the writes. Session layers are never saved (they are in-memory by design); a memory-only stage is exported with flatten_usd_stage instead. When nothing needs saving (every layer clean) nothing is written and the call succeeds with layers_saved 0, saved false and a note. saved is true when at least one layer was written and every dirty layer was; a dirty layer left unsaved -- its Save returned false, or it is anonymous, with no file to write -- fails the call with saved false and a save_error naming it. Use force=true to re-write clean file layers (rare — typically only when a downstream tool requires a specific mtime). list_usd_stage_layers shows which layers are dirty first.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under, OR an absolute file path to auto-open.

params.name: force
params.description: Re-save every file layer of the stack even when it is clean (default false: only dirty layers are written).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, resolution: string, saved: bool, layers_saved: int, layers: [{ identifier: string, real_path: string, is_root: bool, was_dirty: bool, saved: bool, dirty: bool, skipped?: string }], dirty: bool (the root layer after the save), force: bool, real_path: string (the root layer's), note?: string (nothing needed saving), save_error?: string (the dirty layers left unsaved), errors: [string]? }

commands.name: set_usd_attribute_value
commands.description: Author one attribute value on a prim of a registered USD stage, at the current edit target: a time sample at time, else the default; a missing attribute is created with type_name. The JSON value converts to the declared type: bool takes a boolean; integer types a whole number in range; half, float, double and timecode a number; string, token and asset a string; pathExpression the text of the expression; vectors, colors, points and texCoords an array of numbers; a quaternion [x, y, z, w]; a matrix an array of rows; an array type a JSON array of those. Another shape or range, a text that does not parse as a path expression (the error gives USD's parse message), opaque or group (valueless by design) or a new attribute without type_name fails, writing nothing. If USD refuses it, success is false and a created attribute is removed. In memory: save_usd_stage writes it; get_usd_attribute_value reads it back.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage (default the file basename) or create_usd_stage (default "Untitled").

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim on that stage, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: attr_name
params.description: Attribute name to set, e.g. "size"

params.name: type_name
params.description: USD type name of the attribute to create when it does not exist yet, e.g. "float" or "token"; required in that case, and ignored (with a note when it differs) for an existing attribute, whose declared type decides.

params.name: value
params.description: The value: a JSON scalar, e.g. 2.5, "inherited" or true, a JSON array, e.g. [1, 0.5, 0] for a color3f or [[0, 0, 1]] for a float3[], or an object {"value": <value>} whose "type" key, if any, is not used; it is converted to the declared type of the attribute. On UE 5.7 a pathExpression value cannot be written (needs UE 5.8); reading one works.

params.name: time
params.description: Optional USD time code to author a time sample at, e.g. 24; when omitted the default value is authored

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, attr_name: string, set: bool, type_name: string, type: string, created: bool, time?: number, note?: string }

commands.name: set_usd_edit_target
commands.description: Choose the layer of a registered USD stage that later authoring writes to (its edit target): define_usd_prim, set_usd_attribute_value, add_usd_reference and the other USD edit tools then land on that layer. Without layer_index it targets the stage's root layer. Indices are the ones list_usd_stage_layers reports (its root_layer_index, is_root and is_session say which is which): the session layer and its sublayers come first, so the root is usually 1, and a session layer is in-memory only. edit_target is read back from the stage and the call fails if it is not the chosen layer. The choice is stage state held in memory, written to no file; save_usd_stage writes the root layer and its dirty sublayers but never a session layer, so edits aimed at a session layer are lost with the stage. Idempotent; no undo step. An unregistered stage_name, a layer_index that is not an integer or is outside the stack is an error (success=false) and the target stays as it was.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage (list_usd_stages shows it), e.g. "Shot010".

params.name: layer_index
params.description: Optional 0-based index into the stage's full layer stack, as list_usd_stage_layers lists it: the session layer and its sublayers first, then the root layer and its sublayers. Omitted: the root layer (root_layer_index), usually 1.

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, layer_index: int, layer_index_defaulted: bool, edit_target: string, edit_target_real_path: string, is_root: bool, is_session: bool, errors: [string]? } -- edit_target is read back from the stage
