commands.name: set_usd_prim_metadata
commands.description: Author one metadata field (e.g. "comment", "kind", "customData", "apiSchemas", or the well-known "active" (bool; false deactivates the prim and its subtree, the reversible alternative to remove_usd_prim), "instanceable" (bool, USD native instancing), "displayName" (string UI label; the prim name does not change) and "typeName" (token, written as given, not checked against the schema registry)) on an existing prim of a registered USD stage, at the current edit target. The value is converted to the field's type, read from its resolved value or, for a standard field resolving to nothing (kind, comment, hidden, customData, apiSchemas, references...), the type Sdf registers: scalars, vectors, matrices and arrays as set_usd_attribute_value converts them; a dictionary from an object of entries; a list op from {explicit} or {prepended, appended, deleted, ordered, added} arrays of item texts, or of whole numbers for an integer list op such as inactiveIds. Any other field takes the type value names, else its JSON type. A value that does not fit writes nothing; if USD refuses the write, success is false with set=false and its errors. In memory: save_usd_stage writes it; get_usd_prim_metadata reads it back as USD resolves it.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim, e.g. "/World/Cube".

params.name: key
params.description: Registered USD prim metadata field, e.g. "comment", "kind", "customData" or "apiSchemas"; a key USD does not register as prim metadata fails with success false and set=false.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

params.name: value
params.description: The value itself (a scalar, an array, or an object of dictionary entries) or {type?, value}. It is converted to the field's type when that is known, and type is then not used; else type, or the JSON type, decides (bool, number as double, string, object as dictionary). A list op is {"explicit": [...]} or {"prepended": [...], "appended", "deleted", "ordered", "added"}, a reference item "@a.usda@</Prim>", an integer list op item a whole number. On UE 5.7 an integer list op (int, uint, int64 or uint64) cannot be written (needs UE 5.8); reading one works.

commands.returns: { set: bool, prim_path: string, key: string, value: object, declared_type?: string, errors?: [string] }

commands.name: set_usd_prim_specifier
commands.description: Change the specifier of an existing prim on a registered USD stage to Def (a concrete prim), Over (opinions that define nothing on their own) or Class (an abstract template that does not render), authored on the stage's current edit target layer (pick it with set_usd_edit_target). Use it to convert a prim in place; to create one use define_usd_prim, and to add an over where nothing is defined yet override_usd_prim. The edit stays in memory until save_usd_stage, with no undo step. An unknown specifier, an unregistered stage_name or a prim that does not exist is an error and nothing is authored; a write USD refuses fails the call with set=false. specifier is reported only after a successful write (there is no getter to read it back); inspect the prim with get_usd_prim_info. Setting the same specifier again writes it again (idempotent). A prim made Class, or Over with no def on any layer, no longer appears in list_usd_prims, which lists defined, non-abstract prims only.

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of an existing prim, e.g. "/World/Cube", as list_usd_prims returns it.

params.name: specifier
params.description: "Def", "Over" or "Class", case-insensitive; anything else is refused.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by create_usd_stage or open_usd_stage; a stage already in the USD cache also matches by the end of its root layer identifier.

commands.returns: { set: bool, specifier?: string, requested?: object }

commands.name: set_usd_stage_actor_root_layer
commands.description: Assign a USD file as the actor's root layer and transition the stage state.  Wraps AUsdStageActor::SetRootLayer(path) followed by AUsdStageActor::SetStageState(state). SetStageState(OpenedAndLoaded) triggers level-sequence regeneration — this can take a noticeable amount of time on large stages, so the cov harness may observe a transient 'rebuilding' state via follow-up get_usd_stage_actor_info calls. The tool does NOT verify the file exists on disk — SetRootLayer stores the path; the actual load happens during SetStageState(OpenedAndLoaded). When root_layer_path is empty, the existing root layer is preserved.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full actor path (or short name) of the AUsdStageActor.

params.name: root_layer_path
params.description: Absolute file path of the USD file (.usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz).

params.name: stage_state
params.description: "OpenedAndLoaded" (default), "Opened", or "Closed".

commands.returns: { actor_path: string, root_layer_path: string, stage_state: string }

commands.name: set_usd_stage_time_range
commands.description: Set a USD stage's start/end time codes and optionally its frames-per-second, then save the root layer (idempotent — no-op when !dirty).  Both start_time and end_time are required and are written via UE::FUsdStage::SetStartTimeCode / SetEndTimeCode (which write to the stage's root layer metadata). When frames_per_second > 0, also calls SetFramesPerSecond. The Save() at the end is force=false so a layer that wasn't actually mutated by the Set* calls will not produce an unnecessary write.

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under, OR an absolute file path to auto-open.

params.name: start_time
params.description: New start time code (e.g. 0.0).

params.name: end_time
params.description: New end time code (e.g. 24.0).

params.name: frames_per_second
params.description: Optional frames-per-second override; values <= 0 are ignored (use get_usd_stage_info / set_usd_stage_time_range to leave fps untouched).

commands.returns: { stage_name: string, resolution: string, start_time: number, end_time: number, frames_per_second: number, applied: bool, saved: bool, dirty: bool, errors: [string]? }

commands.name: set_usd_variant_selection
commands.description: Select the active variant of one variant set on a prim of a cached USD stage, so the prim composes that variant's opinions; set is the engine's answer. Read the sets, their variants and current selections with list_usd_variant_sets first; create them with add_usd_variant_set and add_usd_variant; clear_usd_variant_selection removes the selection instead. The selection is authored on the stage's current edit target layer (set_usd_edit_target) and stays in memory until save_usd_stage; no undo step. Idempotent: selecting the selected variant again changes nothing. The variant name is not checked against the set's variants, so name one list_usd_variant_sets reports. An unknown stage, a prim that does not exist, or a variant set the prim does not author is an error, checked before anything is written (the guard also keeps the engine's variant-set handle from going invalid).

params.name: prim_path
params.description: Absolute SdfPath of the existing prim that authors the variant set, e.g. "/World/Car"

params.name: variant_set_name
params.description: Variant set to select a variant from, as list_usd_variant_sets reports it, e.g. "color"

params.name: variant_name
params.description: Variant to activate, e.g. "red" (must already be present — use add_usd_variant first)

params.name: stage_name
params.description: Name the stage was registered under by open_usd_stage or create_usd_stage (list_usd_stages shows it), or the end of a cached stage's root layer identifier, case-insensitive, e.g. "Shot010"

commands.returns: { prim_path: string, variant_set_name: string, variant_name: string, set: bool }

commands.name: clear_uv_channel
commands.description: Drop every UV from one UV channel of LOD 0 of a UStaticMesh asset: LOD 0 (its source model, or its render data when it has none) is copied to a transient dynamic mesh, the channel's UVs are cleared there, and the copy is written back over LOD 0 in one undo step and the package saved. The channel itself stays, so the channel count does not change, and an already-empty channel is still written and saved. A uv_channel LOD 0 lacks, a mesh with no source model, a path that does not load or a mesh under /Engine is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false. Inventory first: list_uv_channels; one triangle: set_triangle_uvs; channel count of a DynamicMeshActor: set_num_uv_channels.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Asset path to the UStaticMesh

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: Index of the UV channel to clear (0-based; default 0); one LOD 0 does not have is an error

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, uv_channel, uv_channel_count_before, uv_channel_count_after, cleared, saved }

commands.name: get_uv_health_report
commands.description: Check the layout of one UV channel of one LOD of a static mesh asset, reading its built render data: in_unit_square_triangle_ratio (share of triangles with all three UVs inside 0..1), overlapping_triangle_count (triangles whose UV triangle overlaps another one's with positive area; a shared edge or corner does not count, so a clean unwrap gives 0 and a lightmap channel should), overlap_test_complete, approx_unique_islands, plus vertex and triangle counts, lightmap_coordinate_index and is_lightmap_hard_failing (no lightmap index set, or no UV channels). Pick the LOD and channel with list_uv_channels first; change the lightmap channel with set_static_mesh_lightmap, and edit the asset's UVs with set_triangle_uvs or clear_uv_channel. Read-only and idempotent; nothing dirtied or saved. A mesh that does not load, or a LOD or channel out of range, is an error.

params.name: mesh_path
params.description: Content path of the UStaticMesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock" (the object path "/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.SM_Rock" also works); find_assets_by_name finds it

params.name: lod_index
params.description: 0-based LOD to inspect (default 0), below the total_lods list_uv_channels reports

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: 0-based UV channel to inspect (default 0), below that LOD's uv_channel_count from list_uv_channels

commands.returns: { mesh_path, lod_index, uv_channel, vertex_count, triangle_count, lightmap_coordinate_index, no_lightmap_configured: bool, is_lightmap_hard_failing: bool, overlapping_triangle_count: int, overlap_test_complete: bool, in_unit_square_triangle_ratio, approx_unique_islands, per_triangle_iteration_error?: string } -- overlapping_triangle_count: triangles overlapping another in UV space with positive area (a lower bound when overlap_test_complete is false: the test stops after 20 million pair visits); approx_unique_islands counts distinct UV positions (rounded to 4 decimals), not islands; when per_triangle_iteration_error is set the per-triangle counters stay 0.

commands.name: list_uv_channels
commands.description: List the UV channels of a static mesh asset per LOD: for each LOD uv_channel_count, vertex_count, triangle_count, the mesh's lightmap_coordinate_index and has_lightmap (that index names an existing channel), and one entry per channel with is_lightmap. Use it first to see which LODs and channels exist; then get_uv_health_report checks one channel's layout, get_static_mesh_geometry_stats measures UV area, and set_static_mesh_lightmap changes the lightmap channel. Read-only and idempotent: no undo step, nothing dirtied or saved. Channel and vertex counts come from the built render data, triangle_count from the LOD's source mesh description (0 when it has none); each channel's vertex_count is the LOD's vertex count. A mesh that does not load, or a lod_index past the last LOD, is an error.

params.name: mesh_path
params.description: Content path of the UStaticMesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock" (the object path "/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.SM_Rock" also works); find_assets_by_name finds it

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Optional 0-based LOD to inspect, or -1 to list every LOD (default -1); total_lods in the reply says how many exist, and one past the last is an error

commands.returns: { mesh_path: string, total_lods: int, lods: [{lod_index, uv_channel_count, vertex_count, triangle_count, lightmap_coordinate_index, has_lightmap, channels: [{channel, is_lightmap, vertex_count}]}] }

commands.name: set_triangle_uvs
commands.description: Set the three UV corners of one triangle in one UV channel of LOD 0 of a UStaticMesh asset, a granular edit without a repack: LOD 0 (its source model, or its render data when it has none) is copied to a transient dynamic mesh, the triangle gets three new UV elements there, so it becomes its own UV island, and the copy is written back over LOD 0 in one undo step and the package saved. triangle_id counts the copy's triangles from 0. A negative uv_channel, a triangle or channel the copy lacks, a missing corner, a path that does not load or a mesh under /Engine is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false. Whole channel: clear_uv_channel; check the result: get_uv_health_report.

params.name: static_mesh_path
params.description: Asset path to the UStaticMesh

params.name: uv_channel
params.description: UV channel index (default 0); a negative one, or one LOD 0 does not have, is an error

params.name: triangle_id
params.description: Triangle ID to update (0-based; default 0)

params.name: uv0
params.description: First triangle corner as a [u, v] pair of numbers (required).

params.name: uv1
params.description: Second corner as [u, v] (required).

params.name: uv2
params.description: Third corner as [u, v] (required).

commands.returns: { static_mesh_path, uv_channel, triangle_id, is_valid_triangle, modified, saved }

commands.name: add_water_body_to_zone
commands.description: Link a water body to a water zone for good by pointing the body's WaterZoneOverride at it (UWaterBodyComponent::SetWaterZoneOverride), replacing any override it had: a saved property the engine prefers over spatial overlap, so the body stays in that zone wherever it lies, and the zone rebuilds its water info and mesh around it; both are found by editor label in the editor world. linked is read back: the override and the body's owning zone both name the zone, which is what get_water_body_info (water_zone_label) and get_water_zone_info (linked_body_count) then report; owning_zone_label and previous_zone_label say where it is and was. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level). Idempotent: a body already linked this way changes nothing (changed=false). Inverse: remove_water_body_from_zone. An unknown body or zone label, or a body without a UWaterBodyComponent, is an error.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Editor label (not the object name) of the AWaterBody actor -- lake, river, ocean or custom -- e.g. "Lake_Main", as create_water_body set it; whole label, case-insensitive, first match

params.name: water_zone_label
params.description: Editor label of the AWaterZone actor, e.g. "WaterZone_1"; spawn_actor with type="WaterZone" places one

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, water_zone_label: string, linked: bool, changed: bool, water_zone_override: string (the override's object path, read back), owning_zone_label: string, previous_zone_label: string }

commands.name: create_lake_water_body
commands.description: Spawn a Lake AWaterBody actor, optionally link to a WaterZone, and READ BACK the wave height the factory attached (a lake is born with the OCEAN's waves and nothing else reveals it).

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label to assign to the new water body actor

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin)

params.name: water_zone_label
params.description: Optional label of an existing AWaterZone to auto-link the body to. If given and the zone is not found, `success` is FALSE (the body is still spawned; `linked_to_zone` says so).

params.name: affects_landscape
params.description: When true the body carves the existing landscape via the water landscape brush; defaults to FALSE (non-destructive)

params.name: disable_waves
params.description: OPT-IN, default FALSE. Sets water_waves = None right after the spawn and RE-READS GetMaxWaveHeight() to prove it went to 0. Use it on any basin shallower than ~5 m: the engine's Lake factory attaches the ocean's wave asset (measured 508.125 uu = 5.08 m of crest), which on a pond a few meters deep breaks the water surface -- crest above the lip of the basin, trough below the bed -- with every property of the actor reading green.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, body_type: string, water_zone_label: string, linked_to_zone: bool, affects_landscape: bool, max_wave_height: number (RE-READ from UWaterBodyComponent::GetMaxWaveHeight() AFTER any disable_waves), max_wave_height_on_spawn: number (RE-READ as the factory left it), has_waves: bool, waves_disabled: bool, warning?: string (emitted when a lake was born with waves), requested: { actor_label, location, water_zone_label, affects_landscape, disable_waves } }

commands.name: create_ocean_water_body
commands.description: Spawn an Ocean AWaterBody actor, optionally link to a WaterZone, and read back its wave height (on an ocean the factory's waves are CORRECT -- ~508 uu -- so no warning is emitted here).

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label to assign to the new water body actor

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin)

params.name: water_zone_label
params.description: Optional label of an existing AWaterZone to auto-link the body to. If given and the zone is not found, `success` is FALSE (the body is still spawned; `linked_to_zone` says so).

params.name: affects_landscape
params.description: When true the body carves the existing landscape via the water landscape brush; defaults to FALSE (non-destructive)

params.name: disable_waves
params.description: OPT-IN, default FALSE. Sets water_waves = None right after the spawn and RE-READS GetMaxWaveHeight(). On an ocean you almost certainly do NOT want this.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, body_type: string, water_zone_label: string, linked_to_zone: bool, affects_landscape: bool, max_wave_height: number (RE-READ), max_wave_height_on_spawn: number (RE-READ), has_waves: bool, waves_disabled: bool, requested: { actor_label, location, water_zone_label, affects_landscape, disable_waves } }

commands.name: create_river_water_body
commands.description: Spawn a River AWaterBody actor, optionally link to a WaterZone, and read back its wave height (a river is born at 0.000 -- that is the control case for the lake defect).

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label to assign to the new water body actor

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin)

params.name: water_zone_label
params.description: Optional label of an existing AWaterZone to auto-link the body to. If given and the zone is not found, `success` is FALSE (the body is still spawned; `linked_to_zone` says so).

params.name: affects_landscape
params.description: When true the body carves the existing landscape via the water landscape brush; defaults to FALSE (non-destructive)

params.name: disable_waves
params.description: OPT-IN, default FALSE. Sets water_waves = None right after the spawn and RE-READS GetMaxWaveHeight(). A river has no waves to begin with, so this is normally a no-op here.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, body_type: string, water_zone_label: string, linked_to_zone: bool, affects_landscape: bool, max_wave_height: number (RE-READ), max_wave_height_on_spawn: number (RE-READ), has_waves: bool, waves_disabled: bool, requested: { actor_label, location, water_zone_label, affects_landscape, disable_waves } }

commands.name: create_water_body
commands.description: Spawn a water body actor -- a lake, an ocean or a river, by body_type -- through the Water plugin's own actor factory, optionally link it to a WaterZone, and READ BACK the wave height the factory attached (a lake is born with the ocean's waves and nothing else reveals it; disable_waves removes them and proves it). affects_landscape carves the landscape with the water brush (off by default). The actor exists in memory: save_level puts it on disk. Shape a river or lake with the spline tools; set_water_body_properties sets per-point velocity and audio, set_properties the rest.

params.name: body_type
params.description: One of lake, ocean, river

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label to assign to the new water body actor

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin)

params.name: water_zone_label
params.description: Optional editor label of an existing AWaterZone to link the body to, through its WaterZoneOverride as add_water_body_to_zone does (saved with the level, kept wherever the body lies); linked_to_zone and owning_zone_label are read back from the body. If the zone is not found, success is false while the body is still spawned

params.name: affects_landscape
params.description: When true the body carves the existing landscape via the water landscape brush; defaults to false (non-destructive)

params.name: disable_waves
params.description: Opt-in, default false: sets the water waves to none right after the spawn and re-reads the max wave height to prove it is 0

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, body_type: string, water_zone_label: string, linked_to_zone: bool, water_zone_override: string, owning_zone_label: string, affects_landscape: bool, max_wave_height: number, max_wave_height_on_spawn: number, has_waves: bool, waves_disabled: bool, warning?: string, requested: object }

commands.name: create_water_body_exclusion_volume
commands.description: Spawn an AWaterBodyExclusionVolume (a brush volume that excludes water bodies), build its cube brush, set the exclusion mode, and optionally bind specific water bodies by label.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label to assign to the new exclusion volume actor

params.name: location
params.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location (defaults to origin)

params.name: size
params.description: Optional cube brush size in uu (defaults to 200)

params.name: exclusion_mode
params.description: Optional "remove" (default) or "add": whether water_body_labels are removed from or added to the exclusion

params.name: water_body_labels
params.description: Optional array of AWaterBody labels to bind into the volume's WaterBodies list

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, exclusion_mode: string, water_body_count: int, brush_built: bool }

commands.name: create_water_zone
commands.description: Spawn a new AWaterZone actor in the editor world at location, unrotated, and label it. Not idempotent: every call adds another zone, even with a label already in use. Nothing is saved. Returns actor_label, actor_name and has_water_mesh; link bodies via water_zone_label of create_lake_water_body and its siblings.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label to assign to the new AWaterZone actor

params.name: location
params.description: World location [X, Y, Z] in cm; anything but a 3-number array means the origin.

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, has_water_mesh: bool }

commands.name: get_water_body_gerstner_wave_detail
commands.description: Read the individual Gerstner waves a water body holds (found by actor label in the editor world), as last generated and cached on its waves object: per wave the wavelength and amplitude in cm, the steepness, and the horizontal direction vector. A body without Gerstner waves -- a river, a body with another waves class, or one whose generator produced none -- is a success with wave_count 0 and an empty list. Read-only; an unknown label is an error. For the summary (waves class, count, max height) use get_water_body_info; author waves with set_water_body_gerstner_waves.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Actor label of the AWaterBody in the editor world (case-insensitive; the object name does not match).

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, wave_count: int, waves: [{ wavelength: number, amplitude: number, steepness: number, direction: [number, number, number] }] }

commands.name: get_water_body_info
commands.description: Read back a water body's type, linked zone, surface material and wave state: whether waves are supported and present, the max wave height, the active waves class with its wave count and, for Gerstner waves, the generator class. Read-only; an unknown label is an error. Per-wave detail is get_water_body_gerstner_wave_detail.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBody actor

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, body_type: string, water_zone_label: string, material: string, max_wave_height: number, wave_supported: bool, has_waves: bool, waves_class: string, num_waves: int, generator_class: string }

commands.name: get_water_body_spline_points
commands.description: Read the spline control points of any water body -- river, lake, ocean or custom, found by actor label in the editor world -- as world-space [x, y, z] positions in cm, in spline order. Only point locations come back: no tangents, widths, depths or closed-loop flag. Read-only. An unknown label, or a body without a water spline, is an error. Write them with set_water_body_spline_points; per-point river width and depth: set_river_width_depth_at_point; a generic actor's USplineComponent in local space, with its closed-loop flag: get_spline_points; body type, zone and material: get_water_body_info.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Actor label of the AWaterBody in the editor world (case-insensitive; the object name does not match).

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, point_count: int, points: [[number, number, number]] }

commands.name: get_water_zone_info
commands.description: Read a water zone of the editor world, found by editor label: actor_label, actor_name, has_water_mesh, zone_extent [X, Y] in cm (the complete extent times the actor scale, not a half-extent), overlap_priority, and linked_body_count, the number of water bodies whose own owning zone is this one (by spatial overlap, or by the WaterZoneOverride add_water_body_to_zone sets). Use it before and after set_water_zone_settings, which also reports render-target resolution, world bounds and texel size; for one body's zone, type and waves use get_water_body_info. Read-only and idempotent. A label no AWaterZone has is an error.

params.name: water_zone_label
params.description: Editor label (not the object name) of the AWaterZone actor, e.g. "WaterZone_1"; whole label, case-insensitive, first match. find_actors_by_name with match='label' lists labels

commands.returns: { actor_label: string, actor_name: string, has_water_mesh: bool, linked_body_count: number, zone_extent: [number, number], overlap_priority: int }

commands.name: remove_water_body_from_zone
commands.description: Unlink a water body from a water zone (inverse of add_water_body_to_zone): a WaterZoneOverride naming that zone is cleared, in one undo step that marks the level dirty, so the body falls back to the zone its bounds overlap, if any; owning_zone_label reads that back. A body inside the zone's bounds belongs to it by overlap whatever its override says, so that case is refused before anything changes. Idempotent: a body not linked to the zone is a success with already_unlinked=true and nothing changed. Read the result with get_water_body_info (water_zone_label). An unknown body or zone label is an error.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Editor label of the AWaterBody actor to unlink, e.g. "Lake_Main"

params.name: water_zone_label
params.description: Editor label of the AWaterZone actor to unlink from, e.g. "WaterZone_1"

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, water_zone_label: string, removed: bool, override_cleared: bool, already_unlinked: bool, owning_zone_label: string }

commands.name: set_river_width_depth_at_point
commands.description: Set the width and/or depth of a river water body, found by actor label in the editor world, at the spline point at or before input_key (point i sits at key i; past the last point, the last one), then synchronize the spline so the river rebuilds; nothing is saved. A value below 0.0001 is stored as 0.0001, as the engine's sync does. width and depth are read back from that point, named by point_index. A value already held is not written: applied is false with a note and nothing changes; otherwise the call is one undo step that dirties the actor's package. Neither width nor depth, a non-river body, an unknown label, a spline without points or a key before the first point is an error and nothing changes. All points at once: set_river_widths_depths; point positions: get_water_body_spline_points.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBodyRiver actor

params.name: input_key
params.description: Spline input key at which to set width/depth; a key before the first spline point (below 0) is an error and nothing is changed

params.name: width
params.description: Optional new river width at the point at or before the key (give width, depth or both)

params.name: depth
params.description: Optional new river depth at the point at or before the key (give width, depth or both)

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, input_key: number, point_index: int, width: number, depth: number, applied: bool, note: string? }

commands.name: set_river_widths_depths
commands.description: Set the width and/or depth of every spline point of a river water body, found by actor label: the arrays are indexed by point (point i at key i), each given one with point_count entries. A value below 0.0001 is stored as 0.0001, as the spline sync does. The points are written in one undo step dirtying the actor's package, then the spline is synchronized once to rebuild the river; nothing is saved. widths and depths are read back from the points; applied_widths or applied_depths is true when that array changed a point and every point holds it, and success is false when one does not. Arrays already held change nothing: both false, a note, no undo step. Neither array, a wrong length, a non-river body or an unknown label is an error. One point: set_river_width_depth_at_point.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBodyRiver actor

params.name: widths
params.description: Optional array of per-point river widths (length must equal point_count)

params.name: depths
params.description: Optional array of per-point river depths (length must equal point_count)

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, point_count: int, applied_widths: bool, applied_depths: bool, widths: [number], depths: [number], note: string? }

commands.name: set_water_body_gerstner_waves
commands.description: Build a Gerstner wave set (UGerstnerWaterWaves + simple parametric generator) and apply it to a wave-supporting water body (Lake/Ocean; rivers are rejected). The generator ramps per-wave Steepness from large_wave_steepness to small_wave_steepness; the no-self-intersection (no fold, no black-crest) criterion is total_steepness (returned) <= 1 — lower the two steepness params and/or num_waves if it exceeds 1.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBody actor (must support waves: Lake or Ocean)

params.name: num_waves
params.description: Optional wave count for the generator (>= 1; default 16)

params.name: min_wavelength
params.description: Optional minimum wavelength in uu

params.name: max_wavelength
params.description: Optional maximum wavelength in uu

params.name: min_amplitude
params.description: Optional minimum wave amplitude in uu

params.name: max_amplitude
params.description: Optional maximum wave amplitude in uu

params.name: wind_angle
params.description: Optional dominant wind angle in degrees

params.name: small_wave_steepness
params.description: Optional steepness of the smallest wave (generator default 0.4)

params.name: large_wave_steepness
params.description: Optional steepness of the largest wave (generator default 0.2)

params.name: steepness_falloff
params.description: Optional exponent shaping the small->large steepness ramp (generator default 1.0)

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, wave_supported: bool, has_waves: bool, num_waves: int, max_wave_height: number, total_steepness: number, applied: bool }

commands.name: set_water_body_material
commands.description: Set the surface water material on a water body's UWaterBodyComponent (body found by actor label in the editor world, material loaded by asset path) and rebuild its material instances. The change is one undo step and dirties the level; nothing is saved. The material it already has changes nothing, adds no undo step and still answers set=true; set confirms the component now holds the requested material, and material is that material's short name, not its path. An unknown label, a body without a water body component, or a path that does not load as a UMaterialInterface is an error. Read it back with get_water_body_info; other body settings: set_water_body_properties; waves: set_water_body_gerstner_waves.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Actor label of the AWaterBody in the editor world (case-insensitive; the object name does not match).

params.name: material_path
params.description: Asset path of the UMaterialInterface (a material or material instance), e.g. "/Game/Water/M_Water" (the object path form also works).

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, material: string, set: bool }

commands.name: set_water_body_properties
commands.description: Set only the given settings of a lake, ocean or river water body, found by actor label in the editor world, reading each back with already_set; nothing is saved. Use it over set_properties for water_velocity/audio_intensity, which live per spline point: they go to the point at or before input_key, are read back from it and synchronize the spline. water_height_offset is ocean-only; the ocean's setter clamps it to >= 0 and rebuilds the body. Every other field that changes gets the editor's change notification, updating the water mesh and landscape. All checks run before any write: a spline value without input_key, a key before the first spline point, water_height_offset on a non-ocean body or an unknown label is an error that changes nothing. A value held exactly is not written (already_set true); otherwise the call is one undo step dirtying the actor's package. River width/depth: set_river_width_depth_at_point; waves: set_water_body_gerstner_waves.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBody actor (Lake/Ocean/River)

params.name: water_velocity
params.description: River/spline water velocity to set at input_key (requires input_key)

params.name: audio_intensity
params.description: Spline audio intensity to set at input_key (requires input_key)

params.name: input_key
params.description: Spline input key for water_velocity/audio_intensity (required only when either is set); a key before the first spline point (below 0) is an error and nothing is changed

params.name: target_wave_mask_depth
params.description: Water depth at which waves start being attenuated

params.name: max_wave_height_offset
params.description: Offset added to the automatically calculated max wave height bounds

params.name: collision_height_offset
params.description: Distance above the water surface where collision checks still occur

params.name: shape_dilation
params.description: Shape dilation in uu

params.name: affects_landscape
params.description: Whether the landscape is deformed by this water body

params.name: post_process_blend_weight
params.description: Underwater post-process blend weight (0..1)

params.name: water_height_offset
params.description: Ocean-only additional water height (errors on non-ocean bodies)

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, body_type: string, applied: [string], fields: { <name>: { value, already_set } } }

commands.name: set_water_body_spline_points
commands.description: Set ANY water body's spline path from world points, then synchronize the water spline metadata and RE-READ the spline (point count + closed-loop) to prove it landed.

params.name: water_body_label
params.description: Label of the AWaterBody actor. DESPITE THE COMMAND NAME THIS IS NOT RIVER-ONLY: it works on any water body that has a UWaterSplineComponent -- lake, ocean, river, custom -- and it is the only way to give a LAKE its real shoreline, because the spline the actor factory creates is an arbitrary CLOSED triangle (3 points) that has nothing to do with the basin. `closed_loop` is a property of the spline and is NOT touched here: set 12 points on a factory-made lake and you get 12 points still closed.

params.name: points
params.description: Array of [X, Y, Z] WORLD points (>= 2) defining the spline. Entries that are not a >= 3-element numeric array are skipped silently; `requested_point_count` reports how many survived parsing.

commands.returns: { water_body_label: string, point_count: int (RE-READ), spline_point_count_actual: int (RE-READ, same value, unambiguously named), closed_loop_actual: bool (RE-READ), requested_point_count: int, applied: bool (DERIVED: read-back count == requested count) }

commands.name: set_water_zone_settings
commands.description: Set a water zone's planar extent and/or its water-info render-target resolution, then RE-READ both from the actor (extent, world bounds, texel density) instead of echoing the request back. For a read without changing anything use get_water_zone_info; place a zone with spawn_actor (type="WaterZone"). Only the values passed are written, and one the zone already holds is skipped, so a repeat call changes nothing. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level). applied is derived from the read-back: false, with an error, when the extent read back differs (GetZoneExtent multiplies by the actor scale; see actor_scale) or the resolution does. water_info_texel_size_uu (extent / resolution) tells whether shorelines can resolve. A label no AWaterZone has is an error.

params.name: water_zone_label
params.description: Editor label (not the object name) of the AWaterZone actor in the editor world, e.g. "WaterZone_1"; whole label, case-insensitive, first match

params.name: extent
params.description: Optional [X, Y] planar zone extent. !!! THIS IS THE **COMPLETE** EXTENT, NOT THE HALF-EXTENT / SEMI-AXIS !!! The engine halves it itself (AWaterZone::GetZoneBounds2D: "GetZoneExtents returns the full extent of the zone but BoxSphereBounds expects a half-extent"), so passing 4000000 gives world bounds of [-2000000, +2000000] around the actor -- a 40 km sea, not 80 km. Reading it as a semi-axis gives a sea of DOUBLE the intended size with bounds off the map; the `world_bounds_extent` field in the response is what disambiguates it (half of `zone_extent_actual`).

params.name: render_target_resolution
params.description: Optional [X, Y] water-info render target resolution in texels, whole numbers, e.g. [2048, 2048]. Read back by reflection as `render_target_resolution_actual` (the getter is not exported, so this is the raw UPROPERTY, i.e. BEFORE the r.Water.WaterInfo.RenderTargetResolutionMax clamp).

commands.returns: { water_zone_label: string, zone_extent: [x,y] (RE-READ, kept for compatibility), zone_extent_actual: [x,y] (RE-READ, COMPLETE extent), world_bounds_extent: [x,y,z] (HALF-extent of the real actor bounds), world_bounds_origin: [x,y,z], world_bounds_min: [x,y,z], world_bounds_max: [x,y,z], actor_scale: [x,y,z], render_target_resolution_actual: [x,y] (omitted if unreadable), render_target_resolution_verified: bool, water_info_texel_size_uu: number (zone_extent / render_target_resolution; omitted if the resolution is unreadable or zero), applied: bool (DERIVED from read-back == request), requested: { extent, render_target_resolution } }
